ranked.reason: Highest score (7.7), a requested game, and the teacher already uses its predecessor. Build it first as the suite's SHELL, which every other game reuses: setup, AudienceProfile, teams, turn order, touch judge dock, undo, timer ring, end screen, resume, and board codes that stay mulberry32-compatible with /sinif-oyunu. Ship it with these fixes: LOCK THEN SPEAK (on 'Boards up!' every team shows at once, then the spokesperson says the full answer, not the letter); a whitelist of tile types per level (A1 Genç: picture MCQ, T/F with TPR, listen-and-choose, act-taboo); the kids' retry happens before any shadow board goes up; one comeback mechanic per skin; and c11's Open the Box as a 'speaking-prompt' tile type. The bonus row, Sürpriz değer and side bets wait for v2.

Best classroom logistics in the suite. Every team answers every item and all correct racers move together, so the whole class is active on every question. It is also the teacher's Kahoot/Blooket. Its 'Herkes cevaplar' MCQ core becomes the shared core for c05, c06 and c01: printed A-D cards that are exact copies of the on-screen tiles, a touch marking bar preset to 'all correct', and one big Reveal. Add a mandatory 'Say it!' beat after every reveal, and picture-only options at A1 Genç. v1 is the race only, with 3 skins and Hızlı marking. Lig becomes the platform-wide 'Sınıf Sezonu' module later, and letter analysis is opt-in for 4 teams or fewer.

The main speaking game and the teacher's Taboo (adult 8.7). Live circumlocution gives the most real spoken output in the set. MVP: Hot Seat ANLAT, Reverse Charades and ÇİZ on the classroom whiteboard, with Üç Perde plus Tek mod. It needs a four-button touch judging bar (Doğru, Pas, Yasak/Türkçe, Geri al). At low levels a frame sentence is required before any mime and the guess must be a frame; a 'rival guesser' replaces steal. Password, Deyim Resim, Cümle Sessiz Sinema and Kapışma move to v2. The screen part is thin, so the polish goes into the peek ritual and the recap stamps.

Top score (7.7) with feasibility 8 and teen 8.7. It is the tombala everyone plays at New Year: a calm, whole-class listening game that scales to 40+ students with no phones. Fix the card maths first: a pool of at least 2-2.5x the card cells, the maximum pairwise overlap minimised by a simulator, pairs sharing a card in big kids' classes, and a tie-proof prize ladder ('Stand up if you have a row' plus a spot-check, and a multi-number ÇİNKO pad). Audio comes first; the picture or Turkish shows only at the reveal. Tanışma Tombala moves to x05.

Requested (Hangman), with feasibility 8 and balanced appeal (adult 7.3, teen 7.7). v1 ships Kurtar only, on a shared word-tile component that c15 and c30 reuse later: a letter board, a friendly lives scene (never a gallows), the clue ladder, the solve panel, 'Use it!' and a word card. A1 Genç gets the 'Harf Avı' tray (the word's letters plus distractors chosen by sound) instead of 26 keys. The word is spoken first and the picture waits until 2 letters are in. 'Hepimiz yazalım' gives every team a write-and-show moment and ends the shouting. The Çarkıfelek mode becomes v2 on c11's wheel component. The adult Word Vault drops definition clues so it stays distinct from c30.

İsim-Şehir-Hayvan, which every Turkish student already knows. It scores feasibility 8 and adult 8, and it is the only real productive-recall game in the set; nothing else duplicates it. It needs a proper category bank: 60-200 members per closed category indexed by letter at build time, countries/cities/first names, inflections, and a letter-aware LLM prompt validated against words.js. Other fixes: rotate column ownership per seat; a 'Sheets up!' reveal per column instead of reading team by team; a 'Resim Bankası' mode on by default for A1 Genç; and a 'starts with the SOUND' rule for kids.

Requested (Monopoly-style). With c23 merged in, it is the suite's one board-game engine. Build it as a pure reducer over an action log, which gives undo, autosave and save-and-continue next lesson almost for free. v1: 'Kelime Şehri' on one Standart 20 board with A1-A2 rules (no auctions, no Deal Window). The Oyun Parkı ruleset becomes c23's 'Hazine Yolu' ladder race with Ask/Tell speaking squares and no money. Ask/Tell squares join every ruleset. v1.1 adds an Arena theme that is not childish (for example a theme-park tycoon); v1.2 adds B1+ auctions and trades. Shadow answers are on by default: a team scores when more than half its members show the right card. Adult A1-A2 get 'Cümle kirası lite', and the economy is tightened so money matters.

Speaking fluency and opinions (adult 8) in a suite that is otherwise mostly answering questions. Cut it to one turn engine with three surfaces: Çark (the wheel), Just a Minute (Talk Rocket for kids, BBC rules for adults) and Would You Rather, which also takes c17's Open Rank. Open the Box moves into c01; Story Dice waits for v2. A1-A2 get sentence targets instead of time targets, and every award needs an 'In English' tick. It needs a touch-first control bar and built-in packs cached offline. The wheel is a shared component.

The teacher's Millionaire (adult 8), cheap once the 'Herkes cevaplar' core exists. MVP: Relay plus Show mode (for kids, 'Tek roket' = the whole class as one team), safe steps, the lock-in and reveal ritual, and three lifelines that need no phones. Shadow teams commit face-down BEFORE the hot team talks, with one card per team. The flow is two taps: tapping an option locks it, and 'Göster' reveals. The ritual is said as language ('Final answer: B, giraffe!'), and kids get 'Say it!' picture rungs. The Sırala opener, the station wheel and the sparks economy move to v2.

The teacher's Jeopardy and the best adult quiz (8.3). Build it as a sibling board format on c01's shell: one engine, but its own hub card, so it costs little. It is single-screen first, with a touch teacher bar and a long-press 'göz' peek. The picking team gets full value and other correct teams get half. A mandatory 'Everyone says it' echo follows every reveal, huddles get phrase scaffolds, and a 'What's the question?' category is included. The phone remote and phone buzzers wait for the realtime decision.

An M-size speaking-fluency stirrer that works for 9-year-olds and adults and breaks up the quiz games. It ships as 'Sıcak Patates', so no bomb imagery appears on the homepage. The rules: one object and one active row at a time, a hidden fuse of at least 15 s, Kategori prompts plus Harf parçası from B1, and a picture potato wall at A1 Genç. In Oyun Parkı the holder gets no privilege: the pop triggers a whole-class Silly card and the helper badge rotates, which removes the stalling incentive.

Fills the critics' first gap: there is no TPR/movement game, yet it is the default warmer and brain break for 9-11s and the cheapest whole-class response. M build with two modes: Gogo Says / Captain's Orders (commands with a trap) and Stand Up If / Opinion Line (a spectrum at B levels, which is how adults come in). It needs pre-recorded audio for every built-in command and trap phrase, a coarse once-per-round class estimate, and a big animated caller so the screen carries the game. Adult appeal is low (5.3), so for adults it is pitched as the Opinion Line.

An M-size Wordwall-familiar game (teen 8.3) with the calm energy the suite needs. Add a mandatory 'Predict it' step before the second flip, and 'Point with Gogo!' so the waiting teams have a job. B1/B2 definition grids get asymmetric card faces. LLM generation is limited to relation types with deterministic uniqueness checks. Kids default to 2 rounds of 10-12 cards. Adults get Lock it/Use it collocation and irregular-verb grids; collocation domino (roadmap G05) can come later as a mode.

Requested (RPG), but the most ambitious game and the weakest on logistics (6). It ships last in the first wave and only as the map RPG: fog map, one power per hero team, class votes, a co-op boss, and 'a right answer always succeeds; dice only set the size of the reward'. Size maps with a measured clock (4.5 min per node for Genç, 3 for adults) and get the first scoring moment on screen before minute 3. A1 Genç get a pre-reader profile (picture fork cards with audio); low levels get karaoke read-aloud instead of typewriter text. Challenges come from the shared widget library. The case frame moves to c26, Yol Ayrımı becomes a later light game, and c25's Komut Modu can join it later.

Slap the board / balloon pop (teen 8.3), excellent listening for A1-A2 kids but thin for adults (6). First game of the next wave. It needs a real mirrored split-screen touch duel instead of the fake key-timing photo finish, and 2-team duels in Söyle for large classes. Seated students stay 'hands on heads' until the award, and retries are capped. MVP: Avla! with one item skin per audience, and Eşini Bul! as round 2.

The best adult score in the suite (8.7) and the only error-correction game. Its content is almost free: stem+key from the grammar MCQ banks is an original, stem+distractor is a forgery. Fix the scoring so risk is real (unspent money keeps 1x, a fixed forgery refunds 0.5x) and reveal per lot or every 4 lots. Raise the A1 Genç cap to 6 words and use an audio-plus-picture contrast for kids. Teen appeal is low (6), so it comes after the first wave.

Kelime Oyunu, the tv2 show adults know (8.3), an M build on c03's word-tile component. Düello is the default for 3+ teams. Kids' free prompts go through a 'picture available' gate, and A1 Genç chant the spelling. There is one finale per audience. It is next wave only because c03 fills the reveal-a-word slot first.

Wordle, an M build on the shared word-tile component (adult 7.7, weak for A1 Genç). Ship Relay plus the co-op 'Sınıf vs Kilit' (as the 'Günün şifresi' warm-up), Picture Wordle for kids, near-miss decoys, and an honest 5-6 min per word. Drop the hidden-letter Duel, which cannot work on one screen. A cheap follow-on to c03.

Codenames (adult 8): rich clue-giving and negotiation at B1+. Split it honestly by level: A1-A2 and kids play 'Listening Mission' (the app is HQ, no phone key), and real spymaster play starts at B1. Both spymasters think at the same time to remove idle time. The key sync uses the seed plus an algorithm byte, with an on-screen checksum. It waits for the key-delivery decision.

The only game where every student speaks at the same time, which is the biggest talk-time multiplier for classes of 30-40. v1 is projector + print only, with manual squad scores. Round 2 re-rolls the fact table ('Aynı görev, yeni bilgiler'), and A1 Genç get a turn-taking script mode. It needs print packs and a transport decision before it can join the set.

Battleship where firing IS saying the sentence: spoken question forms and short answers, a grammar-speaking mix nothing else offers. It needs a grid content frame and a no-phone presenter peek. MVP: Ortak Deniz + Düello, with ask/state cells only. Kids drop coordinates, point at the two pictures and hear a 'Dinle-söyle' model first. It takes c23's Dig site.

Fills a real gap: pronunciation and sound discrimination for Turkish speakers (v/w, θ/t, iː/ɪ, final devoicing, -ed). It depends on pre-rendered neural audio for the curated bank, which the whole suite needs anyway. MVP: Ses Avcısı, a track game (not a free maze) and a tongue-twister finale, with one-tap quick-start presets. It is teacher-judged, with no speech recognition (KVKK).

Whole class vs the game: the co-op option the suite lacks (teen 7.3). v1 has one threat model and 6 scenes, with 'Hafif kurallar' as the default (no roles, fixed power instead of dice) and packs sized to the lesson time. The tower grows to a fixed-height rescue and the lava rises only on misses, so the scene reads instantly.

Family Feud (adult 8), with answers in sentence frames and a good 'Our class in numbers' reporting ending. v1 uses built-in and LLM-generated boards ('We asked 100 kids') and a hands-up poll for Genç. The phone survey waits (MEB phone rules, KVKK, and moderation of open text from minors).

XOX / Connect Four / Blockbusters: a strategy layer on top of the questions, and cheap as a board mode on c01's shell. Every claim needs a production step, and English strategy frames are shown at every level ('Here!', 'Block!'). v1: XOX and Dörtle! only, 2 teams, and a fair 'Bitir' button.

Wordwall Group Sort / Unjumble / Rank Order as a relay, and the suite's one sort-and-order engine (BINS and SLOTS). Cards are dealt, not picked. Runners say the content ('Tiger goes in Wild'), not codes. Team talk happens once per heat, and touch targets sit in the bottom 55% of the board. Open Rank moves to c11.

Running dictation with a case-file frame (adult 8): reading, movement and evidence. Flaş/'Herkes izler' is the default for kids and Arena; Duvar is only for Stüdyo with 24 learners or fewer. Wall cards are fold-over flaps, chunk length is capped by memory, and the red-string evidence board is the centrepiece. It later takes x03's dictogloss as its Radyo mode.

The only persuasive-speaking council game (adult 8; Lost at Sea is proven in ESL). It is XL, so it comes later as an MVP on a 'Hikâye Motoru' shared with c04. It needs a one-tap teacher vote grid, a language demand tied to level rather than skin, and every vote chorused in a frame.

Two Truths and a Lie / Alibi with real people in the hot seat: strong question formation for adults (8). It shares the Dedektif engine with c26 (question templates, timeline, print pack) but stays its own game. MVP: Mode 1 plus 'Öğretmenin Sırrı'. Separation happens inside the room (no child sent to the corridor), and Alibi input is one tap on fixed question chips.

Adults love it (8.3), but it is a hidden-role, accuse-a-classmate game that fits 9-11s badly, and the core round gives little language per student. Keep only the quick 'Kelime Sahtekarı' mode, with 'Class vs Cat' for kids. Town Mystery and the kids' case move to c26; Crew mode is cut.

Kim's game / Spot the difference (teen 8.7), the natural home for there is/are and prepositions. The art is an XL, though: a sticker library plus slot-based background templates. Build it after the shared picture layer exists, with Modes 1-2 on screen only.

The detective case (adult 8, teen 5.7) has the biggest scope in the suite: a solver, a clue scheduler and an LLM pipeline. If built, v1 is 6-8 hand-authored cases checked by the solver, with no LLM, no phones, and whole-class agency for kids. It takes c04's case frame and c10's case modes.

Escape room (adult 8.3), but XL: 14 lock kinds and hardware assumptions that break in state schools. Later, as Kilit Modu only, with 6 robust lock kinds, a 'Tek ekran' profile and no-cut folded A4 packs. Komut Modu goes to c04.

The Bir Kelime letters round (adult 7.7, kids 5.7). It needs a 40-60k validation list and an 'Anlamı?' meaning gate so it tests the topic rather than general word breadth. Later, with two modes (Harf Havuzu, and Harf Çorbası for kids); Boggle is cut.

Find Someone Who / mingle: valuable teaching, but the screen does little and it depends on printing. Keep it as a printable warm-up and team-maker utility that takes Tanışma Tombala from c16. It needs absence-proof pair printing, tap-to-confirm pair numbers, and picture grids for kids.

Whisper chain: fun, but each student gets little language, it is three games in one, and the screen matters only at the reveal (6.0). Keep Fısıltı Zinciri as a small later stirrer with a tap-to-toggle reveal. Its dictogloss mode moves to c32.

merged into c02. One board engine (tokens, die, events, undo, camera, teacher dock). Its ladder race with Ask/Tell squares becomes c02's Oyun Parkı ruleset 'Hazine Yolu', and the Ask/Tell square types join every ruleset. The Dig site goes to c20, and the route/expedition map idea goes to c04.

rank.recommendedWhy: These 14 games cover the 4 requested games: Baamboozle as c01, Monopoly-style as c02 (with the ladder race merged in), Hangman as c03 and the RPG as c04. They also cover every other game the teacher named as liked: Kahoot/Blooket as c07, Millionaire as c05, Jeopardy as c06 and Taboo as c09. Two games every Turkish student already knows are included, Tombala (c16) and İsim-Şehir (c19), plus two for 9-13 energy and calm: TPR (x01) and Memory (c12). Speaking is built in three ways. c09, c11 and c24 are speaking-first. The quiz games get 'Say it in full' and choral echo beats. The board game gets Ask/Tell squares, and the RPG gets spoken gates. The set has 14 distinct mechanics: tile board, simultaneous race, ladder, category board, path board, word reveal, bingo, category rush, describe/draw/act, wheel and Just a Minute, hot potato, body response, memory and branching map. Every game has an adult form and a 9-13 form. Build cost stays sane because the set sits on six shared pieces: (1) the c01 shell (setup, teams, judge dock, undo, resume); (2) the 'Herkes cevaplar' MCQ core with matching printed A-D cards (c07, c05, c06, c01); (3) the word-tile component (c03, later c15/c30); (4) a deck + timer + touch judging bar (c09, c24, c11); (5) a seeded card/print generator (c16, A-D cards); (6) the action-log board reducer (c02). The RPG and later games reuse one challenge-widget library. Three games are M builds (c24, x01, c12) and two are cheap siblings on shared engines (c05, c06). Only c02 and c04 are XL, and both are phased. Suggested waves: (1) shell + c01, c07, c05, c06; (2) c03, c09, c24, c11; (3) c16, c19, x01, c12; (4) c02; (5) c04. This way two requested games are playable early and the two XL games reuse everything before them. The strongest near-misses form the next wave: c14 Swat, c22 Grammar Auction (adult 8.7), c30 Kelime Oyunu, c15 Wordle, c18 Codenames, c29 info-gap pairs and c31 pronunciation. They are left out because their slot is already covered (listening by c16/x01, word reveal by c03) or because they wait on a decision or asset (phones, audio clips, the picture layer, print packs).
rank.suiteSummary: Languago Sınıf Oyunları is a projector-first suite built for real Turkish classrooms: one screen, a teacher standing at a touch board, 20-40 students, no student phones and patchy Wi-Fi. After one merge (the ladder race into the board game) it holds 36 games. The first build has 14, sitting on one shared shell and a handful of shared engines. Each game appears in three skins chosen from the group: Oyun Parkı with Gogo the parrot for 7-11, a neon Arena for 12-14 that never looks childish, and a calm quiz-night Stüdyo for adults. The rules, pacing, text load and picture support also adapt by level (A1-B2), so an A1 nine-year-old answers with pictures, sound and body movement while a B2 adult writes, argues and wagers. Every game takes content through the same two doors: a built-in topic from Languago's own banks, or a teacher prompt, Turkish allowed, that the LLM turns into a pack. Code then checks that pack against words.js, the grammar banks and IPA before the teacher previews it. The whole suite follows the same rules. Every team answers every item ('Boards up!' first, then the spokesperson says the full answer). The final answer is spoken as language, not as a letter. Every reveal ends in a choral echo and a word card. Nobody is ever 'out'. Catch-up help is visible, never a hidden rig. And every game has a fair, positive 'Bitir' that fits the lesson clock. Mechanically it spans the formats the teacher already loves (Baamboozle, Kahoot/Blooket, Millionaire, Jeopardy, Hangman, Taboo, Monopoly), two national favourites (Tombala, İsim-Şehir) and a class RPG. Around them sit speaking-first games (describe/draw/act, speaking wheel and Just a Minute, hot potato), movement (TPR) and memory. The next wave adds error correction, clue-giving, info-gap pairs, spoken-grammar Battleship and pronunciation.
detailIdeas: Whose turn it is, without reading: the active team's colour tints a thin frame around the whole screen with the team shape as a faint corner watermark. The team chip shows a '1 2 3 4 5 6' seat row where the chosen spokesperson's number lights up.

'Boards up!' is a ritual: a two-beat drum and a card-flip sound, every team (the active one too) shows its card at once, and only then does the spokesperson say the full answer ('Final answer: B, giraffe!'). Nothing can be copied, the answer is language rather than a letter, and a '5/6 takım bildi' tally gives the teacher a no-names check of understanding.

Points fly as a '+10' chip from the tile to the team score, which rolls up like an odometer. On Undo the chip visibly flies back, so the class sees the correction. A long press on Undo opens the last 10 actions as a timeline to jump back to after a dispute.
The timer ring fades from the team colour to neutral grey, never to red, and ends with a two-note marimba chime instead of a buzzer.

Printed A-D cards carry the letter, the on-screen shape, a black-and-white pattern (for grey printers and colour-blind students) and the seat number on the back. The on-screen option tiles are exact copies of the cards, so one laminated class set serves every game and the spinner.
Tap any English word on a reveal card to hear it at 0.8x. A long press plays it at 0.6x with the stressed syllable lit up in the IPA.
When the teacher accepts an unlisted answer, a quiet toast says 'Bu cevap pakete eklendi', and next time that answer is accepted automatically.
Each team gets one 'İtiraz' card per game. Using it opens a decision screen with the key and the accepted answers side by side, which settles an argument in seconds.
Catch-up help is visible, never a hidden rig: a small wind icon ('Slipstream') appears by a team that hasn't scored for three turns.
A kids' wrong answer becomes a choral moment: Gogo says the word, and a 'Say it with me!' bubble appears twice with a dot bouncing over each syllable.
A sentence-frame strip ('I think it's ___ because ___.') sits under speaking turns. It changes with the level and fades away after three successful uses, as the scaffold stops being needed.

Every solved word ends on a word card (picture, sound, IPA, example, Turkish). The day's cards collect into a printable 'Bugünün kelimeleri' sheet and an exit ticket printed 4 per A4 with the 3 most-missed items, for schools with print quotas.
'Kaçırılanlar' carries over: next lesson, a 'Geçen dersten' door builds a 3-minute warmer for that class from the items it missed last time.

The end screen never says 'kaybeden'. Titles come from real stats (longest streak, fewest hints, biggest comeback, most rescued words). Kids who tie share a 'Dream Team' title; Arena and adults get an estimation tie-breaker ('How many items in this pack start with S?').

A shared 'Class Power' bar fills with every correct answer from any team and unlocks a whole-class dance break, a goal that sits above the team race. Each finished game adds a sticker to the class album, which belongs to the class, not to any student.

Tombala feels like New Year's Eve: the bag shakes, a numbered wooden pul rolls out with the English call, and 'ÇİNKO!' claims are checked by typing several card numbers on one pad. All valid cards get their stamp together.
The resume card shows a board thumbnail, the scores and '12 dk önce'. A long saved game (the board game, the RPG) opens next lesson with a 3-line 'Previously on...' recap, read aloud in kids mode.
The 'Çok gürültülü' button lowers the volume and offers a 60-second silent settler. 'Çok uykulu' offers a 45-second TPR stirrer built from the pack's own verbs.

Board codes are easy English nouns plus a number ('MANGO-42'), and kids' teams get alliterative English names (Brave Bears, Clever Cats) that show the Turkish when tapped: two tiny vocabulary moments during setup.
The 'Arka sıra testi' calibration screen is an eye chart of English sentences ('Can you read line 3?'), so even setting up the screen is English practice.

Every tap on the smartboard shows a soft ripple, with a 400 ms debounce so children don't bang it twice. The teacher dock sits low enough for a standing teacher, and a long-press 'göz' peek shows the answer while the teacher's body blocks the view.
Setup remembers the last packs per class and warns gently: '7-B bu paketi geçen hafta oynadı, yeni sorularla mı?'
Hub cards carry honest chips ('~15 dk · 2-8 takım · A1-B2 · Genç ✓ · baskı yok · hareketli/sakin') and a 3-second silent preview loop, so 'Bugün ne oynasam?' has an answer at a glance.

Calendar touches, all switchable: 23 Nisan balloons and bunting in Oyun Parkı, 'Happy Teachers' Day!' to the teacher on 24 Kasım, and falling leaves in November and snow in January, off with reduced motion.

Pause has personality: Gogo sleeps with a 'Zzz' and yawns awake on resume, Arena shows a scanline 'PAUSED', and adults get a calm analogue clock. Every freeze ends with a one-second 'Thank you!' before the board returns.

openQuestions.question: Who can open the games: is access public or does it need a teacher login?
options: Fully public, no login, built-in packs only
Teacher login required for everything
Public play with built-in packs; login only for AI generation, saved packs and class history
openQuestions.recommendation: Public play, login for AI and saving. A substitute teacher can start a built-in game in 10 seconds, while LLM cost, rate limits and saved class data stay behind an account.

openQuestions.question: Should there be a presenter / second-screen view for the teacher?
options: Single screen only, with a touch teacher dock and a long-press 'göz' peek
Optional second window on the same laptop (window.open + BroadcastChannel) for answers and controls
Teacher phone remote by QR over Supabase Realtime
openQuestions.recommendation: Single screen is the default and every game must work that way, because on most FATİH boards the board IS the computer. Offer the same-laptop second window in v1. Build the phone remote only after v1: Vercel functions can't hold websockets, and school Wi-Fi is unreliable.

openQuestions.question: Can students use phones?
options: Never: paper cards, mini-whiteboards and bodies only
Optional phone mode for adult courses only
Required in some games (survey, spymaster key, secret roles)
openQuestions.recommendation: Never in v1, and every game must be fully playable without phones (MEB's phone ban, KVKK for minors). An opt-in adult-course phone mode can come later.

openQuestions.question: What art style and mascot should the suite use?
options: One shared flat SVG sticker library plus 3 CSS-token skins (Oyun Parkı / Arena / Stüdyo) and Gogo the parrot
Bespoke art per game
Minimal typographic style using system emoji
openQuestions.recommendation: One shared, self-hosted SVG sticker library (Twemoji/OpenMoji/Noto base plus custom pieces) with 3 skins. Pardus boards may lack colour emoji, and the 800-1,200-concept picture layer is a prerequisite for most kids' variants, so schedule it first.

openQuestions.question: Where does the audio come from, and how loud and busy is the sound design?
options: Pre-rendered neural TTS clips (en-GB, optional en-US) for all built-in banks, with browser TTS only for AI packs
Browser TTS only
The teacher reads everything and TTS is optional
openQuestions.recommendation: Pre-rendered clips for built-in content, browser TTS for AI packs, a 5-second audio check at game start and a 'Öğretmen okur' toggle. Keep SFX soft (marimba, card flips, never a buzzer) with one global mute.

openQuestions.question: How are packs saved and shared?
options: Local browser storage only
'Paketlerim' in the teacher's account
Share by pack code or link with colleagues
Public pack gallery
openQuestions.recommendation: 'Paketlerim' plus sharing by code (reading the code aloud is itself a bit of English). No public gallery until there is moderation for LLM-made content.

openQuestions.question: What limits apply to AI (free-text prompt) generation?
options: Logged-in teachers only, about 20 packs a day, cached and reusable
Anonymous use with a small per-IP limit
Unlimited
openQuestions.recommendation: Logged-in only, about 20 packs a day, prompts up to about 300 characters (Turkish allowed). Every pack gets a mandatory preview defaulting to 'Hepsini onayla', code validation against words.js, IPA and the grammar banks, a game × pack feasibility check with a named fallback, and an 'Okul güvenli' filter.

openQuestions.question: In what order should the games be built?
options: Engine-first: shell + c01, then the cheap siblings c07/c05/c06, then the rest
The 4 requested games first
One game per mechanic family first
openQuestions.recommendation: Engine-first, with c03 pulled into wave 2 so two requested games are playable early. c02 and c04 come last because they are XL and reuse the shell, the widget library and the board reducer.

openQuestions.question: How are the skin and age profile chosen, and what about lise (15-18) classes?
options: Automatically from the group: Genç → Oyun Parkı or Arena, adults → Stüdyo
The teacher picks level and skin separately
Add a grade/age field plus a separate content-safety toggle
openQuestions.recommendation: Automatic from the group, with a grade/age field (7-11 → Oyun Parkı, 12-14 → Arena) and an override. Make content safety an independent 'Okul güvenli' axis that is on by default unless 'Yetişkin kursu' is ticked, so lise B1/B2 classes never get beer/casino items.

openQuestions.question: Is competition the default, or co-operation?
options: Team competition everywhere
A co-op 'İşbirliği' rule pack (the class chases one shared target)
Ask at setup ('Rekabet sever mi?')
openQuestions.recommendation: Team competition by default, with an İşbirliği toggle in every scored game and the question asked once in the Stüdyo class profile.

openQuestions.question: How much printing can the games assume?
options: Zero print everywhere
One reusable class kit (laminated A-D cards, mini-whiteboards, team tents) plus optional print packs
Print-heavy games allowed
openQuestions.recommendation: Every game playable with zero printing. Recommend the one-time class kit, and keep print packs (tombala cards, role cards, station cards) optional and paper-saving.

openQuestions.question: Should the games work offline or on weak school Wi-Fi?
options: Online only
PWA cache of built-in packs, audio and art; AI needs a connection
Full offline including saved AI packs
openQuestions.recommendation: Full offline for built-in and saved packs (PWA cache). AI generation needs a connection, so teachers pre-generate at home into Paketlerim.

openQuestions.question: What class data and scores are stored?
options: Nothing is saved
Per-class results and Kaçırılanlar saved locally, with no student names
Account-saved seasons (the 'Sınıf Sezonu' league)
openQuestions.recommendation: Per-class results locally, with team names only and no student names (KVKK). Add the Sınıf Sezonu league as a later platform module fed by any game.

openQuestions.question: Where do the games live on the site?
options: Extend the existing /sinif-oyunu page
A new hub (for example /sinif-oyunlari) with situation filters, keeping /sinif-oyunu as Kutu Avı
Only a homepage section
openQuestions.recommendation: A new hub linked from the homepage, with filters for minutes, energy, noise, movement, printing and minimum age, plus a ready 'Nöbetçi ders' playlist. /sinif-oyunu keeps working and opens Kutu Avı.

openQuestions.question: What happens to the Oxford-derived definitions in words.js?
options: Keep them as they are
LLM paraphrase plus teacher review
Wiktionary/WordNet text with attribution
openQuestions.recommendation: Paraphrase before the games go public. A length limit is not a licence, and every game shows definitions on a public site.

criticGaps: The picture layer that A1/A2 Genç variants depend on does not exist: words.js has no image field, and about 800-1,200 concept stickers plus a concept-to-word map must be built and scheduled before c12, c16, c19, x01 and the kids' version of c01.

Audio foundation: built-in banks need pre-rendered clips, because Pardus ETAP boards often have no English Web Speech voice. Nothing in the plan owns producing, storing and caching these clips across games.

The word bank cannot check open answers: there are no inflected forms, no countries, cities or first names, and few 4-5-letter lemmas. c19, c03, c24 and later c15/x02 need an inflection generator, an irregular-forms table, a proper-noun list and the accepted-answer memory.

The content model still has holes: a 'build' item for use-it-in-a-sentence bonuses (mustUse, target, models, checklist), 'grid' (c20), 'scene' (x04), 'dialogue' with speaker turns, 'command' for TPR (x01), and per-item audio fields.

There is no game × pack feasibility check: grammar packs make most vocabulary games worse, and Wordle, STOP and Battleship need specific content shapes. The picker needs a named fallback ('Bu paketten yalnızca 4 kelime çıkıyor...').
The first build has no pronunciation or sound-discrimination game (c31 is next wave) and no listening to connected speech (dictation or dictogloss via c32/x03), only single-item listening.

Large-class talk time stays low: the only simultaneous whole-class speaking game (c29) and the mingle game (x05) are outside the first build, and a 'Masa modu' (parallel desk play in groups of four for c02, c12, c13) is not designed.
Writing beyond single words is missing from the first build; only c19 and c03 write, and only at word level.
Pre-literate 7-9-year-olds: c19, c03, c09 and c04 each need a declared no-reading variant, or the hub needs a visible 'from age 10' tag. This is not yet specified per game.
Arena (12-14) theming is still undefined for c02, c12 and x01, which risk reading as childish to 13-year-olds.
Flashcard pre-teach ('Önce öğret'), cross-lesson retrieval and an exit-ticket plenary are platform features, but no one owns them yet.

Roadmap mechanics are still unmapped: G03 jigsaw reading, G09 map-directions info-gap, G17 stress changes meaning, G20 discourse chunks, G21 register transformation, G23 predict-and-update, G25 co-op logic puzzle, G26 word families, G28 repair duel and G30 4/3/2 retell. Each should be mapped as a mode or marked out of scope.
The minute estimates in every design are unvalidated. There is no pilot plan in a real 28-40-student public-school class and no timing telemetry to recalibrate the lesson-fit calculator.
Mixed-ability classes: nothing handicaps or differentiates per team when one class spans A1-B1.

Missing content categories: numbers, dates, prices and English letter names as a listening category; calendar packs (23 Nisan, 29 Ekim, 24 Kasım, the Bayrams, Yılbaşı); brand-free gaming words for Arena; YKS-YDT for private courses; classroom survival language for adult A1.

Accessibility beyond reduced motion and shape+pattern colour coding: students with hearing loss (captions on every TTS line), a dyslexia-friendly font option, and non-performing roles for students who will not speak in front of the class.
No testing on target hardware: nothing commits to a play-through on a Pardus ETAP board at 1366x768 with touch only.
Teacher onboarding is unplanned: a 60-second rules demo per game, printable A5 rule cards, and a first-run guide that doesn't nag.

merges.note: Full merge into one board engine (tokens, die, events, undo, camera, teacher dock). c23's ladder race with Ask/Tell squares becomes c02's Oyun Parkı ruleset 'Hazine Yolu', replacing the economy-lite Treasure Island, and Ask/Tell square types join every ruleset. c23's Dig site goes to c20; its route/expedition map idea goes to c04.
Mode move only; c11 stays. 'Speaking-prompt' becomes a tile content type on c01's single power engine, so the site has one power system, not two.

merges.note: Mode move only; c10 keeps the quick impostor mode, and Crew mode is cut.

Mode move, later; command-driven exploration fits the RPG map. c25 keeps Kilit Modu.
Mode move only; opinion ranking belongs with Would You Rather on the speaking wheel.
Mode move only; the mingle version belongs in the mingle/team-maker game.
Mode move only; it becomes c32's Radyo mode on one alignment/reveal engine. x03 keeps Fısıltı Zinciri.

catalog.name: Kutu Avı 2.0 (Tile Board)
catalog.familiarAs: Baamboozle Classic / Classic Jr (rebuild of the existing /sinif-oyunu)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams take turns opening hidden tiles on the projector. Each tile holds a question or a surprise card. Every team answers at once on cards or boards, a seat-number spinner picks who speaks for the active team, and the teacher judges with one key. The same engine is Gogo's treasure chests for 9-11s, a neon 'Challenge' grid for 12-14s, and a quiz night with wagers and steals for adults.
catalog.howItPlays:
REBUILD NOTE: this is the reference game for the shared classroom shell. It keeps the parts of /sinif-oyunu that work: the seeded mulberry32 shuffle, power tiles that look like question tiles until opened, the curated grammar-MCQ units (20 or more items each) as a built-in source, per-option whyOpt feedback, and the teacher's 'decline this card' button. It replaces the four fixed powers (Swap, Double, Steal 10%, Reset) with a surprise deck graded by harshness. It also replaces the İlkokul/Ortaokul/Yetişkin chips with the group chip and the merged AudienceProfile.

SETUP (under 60 s, one screen, Turkish teacher chrome)
1. Group chip, e.g. 'A2 Genç'. A summary line appears: 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk · Değiştir'. A saved class profile loads with one tap, e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena'.
2. Content. EITHER a built-in category: a vocabulary topic from words.js, a grammar unit from grammar_mcq_*, a YLE/MEB picture topic for Genç groups, or an adult life/work task set. OR a free prompt in Turkish or English, e.g. '6. sınıf 3. ünite, yiyecekler, some/any', which goes to the LLM, then the validator, then a preview.
   - The preview shows every tile's item. The teacher can edit it inline or press ↻ to swap it for one from the 30% reserve.
   - Ready packs from the local library load instantly and work offline.
3. Board format.
   - 'Kutular': numbered tiles, or picture tiles for kids, in grids of 12/16/20/24/30.
   - 'Kategori tablosu': Jeopardy-style. Stüdyo and Arena get 4-5 categories × 5 values. Oyun Parkı gets 3 picture columns × 4.
   - A lesson length of 10/20/30 min sizes the board (about 45-75 s per tile including the huddle).
4. Teams: 2-6. Up to 8 with 'Kalabalık sınıf', which shortens huddles and locks on all-answer mode. Names, colours, shapes and mascots or emblems are auto-filled per skin; tap to change. A 'Number off!' slide has students take seat numbers 1-6 inside each team. Names are never entered or shown.
5. Surprise level (the merged 'luck dial'):
   - 0 Yok: no surprise tiles.
   - 1 Sakin: 10%.
   - 2 Canlı: 20%.
   - 3 Kaos: 30%, Stüdyo only.
   It never exceeds the harshness level the mode allows, and each card can be ticked on or off.
6. 'Başlat' enters fullscreen, takes a wake lock and unlocks audio. A PRACTICE TILE follows (20-30 s, unscored): Gogo demos the flow in Oyun Parkı; Arena and Stüdyo get a 'Warm-up' tile.

TURN (question tile)
1. The active team's banner glows and does a small bounce, showing colour, shape and name ('Blue Pandas, your turn!').
   - The seat spinner lands on a number ('Player 3'). It never repeats the last two numbers picked in that team.
   - In Stüdyo the spokesperson number simply rotates, with no spin.
2. The team calls a tile by its number or its picture ('The yellow banana, please!'). A child taps it on the smartboard (tiles sit in the lower two-thirds so children can reach), or the teacher types the digits and presses Enter.
3. The tile flips (0.6 s 3D turn; a fade under reduced motion) and the prompt fills the screen at projector size.
   - A1/A2 Genç: the prompt is read aloud automatically at 0.8x. Everyone else gets a speaker button.
   - Options slide in after the options delay (3-4 s kids, 2.5 s Arena, 2 s adults). They sit on colour + shape + letter cards that match the printable answer cards: A red triangle, B blue circle, C yellow square, D green star.
4. TEAM TALK: a huddle ring of 10 s (kids), 15 s (Arena) or 20 s (adults, with pair consultation). It can be paused and extended by +10 s. A chime ends it with 'Boards up!'.
5. ANSWER MOMENT: the chosen player says the active team's answer aloud. At the same moment every other team raises its A-D card or mini-whiteboard. Kids may use TPR instead: stand = A/True, sit = B/False, hands up = C. Nobody waits idle.
6. JUDGE:
   - C marks the active team correct and W wrong, or the teacher clicks the option they chose.
   - Digits 1-6 toggle the teams whose boards were right (A = all, 0 = none); Enter confirms.
   - Open answers: holding Shift shows the accepted answers only in the small teacher tray.
7. REVEAL (Space/R): the answer and its accepted variants, a one-line Turkish reason (whyTr, or the whyOpt for the wrong option the class chose; whyEn at B), and a speaker button. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo says the answer and the class echoes it twice.
8. SCORE: see SCORING below. The opened tile keeps the colour and shape of the team that opened it, so the board slowly becomes a mosaic of who played what.
9. WRONG ANSWER, by mode:
   - Oyun Parkı: a soft marimba 'boing', then a second try with the next free hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star. The star goes to the class album, not the win count. The chest shows 'still locked'; there are no X marks.
   - Arena: the streak breaks. REBOUND: the first team after the active one in turn order whose board was right steals half the tile value ('STEAL!' strip). The active team loses nothing.
   - Stüdyo: the same rebound for half value. The answer plus a one-line 'why' is shown. Optional minus points (half the tile value) are off by default.
10. Next team, clockwise. The arrow keys override the order.

TURN (surprise tile)
- The card flips with its own sound and a 1-1.5 s animation. Kids chorus the card name with Gogo ('Rainbow!').
- If the card targets a team, the team that opened it chooses the target aloud and the teacher taps that team. Targets are never auto-picked.
- The teacher can press 'Pas geç' to discard any card. Every effect is undoable.

SCORING
- Oyun Parkı:
  - 1-3 stars by difficulty; a second-try answer earns 1 star less (minimum 1).
  - Correct shadow cards earn +1 star.
  - Scores never go down, and there are no speed points.
- Arena:
  - 10/20/30 points by difficulty.
  - COMBO: x1.5 after 3 correct in a row and x2 after 5, based on accuracy only and on the team's own turns only.
  - A rebound earns half the tile value; correct shadow boards earn +5 (outside the combo).
  - Hints take 2 points each off the tile's value, never off the team's score. The floor is 0.
- Stüdyo:
  - 10/20/30 points, or 100-500 on a category grid.
  - Side bets: +5/+50 for each correct board.
  - Optional negatives and wagers.
- 'Sürpriz değer' (Arena/Stüdyo only): the tile's value stays hidden until the answer is correct, then a drumroll reveals 5-30.
- COMEBACK dial (Light by default):
  - SLIPSTREAM: the last team gets +50% on each correct answer and a soft glow.
  - On category grids the trailing team picks the next category.
  - Strong: adds a gold 'bonus row' at x2 midway through.

ROUNDS AND END
- Board rows are grouped into rounds that follow the pacing dial:
  - Oyun Parkı: 3 rounds of 4-5 chests, with Gogo's 45 s stirrer (Simon says) or a 60 s settler (whisper chant) between rounds.
  - Arena: 2-3 rounds of 5-7 min.
  - Stüdyo: rounds of 8-12 min.
  - After 3 boards the screen suggests stopping.
- The last 3 tiles glow gold (x2) and get a drumroll. 'Son tur' (L) jumps straight to the final.
- FINAL:
  - Oyun Parkı, 'Golden Chests': everyone answers and correct cards earn double.
  - Arena, 'Confidence Call': each team writes x1, x2 or x3 on its board before one question. Right = value × multiplier, wrong = 0, never a loss.
  - Stüdyo, 'Final Wager': each team secretly writes a wager up to its own score. One question, a 'lock in' sting, and all boards are revealed together.
- TIE:
  - Oyun Parkı: the teams share the title.
  - Arena/Stüdyo: a sudden-death estimation tile (a qa number item with tolerance). The closest board wins, and speed never counts.
- END SCREEN: per mode (see the versions). It also offers the 'Kaçırılanlar' list, 'Sadece yanlışları tekrar oyna' (replays only the missed items as a mini board), 'Hardest question of the day' (the item with the lowest share of correct boards) and a print button.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Whole class split into 2-6 teams of 3-6. Up to 8 teams with 'Kalabalık sınıf', which forces all-answer mode and shorter huddles.
- Students number off 1-6 inside their team. The seat spinner (Oyun Parkı/Arena) or a rotating spokesperson number (Stüdyo) decides who speaks, so the same fast student never answers every time and nobody is picked by name.
- Every other team answers at the same moment on printed A-D colour-shape cards, mini-whiteboards, or TPR (kids).
- Teacher at the laptop or smartboard; a presenter clicker is supported. Children may tap tiles on a smartboard.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO 'Quiz Night' (A1-B2 adults)

LOOK AND FEEL
- Editorial quiz-night style: cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. System sans. Numbered tiles, or a category × value grid (4-5 categories × 100-500).
- No mascot and no voice lines; a neutral caption strip only ('Round 2 · Travel').
- Sound: woodblock and piano, 1 s or shorter, loudness-normalised. Music is off.
- Team names come from a generator: cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs', 'Present Perfectionists', 'Flat Whites').
- The student screen is in English; the teacher chrome is in Turkish.

TEAMS AND TURNS
- 2-6 teams of 3-5.
- A rotating spokesperson number, with pair consultation during a 20 s huddle.
- SIDE BETS: every other team writes its answer on a board and earns +5 (+50 on a category grid) when right, so nobody idles.
- Wrong answers rebound to the next team whose board was right, for half the value.
- Optional negatives (minus half the value) are off by default.
- The timer is an optional 30 s; speaking tiles get 45-60 s.
- 'Gizli skor' hides the scores until the end.

TILE TYPES
- MCQ: collocation, context, dialogue. 'Fix it' error tiles: the error span highlights as a hint. Open gap-fills. Odd one out, with the reason required at B.
- 'Say it another way' (B1). Word family and transformations (B2). 'Nasıl deriz?' TR→EN tiles for A1/A2 only.
- LIFE/WORK TASK tiles, e.g. 'Your flight is cancelled. Ask for a refund politely in one sentence.'
- 'Describe it' taboo tiles: the speaker faces the screen while the team turns its back.
- 30 s TALK tiles and 'JUSTIFY' tiles, scored against a 3-tick rubric: on task, target language used, kept going. Each tick earns one value tier, and a convincing justification adds +10.
- 'Convince us in 20 seconds...' mini-debates, at B2 only.

HINT LADDER
Definition, then example, then Turkish gloss. Each hint costs 20% of the tile's value. The TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.

SURPRISE DECK (Green + Yellow by default; each card can be ticked and its wording edited)
- Green:
  - Gift 5 (to a team you tap). Everyone +2.
  - Double (your next correct answer).
  - Shield (blocks the next Yellow or Red card aimed at you).
  - Brain break (20 s 'stand up if you...').
- Yellow:
  - Steal: half a middle tile's value from a team you tap, capped at that team's score.
  - Swap turn order.
  - Wager: bet up to 50% of your score BEFORE the question is shown.
  - Mystery Category: bet first, then learn the category.
- Red (opt-in):
  - Reset. It can be renamed, e.g. 'Audit: lose 20%'.
  - Seesaw: swap scores with a team you tap.
  - Virus: the tapped team must answer a bonus question within 20 s or lose 10. If it answers correctly, it passes the virus to a team of its choice (at most 2 passes).
- Adults choose the targets, which starts table talk.

FINAL AND ENDING
- 'Final Wager': a secret wager written on each board, one question at the top of the group's level, a 'lock in' sting, and all boards revealed together.
- Ending: full scores with a modest finale (a 0.6 s chime and the score rolling up).
- The 'Kaçırılanlar' review list can be copied or printed as a homework slip, with 'Sadece yanlışları tekrar oyna' and the hardest question of the day.
catalog.teenVersion:
TWO SKINS WITH TWO RULESETS. Oyun Parkı is the default for A1/A2 Genç; Arena is the default for B1/B2 Genç, and for any Genç group in MEB grade 6-8 or with 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor' ticked. The group label never appears on the student screen.

OYUN PARKI, 9-11: 'Gogo's Treasure Island' (Kutu Avı Jr, Nazik on)

LOOK
- Warm bright colours on cream, rounded shapes and an Andika-type font (single-storey a). The prompt font floor is 6vh.
- 12-16 treasure chests, each with a picture sticker from an A1 set unrelated to the pack topic (animals, fruit, colours, planets). Calling 'The red apple chest!' is speaking practice in itself.
- Gogo the parrot hosts. It demos the practice chest, peeks out from behind unopened chests, says the answer after a miss, leads the echo, hosts the hello and goodbye, and sleeps on the pause screen.
- Teams are animal mascots named in English A1 words, each with its own colour AND shape (Blue Pandas, Red Foxes, Green Frogs, Yellow Lions, Purple Penguins, Orange Tigers).
- Sound: marimba and xylophone, no buzzers. The quiet 'thinking' loop is optional.

THE 3 RULES
A Turkish card for the teacher plus pictograms, explainable in 20 s:
1. Pick a chest and say its name.
2. Team talk, then Player N answers, and everybody shows a card.
3. Right = stars. Not yet = we say it together.

HOW IT RUNS
- Picture-first cards: A1 Genç uses 0-4 words and 2-3 big picture options; A2 Genç allows up to 8 words.
- Automatic read-aloud at 0.8x; options appear after 3-4 s.
- Timer off by default. When on, it is a calm 40 s ring that never turns red, with a marimba chime at 0.
- 10 s team talk.
- Whole-class response every turn: A-D colour-shape cards, or TPR (stand, sit, hands up). On a surprise chest the class choruses the card name.
- Hints are free: picture zoom, then first letter, then listen again.
- Wrong answer: a soft boing and a second try with a hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class echoes it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album.
- Stars (1-3) never go down. There is no stealing, no elimination and no zeroing.

SURPRISE CHESTS (Green only, about 10-15%)
- Treasure: +2 stars.
- Friend Gift: give 1 star to a team you choose. These gifts count toward the 'Kindest Team' title.
- Rainbow: every team +1.
- Double: your next correct answer counts twice.
- Mystery Picture: guess a zoomed-in picture for +2.
- Brain Break: Gogo calls 3 TPR actions such as 'jump, clap, turn around'. The whole class does them and the active team gets +2. At most one per round; the actions can come from the pack's chance-cards.

PACING AND ENDING
- 3 rounds of 4-5 chests (3-5 min each), with a 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler between them, about 20 min in total.
- The last 3 chests turn gold and count double for everyone.
- Celebrations last at most 2 s (a sticker burst, a Gogo dance). Confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale.
- Ending: every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers, Kindest Team, Loudest Echo), with no ranking. A sticker goes into the class album, and a certificate can be printed.

ARENA, 12-14: 'Grid Clash' (Nazik underneath; mild steals only if the teacher opts in)

LOOK
- Dark navy or charcoal with neon accents in the team colours and a condensed display font. The prompt font floor is 5vh.
- 16-20 numbered neon panels. The wording is 'Match' and 'Challenge'.
- No mascot, no pastels and no 'Good job, superstar!'. A commentator strip shows at most one caption per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!', 'STEAL!').

OWNERSHIP AND RULES
- In a 10 s pick, each team chooses an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto. The motto shows on its banner.
- An English rule card with a Turkish toggle.
- 30 s timer, on by default, drawn as a ring in the team colour. 15 s huddle. Seat spinner plus mini-whiteboards.
- 10/20/30 points. The combo is x1.5 after 3 correct in a row and x2 after 5. A flame appears on the team badge at 3 in a row, and the leader wears a small crown.
- Hints (first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example) cost 2 points each off the tile's value. The floor is zero.
- A miss breaks the streak, and the first team with a correct board steals half the value. The original team loses nothing.

SURPRISE DECK AND ENDING
- Green cards: Gift 5, Everyone +2, Double, Shield, and 'Timeout' (a 20 s stand-up challenge).
- Yellow cards, opt-in: Steal 5 (capped at the target's score; Shield blocks it) and Swap turn order.
- Final: 'Confidence Call' (x1/x2/x3; a wrong answer scores 0, never a loss).
- Ending: a top-3 podium plus a stat award for EVERY team (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, Sharpest boards). There is never a 'last place'.
- Synth blips, and combo text for at most 1.2 s.

CONTENT
- The teenSafe filter applies in both skins: no alcohol, dating, violence, gambling, horror, politics, brands, rent, salary, office or boss.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics (school trips, sport, science facts), not abstract debate.
- A 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena visuals with A1 content and full picture and audio support.
catalog.levelTuning:
The CEFR level and the skin are independent. Level sets the text caps, the word bands, the tile types and the answer format; the Kolay/Orta/Zor dial moves the word-band mix inside a level (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words). 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops a whole level.

A1
- Prompt cap: 0-4 words for Genç (the picture carries the meaning), 10 words for adults.
- Tiles:
  - Picture to word, with 2-3 big picture options.
  - Yes/no and True/False with TPR.
  - 'What colour is it?' and 'What is it?' riddles with emoji clues.
  - Listen & choose: minimal pairs as two pictures, e.g. ship or sheep.
  - Tap-bank gaps.
  - Adults also get 'Nasıl deriz?' TR→EN tiles.
- Mostly difficulty 1. Timer 30-40 s when on.
- Hints: picture, then first letter, then listen again. The Turkish explanation is always shown.

A2
- Prompt cap: 8 words for Genç, 15 for adults.
- Tiles:
  - 3-4 option gap-fills (tap bank on the board).
  - Short personal questions ('What do you do on Saturdays?'). The teacher accepts any answer with clear meaning.
  - Chunked unjumble ('every day' stays one chip). Odd one out. Picture-description MCQ.
  - 'Say 3 words about...' from category-list, 15-20 s.
  - True/False on whether a sentence is correct. Simple 'What am I?' riddles.
- 30-40 s.

B1
- Prompt cap: 14 words for Genç, 25 for adults.
- Tiles:
  - Open gap-fill with NO options. 'İpucu: seçenekleri göster' turns it into an MCQ at half value.
  - 'Fix the mistake' error tiles. Collocation choice. 'Say it another way'.
  - Open questions that need 2 sentences.
  - 'Describe it' taboo with 2-3 forbidden words. 30 s talk tiles. Riddles scored 30/20/10 by the number of clues used.
- 45 s for open tiles. Rebound on. The difficulty mix shifts toward 2.

B2
- Prompt cap: 20 words for Genç, 40 for adults.
- Tiles:
  - Transformations and word family (decide/decision/decisive). Idioms and phrasal verbs. Paraphrase.
  - 2-slot gaps are allowed.
  - 'Justify' tiles (+10 when convincing).
  - 45-60 s talk tiles, plus mini-debates for adults only ('Convince us in 20 seconds...').
  - B2 Genç swaps the debates for concrete tasks: explain a rule, describe a process, 'Which trip would you choose and why?'.
- No options unless the teacher asks. Hints only at a cost. About 60% of tiles at difficulty 2-3, and tile values rise with difficulty.

ALL LEVELS
Long items are split into two cards rather than shrunk below the font floor, and the validator rejects any item over the caps.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 15-25 (12-16 chests in 3 rounds plus stirrers); Arena 15-30 (16-20 tiles); Stüdyo 20-40 (24-30 tiles or a 5×5 grid plus the Final Wager). A quick single board runs about 10 min at 12 tiles.
catalog.contentShape:
A board is N tiles (12-30) filled from one content pack. It needs N × 1.3 answerable items, because the 30% reserve feeds ↻ replace. Computed per tile: {tileNo, face (a number, or a picture key for chests), itemId, diff 1-3, value (stars / points / 100-500), category (grid mode), reserveIds[]}.

HOW EACH ITEM TYPE BECOMES A TILE
- mcq: stem, options[3|4] shuffled at presentation onto A-D colour-shape cards, answer, whyTr/whyOpt/whyEn on reveal. The ctx field feeds context and dialogue tiles.
- vocab tile formats:
  - Picture → word: media.emoji/img plus distractors[] as options.
  - 'What's the word?': defEasy (B groups: def).
  - 'Nasıl deriz?' (A groups): defTr.
  - Spell it: only when the computed hangman flag is true.
  - The 'gapped example' hint comes from gap.
- gap: text + answers[][]. bank[] is required for Genç and A groups on the board.
- qa: clue + accept[]. teacherJudge means accept[] appears only in the teacher tray. Number answers with a tolerance drive the sudden-death tie-breaker.
- tf: statement/isTrue/fix/whyTr, played with TPR stand/sit for kids.
- error: wrong/right/span. The span highlight is the first Arena hint.
- odd: items[4]/odd/reasonTr. reasonEn is required as a +bonus at B.
- riddle: clues[3] from hard to easy, revealed one at a time. Value 3/2/1 stars or 30/20/10.
- order: tokens[] as chips (chunked for teens), with alt[][] accepted.
- category-list: 'Name 3...' tiles. members[] are shown to the teacher only.
- speaking-prompt: talk, justify and wyr tiles. Starters are on screen; followUps are for the teacher; secs sets the ring.
- taboo-card: 'Describe it' (adults/Arena) or act mode (kids). defTr is for the teacher check.
- sound: minimal-pair and stress tiles, always with TTS. tipTr shows on reveal.

POWER CARDS
Power cards are engine data, not content: {id, harshness green|yellow|red, effect, amount, needsTarget, skinNames {park, arena, studio}, sound}. The pack's chance-card items only supply flavour and task text, such as Brain Break actions fitted to the topic. Their amount is always clamped by the engine.

PACK RULES
- Genç packs: every item needs an imageKey from the self-hosted SVG set, and unpicturable items are dropped from picture tiles. Everything passes the teenSafe filter.
- Every item carries level, diff and target so the board can mix difficulties and the review list can name the rule missed.
catalog.teacherControls:
KEYS (? shows the help overlay)

Board screen
- Digits + Enter open a tile. ←/→ move the turn manually. E opens the score editor. L = 'Son tur' (go to the final). F = fullscreen.

Question screen
- C = correct, W = wrong (or click the option).
- 1-6 toggle the teams whose boards were right; A = all, 0 = none; Enter confirms.
- Space/R = reveal. H = next hint. S = manual steal/rebound to a team. N = ↻ replace the item from the reserve (no penalty).
- T = pause or resume the timer. + = add 10 s.
- Hold Shift to peek at the accepted answers in the teacher tray.

Anywhere
- B or . = blank or freeze the screen ('Eyes on me'; matches a presenter clicker's black-screen button).
- PageDown = advance (reveal, then confirm, then next). PageUp or U or Ctrl+Z = undo. Undo keeps a full history of scores, opened tiles and power effects.
- M = mute. P = pause the game (Gogo sleeps / 'PAUSED' / 'Ara'). Esc = back to the board.

SETTINGS PANEL (Turkish)
- AudienceProfile override: skin, rule pack, or any single dial.
- Surprise level 0-3, with a per-card allowlist and editable card wording. Harshness Green/Yellow/Red; Red is Stüdyo opt-in only and Yellow is Arena opt-in.
- Comeback: Off / Light / Strong.
- Board format and size. Value mode: fixed / by difficulty / 'Sürpriz değer'.
- Timer (Süresiz, on, length) and huddle length.
- All-answer mode: locked on in Oyun Parkı. Seat spinner on/off. Rebound on/off. Negative points (Stüdyo only). 'Gizli skor'.
- Auto-read, and the TR gloss on/off. Kolay/Orta/Zor and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- Content preview with inline edit and ↻.
- A seeded board code (e.g. '7B-PANDA-42'): replay the same board with another class, or reshuffle so memorised tile numbers don't help.
- Score tray: +/-1, 5 or 10, or set an exact value.
- Class profiles saved locally.
- Automatic resume after an accidental refresh ('Oyuna devam et?').

PRINT PACK
A-D colour-shape answer cards, team signs, the kids' certificate, and the 'Kaçırılanlar' homework slip.

RULE CARDS
Turkish rule card with pictograms (Oyun Parkı), English rule slide with a Turkish toggle (Arena), and an English 'rules for students' slide (Stüdyo).
catalog.delightDetails:
ON THE BOARD
- Tiles flip with a 3D turn and a soft whoosh. Opened tiles keep the colour and shape of the team that opened them, so the finished board is a mosaic of the match.
- Kids' chests wear picture stickers, so choosing a chest is speaking practice. Gogo peeks out from behind unopened chests and naps on the pause screen.
- The active team's banner does a small bounce. Arena teams show their own motto on it.
- The seat spinner has a short tick-tick-tock and never lands on the same player twice in a row.
- The last 3 tiles glow gold with a drumroll.

CARDS AND ANSWERS
- Each surprise card has its own sound and animation, 1 s or shorter. Kids chorus the card name with Gogo.
- A-D options carry colour + shape + letter, so they are colour-blind safe and match the printed cards exactly.
- 'Boards up!' plays as a chime. The Oyun Parkı failure image is 'still locked' with a shrugging Gogo, never a red X.
- Text auto-fits, and a long item splits into two cards.

STREAKS AND FEEDBACK
- Arena: the badge gets a flame at 3 in a row, and the commentator strip ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!') appears at most once per turn.
- Stüdyo: the leader wears a tiny crown (Arena/Stüdyo only), and the score rolls up with a 0.6 s chime.
- Slipstream: the trailing team's badge glows softly when it is on a comeback.

FINALS AND ENDINGS
- Adults get 'lock in' suspense music for the Final Wager, with a volume dial.
- Every kids' team gets a warm title and a sticker in the class album, which grows across lessons.
- Arena gives every team a stat award, so no one is last.
- 'Hardest question of the day' appears on the end screen.
- Kids' confetti uses team colours AND shapes, and only at the finale.

COMFORT AND FIT
- Reduced motion turns every effect into a static stamp.
- An exam-season quiet mode mutes the thinking loop.
- A presenter clicker can run the whole game from the back of the room.
- A board code lets the teacher replay the exact same board with another class.
catalog.risks:
1. POWER LUCK FEELS UNFAIR, especially to strong adult teams (JALT). Mitigations: the surprise-level and harshness dials, per-card ticks, targets chosen by the players (never random), Shield, Wager and Pas geç. Kids get the positive-only Green deck.
2. IDLE TEAMS DURING A TURN. Fixed by the whole-class answer moment every turn (cards, boards or TPR), with shadow stars, points or side bets.
3. STEALS AND LOSSES UPSET YOUNG CHILDREN. Oyun Parkı has no steal, no loss and no zeroing. Arena steals are opt-in and never take the original team below what it had.
4. TEACHER-JUDGED OPEN ANSWERS ARE SUBJECTIVE. Accepted answers show only in the Shift-peek teacher tray, and speaking tiles use a 3-tick rubric.
5. The projected screen could leak answers. Nothing answer-related is ever drawn on the student area.
6. NOISE in all-answer mode. Use the 'Boards up!' chime and B to freeze the screen.
7. Printed cards are missing: TPR fallback.
8. No English TTS voice: 'Öğretmen okur' fallback.
9. LLM PACK ERRORS (wrong key, over the caps, unsafe for teens). Handled by the validator, the teenSafe filter, a mandatory preview, ↻ reserve items and cached packs.
10. Long B2 prompts overflow: split cards.
11. Tile numbers get memorised: seeded reshuffle.
12. The lesson runs over: the lesson-fit sizing plus the 'Son tur' key.
13. 12-14s feel babied: Arena is auto-suggested by grade or the tick box.
14. Overlap with /sinif-oyunu: ship this as its rebuild on the same route, keeping the curated MCQ units and the board code compatible, not as a new game.
15. The engine becomes the shared shell for the other games, so scope creep is real. Build the shell (setup, AudienceProfile, teams, spinner, judge keys, undo, endings) first, then this skin set.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Absorb any standalone 'Jeopardy / category grid' candidate as this game's 'Kategori tablosu' board format, so there is one engine and not two.

issues: ANSWER LEAKAGE THROUGH THE ORDER OF EVENTS. The spokesperson speaks 'at the same moment' as the other teams raise their boards. In a real room this is never simultaneous. Either the active team hears or sees the boards go up (neighbouring desks, 1 m apart), or the shadow teams copy the spokesperson's spoken answer. With 28 kids, shadow scoring then turns into copying whoever answers first.

THE KIDS' SECOND TRY IS HOLLOW. In Oyun Parkı, every shadow team has already raised its A-D card before the active team's 'second try with a hint'. The right answer is visible across the room, so the retry is a free star and teaches nothing.

THE JUDGING LOAD IS TOO HIGH FOR A TEACHER STANDING AT THE BOARD. Each turn needs: C/W, scanning 5-6 raised boards, toggling digits per team, Enter, Space for the reveal, and sometimes H/S/N. Most of this is keyboard-only. On a FATİH smart board the teacher stands at the screen without a keyboard, and a presenter clicker only has next/prev/black. Shift-peek of accepted answers is impossible by touch, and any on-screen teacher tray would be projected to the class.
'KALABALIK SINIF' ALLOWS 8 TEAMS, BUT THE BOARD TOGGLES ARE DIGITS 1-6. Teams 7 and 8 cannot be marked correct. Reading 8 boards per turn is also unrealistic.

THE SEAT SPINNER IGNORES REAL TEAM SIZES. 28 kids in 6 teams gives teams of 4 and 5, and absences change it daily. The spinner will call 'Player 5' in a team of 4, which causes arguments. Kids also swap numbers to push the strong student forward, and the teacher cannot police it.

TURN TIME IS UNDERESTIMATED FOR KIDS. The estimate is 45-75 s per tile. The real kids' path is: tile call, 0.6 s flip, auto-read at 0.8x, a 3-4 s options delay, 10 s huddle, answer, 6-team judging, reveal, echo twice, and often a second try plus another echo. That is 80-110 s. Sixteen chests plus 2 stirrers, the practice chest, card handout and number-off take about 30+ minutes, not 20. A 40-minute Turkish lesson loses 5-8 minutes to settling before the game even starts.

EACH TEAM GETS FEW TURNS. With 6 teams and 12-16 tiles, each team is active only 2-3 times. The Arena combo (x1.5 after 3 in a row, x2 after 5, own turns only) will almost never trigger, so the flame, 'COMBO x3' and the 'Longest streak' award are effectively dead features.

TPR DOES NOT SCORE PER TEAM. When 28 kids stand, sit or raise hands at once in fixed desk rows, the teacher cannot attribute answers to teams. The TPR fallback for missing printed cards therefore breaks shadow scoring. Standing in cramped rows is also a chair-scraping noise event every turn.

SETUP 'UNDER 60 S' IS UNREALISTIC ON FIRST USE. Printed A-D card sets per team (school printers are often unavailable), the number-off slide, mascot assignment and seating kids into teams take 3-5 minutes. The settings surface (about 20 dials, deck ticks, comeback, value mode) invites teachers to fiddle mid-lesson.

OYUN PARKI IS NOT REALLY 'NO RANKING'. Star totals are visible all game, so 10-year-olds will rank anyway and the 'titles, no ranking' ending feels dishonest. 'Friend Gift', and the 'Kindest Team' title it feeds, invites lobbying and gifting to friends, which creates social exclusion politics.

TARGETED CARDS CAUSE STALLS. When a team must choose its target 'aloud', 5 children shouting different targets causes 20-40 s of dead time and arguments, especially with Seesaw or Steal among adults who over-deliberate.

ENTERING THE FINAL IS HEAVY. Confidence Call and Final Wager require the teacher to type a wager or multiplier for each team, then per-team results. Done live with 6 teams, this is 60+ s of typing at the climax.

IT DOES NOT STOP CLEANLY WHEN THE BELL RINGS. 'Son tur' (L) still launches a final. There is no instant 'Bitir' that goes straight to the ending screen mid-question, and in Turkish schools the bell can't be negotiated.

SMART-BOARD TOUCH RISKS. Kids tapping tiles on the lower two-thirds can mis-tap the next tile, open two, or hit banners and score controls. Old FATİH boards have calibration drift and slow browsers, so the 3D flip and fullscreen or wake-lock APIs may fail. Pardus boards often lack an English TTS voice, which breaks the A1/A2 Genç auto-read.

ADULTS (10 PEOPLE). Only 2-3 teams are viable. The seat-number rotation feels school-like, and side bets of +5 against 10/20/30 barely matter. On a 5×5 grid, 25 tiles at about 60 s plus the final is about 35 min, which fits a 40-minute slot only with no talk tiles. Speaking tiles at 45-60 s plus rubric judging push it over.

ONE STRONG STUDENT CAN STILL DOMINATE. The spokesperson rotates, but the team huddle does not, so the strong kid decides and the spokesperson just relays. Shadow boards are likewise written by the fastest writer.
fixes: LOCK THEN SPEAK. On the 'Boards up!' chime, EVERY team, including the active one, raises its card at once, face-out and held until the reveal. Only then does the chosen player say the answer, to justify it or give the open answer. For MCQ, the active team's board is its answer.

REPLACE THE KIDS' SECOND TRY. Either give the retry before any shadow boards go up (shadow teams keep their cards face-down on the desk until the active team's final try), or make the second try a fresh reserve item on the same target. Never retry after the answer is visible.

ADD A TOUCH JUDGE STRIP. A slim bottom bar with big buttons: ✓/✗ for the active team, one chip per team for board-correct (with 'Hepsi' and 'Kimse'), and a single ▶ that does confirm, reveal and next. Show accepted answers on a phone 'teacher remote' page (QR, same session) or a toggle that blurs them for the class, instead of Shift-peek. Map the clicker's next key to the whole flow with sensible defaults (the active team wrong and no shadows correct counts as a no-op).

SUPPORT 1-8 IN BOARD TOGGLES, or cap 'Kalabalık sınıf' at 7. For 7+ teams, default the shadow scoring to 'show of hands per team: count correct teams' with a single 'N teams right' stepper rather than per-team toggles.

MAKE THE SPINNER SIZE-AWARE. Team sizes are set on the number-off slide (4/5/6 per team, editable daily with a quick 'bugün eksik' ±). The spinner draws only from the valid seats and cycles through everyone before repeating (a bag draw, not random), so every child speaks once before anyone speaks twice.

RE-SIZE THE BOARD FROM REAL TIMING. Log the actual seconds per tile during play and auto-shrink the remaining rounds. Use 90 s per kids' tile and 60 s per adult tile as defaults. Show 'Kalan: ~6 dk' in the teacher chrome, and make stirrers optional and skippable.
SCALE THE COMBO TO TURN COUNT. Use x1.5 at 2 in a row and x2 at 3, or count shadow-board streaks too. Otherwise drop the combo when there are 5 or more teams.

RESTRICT TPR. Allow TPR only for a whole-class, unscored echo or warm-up. For scoring without printed cards, add a finger-count fallback (1-4 fingers held on the chest) or 'write the letter on paper'. Offer a one-sheet PDF so a team can draw A-D in 1 min.

ADD A 'HIZLI BAŞLAT' PATH. The last profile plus a ready pack goes to the board in 2 taps. Hide advanced dials behind 'Gelişmiş'. Ship a 'first lesson' script: a 3-minute team-forming slide with a countdown and the number-off.

KIDS' SCORING. Hide star totals during play (the stars fill a shared class treasure meter instead) and show per-team stars only in the ending titles. Or keep the totals and be honest with 'everyone gets a title' and no podium. Remove 'Friend Gift' from 'Kindest Team', or make the gift go to 'the team to your left'.
ADD A 5-SECOND TARGET RULE. The team captain for that turn (the spinner's player) names the target, a 5 s ring shows, and if it runs out the target goes to the leader (adults) or 'everyone' (kids).

BIG TAP-CHIPS FOR THE FINAL. Enter wagers and multipliers with tap-chips per team (x1/x2/x3 buttons, or wager presets of 25/50/75/100% of the score) and judge all teams at once with the board-correct strip.
ADD A 'BİTİR' KEY AND BUTTON. It ends immediately to the ending screen, with titles computed from the current state, and saves the unplayed tiles as 'Kaldığımız yer' for next lesson.

HARDEN TOUCH AND OLD BOARDS. A tile opens only on a deliberate press (a 300 ms hold, or tap then confirm). Lock the chrome away from the kids' reach zone. Detect a missing English voice at setup and switch to 'Öğretmen okur' with a visible cue. Add a 'lite effects' preset for slow boards, and fall back gracefully when fullscreen or wake-lock fails.

ADD A SMALL-GROUP ADULT PRESET (8-12 people). 2-3 teams, no seat numbers ('whoever speaks, but not the same person twice in a row', one tap to mark), side bets at 50% of the tile value, and a talk-tile cap per board so a 40-minute slot holds.

ROTATE THE HUDDLE ROLE TOO. The spinner also names a 'writer' (a different seat from the speaker) each turn. Optionally, 'Solo tile' surprise cards make the chosen player answer without a huddle, for 2x, in Arena and Stüdyo.

issues: Recognition outweighs production. On most tiles the chosen player can just say 'B', and every other team only raises an A-D card. Across a whole board almost all language work is recognising the answer, not producing it. The game can easily turn into choosing colours.

A1 Genç children who barely read are only partly covered. Picture MCQ, T/F with TPR and listen-and-choose work for them. But the tile list for A1 still allows gap, qa, order, error, riddle and category-list, and the other teams are asked to write on mini-whiteboards. Spelling a written answer is out of reach for most 9-year-old A1 learners, so the whole-class moment breaks on any open tile.

The picture requirement cannot be met from the chosen content sources. Every Genç item needs an imageKey from the self-hosted SVG set, and items that can't be pictured are dropped. Grammar units (some/any, present perfect) and LLM prompts such as '6. sınıf 3. ünite, some/any' produce mostly items with no picture. The board then fills too thinly, or falls back to text tiles that A1 children can't read. The rule also applies to Arena B1/B2 Genç, which doesn't need pictures.

The built-in banks are too small. The board needs N × 1.3 items, so 39 for 30 tiles and 26 for 20. The curated grammar-MCQ units hold about 22 items each, and the teenSafe filter (no office, rent, salary, dating, alcohol) will remove adult-flavoured items from them. For Genç groups a single unit can't fill a 16-20 tile board with a reserve.

The 'at most 3 rules' limit for children is met on paper but not in practice. Oyun Parkı still runs a seat spinner, a huddle, shadow cards, second tries, effort stars, six surprise-card effects (Friend Gift, Double, Mystery Picture and others), rounds with stirrers, and golden chests. For 9-11s the real cognitive load is well above the 20-second checklist.

The chest stickers are unrelated to the topic ('red apple chest'). They help A1 children, but they are babyish and repetitive for A2/B1 children, and they add a second vocabulary set that competes with the lesson's target language.
The spinner puts one named seat number on the spot, and at A1 Genç that child must answer in English alone. Weak or shy children freeze, which conflicts with Nazik mod.

A1/A2 adults get an English-only student screen and rule slide ('Boards up!', 'Final Wager', 'Mystery Category: bet first'). Only Arena has a Turkish toggle. Absolute-beginner adults can't follow the meta-rules in English.

The caps and timing clash at the top levels. A B2 adult prompt of up to 40 words, plus 4 options, plus a 20 s huddle, is tight for weaker B2 readers on a projector at the back of the room. The B1 Genç open gap-fill with no options is also hard to judge fairly from mini-whiteboards when spelling differs.

Difficulty labels (diff 1-3) from the LLM are unreliable. Tile values, the Kolay/Orta/Zor mix and the 'hardest question' stat all depend on them, but nothing ties them to the words.js CEFR bands or the grammar unit level.
Turkish MEB prompts ('6. sınıf 3. ünite') depend on the LLM knowing the MEB curriculum. It will guess wrong unit themes, and the teacher will only notice at preview.

The tile mix is too wide. One board can mix 14 item types. That means many different answer formats to explain, which is too much for children, and a validator that is expensive to build when every type has its own level caps.
fixes: Add a 'Say it in full' rule for the active team from A2 up. The spokesperson says the full answer word or sentence, not the letter, and the teacher's C key means 'said correctly'. After every reveal, run a class echo in all modes, not only Oyun Parkı. At B levels, make every 3rd-4th tile a production tile (talk, justify, Fix it, Say it another way).

Give each level a whitelist of tile types. A1 Genç: picture MCQ with 2-3 options, T/F with TPR, listen-and-choose (sound), and act-mode taboo only. No text answers on whiteboards; other teams use A-D cards or TPR only. A2 Genç: add gaps with a tap bank, chunked order, odd one out and riddles, all with answer banks. Open whiteboard answers start at B1.

Make imageKey mandatory only for Oyun Parkı A1/A2. The LLM must choose from a closed list of imageKeys sent in the prompt, with an emoji fallback. For grammar packs, use picture-context MCQ, where the picture sets the scene and the stem tests 'some/any'. Arena and B-level Genç packs need no pictures.

When a unit is too small for the board, let the engine merge the neighbouring grammar units, or top up with LLM-generated items that are clearly marked in the preview. Show 'Bu ünite 16 kutu için yeterli' before the teacher picks a board size. Tag the curated bank items as teenSafe offline, instead of filtering them at runtime.

Ship a real Oyun Parkı v1 with 3 surprise cards only (Treasure, Rainbow, Brain Break), no Double and no Friend Gift, and no shadow-star bookkeeping; the teacher only counts right cards. Put the extra cards behind a teacher option and test the 20 s explanation in class.
Use topic-free picture stickers only at A1 Genç. At A2 Genç, use topic pictures from the pack (they reinforce the target vocabulary) or plain numbers read in English.

Add a 'Takım korosu' (team chorus) option, on by default at A1 Genç: the whole active team says the answer together and the spinner only picks who taps the tile. Add a 'pass to a teammate' lifeline once per round.
For A1/A2 adults, show a Turkish subtitle line under each rule and meta-caption ('Kartları kaldırın'), with a toggle. Keep the tile content in English.

Tie the timing to the caps. The huddle is 20 s plus 1 s for every 5 words over 20. B2 prompts over 30 words split into a context card and a question card. For open B1 gaps, add a teacher-tray 'yazım hatası kabul' toggle so misspellings can be accepted.

Work out diff from data instead of trusting the LLM: word band from words.js, the grammar unit level, and the prompt length. Recalibrate after play using the share of correct boards per item, stored in the local pack.
