Add a MEB unit-theme table (grade → unit → theme, target structures) to src/data and send it in the prompt when a grade or unit is named. If the unit is unknown, ask the teacher to name the topic instead of guessing.
Limit one board to at most 3 item types for Genç and at most 5 for adults. Show a small format icon on each tile face so students know the answer format before it opens.

reviews.mergeWith: Absorb any standalone 'Jeopardy / category grid' candidate as this game's 'Kategori tablosu' board format, so there is one engine and not two.
issues: It is not an L. Three rulesets, three skins, a surprise deck with 3 harshness levels and per-skin names, combo, slipstream, bonus row, side bets, wagers, Sürpriz değer, Confidence Call, Final Wager, the tie estimator, full undo, a seeded board code, class profiles, resume after refresh, a print pack and the Gogo mascot add up to an XL. It is also the shared shell that the other 9+ games depend on. If it slips, the whole suite slips.

Too many catch-up and variance mechanics stack on each other: slipstream +50%, the trailing team picks the category, the gold bonus row, the last-3 x2 tiles, surprise tiles, wagers and Sürpriz değer. Their combined effect can't be tested and scores become noise. Strong adult teams (the JALT risk the design itself cites) will find the result arbitrary.

Judging load per turn is too high. With 4-6 teams, the teacher marks C/W, toggles 1-6 for shadow boards, confirms with Enter, reveals, and sometimes runs the second try or the rebound. Doing that every 45-75 s is realistic for adults and not for a noisy class of 9-year-olds. The 45-75 s per tile budget is also optimistic for Oyun Parkı: 0.8x read-aloud, a 3-4 s options delay, a 10 s huddle, the answer, the reveal, the echo twice, and on a miss a second try with a hint.

Keyboard map collisions. 'A' means 'all teams' while A-D are option letters. 'B' blanks the screen while B is also an option. Digits open tiles on the board, toggle teams on the question screen and are also seat numbers. Teachers will blank the screen when they mean option B.

Touch and smartboard gaps. Hold-Shift peek, the '?' overlay and the key-only actions (S steal, N replace, E score editor) don't exist on a touch board. The design assumes a keyboard, but many Turkish classrooms run the smartboard with no keyboard at hand.

On a single projected screen, the teacher tray is visible to students. The 'Shift peek' accepted answers appear on the projector unless a presenter view (a second window) exists. 'Nothing answer-related on the student area' contradicts one-screen mode.

Asset cost is underestimated. The Genç packs need an imageKey from a self-hosted SVG set for every item AND for every distractor, since A1 Genç uses picture options. Realistically that means 300-600 consistent icons. On top of that come the chest stickers, Gogo's poses (peek, shrug, dance, sleep, demo), 6 mascots × shape × colour, 6 Arena emblems, per-card sounds × 3 skins, and a self-hosted Andika font. Without a closed icon vocabulary, the LLM will invent imageKeys.

LLM reliability risk. Free prompts must yield N×1.3 items of mixed types that respect word caps, have correct keys, and are all picturable for Genç. DeepSeek will produce wrong MCQ keys, answers that appear in the stem, ambiguous distractors, 'odd one out' items with two defensible answers, and riddles whose first clue gives the answer away. The validator can check caps and schema but cannot check that the key is correct.

The type list (14 content types) is too wide for v1. Each type needs its own tile layout, its own reveal and its own judge path (open gap, order chips, riddle clue stepping, taboo mode, TPR, sound pairs). That is 14 mini-UIs, and in practice each will be less polished than a few done well.

English TTS through speechSynthesis is unreliable on Turkish-locale Windows smartboards: voices are missing or load late, and on some browsers the rate of 0.8 is ignored. Automatic read-aloud is a core pillar of Oyun Parkı, so a missing voice breaks the kids' flow.

The seat spinner assumes teams of up to 6 numbered students, but the 'Kalabalık sınıf' option (8 teams) plus 36-student Turkish classes means teams of 4-5 with absentees. The spinner will land on missing seats.

Arena's commentator lines, crown and flame, emblem picker and 3-word motto pick, the 'Number off!' slide and the practice tile all eat the first 2-3 minutes. The 'setup under 60 s' claim does not hold for the student-facing ceremony.
fixes: Split the build into phases. Phase 1 is the SHELL: setup, AudienceProfile, teams, turn order, judge, undo, the timer ring, end screen, resume, board code (keep mulberry32 compatibility with /sinif-oyunu). Phase 2 is Kutular with only mcq, gap (bank), tf, vocab (picture/def) and qa, the Green deck, and all three skins. Phase 3 adds Kategori tablosu, riddle, error, odd and order, the Yellow deck and the finals. Phase 4 adds Red cards, taboo and speaking rubric tiles, and the print pack. Ship the phase 2 build to /sinif-oyunu.

Keep ONE comeback mechanic per skin. Oyun Parkı needs none (no ranking). Arena gets slipstream only. Stüdyo gets the trailing team picking the category plus the Final Wager. Drop the bonus row and Sürpriz değer from v1. Keep the last-3 gold tiles and remove x2 wherever a final also exists.

Make shadow-board judging one gesture: a row of team chips that are ALL pre-lit as 'right' after the reveal, where the teacher taps only the wrong ones, or auto-skip it when shadow scoring is off. In Oyun Parkı, default shadow scoring to OFF and give the whole class one shared 'class star' instead, which removes per-team toggling for kids.

Remap the keys to avoid collisions. Options go on 1-4 (or clicks). Teams go on the F1-F6 row or a touch chip row. 'All' = *, 'none' = 0. Blank = period (.) only, which is what presenter clickers send. Clickers only emit PageUp, PageDown, B/period, F5 and Esc, so make PageDown a strict state machine (open → reveal → judge-all-correct → next) and test it with a real clicker.

Add a touch-first teacher dock: a small bottom-right collapsible bar with ✓ ✗ Reveal Hint ↻ Undo Steal and Score buttons, so every key action has an on-screen twin. Replace Shift peek with a presenter view (window.open plus BroadcastChannel) that shows answers on the laptop. In one-screen mode, show the answer tray only on a deliberate long-press, with a 'projeksiyonda görünür' warning.

Create a closed icon vocabulary of about 250 A1/A2 nouns and actions as an SVG sprite, built from a single style source such as an open-licence line set that is recoloured. Pass the key list to the LLM as an enum. The validator drops or relabels any item whose key is not in the set. Picture options for A1 Genç are restricted to that set. Reuse the same sprite for the chest stickers.

Validator pipeline: a JSON schema per type; word caps per level; a CEFR band check against words.js; the answer must not appear in the stem; options must be unique and not substring-equivalent; a teenSafe regex plus word list. Then a SECOND cheap LLM pass acts as a 'solver': it answers each MCQ blind and flags any item where its answer differs from the key. Flagged items go to the preview with a warning badge instead of being dropped silently. The built-in curated banks need none of this.

TTS: probe getVoices() at setup and show a 'İngilizce ses yok, öğretmen okur' banner before the game starts. Optionally pre-generate audio for the built-in packs. Never block the flow waiting for speech.
The seat spinner reads a per-team 'present count' (teams sized 3-6) set on the teams screen and skips numbers above it. Add a 'yok' long-press that removes a seat for this session.

Budget the kids' time honestly. The echo happens once on a second miss, the options delay is 2.5 s when read-aloud is on (the prompt is being heard anyway), and a board holds 12 chests by default. Measure an end-to-end turn in a real class before promising 20 min.
Make the Arena emblem/motto pick optional and saved in the class profile, so it happens once per class and not once per lesson. Show 'Number off!' only on the first session of a profile.

Polish budget: spend it on the few things that make it feel like a real game. That means the tile flip, the mosaic board, the team banner, the timer ring, the reveal timing, and 5-6 excellent sounds per skin (loudness-normalised, under 1 s). It does not mean 14 tile types. A reduced-motion path and a 60 fps check on a low-end smartboard (Chromium, 1080p) are release gates.

catalog.rankReason: Highest score (7.7), a requested game, and the teacher already uses its predecessor. Build it first as the suite's SHELL, which every other game reuses: setup, AudienceProfile, teams, turn order, touch judge dock, undo, timer ring, end screen, resume, and board codes that stay mulberry32-compatible with /sinif-oyunu. Ship it with these fixes: LOCK THEN SPEAK (on 'Boards up!' every team shows at once, then the spokesperson says the full answer, not the letter); a whitelist of tile types per level (A1 Genç: picture MCQ, T/F with TPR, listen-and-choose, act-taboo); the kids' retry happens before any shadow board goes up; one comeback mechanic per skin; and c11's Open the Box as a 'speaking-prompt' tile type. The bonus row, Sürpriz değer and side bets wait for v2.

catalog.name: Büyük Yarış (Everyone-Answers Race, with a League mode)
catalog.familiarAs: Blooket Racing / Kahoot team mode / board race / Süper Lig standings
catalog.oneLiner: Every team answers every question at the same moment on printed A-B-C-D cards or mini-whiteboards. On the reveal, every correct team's racer moves forward together, so nobody waits. The team at the back gets a Slipstream boost. The same core also runs as 'Lig' mode: 10-question match days feed a Süper Lig-style standings table that carries over from lesson to lesson, with an optional LGS rule for 8th graders and YDS rounds for adults.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 60 s, teacher chrome in Turkish)
1. Pick the class profile (e.g. '8-B · A2 Genç · Arena'). The summary line reads 'A2 Genç · Arena · Nazik · 30 sn · 20 dk' with a 'Değiştir' link.
2. Pick the content. Built-in options are a category, a MEB unit, a grammar unit or an exam type (LGS / YDS / YÖKDİL). The teacher can also type a free prompt, even in Turkish (e.g. '8. sınıf LGS bağlam soruları, Chores ünitesi'). The LLM builds a pack, the validator filters it, and the teacher previews it in a list with 'Değiştir / Sil / Bunu da kabul et' on each item.
3. Pick the mode:
   - YARIŞ: a one-lesson race.
   - LİG MAÇI: a match day inside a saved season.
4. Pick the answer type: Kartlar (A-D cards, the default), Yazı tahtası (mini-whiteboards) or Karma (cards for most items, whiteboards for up to 5 harder ones).
5. The lesson-fit timer proposes the question count, and the track length follows automatically: ceil(questions × 0.7). That way an 80%-accurate team reaches the flag close to the last question.
6. 'Kartları yazdır' makes one A5 set per team:
   - A, B, C and D in fixed answer colours plus a shape and a pattern (A orange circle, B blue triangle, C green square, D purple star), so the cards work for colour-blind students.
   - The team's emblem and lane number in the corner.
   - A plain grey '?' back, so a card held face-down reveals nothing.
   - Optional extra cards: PAS (blank, League), SURE (adults) and a thumbs-up / thumbs-down card for True/False on the back of A/B.
   Laminate the sets once and reuse them all year.
7. Arena teams spend 10 s picking an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. Oyun Parkı teams are given an animal mascot.
8. A non-scoring practice question is demoed by Gogo in Oyun Parkı, or by a neutral 'Warm-up lap' caption elsewhere.

QUESTION LOOP (about 40-60 s per item; the whole class answers on every item)
1. PROMPT. The stem, picture or context appears first. The options fade in after the options delay (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s). A1/A2 Genç groups get automatic read-aloud at 0.8x; everyone else gets a speaker button. With no English voice, the fallback is 'Öğretmen okur'.
2. TEAM TALK. A ring timer runs: kids 10 s (calm, never red, marimba chime at 0), Arena 15 s, adults 20 s. It gets a reading allowance of +1 s per 3 words of context, and League/LGS pacing defaults to 90 s per context item. The seat-number spinner picks this question's card holder or writer in every team by seat number, never by name, so the job rotates. Cards stay face-down on chests.
3. SHOW. A '3-2-1 SHOW ME!' countdown (kids) or '3-2-1 SHOW!' (Arena, Stüdyo) plays with a drum hit, or a marimba hit for kids. Every team raises its card or board at the same moment, so copying is not worth it. A 'Quiet reveal' variant uses cards only, with no calling out.
4. TEACHER MARKS. There are three input styles, chosen in setup:
   - Hızlı: press 1-8 to toggle the teams that were right, then Enter. This is the default in Yarış.
   - Harf: press the team number, then A/B/C/D, or P for pas. This is the default in League; it records what every team chose and powers the 'most chosen wrong option' insight.
   - Hepsi doğru: press '*' and untoggle the few wrong boards. This suits whiteboards.
   On whiteboard items the accept[] list is visible only on the optional teacher phone remote, or behind a hold-to-peek key. 'Bunu da kabul et' adds a new variant to accept[] for the rest of the session.
5. REVEAL AND MOVE. The key lights up, and every correct racer moves at the same time: +1 space, with an 80 ms stagger so it reads as a wave. Movement comes from accuracy only; there are never speed points.
   - SLIPSTREAM (Comeback 'Light', on everywhere by default): the last-placed team moves +2 when it is correct. 'Strong' extends this to every team 4 or more spaces behind the leader and lets the trailing team pick the next lap's category from 3.
   - STREAKS (Arena and Stüdyo): 3 correct in a row gives a one-off Turbo (+1). 5 in a row gives Nitro (+2) and resets the streak count. Items answered after a hint still move the racer but do not build the streak.
6. WRONG ANSWERS, by audience:
   - Oyun Parkı: a soft 'boing'. Gogo gives a free hint (picture, then first letter, then listen again), and only the wrong teams get a second SHOW ME; right on the second try = a hop. If a team is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the whole class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album. A racer never goes backwards; a missed item shows the animal stopping for a sip of water.
   - Arena: the streak breaks and the racer stays put, followed by a one-line why (English, with a Turkish toggle).
   - Stüdyo: the key plus a one-line why. An optional Hard mode (Quizlet-Live style) moves the racer -1 space on a wrong answer, never behind the start line.
7. WHY STRIP (at most 5 s, 20 s in League). whyTr or whyEn, per-option reasons from the curated banks, and a 'Türkçe tuzağı' callout when the chosen distractor is an L1-transfer error (e.g. 'I am agree').

TRACK EVENTS
- CHECKPOINTS every 5th space:
  - Kids: a stamp and a flag photo.
  - Arena: choose Turbo (+1 now) or Shield (ignore the next setback).
  - Stüdyo: choose Turbo, Shield or Banana. Banana makes the current leader skip its next move; it is Yellow, and the same team cannot be hit twice in a row.
- EVENT CARD every 4 questions (3/4/5/off), drawn from the deck allowed by the Harshness dial:
  - GREEN (the only deck for kids): Pit Stop TPR (the whole class does 3 actions: 'Jump! Clap! Spin!', and every racer gets +1), Rain (a settler: the next question is whispered and answered in whispers), Rainbow (everyone +1), Double hop (the next correct answer = +2), Tow (the leading team picks a team to pull +1), Brain break (a 45 s chant).
  - YELLOW (Arena opt-in, adult default): Oil slick (the leader skips one move; nobody ever moves backwards), Swap lanes for the next lap's category pick.
  - RED (adult opt-in): Pile-up (the top two swap positions), Reset lap.
  - ADULT extras: the RISK CORNER, where each team secretly writes a bet of 1-3 spaces before a harder item is shown (right = +bet, wrong = -bet, never behind the start). The optional SURE card is raised with the answer: +2 if right, -1 if wrong.
- LAPS. The race is 3 laps, with a 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler between laps (optional for Arena and Stüdyo). The trailing team picks the next lap's category.

FINISH
- Stüdyo: the first racer to the flag triggers 'Finish!', and the race continues until 3 teams have finished (podium) or the time limit ends (the furthest team wins). Two teams on the same question get a 'Photo finish!' slow-motion; if Stüdyo needs one winner, a 'penaltı atışları' shootout follows (5 sudden-death rapid spelling/vocab items on whiteboards).
- Oyun Parkı: after the first finisher comes a 'Parade lap'. The remaining teams get up to 3 more questions at +2, then Gogo leads everyone over the line: 'Everyone crossed the finish line!'.
- Ties in Oyun Parkı and Arena share the place.
- A 'Race replay' (a 10 s time-lapse bump chart of every lane) plays before the endings.
- If the bell rings, the race state is saved locally and 'Yarışa devam et' resumes it next lesson.

LİG MODE (same core, football or space skin)
1. SEASON. The teacher creates a season for a class (e.g. '8-B · 2. dönem') with 2-6 fixed teams: kit colour, emblem and fictional name (Kartallar, Yıldızlar, Şimşekler, Aslanlar). It is saved to the teacher account and holds team data only, never student names.
2. FIXTURES. A round-robin fixture list is generated for the season. On a match day every team answers the SAME 10 questions (mirroring the 10 English items of LGS), and each team's goals = its correct answers. Each fixture pair is then decided from those goals: '8-B Kartallar 3 - 2 Yıldızlar'. W = 3, D = 1, L = 0. With an odd team count, the bye team plays 'Ortalama FC', whose goals are the rounded-down mean of the other teams' goals, so nobody sits out.
3. LGS KURALI (optional). Every 3 wrong answers cancel 1 goal ('net'), shown as NET and never below 0. The PAS card is allowed, which teaches the blank-versus-guess strategy. It is forced off in Oyun Parkı, off by default in Arena, and not used in the YDS rounds (YDS has no penalty).
4. GOALS. Correct teams get a goal-net ripple at the same time. The ticker updates live.
5. TABLE. After 10 questions, the table updates with the Turkish columns O G B M AG YG AV P. English headers (P W D L GF GA GD Pts) are available in Stüdyo. Tie-breaks: points, then head-to-head, then goal difference, then goals scored.
6. CUP TIES. Level fixtures in a cup final go to 'penaltı atışları'.
7. END OF TERM. A season trophy screen, printable champion certificates, and each team's strongest question type (e.g. 'Okuma %90 doğru').
catalog.playerSetup: Whole class in 2-8 teams of 3-5; 6-8 teams for classes of 30-40. Each team has one laminated A-D card set (Lig adds PAS; adults add SURE) or one mini-whiteboard with a marker. Seats inside each team are numbered 1-5 for the spinner, and the roles rotate every question: card holder/writer, checker, and speaker (for two-step items). Nobody is ever picked by name. Lig: 4 teams (2-6) stay fixed for a season with kit colours, and the teacher may rebalance them once at 'Devre arası' (mid-season), with the points carried over per team. The teacher runs one projector. The keyboard is enough, and an optional phone remote (teacher only, via QR) shows the key and a big tap grid.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: GRAND PRIX / MARATON / KARİYER MERDİVENİ
- LOOK: editorial quiz-night look, on cream or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, with system sans and no mascot or voice lines; a neutral caption strip ('Lap 2 · Travel'). Three skins:
  - 'Grand Prix': a minimal line-art circuit with numbered cars in lane colours and a pit lane.
  - 'İstanbul Maratonu': runners on a stylised route from the historic peninsula across the Bosphorus bridge, with landmark checkpoints (Galata, Kız Kulesi).
  - 'Kariyer Merdiveni': an office race from intern to CEO, for corporate groups.
  Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs', 'Past Perfects').
- RULES:
  - +1 per correct answer, with Slipstream Light (the last team +2 when correct).
  - Streaks: Turbo at 3 correct in a row, Nitro at 5.
  - Checkpoints every 5th space: choose Turbo, Shield or Banana (the leader skips one move).
  - Optional Hard mode: -1 on a wrong answer, never behind the start line.
  - Optional SURE card: +2 if right, -1 if wrong.
  - RISK CORNER every 5th question: each team secretly writes a bet of 1-3 spaces, then a harder item appears.
  - Event decks: Green plus Yellow by default; Red (Pile-up, Reset lap) by opt-in.
- TWO-STEP ITEMS (B1-B2): choose the option, then the rotating spokesperson gives the reason in one sentence for +1 (the teacher judges).
- WHITEBOARD ROUNDS (at most 5 items per race): 'write the noun of decide', 'rewrite using unless', the past participle, fixing the error, and dictation of the missing word from one TTS sentence.
- AFTER EACH REVEAL: a 5 s why line (Turkish at A, English at B, TR toggle), with the Türkçe tuzağı flag.
- PACING: laps of 8-12 min, 20-30 questions, track 20 or 30, 20-30 min in total.
- ENDING: the full standings, the race replay, and the 'Kaçırılanlar' list (the items most teams missed, with key and why), which can be sent to the Material Maker as homework.
- LEAGUE for adults:
  - 'Pub Quiz Ligi' (general English plus work-topic rounds such as travel, meetings, complaints and small talk; no penalty; department teams for corporate groups).
  - 'YDS Kupası': 10-item 'etap's by YDS question type (vocabulary, grammar, cloze, sentence completion, EN-TR equivalent, dialogue completion, near-meaning, paragraph completion, irrelevant sentence) at YDS pace (about 2.25 min per item, adjustable). It draws on readings_yds.js and readings_yokdil.js, grammar_mcq_b2.js and grammar_mcq_c1.js, and LLM context items.
  The full Süper Lig table with averaj is shown. Season stats per question type (e.g. 'Cloze %62, Paragraf %81') tell the teacher what to drill next.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two different rulesets, not one reskin. Level and skin are independent: a 9-year-old B1 class keeps Oyun Parkı, and a 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena with full picture and audio support.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1 and A2 Genç): 'ANIMAL RACE'
- LOOK: a cream background with a warm, bright palette, rounded shapes, big pictures and an Andika-type font. The racers are the team mascots: Panda, Fox, Lion, Frog, Tiger, Rabbit, Penguin and Bear. Each has little expressions: a hop on every step, a sweat drop on a hard item, a flower sniff or water sip when it doesn't move. The track matches the topic (food: a market street; animals: a farm; school: the playground).
- MASCOT: Gogo the parrot hosts. It demos the practice question, holds the finish flag, says the answer after a miss (a parrot repeats, and so does the class), and sleeps on the pause screen.
- THE THREE RULES (on a pictogram card; the teacher reads a Turkish rule card, and it takes under 20 s):
  1. Everyone answers: cards up on SHOW ME!
  2. Right answer = your animal hops.
  3. The animal at the back gets a big jump.
- CARDS: A = ant, B = bee, C = cat (at most 3 options at A1), and D = dog from A2, each with its big letter. True/False uses thumbs cards. The TPR fallback when cards run out: stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C.
- FLOW: picture and audio first, options after 3-4 s, automatic read-aloud at 0.8x. A 10 s calm huddle ring, with no answer timer by default (40 s if on, never red, marimba at 0). The seat spinner picks the card holder.
- WRONG: a soft boing, a free hint from Gogo, and a second SHOW ME for the wrong teams only. If still wrong, the whole class repeats the answer twice and the team gets an effort star for the class album. The score never goes down, there is no elimination and there are no backward moves.
- EVENTS: Green deck only (Pit Stop TPR, Rain whisper round, Rainbow, Double hop, Tow).
- PACING: 3 laps × 4 questions, a 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler between laps, track 10-12, 15-20 min in total.
- ENDING: the Parade lap, then 'Everyone crossed the finish line!'. Every team gets a title picked from its stats: Best Helpers, Super Listeners (most audio items right), Bravest Guessers (most second-try successes), Fastest Improvers, Kindest Cheerers. A sticker goes into the class album, with confetti in team colours and shapes at the finale only (2 s at most per event).
- STICKER LİG (kids' League): goals become stickers in each team's album across lessons. There are no fixtures, no losses and no ranked table; at the end of the season every team gets a cup with its title.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1 and B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç group in grades 6-8 or when 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor' is ticked): 'NEON CIRCUIT'
- LOOK: dark navy and charcoal, neon lanes in the team colours, and a condensed display font. The emblems are bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown and diamond, plus star and arrow for 7-8 teams. Teams spend 10 s choosing an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto, which runs along their lane. Karts leave drift sparks and turbo flames.
- COMMENTARY: no mascot and no pastels, only a commentator caption strip at most once per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!' when the last team overtakes, 'PHOTO FINISH'). The framing is 'Challenge' or 'Match', never 'Good job, superstar!'.
- RULES:
  - +1 per correct answer; Turbo at 3 correct in a row, Nitro at 5.
  - A wrong answer breaks the streak and the racer stays put (floor at zero, never backwards).
  - Slipstream Light.
  - Checkpoints offer Turbo or Shield.
  - Yellow Oil slick only if the teacher opts in.
- TIMERS AND TOOLS: huddle 15 s, answer ring 30 s in the team colour, options after 2.5 s. Hints are first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example; they are shared by all teams and stop streak building. Mini-whiteboards come in from B1.
- PACING: laps of 5-7 min, 15-20 questions, track 15, 15-25 min in total.
- ENDING: a podium for the top 3, then stat awards for every other team (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, Most clutch). Never a 'last place'.
- SINAV LİGİ (Arena League; ideal for 8th graders):
  - A football skin with kits, crowd sound (toggle), goal replays and a 'Haftanın takımı' badge; or the 'Uzay Ligi' skin (planets and star trophies) for classes that don't want football.
  - LGS-like context items: messages, posters, charts and short dialogues.
  - The LGS rule is optional and shown as NET (never negative), and a PAS card is allowed.
  - The Nazik table ranks only the top 3 on the projector. The other teams follow in fixed kit order with their stats but no rank numbers, and the full ranked table is teacher-only (print/export).
- CONTENT: teenSafe throughout (no brands, so no real club names; no dating, alcohol, gambling, office or salary topics). B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics, not abstract debate.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- A1 Genç: the picture carries the meaning. Prompts are 0-4 words ('Find: nose', audio 'Which one is a nose?'), with picture MCQ on 3 cards (ant/bee/cat), picture True/False and 'Which word do you hear?' for colours, numbers and animals. Track 10, huddle 10 s. Every item needs an SVG imageKey; unpicturable items are dropped.
- A1 adult: prompts of 10 words or fewer. Items are gap MCQ from grammar_mcq_a1.js (be, have got, present simple, there is), picture and meaning MCQ for survival vocabulary, and public signs. 4 options, track 12-15.

A2
- A2 Genç: prompts of 8 words or fewer. Items are 3-4 option grammar, odd one out with pictures, TYMM chunks in short dialogues, and spelling dictation of topic words on whiteboards (letters read aloud, first-letter hint). Track 12.
- A2 adult: prompts of 15 words or fewer. Items are 4-option gap MCQ, short messages and signs (KET-style context), dialogue completion (functions), and minimal pairs. Track 15.

B1
- B1 Genç (often LGS): prompts of 14 words or fewer, with longer context allowed as a separate card. Items are 4-option LGS-style context questions (chat messages, posters, charts, short dialogues), inference, error identification ('Which part is wrong?' A-D from the error span), and up to 5 whiteboard items (verb forms, prepositions). Lig: 90 s per item, LGS rule optional.
- B1 adult: prompts of 25 words or fewer. Items come from grammar_mcq_b1.js plus functions, word formation on whiteboards ('write the noun of decide'), and two-step items (choose, then say why for +1). Track 15-20.

B2
- B2 Genç: prompts of 20 words or fewer, on concrete topics. Items are collocation choice with close distractors, word families, short readings and limited transformations; Arena whiteboards.
- B2 adult: prompts of 40 words or fewer. Items are YDS-type rounds (cloze, sentence and paragraph completion, near-meaning, irrelevant sentence, EN-TR equivalent), whiteboard transformations ('rewrite using unless', register switches) with full alt[]/accept[] lists, tighter timers and optional Hard mode. Track 20-30.

Across all levels
- The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial shifts the word-band mix (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words) and how many whiteboard items appear.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the content one level without changing the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 15-20 (3 laps of 3-5 min); Arena 15-25; Stüdyo 20-30; one League match day 15-25 (10 questions plus the explain strips).
catalog.contentShape:
A race deck of 12-30 answerable items. A League match day takes exactly 10 items plus 5 penalty-shootout items. Every item is converted to one of two answer modes.

CARD MODE (A-D, A-C or A/B)
- mcq {fmt, stem, ctx?, options[3|4], answer, whyTr, whyOpt[]?, whyEn?, target, unit?, textRef?}. The key is reshuffled at presentation.
- tf {about, statement, isTrue, fix?, whyTr}, shown as A = True (thumbs up) and B = False.
- odd {kind, items[4], odd, reasonTr, reasonEn?}.
- sound {kind, a, b, ipaA, ipaB, contrast, key, tts}: 'Which word do you hear?' or '-ed: /t/ /d/ /ɪd/'.
- vocab {term, media, defEasy, def, distractors[3], gap}, turned into picture MCQ, meaning MCQ or gap MCQ.
- gap with bank[], where the options come from bank.
- error {wrong, span, right, errorType, whyTr}, turned into 'Which part is wrong?'. The sentence is cut into 4 underlined segments, and the one containing the span is the key.

BOARD MODE (whiteboards; A2+ spelling, B1+ open answers)
- qa {clue, accept[], answerKind, hintTr?, teacherJudge}.
- gap {text, answers[slot][], base?}.
- vocab spelling {term, alt[], tts} ('Write the word you hear').
- vocab family ('write the noun of decide').
- error {wrong, right} ('Write it correctly').

CONTEXT AND EVENTS
- text {title, body, sentences[], glossary[], questionIds[]}: an LGS/YDS reading lap, where the text is shown for 60 s and then 3-4 linked mcq/tf items are asked.
- Event deck: chance-card {kind, task, text, textTr, amount (clamped by the engine to 1-2 spaces), secs}. The built-in Green, Yellow and Red decks are used when the pack has none.

BASE FIELDS AND VALIDATION
Every item carries the base fields (level, diff, topic, teenSafe, media.emoji or imageKey, required for A1/A2 Genç). League stats also use skill, examTag ('LGS'|'YDS'|'YÖKDİL'|none) and unit/MEB theme. The validator enforces:
- the per-group word caps;
- a single defensible key for every mcq, since a disputed key ruins a simultaneous reveal;
- short options for the back row (4 words or fewer for kids, 8 for adults);
- no 'all of the above';
- whiteboard answers of 3 words or fewer below B2.

SOURCES
- words.js: CEFR band, emoji, IPA, family.
- grammar_mcq_a1..c1.js: curated items with whyOpt.
- readings_a1..b2.js, readings_yds.js, readings_yokdil.js.
- LLM generation for free prompts and LGS-style context items.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Mode: Yarış or Lig maçı.
- Teams: 2-8 teams (names, colours and emblems).
- Answer type: Kartlar, Yazı tahtası or Karma.
- Question count, and track length (auto = ceil(questions × 0.7), or 10/12/15/20/30).
- Timing: laps, and huddle length. The answer timer can be Süresiz, 30 s or 40 s, plus the reading allowance.
- Scoring: streak Turbo on/off, Slipstream / Comeback (Off/Light/Strong), Harshness (Green/Yellow/Red, limited by the audience), event frequency (3/4/5/off), checkpoint set (gentle/classic/off), Hard mode, the SURE card, the Risk corner.
- Help and feedback: second chance (kids), hint ladder, why-strip language (TR/EN/off), explain length.
- Sound and noise: Quiet reveal, sounds and crowd volume.
- Printing: A-D cards (+ PAS/SURE/thumbs).
- The lesson-fit timer.

LİG
- Create, save, reset or export a season (CSV).
- Fixture list and match-day selection.
- LGS rule on/off, blanks (PAS) allowed.
- Table view: Nazik top-3 or full; TR/EN column headers.
- 'Devre arası' team rebalance, 'Bonus haftası' (double points for the bottom half), cup final with penalties.
- Print certificates and the table.
- 'Maçın oyuncusu' spotlight: typed on screen only, never stored.

LIVE (keyboard)
- Space: next item / start the countdown.
- 1-8: toggle a team's correct answer (Hızlı).
- Team number then A/B/C/D, or P for pas (Harf).
- '*': mark all correct, then untoggle the wrong ones.
- Enter: reveal and move.
- Z: 'VAR' undo of the last move, with a VAR-review animation.
- Drag a racer to correct a position manually.
- '+': +10 s. T: pause (Gogo sleeps). S: Signal/quiet chime. R: replay audio. H: hint step (shared by all teams). K: hold to peek at the key.
- 'Bunu da kabul et' adds an answer variant. 'Soruyu iptal et' voids a bad item, with no moves.
- Skip or reorder items.
- An optional teacher phone remote (QR) shows the key, accept[] and a big per-team tap grid, so the key never shows on the projector.

INSIGHTS
- After each item: 'En çok seçilen yanlış: C (3 takım)', with the Türkçe tuzağı note.
- End of the race: the 'Kaçırılanlar' list, which can be sent to the Material Maker as homework.
catalog.delightDetails:
THE REVEAL
- The 3-2-1 SHOW! countdown with a drum hit (a marimba for kids), and cards held face-down on chests until the call.
- The signature 'everyone moment': all correct racers launch at once in a staggered wave.
- Motion: dust puffs, turbo flames, drift sparks (Arena), and the kids' animals hopping on every step. A camera zoom when two teams are neck and neck.
- 'Photo finish!' slow-motion with a camera-flash frame the teacher can print.
- The 10 s Race replay bump chart before the endings.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Lane colour + letter + pattern (stripes, dots, chevrons) + emblem on every lane, so no team relies on colour alone.
- Printable cards match their lane: emblem in the corner, answer colour + shape on the face.
- Kids' letter icons are A-words: ant, bee, cat, dog.
- Reduced motion swaps every effect for a static stamp.

CHARACTER AND VOICE
- Gogo the parrot flies the finish flag, repeats answers for the chorus, and naps on the pause screen.
- Arena lanes carry the team motto, and the caption strip says 'CLUTCH!' when the last team overtakes.
- Stüdyo sounds are woodblock and piano, a 0.6 s chime and a rolling score.

LİG
- A goal-net ripple on every correct team at once, a crowd 'ooh' on near-misses, and the match ticker ('8-B Kartallar 3 - 2 Yıldızlar').
- An authentic Turkish table with O G B M AG YG AV P and head-to-head tie-breaks.
- 'VAR incelemesi...' as the undo animation.
- The 'Haftanın takımı' badge, a season trophy screen and a printable champion certificate.
- Ortalama FC as the bye opponent.
- 'En güçlü alan: Okuma %90' cards per team.

ENDINGS
- Every kids' team leaves with a title and an album sticker; every Arena team leaves with a podium spot or a stat award.

LESSON FLOW
- Stirrer and settler interludes, and 'Yarışa devam et' after the bell.
- Accept-on-the-fly variants are remembered in the pack for next time.
catalog.risks:
- COPYING between teams. Mitigation: cards face-down until the simultaneous SHOW, teams seated apart, and the Quiet reveal variant.
- TEACHER MARKING SPEED with many boards. Mitigation: cards by default, whiteboards capped at about 5 items per race, the Hızlı and '*' input modes, and the phone remote.
- NOISE at reveals. Mitigation: the Signal key and Quiet reveal; only event cards are loud.
- AMBIGUOUS LLM MCQs are fatal in a simultaneous reveal. Mitigation: the single-key validator, teacher preview, 'Soruyu iptal et' and VAR undo.
- THE STRONGEST TEAM ALWAYS WINS. Mitigation: Slipstream, the Risk corner, mixed teams, and a Nazik table that hides lower ranks from Genç groups.
- A LONG SEASON DEMOTIVATES WEAKER TEAMS. Mitigation: 'Bonus haftası', the 'Devre arası' rebalance, and Ortalama FC so nobody sits out.
- EXAM DRILL EATS THE FUN. Mitigation: explain strips stay short and optional, and the LGS rule is off by default.
- THE LGS NET RULE CONFUSES 13-YEAR-OLDS. Mitigation: a 20 s pictogram explainer and a floor at zero.
- A FOOTBALL SKIN EXCLUDES SOME STUDENTS. Mitigation: the Uzay Ligi, Maraton and Grand Prix skins.
- NO ENGLISH TTS VOICE ON THE CLASSROOM PC. Mitigation: 'Öğretmen okur' prompts.
- PRINTING COST. Mitigation: laminate the cards once, or use the TPR or finger-on-chest fallback.
- PRIVACY. Seasons store team data only; 'Maçın oyuncusu' is never saved.
- 'LAST PLACE' SHAME for kids and teens. Mitigation: the Parade lap, titles for every team, and a podium plus stat awards only.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Fold any other 'everyone answers the same MCQ' candidate (Kahoot/Millionaire-style quiz show) into this engine. Pull Lig mode out into a shared 'Sezon / Lig' wrapper that any game can feed, instead of building it inside this game.

issues: The core loop is right. Every team answers every item and all correct racers move together, so the whole class is active on every question. That is the best logistics property in the suite, and the chosen card holder is the only bottleneck. The problems are around the core, not in it.

Setup is not 60 s in a real public school. Handing out 7 laminated A-D sets, forming teams, numbering seats 1-5 and running the emblem pick takes 4-6 minutes with 28 kids. Card sets also get lost or bent, or a team ends up with two C cards by week 3. The 60 s figure only covers the screen setup.

It assumes a keyboard, but the smart-board teacher stands at the board with no keyboard in reach. Hızlı (1-8 then Enter), Harf (team number plus letter for 7 teams = 14 keystrokes an item), '*', Z, K and H all need a keyboard or the QR phone remote. In MEB schools the Wi-Fi is often blocked or filtered and teachers are discouraged from phone use in class, so the remote can't be the fallback.

Harf mode as the League default is too heavy. The teacher has to read 7 raised cards, remember each one and type 14 keys while 28 kids hold their arms up. In practice, arms drop, cards get switched after the reveal and there are disputes ('Hocam biz B demiştik!'). The 'most chosen wrong option' insight costs roughly 15-20 s of dead time per item.

Nothing stops a team switching its card late. After SHOW, a team can glance around and flip. Nothing locks the choice and the teacher cannot watch 7 cards at once. The kids' second SHOW ME for wrong teams only makes this worse, because by then the right answer is visible on the other teams' cards.

There are far too many rule systems at once: Slipstream Light/Strong, Turbo, Nitro, streak exceptions for hints, checkpoints with Turbo/Shield/Banana, event decks in 3 colours, Risk corner, SURE card, Hard mode, laps, the category pick, Parade lap, photo finish and a penalty shootout. The teacher can't track which effect applies ('did Shield absorb the Oil slick?'), and neither can the students. The adult Stüdyo default alone has about 8 active modifiers. A misapplied effect makes the race look unfair.

The +1 moves, Slipstream, Rainbow, Pit Stop +1 for everyone, Tow and the Parade lap together compress the kids' race until it is almost meaningless. On a 10-12 track with 12 questions, the winner is decided by event cards and Slipstream timing more than by learning. That's fine for 9-year-olds. Arena 12-14s will notice and call it rigged ('onlar hiç bilmedi ama öndeler').

Slipstream goes only to the single last-placed team. With 7 teams, ties at the back are common, and the rule doesn't say whether a tie at the back shares the boost. Two teams near the back that are both 1 space ahead get nothing, which feels arbitrary.

One strong student can still dominate a team. The seat spinner rotates who holds the card, not who decides, so the strong kid whispers the answer and the card holder just raises it. The design has no mechanic for individual accountability.

Absences are a problem for fixed League teams in a public school. A 5-person team with 2 kids absent plays against full teams, and the design says nothing about it. 'Devre arası' rebalancing once a season is not enough when classes change.

League mode is really a separate product: season storage, fixtures, the table, head-to-head tie-breaks, certificates, CSV export, cup finals and Ortalama FC. It doubles the build and the teacher's setup load. The fixture results (3-2) are also just a relabelling of the scores of teams who answered the same 10 items, so the 'match' framing adds bookkeeping rather than play.

Printing depends on the school. Many teachers pay for their own colour prints and lamination. 7 colour A5 sets with 4-6 cards each is a real cost per class, and it multiplies across 6-10 classes. The TPR fallback (stand = A, sit = B) is chaotic with 28 kids and has no card for D.

Dead time for adults: 10 adults in 3 teams of 3, with a 20 s huddle, the countdown, marking and a 5 s why strip, is fine. But the laps, the Risk corner writing and SURE decisions add friction without much payoff for 3 teams, and the adult laps feel long at 20-30 questions with only 3 lanes. Adults may also find raising coloured cards juvenile if the skin doesn't sell the pub-quiz frame.

Noise: the reveal is fine, but the event cards (Pit Stop 'Jump! Clap! Spin!', crowd sounds, goal replays) with 28 twelve-year-olds in a public school next to other classrooms means 2-3 minutes of recovery each time. That is up to 3-4 times a race at 'every 4 questions'.

Stopping at any moment is only partly covered. 'Yarışa devam et' after the bell is good, but kids who hear the bell before the Parade lap or the titles leave without the ending. There is no 'finish now' button that jumps straight to the ending and awards titles from the current state.

The Oyun Parkı second-chance loop takes extra time per item. The hint, then a second SHOW ME for the wrong teams, then the class repeating twice and the effort star add 20-30 s every time some team is wrong, which is almost every item with 7 teams. 12 items then takes 12-15 min before the events, not 3-5 min laps.
fixes: Give the projector screen a persistent on-screen marking bar: big touch tiles per team along the bottom edge, where one tap toggles correct and a long-press opens the letter picker, plus a big REVEAL button. Make it the smart-board default, keep the keyboard as a shortcut and make the phone remote strictly optional. Keep the key hidden behind a hold-to-peek in the corner of the bar.

Make Hızlı the default everywhere, including League. Offer Harf as an opt-in 'Analiz modu' only for 4 teams or fewer, or collect letters with a single tap per team on a 4-colour tile (one tap, not two keystrokes).

Add a 'Donduk!' lock rule: after SHOW, cards stay up until the reveal chime, and any team that changes its card loses that item. For the kids' second try, have the other teams turn their cards face-down first, or give the second try only as the whole-class chorus without a hop.

Cut the default rule stack to 3 dials per audience. Oyun Parkı: hop, back-of-pack boost, Green events. Arena: +1, streak Turbo, Slipstream. Stüdyo: +1, Slipstream, a Risk corner at most once a race. Put Banana, Shield, SURE, Hard mode, the Red deck and Nitro under a single 'Ekstra kurallar' drawer that is off by default. Show every active modifier as an icon on the lane (a shield badge on the kart) so nobody argues.

Define Slipstream as 'every team tied for last' and add a cap: boosted teams can reach but never pass the leader on a boost alone. In Arena, show the boost's reason ('+2 SLIPSTREAM') so it reads as a rule, not favouritism.

In Arena, tone down the catch-up so accuracy still decides: keep Rainbow and Tow out of the Arena deck, show a 'Doğru sayısı' mini-counter per lane at the end so that 'most correct' earns its own award, and let the podium plus stat awards absorb the fairness complaints.

Add individual accountability to stop one student dominating: a 'Solo turu' item every lap where only the spinner-picked seat may decide, with no talking and cards up within 5 s. In Stüdyo, the spokesperson 'say why' step should go to the spinner-picked seat.

Cut the setup cost: print the cards once per class as a single A4 sheet per team (4 quarters) with a 'kartları topla' checklist screen. Offer a no-print mode: 'Parmak' (1-4 fingers on the chest, then raised on SHOW), which works for up to 4 options with no materials. Replace the stand/sit TPR fallback with it.

Add a 'Hemen bitir' button that jumps to the ending from the current positions (Parade lap compressed to one animation, titles awarded), plus a 5-minute warning prompt that the lesson-fit timer triggers automatically.

Budget the kids' second chance: allow it on at most 1 item per lap (or only when half or more of the teams are wrong). Otherwise do a single whole-class chorus repeat, with no second SHOW ME and no hint ladder.
Cap loud events at 1 per lap in Arena and Oyun Parkı, and offer a 'Sessiz sınıf' preset that swaps Pit Stop TPR for silent actions (thumbs, touch your nose) and turns the crowd sounds off.

Move League out of the MVP. Build Yarış first, then a platform-wide 'Sezon' meta layer (team points across lessons, table, certificates) that any team game can feed (sinif-oyunu, Jeopardy, this race). Keep the LGS NET rule as a Yarış option for 8th graders. Handle absences with a per-match-day 'bu takımda kaç kişi var' input and percentage-based goals, or allow merging teams.

For 10 adults, use 3-4 teams or pairs, a 'Pub quiz' skin with printed answer sheets or a whiteboard per team instead of coloured cards, 15-20 questions instead of 30 (a single lap), and the Risk corner only on the last 3 items as a closer.

Put a 1-line rule card with pictograms on screen at every event and checkpoint, and show a running 'Neden hareket etti?' log line under the track (e.g. 'Tilki +2: Slipstream'). This lowers the teacher's cognitive load and settles disputes.

issues: It is mostly recognition, not language use. On every item the output is a raised letter card, and team talk at A1-A2 Genç (and often A1-A2 adult) will happen in Turkish. Production is capped at 5 whiteboard items per race, and the spoken 'say why' step exists only for B1-B2 adults. At A1-B1 the game is close to 'pick a letter with friends', and the engaging part (the race) is disconnected from English.

A1 Genç readers who barely read have to map an on-screen option to a card letter. Pictures plus ant/bee/cat plus read-aloud handle this, but only if every option tile on the projector repeats the card's colour, shape and animal icon at a large size. The spec defines this for the cards, not clearly for the screen. Otherwise 9-year-olds hold up the wrong letter even when they know the word, and the game then measures mapping, not English.

'Unpicturable items are dropped' at A1 Genç is unrealistic for LLM free prompts, such as a teacher typing 'Daily routines, present simple' in Turkish. The LLM returns abstract or grammar items with no imageKey, the pack shrinks to a handful of items, and the teacher gets no clear feedback. The SVG and emoji coverage of words.js for verbs, adjectives and grammar is uncertain.

Minimal-pair and 'Which word do you hear?' sound items break under the 'Öğretmen okur' fallback. A Turkish teacher reading ship/sheep aloud is not a reliable stimulus, and a disputed key in a simultaneous reveal is exactly the failure the design fears.

Reading load on one projector for 30-40 students: LGS context items (charts, posters, chat screenshots), YDS paragraph completion or irrelevant-sentence items, and 40-word B2 adult prompts cannot be read from the back row, even with a reading allowance. Printed text is mentioned nowhere except the A-D cards.

The YDS Kupası (about 2.25 min per item, 10 items, plus explain strips) is exam practice wearing a race skin. At B2 adult it is a 25-30 minute silent reading session with a single card raise per item. The 'game' feel disappears, and it overlaps with dedicated exam tools.

Dial overload threatens the age fit. For kids the three visible rules are fine, but the teacher runs second chances, hint ladders, stirrers or settlers, event cards, the Parade lap, the TPR fallback and effort stars. For adults there are Turbo, Nitro, Shield, Banana, Oil slick, Risk corner, SURE, Hard mode and Slipstream stacked together. Adult A1 learners (often older or low-confidence) will not follow a SURE card plus a Risk corner plus a Banana, and the teacher will not find the right preset.

Kids' Pit Stop TPR, Rainbow and Tow give free moves with no English attached. That is fine for energy, but combined with Slipstream +2 and the Parade lap +2 the race outcome barely depends on answers for 9-11s. Older kids in Oyun Parkı (a 10-11 B1 class) may notice and disengage.

The error item ('Which part is wrong?', 4 segments) is B1+ appropriate. However, LLM-generated error sentences often contain two defensible errors, or a span that crosses the segment boundaries, and the validator rule is not specified.

The League mode is really a meta-layer (season, fixtures, table), not a game. Tied to this one game, it duplicates what any other suite game (Jeopardy, the tile board, Millionaire) could feed. Building it inside c07 makes the build XL and invites inconsistent seasons across games.

Arena for an A1 13-year-old: hints, commentary captions ('CLUTCH!', 'COMBO x3') and 'why' lines are in English, which is fine as flavour, but the why strip at A1 must be Turkish. The spec says Turkish at A level for Stüdyo, but for Arena it only says 'English, with a Turkish toggle'.

Adult A1-A2 'public signs' and survival vocabulary are appropriate, but the Kariyer Merdiveni and pub-quiz framings assume corporate or social adult groups. There is no neutral skin for adult prep-school or university A1 groups (18-20). This is minor.
fixes: Add a mandatory 'Say it!' beat after every reveal at all levels. The whole class, or each team's rotating speaker, reads aloud the correct option in its full sentence, as a chorus for kids and a spokesperson for adults. At B1+ Genç, extend the 'say why in one sentence for +1' step from adults to Arena. That makes each reveal a production moment instead of only a click.

Make every on-screen option tile an exact visual copy of its printed card: the same colour, shape, animal icon and big letter. At A1 Genç, show picture options only (no text) and point or glow each option while the TTS reads it: 'A... ant... apple'.

At A1-A2 Genç, block LLM generation of items that cannot carry a picture by constraining the prompt to picturable targets. When the pack falls under the minimum count, show the teacher a clear message ('Bu konu resimle anlatılamıyor: 7 soru kaldı. Bir seviye yukarı mı, sesli mod mu?'). Offer an audio-only item type ('Listen and choose') as the fallback instead of silently dropping items.
Allow sound items only when an English TTS voice is detected, or when the pack includes pre-recorded audio. Hide minimal pairs entirely under 'Öğretmen okur'.

Add a 'Metni yazdır' button that prints one A5 context sheet per team for LGS, YDS and reading laps, and apply per-level projector font floors. Cap on-screen context at about 60 words for Genç groups, and put longer texts on paper only.

Move the YDS Kupası out of this game into an exam-practice mode (or the Material Maker). Keep only short YDS types (vocabulary, grammar, near-meaning) in the race at no more than 60 s each, and drop the paragraph-type items from the race.

Ship 3 named presets per audience and hide the rest under 'Gelişmiş'. Examples: Stüdyo 'Klasik' has no SURE, Risk or Banana; 'Pub Quiz' adds Risk and SURE; 'Sınav' is Lig pacing. For adult A1-A2, make 'Klasik' the default.

In Oyun Parkı, tie free moves to English. Pit Stop TPR commands are given in English and the class must follow them. The Rainbow move requires a whole-class chorus of the last answer. Cap non-answer moves at about 25% of all movement so answers still matter.

For error items, have the validator require exactly one error inside one segment, with boundaries set by the engine. Allow them only from B1 and in the curated banks by default; LLM error items need teacher preview confirmation.

Split the League into a suite-wide 'Sınıf Ligi' meta-layer (seasons, fixtures, table, certificates) that any game can report match results into. Keep c07 as the flagship feeder. This cuts c07's build size and keeps seasons consistent across games.
In Arena at A1-A2 level, default the why strip and the hint text to Turkish, and keep the English commentary captions to 1-2 words.
Add a neutral adult skin ('Kampüs' or plain Grand Prix, set as the default) for 18-20 prep and university groups, and keep Kariyer Merdiveni as an opt-in skin.

reviews.mergeWith: Fold any other 'everyone answers the same MCQ' candidate (Kahoot/Millionaire-style quiz show) into this engine. Pull Lig mode out into a shared 'Sezon / Lig' wrapper that any game can feed, instead of building it inside this game.
issues: Scope is XL, not L. As written this is two products: a race game, and a season/league system with fixtures, round-robin, head-to-head tie-breaks, Ortalama FC, cup ties, penalty shootouts, account-saved seasons, CSV export and certificates. It also has 5+ skins (Animal Race, Neon Circuit, Grand Prix, İstanbul Maratonu, Kariyer Merdiveni, Football Lig, Uzay Ligi, Sticker Lig), each needing its own track art, racer sprites and sounds. The art bill alone is bigger than most of the other candidates put together.

Once the track is removed, the core is 'MCQ quiz with a progress bar'. Its polish depends entirely on the simultaneous physical card reveal and the wave movement. Everything else (banana, oil slick, pile-up, risk corner, SURE card, Hard mode, shield, turbo/nitro, checkpoints every 5, events every 4, laps, stirrers) is rule sprawl. The teacher cannot hold all of it in their head live, and the settings screen will look like a spreadsheet.

Too many interacting movement modifiers break the ceil(q x 0.7) track formula. Slipstream +2, streak turbo/nitro, checkpoint turbo, Rainbow, Double hop, Pit Stop +1 for all and parade +2 inflate the pace, so the first finisher arrives around question 60-70% and the race ends early or drags on in 'finish' mode. The track length has to be simulated with the enabled modifiers, not taken from a flat formula.

Slipstream is under-specified. Ties for last place (common early on, when everyone is on 0-2) and 'last-placed' with 8 teams need a rule. A 'Strong' comeback that applies to every team 4+ behind can make the leader the only team moving +1, which reads as punishing the leader.

Marking is the real bottleneck. In a room of 30-40, the teacher has to read 6-8 raised cards from the front and key them in. Harf mode is 16 keystrokes per item, and that is error-prone. Whiteboard items at the back of the room are unreadable to the teacher. The 40-60 s loop estimate is optimistic: with a why strip and marking it is more like 70-90 s, so 20-30 questions do not fit in 20-30 min.

Kids variant: the 3-rule card is fine, but the second-chance SHOW ME for wrong teams only leaves the right teams idle, and 'the whole class repeats' covers it only partly. Parade lap, effort stars, the class album, the sticker league and per-team titles each need their own persistence and UI. That is heavy for v1.

A1 Genç needs an imageKey on every item, with unpicturable items dropped. That requires an SVG picture library mapped to words. Nothing in the repo provides one (words.js has emoji at best), so either the kids mode ships with emoji only or the asset work is large.

Automatic LLM validation cannot enforce a 'single defensible key'. Word caps, option length and no 'all of the above' are easy to check. Ambiguity is not, and LGS-style context items and YDS cloze/irrelevant-sentence items are exactly where DeepSeek produces disputed keys. In a simultaneous reveal, a bad key hits every team at once and destroys trust.

Several parts duplicate existing or common assets: the team setup, colours and emblems of /sinif-oyunu; a 'Kaçırılanlar to Material Maker' export; a phone remote; a print-card generator; a hint ladder. If each game builds its own, polish will vary and the build cost repeats.
The print cards overlap with Plickers-like expectations. Teachers may ask for automatic card scanning, and the spec rightly avoids it, but it should say so explicitly to set expectations.

Build risk: the TTS read-aloud at 0.8x depends on English voices being installed on classroom Windows PCs, which is often not the case. The fallback exists, but the kids flow is designed around audio-first items.

Adult fit is decent (a pub-quiz feel), but adults get much of the same value from the existing Baamboozle clone. The YDS Kupası at 2.25 min per item on one projector for 10 items is a mock exam with a scoreboard, and its pace kills the race feel.
fixes: Ship in phases. v1 = Yarış only, with 3 skins (Animal Race / Neon Circuit / Grand Prix), one track layout per skin that is recoloured by topic tint (not per-topic art), cards mode plus Hızlı and '*' marking, Slipstream Light, streaks (Arena/Stüdyo), the Green event deck, VAR undo, 'Soruyu iptal et', resume after the bell and Race replay. Cut from v1: Banana, the Risk corner, SURE, Red deck, Maraton and Kariyer skins, shootouts, Karma mode.

Build Lig as a shared platform module ('Sınıf Sezonu'): a season, fixed teams and a points table fed by the result of ANY game (Yarış, sinif-oyunu, Jeopardy...). Fixtures, Ortalama FC and cup/penalty rules go into v2 of that module. The Sticker album for kids lives in the same module.

Replace the track formula with a quick Monte-Carlo in setup: simulate 200 races at the expected accuracy (default 70%) with the enabled modifiers, and pick the track length that makes the median first finish land on question N-1. Show 'Tahmini bitiş: ~18. soru'.

Define Slipstream precisely: it applies only when the team is strictly behind every other team, or to all teams tied for last when fewer than half the teams are tied; it never applies in the first 3 questions. Strong mode caps the bonus at +1 extra, and at most half the teams can get it.

Reduce marking load. For MCQ, add a 'Sayım' input where the teacher taps only the teams that were WRONG (usually fewer). Put huge colour+shape card faces on the cards (the shape carries at 10 m). Recommend at most 6 teams by default, and 8 only with the phone remote. Limit whiteboard items to B1+ and to at most 3 per race unless teams are seated at the front.

Budget the time honestly. Per-item time is roughly options delay + huddle + 3 s countdown + marking (~8 s) + reveal animation (2 s) + why strip. The lesson-fit timer should use measured averages from past sessions (stored locally) and propose 12-20 questions, not 30.

LLM validation pipeline: (1) JSON schema + word-cap/option-length checks; (2) a blind solver pass, where a second call answers each item without the key and the item is rejected if it disagrees or reports low confidence; (3) a distractor check, where the model must explain why each wrong option is wrong, and the item is rejected if it cannot; (4) the teacher preview list. Default to curated grammar_mcq banks and deterministic generators from words.js (meaning MCQ, odd one out by POS/band, error segmentation from span), and use the LLM mainly for context items.

Kids A1: accept emoji as the 'picture' in v1 (words.js emoji plus a curated emoji map for the A1 topic words) and drop items that have no emoji. Treat an SVG picture set as a separate, platform-wide asset task shared with other games (Memory, Bingo, Hangman).
Keep the kids second chance, but give the right teams a job: they show the answer with a gesture or chorus it once the reveal happens. Cap it at one retry per item and 5 s.

Share infrastructure across all games: a team setup component (names/colours/emblems/patterns), a print-card generator, the teacher phone remote (QR plus the websocket/Supabase realtime channel), and 'Kaçırılanlar to Material Maker'. Build them once here and reuse them.

Make polish concentrated rather than spread thin. The signature moments are the '3-2-1 SHOW!' countdown, the staggered wave launch, a neck-and-neck camera zoom, Photo finish and Race replay. Do those five superbly with SVG + CSS/WAAPI animation and 6-8 small sound files (under 150 KB total, per skin: tick, drum/marimba, hop, whoosh, chime, fanfare). Skip crowd audio and goal replays in v1.

Drop the YDS Kupası from the race. Offer YDS/LGS item packs inside the normal Yarış with a longer reading allowance, and keep the race pace. A dedicated exam-drill mode belongs to the League module's later phase, if at all.
Settings UX: show 3 presets per audience ('Sade / Klasik / Kaotik') with the full dial list collapsed under 'Gelişmiş'. Saved class profiles store the preset plus overrides.

Input: keyboard plus large on-screen tap targets for smartboards (a team grid at the bottom edge, 64px+). Swipe/drag to correct a racer. Test at a 1280x720 projector resolution and on a 75" touch panel.

catalog.rankReason: Best classroom logistics in the suite. Every team answers every item and all correct racers move together, so the whole class is active on every question. It is also the teacher's Kahoot/Blooket. Its 'Herkes cevaplar' MCQ core becomes the shared core for c05, c06 and c01: printed A-D cards that are exact copies of the on-screen tiles, a touch marking bar preset to 'all correct', and one big Reveal. Add a mandatory 'Say it!' beat after every reveal, and picture-only options at A1 Genç. v1 is the race only, with 3 skins and Hızlı marking. Lig becomes the platform-wide 'Sınıf Sezonu' module later, and letter analysis is opt-in for 4 teams or fewer.

catalog.name: Anlat-Çiz-Canlandır
catalog.familiarAs: Tabu + Hot Seat / Backs to the Board + Heads Up + Pictionary + Sessiz Sinema (Charades) + Activity (the board game's describe/draw/act spinner), with a Password round and a literal-idiom Pictionary deck
catalog.oneLiner: One player guesses a secret word while the team gets it across by describing, drawing or acting it. The forbidden words, timer and rules scale from a picture-and-mime 'Magic Chair' for 9-year-olds to a five-forbidden-word 'Taboo Night' for B2 adults. Nobody ever has to perform alone.
catalog.howItPlays:
CORE. A card holds one secret: a word, chunk, phrasal verb or idiom, or a short sentence in one special round. Each turn has one GUESSER from the active team, and the rest of the team are HELPERS. There are five ways to get the secret across. The teacher fixes one per round, a spinner picks one per turn, or the three-round structure below sets them:
- ANLAT (Describe / Taboo): helpers talk without saying the target or its forbidden words.
- TEK KELİME (Password, B1+): one-word clues only.
- ÇİZ (Draw): on the classroom board, or on the in-app canvas on a smartboard. No letters, numbers or talking.
- CANLANDIR (Act): by default this is Reverse Charades, where the whole team acts for one guesser (for kids, the whole class acts). Solo mime is optional. No sounds, except that animal sounds are allowed at A1 Genç.
- SOR (Heads Up): the guesser asks yes/no questions ('Is it an animal? Can I eat it?'). Helpers may only answer Yes / No / Sort of; kids answer with thumbs.

TWO LAYOUTS. The layout decides secrecy, so everything works on one projector.
A) SIRTI TAHTAYA (Hot Seat) is the default for ANLAT, TEK KELİME, SOR and Reverse Charades. The guesser sits on a chair facing the class with their back to the screen. The card is public to everyone else, so the other teams can police the forbidden words.
B) GİZLİ KART (Secret Card) is used for ÇİZ, solo mime and classic one-describer Taboo. The projector shows only 'Red team is drawing...' plus the timer. The performer gets the card in one of four ways:
  (1) The 'Heads down!' peek ritual: a 3-2-1 chime, everyone else puts their head down, the card shows for 4 s (adjustable 3-6 s), then a cover appears and a 'Heads up!' chime plays.
  (2) A presenter window on the laptop (extended display, synced by BroadcastChannel, no server). The laptop shows the card while the projector shows the cover.
  (3) The teacher's phone, paired by QR code (phase 2).
  (4) A printed deck numbered in deck order, so card #07 is position 7 and the on-screen recap stays in sync.

SETUP (teacher, about 2 min; the teacher chrome is in Turkish)
1. The group chip produces the summary line, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 60 sn · 25 dk', with a 'Değiştir' link.
2. Content comes from a built-in category or a free prompt ('7. sınıf spor ünitesi', 'job interview words'). The deck preview grid shows each card's picture, target, forbidden chips, TR chip, allowed-mode icons, a difficulty dot and a warning flag when the describability check was borderline. Tap a forbidden chip to get 3 replacements or delete it. Cards can be deleted, added, reshuffled by seed or locked. LLM idioms stay 'needs review' until the teacher ticks them.
3. Set up 2-4 teams (up to 6 in Stüdyo). Each student gets a seat number inside the team; names are never used. The rotation dots are saved in the class profile, so the next lesson starts at the next seat.
4. Show the 20-second pictogram rule card, then play one unscored practice card called 'Teacher in the hot seat!'. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo first demos the game in 20-30 s.

TURN (about 90 s including the recap)
5. The screen shows 'Blue team · Player 3 · Hot seat!' with a chair graphic. If the mode is Mix, the spinner click-clacks, landing only on modes the card's drawable/actable flags allow. There are two optional roles:
  - Designated describer ('Describer: 5'), who rotates every card so one strong speaker cannot carry the team.
  - The next team's 'Ears Captain', who raises a paper ear when a forbidden word slips.
6. A 'Turn around!' check appears. The teacher presses Space, a 3-2-1 countdown runs, then the card and the ring timer appear.
7. The teacher judges with one hand: keyboard, big smartboard buttons, or a presenter clicker (PgDn = correct, PgUp = pass, the clicker's black-screen key = freeze). Keys:
  - Space: correct. The card swooshes out, a tick flies to the score and the next card slides in.
  - P: pass.
  - X: Yasak! (target or forbidden word said, spelled, mouthed, or an object in the room pointed at).
  - K: Türkçe! (a Turkish slip).
  - U: undo. T: pause. +: add 10 s. H: show/hide frames. Y: star the best clue. F: freeze ('Sessiz!', the noise signal).
  If 'Full sentence' is on, a card counts only when the guess comes in its frame ('Is it a giraffe?', 'You're swimming!').
8. When time runs out, a soft gong plays. If steal is on, the next team gets one shout at the live card; 'Çal!' flashes in the rival colour.
9. The recap strip stamps every card GUESSED, PASSED or FORBIDDEN, with its picture and a speaker button. The whole class echoes each guessed word twice. Passed and forbidden cards go to the 'Pas kutusu' and return in the Rescue round.
10. Play moves to the next team and the next seat number. Between rounds, kids get a stirrer or a settler.

ROUND STRUCTURES
- 'Üç Perde' (Monikers / Time's Up) plays the SAME deck three times: round 1 describe freely, round 2 one word only (kids: 'Show it'), round 3 act or draw only. Every word is recycled three times, and each round gets funnier.
- 'Çark' (Activity) lets the spinner pick the mode every turn.
- 'Tek mod' keeps one mode for the whole game, e.g. a full Taboo lesson.

SPECIAL ROUNDS
- TEK KELİME / Password: the teacher counts clues with C. A card guessed after 1, 2 or 3 clues scores 3, 2 or 1.
- Deyim Resim (idiom deck): after the guess, the screen reveals the literal Turkish from the 'lit' field in idioms.js ('Fasulyeleri dökmek') with a small doodle. That is the laugh moment. Then it shows the real meaning and the example sentence. A 'Use it!' situation card is worth +1 if the team uses the idiom correctly in context.
- Cümle Sessiz Sinema (B1+): the card is a sentence from an order item ('She was reading when the phone rang'). Word slots on screen fill as the team guesses words; the teacher taps keys 1-9 to fill a slot. The full sentence scores +2, and a stealing team can finish the remaining slots for +1.
- Kapışma finale (Arena/Stüdyo): every team's guesser turns around, and all teams describe the same card at once. EVERY team that gets it within 20 s scores, not only the first, so it is not a speed race.

SCORING depends on the skin (details in the adult and teen fields):
- Oyun Parkı: stars, never minus.
- Arena: points with an accuracy streak combo and a floor at zero.
- Stüdyo: +1 per card, with optional −1 for slips and a wager final.
No mode ever gives speed points: a card is worth the same however fast it was guessed.

END. The finale depends on the skin: titles, a podium, or full scores. All skins show a 'Words we said today' wall with a speaker on every word. The 'Kaçırılanlar' list can be sent to the Material Maker as a worksheet.
catalog.playerSetup:
2-4 teams of any size (Stüdyo allows up to 6), built for Turkish classes of 30-40 students. Roles in each turn:
- One guesser from the active team, or a pair in 'Çift sandalye' for shy students.
- Helpers: the rest of the team. Optionally, one designated describer per card, chosen by seat number.
- An 'Ears Captain' from the next team, who watches for forbidden words, so waiting teams have a job.
- In kids' Reverse Charades and 'Show it' rounds, the whole class acts.
Seats are numbers, never names. The rotation tracker makes sure everyone sits once before anyone sits twice, and it carries over between lessons.
Equipment: a laptop plus a projector or MEB smartboard, one chair turned to face the class, and the board for drawing (or the in-app canvas on a smartboard). Optional: the teacher's phone, a printed numbered deck, a laminated 'guesser's crib card' on the chair (guess frames with pictures, since the guesser cannot see the screen), and mini-whiteboards for Arena.
catalog.contentShape:
DECK. The playable unit is the taboo-card item, joined to its vocab item through ref. Cümle Sessiz Sinema also uses order items.

RUNTIME CARD FIELDS
- id; target (a word, chunk, phrasal verb or idiom; a sentence only in Cümle Sessiz Sinema); form.
- forbidden[0-5].
- trChip: vocab.defTr[0], shown with a no-entry mark. It helps describers and marks the Turkish word as a slip. It can be switched off for immersion.
- frames[]: helper sentence starters, set by level.
- guessFrames[]: 'Is it a...?', 'Are you ...ing?', 'You're ...ing!'. Printed on the crib card and shown on screen in Secret Card layout.
- mode ('describe'|'draw'|'act'|'any'), combined with vocab.drawable, actable and concrete, so the spinner only lands on modes the card allows.
- catHint: e.g. 'It's food'. Helpers say it as their first clue; in Secret Card layout it is shown on screen.
- media: img (a key from the self-hosted SVG set, required for A1/A2 Genç) or emoji.
- For the recap and teacher checks: defEasy or def, example, ipa, defTr. Also alt[] (accepted variants: plural, UK/US spelling) and family[] (derivations; they may not be clues and may not appear as forbidden words).
- lit (idioms only): the literal Turkish from idioms.js, plus a situation for the 'Use it!' bonus.
- proofClue: a model description of 15 words or fewer, within the level word cap, that uses no target, forbidden or family word. It proves the card can be described and doubles as the teacher's emergency hint.
- diff (1-3), teenSafe, needsReview.
- For sentence charades, the order item supplies tokens[] (the on-screen word slots) and alt[][].

FORBIDDEN-WORD PROPOSAL
- The code proposes candidates from words.js: content words in the definition and example sentence, with stopwords, the target and its family removed, nouns first.
- The LLM adds 'the first things people would say'.
- Words proposed by both sources, or appearing in both the definition and the example, rank highest.
- The Turkish gloss is always present as the TR chip.

VALIDATOR
- The target is inside the group's word band, following the Kolay/Orta/Zor mix.
- The forbidden count matches the profile.
- A forbidden word is rejected if it equals the target, an alt or a family member, if either word contains the other (rain/rainbow), or if they share a 5-letter stem (teach/teacher).
- At most ONE superordinate (animal, food, place, job, thing, person) may be forbidden, so the card stays describable.
- Forbidden words are at or below the group level + 1.
- Describability: proofClue must pass the word cap and contain no banned token. If it fails, the generator retries once with one forbidden word fewer, then drops the card.
- Picture-dependent groups drop any card without an SVG key.
- The teenSafe filter applies. There are no appearance or weight words, and nothing that could label a classmate.
- idioms.js has only 40 items with the fields w, t, ex and lit, and no level or child flag. The game therefore keeps a small curated sidecar (kidSafe, level, litDrawable). It marks items such as 'bite the bullet' and 'cost an arm and a leg' as adult-only. LLM-made idioms stay needsReview until the teacher approves them.

DECK SIZE
- Oyun Parkı: 12-16 picture cards, reused over the three rounds.
- Arena: 24-30 cards.
- Stüdyo: 30-40 cards (20-30 when reused in Üç Perde).
- The lesson-fit sizer estimates cards ≈ teams × turns × expected cards per turn (A1 3, A2 4, B1 5, B2 6) × 1.3.
skills: grammar in guess frames (present continuous, past simple and past continuous, relative clauses)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Taboo Night' (default for A1-B2 adults).

Look and sound: an editorial quiz-night look, in cream or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, in a system sans. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Phrasal Verbs'). There is no mascot and there are no voice lines, only a neutral caption ('Round 2 · Travel'). The student screen is in English and the teacher chrome in Turkish. Sounds are woodblock and piano. A forbidden-word slip plays a classic but short 'tok-tok', and the ring timer turns amber at 10 s.

Default game: Hot Seat Taboo with 60 s turns (90 s at A1-A2), the TR chip, and a designated describer who rotates every card.

Default scoring: +1 per card. Two free passes per turn, then −1 per pass. Yasak and Türkçe cost −1 each; these are on by default at B1+ and off at A1-A2. The next team can steal the live card at time-up for +1.

Rounds: either Üç Perde with one deck, or these three:
1. Taboo.
2. TEK KELİME / Password (3/2/1 by clue count).
3. Sessiz Sinema with situations ('waiting for a delayed flight', 'arguing with a taxi driver', 'a job interview going badly') and film/TV genres. Its Reverse Charades option has the whole team act, which lowers embarrassment.

Special decks: Deyim Resim, jobs, workplace and office, travel and airport, personality adjectives, collocations, phrasal verbs. In Deyim Resim, the drawer sketches the literal picture, the reveal shows the 'lit' Turkish, and 'Use it!' earns +1. At B2 the team recalls the idiom freely and invents a situation for another team to answer.

Challenge cards (B1+, optional): 'Only questions', 'Only synonyms', 'No hands', and a register challenge ('like a news reporter', 'like a tour guide'). At B2 there is an optional +1 bonus when the describer uses a relative clause (the teacher judges).

Finale, one of:
- Bahis (wager): before its last turn, each team declares 'we will get N cards'. Hitting the target adds the wager (up to 3); missing it subtracts it.
- Kapışma: all teams play at once, and every team that guesses within 20 s scores.

End: full scores; 'Best clue' (starred with Y; the recap shows the card and the team, never a person); 'Word of the night'; and the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list with definition, example, IPA and TR, which can be exported to the Material Maker. Optional frame-use counts, if the teacher tapped them during play, feed a strategy slide ('You used "It's a kind of..." 7 times').

Adult A1-A2 keeps adult life topics (shopping, home, travel, jobs) with simple words. Pictures are optional, frames are visible, there are no minus points, and the category hint is shown.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two stripped rule sets, not one recoloured game.

OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11; the default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç): 'Magic Chair with Gogo'.

Look: warm bright colours on cream, rounded shapes and an Andika-type font. Card text is at least 6vh, and the picture fills half the card. The hot seat is a big comfy star-chair, and the teams are animal mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog...). Gogo the parrot hosts. He demos every round in 20-30 s, says the answer after a miss, and sleeps on the pause screen.

The three rules (pictograms, plus a Turkish rule card the teacher reads out):
1. Sit with your back to the board and guess.
2. Team: help in English with words, hands and faces.
3. Don't say the word, in English or in Turkish.
Coordinating in Turkish inside the team is fine; the clues must be in English.
This meets the kids' checklist:
- 3 rules, explainable in 20 s.
- No elimination: the seats rotate and everyone plays.
- Stars only, with no score below zero.
- A whole-class response in every turn.
- Soft failure imagery: on a slip, Gogo puts a feather to his beak ('Oops! Shh!') and the card flutters into his 'Later' nest.

Structure: 'Say it · Show it · Draw it', one deck of 12-16 picture cards played three times.
- Round 1, SAY IT: helpers describe with frames on emoji-style icons ('It's an animal. It's big. It can swim.'). Mime is allowed.
- Stirrer (45 s): 'Everybody show it!' Gogo shows 3 pictures and the whole class acts them.
- Round 2, SHOW IT (Reverse Charades): the WHOLE CLASS acts the card for the active team's guesser.
- Settler (60 s): a 'Whisper round' or a calm picture review.
- Round 3, DRAW IT: a pair from the active team gets the card through the peek ritual (Gogo covers his eyes), draws it, and the team guesses. After each guess, everyone air-draws the word for 5 s.
- Finale, 'Gogo's Rescue': the teacher sits in the magic chair, and the whole class helps with the nest cards. Every rescued card gives Everyone +1 star.

Pacing and timer: turns are 'Süresiz' with 3 cards each. An optional calm 90 s sand timer is never red and ends with a marimba chime. Passes are unlimited and free. At A2 Genç, SOR mode is added: the guesser asks 'Is it an animal? Can it fly?' and the class answers with thumbs up or down. Mini Taboo (1 forbidden word) is optional.

Scoring: 1 star per card, and the golden card is worth 2. A shared Class Jar fills with every card any team gets; at 20 it unlocks the class album sticker. A team that ends a turn with 0 cards gets an effort star for the album.

Audio: TTS never plays on reveal, because the guesser would hear it. In the recap, read-aloud runs at 0.8x and the class echoes each word twice.

Ending: every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Actors, Brave Guessers, Great Listeners), the class album gets a sticker, and a 'Words we said today' wall closes the game.
