Content: YLE and MEB topics (animals, food, toys, sports, school things, daily routines, clothes, weather, feelings, jobs). The idiom deck for these groups is 'Draw the compound word': sunflower, butterfly, rainbow, toothbrush, snowman, football.

ARENA (ages 12-14; the default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç class in MEB grades 6-8): 'Codeword Challenge'.

Look: dark navy with neon accents in the team colours, a condensed display font, and emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond). In 10 s, each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto, and the motto stays on the scoreboard. The card appears as a glowing 'forehead card', a nod to Heads Up, above a silhouette of the chair. There is no mascot and no 'superstar' praise. A commentator strip shows at most one caption per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CLEAN SHEET', 'CLUTCH!').

A Match has 3 sets:
1. Describe, with Mini Taboo: 2 forbidden words at B1 Genç, 3 at B2 Genç.
2. The spinner picks Describe, Act, Draw or Ask for each turn.
3. A replay of the same deck, one word or act only.
The ring timer runs 60 s in the team colour (75 s with A-level cards), with 2 free passes per turn. The spinner seat number picks the guesser, and mini-whiteboards are used for steals.

Challenge cards (optional, every other turn; ×1.5 for that turn's cards): No hands, Whisper only, Only questions, One word only, Robot voice.

Scoring: 100 per card. The streak multiplier is ×1.5 at 3 in a row and ×2 at 5; it counts accuracy only, and a pass or slip breaks it. A slip kills the card and resets the streak, with no minus. At time-up the next team may steal the live card (+100), and the active team loses nothing. If the teacher opts into Yellow, steals are open on every dead card. Scores never drop below zero, nobody is named, and no team is shown in public last place.

Rules and sound: an English rule card with a Turkish toggle, synth blips, and an optional quiet loop.

End: a podium plus stat awards (Longest streak, Clean sheet, Most English, Comeback, Best clue), and never a 'last place'.

Content: teenSafe and concrete but richer: sports, tech, inventions, space, nature, school life, travel, film and game genres, with no brands. Deyim Resim uses only the kid-safe idioms: a piece of cake, break the ice, under the weather, hit the books, once in a blue moon, spill the beans, raining cats and dogs. An A1 class in grade 7 gets Arena visuals with A1 picture cards, 0 forbidden words and frames.
catalog.levelTuning:
There are two axes. The level sets the words, forbidden list, frames and guess grammar. The audience mode sets the skin and rules, so a 13-year-old A1 class plays Arena with A1 cards.

A1
- Words: concrete nouns and action verbs (Oxford A1 band), with a picture on every card.
- Forbidden: 0 (only the word itself and the TR chip).
- Helpers: may mime and use words plus frames: 'It's a/an... It's big/small/(colour). It can... You eat/wear/play it.'
- Guesses: one word is accepted.
- Modes: CANLANDIR and ÇİZ lead, ANLAT is used with frames, SOR is off.
- Turn: kids play 3 untimed cards; Arena 75 s; adults 90 s, with the category hint shown and no minus.

A2
- Words: everyday nouns, verbs, adjectives, places and simple chunks ('get up', 'go shopping').
- Forbidden: 2 for adults; at A2 Genç, 1 optional word ('Mini Taboo', off by default).
- Frames: 'It's a kind of... You use it to... You can find it in... It has got...'. Visible for kids; hidden for adults, with H to show them.
- In CANLANDIR the present continuous guess frame is required: 'You're swimming!' / 'Are you cooking?'.
- SOR (yes/no questions) is unlocked.
- Turn: 75-90 s.

B1
- Words: jobs, feelings, everyday objects, collocations ('make a mistake'), common phrasal verbs and transparent idioms.
- Forbidden: 3 for adults (4 on Zor); 2 at B1 Genç.
- Frames: relative clauses ('It's a person who... something that... a place where...') and 'It's the opposite of...'.
- Unlocked: TEK KELİME / Password, and Cümle Sessiz Sinema with past simple and past continuous.
- Steal is on.
- Turn: 60 s.

B2
- Words for adults: abstract nouns (deadline, freedom), idioms (Deyim Resim, with free recall and the 'Use it!' bonus), collocations, phrasal verbs, and work and society topics.
- Words for B2 Genç: richer but still concrete, never abstract debate.
- Forbidden: 5 for adults; 3 at B2 Genç (4 on Zor).
- No frames by default, and no gestures in ANLAT.
- Register challenge cards and the Üç Perde structure.
- Turn: 60 s, with a 45 s option.
- The TR chip is off by default for adults (immersion).

MIXED ABILITY. Inside each group, the Kolay/Orta/Zor dial shifts the word-band mix (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words), moves the forbidden count by ±1 and changes frame visibility. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole profile by one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-40. Kids: about 20 (3 rounds of 4-6 min, plus a 45 s stirrer, a 60 s settler and a 2 min Rescue). Arena: 15-30. Stüdyo: 15-40, sized by the lesson-fit timer as rounds × teams × (turn + 30 s recap).
catalog.teacherControls:
Deck and content
- Deck preview and editing: replace or delete forbidden chips, delete, add, reshuffle by seed, lock, and approve 'needs review' idioms.
- Built-in category or free prompt.
- Kolay/Orta/Zor, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- Mode per round, Mix spinner, or Üç Perde.
- Layout: Hot Seat or Secret Card.
- Secret-card delivery: peek duration, presenter window, printed numbered deck (print CSS, 8 cards per A4), or teacher phone (phase 2).

Timing and turns
- Turn timer length, or 'Süresiz' with N cards per turn; +10 s; pause (T); end turn now.
- Pass limit and pass cost.

Rules and scoring
- Forbidden count (0-5) and the TR chip on/off.
- Frames on/off (H), picture on/off, category hint on/off.
- 'Full sentence' toggle.
- Yasak and Türkçe penalties on/off.
- Steal on/off; designated describer on/off.
- Pair chair ('Çift sandalye').
- Challenge cards on/off.
- Harshness (Green/Yellow) and Comeback dials. Under Comeback Light, the trailing team picks the next mode or category and gets +1 on its first correct card.

During play
- Undo (U); skip a card without penalty ('Kart imkânsız'); move a card to the Rescue pile; freeze (F).
- 'Settle' button: a 30 s calm picture review after acting rounds.
- Keyboard map: Space, P, X, K, U, T, +, H, Y, C, 1-9, F, M, V; presenter clickers are supported.

Setup and display
- Turn order and seat rotation (persisted); jump to a printed card number.
- Sound, music and reduced motion.
- The class profile is saved (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').
catalog.delightDetails:
Rituals and pacing
- A 'Turn around!' chair animation starts every turn.
- The card swooshes out on a correct answer and a tick flies to the team score.
- The ring timer uses the team colour. It turns amber at 10 s for adults and never turns red for kids. The last 5 s tick softly, and the tick can be muted.
- The mode spinner click-clacks between pictograms.
- In the 'Heads down!' peek, Gogo covers his eyes for kids; Arena shows an 'EYES CLOSED' glitch screen instead.

Sounds
- Slips sound kind rather than harsh: a kazoo 'bzzt' for Arena and a woodblock for adults. For kids, Gogo's feather 'Shh' tucks the card into his nest.

Recap and reveals
- The recap stamps each card GUESSED, PASSED or FORBIDDEN, with its picture and a speaker button, and the class echoes each word.
- The Deyim Resim reveal shows the literal Turkish in a playful font with a tiny doodle (spilled beans for 'Fasulyeleri dökmek') before the real meaning.
- Frames light up when the teacher marks them used, which feeds the adults' strategy slide.
- 'Teacher in the hot seat' opens the game and hosts the Rescue.

Keepsakes
- The class Jar and album stickers.
- An 'Idiom of the day' carried to the next lesson's opening screen.
- A 'Class art gallery' of canvas drawings (kept on the device only).

Arena extras
- The forehead-card hologram, the team motto on the scoreboard, and the commentator strip.

Physical extras
- A printable, numbered deck that stays in sync with the app, and a laminated crib card on the chair.
- Seat-rotation dots, so every student can see their turn coming.
catalog.risks:
Each risk below is followed by its mitigation.
- The guesser peeks at the screen: the chair faces the class and 'no peeking' is a rule. Draw and mime secrecy come from the peek ritual, presenter window, printed deck or phone.
- LLM forbidden lists make a card impossible or give the answer away: the validator, the describability proofClue, the teacher preview, and a penalty-free 'Kart imkânsız' skip.
- Shy students freeze: only the guesser is picked; the pair chair, Reverse Charades and pair drawing are available; nobody performs solo in Oyun Parkı.
- Strong speakers dominate: the designated describer rotates by seat number, and the Ears Captain gives waiting teams a job.
- Noise in classes of 30-40: the freeze key, Whisper-round settlers, and only the chair (or the team) guessing aloud.
- Turkish creeps into the clues: the TR chip and the Türkçe key. Kids may still coordinate in Turkish.
- Unfair buzzing: the teacher judges and can undo.
- TTS gives the word away: no audio on reveal, only in the recap.
- Drawing skill decides points (roadmap G14): the guess is scored, not the art; cards are simple and drawable; drawers work in pairs.
- Teasing: no appearance or weight words, no describing classmates, no pointing at people.
- The idiom bank is tiny (40 items, with no level or child flag) and some idioms are violent: the curated sidecar, and LLM idioms stay 'needs review' until approved.
- Speed creep against the no-speed-points rule (roadmap G08): Kapışma scores every team that guesses in time, and streaks count accuracy only.
- The phone's realtime link adds cost: it is phase 2, and everything works without it.
- The printed deck drifts out of order: numbered cards and a jump-to-number field.
- Waiting teams sit idle: the Ears Captain, the whole-class echo, and Reverse Charades.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (G08: describing without forbidden words, a pass right, no speed points, cards made impossible by the forbidden list; G14: do not score artistic skill)
C:/lg/src/data/idioms.js (40 idioms with the fields w, t, ex, lit; no level or kid-safe flag)
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Absorb any separate Taboo, Hot Seat, Pictionary, Charades or Heads Up candidates into this one. Keep it separate from the Baamboozle, Jeopardy and quiz games, because its core loop is live speaking rather than answering.

issues: SCOPE EXPLOSION FOR THE TEACHER. There are 5 modes, 2 layouts, 4 ways to deliver the secret card, 3 round structures, 4 special rounds, a wager, challenge cards, 15+ hotkeys, and Green/Yellow and Comeback dials. The pedagogy is right, but a teacher standing at the board with 28 kids can hold about 4 controls in their head, not 15. The 'about 2 min' setup is realistic only when the teacher accepts every default.

THE KEYBOARD MAP ASSUMES A KEYBOARD. MEB smartboards usually run touch-only, with no keyboard at the board. The teacher is also standing next to the guesser's chair, so the Space/P/X/K/U/T/+/H/Y/C/1-9/F/M/V shortcuts are useless there. The on-screen buttons must carry the whole game.

SOMEONE BLURTS THE ANSWER. In Hot Seat the card is public to the whole room. With 28 kids, someone from ANOTHER team will shout the word within 10 s, whether by accident or as sabotage, and the guesser hears it. There is no rule or button for an opponent blurt, so the teacher has to rule on the spot every turn.

THE TEACHER CANNOT JUDGE WHAT THEY CANNOT HEAR. In ANLAT with 6-7 helpers talking at once, nobody can hear a forbidden word or a Turkish slip. The designated describer is only optional for kids and Arena, so the X/K judging collapses in a big class. The Ears Captain raising a paper ear then turns into a fairness argument: 'he said it!' / 'no I didn't!'.

WHOLE-CLASS REVERSE CHARADES AND THE 'EVERYBODY SHOW IT' STIRRER. 28 standing kids flailing is fun, but getting them back to their seats costs 1-2 min each time. It also makes the guesser's job of reading the room chaotic. One settler is not enough after two acting phases.

KAPIŞMA IN ONE ROOM. When 4 teams describe the same card at once, every guesser hears the other teams' clues. The teacher cannot verify which of 4 guessers got it within 20 s. With kids this is pure noise, and with 10 adults it is still ambiguous.

UNTIMED KIDS' TURNS ('Süresiz', 3 cards). A struggling guesser can hold the class for 3+ minutes while the other 21 kids wait. That breaks both pacing and the 'stop at any moment' promise. The fix only exists as the 'optional' sand timer.

ROTATION FAIRNESS IS OVERSTATED. With 4 teams, one round of 12 cards at 3 per turn gives only 4 guessers. A 20-minute Üç Perde game seats about 12 of 28 kids. The persistent seat-number rotation also breaks when teams are reshuffled, when students are absent, or when a teacher runs two classes on one laptop without switching profiles.
SEAT NUMBERS: 10-year-olds forget their number between lessons. Moving the chair and the student to the front adds 15-25 s of dead time per turn, which the ~90 s turn estimate leaves out.

THE PEEK RITUAL WITH KIDS. 'Everyone else heads down' for 4 s is unenforceable with 10-12 year-olds, and it is also unnecessary: only the ACTIVE team needs to be blind, because the other teams cannot score. The presenter window assumes a laptop with an extended display. Public-school smartboard PCs don't have one, so for kids only the peek ritual really works.

DRAWING ON A SMARTBOARD BLOCKS THE SCREEN. When the drawing pair uses the in-app canvas, the timer and team status are hidden behind their bodies. The drawers can also see the cover, which leaves nowhere to show them the card again. Using the classroom whiteboard next to the smartboard works better, but the design treats the two as equivalent.

RUNAWAY LEADER IN ARENA. The ×1.5/×2 streak multiplier compounds the strongest team's advantage, and Comeback Light is only an optional dial. After two sets a trailing team can be 600+ behind with no realistic path back. For 12-14 year-olds that means disengagement.

STÜDYO PENALTIES (−1 per pass after 2, −1 for Yasak, −1 for Türkçe) plus the wager final can put an adult team below zero or wipe out a lead on the last turn. That is fine for competitive groups, but it needs a clear on-screen explanation or it causes disputes.

A RECAP AFTER EVERY TURN (stamps, speaker buttons, choral echo twice) adds 30-45 s per turn. Over 16-20 turns that is 10+ minutes of low-energy time in a 25-minute slot. Adults especially will find the per-turn echo patronising.

ADULT A1-A2 GROUPS WITH NO PICTURES AND 90 s TURNS: a weak adult describer fills 90 s of silence, which is painful. The design removes pictures for adults exactly where low-level adults need them most.

BUILD SIZE: this is really XL, not L. The describability validator, forbidden-word proposer, SVG-key requirement, idiom sidecar, BroadcastChannel presenter, print CSS, canvas gallery, three skins and a spinner is too much for one release. The risk is shipping a half-finished version of everything.
fixes: SHIP AN MVP CORE. Hot Seat ANLAT, Reverse Charades, and ÇİZ on the classroom whiteboard with an active-team-only peek. Ship Üç Perde plus Tek mod, and all three skins. Defer TEK KELİME/Password, Cümle Sessiz Sinema, Kapışma, the wager, challenge cards, the presenter window, the phone link, frame-use counting and the canvas gallery to v2.

TOUCH-FIRST JUDGING BAR. Four huge buttons pinned bottom-right, within reach of a standing teacher: ✓ Doğru, → Pas, ✋ Yasak/Türkçe (one button; a long-press picks Türkçe), ↶ Geri al. Everything else (pause, +10 s, frames, freeze) goes into one ⋯ menu. Keep hotkeys and clicker support as extras.

BLURT RULE, SHOWN ON THE RULE CARD. If ANOTHER team says the answer, the active team gets the card, so sabotage backfires. Add an 'Kart yandı' button that swaps in a fresh card at no cost. In Arena and Stüdyo, waiting teams may answer ONLY on mini-whiteboards during a steal.

MAKE THE DESIGNATED DESCRIBER THE DEFAULT in every skin when a team has 5 or more students (kids: 2 describers, the rest mime only). Then the teacher only listens to 1-2 voices and X/K becomes judgeable. Drop the Ears Captain as a judge: they may raise the ear, but only the teacher's tap counts.

KIDS' TURNS: DEFAULT TO A SOFT 90 s TIMER, never red, or '3 cards OR 90 s, whichever comes first'. Keep 'Süresiz' as an opt-in. Show a big 'Bitir → Final' button that jumps straight to Gogo's Rescue and the Class Jar, so the bell never catches the game mid-round.

REPLACE SEAT NUMBERS WITH AN ON-SCREEN ROTATION WHEEL. Show each team's rotation as avatar dots (mascot plus number) and highlight 'next up' one turn early, so the student walks to the chair during the recap. Add 'Bugün yok' (absent) toggles and a 'Takımları yeniden kur' action that keeps per-student sit counts.

RAISE THROUGHPUT FOR BIG CLASSES. Offer a 'Çift sandalye' default for kids (2 guessers, so 2x the students seated) and 2 cards per turn in round 3. That seats roughly 20-24 of 28 kids per game instead of about 12.

BRACKET EVERY ACTING PHASE WITH A MANDATORY SETTLE. Whole-class acting runs 20 s at most per card, and seats are required again when the chime plays. Auto-insert the 30 s calm picture review after SHOW IT. Let the teacher limit whole-class acting to 'standing at your desk'.

KAPIŞMA: DROP IT FOR OYUN PARKI. In Arena and Stüdyo, run it as 'all guessers write their answer on mini-whiteboards at 20 s', with one shared describer (the teacher or a neutral student). That removes cross-talk and makes judging trivial.

ARENA: CAP THE STREAK MULTIPLIER AT ×1.5, and make Comeback Light the default (the trailing team picks the category and gets +1 on its first card). Show the gap only as the podium at the end, not as a live bar that drags.
STÜDYO: SHOW A ONE-LINE SCORING LEGEND ON SCREEN. Default the wager final to 'win up to +3, lose at most −1', so the last turn cannot wipe out a lead.
MOVE THE FULL RECAP TO THE END OF EACH ROUND. Per turn, show only a 3-second stamp strip. For adults, make the choral echo opt-in; for kids, keep one echo per word, not two.
ADULT A1-A2: pictures ON by default (the adult skin can use photo-style icons), frames visible, 75 s turns, and 'Kart imkânsız' one tap away.

PEEK: blind only the active team ('Kırmızı takım, başlar aşağı!'), and give Gogo a fair 'I saw someone peek, new card' button. Recommend the classroom whiteboard over the in-app canvas for ÇİZ on smartboards, and keep the timer visible in a corner that the drawers do not block.
LESSON-FIT SIZER: include about 20 s of chair-change time per turn and the per-round recap in the estimate, and warn when the plan exceeds the time the teacher chose.

issues: Too much for one game. It has five modes, two layouts, four ways to deliver the secret card, three round structures, four special rounds and about 16 hotkeys. A teacher running A1 kids or A2 adults cannot hold all of that. The level dials are good, but they are buried under feature surface, and a build size of L is optimistic.

Low-level groups produce very little language. At A1, and in the Show it/Draw it rounds, helpers mime or draw and the guesser says one word. A 20-minute Oyun Parkı session can therefore contain only about 15 English words spoken by a few children. The echo and air-draw steps are recognition drills, not production. For A1 kids the 'describe' in Say it mostly happens in Turkish or in gesture.

The claim that 'nobody ever has to perform alone' is false in Hot Seat. The guesser sits alone facing 35 classmates and guesses aloud. The pair chair is optional, but in Oyun Parkı and for shy adult A1 learners it should be the default.

A1/A2 Genç requires an SVG key on every card, and a card without one is dropped. A free-text LLM prompt ('7. sınıf spor ünitesi', or 'farm tools') will often produce targets the self-hosted SVG set does not cover, so the deck can shrink below 12 with no warning. The built-in categories only work if the SVG set covers the YLE/MEB topic lists.

In the Draw it round, 'Heads down!' for 9-year-olds in a class of 35 is unreliable: children peek, and the 4-second flash is hard to manage. Round 3 therefore depends on a secrecy mechanism that fails exactly with the youngest groups.

The kids' checklist is met on paper (3 rules) but not in practice. Say it, Show it and Draw it each change who acts and how, and the stirrer, the settler and Gogo's Rescue add more procedures on top. For 9-year-olds, each round is effectively a new rule set.
The Password round needs a large vocabulary for one-word clues. It is weak at B1 Genç, where it tends to produce Turkish or give up, and it gated only by level, not by audience.
Cümle Sessiz Sinema has the teacher filling word slots with keys 1-9 while also judging and timing. That is too much for one teacher, and acting out past continuous is abstract for 12-year-olds.

The idiom deck is too small: idioms.js has 40 items, about 7 of them are kid-safe, and only some are drawable. That is not enough for a Deyim Resim round of 24-30 cards unless the teacher reviews many LLM-made idioms. At B2, 'recall the idiom freely' assumes knowledge the learners may not have.

In the automatic forbidden-word proposal, definitions in words.js use generic words ('person', 'something', 'used'). They can pass the stopword filter or crowd out the natural taboo words. The superordinate cap helps, but a B1 card with 3 forbidden words may still block the only simple route to the answer.

In Hot Seat, the guesser cannot see the frames on screen. The guessing grammar the level design relies on (present continuous, 'Is it a...?') therefore depends on a laminated card that many teachers will never print.
The Stüdyo rules are right for adults, but A1 adults playing Reverse Charades with a whole team acting risk feeling childish unless the situations are adult ones.
fixes: Cut version 1 down to a core: Hot Seat (Describe and SOR) plus Reverse Charades, with Üç Perde as the only round structure, and Space/P/X/U/T as the only keys. Move Password, Cümle Sessiz Sinema, Deyim Resim, the presenter window, the phone link and the Kapışma finale to version 2.

Build production into every low-level turn. In Say it, helpers must say at least one frame sentence ('It's an animal') before any mime. The guesser must answer in a frame ('Is it a lion?'), and the frame is shown as a big picture strip on the side wall or printed on the chair. After each correct guess, the whole class makes one sentence with the word, prompted by a picture and a frame.
Make Çift sandalye (two guessers) the default in Oyun Parkı and at adult A1-A2, and let a guesser 'phone a friend' from their own team once per turn.

For the youngest groups, replace the Heads-down peek with the teacher whispering the word, or with the printed numbered card handed to the drawing pair. Keep the peek ritual for Arena and Stüdyo only.

Add an SVG coverage check to LLM decks for picture-dependent groups. The LLM chooses targets only from the SVG key list, or a card falls back to a curated emoji. The preview warns when fewer than 12 cards remain, and topics with poor coverage are marked in the category picker.

Present the Oyun Parkı rounds as one rule ('same cards, new way') with a single pictogram per round, and remove either the stirrer or the settler so that there are at most 2 procedure changes in 20 minutes.
Allow Password only at B1+ Stüdyo and at B2 Genç, and give each card 3 suggested one-word clues as a teacher hint.
Remove slot-filling from Cümle Sessiz Sinema. The teacher taps Correct once, and the team then says the whole sentence from an on-screen jumble for +1. It is Stüdyo B1+ only.
Make the idiom sidecar a curated list of at least 30 items per audience, with a level, kidSafe and litDrawable flag on each. Deyim Resim runs as a 6-8 card special round, not a full deck.
Rank forbidden words from the LLM's 'first things people say' list and use words.js only to validate them. Block generic definition words through a stoplist ('person', 'thing', 'used', 'something').

Show a guess-frame strip on the side of the projected screen that the guesser can see (a small panel angled away from the card), or print a default A3 poster through print CSS. Do not rely on the laminated card being optional.
Give adult A1-A2 Reverse Charades adult situation cards (at the bank, in a meeting) and never use the children's picture set, even when Pictures is on.

reviews.mergeWith: Absorb any separate Taboo, Hot Seat, Pictionary, Charades or Heads Up candidates into this one. Keep it separate from the Baamboozle, Jeopardy and quiz games, because its core loop is live speaking rather than answering.
issues: Scope is XL, not L. The design lists 5 modes, 2 layouts, 4 secret-card delivery methods, 3 round structures, 4 special rounds (Password, Deyim Resim, Cümle Sessiz Sinema, Kapışma), challenge cards, 3 skins that each have their own rule set, a wager final, an in-app canvas, a presenter window, a print deck, phone pairing, seat rotation that carries across lessons, a class album, a jar and a gallery. Built as specified, it will ship late, or it will ship wide and shallow.

The app's core value is thin. The real game happens in the room, and the software is a deck, a timer and a score. Without heavy ritual polish it feels like a timer app with cards. Polish has to go into the turn ritual, card motion, the recap and the reveal, not into feature count.

Steal is broken in the Hot Seat layout. The card is shown publicly to every team except the active guesser, so the next team already knows the answer when time runs out. The same leak hits Password clue counting and the 'Çal!' shout.

Kapışma (all teams describe the same card at once) can't be judged fairly by one teacher. In a room of 30-40 students, four teams shouting clues at four guessers is noise, and the teacher can't hear forbidden-word slips.

The keyboard map is overloaded (Space, P, X, K, U, T, +, H, Y, C, 1-9, F, M, V). Most MEB smartboard teachers use touch, not a keyboard, and one-handed judging needs no more than 3-4 big targets. Recording frame use and starring the best clue while also judging is unrealistic.

The requirement for 'an SVG picture on every card' at A1/A2 Genç is the biggest asset cost and risk. Covering YLE and MEB topics takes roughly 300-600 consistent icons, while LLM free-prompt decks can name anything. So picture-dependent groups either lose most cards generated from free prompts or show nothing.
Emoji fallback varies by OS. The Pardus smartboard, Windows and iOS render emoji differently or not at all, and some glyphs show as tofu boxes.

The automatic describability check is weaker than it looks. The proofClue checks only the words the LLM itself used, with no lemmatization, and words.js has no inflection table, so 'teaches' or 'rained' slip past a banned-token check. It can't detect a clue that is technically legal but useless, or a card that is too hard in practice.

The deck of 40 idioms (idioms.js) can't support a whole Deyim Resim mode. After the kid-safe filter the teen set is about 7 idioms, and LLM-made idioms need manual review, which adds friction in class.

TTS in the recap and on the word wall relies on speechSynthesis. English voices are often missing or robotic on Pardus/Linux smartboards and on offline machines, and the whole-class echo depends on audio.

The presenter window over BroadcastChannel works only with an extended display in the same browser profile. Many classrooms mirror the laptop to the smartboard or run the browser on the board itself, so the peek ritual is the real default and it should be the best-polished method.

Kids' ANLAT at A1 (describe in English with no forbidden words) is really hard for 9-year-olds and quickly drifts into Turkish plus pointing. Reverse Charades and drawing carry the Oyun Parkı version, and the describing round will feel weak.
Cümle Sessiz Sinema with keys 1-9 filling word slots adds another input model and needs order-item alt handling. It is high cost for a niche round.
Seat rotation and class profiles are stored in localStorage on one device. They are lost if the teacher switches between the laptop and the board PC, or if browser data is cleared.
The Deyim Resim doodles (the drawing of the literal Turkish meaning) need bespoke art for every idiom, which is another asset pipeline.

The design overlaps its own family. Password, Heads Up and Pictionary could each be pitched as separate games. Counting them separately toward the '10 games' target would be padding, so they should stay modes of one game.
fixes: Split the build into phases. MVP (M): Hot Seat layout; modes ANLAT, CANLANDIR (Reverse Charades) and ÇİZ on the paper board; Üç Perde plus Tek mod; the peek ritual; the recap with GUESSED, PASSED and FORBIDDEN stamps; the 'Words we said today' wall; 3 skins with their rule dials; deck preview and editing; print deck. Phase 2: Password, SOR, the Çark spinner, challenge cards, the in-app canvas, the presenter window, the Arena and Stüdyo finales. Phase 3: Deyim Resim, Cümle Sessiz Sinema, phone pairing, the album and gallery.

Fix steal. Allow it only in the Secret Card layout. In Hot Seat, replace it with 'Rival guesser': the next team's guesser also sits with their back to the screen during the last 10 s, and only that seated student may answer the steal. Otherwise, turn steal off by default in Hot Seat.

Replace Kapışma with 'Sırayla Kapışma': the same card goes to each team in turn with a 20 s mini-timer, the card is hidden between teams, and every team that succeeds scores. Or drop it and use the Bahis wager final only.

Collapse judging to 3 big touch buttons (Doğru, Pas, Yasak) plus a small 'more' tray (Türkçe, undo, pause, +10 s). Map the clicker to correct, pass and freeze. Move frame counting and best-clue starring to the recap screen, after the timer stops.

Replace the SVG-per-card requirement with a tiered media policy: a curated self-hosted icon set (about 200 icons, e.g. an open-licence set restyled to one stroke weight) for the built-in kid decks, self-hosted Twemoji or OpenMoji SVGs as the universal fallback, and the target word in big type when neither exists. Constrain the kid-deck LLM generator to pick targets from the icon-key list.

Harden the validator: lemmatize with a small suffix stripper (s/es/ed/ing/er/est/ly, y to ies) before the banned-token and 5-letter-stem checks; reject proofClues that are only a category word; attach a borderline flag automatically; generate 1.3x the needed cards so dropped cards still leave a full deck; keep 'Kart imkânsız' one tap away.

Validate LLM output with a JSON schema: fixed field lengths, forbidden count from the profile, targets deduplicated against the deck, a teenSafe blocklist regex, then words.js band lookup. Fill ipa, defTr and example from words.js rather than trusting the LLM.
Make Deyim Resim a built-in curated deck (the 40 idioms, with sidecar level/kidSafe and hand-made doodles for the 15-20 most drawable), not a free-prompt mode. For kids, use the compound-word deck.

Ship pre-generated audio for built-in decks (short OGG/MP3 files, lazy-loaded per deck) and use speechSynthesis only for LLM decks, with a visible 'no voice' fallback that lets the teacher say the word.

For Oyun Parkı, drop the pure-ANLAT round in favour of 'Say + Show': frames plus gestures allowed, with the picture card and frame strip on screen for helpers. Keep 'Say it' as round 1 only from A2 Genç up.
Offer a class-profile export/import as a short code or QR, and store the profile under the teacher's Supabase account when logged in.
Make the peek ritual the flagship polish: full-screen cover animation, the 3-2-1 chime, an adjustable peek time, and a big 'Tekrar göster' (show again) button that requires another heads-down.

Spend the polish budget on a few moments: the turn-around chair animation, the card swoosh with a tick that flies to the score, a ring timer in the team colour, stamp animations in the recap, and a satisfying word-wall build. Target a JS bundle under 60 KB, CSS/SVG animations only, and prefers-reduced-motion support.
Treat Password, Heads Up, Pictionary and Charades as modes of this one game and do not count them toward the 10-game target.

catalog.rankReason: The main speaking game and the teacher's Taboo (adult 8.7). Live circumlocution gives the most real spoken output in the set. MVP: Hot Seat ANLAT, Reverse Charades and ÇİZ on the classroom whiteboard, with Üç Perde plus Tek mod. It needs a four-button touch judging bar (Doğru, Pas, Yasak/Türkçe, Geri al). At low levels a frame sentence is required before any mime and the guess must be a frame; a 'rival guesser' replaces steal. Password, Deyim Resim, Cümle Sessiz Sinema and Kapışma move to v2. The screen part is thin, so the polish goes into the peek ritual and the recap stamps.

catalog.name: Kelime Tombala (Listening Bingo)
catalog.familiarAs: Bingo / Turkish Tombala ('Çinko!')
catalog.oneLiner: The New Year tombala game, played with English. Every student or pair gets a unique numbered tombala card, on paper or on a phone. The screen shakes the tombala bag, pulls out a numbered wooden piece (pul) and calls a clue by ear. Depending on the group, the clue is the word itself, a picture, a Turkish gloss, a description, a definition, a sentence with a beep in the gap, or a synonym. 'ÇİNKO!' and 'TOMBALA!' are checked in seconds from the card number, and the winner reads the row aloud. It is a calm, whole-class listening settler for classes of up to 40 and more, and it ends with a word list students can take home.
catalog.howItPlays:
0) SETUP (teacher, about 60 s). The teacher picks the group chip; the summary line reads e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 15 dk'. Next come three choices:
- Content: a built-in category, a free-text prompt (it can be in Turkish), an existing pack, or Sayı Tombala (numbers made by code).
- Kart türü: Kelime, Resim, Sayı, Kollokasyon, Dilbilgisi, Ses or Tanışma.
- Class size.
The engine then sizes the pool and the card and runs a quick simulation (500 random games) to show an estimate before anything is printed, e.g. 'İlk çinko ≈ 6. çekiliş · Tombala ≈ 18. çekiliş · ≈ 10 dk'.

CARD FORMAT. The default is the real Turkish tombala card: 3 rows, and only full ROWS count, like the real game. Size depends on the audience:
- Oyun Parkı: 3×3 pictures (9 cells).
- Arena: 3×4 (12 cells).
- Stüdyo: 3×5 (15 cells), the classic tombala card, with decorative blank cells between the words.
- Optional 'Klasik Bingo' layout: a 4×4 or 5×5 grid with a free centre, where lines count in any direction (for teachers used to Baamboozle or Flippity).
The pool is at least 1.6× the card's cells: Park 12-15 items, Arena 18-22, Stüdyo 24-30, classic 5×5 at least 36.

CARD DELIVERY. 'Kartları yazdır' makes one A4 PDF: 4 cards per page, cut marks, about 10% spare cards, and a last page 'Çağırıcı listesi' (the caller list). 'Telefon kartları' shows a QR code. Cards come from a seeded game code (e.g. 'TMB-4Q7'), so the projector can rebuild any card from its number, and no student data is stored.

1) START. Cards go out face down, with counters or pencils. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo plays a 30 s practice round (3 calls, no score). In Arena and Stüdyo, the teacher reads a 20 s rule card.

2) ONE DRAW (çekiliş), repeated:
a) The bag shakes for 1 s with a wooden clack, and a pul pops out with the draw number ('#7').
b) The call is heard first. The clue type depends on the level (see levelTuning). Kids hear it twice at 0.8x with a 2 s gap. The text or picture appears after the options delay (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s), or never in a 'Sadece dinle' round.
c) Mark window: kids 10 s, Arena 8 s, adults 6 s. A calm ring runs, never red, with a soft tick. 'Tekrar' (R) replays the call.
d) Reveal. The answer, with its picture, is stamped onto the Çağrı panosu (a master board like the host board in real tombala) and onto the history strip. Then comes the whole-class moment:
- Oyun Parkı: everyone echoes the word twice after Gogo and gives a thumbs up if they had it.
- Arena: thumbs up, with an optional echo on the beat.
- Stüdyo: an echo only when the teacher asks for it.
e) The teacher presses Space for the next draw. Draws are manual by default; auto mode draws every 30 s (Park) or 15-20 s (Arena, Stüdyo).
In the hard setting 'Cevaplar sonda', the answers stay hidden until the recap.

3) CLAIMS follow the real prize ladder: BİRİNCİ ÇİNKO (one full row), İKİNCİ ÇİNKO (two rows), TOMBALA (the full card).
- The student holds up the card and shouts the word.
- The teacher presses Ç and types the card number on a big number pad.
- The card appears with the called cells stamped, each showing its draw number, and any complete rows are detected automatically.
- The claimant reads the row aloud (the pronunciation moment). At B levels they also 'prove one': they say the clue back, or use one of the words in a sentence.
- 'Doğru' brings the banner 'BİRİNCİ ÇİNKO! · Kart 07'. 'Henüz değil' brings a gentle 'Not yet, keep listening!' and play goes on. There is no penalty in Nazik mode. In Stüdyo, a false claim can optionally mean the claimant reads the next clue aloud.
- If two cards complete on the same draw, '+ Kart ekle' checks both and they share the prize ('Ortak çinko').
- A row that was completed earlier but claimed late still counts. In Stüdyo, the option 'Uyuyan çinko' makes a claim valid only before the next pul.

4) NOBODY IS OUT. After each prize the game goes on to the next one. After TOMBALA comes 'Bir kaldı!': everyone who was one cell short stands up for applause. 'İkinci tombala' lets the game run on.

5) RECAP (60-90 s):
- A matching list of every clue and its answer.
- 'Çıkmayanlar': the items that were never called, drilled chorally in 20 s.
- Items the teacher flagged 'Zorlandılar' (Z key).
- A one-click take-home word list (EN, TR, and a picture or IPA), and a 'Bu listeyle başka oyun' handoff to the other games (e.g. Hangman).
Replay options: 'Yeni kartlar, aynı içerik', or 'Aynı kartlar, zor tur' (one less support step).

6) SCORE. The game has no score by default, because everyone plays individually. The optional 'Sıra takımları' mode pools each row of desks into a team jar: 1, 2 and 3 stars (kids) or points for the first çinko, second çinko and tombala. It never goes negative.
catalog.playerSetup:
The whole class plays at once, individually or in pairs sharing a card; it works with 40 or more students. Print about 10% spare cards. No teams are needed.
- Optional 'Sıra takımları': 2-4 teams made from rows of desks or table clusters. Each team pools its çinkos into a team jar. In Arena, teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto in 10 s.
- The class needs one projector, and the teacher runs it from a laptop or tablet. Phone cards are optional and anonymous.
- It also works with no projector at all: the teacher reads from the printed Çağırıcı listesi and checks claims with its checkboxes and draw numbers.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO 'Tombala Gecesi' (quiz-night tombala).

Look and sound:
- Editorial cream theme, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. The real 3×5 tombala card is printed in a two-colour frame. No mascot.
- The caption reads 'Çekiliş 12 · Travel'. A woodblock tick sounds between calls, a 0.6 s piano chime plays on a çinko, and the finale is modest.
- Calls use TTS at natural speed. The teacher sets how many repeats each call gets: 1 by default, or none, or unlimited.
- Students can consult with a partner.

Kart türleri (variants):
1. Tanım Tombala (A2-B1): the call is a definition.
2. Boşluk Tombala (B1): the call is an example sentence with a soft beep at the gap, e.g. 'I missed the [beep], so I took a taxi.'
3. Kollokasyon Tombala (A2-B2): the card shows whole collocations ('make a decision', 'take a photo', 'do homework'). At A2 the call is the Turkish meaning ('karar vermek'). At B1-B2 it is a situation ('You finally choose one of the two job offers.'). This targets typical Turkish L1 errors such as 'do a decision'.
4. Phrasal Verb Tombala (B1-B2): the card shows 'put off', 'run out of' and similar; the call is a sentence with a beep.
5. Dilbilgisi Tombala: the cells are forms (went / has gone / was going / used to go / will have gone) or linkers (although, however, despite, unless). The call is a sentence with a beep, and the validator guarantees exactly one form fits.
6. Deyim Tombala (B2): the card shows idioms; the call is the meaning or a mini-situation. The recap adds the literal Turkish for a laugh.
7. Ses Tombala (A2-B2): both members of a minimal pair appear on cards (ship/sheep, live/leave, full/fool, walk/work, thirteen/thirty). The call is one word in a carrier sentence, so it is true listening.
8. Sayı Tombala: prices, dates, times, years, phone numbers, large numbers and percentages. At B1-B2 there is an optional culture corner of curated British 'bingo lingo' calls ('Two little ducks: twenty-two!').
9. Tanışma Tombala (a mingle, from speaking-prompt items with mode find-someone): the cells read e.g. 'has been to İzmir', 'can cook mantı'. The mingle lasts 6 min. A row needs 3-5 different classmates who said yes. The claim is a 3rd-person report ('Someone at my table has been to İzmir').

Adult rules:
- 'Kanıtla' at every çinko.
- An optional false-claim forfeit: the claimant reads the next clue aloud.
- Optional points for the first çinko, second çinko and tombala (1/2/3), feeding team totals.
- A 'Sadece dinle' round: audio only, no text ever shown.
- 'Çağırıcı modu': the winner of the first çinko reads the next 5 clues from the teacher device, which adds speaking.

Session length: 8-12 min as a warm-up or settler. A 20 min two-round version runs definitions first and then Sadece dinle with new cards.

Ending: the full answer list, plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' review (items flagged with Z, and items that were repeated), plus the take-home list with IPA and TR.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two distinct rule packs, not one reskin.

OYUN PARKI (9-11): 'Gogo's Tombala / Picture Tombala'.

The card: 3×3 big pictures, each with a tiny word underneath in an Andika-type font. The theme is cream and warm. The frame looks like a real tombala card, with little Gogo feathers in the blank corners. The card name is an animal plus a number ('Fox 7'), which is easy to say in English ('Card seven!').

THREE RULES, shown as pictograms:
1. (ear) Listen.
2. (finger) Find it and cover it.
3. (megaphone) A full row? Shout 'ÇİNKO!'. All of them? 'TOMBALA!'.

The call: Gogo the parrot pulls the pul out with its beak and says 'Find the... elephant! ... Elephant!' (0.8x, a 2 s gap). The picture appears on screen after 3-4 s in round 1 and after 6 s in round 2. Then the whole class echoes the word twice and gives a thumbs up; this is the whole-class moment every turn.

Marking: students cover cells with beans, erasers or paper squares. With the 'Boyama kartı' outline print, they colour each called picture, so the card becomes a colouring page to take home.

Rewards: a çinko earns a row sticker and a Gogo dance (at most 2 s, marimba). Tombala earns a big sticker and confetti in team colours AND shapes (finale only).

A false claim gets a head tilt from Gogo and 'Not yet! Keep listening!', with no penalty. There is no elimination, no score below zero and no buzzer. After tombala comes 'Bir kaldı!': students who were one short stand up for applause. Every desk-row team gets a title (Super Listeners, Sharp Ears, Best Helpers), and the class album gets the topic sticker.

Pacing: 3 rounds of 4-5 min, with a 45 s stirrer between rounds ('Gogo says: stand up if you have a lion!'):
- R1 Look and Listen.
- R2 Just Listen (the picture comes later).
- R3 Riddles, A2 Genç only ('It's yellow. Monkeys love it.').
The timer is off and the teacher presses Space. The rule card is in Turkish for the teacher; students see tiny English strings ('Listen!', 'Find it!', 'Not yet!'). Topics follow YLE and MEB units, always with pictures.

ARENA (12-14): 'Tombala Challenge'.

Look: dark navy with neon accents and a condensed display font. The 3×4 cards use sticker-style icons, and phone cards get the student's own neon colour. There are no animals and no mascot voice.

The draw: a glowing hex tile drops from a chute. An optional 90 bpm beat plays quietly, the spoken word lands on the beat, and the text drops 2.5 s later. A commentator strip appears at most once per event ('ÇİNKO #1 · CALL 7', 'ONE CALL AWAY').

Rounds:
- Standard.
- Blind round: the text is never shown.
- Remix round: the call is a synonym or a word-family form.

Optional squad mode: rows of desks become squads with an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto chosen in 10 s. The first çinko, second çinko and tombala earn 1/2/3 points.

The finale is a podium with stat awards: Fastest Çinko, Most Çinkos, Clean Sheet (no false claims), and Sharp Ears (the best result in the Blind round). There is never a last place. A false claim just gets 'Not yet', with no steals and no negatives. The rule card is in English with a Turkish toggle, and the game lasts 10-15 min.
catalog.levelTuning:
Word caps are for the call text; a longer clue is split into two lines revealed 3 s apart. The 3×n formats are the tombala card (full rows count).

A1 Genç (at most 4 words):
- Card: 3×3 pictures; pool of 12-15 concrete, picturable items.
- Call: the word in a frame, 'Find the ___!', twice. The picture follows after 3-4 s.
- Sayı Tombala: numbers 1-20.

A2 Genç (at most 8 words):
- Card: 3×3 or 3×4, a word with a small picture.
- Call: the word, then a 2-sentence description ('It's a fruit. It's yellow.'). Riddle rounds.
- Sayı Tombala: numbers to 100, and clock times with clock faces on the card.

B1 Genç (at most 14 words):
- Card: 3×4, words only.
- Call: a simple definition or a sentence with a beep, played once plus one repeat; the text appears after 2.5 s. Synonyms of concrete words; easy Ses pairs.
- Sayı Tombala: prices and dates.

B2 Genç (at most 20 words, concrete topics only):
- Card: 3×4 or 3×5.
- Call: synonyms, word families ('the adjective of danger'), collocation partners, sentences with a beep. Blind rounds, and no picture support.

A1 adults (at most 10 words):
- Card: 3×4 or 3×5 words.
- Round 1: the Turkish gloss appears on screen with English audio, and students find the English. Round 2: English audio only at 0.9x.
- Sayı Tombala: prices and phone numbers.

A2 adults (at most 15 words):
- Card: 3×5.
- Call: simple definitions or descriptions; Kollokasyon Tombala from TR to EN.
- Sayı Tombala: times, dates and prices.

B1 adults (at most 25 words; calls aim for 18):
- Calls: sentences with a beep, definitions, phrasal verbs, Dilbilgisi forms and linkers, Ses minimal pairs.

B2 adults (at most 40 words; calls aim for 20):
- Calls: synonyms, paraphrases, idiom meanings, word formation, collocation situations. Blind audio at natural speed, with 'no repeat' as an option.
- Sayı Tombala: statistics and bingo lingo.

The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial moves the clue type one step easier or harder. It also changes the picture delay (3 / 5 / 8 s or none), the number of repeats (2 / 1 / 0), and the word-band mix of the pool. Zor also switches on 'Cevaplar sonda'.

'Destekli kart' prints chosen cards with a small grey Turkish gloss or picture. These cards are marked only by a tiny dot that the teacher knows about, so a mixed-ability class plays the same game.

'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the content one level without changing the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 8-20 (one card game takes about 5-12 min; Oyun Parkı plays 3 short rounds, about 15-20 min in total; the Stüdyo warm-up takes 8-12 min)
catalog.contentShape:
THE POOL: 12-40 answer items. Each item becomes one card cell and gets one call recipe.

Where the items come from:
- vocab: term, alt[], media.img or media.emoji (required for A1/A2 Genç), defTr, defEasy or def, gap, example, family[] (for word formation), ipa, syll, concrete.
- pair: the card cell is b and the call is a. The rel types used are 'tr', 'syn', 'colloc', 'idiom-meaning' and 'past'.
- gap (Dilbilgisi): the cell is answers[0][0]; the text is read with a beep.
- qa: answerKind 'word', 'phrase' or 'number'. The clue is the call and accept[0] is the cell, which suits trivia from a teacher's prompt.
- riddle: clues[3] are revealed hard to easy, one every 4 s.
- sound (minimal-pair): a and b both go into the pool; sentenceA and sentenceB are the carrier calls.
- speaking-prompt with mode 'find-someone' (Tanışma): the prompt is the cell.

COMPUTED FOR EACH ITEM:
- calls {audio, picture, tr, describe, def, beepSentence, syn, colloc, form, riddle}, each checked against the group's word cap.
- A difficulty value and a confusion-group id.

Sayı Tombala needs no pack: code generates numbers, prices, clock times (with a clock SVG), dates, years and percentages.

VALIDATOR:
- The pool is at least 1.6× the card's cells.
- No duplicates and no inflection twins (run/running).
- Single-answer check: every call is tested against every pool item, by rules on defTr/syn overlap plus an LLM judge. A call that fits 2 items is rewritten or dropped.
- Near-synonyms are never in the same pool, except that Ses mode deliberately includes both members of a pair.
- The teenSafe filter runs for all Genç groups.
- The picture requirement holds for A1/A2 Genç. If the pool falls below the minimum, the game tops it up from the closest built-in category, or drops to 3×3 and warns the teacher.

CARD GENERATOR: a seeded PRNG built from the game code. Its rules:
- Every card is unique.
- Two cards share at most 60% of their cells.
- Each item appears on about the same number of cards (±1).
- Each row mixes easy and hard items.
- Pictures with similar colours are never adjacent on kids' cards.

GAME STATE (kept in localStorage, so a game can resume): {gameCode, layout, rows, cols, cardCount, pool[], callOrder[], calledIdx, prizes[{kind, cardNos[], callNo}], zorlandilar[]}.

PHONE CARD: languago.site/tombala#<code>-<cardNo>, built from the seed. It needs no login and sends nothing.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Layout: tombala rows, or 'Klasik Bingo' (4×4 or 5×5 with a free centre).
- Card size and number of cards. The count comes from the class size plus 10% spares.
- Kart türü and a clue-type mix for each round.
- Lesson-fit minutes, which sizes the pool and shows the simulated çinko and tombala draw numbers.

PRINT
- 4 cards per A4, black-and-white saver, cut marks, and the Çağırıcı listesi.
- Special versions: Boyama kartı (outlines to colour), Tekrar kullanılabilir (for lamination and counters), and Destekli kart for chosen card numbers.

PHONE CARDS
- On or off, with a QR code.

DURING PLAY
- Manual or auto draw, with the interval.
- Picture delay, the number of repeats and the TTS speed.
- 'Sadece dinle' and 'Cevaplar sonda'.
- History strip mode: answers, clues, or numbers only.
- Which prizes are on: the full ladder, or just çinko and tombala.

CLAIMS AND ENDINGS
- Claim rules: automatic row check, the read-aloud step, 'Kanıtla', a false-claim forfeit (Stüdyo only), and 'Uyuyan çinko'.
- Sıra takımları with a points mode (none, stars or points).
- The Turkish gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
- 'Öğretmen okur': used when there is no English voice. The projector shows 'Öğretmen okuyor...' and the teacher reads from the caller list.

KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS
- Space: next draw. R: repeat. T: pause (or 'Süresiz').
- Ç or C: claim a çinko. B: claim a tombala.
- Z: flag an item 'Zorlandılar'.
- ←/→: previous or next call. H: history. M: mute. F: fullscreen.

AFTER THE GAME
- 'Yeni kartlar, aynı içerik', 'Aynı kartlar, zor tur', 'Kaldığın yerden devam', and 'Özet ve kelime listesi (PDF)'.
catalog.delightDetails:
THE DRAW
- The real tombala bag: it shakes with a wooden clack, and a numbered wooden pul pops out and flips over to show its picture, or a '?' in listening rounds.
- In Oyun Parkı, Gogo pulls the pul out with its beak and then naps on the pause screen. In Arena, a neon hex tile drops from a chute to the beat.

THE CARDS
- The printed cards look like the tombala cards Turkish families use at New Year: a two-colour frame, decorative blank cells, and a big card number in a circle.
- Kids' cards carry names like 'Fox 7'. Colouring cards become a take-home picture.
- A dyslexia-friendly font, stamp marks that work for colour-blind students, and a large-print option.
- An optional 'Yılbaşı Tombalası' skin in late December: pine branches and lights, secular.

ON THE SCREEN
- The Çağrı panosu lights up like the host's master board. A 'Kalan pul' counter shows the pieces left, and a 'last call' bubble lets anyone re-hear the call.
- The 'BİRİNCİ ÇİNKO!' / 'İKİNCİ ÇİNKO!' / 'TOMBALA!' banners are familiar to every Turkish student.
- On verification, check stamps land on each called cell, each showing its draw number.

INCLUSIVE MOMENTS
- 'Ortak çinko' when two cards complete on the same draw.
- 'Bir kaldı!': the students who were one short stand up and get applause.

THE ENDING
- The recap becomes a take-home word list, and the items never called become a quick choral drill.
- Culture corners: bingo lingo for adults; the 1-90 numbers mode that mirrors the real tombala bag.

MOTION AND SOUND
- Reduced motion swaps every animation for a static stamp.
- Every sound is 1 s or shorter and loudness-normalised: marimba for kids, synth blips for Arena, woodblock and piano for adults.
catalog.risks:
- PRINTING OVERHEAD: printing is one click, 4 cards per A4, with a black-and-white saver. Phone cards and shared pair cards are backups, and laminated reusable cards cut printing for later games.
- CLUE AMBIGUITY (two words fit one definition): the single-answer validator runs, and near-synonyms are never pooled together.
- MARKING LATE OR CHEATING: the draw-number stamps on the verify screen and the read-aloud step catch it. Marking after the reveal is harmless learning; 'Cevaplar sonda' is there for strict classes.
- SIMULTANEOUS CLAIMS: 'Ortak çinko'. Unique cards do NOT prevent ties.
- EVERYONE WAITING FOR THE LAST CALL: the prize ladder, 'İkinci tombala' and 'Bir kaldı!' keep the whole class engaged.
- LOW SPEAKING AND LOW ENERGY FOR ADULTS: Kanıtla, Çağırıcı modu and Tanışma Tombala add speaking; keep the game to 8-12 min, as a warm-up or settler.
- NOISE IN 40-STUDENT ROOMS: claims are shouted, but the echo is structured, and the calm tick sets the rhythm.
- TTS VOICES: when there is no English voice, 'Öğretmen okur' with the printed caller list takes over.
- GAMBLING ASSOCIATION: tombala is sometimes played for money. The game never uses money, bets, 'jackpot' or coin sounds; prizes are stickers or points only. Bingo lingo is for adults only.
- 12-13-YEAR-OLDS FEELING TALKED DOWN TO: Arena is auto-suggested from grade 6 up.
- PICTURE DEPENDENCE FOR A1/A2 GENÇ: items that cannot be pictured are dropped, and the pool is topped up from built-in categories.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Any generic Bingo / Listening Bingo candidate (absorb it; keep Klasik Bingo as a layout option). Move Tanışma Tombala out to a speaking/mingle game.

issues: THE CARD-GENERATOR RULES CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. The Oyun Parkı pool can be 12 items with a 3×3 card (9 cells). Two 9-item cards drawn from 12 items always share at least 6 cells (9+9-12 = 6), which is 67%, so the rule 'two cards share at most 60%' cannot be met. At 15 items the minimum overlap drops to 3, but the average random overlap is about 5.4 of 9. With 28-40 cards, keeping every pair at 5 or fewer is very hard, and the generator will either stall or quietly break the rule.

MASS TIES AT 1.6× POOLS. Each card covers 60-75% of the pool, so the cards finish at almost the same time. With 28 cards on a pool of 12-15, many rows complete on the same draw near the end: 5-10 kids shout ÇİNKO or TOMBALA together. The flow is 'Ç, type a number, read the row, + Kart ekle' for each card, so checking one claim takes 15-25 s. A 6-card tie means 2 minutes of dead time while 22 kids wait, and the noise climbs.

CLAIM SPAM FROM 10-YEAR-OLDS. False claims cost nothing in Nazik mode, so impulsive kids shout 'ÇİNKO!' at random, and every false claim still costs the teacher a number-pad entry. After a few of those, the teacher stops checking and fairness breaks down.

THE SMART BOARD HAS NO KEYBOARD. The control scheme leans on shortcuts (Space, R, Ç, B, Z, arrow keys, H, M, F). A teacher standing at a Turkish public-school board (often Pardus/ETAP) has a touch screen and no keyboard, and 'Ç' also depends on the keyboard layout. As designed, the teacher walks back to a laptop for every draw and every claim.

PRINTING AND CUTTING ARE THE REAL SETUP COST. 28 cards plus 10% spares is 8 A4 sheets that have to be cut on the cut marks, about 10 minutes before class. Many public schools have limited printer or paper access. The 60 s setup estimate ignores this, and there is no zero-print path except phones, which are banned in MEB classrooms.

OYUN PARKI ROUNDS NEED FRESH CARDS. Beans and erasers fall off desks and get thrown; pencil X marks or colouring make a card single-use. So R2 and R3, or 'Aynı kartlar, zor tur', need new or cleared cards, but the design assumes cards carry over. 'Boyama kartı' colouring cannot happen inside a 10 s mark window.

KIDS WAIT FOR THE PICTURE INSTEAD OF LISTENING. The picture appears after 3-4 s in R1 while the mark window is 10 s, so weaker students learn to wait for the picture. The listening goal quietly turns into picture matching, and only the stronger listeners mark on the audio.
PAIRS SHARING A CARD. One partner holds the pencil and the other drifts. With 40 students in pairs, about half are passive at any moment, apart from the echo.

LUCK DECIDES THE WINNER. This is a plus for fairness, since a strong student cannot dominate and no team falls hopelessly behind. But there is no incentive to process the clue fast, and 'Fastest Çinko' in Arena rewards luck, not skill.

ADULTS. With 10 adults, a 3×5 card and one repeat, the game works as an 8-12 min settler, but bingo can feel childish, and there is only one speaking moment per çinko (Kanıtla). Kollokasyon, Ses and Tanışma carry the adult value; plain definition bingo is thin for B1-B2.

TOO MANY SETUP OPTIONS. Seven Kart türleri, two layouts, delivery and print variants, per-round clue mixes, and claim rules are a lot for a teacher with 5 minutes of break. The summary line helps, but there are no one-tap presets.

TTS AND CONNECTIVITY. Public-school boards often lack an English TTS voice, and Wi-Fi is unreliable. 'Öğretmen okur' is a good fallback, but only if it is detected automatically and the whole game works offline once loaded, including LLM content that was generated in advance.
IMAGE CONCERNS. 'Tombala' is linked to gambling for some administrators and parents, and a 'Yılbaşı' skin can be contentious in some schools. This is minor, but it can block use.
fixes: FIX THE CARD MATHS. Raise the pool to at least 2× the card's cells for classes over 20: Park 3×3 needs 18 or more items, and Arena 3×4 needs 24 or more. Replace the 60% overlap rule with 'minimise the maximum pairwise overlap, and warn if it goes over 70%'. Stagger completions on purpose: weight the call order and the card assignment so the simulated first çinko goes to 1-3 cards, not 8. Show the simulated tie count ('Aynı anda çinko ≈ 2 kart') in the setup estimate.

FAST GROUP CLAIM FLOW. Add a big on-screen 'ÇİNKO!' button that opens a multi-entry pad: type 7, 12, 19, then Enter, and all cards are checked at once on one split screen. Valid cards get the stamp together as an 'Ortak çinko'. The class reads the row in chorus instead of one student at a time. Cap the read-aloud at 1 claimant, chosen at random, when more than 3 cards tie.

ANTI-SPAM WITHOUT A PENALTY. When a claim is false, say 'Not yet', and that card's next claim is only accepted after the next draw (the lock is invisible to others). Add a 'Sessiz çinko' mode: kids raise the card silently, and the teacher taps 'claims open' after each reveal.

TOUCH-FIRST TEACHER UI. Add a persistent large bottom bar on the board: Next, Repeat, Çinko, Tombala, Flag and Pause, each at least 64 px. Keep the keyboard shortcuts as an extra. Add an optional phone remote for the teacher (the same game code opens a controller page).

A ZERO-PRINT MODE. Add 'Kartını kendin yap': the pool is projected, and students draw a 3×3 in their notebooks and copy 9 items. This adds spelling practice and takes about 3 min. Verification: the claimant reads the row, and the screen highlights any word that has been called (the teacher taps the 3 words on the Çağrı panosu). Also make printing 2 cards per A4 (half-sheet cut, one cut per page) and 'Tekrar kullanılabilir' laminated sets that can be reused all year.

SAFE KIDS' MARKING. The default instruction is 'pencil dot in the corner'. For multi-round play, print the Oyun Parkı card as three mini-grids on one half-sheet (R1 / R2 / R3), or ask for a different colour per round. Move colouring to after the game ('Şimdi resimleri boya!') as the recap activity.

PROTECT LISTENING. In R1, show the picture only after the mark window closes, or halfway through it at most. Add a 'Kulak turu' so the picture appears only at the reveal. Keep the whole-class echo after the reveal so weaker learners still get the word.
ACTIVATE BOTH PARTNERS. When a card is shared, add a 'Rol değiş' pulse every 5 draws: the pencil passes, and the partner without the pencil has to point before the other marks.

STOP REWARDING LUCK AS SKILL. Rename 'Fastest Çinko' to 'First Çinko', or drop it. Add a skill award that does not depend on luck, for example 'Sharp Ears' based on Blind-round accuracy checked through the proof step.

ADULT UPGRADES. Make Kollokasyon, Ses or Tanışma the default adult card type, not plain definitions. Turn on 'Çağırıcı modu' by default after the first çinko. Offer a 'Kanıtla' rotation where the claimant picks another person to use the word.

PRESETS. Put three one-tap starts on the setup screen: 'Hızlı ısınma (8 dk)', 'Dinleme dersi (15 dk)' and 'Sayı Tombala'. Everything else goes under 'Ayrıntılar'. Remember the last settings per class profile.

OFFLINE AND TTS. Pre-cache the game and pack after load. Pre-generate LLM packs, since they can't be made live in class. Test for an English voice when the game starts and switch to 'Öğretmen okur' automatically, with the caller list shown on the teacher device only.
NAMING. Add a 'Kelime Bingo' name and skin toggle for schools that are sensitive about tombala. Keep the Yılbaşı skin opt-in only.

SCOPE. This is an L build, so ship in stages. v1: Kelime, Resim and Sayı card types, print plus the zero-print mode, and touch UI. v2: Kollokasyon, Ses and Dilbilgisi. v3: phone cards, Tanışma and Arena extras.

issues: Picture-first leak for kids: in Oyun Parkı the picture appears 3-4 s into a 10 s mark window (6 s in R2). Children soon learn to wait for the picture, so the listening task turns into picture matching. At A1 Genç that makes the 'listening' game mostly visual.

A1 adult Round 1 shows the Turkish gloss on screen and plays English audio at the same time. Students just read the Turkish and scan the card for the translation, so it is reading translation, not listening. Audio should come first.

Ses Tombala carrier sentences break the listening test. 'sentenceA/sentenceB' in context (e.g. 'The ___ sank in the storm') gives the answer away through meaning, not sound. For a real minimal-pair test the frame has to be neutral ('Number 7: ship').

Dilbilgisi Tombala cannot fill a pool. Linkers (although/however/despite/unless/...) run out at around 10-12 unique forms. Tense forms repeat ('went' fits many sentences), and each cell has to be a unique answer. A 3×5 card needs 24+ distinct forms with exactly one fitting sentence each, which is unrealistic at A2-B1 and fragile from an LLM.

The LLM path clashes with the picture requirement. A teacher prompt such as 'çevre kirliliği' or 'duygular' gives abstract items that emoji cannot picture, yet A1/A2 Genç requires media.img. The top-up from the 'closest built-in category' can quietly replace the teacher's topic, so the game drifts off the lesson aim.

Definition calls at B1-B2 made by the LLM often fit several items in a topical pool of 24-30 (travel: 'trip/journey/tour', 'luggage/suitcase'). Removing near-synonyms makes topic pools thin, and the LLM judge adds cost and latency at setup. The design is sound, but it will often drop items and fall under the 1.6× minimum.

Low production density for most students. Only claimants read a row or 'Kanıtla'. Everyone else does single-word recognition, roughly one item per 30-45 s. Kids get a choral echo, but Arena and Stüdyo make echo optional, so a B1/B2 adult class can spend 12 min almost silent apart from shouting 'Çinko'.

B2 Genç 'word families ('the adjective of danger')' and 20-word calls are metalinguistic and dense for 12-13-year-olds, and heard audio-only in Blind rounds. That is a lot of load, and grammar-term calls turn listening into a terminology test.

Tanışma Tombala (a mingle with 3rd-person reports) is only specified for adults, and its 3-5 different classmates per row is too heavy for 40-student Turkish classrooms with fixed desks. For kids it is not defined at all. A 6-minute mingle does not fit the 'calm settler' role either.
B2 adults may see plain bingo as low-challenge filler. Only the idiom, paraphrase and blind variants really stretch them, and the default Kart türü 'Kelime' with a definition call is about B1 demand.
Riddle rounds for A2 Genç reveal three clues 4 s apart (12 s), which is longer than the kids' 10 s mark window. The timing contradicts itself.
Nine Kart türleri × 3 audiences × 2 layouts is a big surface for an L build. Level coverage will be uneven, and several variants (Dilbilgisi, Ses, Tanışma) will ship half-validated.
fixes: Kids' pictures appear only at the reveal, when the mark window ends, from round 2 on. In R1 the picture shows at 4 s but is blurred or silhouetted until the reveal. Add a whole-class 'whisper it to your partner' step before every reveal so each child produces the word.
A1 adults: play the English audio first, with the Turkish gloss hidden until the reveal. Keep a TR→EN mode only as a labelled 'Çeviri turu' that the teacher selects, not as the default Round 1.

Ses Tombala: force neutral carrier frames ('Number N is ___' or 'I say ___') and forbid disambiguating context. Add a TTS check, with a hand-picked recorded audio set for the core minimal pairs, because browser TTS often blurs ship/sheep and full/fool.

Dilbilgisi Tombala: restrict it to the 'Klasik Bingo' 3×3 or 4×4 layout, and allow repeated forms as separate cells with different sentences (a cell is marked by any matching call). Or recast it as 'form × function' cells. Hide it when the validated pool is under the minimum, and only offer it from the curated grammar_mcq banks, never from free LLM output alone.

LLM path for Genç groups: have the LLM also output 'picturable: true/false' plus an emoji. If fewer than 12 picturable items remain, show the teacher a choice ('Bu konu resimle zor; Kelime kartıyla oyna / yakın konu ekle: ...') instead of topping up silently.

Make the choral echo the default in Arena too (on the beat), and in Stüdyo add a default 'Partner check' (5 s: tell your partner the word and use it) after every reveal. Make Çağırıcı modu one click, so production is not tied only to claimants.

B2 Genç: replace metalinguistic 'adjective of danger' calls with contextual gap sentences ('It's a very ___ road.'), cap calls at 14-16 words, and keep the text reveal in Blind rounds optional for the teacher.

Define Tanışma for kids as a seated 'ask your neighbours' version (the 4-6 students around you, yes/no picture questions, the 'Can you swim?' model), and label it as an energizer, not a settler. For adults, allow a seated variant with fewer cells (3×3).
Riddle rounds: extend the mark window to at least 14 s, or reveal the clues 3 s apart, and let a riddle round turn auto-draw off.

Ship a narrower v1: Kelime/Resim, Sayı, Kollokasyon and Deyim across all levels, with validated level presets. Add Dilbilgisi, Ses and Tanışma in v2 once the validators are proven. In setup, show a per-level 'önerilen kart türü' so B2 adults default to the paraphrase or idiom variants, not plain definitions.

reviews.mergeWith: Any generic Bingo / Listening Bingo candidate (absorb it; keep Klasik Bingo as a layout option). Move Tanışma Tombala out to a speaking/mingle game.
issues: The card maths is broken as specified, and this is the biggest risk. With pool = 1.6x cells and 40 cards, the '≤60% shared cells' rule cannot be met. Kids (9 of 15, each item on ~24 cards): the average pairwise overlap is 15*C(24,2)/C(40,2) ≈ 5.3 cells, which is above the 5.4-cell cap only by rounding. An integer overlap must be ≤5, and the average already exceeds that, so the generator will loop forever or silently break the rule.

Ties will be the norm, not the exception. In a 3x3 card over a 12-15 pool, rows are 3-subsets of 15 items (455 combos), and 40 cards carry 120 rows. The first çinko then lands at around draw 4-6 with several cards at once, and TOMBALA at 9-of-15 lands in the last 2-3 draws for most of the class at the same moment. The same compression hits Stüdyo 15-of-24. Real tombala works because the ratio is 15 of 90 (6x). At 1.6x the game degenerates into a chorus of simultaneous claims, and 'Ortak çinko' is no fix when 8 kids have it.

The scope is XL, not L. The spec has 9 kart türleri, 3 audience rule packs, 8 level tunings, a PDF print pipeline with 4 print variants (normal, B&W, Boyama outlines, Destekli), phone cards, a Monte Carlo estimator, a claim verifier, TTS with beeps, Gogo animations, an Arena beat, and a podium with stat awards. Most of the 'types' are the same engine with different content, but they are listed as features, so they will be built as features.
Tanışma Tombala (find-someone mingle) is a different game. It has no caller, no draw, no pool and no verification by card number. It shares only the grid, and it breaks the calm-listening identity.

TTS timing is unreliable. Beat-synced calls ('the word lands on the beat') are not achievable: speechSynthesis start latency varies by 100-800 ms and there is no accurate onstart. 'Sentence with a soft beep in the gap' needs utterance splitting plus a WebAudio beep. On Chrome, onend events are flaky; Safari/iPad and many school smartboards (Android-based Vestel/Arçelik boards in MEB schools) often have no en-GB/en-US voice or only a robotic one.

Kids pictures depend on emoji or icons that don't exist for free-prompt content. The LLM cannot produce pictures. Emoji render differently on Windows (Segoe flat), smartboard Android and print. The picture requirement for A1/A2 Genç means that free-text prompts for kids silently shrink to whatever the icon set covers. Boyama kartı needs a second outline version of every icon, which doubles the art burden.

The single-answer LLM judge over N×N (call × pool item) pairs is costly and slow when done naively. For free-prompt definitions and riddles it is the real validity risk: 'It's a big animal. It's grey.' fits both elephant and hippo.

Seeded card rebuild has a hidden versioning trap. Printed cards from last week must still verify after a code change to the PRNG or the card-constraint solver. If the generator algorithm is not versioned inside the game code, old printed cards become unverifiable.
'Cevaplar sonda' conflicts with claim verification. The verify screen stamps called cells, which reveals answers mid-game to the whole projector.

Adults above A2 will find it thin. Listening bingo is a good 8-minute settler, but B2 synonym or idiom tombala with 30+ calls of passive marking has little speaking even with Kanıtla. That is why adultFit is lower.

Noise and claim management with 40 kids: several shouting ÇİNKO at once while the teacher types card numbers one by one on a number pad is a bottleneck, especially on a smartboard with no keyboard (Ç key shortcuts don't exist there).

Partial overlap with other likely candidates: a generic 'Bingo' using pair items, 'Spot the Match', and any 'listen and tap' quiz. It is distinct enough through the whole-class, paper-first, listening-caller format, but it should BE the suite's Bingo, not sit next to one.
fixes: Fix the ratios and let the simulator drive them. Set the pool to at least 2.5x cells: kids 3x3 → 22-24 items, Arena 3x4 → 30, Stüdyo 3x5 → 36-40. For a small kids pool, default to PAIRS sharing a card (20 cards for 40 kids). Replace the hard '≤60% overlap' rule with a 'minimise max overlap' greedy solver that has a bounded retry budget and a fallback. The 500-game simulation should gate setup: if the expected number of tied claimants at first çinko is more than 3, warn and propose a bigger pool or pairs.

Make the kids prize ladder tie-proof. With 30+ cards, 'first çinko' should be a class-level event ('Stand up if you have a row!') followed by a quick spot-check of 1-2 random cards, not a race to be verified. Keep the TOMBALA verification only.

MVP (v1, about M-L): one engine that takes a generic (cell, call[]) pool. Ship three sources: Kelime (word/picture/TR/definition/beep-sentence calls from vocab/pair/gap/qa/riddle), Sayı (code-generated, including the 1-90 classic mode), and Ses (minimal pairs). Kollokasyon, Phrasal, Dilbilgisi and Deyim are just built-in category presets on the same pipeline, not separate features. Defer to v2: Boyama outlines, Destekli dot cards, podium stat awards, auto-draw, the Yılbaşı skin, bingo lingo.
Drop Tanışma Tombala from this game. Move 'find someone who' into a speaking/mingle game (or the speaking wheel) where it belongs.

TTS: drop beat sync. Play the Arena loop quietly underneath and speak the call on keypress. Render beep-sentences as utterance A → 350 ms WebAudio beep → utterance B, with a timeout fallback if onend never fires. Probe voices at setup, show a 'Ses testi' button, and default to 'Öğretmen okur' if no English voice exists. For built-in content, pre-generate MP3s at build time (a small self-hosted set for the kids picture vocab: roughly 300 words × ~6 KB), so the most age-sensitive group never depends on device TTS.

Pictures: bundle a curated, self-hosted SVG icon set (e.g. OpenMoji CC-BY-SA, with attribution) mapped to about 400 YLE/MEB picturable lemmas, with outline variants derived by CSS stroke-only rendering rather than new art. For kids free-prompt content, the LLM must choose from the icon lemma list (a constrained enum); items it cannot map are dropped and topped up from the nearest built-in category.

Validation pipeline: (1) Deterministic first. Words.js lookups give level band, POS, and inflection-twin and duplicate removal. Use a synonym/defTr overlap check, and enforce word caps by count. (2) One batched LLM judge call per pack: send the full pool plus all calls and ask for a JSON matrix listing only the call→item fits that are not the intended one. Drop or rewrite the offenders and re-judge once. (3) Riddles/descriptions for kids must include at least one distinguishing feature: require the generator to name the confusable item it excluded.
Encode a generator version in the game code (e.g. 'TMB1-4Q7'). Keep old generator versions in the bundle (tiny) so printed cards always verify.
In 'Cevaplar sonda' mode, verify on the teacher's device (presenter view) or show only the draw-number stamps without cell text on the projector.

Smartboard input: use a big on-screen button bar (Sonraki / Tekrar / ÇİNKO / TOMBALA) plus a big touch number pad. Keyboard shortcuts are secondary. The claim queue should accept several card numbers in one entry (7, 12, 31) and verify them all at once.
Adults: position the game explicitly as an 8-12 min warm-up or settler. Make Çağırıcı modu (a student reads the next calls) and Kanıtla the adult defaults, so speaking is built in.
Print via @media print CSS and browser print-to-PDF, not a JS PDF library. Keep the bundle small, and use the page-break-inside: avoid rule for 4 cards per A4 plus the caller list page.
Declare this THE bingo of the suite. Merge any separate 'Bingo' or 'Kelime Bingo' candidate into it, and keep 'Klasik Bingo' (5x5, lines any direction) as a layout option.

catalog.rankReason: Top score (7.7) with feasibility 8 and teen 8.7. It is the tombala everyone plays at New Year: a calm, whole-class listening game that scales to 40+ students with no phones. Fix the card maths first: a pool of at least 2-2.5x the card cells, the maximum pairwise overlap minimised by a simulator, pairs sharing a card in big kids' classes, and a tie-proof prize ladder ('Stand up if you have a row' plus a spot-check, and a multi-number ÇİNKO pad). Audio comes first; the picture or Turkish shows only at the reveal. Tanışma Tombala moves to x05.

catalog.name: Kelime Kurtar (Hangman without gallows + Çarkıfelek mode)
catalog.familiarAs: Hangman / Adam Asmaca, Wheel of Fortune (Çarkıfelek)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams take turns asking for letters in English to uncover a hidden word, chunk, idiom or sentence before a friendly scene runs out of lives: balloons, laser locks or strikes, never a gallows. A clue ladder unlocks meaning step by step, solving early pays best, and every solve ends with "Use it!" and a word card. Çarkıfelek mode adds the wheel: spin, call consonants, buy vowels and solve.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 60 s, teacher laptop on the projector)
- The setup screen shows one summary line, e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk', with a 'Değiştir' link.
- Mode: KURTAR (hangman rescue, the default); ÇARK (Çarkıfelek); or KARMA (Kurtar rounds, then a Çark final).
- Content: a built-in category, a MEB unit, a grammar unit, idioms, a pasted list, a free-text prompt for the LLM (Turkish or English), or 'Gizli kelime'. With 'Gizli kelime' the teacher or a student types a word while the projector shows a curtain.
- Teams: 2-4 in Park, 2-6 in Arena and Stüdyo, or co-op 'Sınıf vs Oyun' (the class wins if it rescues about 70% of the puzzles).
- Length: the lesson-fit timer turns minutes into a puzzle count (about 1.5 min per word puzzle and 2.5 min per Çark phrase).
- Teams pick a name and look. Park: an animal mascot. Arena: an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto, in 10 s. Stüdyo: a pun or city name.

PRACTICE (never scored)
- Park: Gogo the parrot plays 'cat' alone in 20-30 s, showing 'say a letter', a balloon pop and 'I know!'.
- Arena: one 3-letter warm-up code.
- Stüdyo: an optional sample puzzle.

THE BOARD
- One tile per letter.
- Pre-revealed: spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and, at B2, punctuation. A word is never split across lines.
- Always shown: a category badge, the part of speech and the letter count (e.g. '2 words: 3 + 2').
- The theme scene with a lives meter, the clue-ladder column and the team bar.
- A big on-screen keyboard in the bottom third: ABC order in Park, QWERTY in Arena and Stüdyo (switchable).
- Keys already used grey out; misses also get an X mark, so the state never relies on colour alone.

KURTAR TURN (the default; one letter per turn, so no team runs the board)
1. Pick the speaker. Park and Arena: the seat-number spinner picks the speaker in the active team. Stüdyo: a rotating captain badge. Nobody is ever picked by name.
2. Ask for a letter in English with the level frame: A1 'B, please!', A2 and up 'Is there an M?'. From A2 up each key shows its article ('an F', 'a U'), which teaches a/an before letter names.
