3. Enter it. The teacher taps the key or presses the physical key (a student may tap a smartboard). The recorded letter name plays (kids: 0.8x).
4. Whole-class moment. Park, every turn: the whole class air-writes the letter and echoes its name. Optional in the other modes.
5a. HIT: if the letter occurs more than once, a short suspense drum plays first. Every occurrence then flips in with a click, and the class counts with the host ('Two Es!').
   - Park: 1 star.
   - Arena: +1 per occurrence, times the combo.
   - Stüdyo: +10 per occurrence.
5b. MISS: the letter drops into the 'Not here' tray, the scene loses one life (a balloon pops, a laser lock re-arms, a strike lights) and the turn passes.
6. SOLVE: instead of a letter, the team may solve on its turn.
   - Team talk first: 10 s in Park, 15 s in Arena, 20 s in Stüdyo. Then the speaker says the answer. At B levels the teacher may switch on 'Harf harf çöz', where the team spells the missing letters. The teacher taps Correct or Wrong.
   - Correct:
     - Park: 3 stars.
     - Arena: +5, plus 1 per still-hidden letter.
     - Stüdyo: the puzzle value (50/75/100 by difficulty, minus 10 per clue bought), plus 10 per hidden letter and 10 per life left.
     - Solving early with meaning always beats spamming E, T, A.
   - Wrong:
     - Park: a soft boing, the next hint rung opens free, the turn passes, and no balloon is lost.
     - Arena: one life is lost. Teams whose mini-whiteboards (written during the huddle) show the right answer steal +3. The first team keeps its points.
     - Stüdyo: one life is lost, plus an optional -20 (floor 0 unless negatives are on).
7. CLUE LADDER: the category is always free. If the board stalls, rungs open automatically: the first after 3 misses, the second after 5.
   - Park: all rungs are free and automatic (picture, then first letter, then listen again).
   - Arena and Stüdyo: a team may buy the next rung on its turn before its letter. Arena costs 1-2 points; Stüdyo lowers the puzzle value by 10. Scores never go below 0.
8. OUT OF LIVES: nobody gets hurt.
   - Park: Gogo swoops down with a parachute and lands the basket in a haystack ('Oops! Next mission!').
   - Arena: the vault 'resets'.
   - Stüdyo: the phone battery dies, or the balloon lands on a sandbank.
   - The answer appears with its picture, the host or TTS says it, and the class repeats it twice.
   - Park: every team gets an effort star, which goes to the class album, not the win count. Nobody loses points.
9. USE IT!: after every solve. In Park it also runs after a failed rescue, as a whole-class task.
   - A1 Genç, 'Point and say': 3 pictures appear after a 3-4 s delay; everyone points, says the word twice, and acts it out if it is a verb.
   - A2 Genç: a frame, 'I like / I have / I can ___', earns a sticker.
   - Arena: 15 s to say a sentence, with frame chips on screen. Correct +3, Almost +1.
   - Stüdyo: +20. Optional at A1-A2, always run at B1, and at B2 a paraphrase or 'When would you use it?'.
10. WORD CARD: the item flies into a card with:
   - the word, the IPA (from words.js) and a speaker button (0.8x or 1x);
   - syllable dots with the stress marked;
   - the example sentence with the word highlighted;
   - the TR gloss (toggle; Park shows it only in the teacher chrome);
   - a 'Silent K!' badge if a sound item exists.
   The class echoes the word twice and the card goes into 'Bugünün kelimeleri'.
11. NEXT PUZZLE: the trailing team starts (Comeback: Light) and earns Slipstream, a +1 star, +1 or +10 bonus on its next correct letter.

ÇARK TURN (Çarkıfelek mode)
1. The active team spins: a tap, a flick or Space. The wheel has momentum and ticking pegs.
2. The team calls a consonant. The wedge value times the occurrences goes into the team's round bank. A correct consonant earns another spin (cap: 3 in a row, then the turn passes; toggle). A miss passes the turn.
3. 'Sesli harf al': vowels cost 200 from the round bank in Stüdyo, 2 points in Arena, and nothing in Park. No spin is needed.
4. Solve on your turn by reading the whole phrase aloud intelligibly. The teacher judges and allows one 'say it again'.
   - The team banks its round money, plus a 300 bonus and Use it (+200).
   - TV rule: the other teams' round banks reset. The toggle 'Herkes kazandığını korusun' is always on in Park and Arena.
5. When all the consonants are out, a chime plays and the wheel greys: teams can only buy a vowel or solve.

ROUNDS AND FINALS
- Rounds hold 3-5 puzzles.
- Arena and Stüdyo open each round with an optional TOSS-UP: letters appear one by one, any team raises a hand, and a wrong buzz locks that team out. It only decides who starts, so there are no speed points.
- Between Park rounds: a 45 s stirrer ('Stand up if your name has an A!') or a 60 s settler (air-write today's words).
- Finals:
  - Park, 'Gogo's Big Rescue': one co-op puzzle for the whole class.
  - Arena, 'Final Code': a staged reveal in 3 stages. After each stage every team holds its board up at once; a team scores 5, 3 or 1 at the first stage its board is right, and a wrong board scores nothing.
  - Stüdyo, 'Final Vault': R S T L N E are revealed, the trailing team picks 3 consonants and 1 vowel, and every team writes an answer in 20 s. A team may wager up to half its score (opt-in).

END SCREEN
- Park: every team gets a title, the class album gets a sticker, and the banner reads 'We rescued 7 of 9!'.
- Arena: a podium plus stat awards (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, Code Cracker). There is never a last place.
- Stüdyo: full scores plus 'Kaçırılanlar': the unsolved items and the letter names the class confused (E/I, G/J, A/R).
- Everyone: a printable mini-glossary of today's words with IPA and TR, which can also be saved as a Languago word list.
catalog.playerSetup:
Whole class on one projector.
- Teams: 2-4 teams in Oyun Parkı; 2-6 in Arena and Stüdyo. Suggested size: 4-8 students per team.
- Co-op mode 'Sınıf vs Oyun': the class plays against the game. It is the default option offered for a very young class or for A1 Genç with a single group.
- Who speaks:
  - Park and Arena: the seat-number spinner picks the speaker in the active team, so nobody is chosen by name.
  - Stüdyo: a rotating captain badge, with 20 s of pair consultation before a solve.
- Arena teams need one mini-whiteboard each for Team talk, steals and the Final Code.
- A student may operate the smartboard keyboard, or the teacher types the letters.
skills: English letter names and the alphabet (including a/an before letters)
chunks, collocations, phrasal verbs and idioms (B1-B2)
catalog.contentShape:
The code builds a Puzzle from pack items. The LLM never writes a Puzzle directly.

PUZZLE FIELDS
- id, srcType, srcId.
- answer: the display text. ASCII letters, space, apostrophe and hyphen only; B2 sentence puzzles may also contain . , ? !
- norm: A-Z only, uppercased with en-US casing.
- slots[]: each slot is a letter, a space or punctuation; punctuation is pre-revealed.
- words: the word count. len and uniq (distinct letters) are computed. rare: the count of J Q X Z K V.
- diff: computed from len, uniq, rare and the words.js band. It orders the puzzles easy to hard and sets the Stüdyo value (50, 75 or 100).
- category: {en, tr, emoji or imageKey}; pos.
- rungs[]: ordered per audience. Each rung is {kind, payload, cost}. Kinds: picture, blurPicture, emoji, firstLetter, allVowels, listen, defEasy, def, gapExample, synonym, tr, lit, riddleClue.
- card: {ipa, syll, stressIdx?, defTr, example, family[]?, lit?, silent[]?, tts: true}.
- useIt: {mode ('pick3'|'frame'|'sentence'|'paraphrase'|'register'), frames[], pickMedia[2] (from the distractors' media)}.
- imageKey, teenSafe.

WHERE PUZZLES COME FROM
- vocab: the main source. Only items with hangman == true (letters only and 3-12 long, or a phrase at B levels).
  - term becomes the answer and alt[] the accepted solves.
  - media gives the picture rung; defEasy (A) or def (B) the definition rung; gap.text the gapped-example rung; defTr the TR rung; lit the literal-Turkish rung for idioms.
  - ipa and syll feed the card; distractors' media feed Use-it pick3.
- qa (answerKind word or phrase, and teacherJudge false): clue is a rung, and accept[] are all valid solves.
- riddle: clues[3] (hard to easy) form the whole ladder under the 'What am I?' frame.
- category-list (open = false): the label becomes a Çark round category and each member a puzzle ('THINGS IN A KITCHEN').
- order (kind 'sentence'): the joined tokens make a B1-B2 Çark sentence puzzle; hintTr becomes a rung.
- speaking-prompt: starters and useful supply the Use-it frames.
- sound (silent-letter or stress): decorates the word card.
- chance-card: fills the Çark 'Task' and 'Joker' wedges ('Say 3 words that start with B'). Only reward and bonus kinds for kids.

BUILT-IN FEEDS
- words.js {w, p, d, e, i, t} gives term, pos, def (only if it is 18 words or fewer and does not contain the term), example, ipa and defTr.
- idioms.js {w, t, ex, lit} gives the B2 idiom rounds.
- grammar_a1..c1 model sentences, as order items, give the sentence puzzles.
- The LLM fills defEasy, gap, emoji and kid-safe clues. The code overwrites ipa and defTr from words.js whenever the term exists there, and never trusts LLM IPA.

VALIDATOR
- Reject Turkish letters and diacritics (ç ğ ı İ ö ş ü).
- Length caps per level and audience.
- At least 3 distinct letters, so 'mama' or 'eye' are never solved by one guess.
- No proper nouns unless the category asks for them.
- Clues must never contain the answer, its alt[] or a family stem of 4+ letters.
- The gapped example must hide every occurrence of the answer. Pattern examples ('drink something, ...') are rejected.
- Clues obey the text-load caps.
- teenSafe filter for every Genç group.
- Picture-dependent groups (A1 and A2 Genç) drop items with no imageKey.
- Duplicates are removed.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'WORD VAULT' (Kurtar) and 'PHRASE WHEEL' (Çark), A1-B2 adults

LOOK AND SOUND
- Editorial quiz-night look: cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme.
- A TV-style letter board whose tiles light up one by one. System sans, no mascot, no voice lines.
- A neutral caption such as 'Round 2 · Travel'. Woodblock and piano sounds; a 0.6 s chime as the score rolls up.

SCENE SKINS (never a gallows)
- Word Vault: 6 strike lamps. The default.
- Hot-air balloon: a sandbag drops per miss; a solve lands the balloon on an island, and running out lands it on a sandbank.
- Phone battery: 100% down to 0%, then 'phone died'.
- Coffee getting cold: the steam fades per miss.
- One life left: the background dims calmly, with no flashing.

WORD VAULT RULES (Kurtar)
- Lives: 6, or 7 at A1.
- Letters: +10 per occurrence, one letter per turn.
- Clue ladder: definition (defEasy at A, Oxford def at B), then a gapped example, then the TR gloss or the idiom's literal Turkish. Each rung lowers the puzzle value by 10.
- The TR rung can be switched off for immersion classes. At B1+ a synonym or collocation can replace it.
- Solve: the puzzle value (50/75/100) + 10 per hidden letter + 10 per life left.
- Wrong solve: one life, plus -20 if negatives are on.
- Optional wager: before a solve, a team may stake up to 50 of its own points.
- Use it: +20. At B2 the team paraphrases the meaning or says when it would use the phrase, with an optional register challenge ('Say it more formally').

PHRASE WHEEL RULES (Çark)
- A 16-wedge wheel, big enough to read from the back: 100-1000, PAS (lose the turn), JOKER (cancel one later PAS or miss), ÇİFTE (doubles the next consonant) and SERBEST SESLİ (a free vowel).
- Harshness dial: Rüzgâr (lose half the round bank) is on by default (Yellow). İFLAS (lose the round bank) is off unless the teacher opts into Red.
- Vowels cost 200 from the round bank. A correct consonant earns another spin, up to 3 in a row.
- Solve by reading the phrase aloud intelligibly: bank the round money plus 300, and Use it! earns +200. The TV rule resets the other teams' round banks (toggle).
- 'Adil çark': each team draws wedge values from its own shuffled bag, so luck evens out. 'Sabit değer' replaces the wheel with a fixed 300 per consonant for classes that dislike randomness.

CONTENT
- Collocations (make a decision), phrasal verbs (give up), business and travel phrases ('Could you send me the file?'), small talk, complaints, and grammar model sentences ('I have never been to Paris').
- B2: idioms from idioms.js and proverb halves.

FINAL AND END
- Final Vault: R S T L N E revealed, the trailing team picks the letters, and every team writes its answer with an optional wager.
- End: full scores plus 'Kaçırılanlar' and the glossary.
- Pacing: rounds of 8-12 min, 20-40 min in total. An optional 30 s turn timer; +10 s, pause and 'Süresiz' are always available.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two real young-learner variants, chosen by the audience dial (not by level).

OYUN PARKI (9-11, default for A1 and A2 Genç): 'BALLOON RESCUE' with Gogo the parrot

LOOK
- Gogo's friend, a kitten, floats in a basket under 8 colourful balloons.
- Warm cream palette and an Andika-type font with a single-storey a.
- Lowercase tiles at least 9vh tall, which also avoids the dotted-İ problem.
- A big ABC keyboard with rounded keys. Each key says its English letter name on tap (recorded, 0.8x).
- Animal team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog...).

THE 3 RULES (pictograms, 20 s, read from a Turkish rule card)
1. Say a letter.
2. A right letter is a star; a wrong letter pops one balloon.
3. Know the word? Say 'I know!' and read it.
There is no elimination and no score below zero. Stars go to teams, while the balloons are the whole class's shared goal.

EVERY TURN
- The seat spinner picks a speaker.
- The whole class air-writes the letter as Gogo says it ('B! B for ball!').
- On a hit, everyone counts with Gogo ('Two Es!').
- A1 Genç: the first letter is pre-filled and the picture is visible from the start (spelling a known picture word).
- A2 Genç: a Polaroid picture that develops sharper with each correct letter.
- Free automatic hints: first letter after 2 misses, then 'listen again' after 4.

WRONG ANSWERS AND FAILURE
- A wrong solve gets a soft boing and a free hint, and no balloon is lost.
- At 0 balloons, Gogo parachutes down, catches the basket and lands it in a haystack ('Oops! Next mission!'). Gogo says the word, the class repeats it twice, and every team gets an effort star.
- Balloons pop in a descending marimba scale, with no buzzers.

AFTER EVERY SOLVE
- The basket lands on the island and the kitten waves.
- A sticker burst in the category's theme (a banana sticker for Food), 2 s at most.
- Use it: A1 points to the right picture among 3, then says the word twice and acts it out if it is a verb. A2 uses the frame 'I like / I can / I have ___'.

OPTIONS AND PACING
- Alternative skins: Build a Snowman (correct letters add parts; misses bring the sun out, and at 0 the snowman puts on sunglasses and hides in a fridge) and Rocket Launch (a solve launches it; at 0 it rolls back into the hangar).
- 'Gogo'nun Çarkı', optional: a 6-wedge picture wheel of 1, 2 and 3 stars, Free letter, Everyone +1 star and Dance break. The wheel only sizes the reward and vowels are free, so there are still 3 rules.
- 3 rounds of 3-5 min with a stirrer or settler between them, 15-25 min in total. Timer off by default (a calm 40 s ring when on).
- Finale 'Gogo's Big Rescue': the whole class plays together, then confetti in team colours and shapes, a title for every team (Super Spellers, Letter Detectives, Bravest Guessers, Best Helpers) and a class-album sticker.

ARENA (12-14, default for B1 and B2 Genç; any Genç group at grade 6+): 'CODE BREAKER'

LOOK
- Dark navy with neon in the team colours and a condensed display font.
- The hidden word is a vault code guarded by 6 laser locks (7 at A1 and A2).
- No animals, no talking mascot and no pastels. Geometric team emblems plus a 3-word motto picked in 10 s.
- 'Match' wording. A commentator strip at most once per turn: 'COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!' (a solve on the last lock), 'CLEAN SHEET'.

RULES
- +1 per occurrence, with the combo from accuracy only: x1.5 at 3 correct actions in a row, x2 at 5.
- Solve: +5, plus 1 per hidden letter.
- Hints: first letter (1), all vowels (2), gapped example (2). The floor is 0.
- Mini-whiteboards: during the 15 s Team talk before a solve, every team writes an answer. If the solver is wrong, correct boards steal +3 and the first team loses nothing.
- Mild steals (Steal 3 wedge) only if the teacher opts in.
- 'Spin Match' Çark option: wedges 1-5, x2, Shield, Free vowel and PAS; vowels cost 2.
- Out of locks: the vault 'resets' and the code is shown and echoed. No failure imagery.

TIMING AND ENDING
- 30 s timer in the team colour; +10 s and 'Süresiz' always available.
- Rounds of 5-7 min, 15-30 min in total. A toss-up decides who starts.
- Final Code: a staged reveal with boards up. The podium shows stat awards and never a last place.

CONTENT (all Genç groups, through teenSafe)
- YLE and MEB topics: no alcohol, dating, brands, horror or office words.
- B2 Genç means richer concrete language (run out of, look forward to, compound nouns), not abstract idioms.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Answers: concrete picture words (cat, bus, red, pen) of 3-5 letters for Genç and 3-6 for adults. Adult Çark allows 2-3-word chunks with the vowels shown ('I AM HAPPY').
- Lives: Park 8 with the first letter pre-filled; Arena 7; Stüdyo 7.
- Clues:
  - Park and Arena: the picture or emoji is always visible.
  - Stüdyo: the ladder starts with the TR gloss, then defEasy of 10 words or fewer.
- Frame: 'B, please!'.
- Use it: Genç point to the picture among 3 and say it twice; adults use an optional 'I have / I like ___'.
- Text cap for clues: 0-4 words for Genç, 10 for adults.

A2
- Answers: 4-8 letters, now including verbs, adjectives and irregular past forms, with a base-form clue such as '(go)' giving 'went'. Two-word phrases (get up, bus stop). Adult Çark adds 3-5-word unit questions ('What time is it?').
- Lives: Park 8; Arena 7; Stüdyo 7.
- Clues: Park uses the developing Polaroid picture; the adult ladder is defEasy, then the gapped example, then TR.
- Frame: 'Is there a/an __?', with a/an shown under each key.
- Use it: Genç use 'I like / I can / I have ___'; adults make an optional sentence.
- Text cap: 8 words for Genç, 15 for adults.

B1
- Answers: 6-10 letters, abstract nouns, phrasal verbs, collocations and functional phrases ('Can I borrow your eraser?' for Genç, 'Could you send me the file?' for adults). Short sentences up to 30 characters in Çark.
- Lives: 6.
- Clues: TR off by default (a teacher toggle), and the definition costs points. A synonym or collocation rung replaces TR.
- Frames: 'I'd like to buy an E' and 'We'd like to solve'.
- Use it: always runs, one sentence. Optional 'Harf harf çöz'.
- Text cap: 14 words for Genç, 25 for adults.

B2
- Answers:
  - Adults: idioms (idioms.js), proverb halves, and sentences up to 45 characters with the punctuation pre-revealed.
  - B2 Genç: longer concrete phrases (run out of, look forward to, compound nouns), never abstract debate idioms.
- Lives: 6. Only the category is free; no letters are given in Çark.
- Clues: def (Oxford only if it is 18 words or fewer) and the literal-Turkish rung for idioms, both paid.
- Use it: a paraphrase of the meaning, or 'When would you use it?', plus an optional register challenge. The read-aloud solve is judged more strictly on pronunciation.
- Text cap: 20 words for Genç, 40 for adults.

MIXED ABILITY
- 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' inside any group shifts the word-band mix (A2-Kolay is 60% A1 words), the length range (±2 letters), lives (±1) and the free rungs, without changing the skin.
- Kolay also pre-reveals one vowel.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops a whole level for public-school classes whose nominal level is too high.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 5-40: a 5-min warm-up of 3 words; Oyun Parkı 15-25; Arena 15-30; Stüdyo 20-40. A single word puzzle takes 1-2 min; a Çark phrase takes 2-3 min.
catalog.teacherControls:
MODE AND SETUP
- Mode: Kurtar, Çark or Karma. Scene skin per audience. Number of puzzles, or the lesson-fit minutes. Co-op or teams. Turn order.
- 'Last team starts' (Comeback: Off, Light or Strong).

LETTERS AND LIVES
- Lives: 5-10.
- First-letter pre-fill: on or off. 'Reveal a vowel'.
- Picture: visible, developing, or off.
- Keyboard layout: ABC or QWERTY. Letter-name audio: on or off, 0.8x or 1x.
- 'Letters in a row': 1 or 2 in Kurtar; the Çark cap is 3 or none.

CLUES AND SCORING
- Clue ladder: auto-open thresholds and rung prices. The TR rung on or off (immersion). Hide the category label (hard mode).
- Solve penalty and negatives on or off. Wager on or off. 'Harf harf çöz' on or off.
- The Use it! bonus: off, optional or always, with its points.

ÇARK SETTINGS
- The wedge editor: values; PAS, Rüzgâr and İFLAS by the Harshness dial; Joker, Çifte and Task wedges.
- Vowel price. The TV bank rule or 'Herkes kazandığını korusun'. 'Adil çark' or 'Sabit değer'.

TIMERS
- Off, 30 or 40 s, plus +10 s and 'Süresiz'. Team talk length.

CONTENT
- Built-in category, MEB unit, grammar unit, idioms, a pasted list, or an LLM prompt (Turkish is fine).
- 'Gizli kelime': a student or the teacher types a word behind a curtain. With two displays, presenter mode shows the answer only on the laptop.
- Reorder, edit or skip items before the game.

LIVE CONTROLS (on screen and on the physical keyboard)
- Letter keys make guesses. Here the global T-pause shortcut is remapped, because T is a letter.
- Esc: pause. Space: spin. Enter: the solve panel with Correct and Wrong. Backspace: undo the last letter (it restores the life and the score). '?': the next rung. Right arrow: next puzzle. '+': +10 s. Digits 1-6: pick the team in a toss-up.
- Reveal answer, skip puzzle, ±points per team, and 'Almost' for Use it.
- Turkish keyboard: ı and İ map to I; ç ş ğ ö ü show 'not an English letter' and are ignored.

OUTPUT
- The end-of-game glossary: print, or save as a Languago word list.
- Everything is saved to the class profile.
catalog.delightDetails:
- Letters flip in with a typewriter click; each tile bounces once.
- A short suspense drum plays before a letter that occurs 2 or more times, then the host counts in English: 'Three Es!'.
- Kids: balloons pop on a descending marimba scale, so a round is also a little tune. Gogo pairs each letter with a picture word ('B! B for ball!') from the A1 picture set. Gogo sleeps holding a balloon string on the pause screen.
- A2 Genç: the picture 'develops' like a Polaroid with each correct letter and snaps into focus on the solve.
- a/an captions under the keys from A2 ('an F', 'an M', 'a U'). Most classes never realise that letter names take an article by sound.
- Letter-name coach: when the class calls I but the word has E, a gentle 'I /aɪ/ ≠ E /iː/' chip appears. The confusions are logged for the 'Kaçırılanlar' list.
- Misses fall into a 'Not here' tray with an X mark, never shown by colour alone.
- The wheel has real momentum, a ratchet flapper and ticking pegs that slow believably, and a flick sets its speed.
- A 'CLUTCH!' strip in Arena for a solve on the last lock. 'CLEAN SHEET' for a puzzle with no misses.
- One life left: the adult background dims calmly with no flashing, and the kids' last balloon glows gold.
- Word card animation: IPA, a speaker button, syllable dots with a bouncing stress dot, and the example sentence with the word highlighted. A 'Silent K!' badge on knife and knee.
- A category-themed sticker per rescue (a banana for Food, a snowflake for Weather), and a class album page that fills over the term.
- The end screen reads 'We rescued 7 of 9 missions!', with a one-click printable mini-glossary as homework.
catalog.risks:
RANDOM LETTER SPAM (E, T, A)
- Only one letter per turn.
- The solve bonus grows with every still-hidden letter.
- Clue rungs push meaning before letters.
- Use it! and the word card carry the pedagogy.

ONE STRONG TEAM DOMINATING
- Turns rotate after each letter, and the Çark cap is 3.
- The trailing team starts every puzzle, with a Slipstream bonus.
- Stars and points never go negative for Genç groups.

TURKISH CASING AND KEYBOARD
- 'i'.toLocaleUpperCase('tr') gives İ, so normalise with en-US toUpperCase and mark the board lang='en' inside the Turkish layout.
- On a Turkish Q keyboard ı and İ map to I.
- The validator rejects Turkish letters in answers.

LETTER NAMES
- A1 Turkish children say 'e' for I, and they mix up G/J and A/R.
- Recorded letter-name audio (TTS reads a lone 'A' as /ə/), the key shows the letter, the teacher confirms, and the coach chip helps.
- No English voice: 'Öğretmen okur'.

CLUES
- Definitions that leak the answer, and Oxford definitions that are too hard: use a family-stem leak check and defEasy.
- Homographs ('chair' as a verb): show pos on the board.
- Pattern examples ('drink something, ...') are rejected.

MULTI-WORD ANSWERS
- Words are never split across lines, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes are pre-revealed, and row length is capped per audience.

WHEEL RANDOMNESS FRUSTRATING ADULTS
- 'Adil çark' or 'Sabit değer'. İFLAS is off by default.

THEMES THAT UPSET CHILDREN
- No gallows, bombs, sharks or death anywhere. A cute sleeping-dragon skin was deliberately left out for under-10s.

STALLS AND GIVEAWAYS
- A spoken solve is hard to judge in noise: the teacher allows one 'say it again' and may switch on 'Harf harf çöz'.
- The answer must never reach the projector: use the curtain for 'Gizli kelime' and presenter mode with two displays.
- Picture-dependent Genç groups need an imageKey for every item: unpicturable items are dropped, not shown with text.

issues: A1 Genç becomes trivial and unfair. The picture is visible from the start and the first letter is pre-filled, so 'c _ _' next to a cat picture is solved on the first turn by whoever holds it. Turn order, not skill, decides every puzzle, and the Comeback rule hands the trailing team a free solve each time. The solve is spoken ('read it'), so the spelling the mode is meant to practise is never tested.

Shout-outs will leak answers. With 28 children, the moment a word is guessable someone from another team yells it (often in Turkish: 'KEDİ!'). Park rule 3 ('Say I know!') invites shouting, and nothing in the design covers an out-of-turn blurt. Only turn-holders can solve, so a team that knows the word has to wait a whole rotation, and that waiting is exactly when blurting happens.

Very few students are active. Park caps at 4 teams, so 28 children means 7 or more per team. One seat-picked speaker per turn means each child speaks about once or twice in 20 minutes. Air-writing every turn is the only whole-class moment. After about 10 repetitions it turns rote and noisy, and 12-year-olds placed in Park by a teacher who kept the A1/A2 Genç default will find it babyish.

The pacing numbers are optimistic. A Park turn (spinner, letter, teacher tap, letter-name audio, air-write and echo, suspense drum, counting) takes 15-25 s. A 5-7 letter word needs 6-10 turns, and each solve adds Use it, the word card, a double echo and a sticker. A realistic puzzle takes 3-4 minutes, not 1.5, so the lesson-fit timer will overrun and a '20 dk' session will fall short of its planned puzzle count.

The seat-number spinner assumes infrastructure a public school does not have: fixed seat numbers per team, stable team membership, and a no-repeat draw. With 14 per team and a plain random spinner, some children are picked twice and others never. Setting numbers up at the start of the lesson adds 3-5 minutes.

Mini-whiteboards are assumed for Arena Team talk, steals and the Final Code. Most Turkish state classrooms don't have them. Checking 4-6 boards after every wrong solve, then tapping +3 for each team, adds 20-30 s and several clicks per event.

The teacher is standing at a smart board, not at a laptop. The design leans on keyboard shortcuts (Enter, Backspace, '?', arrows, digits), which don't exist there. The on-screen keyboard sits in the bottom third where students tap, so a child can enter a letter while the teacher is talking. Undo exists, but it is one more thing to police.

The mode and dial surface is too large for live use. Kurtar, Çark and Karma each score differently in each of three audiences, with wager, negatives, Harshness, the TV bank rule, the steal toggle and the Harf harf çöz toggle. A teacher who switches classes between lessons won't remember which rules are live. Karma mixes Kurtar points with Çark bank values (e.g. 10s vs 100s), so the Çark final swamps everything before it.

In a big class Çark is mostly waiting: every spin takes 5-8 s of watching, and in Stüdyo the TV bank reset feels arbitrary. For 10 adults it works well. For 28 children it adds dead time on top of an already slow turn cycle.

Letter names are the real bottleneck for A1-A2 children, and the design under-specifies the teacher's call. Children will say 'ce', 'ge', 'je' in Turkish. The coach chip only covers the I/E, G/J and A/R confusions, so it is unclear whether a Turkish-named letter counts, and the teacher mis-hearing a letter in a noisy room happens often.
'Gizli kelime' on a single smart board is not secret: the on-screen keyboard highlights each key as it is pressed, and the class watches the student's hand.

There is no explicit 'stop now' path. The bell rings in the middle of a puzzle and the design has no 'Bitir' button that jumps to the end screen, glossary and album sticker with a fair result. The mandatory co-op final also can't be skipped.

Stüdyo B1-B2 hangman can feel juvenile to adults if it is used for single words. The adult value lies in the phrase, collocation and idiom puzzles, and the design does not steer adult content toward them strongly enough.

The fixed per-puzzle ceremonies (Gogo practice, the multi-occurrence drum, a double echo on every card, stickers) are charming the first time and turn into dead time and fatigue in a second session with the same class.
fixes: For Genç A1 in picture mode, make the core task spelling. Either the picture stays hidden until 2 correct letters are in, or a solve means spelling the word aloud or tapping it out. Better still, when a team solves, every team writes the spelling on paper, and every correct paper earns a star. The turn-holder then gets no free win.

Add a 'Hepimiz yazalım' (everyone writes) moment. At a teacher tap, or automatically after every 3rd hit, every team writes the word on scrap paper and holds it up. Correct teams earn a star or points. This gives a quiet channel for students who know the word, rewards knowing it without blurting, and raises the number of active students.

Add a one-tap blurt rule and button: 'Sızdırıldı! / Leaked'. Tapping it skips to a spare puzzle of the same difficulty, and the answer is only revealed later (no penalty in Park, optional -5 in Arena). Put 'Don't shout the word, write it!' on the pictogram rule card.

Allow 2-6 teams in Park (8 mascots already exist) and recommend 5-6 teams of 4-6 for classes of 25 or more. Replace the random seat spinner with a no-repeat 'bag' per team. Allow 'Sıra ile' (the child next to the last speaker speaks next) so the teacher needs no seat-number setup.

Recalibrate the lesson-fit timer from observed pace. Use defaults of about 3 min per Park puzzle and 2 min per Stüdyo word, measure the class's real pace after puzzle 2, and trim the remaining queue on the fly so the session ends on time.

Keep air-writing, but thin it out: every turn for the first puzzle, then only on misses or new letters, with a toggle. In Arena replace it with 'thumbs up/down if you think it's in the word', which works as a quick whole-class prediction.

Add a large touch-friendly teacher strip that is separate from the student keyboard, e.g. a locked right-edge rail with Correct, Wrong, Undo, Hint, Next, Pause and Finish. Add a 'keyboard lock' toggle so only the teacher can enter letters. Treat keyboard shortcuts as a bonus for laptop use only.
Give the mini-whiteboards a paper fallback (A4 sheets folded per team) and shorten scoring to one tap: select the teams whose boards are correct in a single multi-select, then confirm.

Cut the scope for v1. Ship Kurtar in all three audiences first. Ship Çark only in Stüdyo and Arena with 'Sabit değer' as the default. Drop Karma, or normalise Çark values to the Kurtar scale. Keep Gogo's Çark as a later add-on.

Add a 'letter said in Turkish' tap. It plays the English name, the class echoes it, and the turn still counts, with no penalty. Log it for Kaçırılanlar. Also add a 'Tekrar söyle' (say it again) tap for noisy mis-hearing before the letter is committed.
For 'Gizli kelime' on one screen, blank the on-screen keyboard's key highlights, use password-style dots, or require the laptop's physical keyboard. Presenter mode stays the best option.
Add a permanent 'Bitir' button. It ends the game immediately, shows the end screen with only the puzzles actually played, and makes the finale optional. Keep it a single tap plus confirm.

Save the class profile's history: skip Gogo's practice after the first session, let the teacher mute the recurring ceremonies (drum, double echo) with a 'Hızlı tempo' switch, and avoid words used in the last 3 sessions.
In Stüdyo, default B1-B2 content to multi-word chunks, collocations and idioms, with Phrase Wheel as the default mode, so adults don't meet single-word hangman above A2.

issues: A1 Genç kids who can barely read or spell end up guessing letters at random. English spelling is opaque ('chair', 'knife', 'eight'), so with a full 26-key keyboard, a pre-filled first letter and the picture already showing, a Turkish 9-year-old knows the word but has no way to get from its sound to its letters. They click, they don't learn. The picture is shown from the start, so the meaning challenge is gone too.

The clue ladder for kids puts sound last: picture, then first letter, then 'listen again' after 4 misses. For children who barely read, hearing the word is the most useful clue for spelling it, so it should come first. As designed, the game tests spelling knowledge they don't yet have.

Most students produce very little language. One letter per turn from one seat-picked speaker, in a class of 30 with 4 teams, means a student says one letter name every 10-15 minutes. The whole-class moment is compulsory only in Oyun Parkı. In Arena and Stüdyo it is optional, so most of the class watches between turns.

For B1-B2 adults, guessing letters of a single word has little learning value. The learning sits entirely in Use it! and the word card, which the scoring treats as bonuses. A B2 adult group will find guessing the letters of 'determination' filler. The Çark phrase and sentence puzzles and the idioms are where adults actually get value, but Kurtar is the default mode.

The picture requirement quietly limits content. A1 and A2 Genç drop any item without an imageKey, but none of the listed repo assets (words.js, grammar banks, idioms) includes images. A teacher's LLM prompt ('meslekler ve iş yerleri', a MEB unit) may therefore return almost no playable puzzles for the two groups that need it most. There is no pre-flight count or fallback.

The LLM prompt path is fragile for anything beyond single words. The hangman == true flag, the length caps, the 3-distinct-letter rule, the ban on Turkish letters and the clue-leak checks will reject many LLM items, especially multi-word chunks and idioms. At B2 Genç, 'concrete phrases, not abstract idioms' is hard for an LLM to hold without explicit examples.

The pacing estimates are optimistic for Oyun Parkı. Each puzzle stacks the seat spinner, air-writing, the counting echo, the suspense drum, Use it! (a 3-4 s delay, pointing, saying it twice, acting it out), the word card echoed twice and a sticker burst. A realistic time is 2.5-3.5 min per puzzle, not 1.5, so a '20 dk' setting yields about 6 puzzles, not 12.

The kids variant keeps its 3-rule claim only on paper. Gogo'nun Çarkı, Polaroid development, stirrers and settlers, effort stars, the class album, alternative skins and a co-op final all add procedure the teacher has to run. The 20-second explanation holds, but the teacher's cognitive load does not.

Stüdyo scoring is hard to follow: a value of 50/75/100, minus 10 per rung, plus 10 per hidden letter, plus 10 per life left, plus an optional -20, a wager and +20 for Use it. Adults will not trust a score they cannot predict. The Arena combo of x1.5 on +1 points also produces fractions.

The Çark phrase-read solve depends on the teacher judging intelligibility in a noisy room, and at B2 it is judged 'more strictly' with no criteria. Across teams this is inconsistent and invites disputes among competitive 12-14-year-olds.

A1 adults can feel babyish playing letter-by-letter picture-word hangman, even without a mascot. The Stüdyo A1 ladder starts with the TR gloss, which turns every puzzle into 'translate, then spell': fine for spelling, but it rewards translation over English meaning.

Scope is L with three modes (Kurtar, Çark, Karma), three audience variants, 3-5 skins, a wheel with physics, finals and toss-ups. This is too much for one game in a 10-game suite, and much of the level and age tuning effort is spread across skins instead of the language dials.
fixes: A1 Genç 'Harf Avı' tray: replace the 26-key keyboard with a reduced tray of the word's letters plus 3-4 distractor letters chosen by sound (for 'cat': c, a, t, k, e, o). Letter guessing becomes a sound-to-letter decision the child can actually make. Offer the tray as an option for A2 Genç and A1 adults.

Reorder the kids' ladder: the word is spoken once at the start ('Listen! ... cat'). The picture comes next at A2 Genç (A1 already has it). The first letter is the last free rung. At A1 Genç the listen rung is always on, so the task is 'spell what you hear and see', which is honest phonics practice.

Make the whole-class moment compulsory in every audience, with an age-appropriate form. Park: air-write and echo. Arena: every team writes its predicted next letter on its mini-whiteboard, and a hit scores for all correct boards. Stüdyo: on each hit the class says a word containing that letter pattern. Every student then produces something every turn.

For B1-B2 adults (and B1-B2 Genç), make KARMA or ÇARK with phrase and sentence puzzles the default, and make the definition rung free first ('meaning-first'). Put Use it! inside the solve score (at B levels, a solve without a Use it! sentence scores half), so the language task is not a skippable bonus.

Add a content pre-flight on the setup screen: 'Bu içerikten 14 bulmaca çıktı (3'ü resimsiz olduğu için elendi)'. Offer a self-hosted Twemoji or OpenMoji set as the picture fallback, and have the LLM prompt return an emojiKey chosen from a closed list. If fewer than 6 puzzles survive, suggest widening the category or switching to a built-in one.

For the LLM path, send the level's length caps, the letters-only rule and 3 few-shot examples per level and audience in the prompt, and ask for 1.5x the needed items so the validator has headroom. At B2 Genç, list the allowed phrase kinds (phrasal verbs, compound nouns, fixed phrases from school life) with examples.
Make the lesson-fit timer audience-aware: about 3 min per puzzle in Park, 2 in Arena, 1.5-2 in Stüdyo. Let the teacher collapse Use it! plus the word card into one 20 s step for fast pacing.

Trim the Park variant for v1: drop Gogo'nun Çarkı and the alternative skins, and keep one skin (Balloon Rescue), the stars, the co-op final and one stirrer. Hide the others behind a 'Daha fazla' panel.

Simplify Stüdyo scoring to +10 per letter and a solve worth 10 × the hidden letters + 20, with the running puzzle value always visible on screen ('Şu an çözerseniz: 70'). Use integer combos in Arena (+1 bonus at a streak of 3, +2 at 5).

For read-aloud solves, show a 3-point rubric chip to the teacher (every word said, stress understandable, no missing ending), and let the teacher accept 'Harf harf çöz' as a fallback at every level. At B2, judge only intelligibility, not accent.

For A1 adults, start the ladder with defEasy plus a picture, with TR as a paid last rung. Default A1 adults to short chunks in Çark ('I AM HAPPY', 'SEE YOU') rather than single picture nouns, so it feels like survival English, not kids' spelling.

Cut scope to a medium-sized first release: Kurtar in all three audiences plus the Stüdyo and Arena Çark. Leave out the Park wheel, alternative skins, toss-ups and the wager until the game has been tested in class. Put the saved effort into the reduced letter tray, the audio rungs and content pre-flight, which drive level fit.

issues: Scope is badly underestimated. The spec is two games (Kurtar and Çark) times three audiences, plus Karma, toss-ups, three different finals, wagers, whiteboard steals, Harf harf çöz, presenter mode, a class album, slipstream and comeback, a wedge editor, a harshness dial and 'Adil çark' bags. As written this is XL, not L, and it is the flagship of a 10-game suite. The risk is that nothing ships polished.

Çark mode is a separate game in all but name. It has its own physics wheel, a round bank and a total bank, the TV reset rule, wedge semantics (PAS/Rüzgâr/İFLAS/JOKER/ÇİFTE/Task), a consonant/vowel economy and a spoken-solve judgement. Bundling it doubles the QA matrix (3 audiences x 2 modes x 4 levels) and muddies the Park '3 rules' promise ('Gogo'nun Çarkı' quietly adds wedge meanings: Free letter, Dance break, Everyone +1).

The picture dependency is the biggest asset risk and it has no source. A1/A2 Genç drop every item without an imageKey. The Polaroid rung, Point-and-say pick3 from the distractors' media and 'B for ball' all need a curated image library. words.js has no images, and an LLM prompt ('hayvanlar ama çiftlik hayvanları') will return words the library cannot picture, so teacher-prompted packs for kids will come back half empty.

The audio asset list is large and hidden. It needs 26 recorded letter names (TTS reads a lone 'A' as /ə/, as the spec itself notes) at two speeds, count lines ('Two Es!', 'Three Es!' means count x letter-plural combinations), Gogo voice lines ('Oops! Next mission!', 'B! B for ball!' for every letter), marimba pop notes, a suspense drum, typewriter clicks, a wheel ratchet, chimes and stickers. Without the recordings the kids' version loses most of its charm.

Word-card data is only partly derivable. words.js gives IPA, definition, example and TR, but no syllable split, no reliable stress index for multi-word items and no silent-letter data. The 'Silent K!' badge depends on a 'sound' pack item that won't exist for most words, and the syllable dots will be wrong for many words if they are heuristic.

LLM validity is manageable but not free. defEasy and kid clues leak the answer or its stem (the leak check handles that). Gapped examples use inflected forms ('went' vs 'go'). Multi-word chunks come back with Turkish punctuation or curly apostrophes. The 3-distinct-letter, length-band and teenSafe filters will reject a large share of any generated batch, so one LLM call often yields fewer puzzles than the lesson-fit timer asked for.

Physical keyboard conflicts: Space spins in Çark but is a harmless key in Kurtar, T is remapped, '?' needs Shift on a Turkish Q layout, Backspace inside a focused solve-panel input could undo a letter, and digits 1-6 are overloaded. Smartboards often emit synthetic key events or double taps, so double-entry protection (debounce plus an 'already used' guard) is required.

The spoken solve and the whiteboard steals are judged manually. This is fine pedagogically, but it means the teacher's click is the bottleneck, and the Correct/Wrong UI must be fast and forgiving (undo), or pacing dies in a noisy room.

It overlaps with generic 'guess the word' reveal games. Its distinctiveness rests on the letter-level turn, the clue ladder and the scene skins, so if the skins end up static PNGs with a counter it will feel like Wordwall's Hangman template with Turkish UI.

The multi-skin promise (Balloon, Snowman, Rocket, Vault, Strike lamps, Sandbag balloon, Phone battery, Coffee) is 8 animated scenes. Each needs a lose state, a win state, a last-life state and a per-miss step, which is a lot of SVG animation work for marginal gain.

Saving to a Languago word list needs auth and the Supabase schema, and the class album 'over the term' needs persistent storage. Both are out of scope for a localStorage class profile and create hidden backend work.
fixes: Ship Kurtar only in v1. Split Çark into its own suite entry ('Çarkıfelek'), or merge it with any other wheel or spin candidate in the suite, built on a shared wheel component. Karma comes later, once both exist.

Cut the v1 feature set to the core that makes it great: a letter board with flip and count, a lives scene, the clue ladder (auto in Park, paid in Arena/Stüdyo), a solve panel with Correct/Wrong/Undo, 'Use it!', the word card, the end glossary and the lesson-fit timer. Defer to v2: wagers, toss-ups, whiteboard steals, Harf harf çöz, Final Vault/Final Code, slipstream, the class album and saving to a word list.

One skin per audience at launch: Balloon Rescue (Park), Code Breaker vault (Arena) and Strike lamps (Stüdyo). Build each as a parametric SVG with CSS/WAAPI animations driven by lives/maxLives, so the lives count 5-10 needs no extra art. Add Snowman, Rocket, Battery and Coffee later as data-driven skins on the same interface: render(lives, max), onMiss, onSolve, onFail.

Build a curated picture set before the kids' mode: about 400-600 A1/A2 YLE and MEB nouns and verbs mapped to self-hosted OpenMoji or Twemoji SVGs (check the licence attribution). Store it as imageKey = emoji codepoint. Constrain LLM prompts for picture-dependent groups to choose ONLY from that whitelist (send the list or the category subset in the prompt), and show the teacher 'X kelime resimsiz olduğu için çıkarıldı' with a one-click swap.

The audio budget is one recorded voice pack (about 60 clips): 26 letter names, the numbers 2-6, 'Oops! Next mission!', 'I know!', 5-6 praise lines and a few game-flow cues. Generate 'Two Es!' as two clips, number then letter-plural, or just the number. Use WebAudio-synthesised SFX (marimba notes, clicks, drum roll) instead of sample files to keep size small. TTS only for the word and example sentence, with the 'Öğretmen okur' fallback.

Derive the card's stress from the IPA ˈ mark in words.js. Derive the syllable count from the IPA vowel nuclei, not from spelling, and hide the syllable dots when confidence is low. Ship a small hand-made silent-letter list (knife, knee, write, climb, hour, island...) instead of depending on sound pack items.

The LLM contract: ask only for {term, pos, defEasy, gapSentence, emojiHint?, teenSafe} as JSON. Over-request by 50% (e.g. 18 for a target of 12) because the validator rejects many. Run the deterministic validator (letters-only after normalising curly apostrophes and dashes, length band, ≥3 unique letters, the stem-leak check on defEasy, the gap check that every occurrence is hidden, including inflections via a small lemma map, the Turkish-letter reject). Auto re-request only the shortfall once, then show the teacher a pre-game review list where they can edit or skip. Cache accepted packs per prompt hash to save rate limit.

Input layer: one command dispatcher with a mode-scoped keymap. Letters only when no text input has focus; Space only in the wheel; '?' also bound to H and F1 for Turkish keyboards. Guard against double input: ignore a repeat of the same letter within 400 ms, and used keys are inert. Keep 64px+ on-screen hit targets and pointer events (not click) for smartboards. Put the Undo stack in the reducer so Backspace and the Undo button are the same action.

Architect it as a pure game-state reducer (state, action) → state with a serialisable history, with the renderer separate. That gives Undo, presenter-mode sync over BroadcastChannel (window.open for the second display, with the answer only in the presenter view) and resume after a projector cable glitch essentially for free.

Put the shared suite components into a common module used by all 10 games: the team bar with mascots/emblems, the seat-number spinner, the timer with +10 s/Süresiz, the lesson-fit planner, the audience/level profile, the pause screen, the end-screen podium without a last place, and the glossary print. Otherwise this one game will re-implement half the suite.
Keep the Park rules card to exactly 3 rules and make the optional Gogo wheel a teacher-only variant not offered by default. That keeps the kids checklist honest.

Replace 'save as a Languago word list' with 'Yazdır / PDF' plus a copyable list in v1, and add the Supabase save later behind login. Keep the class album in localStorage with export/import JSON so a lost browser does not lose the term's stickers silently.

catalog.rankReason: Requested (Hangman), with feasibility 8 and balanced appeal (adult 7.3, teen 7.7). v1 ships Kurtar only, on a shared word-tile component that c15 and c30 reuse later: a letter board, a friendly lives scene (never a gallows), the clue ladder, the solve panel, 'Use it!' and a word card. A1 Genç gets the 'Harf Avı' tray (the word's letters plus distractors chosen by sound) instead of 26 keys. The word is spoken first and the picture waits until 2 letters are in. 'Hepimiz yazalım' gives every team a write-and-show moment and ends the shouting. The Çarkıfelek mode becomes v2 on c11's wheel component. The adult Word Vault drops definition clues so it stays distinct from c30.

catalog.name: İsim-Şehir STOP! (Category Rush)
catalog.familiarAs: İsim-Şehir-Hayvan / Scattergories / Stop the Bus
catalog.oneLiner: This is the İsim-Şehir-Hayvan game every Turkish student already knows, played in English. A letter is drawn from a pool that is guaranteed to be playable, and teams write one word for each category at their level. Any team can call STOP. Every answer is checked live against the word bank, which shows a level badge, the Turkish meaning and 'Did you mean…?'. Unique answers score double, and after each column the class learns the words nobody found.
catalog.howItPlays:
0) SETUP (teacher, about 1 minute). The group chip sets the profile line, e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk'. The teacher then picks a category source:
- a built-in preset: 'Klasik İsim-Şehir' = A name · A city or country · An animal · A plant or food · A thing
- a topic pack (Food & drink, School, Home, Travel, Work…)
- a MEB unit pack (e.g. '6. sınıf · Yummy Breakfast')
- computed 'twist' columns
- a typed prompt ('hayvanlar ve yetenekleri' → 'An animal that can swim', 'An animal that can fly'…)
The columns appear as swappable cards. Under them the PLAYABLE LETTER POOL updates live: 'Bu kategorilerle 11 harf oynanabilir: B C D F G H M P R S T'. Each letter has a dot: green = 5+ answers at the level in every column; amber = only 2-4 in at least one column. Swapping a thin column (e.g. Colour) visibly widens the pool. Printable A4 sheets are optional; each has a red STOP paddle on the back.

1) LETTER (10-15 s). The teacher taps Spin (or Space).
- The skinned wheel draws a letter, weighted by coverage. A letter never repeats within a game, and used letters stamp along the top.
- The letter is said by its ENGLISH NAME ('G, /dʒiː/!') and the class repeats it once. This drills the letter names Turkish learners mix up (G/J, E/I, A/E).
- The teacher may type a letter manually instead. Any column that is thin for that letter then becomes a ★ Bonus column: it may be left empty when calling STOP.

2) WRITE (60-150 s by level and audience).
- One box per column per team. Teams write on the shared sheet, a mini-whiteboard or a phone.
- Rules: the answer must start with the letter (articles are ignored); one answer per box; the team agrees quietly. Writing is the team-talk phase.
- The round clock is skinned per audience and is never red for kids. Keys: T pause, +10 s, Süresiz.
- 'Stuck help': if at half-time many boxes are blank, the teacher taps İpucu and a CLASS-WIDE hint appears for every column (a silhouette for kids, 'B _ _ _ _' for Arena, a Turkish gloss for adults). The hint is shown to everyone, so it stays fair.

3) STOP.
- A team that has filled every box (★ Bonus columns may stay empty) holds up its red STOP paddle, or presses STOP on its phone.
- The teacher taps STOP or presses S, so nobody needs to shout in a loud room.
- A 'STOP!' stamp appears in that team's colour. Everyone else gets '5-4-3-2-1 Pens down!'. A clock that runs out ends the round the same way.
- STOP earns no speed points; its only advantage is ending the round.
- A too-early STOP is handled per audience: kids hear 'Oops, keep writing!'; the adult Clean/Dirty STOP rule is applied at scoring.

4) CHECK (the heart of the game; one column at a time).
The screen spotlights a column, e.g. '🐾 An animal · B'. A seat-number spinner picks the reader in the starting team (the starting team rotates each column; nobody is picked by name). The reader says the answer and, if asked, spells it with English letter names.
- PAPER MODE: the teacher types 2-3 letters and taps the autocomplete chip. Chips come from that column's byLetter list plus the word bank, so each distinct word is typed only once. The card lands on the board and the app asks 'Who else has BEAR?'. Every team with the same word holds up its sheet (kids stand up), and the teacher taps their chips (keys 1-8) onto the card, which makes it a shared answer. The next team reads a word that is not yet on the board. This is a whole-class response moment every turn.
- PHONES MODE: answers are already collected, normalised and grouped. Readers still read them aloud.
Every card gets an instant status:
- ✓ In the pack or bank: level badge (A1…C2), Turkish gloss (toggle), picture or emoji, speaker button.
- ~ Close spelling: 'Did you mean giraffe?' It is scored by the spelling dial. The correct spelling is shown big and read aloud, and the class spells it together.
- ? Not in the bank: the VAR button (a football-style replay mini-animation) asks the LLM validator whether the word is real, fits the column, and how it is spelled, with a short Turkish reason. The teacher always makes the final tap: Kabul / Yarım / Ret. Accepted words go into the class's 'Onaylı kelimeler' list and are auto-accepted next time.
- ✗ Wrong letter, wrong column, or a Turkish word, with the reason shown: 'balık → fish'; 'cat is an animal, not a food'.
Keys: A accept, H half, R reject, V VAR, U undo, Enter next column.

5) SCORE. The İsim-Şehir convention: a unique valid answer = 10, a shared one = 5, blank or invalid = 0. Unique cards glow gold with an 'Only you!' tag, and each team's score rolls up at the end of the column. House-rule toggles cover regional habits: 'Tek yazan 20' (you are the only team with any answer in the column) and 'Sadece özgün' (1 point for unique answers only). Audience variants below change the currency (stars, points with combos, points with bonuses).

6) LEARN (20-30 s per column; toggle). Before moving on, the screen reveals 4-6 more valid words for that letter and column that nobody wrote. They favour the group's level and come with a picture, Turkish (toggle) and audio. The class repeats each one chorally. Arena and Stüdyo first get a 10-s HUNT: any team may hold up one extra valid word that is not on the board, for +3.

7) SPEAK (B1 and up). After the last column, each team picks its best unique word, and the spinner-chosen member uses it in a correct sentence for +5. Challenges happen during CHECK (rules per audience below).

8) NEXT ROUND. Comeback (Light): the trailing team picks the next letter from 3 feasible letters the wheel offers, or swaps one column. There are 3 rounds for kids and 4-5 for adults; the lesson-fit timer suggests the number.

9) FINALE.
- The audience-specific ending: titles, a podium with stat awards, or full scores plus 'Kaçırılanlar'.
- The Word Wall shows every accepted word from the game. Tapping a word gives IPA, TTS and the example sentence.
- Export: a PDF homework list, or 'Bu kelimelerle oyna', which sends the class's own words as a vocab pack to Hangman, Memory or Kelime Oyunu.

WHO DOES WHAT
- The teacher: spins, taps STOP, types or taps answers, and makes the final call.
- Students: write in teams, read, spell, stand up or hold up sheets for shared answers, repeat new words, defend challenges.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Teams: 2-6 teams of 2-5 on a projector, or up to 8 teams in phones mode or peer-check mode. In crowded public-school rooms, each row is a team and shares one printed A4 sheet or a mini-whiteboard.
- Screen: the teacher's laptop drives the projector.
- Phones (optional): one phone per team via a room code. This suits adults and private courses; Oyun Parkı defaults to paper because of school phone rules.
- Individual mode: small adult classes of up to 10 players, one sheet each.
- Readers: during checking, the reader is picked by a seat-number spinner (kids, Arena) or by a rotating spokesperson (adults). Nobody is ever named.
- Team identity per skin: animal mascots (Oyun Parkı), emblem + colour + 3-word motto picked in 10 s (Arena), or city, coffee or grammar-pun team names (Stüdyo).
catalog.contentShape:
PRIMARY: 'category-list' items, one per column:
- label (EN, 4 words or fewer; A1 Genç shows a picture plus 1 word)
- labelTr
- media.emoji, plus an imageKey from the self-hosted SVG set (required for Genç)
- open (bool): for columns like 'A reason to be late' or 'A name', any valid answer counts, the teacher judges, and members are only examples
- members[{text, alt[], level, tr}] (8-40)
- byLetter (computed)
- minPerLetter (feasibility threshold: kids 3, adults 2)
- multiWord (bool)

SESSION DATA, computed by code:
- letterPool {letter: {minCount across the chosen columns, dot: green|amber, weight}}
- bonusColumns per letter (columns that are thin for that letter)
- usedLetters

WHERE THE MEMBERS COME FROM
(1) Built-in curated sets:
- Kids: YLE Starters/Movers/Flyers topics and MEB grade 2-8 units, each with a picture. This supplement is REQUIRED, because words.js is Oxford-based and lacks many children's nouns (giraffe, zebra, tiger, penguin, kite, hippo and crayon are all absent).
- Adults: life and work sets (travel, work, hotel complaints, personality…).
- Places: an English exonym list of countries, cities and nationalities (Germany, not 'Almanya'; both Istanbul and İstanbul; both Turkey and Türkiye).
(2) Computed twist columns, built by code from words.js: the p field for part of speech, the level lists a1..c2, suffix regexes and syllable counts. Examples: 'A noun ending in -ment' (B2), 'A verb ending in -ize', 'A word with 3 syllables', 'An adjective ending in -ful'.
(3) LLM prompt output: 4-8 categories with 12-40 members each. Code then:
- checks every member against words.js and the YLE lists (the word exists; its level is at most the group level + 1)
- runs the teenSafe filter for Genç groups
- enforces the label cap
- drops any category that meets minPerLetter for fewer than 6 letters

LINKED 'vocab' ITEMS feed Learn, the Word Wall and the answer cards: term, alt[] (UK/US spellings, plurals), pos, media.emoji, defEasy, defTr, example, ipa. These are mapped from words.js {w, p, d, e, i, t}, and from the YLE supplement for kid words.

VAR VALIDATOR RESULT, cached per (word, categoryId): {isEnglish, realWord, fitsCategory, correctSpelling?, reasonTr (90 chars or fewer)}.

NORMALISATION, applied before duplicates are grouped:
- lower-case and trim
- strip a/an/the
- fold Turkish keyboard letters (İ→I, ı→i)
- plural→singular via alt[] and rules
- UK/US pairs (colour/color, grey/gray, pyjamas/pajamas)
- hyphen/space variants (ice-cream = ice cream)
- LETTER RULE: the first letter of the first word, after articles, must match. In the 'Son harf' variant, the last letter of the last word must match.
- REVERSE LOOKUP on words.js t (the Turkish gloss) to spot answers written in Turkish and show their English equivalent.

LOCAL CLASS DATA, per class profile: approvedWords[{text, categoryId, by: teacher|VAR}], rejectedWords, the rarest word of each game, and album stickers.
skills: spelling (including English letter names for spelling aloud)
speaking (reading aloud, challenge defences, sentence bonus)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO 'Category Rush': an editorial quiz-night look (cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme), system sans, no mascot and no voice lines, and a neutral caption such as 'Round 2 · Letter M'. The letter comes from a slot-machine wheel with ticking pegs and a slow-down, with woodblock ticks and a piano chime. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').

COLUMNS: 6-8 per round, including one twist column. The categories are lexical and functional:
- A job; Something you do at work; Something you pack for a business trip; A reason to be late; Something you'd complain about in a hotel
- An adjective for a person (B1); A collocation with make/do (B1-B2); A phrasal verb with 'up' (B2); A noun ending in -tion/-ment (B2)
- Country + nationality (both halves must be right: 'Greece / Greek')
Open columns such as 'A reason to be late' are judged by the teacher. Multi-word answers are allowed where the column says so, and phrasal verbs are checked as whole chunks.

CLOCK: 60-90 s, or STOP mode with a 120 s cap. The clock is optional; T pauses it.

SCORING
- 10 / 5 / 0.
- LEVEL-UP +5 for a correct word above the group's level (by the words.js band).
- CLEAN STOP: +5 if every answer of the stopping team is valid, otherwise 0. The 'Dirty STOP −5' toggle is off by default.
- Minus points for invalid answers: optional, off by default.

CHALLENGE: once per team per round. The owner of a doubtful answer has 10 s to use it in a correct sentence (lexical columns) or to justify it ('Why is that a good reason to be late?').
- If the defence holds, the defender gets +5.
- If it fails, that answer scores 0.
- An optional −5 for a failed challenge is off by default.

OTHER RULES
- SPEAKING BONUS: each team's best unique word in a sentence, +5.
- HUNT: +3 for an extra valid word before the Learn reveal.
- Hint ladder in phones mode: a Turkish gloss hint for one column costs 2 points.

VARIANTS
- 'Son harf': the answer must END with the letter.
- 'İçinde': the answer must contain a letter pair such as 'TR'.
- 'İki harf': the answer must start with a two-letter combination (B2).
- '6+ harf': answers need at least 6 letters.
- 'Collocation grid': every column is a verb (make / do / take / have) and answers must collocate with it.
- A final 'Double round': all points count twice.
- Individual mode for small groups.

PACING: 4-5 rounds of 5-7 minutes, 20-35 minutes in total.

ENDING: a modest finale with full scores and each team's best word with its level badge. It also shows the 'Rarest word of the night', the teacher's crown for 'Sınıfın en yaratıcı cevabı', and the 'Kaçırılanlar' list (the best valid words nobody found in each round) as a review list or PDF. Effects are a 0.6 s chime with the score rolling up.
catalog.teenVersion:
TWO SKINS WITH DIFFERENT RULES, not one skin recoloured.

A) OYUN PARKI 'HARF TRENİ' (Letter Train)
Ages 9-11; the default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç.

LOOK: a warm palette on cream, rounded shapes, an Andika-type font and animal team mascots (Panda, Fox, Lion, Frog…). A little train chugs across the screen. The carriage door opens, Gogo the parrot hops out holding the letter card and says 'B! B… B for bear!', and the class repeats it.

COLUMNS: 3-5 big picture headers from the SVG set, each with a one-word English label: 🐾 Animal, 🍎 Food, 👕 Clothes, 🎨 Colour, ✏️ School thing, 🚗 Vehicle, 🧸 Toy, 👪 Family, 🏠 Home.

THREE RULES, read from the Turkish rule card with pictograms in under 20 s. Gogo first demos them in an unscored 30-s practice round.
1) Write, or draw, one thing for each picture. It must start with the letter.
2) All boxes full? Hold up the STOP paddle! Everyone: 5 seconds, pens down.
3) A right word = 1 star. A word no other team has = 2 stars.

STARS AND FAIRNESS
- Unique words get a gold 'Only you!' sticker.
- 'Draw it & say it' (A1 Genç only): a drawing counts as 1★ if the team can say the word.
- Close spelling earns the full star at A1 Genç, but the correct spelling appears big, Gogo spells it with English letter names and the class spells along.
- Stars never go down. There is no STOP penalty ('Oops, keep writing!'), no team-vs-team challenges and no minus points.

WRONG ANSWER: a soft marimba 'boing', then a second try. The team may offer another word orally, with the picture hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo says a correct word ('Banana! B, banana!'), the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album (it does not count towards the win).

WHOLE-CLASS MOMENTS EVERY TURN
- choral letter names
- 'Stand up if you wrote it too!' for shared words
- choral repeats of every accepted word and of the Learn words
- a TPR option for animal and action words ('Show me a bear!')

CLOCK: off by default; the round ends on STOP or when the teacher taps 'Pens down'. When it is on, it runs 150 s: the train slowly crosses a track at the top, calm and never red. The last 10 s are a soft whistle, and a marimba chime sounds on arrival.

LETTERS: computed from the kid picture lists, usually B C D F G H M P R S T. Q, X, Z, Y and J are never used by default.

HINTS (free): tap a picture header and Gogo shows a silhouette for the whole class.

CLASS GOAL: if the class together finds 12 or more different words in a round, the whole class earns a sticker for the Word Garden.

PACING: 3 rounds of 4-6 minutes, with a 45-s stirrer between rounds ('Gogo says: find something blue in the room!'), 15-20 minutes in total.

ENDING
- Every team gets a title: Super Finders (most words), Only-You Stars (most unique), Best Spellers, Brave Artists (most drawings).
- The round letters become stickers in the class album ('We played B, M, S!').
- The Word Garden grows every accepted word as a flower in its team's colour.
- Confetti in team colours AND shapes appears only at the finale. Every effect lasts 2 s or less, and reduced motion replaces it with a static stamp.

SHEET: A4 landscape with picture headers, big boxes with handwriting lines and a draw box under each word box. It carries the team's mascot, the theme name and a school-logo field, with the red STOP paddle on the back.

B) ARENA 'LETTER LOCK'
Ages 12-14; the default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç, suggested for any Genç group at grade 6+ or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor'.

LOOK: dark navy with neon team colours, a condensed display font, and geometric emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond). In 10 s teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. The game is framed as 'Category Rush · Match 1'. There is no mascot; a commentator strip shows 'ONLY YOU', 'RARE FIND' or 'COMBO x3', at most once per team per column. The letter is cracked like a vault: three reels spin and lock one after another, ending on 'LETTER LOCKED: M'.

RULES
- 5-6 columns with emoji headers and short English labels.
- A 90 s ring in the team's colour. STOP triggers a 5-s countdown.
- 'Clean STOP' (all boxes valid) earns a stat, not points, because there are no speed points.

SCORING
- 10 / 5 / 0 with a floor at 0.
- STREAK: consecutive valid answers across columns and rounds, based on accuracy only. 3 in a row = x1.5, 5 in a row = x2. A blank or invalid answer breaks the streak and costs nothing.
- HUNT: +3 for an extra valid word before the Learn reveal.
- Green luck only. The Yellow opt-in adds 'Steal the word': offer a valid replacement for another team's rejected answer and win +3; the other team loses nothing.

CHALLENGE TOKENS: 2 per team per match. The spinner-picked member of the challenged team defends the word in a sentence within 15 s (or by mime and explanation at lower levels).
- If the defence fails, the answer scores 0 and the challenger keeps its token.
- If the defence holds, the challenger loses the token.
- Nobody loses points.

HINTS: the class-wide 'B _ _ _ _' stuck help is free. In phones mode a team may buy a private hint for 2 points, never going below 0.

CONTENT: YLE / Key-for-Schools topics. B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics: an adjective ending in -ful, a phrasal verb with 'up', a job ending in -er/-ist, something in a science lab, a sport plus play/go/do. There are no adult domains (office, salary, rent).

ENDING: a podium with stat awards: Rare Hunter (most unique), Longest Streak, Clean STOP, Comeback, Best Sentence. There is never a last place. Effects are 1.2 s or less, with synth stings.

BOTH SKINS
- The group label never appears on screen.
- Every column passes the teenSafe filter (no brands, alcohol, dating, violence…). Drinks become 'A drink for breakfast'.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1 (A1 Genç: 3-4 picture columns; A1 adults: 4 columns)
- Columns: only concrete nouns. Genç: Animal, Food, Colour, Toy/Clothes. Adults: Food & drink, A job, Something in a house, A country.
- Letters: minPerLetter = 3 within the A1 band plus YLE Starters, usually 9-11 easy letters.
- Clock: 150 s for kids (off by default), 120 s for adults.
- Spelling: Cömert for Genç (close spelling is full credit and is corrected aloud); Yarım for adults (close spelling = half).
- Drawing is allowed (Genç only). Single words only.
- The Turkish gloss is shown after each check. No challenges and no sentence bonus. Prompts are a picture plus 1 word for Genç, and 10 words or fewer for adults.

A2 (Genç: 4-5 columns; adults: 5)
- Adds a verb column with a pictogram ('Something you do': daily routines), Clothes, Place in town, Job, and adjective opposites.
- Letters: minPerLetter = 3 across the A1+A2 bands.
- Clock: 120 s for Genç, 100 s for adults.
- Spelling: Yarım for both, since Movers and Key expect correct spelling.
- Two-word answers are allowed in labelled columns (ice cream, bus stop). Drawing is off unless 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' is on.
- The Turkish gloss is shown after checking. Challenges are 'show it' only (mime or point).

B1 (Genç: 5-6 columns; adults: 6-7)
- Columns: a personality adjective, a free-time activity (-ing), a phrasal verb (with the particle given), a travel item. Genç add 'Something in your school bag'; adults add 'Something you do at work' and one open column ('A reason to be late').
- Letters: minPerLetter = 2.
- Clock: 90 s.
- Spelling: Katı (strict); UK/US spellings and plurals are always accepted.
- Challenges must be defended in a sentence. The sentence bonus of +5 is on, and adults get the Level-up +5.
- The Turkish gloss is hidden until the teacher toggles it.

B2 (Genç: 6-7 concrete columns; adults: 8)
- Columns: collocations with make/do/take, word formation (-ment, -tion, -ness, -ful/-less), phrasal verbs with up/out, and twist columns (3 syllables, ends with). Adults add animal idioms from idioms.js.
- Letters: a wider pool, with V, W and K allowed.
- Clock: 60-90 s.
- Spelling: strict. A challenge must be defended.
- The 'Son harf', 'İçinde' and '6+ harf' variants are unlocked.
- Level-up applies only to B2 and higher words. The Turkish gloss is off by default (immersion).

MIXED ABILITY ('Kolay / Orta / Zor', which never changes the skin)
- Kolay: shifts feasibility and the Learn words towards the band below (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words). Each column header shows one model answer with a different letter, and spelling and drawing are one step more generous.
- Zor: removes the model answers and adds one column above the level.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır': drops the whole content profile one level, because MEB's nominal levels often overstate public-school classes.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Kids (Oyun Parkı): 15-20 minutes, 3 fixed rounds. Arena: 15-25 minutes. Adults (Stüdyo): 20-35 minutes, 4-5 rounds. A round takes 4-7 minutes: about 15 s for the letter, 60-150 s of writing, 2-4 minutes of checking and 30 s for Learn. The lesson-fit timer sizes the number of rounds and columns.
catalog.teacherControls:
CONTENT
- Category source: a built-in preset (Klasik İsim-Şehir, topic packs, MEB unit packs), computed twist columns, or a typed prompt (Turkish or English).
- Column editor: swap, reorder, 3-8 columns, open or closed, multi-word on/off.
- A live preview of the playable letter pool with green and amber dots.
- Letter pool: exclude letters, type a letter manually (thin columns become ★ Bonus), no repeats.

TIMING AND ROUNDS
- Clock on/off and its length; +10 s, T pause, Süresiz.
- STOP mode: paddle plus teacher key (S), phones, or off (timer only).
- Number of rounds, suggested by lesson fit.

SCORING
- House scoring: 10/5/0, 'Tek yazan 20', 'Sadece özgün 1/0', optional minus points.
- Clean/Dirty STOP toggle, Level-up bonus, Hunt, sentence bonus.
- Challenge rule: off, tokens, or once per round; optional −5 for a failed challenge.

CHECKING
- Spelling dial: Cömert / Yarım / Katı. Drawing on/off.
- Turkish gloss: shown after the check, hidden until tapped, or off.
- Checking mode:
  - read everything aloud
  - 'check 2 columns aloud, peer-check the rest' (sheets swap clockwise and the screen lists the accepted words for each column)
  - phones auto-collect
- VAR on/off (it uses the LLM).
- One-tap Kabul / Yarım / Ret, and Undo (keys A, H, R, U, V, 1-8).
- Edit the class's 'Onaylı kelimeler' list.
- Learn step on/off, with 3-6 words.

TEAMS, OUTPUT AND AUDIENCE
- Team names, colours, mascots or emblems.
- Printing: A4 sheets with team name, theme and a school-logo field, plus the STOP paddle.
- Export: the Word Wall as a PDF homework list, or send it as a pack to Hangman, Memory or Kelime Oyunu.
- Audience override: skin, Nazik, any single dial, the Kolay/Orta/Zor dial and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır', saved to the local class profile.
catalog.delightDetails:
FAMILIAR ON DAY ONE
- The 'Klasik İsim-Şehir' preset (Name · City/Country · Animal · Plant/Food · Thing) makes it familiar instantly, so there is almost nothing to explain.
- The city and country column quietly teaches English names for places (Almanya → Germany, Yunanistan → Greece).

LETTER REVEAL
- The letter always arrives with its English name, and the class repeats it.
- A different reveal per skin: Gogo's letter train (kids), a neon vault with three locking reels (Arena), a slot-machine wheel with ticking pegs and a slow-down (adults).
- Used letters stamp along the top of the screen.

STOP AND VAR
- STOP is a printed red paddle, not shouting.
- A huge 'STOP!' stamp in the stopping team's colour. The sound is skinned: a friendly marimba train toot for kids, never a buzzer; a synth sting for Arena; a woodblock for adults.
- The dispute button is a football-style VAR with a mini replay animation (kids get 'Gogo checks the big book').

SCORING MOMENTS
- Unique answers glow gold with an 'Only you!' tag.
- 'Did you mean giraffe?' spelling rescues, with the class spelling aloud together.
- Turkish answers are caught kindly: 'balık → fish'.
- A running 'Rarest word of the day'. The teacher can crown 'Sınıfın en yaratıcı cevabı'.

THE CLASS'S OWN WORDS
- The Learn reveal shows the words nobody found, with pictures and audio.
- The end screen shows each team's best word with its level badge.
- The class Word Wall becomes a Word Garden for kids. It exports as a PDF homework list or as a playable pack for other games, so the words the class produced become their next game.
- Teacher-approved words are remembered next time.

PRINT AND PACE
- The printable sheet (picture headers, draw boxes, theme name, school-logo field) can go into the class portfolio.
- The last 10 s get a soft whistle (kids) or a team-colour pulse (Arena), never a red alarm.
- 'Stuck help' makes sure no team stares at a blank sheet. A class goal sticker lets kids win together.

ACCESSIBILITY: every sound lasts 1 s or less and is loudness-normalised. Reduced motion replaces every effect with a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- CHECKING IS SLOW (6 teams × 6 columns). Mitigations: each distinct word is typed once with autocomplete, shared answers are claimed by hands up, keyboard shortcuts, the 'check 2 aloud, peer-check the rest' mode, phones mode, and fewer columns for bigger classes. The lesson-fit timer warns when teams × columns won't fit.
- THIN LETTER/COLUMN PAIRS (e.g. Colour, or U at A1). Only letters that meet minPerLetter in every column are drawn. The setup preview shows how a thin column shrinks the pool, and a manually chosen letter turns thin columns into ★ Bonus.
- GAPS IN words.js. It is Oxford-based and misses many children's nouns (giraffe, zebra, tiger, penguin, kite, crayon and hippo are absent). A curated YLE/MEB picture supplement is required, and 'not in the bank' must never auto-reject; it goes to VAR or the teacher.
- LLM VALIDATOR latency, errors and rate limits. Results are cached per word and column, VAR times out after about 4 s to 'Öğretmen karar verir', and the teacher always has the final tap. Prompt-generated columns are validated against the banks and dropped if they are not feasible.
- DISPUTES OVER OPEN COLUMNS. Examples are shown on the column card, the teacher judges with one tap, and challenges have clear time limits.
- PHONES USED AS DICTIONARIES. A phones-away rule sits on the rules screen. In phones mode, input fields turn off autocorrect, autocomplete and spellcheck.
- NOISE AROUND STOP. The paddle plus the teacher's key and a visual countdown. Copying between neighbouring teams: seat teams apart, or give each team its own letter row in individual mode.
- NORMALISATION PITFALLS: Turkish keyboard İ/ı, plurals, UK/US spellings, hyphens, proper-noun capitals, articles, multi-word answers and phrasal verbs.
- DISCOURAGEMENT. Strict spelling or blank sheets can discourage weak groups. Mitigations: the spelling dial, the Kolay dial, stuck help, the effort-star album, and letting the trailing team pick the letter.
- teenSafe. Prompt-generated columns for Genç groups must pass the filter, so there are no adult domains or brands.

issues: The time budget for the kids' class is wrong. With 28 students there are 7 row-teams and 4 columns, so 28 answers per round have to be read, typed or tapped, and the 'who else?' stand-ups resolved. Realistically each column takes 60-90 s, so checking takes 4-6 min. Add about 2.5 min for writing and 2 min for Learn and it comes to 9-10 min per round. Three rounds is about 30 min, not the stated 15-20. The lesson-fit timer will keep cutting to 2 rounds, or the teacher will skip Learn, which is the best part.

Checking is dead time. While one team's reader speaks, the other 6 teams (24 kids) only wait for the 'stand up if you wrote it too' moment. At 10-12 years old, attention goes after about 40 s and the room gets loud. The checking phase is the chaos hotspot, not STOP.

One scribe does the work. A row-team of 4-7 kids sharing one A4 sheet means one fast writer holds the pen and writes everything, while 3-6 kids are passive or chatting. This is the biggest fairness and activity problem in a public-school room. 'The team agrees quietly' will not happen; the strongest student will just decide.

Honesty problem in shared claims. When the app asks 'Who else has BEAR?', kids will stand up without having written it. From the board the teacher cannot check 7 sheets. Because shared = 1★ and blank = 0, fake claims pay off, and within two rounds they become the class norm.

The STOP race favours the strongest team every round. The same fast team fills its boxes in 50 s and cuts everyone else off after a 5-s countdown.
