'No speed points' does not fix this, because ending the round early is itself the reward, and the weak teams are left with blanks every round. Letting the trailing team pick the letter is too weak a comeback.

The smart-board input model conflicts with itself. Paper mode relies on typing 2-3 letters plus the single-key shortcuts A/H/R/U/V/S/T and 1-8. On a smart board the teacher uses touch and an on-screen keyboard. Worse, if the autocomplete field has focus, pressing 'A' to accept types an 'a'. A standing teacher cannot type quickly on an on-screen keyboard while 28 kids wait.
Drawings (A1 Genç 'Draw it & say it') cannot be judged from the board. The teacher has to walk to each row to see the drawing, which multiplies the checking time and leaves the board unattended.

Spelling aloud with English letter names, while useful, is a time sink and makes weak readers freeze in front of 27 peers. Picking the reader with a seat-number spinner also means the weakest student is regularly put on the spot for their team's score.

Printing and props are assumed. Many public schools cannot print colour A4 sheets and red STOP paddles every lesson. Without a fallback, setup either fails or turns into 5 min of drawing grids on the board.

Peer-check mode breaks the scoring model. If sheets swap and teams mark each other, the app never learns which answers were unique or shared, so the 10/5/0 system and the 'Only you!' moments cannot be computed unless every word is still entered.

The teacher faces too many settings. The setup has more than 20 dials: source, column editor, letter pool, clock, STOP mode, 5 scoring toggles, challenge rule, spelling dial, gloss mode, checking mode, VAR, Learn, Hunt, Speak, streak, audience, Kolay/Orta/Zor. A teacher 3 minutes before class, or between lessons in a 10-minute break, will not get through it. The '1 minute' setup claim only holds with a one-tap preset.

There is feature pile-up during play. Arena alone has streaks, Hunt, challenge tokens, steals, private hints, Clean STOP stats, the commentator strip and Learn. Each extra step adds 10-30 s per column plus more for the teacher to track. Hunt ('any team may hold up one extra word') produces a shouting burst in a room of 28.

Stopping in the middle is not specified. A bell mid-check leaves a half-scored round. There is no 'finish now: score only the checked columns and go to the podium' path, and in a public school the bell does not wait.
Unique scoring causes noise and copying in both directions. Teams whisper, but neighbouring rows overhear, and in crowded rooms with rows as teams, 'seat teams apart' is impossible.
The class-wide silhouette hint hands every team the same word. The column then turns into all-shared answers, which quietly kills the 'Only you!' moment the scoring is built around.

Adults (10 people): mostly smooth. The main risks are the open columns ('A reason to be late') leading to slow debates, and the challenge and VAR rituals running long. Individual mode with 10 players and 6-8 columns means 60-80 answers to check per round, which is too slow read one by one aloud.
Replayability and familiarity are excellent (letters × columns × packs), so setup cost is paid off over many lessons. That is a genuine strength.
fixes: Rotate column ownership to kill the one-scribe problem. Each team member owns one column: seat 1 writes Animal, seat 2 writes Food, and so on, and the others may only whisper help. The sheet prints seat numbers on the column headers, and ownership rotates each round. With 5-7 per row, extra members get the 'spell-checker' and 'STOP holder' jobs. The reader in CHECK is that column's owner, so everyone speaks once per round.

Replace sequential reading with a 'Sheets up!' simultaneous reveal per column for Oyun Parkı and big classes. The app says 'Show your ANIMAL!' and all teams hold up a mini-whiteboard or sheet at once, which is itself a whole-class moment. The screen then shows a pre-built TAP GRID: the 12-20 most likely valid words for this letter and column as big touch tiles, plus a '+ other' tile. The teacher taps each team's word, and the team colour chips auto-appear, so there is no typing. Shared or unique falls out of what was shown, which also ends fake stand-up claims.

Make the touch-first control surface the default. Big Kabul / Yarım / Ret / Geri al buttons in a bottom bar reachable at standing height (hand zone at 1.2-1.5 m on the board). Single-key shortcuts only work when no text field has focus, and are shown only when a physical keyboard has been used. Add a 'remote' option: the teacher's phone as a clicker via a room code.

Protect the STOP race in Nazik mode and optionally elsewhere. STOP unlocks only after a minimum time (for example 50% of the level clock). After STOP the others get 15 s instead of 5. A team that STOPped this round cannot STOP next round ('Rest the paddle'). Or kids can use 'Class STOP': the round ends when 3 teams, or half the teams, have raised paddles.

Add a real scoring comeback. In kids mode the team with the fewest stars in a round gets a guaranteed 'bonus column' of its choice next round, or each column's first unique answer from the trailing team counts as 3★. Show only team titles at the end, never a ranked total, which the design already half-does.

Use a 'Hızlı Başla' one-tap preset per audience (for example '28 kişilik sınıf · 4 sütun · kâğıt · Harf Treni'), with the full dial panel under 'Gelişmiş'. The lesson-fit timer should adjust the column count to class size and minutes BEFORE the game starts: 7 teams → 3-4 columns and 2-3 rounds.

Add 'Şimdi bitir': at any moment, score the checked columns only, skip Learn and Speak, and jump to the finale in under 10 s. Auto-save so the next lesson can resume the same game ('Kaldığımız yerden').

Budget realistically. Kids with 5+ teams: default 2 rounds plus 1 optional round. Learn is capped at 3 words per column, or batched as one 60-s Learn at the end of the round. Hunt, Speak and challenges are off by default for classes above 20. Show the teacher the predicted end time during play.

Zero-print fallback: a 'Tahtaya çiz' template (the app shows how to rule a notebook page into columns in 20 s). Paddle fallback: 'stand up, both hands up'. Mini-whiteboards or notebooks by default for public schools; printed sheets optional.

Drawings: accept only the 'say it' part. The owner says the word aloud and the drawing is just a memory aid, so the teacher never walks to sheets. Alternatively, drop drawing from the board-checked flow entirely.

Spell only on demand. Spelling aloud is triggered only for close-spelling or disputed cards, and for kids it is done chorally by the class ('Let's spell it together'), not by the nervous reader. In kids mode the reader is a volunteer from the team rather than a random spinner, with the spinner as a fallback only.

Peer-check mode: use simplified scoring (1 point per valid answer, and uniqueness only for words the teacher taps in an 'Only you?' lightning round). Or drop the peer-check claim and state that the tap grid is the fast path.

Replace the class-wide silhouette hint with a category nudge that does not give away one word (for example 'think: farm / sea / jungle', or 3 pictures from other letters). This keeps uniqueness alive.

Adults in individual mode: in checking, first show all answers on the screen via phones, or read each column in a fast round-robin with the teacher tapping the grid. Cap open columns at 1 per round, with a 15-s teacher ruling and no debate beyond one challenge.
Hunt and steal in Arena: one team at a time in rotation, never 'any team shouts', so Hunt doesn't create a noise spike in a class of 28.

issues: A1 Genç (9-10 year olds who barely read) is the weakest group. The game depends on free recall plus spelling from memory under a letter constraint, which is the hardest kind of output for Turkish A1 children. Expect many blank boxes, sheets full of drawings, and a game that turns into 'draw and say'. The drawing rule rescues the score but removes the spelling and reading practice the game claims to give.

Letter and sound mismatch: Turkish children spell by sound. They will write 'kat' for cat and 'jiraf' for giraffe, and will look for 'c-words' like 'city' in the wrong place. Close-spelling logic catches 'jiraf → giraffe' but gives no credit for 'kat' under C, because the first letter is wrong and the ✗ 'wrong letter' status fires. That is a harsh, confusing failure for exactly the phonics error the game should be teaching.

Rule conflicts between levelTuning and the skins. (a) A2 Genç defaults to Oyun Parkı, which says 'no team-vs-team challenges', but levelTuning A2 gives 'show it' challenges. (b) A2 Genç spelling is 'Yarım' (half credit), but Oyun Parkı pays in whole stars with no half-star defined. (c) Oyun Parkı promises 'at most 3 rules', yet with drawing, second tries, effort stars, Only-you stickers and the class goal it really has about 6 mechanics.

The Klasik İsim-Şehir preset carries the least useful columns: 'A name' (Ayşe, Burak) produces almost no English, and 'A city or country' for Turkish kids mostly produces Turkish cities written the same in both languages. Familiarity is bought with two of the five columns doing little language work, and this preset is exactly what teachers will pick most.

B2 feasibility is overstated. A letter plus a morphology constraint ('noun ending in -ment' starting with a given letter, a 'phrasal verb with up' starting with a given letter) is a double filter. Within the B2+1 band many letters will be amber or empty, and the level cap cuts further. The pool will shrink to a handful of letters or rely on ★ Bonus columns, and the B2 round becomes 'guess the one word the bank has'.

Kids' STOP is structurally unfair: with the clock off by default, the fastest (strongest) team always ends the round and weaker teams get 5 s. In a mixed public-school class the same 1-2 teams will STOP every round, while the others learn nothing new and feel cut off. That conflicts with the Nazik mode intent.

Unique answers score double, which in Oyun Parkı pushes teams to hunt for obscure words or copy tricks rather than consolidate core vocabulary. Among 9-year-olds, 'Only you' also rewards the team with the one strong kid.

Checking time for kids: second tries for wrong answers, choral repeats of every accepted word, 'stand up if you wrote it', the Learn reveal and TPR per column. With 4-6 teams and 4 columns, a 'round' is closer to 8-10 minutes, not 4-6, so the 15-20 minute session will fit 2 rounds, not 3.

Real learning is mostly retrieval of words students already know. New input comes only from the Learn step (4-6 words), which is optional and gets skipped when time runs short. At B1-B2 adult level the game is a good fluency and spelling warm-up but a weak vehicle for target vocabulary from a unit unless the columns are tightly tied to that unit.

LLM prompt path for kids: generated members are validated against words.js, which lacks many children's nouns. The YLE supplement fixes this only for curated topics. A teacher prompt such as 'deniz hayvanları' (octopus, jellyfish, seahorse, dolphin) will lose most members and then fail the 6-letter feasibility check, so the teacher gets 'dropped' columns with no explanation. Open, capability-style LLM columns ('An animal that can swim') also shift judging load back onto the teacher.

Open columns ('A reason to be late', 'Something you'd complain about in a hotel') are good speaking prompts for adults, but combined with a first-letter rule they make answers awkward ('B: bus... broken bus'). The letter rule for multi-word open answers (first letter of the first word after articles) invites trivial answers like 'bad traffic', 'big problem'.

Adults: fine and credible (Scattergories is a known adult ESL staple). Stüdyo could still feel like a kids' game at A1-A2 if the columns are Animal and Colour, but the adult column sets avoid that. Minor issue: 'Tek yazan 20' and the number of house-rule toggles add configuration weight that most teachers will never touch.
fixes: Add an A1 Genç 'Resim Bankası' support mode, on by default for A1 Genç and optional at A2: the sheet or screen shows 12-16 labelled pictures per column (a mix of letters). Kids find the ones that start with the letter and copy the word. This turns production into recognition, reading and copying, which is achievable and still practises spelling. Kolay = word bank visible; Orta = pictures only, no words; Zor = nothing.

Add a phonics-aware letter rule for Oyun Parkı: 'starts with the SOUND' mode. Draw sound-letters (b, d, f, m, p, s, t, and hard c/k as one card 'C or K /k/'), and give a friendly correction for sound-right, letter-wrong answers ('kat → cat: /k/ can be C!') as a close-spelling case, not ✗. Exclude G and C for A1 Genç by default because of the soft/hard split.

Resolve the rule conflicts with one precedence rule: the audience rule pack overrides levelTuning. A2 Genç in Oyun Parkı gets no challenges. Spelling in Oyun Parkı is Cömert or 'Correct-it' (the full star comes after the team re-spells it aloud), never half. Recount the kid ruleset to 3 printed rules and move drawing, second try and effort star to teacher-side mechanics that are never explained to the kids.

Replace the default columns of the Klasik preset per audience. Keep the familiar İsim-Şehir name and frame, but swap 'A name' for 'A job' (adults) or 'Clothes' (kids). Make 'City/Country' mean 'A country (in English)' so it forces exonyms (Germany, Greece), and add a 'nationality' half at A2+.

At B2, never combine the letter rule with a morphology column by default. Either drop the letter for twist columns (for example, '-ment nouns: as many as you can in 60 s', a letter-free round), or use the 'İçinde' or 'Son harf' variants only on plain lexical columns. The setup preview should refuse, not just amber-flag, pools under 6 letters.

Fix kids' STOP fairness. In Oyun Parkı the first STOP gives everyone 30 s ('Train is leaving in 30!'), not 5 s. Or end the round when the class goal is reached or 2 teams have stopped. Rotate a 'STOP needs 3 of 4 boxes' handicap for the leading team only if the teacher opts in.

Cap the unique-answer reward in Oyun Parkı: 1★ valid, +1★ unique only for words from the level list (A1/Starters band), so obscure words do not dominate. Emphasise the whole-class goal (class total distinct words) more than inter-team ranking.

Budget kids' checking: the second-try step is limited to one per team per round; choral repeat applies to new or unique words only (not every shared one); Learn shows 3 words for kids. Make the lesson-fit timer use measured per-column time from the first round to resize later rounds automatically.

Tie content to learning targets. The 'Bu üniteyle oyna' preset should build columns from the MEB or topic unit words and make Learn mandatory (at least 3 words) when a unit pack is used. After the game, show 'Hedef kelimeler: 14/22 bulundu' against the unit list, so the teacher sees coverage and gets a follow-up list.

LLM path: validate kid members against words.js ∪ YLE ∪ a larger children's-noun list (for example a CC0 picture-noun list of about 1,500 words) instead of words.js alone. When a generated column fails feasibility, show the teacher why ('Bu kategoride B harfiyle yalnızca 1 kelime var') and offer auto-fixes (merge it with another column, make it ★ Bonus, or switch to letter-free).

Open columns: allow them only at B1+ and exempt them from the letter rule by default, with the letter applying to a keyword instead ('Late because of a B...: bus, baby, boss'). Or mark them 'Serbest' and score them on the teacher's creativity tap, so they become real speaking moments rather than letter puzzles.
Hide advanced house-rule toggles (Tek yazan 20, Sadece özgün, Dirty STOP, minus points) behind 'Gelişmiş' so the default setup stays at one minute for busy public-school teachers.

issues: It is not a quiz with a skin. This is a real productive-recall game that Turkish students already know, and nothing else in the suite (Baamboozle board, Hangman, Jeopardy, Millionaire) duplicates it. Keep it as its own game. Group Sort, Hot Potato and Impostor use the same category-list data, but their play is different, so share the data layer and don't merge the games.

The letter-pool maths fails with the specified pack size. members are capped at 8-40 per category, which spread over about 20 usable letters is 0.4-2 words per letter. With 4-5 columns, 'green = 5+ in every column' and even 'minPerLetter 3 in every column' will leave almost no playable letters. The feasibility preview, the weighted wheel, the Learn reveal (4-6 unfound words per letter and column) and 'Did you mean' all need about 60-200 members per category.

words.js has no semantic category tags, so 'An animal', 'Food' or 'A job' cannot be computed from it. Every non-twist column needs a hand-curated list. For kids, each item also needs an SVG picture. That content and art cost (roughly 30 categories × 80 words, plus 300-500 icons) is the real build size, bigger than the code.

LLM category generation has the same problem. Asking for '12-40 members' gives lists skewed towards the common letters (B, C, S, P), and many categories will then fail the 'at least 6 feasible letters' check. The validator will drop them, and the teacher's typed prompt will seem to do nothing.

Checking is the bottleneck, and paper mode puts all of it on the teacher's keyboard. 6 teams × 6 columns at about 10 s each is 6+ minutes per round, far over the 2-4 minutes budgeted. Several features also need a record of every team's answer for every column, including blanks: the Arena streak, Clean STOP, 'Tek yazan 20' and the class goal. The flow only enters distinct words and hands-up claims, so a team that never claims a card has no record, and the streak cannot be computed.

Peer-check mode (sheets swap and the screen lists accepted words) cannot compute unique vs shared or streaks unless the teacher enters per-team results. The mode and the scoring model contradict each other.

Phones mode needs a realtime room backend (room code, answer collection, grouping, STOP broadcast). That is a separate L-sized subsystem. If this game builds it alone, it is high-risk; it should be shared suite infrastructure.

Rule and dial sprawl. The spec lists Clean/Dirty STOP, Level-up, Hunt, Speaking bonus, challenge tokens, streak multipliers, a paid hint ladder, 'Tek yazan 20', 'Sadece özgün', 3 spelling dials, 5 variants, Double round and Kolay/Orta/Zor. That is too many to build, test and explain, and the setup screen will look like a settings panel rather than a game.

The kids variant technically has 3 rules, but features have crept back in: draw-it, the second oral try, effort stars, the class goal, the Word Garden, stickers, the between-round stirrer and silhouette hints. Each is small, but together they make a lot of UI states and a lot of teacher decisions per card.

Writing load for 9-year-old A1 Turkish public-school pupils is high. Most can't spell 'giraffe', and 3 rounds × 4 columns of free writing is hard for weak classes. The drawing option helps, but teachers then have to judge drawings plus 'can say it' for every card. Teen fit is therefore below adult fit.

There are three bespoke letter-reveal animations (train with parrot, 3-reel vault, slot machine) plus a VAR replay, a STOP stamp and the Word Garden. The polish is good, but that is many one-off animations to build and keep working under reduced motion.

Letter names via browser speechSynthesis are unreliable. On Turkish-locale Windows or smartboards the default voice may be Turkish ('ce' for C), and some voices read a single 'A' as the article /ə/. The core pedagogical drill (G/J, E/I) would then teach the wrong thing.

The VAR 4 s timeout is optimistic for DeepSeek through the existing rate-limited endpoint. Several VAR taps in one check will hit the rate limit, and the class stares at a spinner. Checking 'fitsCategory' for open columns ('A reason to be late') is subjective and the LLM will be inconsistent.

Normalisation has blind spots. Singularising plurals by rule (buses, knives, mice) and via alt[] only works for bank words, and a free-typed 'childrens' or 'fishs' will slip through. Reverse Turkish lookup on words.js t will match ambiguous glosses ('yüz' gives face and hundred and swim).

Printing. A4 sheets with the team mascot, school-logo field and a STOP paddle on the back need careful print CSS (duplex alignment of the paddle is unreliable). A client-side 'PDF homework' export adds a PDF library or has to rely on print-to-PDF.
fixes: Raise the member spec to 60-200 per closed category, and store members pre-indexed byLetter at build time. Make the curated category lists (kids YLE/MEB with imageKey, adult life/work, exonym places) a first-class shared data file used by Group Sort, Hot Potato, Impostor and this game. Budget the icon set separately. For the MVP, use emoji for kid pictures and add SVGs progressively.

Make LLM generation letter-aware: ask for 'for each of these letters [B C D F G H M P R S T W], give 3-5 members per category', validate each member against words.js and the YLE list, then compute feasibility. When a generated category fails, show which letters are thin instead of dropping it silently.

Redesign CHECK as a per-column grid: team rows × one cell, default 'boş' (blank). The teacher types a word once, taps the chips of every team that has it, and unentered teams stay blank. This gives complete data for uniqueness, streak, Clean STOP and the class goal at no extra cost. Add a 'hepsi aynı / hiç yok' quick action.

Cut checking time. Default to 4 columns for classes of more than 4 teams, and have the lesson-fit timer enforce teams × columns ≤ 24 per round. Make 'Hızlı kontrol' the default: only unique-candidate words are read aloud, and shared words are claimed by hands up.
Drop peer-check as a scored mode, or reduce it to 'teams self-report count of valid / unique per column' (two number taps per team), with no streaks.
Ship v1 without phones mode (paper and projector only). Add phones later on a shared room/realtime service built once for the whole suite (Kahoot-style games need it too).

Cut the rules down. Stüdyo MVP: 10/5/0, Clean STOP +5, one challenge per team per round, Learn and Hunt, spelling dial. Arena MVP: 10/5/0, streak, 2 challenge tokens. Oyun Parkı: stars, Only-you sticker, class goal. Move 'Tek yazan 20', 'Sadece özgün', Level-up, the hint ladder, the Speaking bonus and the Son harf/İçinde/İki harf/6+ variants to an 'Ev kuralları' (house rules) drawer that is collapsed by default, and ship the variants in v2.

For kids, allow 'say it' (oral) as the default check path, and make drawing just an aid for the sheet. Offer a 'Resimli seçenek' mode for A1 Genç, where each column shows 6 picture tiles for the letter and teams must name and write one. This lowers the spelling barrier without losing the mechanic.

Build ONE parametric reveal component (reel or wheel with skinnable frame, sounds and easing) and skin it three ways, instead of three bespoke animations. Treat VAR as a 1 s stamp animation, not a replay sequence.

Pre-record or pre-generate the 26 English letter names (and the 'B for bear' carrier phrases for the kid letter set) as small audio files in a neutral native voice. Use speechSynthesis only as a fallback, with lang forced to en-GB/en-US.

Make VAR non-blocking: the teacher can tap Kabul/Ret immediately while the LLM result loads, then show it as advice. Batch every '?' word of a column into one request. Cache per (word, category) in Supabase so it is shared across classes, not only per class. Skip the LLM for open columns and let the teacher judge.

Define normalisation as a tested pure module with a fixture list: irregular plurals, UK/US, hyphens, İ/ı, articles, phrasal verbs, Turkish input. Show reverse-lookup results as a suggestion ('balık → fish?') for the teacher to confirm, never as automatic.

Printing: print CSS only for v1 (sheet and a separate paddle page, no duplex dependence). Export the word list as print-to-PDF plus 'Bu kelimelerle oyna' (a pack sent to Hangman/Memory), which is the real delight feature.

Estimated build: L for the engine (setup plus feasibility, reveal, timer, check grid, scoring, Learn, finale), plus a separate content effort. Suggested MVP: 3 skins, Klasik and topic presets, paper mode, VAR, Learn, Word Wall export. That is shippable and will feel like a proper game.

catalog.rankReason: İsim-Şehir-Hayvan, which every Turkish student already knows. It scores feasibility 8 and adult 8, and it is the only real productive-recall game in the set; nothing else duplicates it. It needs a proper category bank: 60-200 members per closed category indexed by letter at build time, countries/cities/first names, inflections, and a letter-aware LLM prompt validated against words.js. Other fixes: rotate column ownership per seat; a 'Sheets up!' reveal per column instead of reading team by team; a 'Resim Bankası' mode on by default for A1 Genç; and a 'starts with the SOUND' rule for kids.

catalog.name: Kelime Şehri / Hazine Adası (Monopoly-style Board)
catalog.familiarAs: Monopoly / Emlak Ticaret (a property board game; neither name nor its art ever appears in the UI)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams roll and hop around a looped board where every colour group is a subtopic of the chosen content. They answer to claim a place, answer to cut the rent on a rival's place and answer harder items to build. Adults run a city economy with auctions and English negotiation, 12-14-year-olds claim planets in a neon space Match, and 9-11-year-olds sail Treasure Island collecting treasures with no money, no rent and no bankruptcy. Every game is time-boxed and can be saved and continued next lesson.
catalog.howItPlays:
ONE ENGINE, THREE RULESETS. The same board engine runs 'Hazine Adası' (Oyun Parkı), 'Orbit Match' (Arena) and 'Kelime Şehri' (Stüdyo). Türkiye Turu, the Zoo and World Cities are skins of that engine, not separate games. The merged AudienceProfile picks the ruleset, and the teacher can override the skin or any single dial. Values below are written as [Park / Arena / Stüdyo].

BOARD. A ring runs around the projector edge. The centre holds the dice, the active card and the team strip (money, stars or credits). Colour groups are subtopics of the pack (Food gives Fruit & Veg / Cooking Verbs / At the Restaurant / Countable-Uncountable). There are three sizes, and the lesson-fit timer suggests one:
- Kısa 16: 4 corners, 4 groups x 2 places, 4 specials.
- Standart 20: 4 corners, 4 groups x 3 places, 2 Şans, 1 Kamu Fonu, 1 Herkes Cevaplar.
- Uzun 28: 4 corners, 6 groups x 3 places, 2 Şans, 1 Kamu Fonu, 2 Herkes Cevaplar, 1 Kelime Vergisi.
Inside a group the places are tier 1-2-3, so price and question difficulty rise together (the cheap place asks a diff-1 item, the dear one a diff-3 item). Stüdyo corners: START, Kütüphane (jail), Konuşma Parkı (the pot of fines) and Kütüphaneye Git.

SETUP (2 min or less). The teacher picks the group chip and the content (a built-in category, 'Karma tekrar: ünite X-Y', or a free-text prompt, possibly in Turkish). The setup screen shows one summary line, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 sn · 35 dk · Kelime Şehri', with a 'Değiştir' link. Teams (2-6, 4 is best) pick a token, emblem or mascot and number their seats 1-6. A spinning roulette of team colours sets the order. Park and Arena start with a 20-30 s practice turn that does not score; in Park, Gogo demos it.

A TURN (about 60-75 s for kids, 90-120 s for adults):
1 WHO. The seat spinner [Park/Arena] or the rotating spokesperson tile [Stüdyo] shows 'Now answering: Blue · seat 3'. The roller and mover roles rotate too. Nobody is ever picked by name.
2 ROLL. Space or the big button rolls animated dice: 1 die in Park (the class counts every hop aloud in English), 1 die in Arena, 2 dice in Stüdyo. With a real foam die the teacher types the number (1-6, or two digits for two dice). 'Sabit adım' always moves 3 squares, for fairness. Stüdyo also has an optional 'Beceri zarı': instead of rolling, the team answers a tier-3 item and chooses its own move of 1-6.
3 HOP. The token hops square by square with a tick. Passing START pays [+1 star / +3 credits / +200].
4 RESOLVE THE SQUARE.
 a) UNCLAIMED PLACE. The deed card flips and shows the name, price, a five-pip rent ladder and the place's item. The question shows first and the options follow [3-4 s / 2.5 s / 2 s]. Then Team talk [10 / 15 / 20 s] and 'Boards up!'. MCQ, tap and bank items check themselves; spoken and typed answers get big Doğru/Yanlış buttons (keys D/Y), with the model answer shown on reveal.
   A correct answer claims the place: Park collects the treasure automatically, Arena claims the planet and pays its price automatically, and Stüdyo chooses Buy or Pass (auto-buy at A1).
   A wrong answer shows the right answer and its 'why', and the place stays open. In Park the treasure 'goes back to sleep' for the next visitor. In Arena the next team in turn order whose mini-whiteboard is right may steal-claim it at half price, and the first team loses nothing. In Stüdyo A1-A2 the place just stays open; at B1-B2 it goes to a 10 s sealed-bid auction: bids go up on mini-whiteboards together and the teacher types the highest. Nobody shouts.
 b) RIVAL'S PLACE. The visitor answers an item from that group at the place's tier, plus 1 tier per building (max 3).
   Stüdyo: correct = half rent; wrong = full rent, and the owner may steal the same item for +50.
   Arena: correct = no docking fee plus the answer bonus. Wrong: under Nazik the bank pays the owner and the visitor loses nothing; with Yellow opted in, the visitor pays, capped at its credits.
   Park: a 'Visit'. Both teams answer together, and if they are right BOTH get a star.
 c) OWN PLACE. Stüdyo/Arena: 'Renovate' means one extra item for +50 / +2. Park: 'Home sweet home': Gogo says a word, the class repeats it, and the team gets +1 star.
 d) SPECIALS.
   Şans / Signal / Magic card: the card spins, is read aloud, and holds a task or an event from the pool the harshness level allows.
   Kamu Fonu / Supply Drop: a joker (50:50, Pas for a new item, or Kalkan: the next rent is 0). A team holds 2 at most.
   Herkes Cevaplar: every team answers on mini-whiteboards, and each correct team gets [+1 star / +2 / +50]. The trailing team picks which colour group the question comes from.
   Kelime Vergisi (Uzun board only): 'Say 3 [category] words in 10 s or pay 100 into the Park pot.'
 e) CORNERS.
   Jail (Kütüphane / Asteroid Belt): leave by fixing an error sentence (one try per turn) or by paying 50. Automatic release after 2 turns in Stüdyo; in Arena the team flies out next turn anyway. Park has no jail time: 'Stuck in the Sand' means the whole class answers a picture question and the team is free at once.
   Konuşma Parkı: talk for 30 s on a speaking prompt. The teacher taps Great (the whole pot), OK (half the pot) or Try again (0, and the prompt stays for the next visitor).
   Go to jail: Kütüphaneye Git in Stüdyo, Tractor Beam in Arena. Park replaces it with the Windy Corner: fly to any free treasure and try it.
5 BUILD (Stüdyo and Arena, at the start of your own turn, once per turn). A team that owns a full colour group can build.
   A house (Arena: module) needs a tier-2 production item: a gap without a bank, or one new sentence. A hotel (Arena: station ring) needs a tier-3 task: a 30 s talk, 'Explain the difference between...', or persuading the bank.
   Each place's rent ladder is base 20% of the price, full set 40%, house 70%, hotel 100%. Rent never exceeds the price, which works as the runaway brake.
6 END OF TURN. Undo is always visible, and the game autosaves after every action.

MONEY AND NO ELIMINATION. The app does all the arithmetic. Nobody goes below 0 or goes bankrupt. A team that cannot pay pays what it has and the rest is forgiven; on its next turn it may take 'Banka işi': 2 quick items, +100 each. Comeback is set to Light: the trailing team gets a quiet Slipstream bonus (+50) on every correct answer and a 'Lucky Fountain' +100 when it passes START. The 'Adil şans' toggle weights the Şans deck so trailing teams draw more reward cards.

ENDING. The game is time-boxed by default. Warnings come at 5 and 3 minutes, then a 'Final round' banner gives every team the same number of turns, then the bell. Or the teacher taps 'Sonraki derse kaydet': the exact state goes to a named slot ('7-B · Salı'), and next lesson opens with a 10 s 'Last time...' flyover of the map.
Winners: Stüdyo uses net worth (cash + prices + buildings) plus a separate 'Language MVP' for the most correct answers. Arena shows a podium plus stat awards. In Park every team gets a title. Every mode ends with 'Words we met', with missed items highlighted; Stüdyo calls this list 'Kaçırılanlar'.
catalog.playerSetup:
2-6 teams of 3-6 students on one projector. 4 teams is best: above 6 the wait between turns is too long, and the 16-square kids board gets crowded. The class can be 12-36 students. The teacher is banker and judge, and the app does all the maths. Seats are numbered 1-6 inside each team, and the roles rotate every turn: roller, mover (in Park the whole class counts the hops) and spokesperson.
Participation by mode:
- Park: the whole class responds every turn with printed A-B-C cards or TPR (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C).
- Arena: one mini-whiteboard per team, for Herkes Cevaplar, steals and trade proposals.
- Stüdyo: pair consultation inside teams, a rotating spokesperson, and whiteboards for sealed bids and Herkes Cevaplar.
Nobody is ever picked by name.
catalog.contentShape:
ENVELOPE. pack.frames.board = {skinHint?, groups[4-6]: {key, label (EN, 4 words or fewer), labelTr, emoji, placeNames[2-3]?, tiers: {t1: itemIds[], t2: itemIds[], t3: itemIds[]}}}.
Place names: Stüdyo may use LLM names (3 words or fewer, validated, no brands or addresses: 'Irregular Verb Avenue', 'Café Corner'). Park and Arena names come from code templates tied to the skin's sticker set ('Banana Beach', 'Planet Verbo'), so they are always picturable.

VOLUME. Standart 20 with 4 teams for 35 min is about 28 turns, which needs about 60 unique answerable items. Per group that means at least 5 tier-1, 4 tier-2 and 3 tier-3 items. There are no repeats in a session; missed items can come back once in the review.

TIER MAP.
- Tier 1 (the cheap place; rent on an unbuilt place): vocab (picture/emoji → word, TR → EN, defEasy → word), pair (picture-word, word-TR), tf (about 'picture' at A1), mcq (fmt gap / meaning / picture; 3 options for Park A1, which may use 2; 4 otherwise), odd (Arena, fast whole-team item).
- Tier 2 (the dear place; houses; rent on a built place): gap (bank required for Park and A groups; typed or said at B), mcq (fmt collocation / dialogue / context with a short ctx notice or chat), qa (answerKind word or phrase), error (fix it).
- Tier 3 (hotels; rent on a hotel; Beceri zarı): qa with teacherJudge=true (answerKind sentence), speaking-prompt (talk / describe / opinion, secs 20-30, starters and useful words shown), roleplay (short, B1+).

CORNERS AND SPECIALS.
- error x8: jail escapes, errorType chosen by level.
- speaking-prompt x6: Konuşma Parkı. Park uses picture 'describe' prompts with starters.
- category-list x6 (open=true, 8 or more members): Kelime Vergisi, Word Rain, and 'name 5 in 10 s' cards.
- taboo-card x4 (mode describe/act): Arena Signal cards and Park Magic 'act it' cards.
- chance-card deck of 12-16: kind reward / penalty / task / swap / bonus; task speak / act / spell / draw; the engine clamps 'amount' to the mode's scale (stars / credits / coins) and filters by harshness; textTr is required for A1 Genç.
- roleplay x2-4: Stüdyo B1+ life-event Şans (complaint, small talk, tour-price negotiation), with checklist[] as success criteria.
- Herkes Cevaplar pulls any auto-checkable tier-1/2 item (mcq, tf, gap with a bank).
- The Deal Window phrase frames are a fixed, curated set per level, never generated.

BUILT-IN CONTENT. Four related grammar_mcq units become 4 groups (whyOpt is carried through). words.js CEFR themed lists feed tier-1 vocab (defTr, ipa, example). idioms.js feeds the B2 hard-rent tier. Kids categories follow YLE/MEB topics with pictures.

LLM CONTENT. The prompt (Turkish or English) must return 4-6 named subtopics with tiered items. The validator enforces:
- word caps and teenSafe;
- item counts per tier;
- no duplicates across groups;
- an imageKey on every Park item (unpicturable items are dropped).
If a group falls short, code fills it from the built-in banks at the same level, or drops to the Kısa board.

TÜRKİYE TURU. Place names, regions and one fact per landmark per level come from a curated static file, never from the LLM. The LLM only writes questions tagged to the unit's theme (weather, directions, food, travel, comparatives).
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Kelime Şehri / Language City'. Default for A1-B2 adults.

LOOK. An editorial quiz-night city map, on cream or in the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. Clean illustrated districts with no brands or real addresses, system sans, no mascot and no voice lines; the only caption is neutral ('Round 2 · Travel'). Tokens: çay bardağı, simit, vapur, bicycle, headphones, plant, laptop, coffee cup. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs'). Student-screen text is English; the teacher chrome is Turkish.

ECONOMY. Neutral coins, with an optional ₺/£ symbol. Start with 1500. Prices rise around the board from 100 to 300. START pays +200. A house costs 100 and a hotel 150, each on top of its question. The rent ladder is 20 / 40 / 70 / 100% of the price, and a correct rent answer halves the rent.

ADULT RULES ON TOP OF THE CORE TURN.
- Buy or Pass decisions (A2+).
- A 10 s sealed-bid auction on a place someone missed (B1+, bids on mini-whiteboards).
- Rent challenge with an owner steal (+50).
- 'Cümle kirası' (Sentence rent, B1+): the visitor must say a NEW sentence with the place's word or structure. The teacher taps OK or Not yet; Not yet means full rent.
- Deal Window (B1+, default every 2 rounds, 60 s, one pair of teams at a time). Teams trade properties or cash out loud using on-screen frames: 'Would you consider X for Y?', 'That's a fair offer, but...', 'How about 200 plus...?', 'I'll give you... if...'. A deal counts only if both sides used a frame, which the teacher ticks; then the teacher taps 'Anlaşma' and the property or cash moves.
- B2 adds 'Convince the bank your district deserves a hotel' tasks and register rent ('Say it more formally').

ŞANS. Life events as speaking tasks, with success criteria printed on the card:
- 'Your flight is cancelled. Complain politely to the airline in 3 sentences: +100.'
- 'Small talk: ask the receptionist 2 questions.'
- 'Your manager wants a quick update: explain your weekend plans in 3 sentences.'
The teacher rates them Great +100 / OK +50 / Try again 0, and Try again comes with a hint for one retry.

OTHER SQUARES AND DIALS.
- Kamu Fonu gives jokers. The Konuşma Parkı pot collects every tax, fee and jail payment.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default ('Take 100 from a team you tap', capped; 'Swap turn order'). Red is opt-in: 'Swap one property with any team', 'Rent strike: no rent for one round', 'Audit: the next rent you collect goes to the pot'.
- Hints cost coins: definition 20, then example 20, then Turkish gloss 30. The Turkish gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
- Wrong answers show the correct answer plus a one-line why (whyTr, or whyEn at B).
- Optional 30 s timer. Team talk 20 s.

SOUND AND FEEL. Woodblock and piano, a soft cash-register chime on rent (1 s or less), music off by default. Celebrations are a 0.6 s chime and a roll-up. As the clock runs, the city moves from afternoon to dusk to night, and owned places light their windows in the team colour.

FINALE (modest). Net-worth podium, a 'Language MVP' ribbon (most correct answers), 'Best Deal' if trading was on, the full score table, a net-worth line chart, and a skyline built from each team's houses. The 'Kaçırılanlar' list can be printed or sent to the Material Maker as a review worksheet.

SKINS. Kelime Şehri (default), World Cities, and Türkiye Turu 'Business Trip': show a foreign colleague around, recommend a place, negotiate a tour price, handle a hotel complaint. In Türkiye Turu the regions are the colour groups and the landmark facts are curated; it suits adults in tourism and customer service.

LENGTH. 30-45 min, or two lessons with save and continue.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two stripped rulesets, not recolours. The group label never appears on screen, and Nazik mode runs underneath both.

OYUN PARKI: 'Hazine Adası / Treasure Island' (default for A1 and A2 Genç, ages 9-11).

THE 3-RULE CARD. The teacher reads it in Turkish in 20 s, with pictograms.
1 'Roll and hop!' One big die; the class counts every hop aloud in English.
2 'Everyone answers!' The whole class shows A-B-C cards or TPR. The answer of the active team's seat-number student counts. If it is right, the team collects that place's treasure sticker and plants its animal flag.
3 'Visit a friend!' On another team's treasure, both teams answer together. If they are right, both get a star.
Every other square explains itself with a pictogram:
- Magic card: a class task such as 'Walk like a penguin and say penguin 3 times', 'Show me 5 blue things', or a Green event: Gift a star to a team you tap, Everyone +2 stars, Double next treasure, Brain break.
- Word Rain: the class says 3 fruits together, +1 star.
- Hep Birlikte: a whole-class question, and every team that is right gets +1 star.
- Harbour (START): Gogo asks the class a quick picture question.
- Stuck in the Sand: the class rescues the team with a picture question, and it is free at once.
- Gogo's Nest: a 45 s song/stirrer or a 60 s settler, and everyone gets +1 star.
- Windy Corner: fly to any free treasure and try it.
There is no money, rent, buying decision, bankruptcy, jail time or building. A full colour pair becomes a Treasure Chest that opens with spilling gems (+3 stars). Stars only ever go up.

BOARD AND LOOK. The Kısa 16 board is fixed: an island with a beach, a jungle, a friendly volcano and a ship (no pirates, nothing sinks). Places are picture topics from YLE and MEB units (Animals gives Jungle and Zoo; Food gives Fruit Market and Bakery). Team mascots are the panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin and bear. Warm cream palette, an Andika-type font, prompts at 6vh or larger, 4 words or fewer at A1. Every item has a picture and is read aloud automatically at 0.8x.

GOGO. Gogo the parrot rides the active token. It demos a practice turn that does not score, calls 'Your turn, Pandas!', repeats the answer after a miss so the class says it twice, and naps on the pause screen.

WRONG ANSWERS. A soft boing, then a second try with a free hint (picture, then first letter, then listen again). If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team earns an effort star for the class album. The treasure 'goes back to sleep' for the next visitor.

TIMING AND SOUND. The timer is off; when on, it is a calm 40 s ring, never red, with a marimba chime at 0. Team talk is 10 s. Marimba and xylophone sounds, never a buzzer. Sticker bursts last 2 s or less, and confetti comes only at the finale. A fixed 20 min: 3 rounds of about 5 min with a Gogo's Nest interlude between them. The 5-minute warning is 'The ship leaves in 5 minutes!' with a sand timer.

CLASS LIGHTHOUSE. A shared goal, not a team score. When most of the class shows the right card, the teacher taps 'Sınıf!' and the lighthouse fills. A full lighthouse means a whole-class dance and brain break.

ENDING. The island map shows every flag. Every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers, Treasure Hunters, Kind Visitors), the class album gets a sticker, and a treasure-map certificate can be printed.

KIDS CHECKLIST. 3 rules; explainable in 20 s with pictograms; no elimination; never below zero; a whole-class response on every square; failure imagery is a sleeping treasure. All pass.
Other Park skins: Hayvanat Bahçesi (habitats to collect, with a baby-animal chest), and Türkiye Turu Kids (a cartoon map, a family-car token, a passport stamp per region).

ARENA: 'Orbit Match'. Default for B1 and B2 Genç. It is also suggested for any Genç group at grade 6-8, or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor'. Ages 12-14.

LOOK AND OWNERSHIP. Dark navy with neon team colours and a condensed display font. Emblems: bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond. In 10 s each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. It is called a 'Match', never a lesson game. No mascot, cartoon animals, pastels or 'superstar'. The only commentary is a caption strip, at most once per turn: 'COMBO x3', 'SECTOR LOCKED', 'CLUTCH!'.

BOARD AND ECONOMY. Standart 20: 4 sectors x 3 planets, 2 Signal cards, 1 Supply Drop, 1 Scan (everyone answers). Credits stay small: start with 20, planets cost 4/6/8, docking fees are 1/2/3 plus 1 per module, and the Launch Pad pays +3.

RULES.
- A correct answer claims the planet automatically and earns +2. The combo raises it to x1.5 at 3 correct in a row and x2 at 5. It counts accuracy only; there are no speed points.
- A wrong answer breaks the streak. The next team in turn order whose whiteboard is right may steal-claim the planet at half price. The first team loses nothing.
- Docking: a correct answer means no fee. After a wrong answer the bank pays the owner under Nazik; with Yellow opted in, the visitor pays, capped at its credits, with a floor of 0.
- Modules come from tier-2 items (from A2 Genç), and station rings from 20-30 s talks (B1+).
- Wormhole corner: jump to any unclaimed planet. Asteroid Belt (jail): fix an error sentence now, or fly out next turn.
- The trade window is opt-in for B1/B2 Genç, with teen frames ('Do you want to swap...?', 'What about... plus 2 credits?').

TIMING AND SOUND. A 30 s timer is on, with the ring in the team colour. Team talk is 15 s. Hints (first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example) cost 1 credit each but never take a team below 0. Short synth blips, combo text of 1.2 s or less, and an optional quiet thinking loop.

ENDING. A podium plus stat awards (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, Most planets, Best trade), never a last place, and the galaxy map glowing in team colours.

CONTENT. teenSafe throughout: no brands, rent, salary, office or boss. Signal cards are school-life and space events. Plays 25-35 min.
catalog.levelTuning:
Level and audience are independent. The level decides the items and which features unlock; the audience decides the rules and the look. So a 9-year-old B1 class keeps Park, and a 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena with full picture and audio support. Word caps are given for adults first, then for Genç.

A1 (10 words / Genç 0-4).
- Items: picture-word pairs, emoji → word, TR → EN words, picture tf, MCQ with 3 options (Park A1 may use 2), numbers, colours, 'What's this? It's a...'.
- Rules: auto-buy or collect, fixed prices, no building, no auction or trading, rent and visit challenges always tier 1, a single die in every audience, a TR hint card allowed, Kelime Vergisi off.
- Jail errors: be+verb, article, plural, capital. Şans cards are TPR or 'say 3 animals'.

A2 (15 / Genç 8).
- Items: 4-option MCQ, gaps with a bank, dialogue MCQ, 'ask a question' tasks ('At the café: order a drink'), 'Tell me 2 things about...'.
- Rules: Stüdyo gets Buy/Pass decisions and houses via tier-2 gaps; hotels are still off. Arena A2 Genç turns modules on.
- Jail errors: 3rd-s, aux-question, past simple. Şans: 'say 3 words about...' and two-sentence tasks.

B1 (25 / Genç 14).
- Items: open qa (typed or said), gaps without a bank, context MCQ with a short notice or chat, error correction as the rent challenge. Tier 3 is a 30 s talk, a 3-sentence past-simple story, comparatives between two places, or recommendations with should.
- Rules: Stüdyo turns on Sentence rent and hotels, sealed-bid auctions (default on) and the Deal Window (every 2 rounds). Arena B1 Genç gets station rings and an opt-in trade window.
- Jail errors: tense, for/since, preposition.

B2 (40 / Genç 20).
- Items: transformations (gap with base), collocations and idioms (from idioms.js) on the hard-rent tier, register ('Say it more formally'), speculation, conditionals. Tier 3 is defend, compare or persuade ('Convince the bank...'), and Şans cards are roleplays (a complaint, negotiating a tour price).
- Rules: auctions and trading on by default, Beceri zarı offered.
- Jail errors: word-choice, word-order.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics (compare two planets or places, explain a plan), never abstract debate or adult domains.

DIFFICULTY INSIDE A GROUP. 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' shifts the word-band mix and hint availability (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words). 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the items one level without changing rules or skin. Inside every colour group the tier 1-2-3 ladder always spans diff 1-3 relative to the chosen level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Park: a fixed 20 (range 15-25). Arena: 25-35. Stüdyo: 30-45 (Kısa 16 is about 20 min, Standart 20 about 30-35, Uzun 28 about 45). Any game can be saved and continued across two lessons.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP.
- The summary line with 'Değiştir'. The group chip and a saved class profile ('7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').
- Skin per audience: Hazine Adası / Hayvanat Bahçesi / Türkiye Turu Kids; Orbit / Türkiye Turu Arena; Kelime Şehri / World Cities / Türkiye Turu Business Trip.
- Board size 16 / 20 / 28, or 'ders süresine göre' (sized from the lesson length). Time limit or number of rounds.
- Mapping subtopics to colours: automatic from the category, drag to edit, or 'Karma tekrar: ünite X-Y'.
- Teams: count, names, tokens.
- Economy: starting cash; buy mode (auto / choose); rent mode (discount / sentence rent / visit-only); houses and hotels on or off.
- Features: auction on or off; Deal Window off / every round / every 2 rounds; steals on or off; jail on or off.
- Dice: 1 or 2, real-dice entry, Sabit adım 3, Beceri zarı.
- Answer timer: Süresiz / 30 / 40 / 60, with +10 and T to pause.
- Hints: ladder costs, TR gloss on or off.
- Dials: harshness Green / Yellow / Red; comeback Off / Light / Strong; 'Adil şans' weighting.
- Whole-class response method: cards / TPR / whiteboards. Shadow answers on or off. Kolay / Orta / Zor and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.

IN PLAY.
- Big Doğru/Yanlış buttons (D/Y) and the Great / OK / Try again rubric.
- Space to roll; digit keys for a real die.
- Multi-step Undo, always visible. Move a token by hand. +/- money, stars or credits per team.
- New item or skip card; reveal the answer; replay audio (R); hint (H).
- Pause/freeze (T): it blurs the board, and Gogo sleeps in Park.
- 'Sınıf!' fills the lighthouse. Approve a trade; enter the winning bid.
- 'Son tur şimdi', 'Şimdi bitir ve puanla', 'Kaydet ve sonraki derste devam' (named save slots).
- Autosave after every action, so a sleeping projector PC resumes where it stopped.
- Print an A3 board and card sheets for offline days.
catalog.delightDetails:
DICE AND MOVEMENT.
- A big 3D dice tumble; with reduced motion the number just appears. The foam-die mode animates the typed roll the same way.
- Tokens hop with a bounce and a tick, and in Park a big 'one, two, three...' pops above each square as the class counts.

CARDS, CLAIMS AND MONEY.
- Deed cards flip like real cards, with a mini illustration, the colour band and a five-pip rent ladder.
- Flag planting in the team colour and emblem, and a 'SET COMPLETE!' stamp (never the trademark word).
- Money moves differently in each mode: coins fly between team badges with a cha-ching (adults), gems spill from an opening chest (kids), and credits stream as a neon beam (Arena).
- The Şans card spins and zooms. A 'Lucky Fountain' splash marks the comeback bonus.

THE BOARD COMES ALIVE.
- Houses pop onto their squares and the skyline grows.
- The adult city moves from afternoon to dusk to night with the game clock, and owned windows light in team colours.
- Arena planets gain an orbit ring per module, a locked sector pulses, and each team's motto shows under its emblem.
- Gogo flaps on 'Treasure!' and naps on pause with a 'zzz'. The Lighthouse class meter fills with each 'Sınıf!' tap.
- Türkiye Turu has passport stamps per region and regional stingers of 1 s or less.

ENDINGS AND RETURNS.
- A 'Final round' banner and a bell. A resume opens with a 10 s 'Last time...' flyover of the map.
- The end map of who owns what is a screenshot moment, printable as a certificate (a treasure map for kids).
- 'Words we met' highlights the missed items.

SMALL TOUCHES.
- Adult tokens include çay bardağı, simit and vapur.
- Student strings stay tiny and English: 'Your turn!', 'Roll!', 'Treasure!', 'Visit!', 'Boards up!'.
- The Kids 3-rule card is a pictogram poster that can also be printed.
catalog.risks:
- Long, luck-heavy games and idle teams. Answers: a hard timer with an equal-turns final round, lesson-fit board sizing, Herkes Cevaplar squares, whole-class responses in Park, whiteboard steals and sealed bids, Sabit adım and Beceri zarı, Slipstream.
- A runaway leader. Answers: rent capped at the price, half rent on a correct answer, the comeback bonus, and hidden weighting in the Şans deck.
- Rule overload. Kids get the 3-rule card and Gogo's practice turn. Adults get a 60 s animated how-to plus a demo turn. Features unlock by level (A1 has no building, auction or trade).
- Noise in auctions and trades. Bids are sealed on whiteboards, only one Deal Window runs at a time, and the teacher must approve it.
- Teacher-judged answers slow play. Big rubric buttons and success criteria printed on the card help, and MCQ, tap and bank items check themselves.
- Content depth. A 35 min game needs about 60 unique items. The validator checks each tier, fills gaps from the built-in banks, and never repeats an item.
- Arithmetic must be 100% automatic.
- Trademark. Never use the Monopoly or Emlak Ticaret names or art in the UI, and no police or jail imagery.
- Türkiye Turu facts. Landmark facts come only from the curated file, never from the LLM. Keep them neutral and positive, with no regional stereotypes.
- Money themes for children. Park removes them entirely. Arena credits are game points with no wagering. The teenSafe filter runs on every Genç group.
- A crowded board. Six teams on the 16-square board get cramped, so recommend 4 and cap Park at 6.
- Scope. This is XL. Ship the engine with Stüdyo Kelime Şehri and Park Hazine Adası first, then the Arena and Türkiye Turu skins. Snakes & Ladders ('Yılan-Merdiven') can share the dice and token code, but it is a separate game in the suite, not a mode of this one.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Snakes & Ladders / board race (Park 'Hazine Adası' ruleset only)

issues: The kids' turn is longer than the plan says. Seat spinner 5 s, roll and counting the hops 8-10 s, the prompt read at 0.8x plus options 4 s, team talk 10 s, 'Boards up' and the teacher finding the right student 5-10 s, the claim animation 2 s. That is already 40-45 s. A miss adds a second try with a hint, then Gogo, then the class repeating twice: another 15-20 s. So turns run 60-90 s, and with 4 teams each team waits 3-4.5 min. Take out the 3 Gogo's Nest interludes (about 3 min) and the practice turn, and a 20 min game gives each team only about 3-4 rolls. That is too few for a board game to feel like one, and too few to complete Treasure Chest pairs.

In Park the whole class answers, but only one student's card counts. Kids aged 10-12 notice within 2-3 turns that their card changes nothing (it only feeds the Lighthouse, which the teacher taps by eye). Participation then collapses into copying and chatting. The cards also go up at once, so the counted student can just copy the class.

The teacher has to scan the room for 'Blue seat 3' among 28 raised cards. At the board, with numbers on nobody's desk, that means asking 'who is Blue 3?' every turn, which is dead time and noise. Seat numbers also break as soon as someone is absent or a team has fewer members than the seat the spinner lands on.

TPR for A-B-C (stand, sit, hands up) with 28 kids on every turn is chaos in a Turkish public-school classroom: desks, bags, noise complaints from the next room. After 10 turns it wears out. The printed A-B-C cards also need handing out and collecting, 3-5 min the first time, and nothing says who prepares 28 sets.
Mini-whiteboards are assumed in Arena (steals, Scan) and Stüdyo (sealed bids). Most state schools don't have a class set, and the design has no fallback.

Park is a 3-rule card in name only. The kids also have to learn 7 pictogram specials (Magic, Word Rain, Hep Birlikte, Harbour, Stuck in the Sand, Gogo's Nest, Windy Corner) and track 6 parallel reward systems (treasures, stars, effort stars, the Lighthouse, chests, the class album). Kids ask 'what is this one?' on every special, and the teacher can't explain at the end who 'won' what.

The Arena steal goes only to 'the next team in turn order'. That is a fixed structural advantage: the team seated after the weakest team collects its misses all game. Combos (x1.5 at 3, x2 at 5) then compound the strong team's lead. The comeback settings (Slipstream +50) are written in adult coin scale and are unclear for credits.

In Stüdyo the adult economy has no time to develop. Two dice on 20 squares, about 20 turns in 35 min, so about 5-7 turns per team, and wrong answers leave places open. Completing a colour set, which houses, hotels, rent ladders and trades all need, will rarely happen. Much of the most complex rule surface (building, Deal Window, register rent) goes unused in a single lesson unless the game carries over to a second one.

The teacher's load in Stüdyo B1-B2 is high. They judge sentence rent, run the Great/OK/Try again rubric, tick deal frames for both sides, read and type sealed bids, run the hint ladder, pay out jokers and pots, and press Undo, all while standing at a projector. The design leans on keyboard keys (D/Y, Space, T, H, R, digits), which don't help a teacher standing at the screen or working a touch board.

The smart board creates risk of stray touches. Big Roll and Doğru/Yanlış buttons within a child's reach at the bottom of the board mean eager 10-year-olds will tap them. The design has no touch lock and no teacher-only zone.
The Deal Window idles 8 of 10 adults for 60 s every 2 rounds. That is fine as a spectacle once, but it adds up to several minutes per lesson with nothing to do for most of the room.
The equal-turns final round can run past the bell. If it is triggered at the 3-min warning, 4 teams x 90-120 s = 6-8 min, and in a Turkish public school the bell is absolute.
Save-and-continue ignores that the class changes. Next lesson students are absent, teams need rebalancing, and a different PC or browser may lose the autosave, since local storage is per device.

Team setup takes longer than 2 min with 12-14-year-olds. Picking an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto 'in 10 s' really means 2-4 min of arguing across 4 teams. That is a realistic 5-7 min of setup in a 40-min lesson.

One strong student can still dominate. In a 10 s team talk the fastest kid decides, and the rotating spokesperson only reads out that answer. Nothing makes the weaker student hold the answer before the team hears it.

The build is XL, with three rulesets that are effectively three games. It risks shipping none of them polished, and the kids version overlaps heavily with a separate Snakes & Ladders game and the existing /sinif-oyunu tile board.
fixes: Make every card count in Park. Each team scores 1 star when more than half of its members show the right card, counted by the teacher with one tap per team or by eye, with 'Sınıf!' as a bonus. Drop the single seat-student rule, or use it only for the team's spoken 'say it' line. Add a '3-2-1 cards up!' countdown so everyone reveals at once and nobody can copy.

Replace TPR as the default with 'fingers 1-2-3 on your chest' or printed cards. Offer an A4 PDF with A/B/C/D on four colours: one sheet per student, folded, reused every game. Show a 'kartları dağıt' checklist on the setup screen. Make TPR an occasional Magic card, not every turn.

Give Arena and Stüdyo a no-whiteboard fallback: a folded A4 sheet or a notebook page held up. For sealed bids, a team writes on paper and the spokesperson hands it to the teacher. Let the teacher pick 'Beyaz tahta yok' in setup, and adapt the steal and Scan rules to raised hands in team order, with a random tiebreak.

Shorten the Park turn so each team gets 6 or more rolls in 20 min. Cap a miss at one hint retry, then 'the class says it once'. Merge the practice turn into the first real turn. Make Gogo's Nest optional and cut it from 3 to 1 mid-game break. Consider a 2-team 'class vs class halves' option for 28 kids, which roughly halves the waiting.

Give Park at most 4 special-square types (Magic, Hep Birlikte, Windy Corner, Harbour) and fold 'Stuck in the Sand' and Word Rain into Magic cards. Show one score per team (stars) plus the Lighthouse. Effort stars simply add to the team's stars, and the class album and titles appear only at the end.

Make the Arena steal priority fair. Any team with a correct board may steal: pick among them at random with an on-screen spin, or give it to the lowest-scoring correct team. Cap combos at x1.5, or reset them each round. Restate the comeback settings per mode (+1 credit, +1 star).

Make the adult economy develop within one lesson. Deal out 1 random place per team at the start (a 'starter deed'), which means fewer places and sets that complete faster. Use the 16-square board as the one-lesson default and 20 or 28 squares only for two-lesson saves. Allow building from 2 of 3 places in a group at B1+. Otherwise mark building and trading as 'second-lesson features' in the lesson-fit suggestion.

Build a teacher remote: a phone page (QR pairing, local session) with Roll, Doğru/Yanlış, Great/OK/Try, Undo and Pause, so the teacher can walk the room. On touch boards, put all judge buttons in a teacher strip at the top of the screen and require a long-press on Roll, which stops kids from tapping it.

Keep the teacher's decisions to one tap each. Deals count on a single 'Anlaşma geçerli' tap, not frame ticks per side. Enter bids by tapping a team, then +/- steps. Rename hints and jokers so the app auto-applies costs. Show a 'next step' prompt in the teacher strip, so the teacher never has to remember a rule.

Keep the Deal Window from idling the room. Open it to all teams at once as a 30 s whiteboard 'offer drop', then one spoken exchange for the best offer. Or have spectators vote 'fair deal?' with thumbs, for a +10 bonus.

Plan the final round from the clock. The app estimates the final round's length from the average turn time and starts it so the game ends at the set time. Add a hard 'Zil çalıyor' button that scores instantly without an equal-turns round; the uneven turns are shown in the results.

On resume, show a 30 s roster screen: move absent students, rebalance the teams, re-spin the seats. Let the teacher export or import a save as a code or file (or save it to the Supabase account) so a different classroom PC can pick it up.

Speed up setup. Give preset team identities (auto-assigned emblem, colour and motto, with a 'değiştir' option), and move motto-picking into the first team's practice turn. Give each team a printable name card. Save team lists in the class profile so the next game starts in under 60 s.

Prevent domination with 'think first, then talk'. Show 3 s of silent individual thinking (a 'Think' icon) before team talk. Sometimes pick the spokesperson AFTER team talk (seat spin at 'Boards up'), so everyone must know the answer.

Cut the scope. Ship the engine with Stüdyo (Kısa 16 default) and Park as v1; make Arena a Stüdyo-lite ruleset with the Arena skin, not a third design. Put Türkiye Turu later. Reuse the /sinif-oyunu team strip, judge buttons and question pipeline.

issues: Language density is low for what it costs in time. Stüdyo gives about 28 turns in 35 min, with one item per turn answered by one spokesperson, so each student produces English about 1-2 times a lesson and the other 3 teams mostly wait while the dice roll, the token hops and the deed flips. Baamboozle or Kahoot-style games get 3-5 times more items per minute. The 'Shadow answers' toggle exists but is buried in the teacher dials, and non-active teams get nothing for being right.

The adult A1 and A2 groups lose most of what makes the adult version fun. A1 has auto-buy, fixed tier-1 rent, and no building, auction, trading or Kelime Vergisi. What is left is a luck-driven quiz with a money counter. The only adult-specific production mechanics (Sentence rent, Deal Window, hotels) start at B1, so A1-A2 adults get almost no speaking beyond the Konuşma Parkı corner.

Park at B1 and B2 (for example a strong 10-year-old class or an international-school class) has no production tier: no building, no tier-3 items, and Konuşma Parkı is replaced by picture questions. The design says 'a 9-year-old B1 class keeps Park', but Park's rules cap the language at tier-1/2 recognition, so level and audience are not really independent here.

Park A1 non-readers. 'Everyone answers with A-B-C cards' assumes children can map a written option to a letter. For children who barely read, the options must be pictures with a big A/B/C badge, and the options must be read aloud. As written, 'MCQ with 3 options' in the tier map does not guarantee this. Having the seat-number student's card decide the answer also lets them copy from the rest of the class, so the individual check is weak. That is fine for learning, but it should be designed for on purpose.

The jail is called Kütüphane (library). Framing the library as a punishment square in a language-learning game sends the wrong message, especially to children and to MEB-minded teachers. Park and Arena already rename it; Stüdyo should too.

The built-in content cannot fill the tier map. grammar_mcq banks are MCQ only (~22 per unit), so tier-2 'gap without bank / qa phrase / error fix' and tier-3 speaking prompts, roleplays, error x8, category-list x6 and chance-cards have no built-in source. words.js has CEFR bands and TR glosses but, as far as described, no theme tags and no imageKey. So 'pick a built-in category' for Park (every item needs a picture) and for tier 3 depends on curated banks that do not exist yet.

LLM content is fragile for this game. One prompt must return 4-6 subtopics with at least 60 tiered items, a correct difficulty ladder inside each group, plus specials decks. LLMs label difficulty unreliably, so a tier-1 'cheap' place may ask something harder than tier 3, which breaks the price/difficulty promise. An abstract teacher prompt ('present perfect vs past simple') for Park will lose most items to the imageKey filter and silently fall back to unrelated built-in content.

Rule and vocabulary load for the teacher is very high: three rulesets, each with its own names for the same squares (Kamu Fonu / Supply Drop / Magic card; Kütüphane / Asteroid Belt / Stuck in the Sand), about 25 dials, and three different currencies. A teacher switching between a 5th-grade class and an adult class mid-day will mis-explain rules, and the 20 s explanation promise only holds for Park.

The Arena economy adds arithmetic without language: planet prices, docking fees, modules, half-price steals and a combo multiplier. 12-14-year-olds will enjoy it, but much of the turn goes on economic decisions rather than English. At A1 Genç Arena (13-year-olds, modules off) it degenerates into a quiz with credits, the same problem as adult A1.

The Deal Window (B1+) is the most authentic speaking in the game, but the teacher checks it by ticking whether a phrase frame was used. That rewards saying the formula, not negotiating, and the other teams sit idle for 60 s while one pair trades.

Park turns get repetitive. Counting every hop aloud is great for A1 numbers for the first round, but by round 3 at A2 it is dead time. 'Home sweet home' (repeat a word for +1 star) and the auto star on Hep Birlikte give stars for echoing rather than for retrieval.
The homepage name 'Kelime Şehri / Hazine Adası' plus Orbit Match is three names for one tile. That is confusing, and the teacher may think these are three separate games.
fixes: Turn shadow answers on by default in all modes. On every auto-checkable item, every non-active team answers on its whiteboard, and each correct team gets a small fixed reward (+1 star / +1 credit / +20). The active team still gets the place. Keep the whole-class moment on every turn, not just on Herkes Cevaplar squares, and aim for 1 item per 60 s or less.

Give adult A1-A2 a production path that fits the level. Add 'Cümle kirası lite' from A2: complete a sentence frame shown on screen ('I usually eat ___ for breakfast'). Turn houses on at A1 with a picture-free tier-2 item (TR to EN word typed, or a gap with a bank). Add an A2 'Mini deal' with 2 fixed frames ('Do you want to swap X for Y?' / 'Yes, OK' / 'No, thanks').

Unlock by level inside Park. At B1-B2 in Park, add a 'Show and Tell' square that replaces Windy Corner: a 20 s picture-describe task with starters, rated with Great/OK. Let a full Treasure Chest need one tier-2 gap. Level then really changes the language demand while the rules stay at 3.

Make picture options a hard rule for Park A1 and A2 Genç: each option is a picture with a large A/B/C colour badge (A red, B blue, C green, matching the printed cards), auto-read at 0.8x. Add an optional 'Tek başına' step where the seat student answers first and the class shows cards second, so the individual check is real.
Rename the Stüdyo jail to something neutral with no library or police imagery ('Trafik', 'Kayıp Eşya', 'Bekleme Salonu') and keep the error-fix escape.

Before building, create the missing curated banks: a speaking-prompt bank per level (at least 40), an error-sentence bank per level with errorType (at least 30), chance cards per mode and harshness, category-lists, and a theme tag plus imageKey map for the YLE/MEB A1-A2 subset of words.js (roughly 600-800 picturable words). Without them, the built-in path works only for adult MCQ.

Harden the LLM pipeline. Ask for items per subtopic without tiers, then assign tiers in code using a difficulty score (the word's CEFR band from words.js, sentence length, item type) instead of trusting the LLM's labels. Show the teacher a preview grid by group and tier with counts and a 'yeniden üret' button per group. If more than 30% of Park items are dropped for lacking a picture, warn the teacher in Turkish ('Bu konu küçük yaş için resimlenemiyor') instead of silently filling from other topics.

Give squares one set of names in the teacher chrome (Şans, Joker, Herkes, Bekleme, Konuşma) with skin-specific display names only on the student screen. Ship a one-page Turkish rule card per mode and cut the exposed dials to about 8, with the rest under 'Gelişmiş'.

Simplify the Arena economy. Use fixed prices (say 5), docking fee = tier, and the combo only. Make steals mean answering, not paying. Keep modules as the language gate (tier-2 item) so every economic action needs English.

Score the Deal Window on a 2-item rubric: a frame was used, and a reason or condition was given ('...because...' / 'if...'). Let the other teams vote Fair/Unfair on their whiteboards so they stay engaged, or run the Deal Window as a simultaneous 60 s phase where all pairs negotiate and teams hand in written deals.

Fade the hop counting after round 1 (the class counts only when the roll is 4 or more, or they count in 2s or backwards at A2). Replace 'repeat a word' rewards with quick retrieval ('Gogo shows a picture: say it!') so stars follow recall, not echo.

Use one homepage tile, 'Kelime Şehri', with the skin chosen automatically from the class profile (Hazine Adası / Orbit Match appear as the skin name in setup). Ship Stüdyo and Park first, as the risk list suggests, and hold Arena until shadow answers and the tier calibration are proven in class.

reviews.mergeWith: Snakes & Ladders / board race (Park 'Hazine Adası' ruleset only)
issues: Scope is really 3 games plus 5 skins, not one XL game. The three rulesets share dice and tokens but little else: Park has no economy, Arena has a small credit economy with combos, and Stüdyo has an economy with auctions and a Deal Window. Each needs its own balancing, art set, sound set, end screen and how-to. As written, this is 2-3 months of solo work and blocks the rest of the 10-game suite.

Stüdyo economy is too loose to matter in 30-45 min. A 1500 start against 20-60 base rent (20% of 100-300) and START +200 means no team ever feels pressure. Net worth also counts property prices, so buying is value-neutral, and the winner is mostly whoever landed on unowned squares (dice luck). Language accuracy barely moves the result, and the separate 'Language MVP' admits this.

Idle time. At 90-120 s per turn with 4 teams, each team acts once every 6-8 min. The whole-class moments (Herkes Cevaplar on 1-2 squares, steals, sealed bids) are occasional. 'Shadow answers' exists only as a toggle; it is not the default loop.

Teacher overload in Stüdyo B1+. In one turn the teacher may be banker, judge (D/Y), rubric rater, auctioneer (typing the highest sealed bid) and Deal Window referee (ticking frame use on both sides, then approving). That is too many modal decisions for one person at a projector, and trades stall the other teams for 60 s.

The control surface is huge: 30+ setup dials (rent mode, buy mode, harshness, comeback, Adil şans, dice mode, Beceri zarı, hint ladder...). Without presets it will feel like a settings form, not a game, and most combinations will never be tested.

Park's core rule is ambiguous. 'The whole class shows A-B-C cards, and the active team's seat-number student counts' means the teacher has to find one child's card in a sea of 30. 'Visit: both teams answer together' needs two readable responses at once. The 3-rule card hides 7 more self-explaining squares (Magic, Word Rain, Hep Birlikte, Harbour, Stuck in the Sand, Gogo's Nest, Windy Corner), so the real rule load is well above 3.

Park is barely a property game. With no ownership consequence beyond a shared 'Visit' star, it is a roll-and-collect board race. It overlaps heavily with the planned Snakes & Ladders / board-race game and risks feeling like an MCQ quiz on a map.

Asset load is underestimated. Park needs an imageKey on EVERY item, so a picture library of 300-600 consistent icons is required, or LLM items get silently dropped until the pack is empty. It also needs 3 illustrated boards (island, city with a day-night cycle and lit windows, galaxy), deed-card mini illustrations, a Gogo mascot with 4-5 animation states, 8 animal mascots, 6 emblems, adult tokens, a chest/gem animation, and 3 separate sound palettes (marimba, woodblock/piano, synth).

Read-aloud at 0.8x relies on the Web Speech API. On Turkish-locale Windows classroom PCs and smartboards, often only the Turkish voice is installed, so English prompts get read with Turkish phonology or not at all. The same goes for Gogo's 'say the answer'.

LLM generation is the weakest link. One prompt has to return 4-6 subtopics, about 60 tiered items across 8+ item types, plus 8 errors, 6 speaking prompts, 6 category lists, 4 taboo cards, 12-16 chance cards and roleplays: over 100 objects in one JSON. DeepSeek will truncate, repeat, mislabel difficulty tiers (it cannot reliably tell a diff-1 item from a diff-3 one), and produce gap items with more than one correct answer. It also hits the rate limit and takes 30-60 s, and the teacher is standing in front of the class while it runs.

Tier-3 and specials content does not exist in the repo. grammar_mcq and words.js cover tiers 1-2, but there is no curated bank of speaking prompts, error sentences by errorType, category lists, taboo cards, level-tagged chance cards, or Deal Window frames. The 'fill from built-in banks' fallback cannot fill those slots.

Pedagogical and naming problems. 'Kütüphane' as the jail frames the library as punishment, which is a bad message from an English teacher. 'Konuşma Parkı' (the pot corner) and 'Park pot' collide with the 'Oyun Parkı' audience name in the teacher UI. 'Kamu Fonu' and 'Şans' are the literal Turkish Monopoly deck names, which brings the trade dress closer than needed.

Board legibility on a projector. A 20-28 square ring around a 16:9 screen gives squares about 6-8% of the width, and names like 'Irregular Verb Avenue', rent pips and ownership flags will not be readable from the back row. The design never says where the card and question appear relative to the ring.

Multi-step Undo, autosave after every action, named save slots and the 'Last time...' flyover are all promised. If the state is built as mutable objects they will be buggy, and undoing across animations and teacher-judged steps is a classic source of desync.
Arena and Park price, rent, star and credit numbers are unrelated scales. The engine has to clamp every chance-card amount per mode, and each mode needs separate tuning and testing.
fixes: Phase the build explicitly. v1 = engine + Stüdyo 'Kelime Şehri' on the Standart 20 board with 1 skin, and A1-A2 rules only (no auction and no Deal Window). v1.1 = Arena 'Orbit Match'. v1.2 = B1+ auctions and trades. Türkiye Turu and World Cities come later. Consider moving Park 'Hazine Adası' into the Snakes & Ladders / board-race game as its kids mode (mergeWith for the Park ruleset only), and give kids a simpler ownership twist there, so this game stays a true property game for 12+ and adults.

Architect the state as a pure reducer over an action log (ROLL, MOVE, ANSWER_JUDGED, CLAIM, PAY, ...). Undo, autosave (store the log plus the seed in localStorage under a versioned schema), save slots and the 'Last time...' flyover (replay the CLAIM actions) then come almost for free. Keep animations as views of the state, never sources of it.

Make accuracy drive the win. Retune Stüdyo: start 600, START +100, rent ladder 30/60/100/150% with a per-landing cap, and a +40 bank payout for every correct answer. Score = cash + 50% of property value + correct-answer points, which merges 'Language MVP' into net worth. Simulate 1000 games headless (a Node script over the reducer) to check that luck explains less than half of the variance in the final ranking.

Make shadow answers the default loop for Arena and Stüdyo. Every non-active team answers the same item on its whiteboard, the teacher taps the team chips that are right, and each gets a small payout (+10 / +1). This kills idle time and costs one tap row.

Cap teacher load. The teacher chrome shows one decision at a time as big buttons, never a form. Replace the sealed-bid auction typing with tap-to-award: tap the winning team chip, then choose from 4 preset bid chips. Deal Window: a single 'Anlaşma onaylandı' button with property and cash pickers; drop the frame-ticking and just show the frames.

Ship 3 presets per audience ('Hızlı', 'Standart', 'Tam') with a single summary line. Put the other dials behind 'Gelişmiş' and remove the untested combinations (for example, Red harshness only in 'Tam').
