Park, if kept here: drop the seat-number-in-crowd rule. The active team answers on its own big A-B-C card (one card per team), and the class TPR response is a separate 'Sınıf!' lighthouse tap. Count the real rules honestly, either merge the specials into 3 square types (Treasure / Magic / Friend) or cut them, and test the 20-second explanation with a stopwatch.

Picture pipeline: use a single self-hosted or CDN emoji-style SVG set (e.g. Twemoji or OpenMoji via jsdelivr) mapped to a curated imageKey whitelist of about 400 keys. The LLM must pick imageKeys from that list (it is given the list in the prompt), and the validator rejects anything else. For kids, drop items without a key, but backfill from the built-in bank before the game starts, not mid-game.

Audio: at startup, check speechSynthesis for an en-* voice and show a Turkish warning with a fallback toggle ('Öğretmen okur'). For built-in kids banks, pre-generate MP3s at build time (short words only, well under 5 MB) so read-aloud works with no voice installed.

LLM pipeline: split generation into parallel per-group calls (about 15 items each) with JSON-schema validation and one repair retry per group. Assign difficulty tiers IN CODE from the words.js CEFR band and the item type, not from the LLM's label. Check gap uniqueness with a second cheap LLM pass or a rule (one bank option only; reject sentences where two bank words fit). Take all corners and specials (errors, chance cards, speaking prompts, taboo cards, frames) from curated static banks by level, never from the LLM. Show a generated-pack preview with swap buttons, and cache packs so the next lesson needs no call.

Write the missing curated banks before coding the modes: about 40 error sentences per level tagged by errorType, 30 speaking prompts per level, 20 category lists, 40 chance cards per audience, and Deal Window frames. This is the real content cost; budget for it.

Rename for clarity and pedagogy. Jail becomes 'Tamir Atölyesi / Fix-it Garage' (fix a sentence to drive out). The pot corner becomes 'Sahne / Open Mic'. 'Kamu Fonu' becomes 'Joker Kutusu'. Keep 'Şans' only if it tests well; 'Sürpriz' is safer and clearer.

Layout for the projector: a ring of large squares showing only an icon plus a colour band, with names in a legend. Every question or card opens as a full centre overlay at 5vh+ type, and the camera zooms on the active square during the hop. Test at 1280×720 with a 3 m viewing distance, and give touch targets of at least 64 px for smartboards.

Keep assets modest but distinctive, because that is what makes it feel like a real game rather than a skinned quiz: a CSS-3D die, a card flip, token hops, coin fly-to-badge, and a skyline and night-window shader as SVG layers. Keep one sound palette per mode to 8 or fewer short OGG/MP3 files (under 300 KB total). Code-split each skin's SVG/audio bundle so the page loads only the chosen skin.

catalog.rankReason: Requested (Monopoly-style). With c23 merged in, it is the suite's one board-game engine. Build it as a pure reducer over an action log, which gives undo, autosave and save-and-continue next lesson almost for free. v1: 'Kelime Şehri' on one Standart 20 board with A1-A2 rules (no auctions, no Deal Window). The Oyun Parkı ruleset becomes c23's 'Hazine Yolu' ladder race with Ask/Tell speaking squares and no money. Ask/Tell squares join every ruleset. v1.1 adds an Arena theme that is not childish (for example a theme-park tycoon); v1.2 adds B1+ auctions and trades. Shadow answers are on by default: a team scores when more than half its members show the right card. Adult A1-A2 get 'Cümle kirası lite', and the economy is tightened so money matters.

catalog.name: Konuşma Çarkı (Speaking Wheel, Story Dice & Just a Minute)
catalog.familiarAs: Wordwall Random Wheel / Open the Box / Baamboozle Story Dice / BBC Just a Minute / Would You Rather
catalog.oneLiner: A speaking-first game with five modes that share one scoreboard. Spin for a speaker and a topic, open mystery boxes, roll picture dice to build a class story in the target grammar, keep talking through a fair Just a Minute challenge, or pick a side in Would You Rather. Children get a talk rocket and picture frames, and adults get the full BBC rules.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 60 s, teacher chrome in Turkish)
1. One summary line (e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk') with a 'Değiştir' link.
2. Content: pick a built-in category or MEB unit, or type a free prompt (Turkish is fine, e.g. '8. sınıf Teen Life, hafta sonu alışkanlıkları'). The LLM returns a pack. A preview grid shows every card, each with 'Bu kartı değiştir' and 'Yeniden üret' buttons.
3. Pick one mode, or a 'Ders akışı' preset that fills a 40-minute Turkish lesson, e.g. Would You Rather 5 → Wheel 10 → Story Dice 15 → Just a Minute 8 → review 2.
4. Teams: 2-6, each with its mascot, emblem or name from the audience skin. The speaker source is ALWAYS a seat number inside a team (1-N). No student name is ever typed, shown or stored. 'Herkes bir kez' is on by default: a seat that has spoken greys out until every seat has had a turn.
5. Practice round, not scored. Oyun Parkı: Gogo the parrot spins, lands on 'My pet' and gives a model answer by TTS ('I have a cat. It is orange. It is funny.'), 20-30 s. Arena and Stüdyo: an 'Örnek cevap' button plays a model answer at the group's level.

MODE A: WHEEL (the core loop, about 90 s per turn)
1. Space spins the speaker spinner, which picks a team emblem and then a seat number. With the Light comeback, the trailing team may instead choose one of 3 revealed topic segments.
2. Space spins the topic wheel: 6-12 segments, each an emoji plus 2 words at most. The winning segment expands into the full prompt card. A1/A2 Genç hear it read automatically at 0.8x; everyone else has a speaker button. For Would You Rather cards, the two options appear after the options delay (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s).
3. Team talk huddle (kids 10 s, Arena 15 s, adults 20 s). The starters[] and useful[] words stay on screen, and teammates whisper ideas.
4. The speaker talks for the level's target time (table in levelTuning). An ON AIR light glows and decorative sound bars bounce. There is an optional live mic-level mode: local only, never recorded, never scored, off by default.
5. Follow-up: a listener from another team asks one follow-up question, scored +1 if it is a real, on-topic question. The 'Dig deeper' button reveals followUps[] easiest first (question ladder G24). Kids read the follow-up in chorus and the speaker answers.
6. Thumbs: the class shows 1-3 fingers (clear / interesting / used the helper language). The teacher taps the final award with one key. The segment is then removed ('Çıkar' on) or stays.

MODE B: OPEN THE BOX (Wordwall Open the Box + Baamboozle power tiles)
The grid has 12 boxes for kids, 16 hex tiles in Arena and 20-24 envelopes for adults, all numbered. The active team calls a number and the box opens. About 75% hold a prompt, which runs steps 3-6 above. About 15% hold a power from the Harshness level: Green (Gift 5 to a team you tap, Everyone +2, Double, Shield, Brain break), Yellow opt-in (Steal 5 capped at the target's score, Swap turn order), Red opt-in for adults (Reset, Swap scores, Virus). About 10% hold a mini-challenge (act it, sing the line, describe the picture without saying the word, or a B1+ two-speaker role-play with information-gap cards, 60 s). The round ends when the grid is empty or the lesson-fit timer calls it.

MODE C: STORY DICE + CHAIN STORY (co-operative, 12-18 min)
1. An opener line appears on a parchment 'story scroll'.
2. Roll 3-9 picture dice (the count depends on level): WHO, WHERE and WHAT, plus FEELING at A2, TWIST from B1, and an ENDING die at B2.
3. Chain Story layer: at the start, each team gets one face-down secret card (a word and picture). Using it at a sensible moment is worth +1, and the card flips when it is used.
4. In turn, each team picks one unused die and adds one sentence (1-3 for adults). The sentence must use the die's picture and the target structure, e.g. A2 'past simple', B1 'past continuous + suddenly', B2 'past perfect / third conditional'. From B1 it also needs a connector from the level list (then, suddenly, however, while, by the time).
5. The teacher taps ✓picture ✓structure ✓connector ✓secret, and can type the sentence or just tap 'eklendi' (the scroll then shows the die icon and a quill).
6. Kids repeat the new line in chorus. From B1, a listener from another team retells the story so far in one sentence.
7. Each team has one re-roll per story. The used die slides into the scroll as an illuminated capital. The last die is 'The End', and that team must close the story.
8. A shared 'Story stars' meter rewards the whole class, so the co-op goal matters more than the points. Finale: the class votes on a title and the funniest twist (+2 to its team; with kids, every team also gets a title). 'Yazdır' prints an A4 'Our Story' page with the dice pictures as illustrations and team emblems but no names.

MODE D: JUST A MINUTE (competitive fluency, called 'Talk Rocket' in Oyun Parkı and 'Mic Challenge' in Arena)
1. Spin the topic (only prompts that are open enough, jamOk). The speaker gets 10 s to think with starters on screen.
2. The timer runs for the target time. Any rival team can press its challenge key (1-6) or shout 'Challenge!'. The timer freezes and the teacher picks the reason with H (Hesitation: silence over 5 s at A1/A2, 4 s at B1, 3 s at B2), D (Deviation, from B1; for adults this also covers factual nonsense) or R (Repetition: the same content word more than twice; B2 only; words printed on the card and function words are exempt, as on the BBC show). The teacher then rules Y or N.
3. Stüdyo scoring (full BBC): a valid challenge gives the challenger +1 and its speaker takes over the same topic for the remaining time. An invalid challenge gives the speaker +1. Whoever is speaking at the whistle gets +2. A turn with no valid challenge gets +3 and a gold 'Clean minute!' badge.
4. Arena (Nazik): a valid challenge gives the challenger +1 'Sharp ears', but the speaker keeps the floor and every point. The takeover 'relay' only applies when the teacher opts into mild steals.
5. Oyun Parkı: no challenges at all (see teenVersion).
6. Anti-spam: each team may make 2 wrong challenges per round, after which its key locks until the next round.
7. Twists: 'Yasak kelime' (B1+ opt-in, B2 default for adults: the speaker cannot say very / thing / good / like as a filler), and an adult 90-second 'Double or nothing' wager on a surprise topic.
8. Two alternative modes: 'Koç modu' (no challenges, just topics and a timer), and 'Herkes konuşur' (simultaneous; below).

MODE E: WOULD YOU RATHER (warmer, stirrer or settler, 3-8 min)
1. Two pictured options appear.
2. The class votes with their bodies: move to the left or right wall, or, for fixed desks, stand for A and sit for B, or raise A/B cards.
3. The teacher taps the counts and two vote bars race.
4. Two volunteers from each side give a reason with the on-screen frame. From B1, each side may answer back once ('But if you..., you'd...'). At B2, reasons use concession ('Even though..., I'd still...').
5. Optional +1 'Best reason'. By default it is unscored, as a settler.

HERKES KONUŞUR (large classes of 30-40, A1-B1)
Groups of 3-4 number themselves. The screen shows only the topic, the starters, the timer and 'Speaker 2 →'. Kids' listeners are 'Word spotters' who tick the helper words they hear, while adult listeners count their own 'ums'. Each listener asks one question at the end, and then the screen rotates to the next number. No score, or teams self-report a star.

PAIRS
The screen assigns roles: A speaks, B uses the follow-up ladder. After a chime they switch and a new card appears.

SCORING (follows the audience dials)
- Kids: 1-3 stars per turn (spoke / used a helper word or frame / the rocket landed). Stars never go down. An effort star goes to the class album.
- Arena: points, plus a combo for consecutive clean turns (a teacher-confirmed full-length turn with the target language): x1.5 at 3 in a row, x2 at 5. The floor is 0.
- Adults: points, optional negatives (a wrong challenge -1) and wager rounds.
- There are no speed points anywhere.
- Hint ladder, used when a speaker is stuck. Kids: picture, then a starter read aloud, then Gogo's model sentence, all free. Arena: starter, then useful words, then the model first sentence, each costing 1 point from that turn only (never below 0). Adults: useful words, then starter, then the Turkish gloss of the prompt (can be switched off).
- Endings follow the dial: kids' titles, the Arena podium with stat awards, and the adults' full scores plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' review (see adultVersion).
catalog.playerSetup: Default: the whole class in 2-6 teams on one projector (kids 3-4 mascot teams, Arena 2-6 emblem teams, adults 2-4 teams or individuals with a rotating spokesperson and pair consultation). The speaker is chosen by the team + seat-number spinner and never by name. 'Herkes bir kez' guarantees every seat speaks before anyone repeats. Alternatives: Pairs mode (A speaks, B asks follow-ups, then swap); 'Herkes konuşur' simultaneous groups of 3-4 for crowded Turkish state-school classes of 30-40, where the screen only runs the topic, timer and speaker number; and a no-score 'Koç modu' for anxious or brand-new classes. Story Dice is co-operative, with the whole class behind one scroll and teams taking turns.
catalog.contentShape:
One content pack feeds all five modes.

(1) speaking-prompt items, the core, 24-60 per pack.
- mode: talk | describe | wyr | opinion | debate | story | hypothetical | jam | ask.
- prompt: within the group's word cap (A1 Genç 0-4 words, where media.emoji or img carries the meaning, e.g. '🐶 My pet'; A2 Genç 8; B1 Genç 14; B2 Genç 20; A1 10; A2 15; B1 25; B2 40).
- optA/optB: when mode='wyr'. Each needs its own picture in Genç groups.
- side: for debate.
- starters[≤3]: frames that use only grammar on the level whitelist. They are always shown to kids, and each is at most 5 words for Genç.
- followUps[≤3]: the question ladder, easy to deeper.
- useful[≤5]: helper words. They are also exempt from the B2 repetition challenge.
- secs: overridden by the level/audience time table.
- target: e.g. 'unit:a2-09', 'fn:giving reasons'.
- media.emoji: required for every Genç prompt.
The game computes: wheelLabel (emoji + 2 words at most, for the wheel segment), jamOk (open enough for 45-60 s: modes talk/describe/opinion/jam/debate) and boxOk.

(2) vocab items: the story-dice faces and the Chain Story secret cards. Every face needs media.emoji or img at every level, because dice are pictures. The game uses term, pos, concrete=true, defEasy (tap a face to hear it) and example (the model sentence for Gogo and the hint ladder).

(3) chance-card items for the Open-the-Box power and mini-challenge boxes.
- kind: reward | bonus | swap | task.
- task: speak | act | sing | draw.
- text, plus textTr for A1 Genç.
- amount: clamped by the engine to the Harshness level (Green only for kids).
- secs.

(4) roleplay items, B1+: the two-speaker box and wheel segment. Fields: scenario, setting, roleA and roleB (each with title, info[], goals[≤3], useful[]), twist?, checklist[] (the teacher's success criteria) and secs (60-90).

Envelope pack.frames.dice:
- opener: the story's first line, within the cap.
- faces: {who[], where[], what[], feeling[]?, twist[] (B1+), ending[] (B2)}, each a vocab id or a short event face {label, emoji} such as '⚡ The lights went out'.
- connectors[]: by level.
- targetGrammar: {id, frameEn, e.g. 'Yesterday, the ___ + past simple', checkTr}.

Model answers ('Örnek cevap', Gogo's demo) are generated on demand at the group's level and cap, and are not stored in the item.

RUNTIME-ONLY DATA: seat ticks, team names, emblems and mottos, vote counts, the story-scroll text and the teacher's 'Duyduklarımız' notes. These are kept only in localStorage inside the local class profile, never sent to the server or the LLM, and wiped by a 'Temizle' button.

VALIDATOR:
- Word caps. A long prompt is split into two cards rather than shrunk.
- The grammar whitelist for starters.
- The teenSafe filter for every Genç group: no dating, alcohol, horror, violence, gambling, politics, brands or adult domains.
- A privacy filter: no questions about family income, religion, parents' jobs, health or real appearance, and personal-sounding prompts are rewritten into a dream or fictional frame ('Describe your dream house', not 'Describe your house').

BUILT-IN CATEGORIES:
- Kids (YLE / MEB grade 5-6): Animals, Food, My day, School, Hobbies, Weather, Superpowers, Space, Holidays, plus MEB units such as My Town, Games and Hobbies, Party Time, The Animal Shelter, Festivals.
- Arena (MEB grade 7-8): Friendship, Teen Life, In the Kitchen, On the Phone, The Internet, Adventures, Tourism, Chores, Science, Natural Forces.
- Adults: Travel, Job interviews, Small talk, Complaints, Eating out, Technology, City life, Habits and health, Money decisions, 'Tell us about a time when...', Hypotheticals.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO, 'Speaking Night'. An editorial quiz-night look: cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, system sans and serif numerals. No mascot and no voice lines, only a neutral caption ('Round 2 · Travel'). Woodblock and piano sounds, and a 0.6 s chime with the score rolling up. English on the student screen, Turkish in the teacher chrome. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs', 'Present Perfectionists').

- Speaking Wheel: a game-show wheel with a woodblock tick. Turns run 30-60 s. The 'Dig deeper' button pushes past one-line answers with 2 follow-ups.
- Open the Box: 20-24 sealed envelopes that tear open. Green and Yellow powers by default; Red (Reset, Swap scores, Virus) is opt-in. B1+ role-play envelopes: a job interview with a hidden weakness, a hotel complaint where the receptionist has a secret policy, a flatmate negotiation.
- Story Dice: 'Story Cubes night' with adult openers ('The business trip that went wrong', 'The last train home', 'Nobody noticed the missing painting until…'). Narrative tenses are required from B1, with a one-sentence retell by a listener.
- Just a Minute: the full BBC rules. Hesitation (3-4 s), Repetition (B2) and Deviation (including factual nonsense). A valid challenge gives +1 and the challenger takes over. An invalid challenge gives the speaker +1. Speaking at the whistle is +2, and an uninterrupted turn is +3 with the gold 'Clean minute!'. There are 2 wrong challenges per team per round, the 'Yasak kelime' filler ban (very / thing / good / like), a 90 s 'Double or nothing' wager on a surprise topic, and optional negatives (a wrong challenge -1).
- Would You Rather: four corners with second conditionals ('Would you rather work four long days or five short days?'), one rebuttal per side, and concession at B2.

Adults answer through a rotating spokesperson with 20 s pair consultation. Nobody is picked by name.

DELAYED CORRECTION: 'Duyduklarımız'. During turns, the teacher presses N and types a sentence they heard. It is stored without the speaker, and in presenter view on an extended display it stays off the projector. At the end, the 'Kaçırılanlar' board shows 5-8 anonymous sentences for a 3-minute whole-class 'fix it', plus the starters and useful words the class never used. Full scores are shown and the finale is modest.
catalog.teenVersion:
TWO SKINS FOR 9-13, EACH WITH ITS OWN RULE PACK (not a re-colour). The group label never appears on the student screen.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1/A2 Genç): 'Gogo's Talk Park'
Look: warm cream, rounded shapes, big pictures, an Andika-type font with a single-storey a, and animal team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin, bear). The host is Gogo the parrot: it repeats words, models the choral answer, demos every mode in a practice round, and sleeps on the wheel during the pause screen. Sounds are marimba and xylophone, never buzzers.

The pictogram rule card has 3 rules, read in Turkish by the teacher in under 20 s: ① Spin! ② Say it with the helper words. ③ Everyone says it too.
Checklist: no elimination, no score below zero, a whole-class response in every turn, and no violent failure imagery.

A turn:
1. The team's mascot glows and a seat spinner picks 1-5.
2. The picture prompt appears and is read aloud at 0.8x.
3. CHORUS: the whole class says the starter ('I like...').
4. A 10 s Team talk.
5. The speaker talks while a rocket rises. The timer counts UP to a goal (A1 20 s, A2 30 s) with a calm ring that is never red. Stopping early lands the rocket on the Moon (★★); reaching the goal lands it on Mars (★★★). It never crashes.
6. 'Rocket landed!' Everyone claps twice in rhythm.
7. Gogo reads a follow-up question ('What colour is it?'), the class echoes it, and the speaker answers.
8. Stars (1-3) and a sticker.

Help card: each seat has one per game. The speaker picks a friend who whispers a starter; the speaker still says it and still earns stars.
If the speaker is stuck for 5 s, the teacher presses W. The rocket wobbles gently, the starters grow, and the TTS reads one. If the speaker is still stuck, Gogo says a model sentence, the whole class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album.
There are no challenges at all.

Modes:
- Gogo's Wheel: 8 fat picture segments.
- Surprise Boxes: 12 boxes. Gogo pops out of each. Green powers only; the Brain break is 'Stand up and move like a robot, 20 s'.
- Story Dice: 3-5 big picture dice (pirates, monsters, zoo, space). The class choruses every new line.
- This or That?: stand or sit, or 'hands on head for A, shoulders for B' for fixed desks.

Pacing: 3 rounds of 3-5 min with a 45 s This-or-That stirrer or a 60 s whisper-the-frame settler in between, 15-25 min in total.
Ending: every team gets a title (Brave Speakers, Super Listeners, Best Storytellers, Big Voices), confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale, and the printed story becomes a page in the class album.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1/B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç group at MEB grade 6-8 or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor'): 'Mic Challenge'
Look: dark navy and charcoal with neon accents in the team colours and a condensed display font. Emblems are bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown and diamond. In 10 s, each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. There is no mascot and nothing cute, pastel or 'Good job, superstar!'. A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('CLEAN 45!', 'SHARP EARS', 'COMBO x3'). Short synth blips, and at most 1.2 s of combo text.

Modes:
- Spin Match: a neon wheel whose winning segment glows in the team colour.
- Hex Grid: 16 hex tiles. Green powers, with Yellow as opt-in.
- Plot Dice: dice with a twist die. The target grammar is past continuous + suddenly at B1 and past perfect at B2.
- Pick a Side: Would You Rather.
- Mic Challenge: Just a Minute for 30-45 s. Challenges are for hesitation (5 s at A1/A2, 4 s at B1, 3 s at B2) and, from B1, going off topic. A valid challenge gives the challenger +1 'Sharp ears', but the speaker keeps the floor and every point; a takeover only happens if the teacher opts into mild steals. A wrong challenge gives the speaker +1. Each team gets 2 wrong challenges per round. Speaking at the whistle is +2 and a clean turn is +3.

Scoring: a combo for consecutive clean turns (x1.5 at 3 in a row, x2 at 5), with a floor at zero.
Content: teenSafe, concrete topics (school rules, sport, gadgets without brands, dream trips, games and apps as habits). Personal questions are always framed as dream or fictional.
Ending: a podium with stat awards (Longest streak, Sharp Ears, Clean 45, Comeback, Best twist). There is never a last place, and nobody is ever named.
catalog.levelTuning:
LEVEL AND AUDIENCE ARE SEPARATE DIALS.

Target talk time:
| Group | Oyun Parkı / Arena | Stüdyo (adults) |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | 15-20 s | 30 s |
| A2 | 25-30 s | 40 s |
| B1 | 40 s | 60 s |
| B2 | 45 s | 60 s, 90 s wager |

A1:
- Prompts: picture + 0-4 words for kids, 10 words or fewer for adults. Modes describe/talk/ask.
- Frames: 'I have / I like / It is / There is / I can see', always on screen.
- Story Dice: 3 dice (WHO, WHERE, WHAT), present tense ('The cat is in the kitchen.').
- Follow-ups: a yes/no question read in chorus.
- Just a Minute: rocket or Koç modu only; hesitation is a 5 s nudge with no penalty.
- Would You Rather: pictures, 'I like A.'
- Adults: 'Tell me about your morning', with the TR gloss allowed.

A2:
- Likes and dislikes with 'because', 'going to' plans.
- Story Dice: 4-5 dice (adds FEELING) in past simple ('Yesterday... Then...'). Connectors: and, but, then, because.
- Hesitation-only challenges at 5 s.
- Follow-ups: simple wh-questions from the ladder.

B1:
- Opinions with because/so, 'Have you ever...?' experiences, 'used to', 'I'd rather... because...'.
- Story Dice: 6-7 dice with a TWIST die, past continuous + suddenly. Connectors: however, while, after that, suddenly.
- Just a Minute: hesitation (4 s) and deviation.
- Would You Rather: one rebuttal per side.
- Follow-ups must be wh-questions. Role-play boxes switch on. A listener retells the story in one sentence.

B2:
- Second and third conditionals, speculation (might / must have), concession (even though, whereas), debate cards with an assigned side.
- Story Dice: 8-9 dice with TWIST and ENDING, and narrative tenses including past perfect.
- Just a Minute: all three challenges (hesitation 3 s, repetition, deviation) plus the 'Yasak kelime' filler ban. Adults also get the 90 s wager.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics ('Should school start at 10?', 'Plan the perfect class trip'), not abstract debate.

MIXED ABILITY: 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' changes the time (-10 s / 0 / +10 s), the helper words shown (5 / 3 / 0), whether the starters are on screen, and the word-band mix. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one whole level, because MEB's nominal levels often overstate state-school classes.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 3-10 as a warmer, stirrer or settler (one Would You Rather or 3 wheel spins); 15-20 for a Wheel, Box or Story Dice round; 20-35 for a full Just a Minute match (adults). Kids' sessions are capped at 15-25 min by the pacing dial.
catalog.teacherControls:
PER MODE
- Wheel: speaker source (team + seat numbers only), 'Herkes bir kez' on/off, remove the prompt after it is used, 6-12 segments, spin length 2-6 s, and 'let the trailing team choose'.
- Boxes: box count 12-24, power mix (%), Harshness level (Green / Yellow / Red, locked to Green for kids).
- Story Dice: dice count 3-9, which dice sets (WHO / WHERE / WHAT / FEELING / TWIST / ENDING), target grammar, connector list, secret cards on/off, one re-roll per team, type-along or tap-only, and print the story.
- Just a Minute: time per turn, allowed challenge types, hesitation threshold, takeover relay on/off (off in Nazik), wrong-challenge cap, word-ban list, wager round, Koç modu, and 'Herkes konuşur' simultaneous mode.
- Would You Rather: voting style (walls / stand-sit / cards), rebuttal on/off, 'Best reason' point on/off.

GLOBAL
Scores on/off, points per event, optional negatives (adults), combo on/off, Comeback (Off / Light / Strong), think time, speaking timer or 'Süresiz', read-aloud speed, TR gloss toggle, audience skin / rule pack / level overrides saved in the local class profile, 'Kolay / Orta / Zor', 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır', per-card edit / replace / regenerate in the preview, the 'Ders akışı' lesson-fit presets, presenter view on an extended display (teacher notes and controls stay off the projector), reduced motion, and 'Temizle' to wipe the local class data.

KEYBOARD
| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Space | spin, roll or next |
| Enter | confirm award |
| 1-6 | team challenge |
| H / D / R | challenge reason |
| Y / N | valid / invalid |
| W | nudge a stuck speaker |
| = | +10 s |
| T | pause |
| S | Süresiz |
| U | undo last score |
| N | note (Duyduklarımız) |
| B | blank screen |
| F | full screen |
| P | print |
catalog.delightDetails:
- Wheel: a pointer flap bends and ticks over each peg as the wheel slows on an ease-out curve, with a last-peg 'creep' for suspense. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo flutters onto the pointer and squawks the topic word. In Arena the winning segment flashes a 'LOCKED IN' stamp in the team colour. In Stüdyo there is a woodblock tick and serif numerals.
- Boxes: Gogo pops out of kids' boxes, neon seams split open Arena hex tiles, and adult envelopes tear open with a paper sound.
- Dice: they tumble in CSS 3D and land face-up with a wooden clack (kids get marimba), then slide into the story scroll as illuminated capitals. Each new sentence types in like a storybook, and the printed 'Our Story' page carries the dice pictures and team emblems.
- Just a Minute: a red ON AIR light and bouncing sound bars (decorative; no recording ever). Each team's challenge key has its own blip, and a gold 'Clean minute!' badge appears. In Oyun Parkı the rocket rises with a soft trail and lands on the Moon or Mars, followed by the whole class's two-clap 'Rocket landed!'.
- Would You Rather: the vote bars race as the teacher taps the counts.
- A 'Story stars' meter fills for the whole class.
- The pause screen shows Gogo asleep on the wheel (kids) or a slow neon pulse (Arena).
- End titles: Brave Speakers and Super Listeners for kids; Sharp Ears and Longest streak in Arena; 'Best speaker of the day' goes to a team, never to a named student.
- Reduced motion swaps every animation for a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- Assessment rests on the teacher's judgement: the app never claims to judge speech. It gives one-key awards, peer thumbs and a checklist to make judging fast and consistent.
- A few students dominate: 'Herkes bir kez', seat-number spinners, team-level scoring, and Pairs or 'Herkes konuşur' modes that raise talk time in classes of 30-40.
- Speaking anxiety, especially for weaker speakers: Koç modu, the rocket that counts up and never fails, help and pass cards, chorus starters, 'Örnek cevap', and no challenges for kids.
- Challenge spam or conflict in Just a Minute: a cap of 2 wrong challenges, the teacher rules every challenge, and Nazik keeps the speaker's points and floor for teens.
- Privacy: no names, no recording, and the optional mic level is local and visual only. The scroll and notes stay in localStorage with 'Temizle'. Personal prompts for minors are rewritten into dream or fictional frames.
- Unsafe or unsuitable LLM content (commercial Would You Rather decks often have it): the teenSafe and privacy validator, and preview with per-card regenerate.
- Stories drifting or running long: the dice limit, the 'The End' die and lesson-fit timing.
- Noise in simultaneous and body-voting modes: the calm 'settler' presets and blank screen (B).
- Five modes make the build large: ship Wheel + Just a Minute first, then Boxes, then Story Dice and Would You Rather, all on one shared turn engine.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (G19 shared branching story, G24 question ladder; no recording, no student data stored)
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Open the Box -> merge into the existing /sinif-oyunu Baamboozle tile board as a 'speaking-prompt' content source. Story Dice -> ship later as its own game (or phase 2), not as mode C of this one.

issues: SMART-BOARD CONTROL IS BUILT FOR A KEYBOARD. The whole flow runs on keys: Space, 1-6, H/D/R, Y/N, W, =, T, U, N and B. A MEB interactive board (often Pardus, touch only) usually has no keyboard within reach of a teacher standing at the board. As written, Just a Minute adjudication and the W nudge cannot be done at the board.

SETUP IS NOT 60 SECONDS. Checking an LLM pack of 24-60 cards in a preview grid, choosing a mode or Ders akışı, setting up 2-6 teams and entering seat counts takes 3-6 minutes in front of 28 restless kids. The LLM call also needs working internet, which is often unreliable in state schools.

WHEEL MODE LEAVES MOST STUDENTS IDLE. One speaker per turn means 1 of 28 is talking. The '90 s per turn' figure is optimistic: two spin animations of 2-6 s each, a 10 s huddle, 20-30 s of talk, a follow-up, a thumbs vote and the award come to about 2-2.5 minutes with kids. A 15-minute round gets 6-7 speakers, so about 21 kids speak alone zero times. The chorus lines are the only moments where everyone is active.

'HERKES BIR KEZ' CANNOT FINISH IN ONE LESSON with 28 seats, and nothing says it continues across lessons. There is also no handling for absent students: the spinner lands on seat 6 of a team where 6 is absent, or teams are uneven (7/7/7/6).

KIDS DON'T REMEMBER SEAT NUMBERS. At 10-12, 'Panda seat 4' produces 'Me? No, I'm 5!' arguments unless the numbers are physically on desks or cards. The design never mentions giving out number cards, and each dispute adds 20-30 s.

JUST A MINUTE ADJUDICATION IS HEAVY. The teacher has to listen, count 3-5 s silences by feel, press a team key, a reason key and then Y/N, all while 5 teams shout 'Challenge!'. With kids this becomes a noise spike every turn and a string of fairness arguments ('it was only 3 seconds!'). The app cannot show the silence because the mic is off by default.

THE ARENA CHALLENGE INCENTIVE TARGETS WEAK SPEAKERS. Because a valid challenge scores +1 'Sharp ears', teams gain the most by hunting the most hesitant speaker. This happens even under Nazik mode, and in a 13-year-old class it is social cruelty with a scoreboard attached.
PEER THUMBS (1-3 fingers) FOR 10-12 YEAR-OLDS turns into a popularity vote: friends get 3, rivals get 1. It also adds 15-20 s per turn, and the teacher overrides it anyway.

STORY DICE DEAD TIME. With 4 teams and 5-9 dice, each team spends 30-60 s building a sentence under a grammar constraint while the others wait. Typing the sentence at a touch board is impractical. 'Yazdır' assumes a classroom printer, which most state classrooms lack.
THE STORY CANNOT BE STOPPED AT THE BELL. The story only closes when a team plays 'The End', so if the bell rings mid-story the teacher has no one-tap ending.
BODY VOTING (walls) with 28 kids in fixed rows of desks is chaotic and loud. Stand/sit is the only realistic option, but the default wording lists walls first.
SCORING THE FOLLOW-UP QUESTION (+1 if 'real and on-topic') adds another teacher judgment every turn. Stacked with the thumbs vote and the award, that is three judgments per turn.

DUYDUKLARIMIZ IS NOT PRIVATE ON A MIRRORED SCREEN. Most classrooms mirror to one display, so presenter view is rare, and typing N notes while the student is still talking pulls the teacher's attention off the speaker. Note text risks showing on the projector.

FIVE MODES AND A 20-DIAL CONTROL LIST are too much cognitive load for a live lesson. The teacher-controls list is far longer than a teacher will touch, and switching modes mid-lesson means re-orienting the class to new rules each time (the kids' 3-rule card changes per mode).
OPEN THE BOX DUPLICATES the existing /sinif-oyunu Baamboozle-style tile board (numbered tiles, power tiles, team turns). It adds build cost without adding a new classroom experience.

SIMULTANEOUS 'HERKES KONUŞUR' with 8-10 groups of kids cannot be monitored by one teacher. 'Word spotter' ticking needs paper sheets that are not provided, and the team self-reported star invites inflation.
The optional live mic-level mode will trigger a browser permission prompt on a shared school board, which confuses kids and IT. It does little for the lesson and should not be offered.

ADULTS (10 people) FIT WELL, with one caveat. At A1-A2, adult Just a Minute breaks because 30-40 s of talk with hesitation challenges is punishing. Wager rounds and negatives only suit B1+. For individuals in a group of 10, the rotating spokesperson plus 20 s pair consultation is fine.
fixes: TOUCH-FIRST CONTROL BAR. Add a large, always-visible bottom strip with ▶ Spin/Next, ⏸, +10 s, 🙋 Nudge, ↶ Undo and ⛶ Blank. Put team-coloured challenge buttons on the board edge, and make a challenge a single tap sequence: team, reason, ✓/✗, each at least 64 px. Keep the keyboard shortcuts as an extra for laptop and projector rooms, and add an optional phone remote (a QR code pairs the teacher's phone to the teacher controls).

OFFLINE-FIRST CONTENT. Ship built-in packs that are cached (built-in categories and MEB units need no LLM call). Pre-generate LLM packs at home and save them to 'Paketlerim'. The preview should default to 'Hepsini onayla' with spot-regenerate, so class setup takes about 30 s: open a saved class profile, open a saved pack, press Start.

EVERYONE TALKS BEFORE ANYONE IS PICKED. Every wheel turn opens with a 15 s 'Partner'ına söyle' step: all pairs say their answer using the starter, and only then does the seat spinner pick a speaker. Put this in the kids' 3-rule card instead of 'Everyone says it too'. It raises active students from 1 to 28 every turn and makes it safe to be picked.

SEAT LOGISTICS. Provide a printable set of desk cards (mascot/emblem plus a number) with a setup tip. Store uneven team sizes per team. Give the speaker card a 1-tap 'Yok / Atla' button that re-spins. Persist 'Herkes bir kez' across lessons in the local class profile, with a visible 'Bu tur: 11/28 konuştu' progress ring for the teacher only.

TURN BUDGET. Cap each spin animation at 2 s for kids and let them skip it. Replace peer thumbs for kids with the teacher's 1-3 star tap and a class two-clap. Make the follow-up question unscored by default. Target 75 s per turn and show the teacher a 'about N more turns before the bell' estimate.

JUST A MINUTE FOR TEENS. In Arena, make challenges earn the challenger nothing (or a class-level 'Sharp ears' meter only). If a challenge is valid, the speaker gets 3 s to restart with a starter. Cap the challenges one speaker can receive at 1 per turn. Default Arena to hesitation-only challenges with 'Koç modu' as an easy fallback. Keep full BBC competitive rules for adults at B1+ only, and default adult A1-A2 to Koç modu.

OPTIONAL SILENCE METER. Offer a local, never-stored silence meter that shows a hesitation bar ('4 s sessizlik'), so challenges are settled by a visible fact rather than the teacher's guess. Keep it off by default, and turn it on only through a teacher setting that explains the mic prompt. Otherwise drop the mic feature entirely.

STORY DICE PACING. Give each team 20 s of sentence-planning time while the previous team is speaking (the next die is revealed early). Default to tap-only (no typing). Add a one-tap 'Hikâyeyi bitir' that turns the next team's die into 'The End' or lets Gogo read a generated closing. Add 'PDF olarak kaydet / Tahtada göster' as the default instead of print.
WOULD YOU RATHER DEFAULTS. Default to stand/sit (kids) or A/B hand signals, and move 'walls' behind a 'Geniş sınıf' option. Put a 30 s hard cap on the reasons segment so the stirrer stays a stirrer.

SCOPE. Cut Open the Box from this game and instead let /sinif-oyunu (the tile board) import speaking-prompt packs as its prompt tiles. Ship Wheel + Talk Rocket/JAM + Would You Rather as v1, and Story Dice as v2. Mode switching inside a lesson happens only through 'Ders akışı' presets, which show a 10 s pictogram rule reminder between modes.

TEACHER CONTROLS TIERING. Surface only 5 dials in the setup summary: mode, time, scores on/off, Kolay/Orta/Zor and Nazik. Move everything else under 'Gelişmiş'. Save the whole configuration per class profile so the second lesson is one click.

PRIVATE DUYDUKLARIMIZ. Notes open in a small overlay that hides the moment the teacher taps outside it and never renders on the student canvas. The teacher can also dictate or type notes afterwards from a list of 'turn N' placeholders created by a single tap. The Kaçırılanlar review is revealed only by an explicit teacher action.

HERKES KONUŞUR SUPPORT. Provide a printable word-spotter sheet per topic, rotate the speaker every 40 s with a chime, and tell the teacher to circulate. Make it unscored for kids. Show a 'Sessiz sinyal' (hand up = quiet) pictogram on screen to reset noise between rotations.

FAIRNESS. Normalise kids' team stars by the number of turns taken, not raw totals. Keep Comeback Light as the default for Arena. Show the podium by stat awards so a small or weak team is never visibly last.

issues: Talk-time targets do not fit A1 young learners. A 15-20 s solo turn for an A1 9-year-old who barely reads is a monologue they cannot produce; realistic output is 1-3 frame sentences. Because the rocket measures seconds, it rewards stalling, 'ummm' and Turkish filler rather than English. Duration is the wrong success measure at A1 and A2 for both kids and adults.

Nothing checks that the speech is in English. Rocket stars, ON AIR time, 'Clean 45' and 'Clean minute' all reward staying on the clock. In Turkish state-school classes a speaker can code-switch through a 'full' turn, and one-key teacher awards do not separate 'talked' from 'talked in English with the frame'.

Per-student talk time is low in the default whole-class mode. At about 90 s per turn with 8 steps (spin, spin, huddle, talk, follow-up, thumbs, award), a class of 30-36 gets roughly one turn per student per 45-minute lesson. Kids' turns (chorus, clap, echo) add even more. 'Herkes konuşur' and Pairs are where the real learning happens, yet they are listed as alternatives.

The kids' 3-rule card hides a much bigger procedure: seat spinner, chorus starter, team talk, rocket, clap, echo follow-up, stars, stickers, help card and the W nudge. It is simple for pupils but heavy for the teacher to run. The '20 s explanation' test passes only because the teacher carries the complexity.

Kids never form questions. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo reads the follow-up and the class echoes it, so question formation (a listed skill) happens only for Arena and adults. A2 Genç can manage simple wh-questions and should produce them.

Arena at A1/A2 is undefined for Just a Minute. The A1 row says 'rocket or Koç modu only', but the rocket belongs to the Oyun Parkı skin. A 13-year-old A1 class routed to Arena therefore has no specified Mic Challenge rule, and the Arena section lists hesitation thresholds for A1/A2 that contradict the level table.

Just a Minute is a poor fit below B1 for any age. Hesitation challenges at A2 punish the natural pausing of low-level learners and turn listening into fault-hunting, not comprehension. For 12-14 year olds, even 'Nazik' challenges make peers police each other, which raises anxiety for exactly the weaker speakers the risks section says it protects.

B2 Genç Story Dice asks for 8-9 dice with past perfect and third conditional. That is too long and too abstract for 12-14 year olds in a 12-18 minute slot, and teachers cannot reliably verify a tense in fast oral turns.

The kids' Story Dice line 'pirates, monsters' conflicts with the teenSafe filter (no horror or violence) unless the faces are curated. The LLM will also produce event faces ('⚡ The lights went out') that emoji cannot depict clearly for pre-readers.

Content from built-in categories is not as cheap as it looks. words.js has no emoji, concreteness flag or picture, so the dice faces, secret cards and required Genç media.emoji need a hand-curated, emoji-mapped subset. The LLM can generate prompts easily, but it cannot be trusted to keep starters on the grammar whitelist or to choose unambiguous emoji for abstract prompts, and the validator can only approximate the whitelist check.

Adult delayed correction ('Duyduklarımız' / 'Kaçırılanlar') is the strongest learning feature, but it is adult-only. Arena and B1/B2 Genç groups, who make the most fossilising errors in fluent speech, get none.
The adult 'four corners' Would You Rather has only two options, so the rule is inconsistent. The adult A1 'TR gloss allowed' plus a 30 s target makes Turkish explanation the easiest path.
Open the Box largely duplicates the existing /sinif-oyunu tile board and its power tiles. Its 75% prompt boxes are just a slower wheel, which adds scope without adding level or age value.
fixes: At A1 and A2 (both audiences), replace time targets with sentence targets: A1 = 2-3 frame sentences, A2 = 3-4 sentences with 'because', B1+ = time. The rocket rises one stage per English sentence the teacher taps (Space = +1 sentence), not per second.

Add an 'In English' check to every award. The teacher's award key offers 'spoke' and 'spoke in English with a frame'. Stars, combos and 'Clean' badges require the English tick, and the helper-word star requires that a displayed useful[] word was actually used.

Make Pairs the default at A1-B1 for classes of 24 or more, and 'Herkes konuşur' the default for 30-40. Make whole-class Wheel a 'demo turn': one team speaks on screen, then every pair does the same card for 60 s.

Collapse the kids' turn to 5 steps: see the picture (read aloud) → class chorus of the starter → speaker says the sentences → the class repeats one of them → stars. Move the clap, sticker and help-card rules into optional teacher dials.
From A2 Genç, a listener asks the follow-up from a 2-choice question frame ('What colour...? / Where...?') instead of echoing Gogo. At A1 Genç, keep the chorus echo.

Define Arena at A1/A2 explicitly: Mic Challenge becomes 'Koç modu' (a count-up bar in Arena styling, no challenges). Hesitation challenges switch on only from B1 for all audiences; A2 adults may opt in.

Cap Genç Story Dice at 3 (A1), 4 (A2), 5 (B1, with twist) and 6 (B2) dice. At B2 Genç the target is past continuous + past perfect, with third conditional only in the ending sentence. Use tap-only checks for 'structure' at 2 target forms maximum per story.

Ship a curated, emoji- or illustration-mapped dice bank (about 150 concrete faces tagged WHO/WHERE/WHAT/FEELING, from A1-A2 words.js entries). Have the LLM choose only from it by id, or send its new faces through a mandatory preview with a 'no clear picture' flag. Rename 'monsters' to 'friendly monsters / aliens' under teenSafe.

Extend 'Duyduklarımız' and 'Kaçırılanlar' to Arena B1/B2 Genç as an anonymous 'Fix it' round of 3-5 sentences framed as a team challenge. Keep it off for Oyun Parkı, where the teacher gives recasts instead.

Validate the LLM's starters with a deterministic check against the level's grammar whitelist, using regex templates per frame (e.g. forbid 'would/have + past participle' below B1), and fall back to built-in frames per mode and level when a starter fails.

Fix Would You Rather: two walls or stand/sit only, and 'four corners' only when the card has 4 options (mode wyr4). At A1 adults, show the TR gloss only after a 5 s delay and never on the model answer.

Cut Open the Box from this game and put its prompt-box and power-tile mechanics into the existing /sinif-oyunu engine as a 'speaking prompt' tile type. Ship Wheel (with Pairs) and Story Dice first, then Would You Rather; Just a Minute ships for B1+ Stüdyo and Arena only.

reviews.mergeWith: Open the Box -> merge into the existing /sinif-oyunu Baamboozle tile board as a 'speaking-prompt' content source. Story Dice -> ship later as its own game (or phase 2), not as mode C of this one.
issues: SCOPE: this is five games under one name, and that makes it L+, not L. Wheel, Open the Box, Story Dice (3D dice, scroll, print), Just a Minute (a challenge state machine) and Would You Rather each have their own UI, three skins and three rule packs. That comes to roughly 15 skin/rule combinations to QA. It is the highest build risk in the suite, and the most likely to ship as five half-polished modes.

DUPLICATION: Open the Box repeats the existing /sinif-oyunu tile board (numbered tiles, power tiles, Green/Yellow/Red powers, teams). Running two Baamboozle clones on one site means two power engines that drift apart. Story Dice is a strong standalone game (co-op, print, grammar target) that gets lost as mode C. Would You Rather is a 5-minute warmer, not a game.

The design is built around the keyboard, but Turkish state classrooms mostly use MEB/Vestel touch smartboards with no keyboard in reach. Space, H/D/R, Y/N, 1-6, W, U and N all need touch equivalents. The Just a Minute challenge flow (freeze, pick team, pick reason, rule Y/N) is 4 taps on a board while the teacher is also listening and judging. That is too slow and too busy.

Presenter view on an extended display is rare in Turkish classrooms (the board is usually the only screen), so 'Duyduklarımız' notes typed with N would appear on the projector. The typing UI also blocks the game while the teacher types.

'Model answers are generated on demand and not stored': a live LLM call in the middle of a lesson depends on school Wi-Fi, adds 2-6 s of latency and hits the rate limiter. Gogo's demo would stall in front of 30 kids. They must be generated with the pack and stored.

TTS dependence: Web Speech API voices differ by device. MEB boards and old Windows images often have no good en-US/en-GB voice, or none at all. Gogo's voice, the 0.8x read-aloud and the chorus model all break silently. There is no stated fallback.

EMOJI AS ART: Windows Segoe emoji look flat and inconsistent, some are missing on older Android/board OS builds, and emoji skin/gender variants look different across devices. The dice faces and every Genç prompt rely on emoji ('required'), so the kids' version looks cheap or shows tofu boxes on exactly the hardware schools have.

words.js has no emoji or image mapping, so 'every dice face needs media.emoji or img' requires a hand-curated concrete-noun-to-icon map (~300-500 entries) that does not exist. An LLM will happily return emoji that do not match or do not render.

LLM VALIDATION GAPS: word caps, emoji presence, field counts and mode enums can be checked mechanically. 'Starters use only whitelisted grammar' cannot be checked reliably without a parser (regex heuristics at best). teenSafe/privacy need EN and TR keyword lists plus a second LLM moderation pass. Rewriting personal prompts into a 'dream frame' is an LLM transformation that can itself fail. For wyr items, optA and optB must be parallel and balanced, which is also hard to validate.
The built-in categories list about 35 topics x 8 groups. Hand-authoring (or LLM-drafting plus curating) 24-60 prompts each is a large content job, larger than the code, and it is not costed.

The speaker spinner (team, then seat) followed by the topic spinner means two spins of 2-6 s plus a 10-20 s huddle plus follow-up and thumbs. That is about 90-120 s per turn, so a 30-student class gets roughly 12 speakers in 20 min. 'Herkes bir kez' also needs team sizes to be entered, which the setup does not ask for.

Arena Just a Minute under Nazik: the challenger gets +1 but the speaker keeps the floor and the points. That removes the tension that makes JaM fun, and 13-year-olds will game it by challenging freely (+1 each time, up to the cap). The wrong-challenge cap then becomes the main mechanic.

Kids' rocket: the timer counts up automatically, so who decides the speaker 'stopped early'? The teacher has to press stop at the right moment. This is not specified, and it is the most important interaction in the kids' mode.

Story Dice mixes co-op ('Story stars' meter) with per-team points (+1 per sentence, +2 funniest twist). With kids, the points undercut the co-op message, and the teacher has to tick four checkboxes per sentence (✓picture ✓structure ✓connector ✓secret), which is too much judging.
Optional live mic level: a getUserMedia permission prompt on a shared board and privacy worries from parents and administrators, for a purely decorative effect. The risk outweighs the value.

Too many teacher controls: roughly 40 settings across modes. The teacher 'loves details', but the setup UI will be a wall of toggles unless it is heavily layered. 'Ders akışı' presets that chain modes add cross-mode state and timing logic.

Without careful motion design it risks feeling like the free Wordwall Random Wheel with a skin. The real differentiator is the turn engine (speaker fairness, huddle, starters, follow-up ladder, one-key award, delayed correction), and the spec does not put it first.
fixes: Cut the game down to one shared TURN ENGINE (speaker pick, prompt reveal, huddle, talk timer, follow-up, award, undo) plus three surfaces: Çark (wheel), Just a Minute (Talk Rocket / Mic Challenge / BBC), and Would You Rather as a 'Isınma' preset. Order: v1 = Wheel + JaM, v1.1 = WYR.
Move Open the Box into /sinif-oyunu: add 'speaking-prompt' as a tile content type there and reuse its existing power engine, so the site has one power system, not two.

Spin Story Dice off as its own game ('Hikâye Zarları') with its own review. Keep the co-op meter only, with no per-team points for kids. Reduce the teacher checks to 2 big buttons: 'Kullandı ✓' (picture + structure) and 'Bonus' (connector or secret).

Touch-first teacher control: a collapsible bottom drawer with 56 px buttons. JaM challenge becomes team chip tap, then one of three large reason buttons that commit as valid, with a 3 s 'Geri al' toast replacing the separate Y/N step (2 taps). Keys become shortcuts to the same buttons. Test on a 1920x1080 touch board at arm's length.

Single screen by default: the N note opens a small overlay that blurs or hides itself, or the teacher records a quick tag instead of typing ('grammar / word / pron' plus an optional word). Build a phone remote (QR, same session) only if presenter view is dropped; otherwise defer both.

Generate model answers, followUps and TR glosses inside the pack at creation time and store them. Zero LLM calls during play. Cache the whole pack in localStorage/IndexedDB so the game runs offline once loaded.

TTS: probe the available voices at setup and show 'Sesli okuma: hazır / uygun ses yok'. Pre-render Gogo's fixed lines (about 40 phrases: rules, 'Rocket landed!', praise, chorus cues) as small Opus/MP3 files. Where there is no voice, fall back to the teacher reading aloud with the text shown large.

Replace system emoji with a self-hosted SVG icon subset (OpenMoji or Twemoji, CC-BY, about 400 icons, lazy sprite). Build a curated concept-to-icon map for concrete nouns in the A1-B1 bands. The LLM must choose from an icon id enum sent in the prompt, and it may not invent emoji.

Validator pipeline: JSON schema (strict enums and counts) + word counter + icon-id check + EN/TR blocklists (teenSafe, privacy: income, religion, parents' jobs, appearance, health) + a starter-grammar heuristic (per-level banned tokens, e.g. no 'would have' at A2) + a WYR balance check (similar option length) + dedupe. Failures trigger per-item regeneration (max 2), then fall back to a built-in item. Show a small 'düzeltildi' badge in the preview.

Seed the built-in bank by LLM-drafting offline and then having the teacher curate. Start with 12 categories x 3 audiences (not 35 x 8); the level dial filters by cap. Ship JSON in src/data like the grammar_mcq banks.

Speed up turns: one combined slot-machine spin (emblem + seat + topic reels stop in sequence, about 3 s total). Ask for 'kişi sayısı' per team (default: class size / teams). Make the huddle skippable. Target 60 s per turn.

Arena JaM: a valid challenge gives the challenger +1 AND ends the speaker's +3 clean bonus (the speaker keeps +2 at the whistle), which restores tension without a takeover. A wrong challenge gives the speaker +1 and costs one of the 2 caps.

Kids' rocket: Space/tap = 'bitti'. Reaching the goal lands the rocket automatically on Mars. The teacher's tap before the goal lands it on the Moon. Big 'Bitti' button on touch. W (help) is a visible 'Yardım' button with a lifebuoy icon.
Drop the live mic mode from scope. Keep the decorative sound bars driven by a random, rhythm-based animation instead.
Settings: show 5 'Hızlı ayar' presets plus an 'Gelişmiş' accordion. Make 'Ders akışı' a simple ordered playlist of mode+minutes that only advances when the teacher taps, with no auto-chaining state.

Polish budget, where it earns 'proper game' feel: a physics-y wheel (canvas, ease-out, peg flap, creep), a slot-reel speaker pick, the rocket with a trail and landing, the ON AIR light, a score roll-up, and about 25 SFX per skin family (CC0, under 400 KB total, preloaded after the first tap to satisfy autoplay). Gogo as one SVG rig with 5 poses (idle, flutter, point, pop, sleep). Self-hosted Andika subset plus a condensed display face (Barlow Condensed/Oswald).

Event-sourced score log (append-only) to make U/undo, finale stats (Longest streak, Sharp Ears, Comeback) and 'Kaçırılanlar' trivially correct. Persist to localStorage so an accidental refresh mid-lesson resumes.

catalog.rankReason: Speaking fluency and opinions (adult 8) in a suite that is otherwise mostly answering questions. Cut it to one turn engine with three surfaces: Çark (the wheel), Just a Minute (Talk Rocket for kids, BBC rules for adults) and Would You Rather, which also takes c17's Open Rank. Open the Box moves into c01; Story Dice waits for v2. A1-A2 get sentence targets instead of time targets, and every award needs an 'In English' tick. It needs a touch-first control bar and built-in packs cached offline. The wheel is a shared component.

catalog.name: Milyoner Merdiveni (Millionaire Ladder)
catalog.familiarAs: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire / Kim Milyoner Olmak İster (with Wordwall Gameshow Quiz lifelines and Plickers-style printed answer cards)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams climb their own difficulty ladder one question at a time, relay-style, with safe steps, three phone-free lifelines and the 'Final answer?' lock-in. Every other team shadow-plays each question on printed A-D cards and earns sparks that refill its own lifelines, so nobody sits idle.
catalog.howItPlays:
MODES. (a) 'Bayrak' (Relay, the default): 2-4 ladders sit side by side and the teams take turns question by question. (b) 'Sahne' (Show): one hot-seat team climbs until it misses or walks away, then the seat passes on. Show mode handles 5-6 teams, the whole class as one contestant, or a one-to-one private lesson. (c) 'Tek roket' (kids): the whole class flies one rocket together, with no competition.

SETUP (teacher, about 1 min). Pick the group chip. The summary line shows the result, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 sn · 25 dk · 3 takım · 12 basamak'. Then pick a built-in category or type a free-text prompt. The 'Merdiven önizleme' screen shows every rung, key and spare on the teacher view only; it is hidden in projector mode. The teacher can drag rungs to reorder them, swap items, or edit a key or a why line. 'Ders süresine sığdır' proposes the ladder length and team count. On first use, 'Kart yazdır' prints one A-D card per student. Each letter has a colour and a shape: A orange triangle, B blue diamond, C yellow circle, D purple square. Kids also get a thumbs Yes/No card.

1 TEAM IDENTITY. Park: animal-pilot rockets; tap a rocket to change its animal. Arena: teams get 10 s to pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. Stüdyo: generated names (cities, coffee drinks, grammar puns).

2 PRACTICE. Park: Gogo the parrot flies a 25 s demo rung that does not score. Arena and Stüdyo: an optional warm-up question.

3 OPENER 'Sırala!' (Arena and Stüdyo, optional, 60 s). Every team orders 4 items (sentence tokens, events or dialogue lines) on its whiteboard. Correct teams take the first turns, and the spinner breaks ties. It gives no points and there is no speed scoring. Park skips it: the class counts '3, 2, 1, blast off!' and the spinner sets the order.

4 LOW RUNGS TOGETHER ('Hep birlikte', on by default with 3+ teams). The rungs below the first safe step are played by all teams at once. Everyone answers the same question on boards or cards, and every correct team climbs. This saves a lot of time, and every team gets early success.

5 THE TURN (from the first safe step, about 50-70 s). The active ladder lights up and the seat spinner shows e.g. 'Team Fox · Seat 3'. It never shows a name, and no seat plays twice until every seat has played. The question appears and is read aloud: automatically at 0.8x for A1/A2 Genç, from a speaker button everywhere else. The options appear after the delay: kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s. Team talk follows (10/15/20 s). Then the Seat 3 student says the ritual line 'Final answer: B!'. Decision frames by level sit on screen: A levels 'I think it's B.'; B1+ 'I'd go with B because…', 'It can't be C because…'. Meanwhile every other team chooses silently and holds its card face-in against the chest.

6 LOCK-IN. The teacher clicks B or presses the B key, and B glows amber. On 'Show!' all shadow cards go up. A light sweeps across the options during a suspense pause that grows with the rung's height: 0.5 s on low rungs, up to 3 s on the top rung in Stüdyo, capped at 2 s for kids and 1.2 s for Arena, and settable to 0. Then the reveal: the key turns green with a ✓. On a miss, the chosen option turns red with a ✗; for kids it goes grey and dashed, never red.

7 AFTER THE REVEAL. The ladder climbs one rung with a rising note. Every rung is the next note of a scale, so the class hears progress as well as sees it. A one-line explanation shows for 5 s: whyTr at A levels, whyEn with a TR toggle at B. The class says the answer or key sentence together once (kids twice, led by Gogo). The teacher taps the chips of the shadow teams that showed the right card; a 'Hepsi' button selects all, then the teacher untaps the wrong ones. Each of those teams earns a spark ✦. Three sparks give back one used lifeline, so shadow play feeds the team's own climb. Then the next team takes its turn.

8 WRONG ANSWERS by mode.
- Park: a soft 'boing', and the wrong picture fades. Gogo gives a free hint (the picture, then the first letter, then listen again) and the team tries once more. A right second try still climbs. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the whole class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album. The rocket hovers where it is; it never goes down.
- Arena: the streak breaks and the team stays on its rung, losing nothing. Every shadow team that showed the right card steals half the rung's XP ('STEAL!').
- Stüdyo: the classic rule. The team drops to its last safe step (or the step it locked) and plays on next turn.

9 LIFELINES (once per game each, shown as icons under each ladder).
- 50:50 removes two wrong options, always keeping the 'trap' distractor so the choice still teaches. With 3 options it removes one.
- 'Sınıfa sor': the shadow teams show their cards BEFORE the lock. The teacher taps a coarse level per option (Az / Orta / Çok) or enters exact counts, and the bars grow like on TV. These votes also count as the teams' shadow answers, which prevents sabotage.
- 'Arkadaşa danış': the hot team picks another TEAM, whose spinner seat gives 15-20 s of advice. If the answer is right, the helper team earns a spark.
- Optional fourth lifeline for Arena and Stüdyo: 'Soru değiştir' swaps in a spare from the same band.
- B1+: after any lifeline, the spokesperson says whether the team follows it and why; a good reason earns a spark.

10 SAFE STEPS. Reaching one plays a gold-rim chime. Park adds a planet sticker to the rocket that can never be lost. Arena shows 'CHECKPOINT'. Where it is on, the station wheel spins:
- Green slices: everyone +1, gift 1 to a team you tap, lifeline refill, brain break (a chance-card task).
- Yellow slices (Arena, opt-in): steal 5 XP (capped at that team's score), swap turn order.

11 BANKING (Stüdyo, 'Bırak'). At the start of its turn, before the question appears, a team may lock its current rung as a new safe step instead of answering. That costs the turn: tempo traded for safety.

12 COMEBACK (Light). A team 3+ rungs behind the leader climbs 2 rungs on its next correct answer ('Rüzgâr'). The trailing team also picks the category of its next question from two.

13 END. When a team reaches the top, the round finishes so every team has had the same number of turns. Otherwise the lesson-fit timer or a turn count ends the game. Ranking goes by highest rung (Stüdyo: banked value; Arena: XP), then sparks, then a closest-number tiebreak on whiteboards.
- Park: 'Last fuel', one whole-class card question. If most of the class is right, every rocket lands on the Moon together, and every team gets a title.
- Arena: a podium plus stat awards.
- Stüdyo: the final board plus 'Kaçırılanlar' (missed items with key and why). One click turns them into next lesson's warm-up ladder.
- Printable certificates for all.
catalog.playerSetup: Relay (default): 2-4 teams of 3-8, with 3 ideal. Each team has its own ladder. A seat-number spinner picks the spokesperson for every question; the teacher can set 'pairs in the hot chair' instead. Every non-active team shadow-plays every question on printed A-D cards or mini whiteboards. Kids: the whole class responds every turn. Show mode: 1-6 teams (one in the hot seat, the others shadowing), or the whole class as one contestant with a rotating seat, which also suits one-to-one private lessons. 'Tek roket' mode: the whole class plays together, for the youngest groups. Nobody is ever picked by name.
catalog.contentShape:
A 'ladder pack' is a set of items plus pack.frames.ladder {steps, safe[], shared (rungs played together), bands[{from, to, diff, itemIds[], spareIds[]}]}.

RUNG ITEMS
- mcq (fmt picture|meaning|gap|collocation|dialogue|context|reading), each with: options[3|4], answer, whyTr (90 chars or fewer), whyOpt[] where available, whyEn (B groups), target/unit, diff (1-5), a 'trap' flag on the most plausible distractor (50:50 keeps it), media.emoji or imageKey (required on A1/A2 Genç rungs), and TTS text.
- Code turns these into MCQ rungs:
  - vocab items become picture, meaning or gap rungs built from term, defEasy/def, gap and distractors[3].
  - gap items with a 3-4 word bank.
  - odd items (4 items).
  - tf items: Yes/No rungs 1-2 for kids; 'Is it correct?' at A levels.
  - sound items: a minimal-pair 'Listen and choose' rung.
  - riddle items: the kids' Moon rung, with clues from hard to easy and picture options.
  - text items plus their mcq/tf by textRef, for B1+ top rungs.

FRAMES
- 1-2 order items for the 'Sırala!' opener.
- 1-2 qa number items with tolerance for the tiebreak.
- 4-6 chance-card tasks (Green, teenSafe) for the wheel's brain break.

BUILT-IN SOURCES
- grammar_mcq_a1..c1 (curated keys and whyOpt), mixed across the units of the level.
- MCQs derived from words.js. Distractors share the key's part of speech and word band, and are never a synonym of the key.
- idioms.js for B2 idiom meaning.
- readings_* for context rungs.

DIFFICULTY is the item's diff blended with:
- the word band of the key and the distractors;
- stem length;
- a format weight (picture < meaning < gap < collocation < context < reading);
- unit order;
- this class's own accuracy from earlier games (stored locally, recalibrating over the weeks).

POOL CHECK. Each band needs at least teams × relay rungs in the band × 1.3, plus 2 spares. For example, 3 teams on 12 rungs with 4 shared rungs need about 35 items. If the pool is short, the setup offers fewer teams, a shorter ladder or 'LLM ile tamamla'.

LLM PATH. The teacher's prompt (Turkish is fine) produces a graded ladder JSON: bands with spares, diff, the trap distractor, and whyTr. The validator then checks:
- exactly one correct option, confirmed by a second LLM self-check plus rules: no duplicate options, no 'all of the above', options of similar length and the same form, and the key never the only long option;
- the group's word caps and the CEFR band of every word;
- teenSafe for Genç groups;
- band difficulty that never goes down up the ladder;
- balanced key positions: after shuffling, never the same letter 3 times in a row;
- images present on picture rungs (unpicturable rungs are dropped for A1/A2 Genç).
The teacher preview comes before play.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO, titled 'The Ladder' on screen: no show name, logo, set design or signature music.

LOOK AND SOUND
- Editorial quiz-night look in cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, with one spotlight sweep and gold-rimmed safe rungs. System sans font, no mascot, no voice lines, and a neutral caption ('Rung 7 · Travel').
- Sound: a woodblock tick, a low piano cluster on lock-in, and a bright chord or soft two notes on the reveal. Each rung plays a rising piano note. Music is off by default; an optional low tension bed starts at rung 10.

LADDER
- 12 rungs (safe at 4 and 8). B2 and Show mode: 15 rungs (safe at 5 and 10). A1 adults: 10 rungs (safe at 3 and 7).
- Values as plain points, or as a joke flourish, a money-style ladder from 100 to 1.000.000 puan that rolls up like a split-flap board.

RULES
- 4 options (3 on A1 rungs 1-3).
- A rotating spokesperson with pair consultation; 'solo hot chair' is an option.
- Optional 30 s timer (45 s on rungs 9+).
- The classic fall to the last safe step.
- 'Bırak' banking as a tempo-for-safety decision.
- Three lifelines plus an optional 'Soru değiştir'.
- Sparks from shadow play refill lifelines.
- Hints (definition, then example, then Turkish gloss) cost points; the TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes. Minus points are optional and off by default: the fall is the penalty.
- B1+: 'Neden?' on rungs 9+ and after every lifeline, with decision frames on screen ('I'd go with…', 'It can't be… because…', 'I'm torn between… and…').
- B1-B2: 'Seçeneksiz bil' on the top three rungs. The stem shows alone for 10 s, and a team that writes the right answer on its whiteboard before the options appear climbs one extra rung ('Called it!'). This rewards real confidence instead of gambling.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default and Red opt-in (swap ladders). The station wheel is off by default.

CONTENT
Life and work tasks: travel, job interviews, complaints, small talk, 'Which reply is most polite?', and reading a sign, a short email or a notice. Also collocations, idiom meaning, register, and exam-style gap options with YDS/YÖKDİL/IELTS flavour at B2.

ENDING
Full scores with a modest chime and the score rolling up, then the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list and a certificate ('The Irregular Verbs · Basamak 11'). 'Sınıfın rekoru' is saved in the class profile.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two real rule variants, not a recolour. The group label never appears on screen, and Genç groups never see money values.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; the default for A1/A2 Genç) 'Rocket to the Moon'

Visuals
- A cream sky that darkens to a starry blue.
- Each team is a rocket in its colour AND a shape, with its animal pilot in the window (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin, bear).
- The rungs pass treetops, clouds, a hot-air balloon, a plane, a rainbow, a satellite, stars and the Moon.
- Safe steps are space stations that give a planet sticker, which can never be lost.
- Font floor 6vh.

Host
Gogo the parrot demos the practice rung, reads every question at 0.8x, repeats the answer like a parrot, and sleeps on a crescent moon on the pause screen.

Ladder
8 rungs (10 at A2 Genç), with stations at 3 and 6 (3 and 7 at 10 rungs); the rungs below the first station are played together.

Rules (a Turkish rule card with pictograms, explainable in 20 s)
1. Team talk, then 'Final answer!'
2. Everyone shows a card.
3. Right = the rocket goes up; wrong = try again with a hint.

How it runs
- Rungs 1-2 are picture Yes/No questions with the thumbs cards; later rungs have 3 picture options.
- Team talk lasts 10 s. There is no timer by default; the optional one is a calm 40 s ring, never red, with a marimba chime at 0.
- Whole-class response every turn (A-B-C cards, or TPR: stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C), plus the seat spinner for the active team.
- Hints are free (the picture, then the first letter, then listen again). The three friendly lifelines are a magic wand (removes one wrong option), a megaphone (ask the class) and a high five (help from a seat in another team).
- Nothing ever goes down: no fall and no elimination. Scores are stars only, stickers come at the stations, and effort stars go to the class album.
- Sound is marimba, and the 8-rung ladder is exactly one octave. Celebrations last 2 s or less.
- One 45 s stirrer at the first station, 'Rocket countdown': the class counts from 10 to 1 in English and jumps.

Finale
- 'Last fuel', a whole-class question. Every rocket lands on the Moon.
- Every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers, Sharp Eyes), and the class album gets a Moon sticker.
- A 'Say cheese!' class-photo screen.

ARENA (12-14; the default for B1/B2 Genç, suggested for any Genç group in grades 6-8 or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor') 'Level Up'

Visuals
- Dark navy with neon team colours, a condensed display font, geometric emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), and a 3-word motto chosen in 10 s.
- The ladder is a rank tower: Bronze I-III, Silver (checkpoint at 4), Silver II, Gold I-II, Platinum (checkpoint at 8), Diamond I-II, Master, Legend. 12 rungs; 10 when an A1/A2 Genç class plays in Arena.
- No mascot and no pastels. A commentator strip shows at most one caption per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CHECKPOINT', 'STEAL!', 'CLUTCH!').

Rules
- A 30 s ring in the team colour, 15 s of team talk, the seat spinner and mini-whiteboards.
- XP: 10 per rung on rungs 1-4, 20 on 5-8 and 30 on 9-12. x1.5 at 3 correct in a row and x2 at 5, based on accuracy only.
- +5 XP for each correct shadow answer. When the hot team misses, shadow teams steal half the rung's XP.
- A miss never lowers XP or the rung (Nazik), and the floor is 0.
- Hints (first letter, then 50:50-lite, then a gapped example) cost 1-2 XP, never below 0.
- Synth blips and combo text of 1.2 s or less.
- An English rule card with a TR toggle.

Opt-ins
Yellow wheel slices, and a 'Hardcore' fall to the checkpoint, available only if the teacher turns Nazik off.

Finale
A podium for the top three and a stat award for every other team (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet = no lifeline used, Sharpest shadow). There is never a last place. Rank-badge certificates.

Content (both variants)
Everything passes the teenSafe filter (no dating, brands, money, rent or office topics). Topics follow YLE and MEB units. Arena's top rungs use LGS-style context items: a short chat, a notice, a poster.
catalog.levelTuning:
Every ladder spans a mini range inside the group: the low rungs revise the level below, and the top rungs stretch just above the level. 'Kolay/Orta/Zor' shifts the band mix without changing the skin, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one level.

YOUNG LEARNERS
- A1 Genç: 8 rungs. Prompts of 0-4 words, where the picture or the audio carries the meaning ('Find: giraffe'). Rungs 1-2 are Yes/No; after that, 3 picture options. Topics from YLE Starters and MEB grades 2-4: animals, colours, numbers, food, toys, body, family, classroom. The Moon rung is a picture riddle ('What am I?').
- A2 Genç: 10 rungs. 8 words or fewer. 3 options on rungs 1-4, then 4, with pictures on the low rungs. Grammar: can/can't, there is/are, present simple routines, was/were. Topics: weather, places in town. One 'Listen and choose' rung (a minimal pair like ship/sheep).
- B1 Genç: 12 rungs, 14 words or fewer, 4 options. Grammar: comparatives, present perfect, will/going to, past continuous, everyday phrasal verbs. Top rungs are LGS-style context items: a chat, a notice, a poster.
- B2 Genç: 12 rungs, 20 words or fewer. Richer language on concrete topics (science facts, environment, sport, technology, festivals): collocations, word families, the passive, conditionals, a short text with evidence. 'Neden?' is optional.

ADULTS
- A1: 10 rungs (safe at 3 and 7), 10 words or fewer. 3 options on rungs 1-3, then 4. Grammar: to be, have got, there is, present simple, can, prepositions of place. Everyday signs and menus. Emoji vocabulary on the low rungs. Frame: 'I think it's B.'
- A2: 12 rungs, 15 words or fewer, 4 options. Grammar: past simple irregulars, comparatives, going to, countables. KET-style short messages and notices on the top rungs.
- B1: 12 rungs, 25 words or fewer. Distractors are built on typical Turkish-speaker errors ('He don't', 'I am agree', 'since three years'). Grammar: present perfect vs past simple, first and second conditionals, the passive, collocations. A short email or sign to read on rungs 10-12. 'Neden?' on rungs 9+. 'Seçeneksiz bil' is optional.
- B2: 12 or 15 rungs, 40 words or fewer. Four close options: register, near-synonyms, prepositions, collocation nuance, idiom meaning, mixed conditionals, inversion, 'Which reply is most polite?'. The top rungs reach C1-lite. The top three rungs show the stem alone for 10 s ('Seçeneksiz bil'). 'Neden?' follows every lifeline, and banking becomes a real strategy.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 15-20 (3 teams, 8 rungs with rungs 1-2 played together, one stirrer, the 'Last fuel' finale); Arena 20-25; Stüdyo Relay 20-35; Show mode 10-15 per ladder; a 'Kaçırılanlar' warm-up ladder takes 5
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Mode: Bayrak/Relay, Sahne/Show, or Tek roket.
- Team count.
- Ladder length (6/8/10/12/15), with safe steps you can drag.
- 'Hep birlikte' low rungs on or off.
- Options: 3 or 4 (automatic by level).
- Content: a built-in unit or category, several units mixed, or a free-text LLM prompt. The preview lets you reorder, swap, edit a key or why line, or delete.
- 'Ders süresine sığdır' uses the pacing numbers (about 60 s per kids turn, 50 s Arena, 60-70 s Stüdyo) to propose a ladder length and team count, so that a team answering 3 of 4 right reaches the top in the final round. Example: '20 dk · 3 takım → 8 basamak, 1-2 birlikte'.
- Kolay/Orta/Zor and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- Skin, rule-pack and dial overrides, saved to the class profile.

DIALS
- Options delay and the suspense ramp (0-3 s).
- Timer: Süresiz, 30, 40 or 45 s, plus a +10 s button.
- Team-talk length.
- Hot-seat rule: every question, every 3 questions, per visit, pairs in the hot chair, or solo (Stüdyo only).
- Each lifeline on or off, plus 'Soru değiştir'.
- Spark recharge and shadow scoring.
- Arena steal; Stüdyo banking.
- 'Neden?' and 'Seçeneksiz bil'.
- Explanation time and the TR gloss.
- Station wheel and harshness level; Comeback dial.
- Plain or money-style values (Stüdyo only).
- Music and SFX volume; reduced motion.
- 'Öğretmen okur' when no English voice is available.

LIVE KEYS
- A-D choose an option; L locks; R reveals.
- Space or PageDown moves on, so a presenter clicker works.
- 5 = 50:50; S = Sınıfa sor; F = Arkadaşa danış; K = Bırak (bank).
- X = 'Soru hatalı': swaps in a spare with no penalty and hides the item for this class.
- U or Ctrl+Z undoes, including unlocking an amber answer before the reveal.
- T pauses (Gogo sleeps); + adds 10 s; M mutes.

LIVE ACTIONS
- Drag a rocket or badge to correct a rung.
- 'Koltuğu ver' hands the seat to any team.
- End the game now.

AFTER THE GAME
- Print certificates.
- Save the class record.
- Replay 'Kaçırılanlar' as a ladder.

PRINTABLES
A-D card sets (one per student or one per pair), Yes/No thumbs cards, and the kids' Turkish rule card with pictograms.
catalog.delightDetails:
- The 'Final answer?' ritual: the chosen option glows amber, a light sweep crosses the options, then green ✓ or red ✗ (kids: grey dashed with a little cloud). Letters carry shapes and icons so colour-blind students can follow.
- The ladder is a musical scale: each rung plays the next note (marimba, synth or piano by mode). The 8-rung kids ladder is exactly one octave and ends on the Moon.
- Suspense grows with height, and the screen dims for the final rung.
