- 'Sınıfa sor' bars grow and count up TV-style. A 'The class knew!' caption appears when the majority was right.
- 'Arkadaşa danış' is a phone-free paper-cup telephone on a string (kids: a high-five), and the helper team's spark flies across to its ladder.
- Rockets puff flame as they climb and collect planet stickers at the stations. Gogo flaps beside the active rocket and snores 'zZz' on a crescent moon when paused.
- Arena rank badges morph from Bronze to Legend with a metallic glint. The combo meter fills. Each team's motto rides on its tower and on the podium.
- Stüdyo values roll up like a split-flap board. 'Bırak' shows a padlock clicking shut on the rung.
- The seat spinner follows 'nobody twice before everyone once' for the whole lesson.
- Answer positions are balanced, so it is never B three times in a row.
- Certificates to print: 'Team Fox reached the Moon!', 'Comet · Diamond II', 'The Irregular Verbs · Basamak 11', with the date and never a level label for Genç groups.
- A 'New class record!' banner draws on 'Sınıfın rekoru' in the class profile.
- 'Kaçırılanlar' becomes next lesson's 5-minute warm-up ladder in one click.
- Kids get a 'Say cheese!' class-photo pose after the Moon landing, for the class album.
catalog.risks:
- Idle teams while one team plays. Fixed by: shadow play on every question, sparks that refill lifelines, the 'Hep birlikte' low rungs, and the whole-class response for kids. Keep Relay to 2-4 teams and use Show mode for more.
- Time. Suspense, huddles and explanations add up. Fixed by: the lesson-fit sizing, suspense settable to 0, and a shorter explanation time.
- The difficulty order must be real. Fixed by: the blended difficulty score, the class's own accuracy data, the preview before play, and the 'Soru hatalı' swap.
- Weak or ambiguous LLM distractors (two defensible answers, giveaway lengths). Fixed by: the validator, the LLM self-check and the teacher preview. The curated banks are the default.
- The item pool runs short with many teams. Fixed by: the setup warns and offers fewer teams, a shorter ladder or an LLM top-up.
- Pressure on shy students. Fixed by: team talk before every answer, pairs in the hot chair, nobody named, and kids never lose height.
- Sabotage in 'Sınıfa sor'. Fixed by: the votes count as the voting team's own shadow answers.
- Hand counts are fiddly. Fixed by: the coarse Az/Orta/Çok buttons.
- Copying cards. Fixed by: cards stay face-in until 'Show!', which comes after the lock.
- Trademark. Fixed by: no show name, logo, set design or music.
- Strong teams running away with it. Fixed by: Comeback Light ('Rüzgâr') and equal turns at the end.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Absorb any generic 'Kahoot/quiz-show MCQ' candidate into this one. It should be the suite's single MCQ show game, sharing an MCQ item engine and validator with /sinif-oyunu.

issues: Turn length is underestimated. One relay turn has: read aloud (0.8x), options delay, 10-20 s team talk, 'Final answer', lock, 'Show!', suspense, reveal, 5 s why line, choral repeat (twice for kids), tapping the chips of right shadow teams, spark and lifeline bookkeeping, then the next spinner animation. That comes to about 75-95 s, not 50-70 s. A kids miss with a hinted retry plus two choral repeats takes 100-120 s. With 28 kids in 3 teams, 6 relay rungs each gives 18 turns, which is 25-30 min, not 15-20. 'Ders süresine sığdır' will plan ladders that do not finish.

The shadow cards can be copied. The hot team talks out loud for 10-20 s and the spokesperson says 'Final answer: B!' while the shadow teams are still choosing, so they only have to listen. Holding cards face-in until 'Show!' does not help, because the answer has already been said aloud. Sparks then reward eavesdropping, and the 'Sınıfa sor' data is polluted.

Shadow scoring is undefined at team level. Each student holds a card but sparks go to teams. Is the team right when all its members are right? Most of them? Any one of them? Nobody can scan 9 raised cards per team on 3 teams in 3 seconds while standing at the board. The teacher will tap 'Hepsi' every time and the spark economy stops meaning anything.

Teacher load per turn is too high for someone standing at a smart board. They must choose the letter, lock, reveal, tap the shadow chips, untap the wrong ones, handle lifeline prompts and the spark refill, spin the wheel at stations and watch for Rüzgâr. The live keys (A-D, L, R, 5, S, F, K, X, U) only work with a keyboard, and at a touch board the teacher has none. The design also stacks too many subsystems at once: sparks, 3-4 lifelines, the station wheel, banking, Rüzgâr, steals, 'Seçeneksiz bil', 'Neden?', the 'Sırala!' opener and the XP combos. A tired teacher in lesson 6 will get something wrong, and the kids will notice right away.

The answer key can leak on a one-screen device. The 'Merdiven önizleme' shows every key and is only hidden in projector mode. On a smart board, the teacher's screen IS the class's screen. Opening the preview or editing a key mid-lesson shows the answers to 28 kids.

Printed cards are costly to run in a Turkish public school. Printing 28 A-D sets is often not possible (photocopy quotas). Handing them out and collecting them takes 2-3 min each lesson. Cards get lost, bent, swapped and waved as toys. The Yes/No thumbs card doubles the number of pieces. Mini-whiteboards are used as a fallback but many classes do not have them.

Teams of 9-10 kids make team talk loud. Ten 10-year-olds huddling for 10 s produces noise and gives no real discussion. The 1-2 strongest kids decide every time, and the seat spinner only picks who says it aloud. 'Seat 3' also needs numbered seats inside each team, which no setup step creates.

Arena steals break the audience defaults. Shared context says mild steals in Arena are opt-in, but the design has shadow teams steal half the rung's XP by default. 'STEAL!' framed as taking from the hot team is also a loss message (even though the hot team loses nothing), and it pushes shadow teams to hope the hot team misses.

Arena uses two progress metrics: rung height on the tower and XP (with combos, shadow +5 and steals). A team can be highest on the tower but third in XP. At 12-14, that brings 'but we're higher!' arguments at the end.

The kids' 'no fall, retry with hint' rule makes nearly every team reach the Moon. The race means little. That is fine as a design choice, but then the per-team ladders, lifelines and sparks cost time without changing any outcome. It also works against the 3-rule checklist: stars, stickers, lifelines, the spinner, the stirrer and the retry all have to be explained.
Show mode with a big class leaves 5 teams shadowing for 10-15 min each, which is boring for 28 kids. Only the adult or one-to-one case really fits Show mode.

Stopping at any moment is unfair. 'End the game now' in the middle of a round leaves teams with unequal turns, and the certificates and titles then feel arbitrary. The bell in Turkish schools does not wait for the round to finish.

Stüdyo harshness with only 10 adults: 3 small teams of 3-4, the classic fall of up to 3-4 rungs, and banking can leave one team stuck around rung 4 for the last 10 minutes. Rüzgâr only helps after a correct answer, and a weak team is exactly the team not answering correctly.

TTS at 0.8x depends on an English voice being installed on the board PC. Many MEB smart boards (Pardus or older Windows) have none, so 'Öğretmen okur' will often be the real mode. That adds reading load for the teacher on every turn.

Setup is 'about 1 min' only for a repeat class. On first use the teacher has the group chip, mode, content, preview, lesson-fit sizing, printing, team identity (10 s motto in Arena), the practice rung and the 'Sırala!' opener. That is realistically 5-8 min of a 40-min lesson.
fixes: Change the order of the turn. Shadow teams commit first: as soon as the options appear, each shadow team's card goes face-down on the desk, or the 'Sınıfa sor' vote is taken. Only after that does the hot team talk, in a whisper, or by writing on the board with no spoken 'Final answer' until the lock. Alternatively, the hot spokesperson points at the screen instead of speaking.

Make shadow scoring one card per team (or one per pair), not one per student, with one 'team card holder' per turn picked by the spinner. The teacher then checks 3 cards, not 28. Taps default to 'Hepsi doğru' and the teacher untaps the wrong ones, which the design already has, and there are only 3 chips to look at. For Oyun Parkı, drop sparks entirely and show only a whole-class 'The class knew!' meter.

Add card-free response options and make them the default for kids: TPR (stand/sit/hands up), fingers 1-2-3 held on the chest, or classroom corners. Printed cards become optional. Offer one card per pair, with a numbered card doubling as the seat number.

Add a two-tier teacher UI for one-screen use: a large touch-friendly teacher strip (Kilitle, Göster, Doğru takımlar, Sonraki), with the key hidden. The key appears only on a long-press 'göz' button that shows a small non-letter hint (for example a dot on the right option for 1 s), or is behind a PIN on the preview. Optionally allow a phone as a remote (QR pairing) where Wi-Fi exists. Never open the preview on a detected touch board without a warning.

Recalibrate pacing with measured defaults: kids about 90 s per relay turn, Arena about 70 s, Stüdyo about 75 s. Log real turn times in the class profile and let 'Ders süresine sığdır' learn from them. Add 'Bu tur son' (finish the current round, then the finale) and a 'Zil 3 dk' button that jumps straight to a whole-class final question, with equal turns guaranteed.

Cut v1 scope. Remove the station wheel, the 'Sırala!' opener, 'Seçeneksiz bil' and the fourth lifeline (keep them as later toggles). In Oyun Parkı, replace per-team lifelines and sparks with free Gogo hints only, so the 3-rule card really holds.

Make Oyun Parkı default to 'Tek roket' or 4 small teams (7 kids, desk pairs) rather than 3 teams of 9-10. Seat numbers come from a number sticker or card handed out at setup, and a 'Koltuk atla' button covers absent or refusing students.

Arena: turn steals OFF by default, as the shared rule pack says. Rename the mechanic 'BONUS!' (shadow teams earn XP when right, and the hot team loses nothing). Use one metric: tower rung = rank, with XP only as a tiebreak and stat line, or convert XP into rung progress.

Stüdyo small-group option: 2 teams or pairs for 8-12 adults, a 'Yumuşak düşüş' dial (fall 1-2 rungs instead of to the safe step), and Rüzgâr triggered by being behind rather than by a correct answer (for example a free 50:50 refill).

Put a short, honest setup path first: a 'Hızlı başla' default (class profile + last content + auto length) that takes under 30 s, while team identity and the practice rung run in parallel on screen. Save identities in the class profile so later lessons skip them.
Show mode: limit it by default to 1-3 teams, or to adult or one-to-one use. For large classes, suggest Relay or Tek roket instead.
Detect an English TTS voice at setup and warn: 'İngilizce ses bulunamadı, sorular için Öğretmen okur açık'. Pre-generate audio for the curated banks so they do not depend on the device.

issues: Mostly recognition. Nearly every rung is MCQ, and the spoken ritual 'Final answer: B!' is a letter, not language. At A levels the decision frame 'I think it's B.' produces no target language at all. Real production only exists at B1+ ('Neden?', 'Seçeneksiz bil') and in the choral repeat.

Pre-literate and weak-reading A1 Genç (age 9, MEB grade 3-4): the built-in banks have no pictures. words.js and grammar_mcq_* are text only, so the 'picture rung required' rule depends on an emoji map. That map covers concrete nouns but not verbs, prepositions, adjectives or grammar. Once unpicturable rungs are dropped, an A1 Genç grammar topic (can/can't, there is/are, have got) may not fill 8 rungs, and the built-in path for the youngest group is largely unproven.
The whyTr line shows for 5 s. That is too short for 9-10-year-olds reading Turkish on a projector, and nobody reads it aloud, because Gogo's TTS is English only.

Kids' retry: with 3 options, a free hint, a faded wrong picture and a second try, the answer is close to a 50-50 or certain guess. The class can climb without knowing the word. Nothing requires saying the word before the rocket moves.

Arena turns on the half-XP 'STEAL!' for shadow teams by default. That contradicts the shared rule that Arena is Nazik with mild steals only when the teacher opts in, and it adds a score-swing mechanic for 12-year-olds that the audience rules did not approve.

Rule load in Stüdyo and Arena is very high: relay, shadow cards, sparks, 3-4 lifelines, banking, Rüzgâr comeback, station wheel, Seçeneksiz bil, Neden?, streak multipliers. A1 and A2 adults (often older, less gamified learners) and A-level Arena classes will spend classroom English time learning rules explained in Turkish. The kids' '3 rules' list also hides lifelines, stars, stickers and titles.

The pacing math does not close. Arena: 12 rungs, 3 teams, about 50 s per turn, with 3-4 shared rungs gives roughly 8-9 relay rungs × 3 × 50 s ≈ 22 min, before the opener, checkpoints and explanations. That overshoots the stated 20-25 min, and B2 15-rung Stüdyo is worse. Oyun Parkı with second tries and the stirrer is also borderline for 15-20 min, so younger classes will rarely reach the Moon, which is the payoff.

Distractor quality from words.js: 'never a synonym of the key' needs synonym data that words.js does not have (only POS, definition, band and TR). Same-POS, same-band distractors will sometimes be defensible answers, especially meaning rungs at B1-B2.

The LLM path for kids: a Turkish free prompt ('3. sınıf, hayvanlar ve yiyecekler') must return picture-backed options, but the spec does not say where the images come from. The LLM will invent imageKeys that don't exist, or emoji that render differently across projector OSes.
B2 adult ceiling: four-option recognition at B2 feels like a test prep worksheet. Seçeneksiz bil covers only 3 rungs, so most of a B2 lesson is still pick-a-letter, with low stretch.

Adult babyishness is mostly avoided (Stüdyo has no mascot), but the shared 'Tek roket' and rocket assets must never leak into adult A1. If a teacher overrides, the A1 adults' easy emoji rungs plus the scale sounds could read as childish.

The Arena ranks at A1/A2 Genç (13-year-olds with A1 content): the 10-rung tower keeps Bronze to Legend naming, but the LGS-style context top rungs assume B1. A1-level Arena content for its top rungs is not specified.
The spec never shows 'sound' minimal-pair rungs working with browser TTS. Ship/sheep via speechSynthesis is often indistinct, and there is no teacher-read fallback per rung.
fixes: Make the answer spoken as language, not as a letter. The ritual becomes 'Final answer: B, giraffe!' (A levels: say the option word; B levels: say the full completed sentence). The teacher's lock-in button stays the same. The choral repeat is always the key word or sentence, never the letter.

Add production rungs per level. A1/A2 Genç: 'Say it!' picture rungs where the team names the picture before the options appear (the options are a fallback, and a correct answer without options earns a star). A2+: one short whiteboard-write rung per band (spell the word, or complete the gap without options). This extends Seçeneksiz bil downward in easier forms.

Kids' retry rule: the second try only counts after the active team says the word aloud following Gogo's model. The rocket moves on the saying, which turns the guess into a pronunciation rep. The hint order becomes: listen again, then the first letter, then the picture.

Ship curated picture packs for A1/A2 Genç: 12-16 YLE Starters/Movers topics with a vetted image or emoji set, including action verbs and prepositions drawn as simple SVGs. Restrict the LLM to choosing imageKeys from that whitelist; any other key fails validation. Show a pool-count badge per topic in setup.
Have Gogo (TR voice, or 'Öğretmen okur') read whyTr aloud for Oyun Parkı. Raise the explanation time to 8 s for kids, or make it tap-to-advance, and show only a picture plus 3-5 Turkish words.
Default Arena steal to OFF and make it an opt-in dial, in line with the Nazik rule. The default shadow reward is +5 XP for a correct card, with no taking from the hot team.

Make three rule tiers visible in setup: 'Basit' (relay, shadow cards, 50:50 only), 'Standart', 'Tam'. The default for A1/A2 adults and A-level Arena is Basit. Show a one-slide rule card per tier and keep the kids' lifelines as one-tap icons that are introduced only when first used.

Fix the pacing: compute the ladder length from real per-turn times, including second tries and explanations. Default Arena to 10 rungs for 3 teams, Stüdyo 15 rungs to Show mode only, and Park to 6 relay turns per team at most. Add a 'Moon guarantee': in the last 3 minutes the teacher can trigger 'Last fuel' early so the finale always happens.

Distractor safety: exclude words whose TR gloss matches the key's gloss, or whose definitions share the head noun or verb, as a cheap synonym proxy. Prefer the curated grammar_mcq_* and idioms.js for B1-B2 meaning rungs. Flag low-confidence derived rungs in the preview.

B2 adults: make Seçeneksiz bil available on every rung from 7 up, add 'Justify' rungs where the team must say why the trap is wrong for a spark, and add error-correction rungs (error items) from the bank.
Specify A1/A2-in-Arena content: use the same YLE-based items, but Arena's top rungs become a short picture notice or chat of 2-3 lines at A1 level, not LGS B1 texts.
For sound rungs, pre-record or teacher-read: show both words to the teacher only, add 'Öğretmen okur' per rung, and drop sound rungs automatically when no English voice is detected.
Audit that no Oyun Parkı asset or sound can appear under the Stüdyo skin, and give adult A1 photo or clean-icon picture rungs instead of cartoon emoji.

reviews.mergeWith: Absorb any generic 'Kahoot/quiz-show MCQ' candidate into this one. It should be the suite's single MCQ show game, sharing an MCQ item engine and validator with /sinif-oyunu.
issues: Scope is XL, not L. There are 3 play modes × 3 skins × about 25 dials, plus a Sırala opener, a station wheel with Green and Yellow slices, sparks, banking, Rüzgâr comeback, Seçeneksiz bil, Neden?, per-class difficulty recalibration, drag-to-reorder rungs, split-flap money values, certificates and a class record. Each of these is small, but together they make a combinatorial state machine that is very hard to test across 8 groups. That is the main build risk.

At its core it is an MCQ quiz with a theme, and it overlaps /sinif-oyunu (team MCQ board) and any Kahoot-style candidate. What makes it distinct is the escalating ladder, the lock-in and reveal ritual, lifelines and safe steps. Those must carry the whole feel, or it reads as a generic quiz in costume.

The teacher has to click too much each turn: choose the option, lock, 'Show!', reveal, tap the shadow-team chips (Hepsi, then untap the wrong ones), then next. With lifelines added (Az/Orta/Çok per option), that is 6-10 inputs per turn over about 30-40 turns. On a smartboard, at arm's length, while managing the class, this breaks the pace.
Keyboard shortcuts (A-D, L, R, 5, S, F, K, X, U) do nothing on a touch smartboard, which is the main Turkish classroom device. The touch control bar is not specified, and the plan relies on the keys.

One screen with a teacher-only 'Merdiven önizleme' carries a real risk that the key leaks onto the projector: the teacher opens the preview mid-lesson, or the 'Soru hatalı'/edit flows show keys. Nothing defines a hard projector-safe state.

Layout crowding: 3-4 ladders side by side, plus the question stem, 3-4 picture options, the seat spinner, lifeline icons, decision frames, the spark counters and Gogo, all at a kids' font floor of 6vh on a 16:9 projector. This will not fit as described.

Arena contradiction: the shared rules say Nazik is ON in Arena and mild steals are opt-in, but this design makes 'STEAL!' (half the rung's XP) the default Arena rule. Several shadow teams stealing at once, on top of +5 per shadow answer, can also out-earn the hot team for a miss. Shadow play may pay better than climbing.

In Oyun Parkı, a miss means retry with a hint and nothing goes down, so the ladder's suspense is gone and every rocket ends on the Moon. The lock-in pause and 'Final answer' ritual become theatre with no stakes. That is fine for 9-year-olds, but the escalating-stakes mechanic that defines Millionaire is absent there. 'Tek roket' duplicates Show mode with the whole class as the contestant.

LLM reliability: single-key MCQs are the most reliable content type for an LLM, but a model's own difficulty ordering is unreliable, and 'band difficulty never goes down' cannot be verified from the LLM's diff field. The 'second LLM self-check' doubles cost and counts against the Material Maker rate limit. The trap flag and whyTr under 90 chars will often be missing or malformed.

Picture rungs for A1/A2 Genç: 'imageKey' implies an image library that does not exist. Only emoji are realistic, and native emoji rendering differs between the Windows smartboard, Chromebooks and Android panels (some panels show tofu). Many A1 words (was/were, can) cannot be pictured, so the pool shrinks.

The pool math is heavy. For example, 3 teams × 12 rungs means at least 35 items with a monotonic difficulty spread. The curated grammar_mcq banks hold about 22 items per unit and have no reliable diff, so 'mixed across units' plus words.js-derived items become the real default. Distractor quality from words.js needs a synonym check that does not exist. The words have no synonym field, so 'never a synonym of the key' cannot be checked.
TTS at 0.8x depends on an English speechSynthesis voice. Windows usually has Zira/David, but school images and Android panels vary. Gogo's 'voice lines' cannot be recorded assets within budget.
Per-class accuracy recalibration stored in localStorage is invisible, fragile across devices, and reorders ladders in ways the teacher cannot predict. It is poor value for v1.
Session time is tight: Stüdyo Relay at 60-70 s per turn × 3 teams × 8-10 relay rungs, plus misses and falls, can overrun 35 min. The time-fitting tool is hard to get right with a variable miss rate.
fixes: Ship an MVP core first. Relay mode plus Show mode, where Show is a single-ladder Relay and 'Tek roket' is a preset of it: class as one team, Oyun Parkı skin. Safe steps, the lock-in and reveal ritual, and three lifelines: 50:50 keeping the trap distractor, Sınıfa sor with coarse Az/Orta/Çok buttons, Arkadaşa danış. The seat spinner, 'Hep birlikte' low rungs, the preview, 'Soru hatalı' swap, Kaçırılanlar-to-warm-up, printable A-D and Yes/No cards, and the 3 skins. Move to v2: the Sırala opener, station wheel, Rüzgâr, Bırak banking, Seçeneksiz bil, split-flap money values, difficulty recalibration and drag-to-reorder rungs.

Collapse the per-turn flow to two taps. Tapping an option locks it (amber). One large 'Göster' button runs the card-show cue, the suspense and the reveal together. After the reveal, the shadow chips default to 'nobody' and are optional. Sparks can be turned off entirely for kids, where a whole-class choral response replaces them. Target 3 or fewer touches per turn without lifelines.

Design touch first: a fixed bottom control bar at least 64px tall, with Lock/Göster/İleri/Geri al and a lifeline drawer. Put it on the side the teacher stands (a left/right toggle). Keys are a bonus for clicker and laptop users.

Add a hard projector-safe state. Keys and whyTr appear only after the reveal, the preview needs a hold-to-open (2 s) and blanks the stage, and an optional presenter window (a second window synced over BroadcastChannel) shows keys to the teacher only.

Layout: the active question takes about 70% of the stage and the ladders become a slim side rail of mini-ladders, with the active one enlarged. For 4 teams, show the ladders as a single shared 'altitude' track with team tokens instead of four full ladders. Test at 1280×720 and 1920×1080 at 6vh.

Arena: make STEAL opt-in, as the Nazik rules require. The default is +5 per correct shadow answer, capped below the hot team's rung XP. With steals on, split half the rung's XP among the correct shadow teams, never give each of them half.

Oyun Parkı: keep the stakes gentle but real. Correct on the first try earns a 'full thrust' (a bigger flame and a star), a correct second try climbs with no star, so the reveal still matters. Present 'Tek roket' as a preset, not a separate mode.

LLM path: generate unordered MCQs with a proposed diff, then compute difficulty in code (words.js band of the key and distractors, stem length, format weight) and build the ladder from that. Validate with a strict JSON schema, deterministic rules (duplicates, length outliers, key position, word caps via words.js lookup, a teenSafe keyword list), and ONE combined self-check call run only on items that fail the rules, which keeps the rate limit in hand. The teacher preview flags items under 'Kontrol et' instead of silently dropping them.

Images: self-host a curated OpenMoji or Twemoji SVG subset (about 400 icons mapped to A1/A2 YLE words) so kids' picture rungs render the same everywhere. The LLM may only choose from that key list. Unmapped words drop to non-picture rungs, and the pool check counts only picturable items.

Distractors derived from words.js: same part of speech plus same band, excluding words that share a Turkish translation with the key and words that appear in the key's definition. That is a cheap stand-in for a synonym check.

Voice: detect an English voice at setup. If there is none, switch to 'Öğretmen okur' automatically and show a speaker-to-teacher icon. Gogo speaks through TTS with speech bubbles; no recorded voice assets.

Assets budget: 8 animal-pilot rocket SVGs (one base rocket plus animal face swaps), Gogo in 4 states (idle, flap, talk, sleep), a 3-layer parallax sky, 12 Arena rank badges made as one SVG with tier colours plus a glint shader, 3 certificate templates, printable A-D and Yes/No card PDFs, and WebAudio-synthesised SFX (marimba, synth, piano scale notes; no audio files). Specify these explicitly so that polish is planned rather than hoped for.

Pacing: show a live 'kalan süre / kalan tur' estimate. If the game is running over, prompt the teacher to switch to 'son tur' so every team gets equal turns, rather than relying only on the up-front fit calculation. Default the suspense to 0.5-1 s and the explanation to 3 s.
Share the MCQ item engine, validator and preview UI with /sinif-oyunu and any quiz candidate, so the cost is paid once across the suite.

catalog.rankReason: The teacher's Millionaire (adult 8), cheap once the 'Herkes cevaplar' core exists. MVP: Relay plus Show mode (for kids, 'Tek roket' = the whole class as one team), safe steps, the lock-in and reveal ritual, and three lifelines that need no phones. Shadow teams commit face-down BEFORE the hot team talks, with one card per team. The flow is two taps: tapping an option locks it, and 'Göster' reveals. The ritual is said as language ('Final answer: B, giraffe!'), and kids get 'Say it!' picture rungs. The Sırala opener, the station wheel and the sparks economy move to v2.

catalog.name: Kategori Kapışması (Category Board)
catalog.familiarAs: Jeopardy / Factile category board (quiz-show "categories × values" game)
catalog.oneLiner: A board of 4-6 visible categories with values that rise down each column. Teams choose where to play, then every team answers each clue at once on mini-whiteboards, so no single team can dominate by buzzing first. The game adds a hidden double cell, one challenge card per team and a final round (with a secret wager for older students). The same board plays as a kids' treasure island, a teen neon match and an adult quiz night.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (2-3 min, teacher laptop on the projector)
1. The group chip produces the summary line, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 sn · 30 dk', with a 'Değiştir' link. The teacher picks a content source:
   (a) Hazır kategoriler: drag 4-6 category cards from the level library onto the board. Each card previews its easy-to-hard ladder.
   (b) Konu yaz: a free prompt, Turkish is fine (e.g. '8. sınıf Friendship ünitesi + phrasal verbs'). The LLM returns 4-6 categories and the validator checks them. The teacher can regenerate one cell or one whole category, lock the good ones, and edit any clue inline.
   (c) Karışık: a mix of both.
   The lesson-fit timer suggests a board size, e.g. '5×5 + Final ≈ 32 dk' or '4×3 + Büyük Hazine ≈ 18 dk'.
2. Teams: 2-6. Names and emblems follow the audience mode (animal mascots / geometric emblems / quiz-night names).
3. Presentation mode: 'İkinci pencere' opens the student board on the projector while the teacher window keeps the answers, the location of the hidden double cell and the marking panel (the two windows sync through BroadcastChannel). With only one screen, answers stay hidden until the teacher presses R. The teacher's phone can also be a remote (QR).
4. Opening: the value tiles flip in with a 'board fill' animation, then the categories flip in one at a time with a drumroll while the teacher (or TTS) reads each name. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo plays a 20-30 s practice chest that does not score. In Arena, teams get 10 s to pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.

ONE TURN (about 60-80 s in the default mode)
1. PICK. The picking team (fixed rotation) names a category and a value. The teacher taps the cell or types its code, e.g. 'C3' (column letter, row number); the code echoes large on the board, and the chosen cell glows in the picking team's colour. Comeback (Light): at the start of each new rotation the trailing team picks first, and when it answers correctly it gets a small Slipstream bonus.
2. CLUE. The cell zooms to full screen and the clue is read aloud: automatic TTS at 0.8x for A1/A2 Genç, a speaker button for everyone else, and 'Öğretmen okur' when no English voice is available. For choice formats the options appear after the options delay (Stüdyo 2 s, Arena 2.5 s, Oyun Parkı 3-4 s).
3. TEAM TALK. Huddle for 20 s (Stüdyo), 15 s (Arena) or 10 s (Oyun Parkı). Then the writer, chosen by the seat-number spinner, writes the team's answer on its mini-whiteboard. The spinner rotates so everyone writes, and nobody is ever picked by name.
4. BOARDS UP. On '3-2-1… Boards up!' ('Show me!' for kids) every team raises its board at the same moment, which stops copying. Single-choice items also get a whole-class response (A/B/C cards or TPR) in Genç groups.
5. MARK. The teacher presses R: the answer appears with its one-line 'why' (whyTr at A levels, whyEn at B), an example and the IPA. Number keys 1-6 toggle each team's chip to correct, 0 toggles all teams, and Enter applies. Scores roll up.
6. SCORE. Every correct team earns the cell value. If the picking team was correct it also gets the Picker's bonus of +20% (+20 on a 100 cell, +100 on a 500 cell). This rewards choosing hard cells but stays too small to decide the game. The used cell greys out and keeps a small dot in the colour AND shape of every team that got it right, plus a stripe for the picker, so by the end the board is a visual history of the game.
7. WRONG ANSWERS follow the audience rules: kids get a second try with a hint; in Arena the streak breaks; adults see the answer plus the 'why'. In the default mode a wrong answer never costs points.
8. Play passes to the next team in the rotation. Every 5-6 cells in Oyun Parkı (and optionally in Arena) a stirrer or settler interlude runs.

ANSWER MODES (teacher choice; the default is 'Herkes cevaplar' for every audience)
- Herkes cevaplar: the turn described above.
- Sıra (classic): only the picking team answers, through a rotating spokesperson. On a miss, ONE other team may steal (the first hand up, or the spinner picks the team). The first team loses nothing unless adult negative points are on.
- Buzzer (opt-in for Stüdyo and Arena, never for kids): laptop keys A, L, Z, M, Q, P with a 'runner' per team who walks up (the runner rotates by seat number), or one phone per team as a buzzer through a QR code. Buzzing only opens when a 'ready' light shows after the clue has been read. An early buzz locks that team out for 0.25 s. The buzz queue slides in, in team colours. A team that buzzes and answers wrong is locked out for that clue, and the next team in the queue answers. There is also a 'teacher decides' lock.

HINT LADDER (teacher presses H; every hint is shown to all teams)
- Oyun Parkı: picture, then first letter, then 'listen again'. All hints are free.
- Arena: first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example. Each hint lowers the cell's value one step for everyone (400 becomes 300), never below the lowest row.
- Stüdyo: definition, then example, then Turkish gloss (the gloss can be switched off for immersion classes). Each hint costs one step, as in Arena.

SPECIAL CELLS
- Double cell: 'Double Down' (Stüdyo), 'Power Cell' (Arena), 'Mystery Chest' (Oyun Parkı). There is 1 per board, or 2 on a 6×5 board or a second round. A seeded RNG places it at the start, in rows 3-5, never two in one column. Only the teacher window shows the seed and the location, so the placement cannot be disputed. Only the picking team plays it.
  · Stüdyo: the category is shown, then the team wagers BEFORE seeing the clue, with a slider from 5 up to the larger of its score and the top board value, plus an 'All in!' button. Correct adds the wager. Wrong subtracts the wager, but not below 0 unless negatives are on.
  · Arena: the wager is capped at half the team's score (minimum: the cell's value), the score never goes below zero, and the commentator shows 'CLUTCH!' on a correct answer.
  · Oyun Parkı: the chest opens to a random risk-free Green treasure (Double stars, Gift a star to a team you tap, Everyone +1 star, Pick again, or Brain break, where Gogo dances for 30 s).
- 'Say it!' cells (pronunciation): the picking team's spinner-picked student says the item and the teacher judges it. Then the TTS model plays and the whole class echoes it twice. In all-answer mode the other teams play the same cell as 'Which one did you hear? A or B' with hand signals, for the same value.

İTİRAZ (challenge) CARD (Arena and Stüdyo; off in Oyun Parkı)
Each team gets one per game. The team taps its chip, or the teacher presses I plus the team number. That opens a 30 s window in which the spokesperson argues the answer (in English at B levels; Turkish is fine at A levels). The teacher upholds or overturns the decision. Every challenge is logged and can be undone. A team that wins its challenge keeps the card.

FINAL ROUND (when the board is cleared, or when the lesson-fit timer offers 'Final'e geç')
- Stüdyo 'Final Bet':
  1. The category is shown, and teams get 20 s.
  2. Each team writes a secret wager (0 up to its score) on the back of its whiteboard. The teacher enters the wagers privately, on the teacher window or the phone remote.
  3. The clue appears, with 30-60 s and a quiet thinking loop that can be muted.
  4. Boards go face down.
  5. Teams are revealed one at a time, lowest score first: answer, then wager, then the score rolls.
  A team at 0 or below plays a 'Free shot' worth the lowest board value.
- Arena 'Last Stand': the same flow, with wagers capped at half the score.
- Oyun Parkı 'Big Treasure': no wager. Every team that gets it right earns 5 stars.
- Tiebreak (Arena and Stüdyo): an estimation question (a qa item with a number answer and a tolerance). The closest team wins. In Oyun Parkı, tied teams share the title.

END
- Oyun Parkı: team titles and a class-album sticker.
- Arena: a podium plus stat awards.
- Stüdyo: full scores plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list.
- Every mode: a per-category heat map for the teacher ('Zayıf kategori: Phrasal verbs') that feeds the review list.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Teams: 2-6 teams of 3-5 students (up to about 36 students).
- Materials: one screen, plus one mini-whiteboard (or an A4 sheet in a plastic sleeve) and a marker per team. Oyun Parkı teams also get printed A/B/C answer cards; the setup screen offers them as a print sheet.
- Roles: students have seat numbers 1-5 inside their team. The seat spinner uses them to choose the writer, the spokesperson, the buzzer runner and the Say it! speaker, so nobody is ever picked by name.
- Optional devices: the teacher's phone as a private remote (answers, wagers, the double-cell location). For adult or private-course groups only, one phone per team as a buzzer or answer pad, joined by QR with random nicknames. Oyun Parkı runs on the teacher's device only.
skills: listening (clues read aloud, 'Which did you hear?', spelling dictation)
question formation ('What's the question?' category, optional question-form rule)
catalog.contentShape:
BOARD ENVELOPE (pack.frames.board)
{title, titleTr, categories[4-6], final, tiebreaks[2]}
- Each category: {id, labelEn (4 words or fewer), labelTr, icon (emoji or SVG key), template, itemIds[3-5]}. itemIds are in ladder order, easy to hard.
- template is one of: 'picture' | 'define' | 'tr-en' | 'spell' | 'fix' | 'fill' | 'tf' | 'odd' | 'riddle' | 'sayit' | 'order' | 'question' | 'opposites' | 'mixed'.
- final: {categoryLabel, itemId}.
- tiebreaks: qa items with answerKind 'number' and a tolerance.
- The CODE, never the LLM, computes values, the double-cell positions and the seed.

HOW EACH ITEM TYPE BECOMES A CLUE
- vocab:
  · 'picture': media.emoji or media.img, answer = term.
  · 'define': defEasy for A groups, def for B groups, answer = term.
  · 'tr-en': defTr, answer = term.
  · 'spell': TTS says the term and the example; teams write the spelling; no fuzzy matching.
- qa: clue and accept[]. teacherJudge=true for open answers.
- mcq: options appear after the delay. In B-group 'open' categories the options are hidden and the key becomes the accepted answer, but only when the key is 4 words or fewer.
- gap: bank[] for A groups and teens; typed or written at B.
- error: 'Fix it'. Show wrong; answer = right; the span is highlighted on reveal.
- tf: kids answer with thumbs up or down.
- odd: write the odd one out. At B levels a correct reason (reasonEn) earns +1 step.
- riddle: the cell's value sets how many clues are shown. 100 shows all three clues, 300 the two hardest, 500 only the hardest.
- sound: a Say it! cell, or 'Which did you hear?' with a/b.
- order: write the full sentence. alt[][] lists the other accepted orders.
- pair: 'Opposites' or 'Past forms'. Show a, answer b.
- 'question': a qa item whose clue is an answer ('Because I was ill.'); teams write the question (teacherJudge, model answer in accept[]).

ANSWER MATCHING (phone mode, and the suggestion shown in the teacher window)
Normalise case, spaces and apostrophes; strip the leading articles a/an/the. Accept every form in accept[] or alt[], including UK/US spellings, plurals and contractions. At Levenshtein distance 1 on answers of 5 or more letters, flag the answer yellow 'Yakın' for the teacher to decide; this never applies to spelling categories.

BUILT-IN LIBRARY
- grammar_mcq_* units: one unit becomes one category. The 5 items are ranked by per-item difficulty. 'Fix it' items are built by substituting a curated wrong option into the stem, with whyTr taken from whyOpt[].
- words.js: w/p/d/e/i/t give 'define', 'tr-en' and 'spell'. words.js has no topic tags, so topical categories need a small curated topic index (topic to headwords).
- idioms.js: 'Idioms', with the literal Turkish from lit.
- Plus YLE/MEB picture sets for the Genç groups.

LLM GENERATOR
- Input: the merged AudienceProfile plus the teacher's prompt.
- Output: 4-6 categories × 5 items in ladder order, plus the final and 2 estimation tiebreakers. Content is in English; labelTr is included.

VALIDATOR
- Clue length is within the text-load cap. An item that is too long is split or dropped, never shrunk.
- A clue never contains its answer or the answer's stem.
- Answers are unique across the board and never appear in another clue.
- Difficulty must rise within each category. Difficulty is computed from the answer's CEFR band in words.js, a format weight, clue length and grammar target. If the order is wrong the validator reorders; if a rung is missing it regenerates only that rung.
- teenSafe filter for every Genç group.
- A1/A2 Genç items need an imageKey or are dropped.
- The final item aims for about 50% success. Tiebreaker answers must be well-known numbers.
catalog.adultVersion:
'CATEGORY NIGHT' (Stüdyo, A1-B2 adults)

LOOK AND SOUND
- Editorial quiz-night look: a cream paper board with ink-navy tabular numerals, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme (deep navy board, white numerals, thin gold rules). System sans, no mascot, no voice lines.
- Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs', 'Present Perfectionists', 'Flat Whites').
- Captions stay neutral ('Round 1 · Travel').
- Sound: woodblock and piano, a 0.6 s chime plus the score rolling up. Music is off by default.
- English on the student screen, Turkish in the teacher chrome.

BOARD
- 5×5 (100-500) as standard; 6×5 for 40-minute lessons; 5×4 for 20 minutes.
- Optional second round 'Double Board': values 200-1000 and 2 Double Down cells. Categories carry over or are swapped.

RULES
- 'Herkes cevaplar' by default, with a rotating spokesperson and pair consultation inside the team. 20 s team talk; optional 30 s timer.
- Sıra and Buzzer modes are opt-in.
- Negative points are OFF by default. When switched on they apply only in the Buzzer and Sıra modes, where a team chooses to answer; they are suggested for B2 buzzer games.
- Double Down: real wager with an 'All in!' button.
- Final Bet: secret wagers, reveal from lowest score to highest.
- One İtiraz card per team.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default. The Red 'twist cells' (Reset, Swap scores, Virus) are off by default because they undo the strategy that makes this game.

OPTIONAL ADULT RULES
- Question-form rule (B1/B2): answers must be phrased 'What is a deadline?'. The acceptance is lenient: What/Who/Where + is/are, and articles are optional.
- 'Hard mode' (B2): answers must be full sentences.
- 'Open or options?' (Sıra mode): answer open for full value, or ask for the options at half value.

EXAMPLE CATEGORIES
Phrasal verbs with GET; False friends for Turkish speakers (sympathetic ≠ sempatik, actually ≠ aktüel); Silent letters; Say it politely (rewrite 'Give me the report.'); Fix the mistake; Collocations: make or do?; Word families (decide → decision → decisive); Idioms (with literal Turkish in the reveal); At the airport; Job interview; Small talk; What's the question?; Numbers & trivia in English.

END
- Full scores; the 'Kaçırılanlar' list (every missed item with answer, why and example) that can be printed or sent to the Material Maker as homework; the category heat map.
catalog.teenVersion:
TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT RULESETS, NOT A RE-SKIN. The group label is never shown to students.

1) OYUN PARKI (9-11 years; default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç): 'TREASURE ISLAND' (Hazine Adası)

Look and sound
- A cream-and-sunshine map. Categories are picture flags (🐼 Animals, 🍎 Food, 🎨 Colours & Shapes, 🎒 In my school bag, 🔢 Numbers, 🧍 My body, 🌦 Weather), and the cells are treasure chests. Values are shown as 1-4 stars, never numbers.
- Andika-type font; the prompt font is at least 6vh.
- Team mascots: Panda, Fox, Lion, Frog, Tiger, Rabbit.
- Host: Gogo the parrot. Gogo lands on the chosen chest, reads the clue aloud, says the answer after a miss, and sleeps on the pause screen.
- Sound: a marimba pack with no buzzers.
- Student-facing strings are tiny English ('Panda team, pick a chest!', 'Show me!', 'Well done!'). The teacher gets a Turkish rule card with pictograms.

Three rules
(1) Pick a chest. (2) Talk with your team, then Show me! (3) A right answer wins stars.
The Mystery Chest and Big Treasure are not rules the children need to learn; Gogo explains them when they happen.

Turn
1. A child from the picking team comes up and taps the chest; the spinner chooses the seat number.
2. A picture clue appears and is read at 0.8x.
3. After 3-4 s, 3 picture or word cards appear.
4. 10 s team talk.
5. 'One, two, three… Show me!': team boards or A/B/C cards go up, and the whole class answers with TPR (stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C).
6. The chest opens (coins, shells, gems) and stars fly to every team that was right.

Wrong answers
A soft 'boing' plays and the chest wiggles shut. A free hint (picture, then first letter, then listen again) gives every team that missed a second try. If they still miss, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album (not the win count).

Other rules
- No picker's bonus: the picking team's reward is getting to open the chest.
- Mystery Chest: a risk-free Green treasure.
- No wagers, no İtiraz, no buzzers, no steals.
- Timer off by default; when on, a 40 s calm ring that never turns red.

Pacing and ending
- Board: 4×3 (about 15-18 min) or 4×4 (about 25 min).
- Every 5-6 chests the ship sails to the next island for a 45 s stirrer ('Stand up if you have a cat!') or a 60 s settler (trace the word in the air).
- Finale 'Big Treasure': every team that gets it right earns 5 stars. Confetti in team colours and shapes, used only here.
- Every team gets a title from its stats (Super Listeners, Sharp Spellers, Bravest Guessers, Best Helpers, Treasure Hunters), and the class album gets an island sticker.

Kids checklist: 3 rules, 20 s to explain, no elimination, no score below zero, a whole-class response every turn, and gentle failure imagery (a closed chest, a fizzled sparkle; no bombs or skulls). It passes.

2) ARENA (12-14 years; default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç, and suggested for any class in grade 6+ or when 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor' is ticked): 'GRID CLASH' (a Match)

Look and sound
- A dark navy/charcoal grid with neon cell edges in team colours and a condensed display font.
- Emblems: bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond. In the 10 s ownership moment teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
- No mascot, no pastels, no 'superstar'. A commentator strip shows 'COMBO x3', 'CLEAN SWEEP' (all teams right) or 'CLUTCH!', at most once per turn.
- Short synth blips; 1.2 s combo text.
- English rule card with a Turkish toggle.

Board and rules
- 5×4 (about 20 min) or 5×5 (about 30 min), values 100-500.
- 'Herkes cevaplar' with mini-whiteboards, the seat spinner, a 15 s huddle and a 30 s timer ring in the team colour.
- Streaks and combos: x1.5 at 3 correct in a row, x2 at 5, based on accuracy only. The score floor is zero.
- Hints lower the cell value by one step.
- Power Cell wager is capped at half the team's score.
- Sıra mode allows one steal, and the first team loses nothing.
- One İtiraz card per team.
- Yellow harshness is opt-in: 'Glitch cells' (Steal 5 from a tapped team, capped at that team's score, or Swap turn order).
- Final 'Last Stand': the wager is capped at half the score.

Categories
MEB-flavoured: Teen Life, Sports, Wild Animals, In the Kitchen, The Internet, Fix the glitch (error), Make the question, Phrasal verbs, LGS context (mcq with a short chat or poster).

Ending
A podium for the top 3 plus stat awards for the others (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, Category specialists, Big Bet). Never a 'last place'; nobody is ever named.

A 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena visuals with A1 content, full picture support and TTS. A 9-year-old B1 class keeps Treasure Island.
catalog.levelTuning:
SHARED LADDER RULE
Inside each category the values follow a ladder:
- Row 1 uses a word from one band below the level or the easiest format.
- The middle rows are at the level.
- The top row is a stretch item from one band above, or a harder format.
The code computes values from difficulty; the LLM never sets them. The 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' dial shifts the band mix (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words; Zor adds more top-row stretch items). 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole board one level.

A1 (adult cap 10 words; Genç 0-4 words, the picture carries the meaning)
- Formats: picture → word, TR → EN single words, yes/no statements, 3-option choices shown after the delay, gaps with a word bank (am/is/are, a/an, plurals), and 'spell it' at the 100-200 rows only.
- Genç: picture-only clues from the self-hosted SVG set (items without a picture are dropped), automatic 0.8x audio, A/B/C cards and TPR.
- Adults: short TR prompts are allowed in the teacher chrome; clues are simple English with a Turkish gloss as the last hint.
- Riddles are not used at A1.

A2 (adult cap 15; Genç 8)
- Formats: defEasy → word, past forms (go → ?), opposites, 4-option choices or one-word written answers, gaps with a bank or typed, tf about meaning, 3-clue riddles ('What am I?'), and 'Which did you hear?' minimal pairs.
- Genç: pictures still on every item; YLE Flyers and MEB grade 5-6 topics (My Town, Health, Weather and Emotions, Occupations).

B1 (adult cap 25; Genç 14)
- Formats: open short answers (teacherJudge with accept[]), fuller definitions, collocations (make/do, take/have), Fix it error correction, Finish the sentence, 'What's the question?' question formation, odd one out with a reason for +1 step, phrasal verbs, LGS-style context MCQs (Arena), and riddles where the value decides how many clues are shown.
- Stüdyo: the question-form rule becomes available (off by default).

B2 (adult cap 40; Genç 20)
- Adults: paraphrase and register ('Say it politely'), idiom meaning, word formation, 2-slot gaps, full-sentence answers ('Hard mode'), the optional question-form rule, wager rounds on grammar judgments, and estimation trivia in English.
- B2 Genç: richer language on CONCRETE topics (Planets, Natural Forces, Science, Tourism), plus word formation and collocations. No abstract debate and no adult domains.

TIMING AND SUPPORT BY LEVEL
- Options delay and hints: A1/A2 always show options after the delay. B levels hide options in 'open' categories. The TR-gloss hint can be switched off at B levels.
- Timers: A-level classes get +10 s by default in every mode.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-45. Oyun Parkı 15-25 (a 4×3 or 4×4 board with 2 interludes and Big Treasure). Arena 20-30 (5×4 or 5×5 plus Last Stand). Stüdyo 25-45 (one 5×5 board plus the Final is about 32 min; 6×5 or a second 'Double Board' round is about 45). The default mode takes about 60-80 s per cell.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Board size: 4×3, 4×4, 5×4, 5×5 or 6×5; optional second round.
- Value set (100-500, 200-1000, or 1-4 stars).
- Category source: library, prompt or mix. Drag to reorder columns; regenerate or lock a category or a single cell; edit a clue or its accept[] inline.
- 'Kategori değiştir': swap a whole category live for another library category at the same level when it proves too hard.

MODES AND RULES
- Answer mode: Herkes cevaplar / Sıra / Buzzer. Buzzer lock: on / off / teacher decides. Early-buzz lockout on or off.
- Timers: reading timer and answer timer (Süresiz / 30 s / 40 s / custom), +10 s, pause.
- Hints: the hint ladder on or off; the TR gloss on or off.
- Scoring: Picker's bonus (0 / 10 / 20%); negative points (Sıra and Buzzer modes only); Comeback dial (Off / Light / Strong); Harshness level (Green / Yellow / Red, per audience limits).
- Special cells and final: number of double cells (0-2); wager on or off; Final on or off, with wager caps and reveal order (lowest first / highest first / table order); tiebreaker on or off.
- İtiraz cards on or off.
- The question-form rule and 'Hard mode' (B1/B2 Stüdyo).

LIVE
- Manual score edit (click a score).
- Multi-level undo of any scoring event, including wagers and challenges.
- Skip a cell or mark it 'kimse' (nobody).
- 'Final'e geç' and 'Satırı kapat' (close the remaining 100 row) when time runs short. The lesson-fit timer offers these at 8 minutes left.
- Presentation mode (a second window or the phone remote, which privately shows answers, wagers and the double-cell location).
- Reduced motion; music mute.

KEYBOARD
- Column letter + row number, e.g. C3, opens a cell (Enter).
- R: reveal the answer.
- 1-6: toggle a team as correct; 0: toggle all; Enter: apply; Shift+1-6: mark wrong (negatives).
- H: next hint.
- S: spin a seat number.
- T: pause; +: add 10 s.
- I followed by a team number: İtiraz.
- U: undo.
- G: go to the Final.
- M: mute.
- F: fullscreen.
- Esc: back to the board.
- Buzzer keys A / L / Z / M / Q / P are live only while a clue is open in Buzzer mode.

SAVING
The audience profile and the board are saved to the class profile ('7-B · A2 Genç · Arena'). The lesson-fit estimate learns this class's average seconds per cell.
catalog.delightDetails:
- The value tiles flip in with the classic 'board fill' cascade, then the categories flip in one at a time with a drumroll. The sound follows the audience: a marimba roll for kids, a synth riser in Arena, a soft piano roll for adults.
- A typed cell code ('C3') echoes large on the board, the cell glows in the picking team's colour, and it zooms open to full screen.
- Used cells keep dots in the colour AND shape of every team that got them right, plus a picker's stripe. The finished board reads as a history of the game, and the markers stay usable for colour-blind students.
- Double-cell reveals:
  · Stüdyo: a spotlight sweep and a gold foil 'DOUBLE DOWN' stamp.
  · Arena: a glitch-flash 'POWER CELL'.
  · Oyun Parkı: the chest shakes, sparkles pour out and Gogo gasps.
  The wager slider has an 'All in!' button that fires a small burst (adults).
- 'CLEAN SWEEP' when every team is right; in Oyun Parkı that also adds a class star to the album.
- A riddle's value controls its clues: 100 shows three clues, 500 only the hardest.
- The answer card shows the IPA, a speaker button and a real example sentence. For idioms it adds the literal Turkish, which gets a laugh.
- The final uses a 30 s thinking loop that can be muted, face-down boards, and a reveal from the lowest score to the highest with the score rolling up. In Arena the podium lifts.
- In Oyun Parkı the ship sails between islands at interludes. Every team leaves with an earned title and the class album gets a sticker.
- Teacher's end screen: a per-category heat map ('Zayıf kategori: Phrasal verbs') and a one-click 'Kaçırılanlar → ödev' export to the Material Maker.
- In the teacher window, near-miss answers are flagged yellow 'Yakın' so the teacher can accept them with one tap.
- Reduced motion replaces every effect with a static stamp. Every sound effect is 1 s or shorter and loudness-normalised.
catalog.risks:
- Buzzer chaos and fast students dominating. Buzzers are off by default; whiteboards with a simultaneous 'Boards up!' are the default. When buzzers are on: an early-buzz lockout, a lockout after a wrong buzz, and a rotating runner.
- Strong teams dominating. All teams score on every cell, the picker's bonus is only 20%, the trailing team picks first on each rotation, and there is a Slipstream bonus.
- Marking time with 6 whiteboards. Number-key toggles with 0 = 'toggle all'; phone answer pads with auto-matching can come in phase 2.
- Open-answer disputes. accept[] lists every valid form, the teacher window flags 'Yakın' near-misses, and teams have an İtiraz card with undo.
- Wager arithmetic confuses kids. Oyun Parkı has no wagers; Arena wagers are capped at half the score with a floor at zero.
- Answers leaking into clues, or ladders that do not rise. The validator checks both, the code computes values, and only a failing rung is regenerated.
- words.js has no topic tags, so topical built-in categories need a curated topic index.
- Overlap with /sinif-oyunu. It shares the team, score, spinner and sound engine and can launch as a sibling board type. It stays a distinct game because the categories and values are visible and choosing where to play is the strategy.
- Lessons overrunning. The lesson-fit timer offers 'Final'e geç' or closing a row.
- Projector legibility. Font floors are enforced and long items are split.
- Trademark. Avoid the 'Jeopardy' and 'Daily Double' names; use Kategori Kapışması, Double Down, Power Cell and Mystery Chest.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Share its engine with /sinif-oyunu (the Baamboozle-style tile board) as a sibling board type. Keep it a separate game in the menu.

issues: The control model is built for a laptop, not a smart board. The core loop runs on keys (typing 'C3', R, 1-6, 0, Enter, H, S, I+n, U). In most Turkish public schools the board PC is the only computer. The teacher stands at the touch surface with no keyboard, and an on-screen keyboard covers the board. The second window and the BroadcastChannel remote also assume a second display, which these classrooms rarely have.

The phone remote cannot work as specified. BroadcastChannel only syncs tabs inside one browser, so a QR-joined phone needs a server relay such as Supabase realtime. School Wi-Fi is often missing or filtered, and phones are often banned. Without the remote, wagers, answers and the double-cell location all have to sit on the shared screen.

Marking six whiteboards is the real bottleneck. From the front, the teacher cannot read six handwritten answers from 10-year-olds held up across a crowded room, so the teacher has to walk the aisles, which breaks 'standing at the board'. That realistically takes 20-40 s per cell, on top of the time it takes to decide which chip matches which team.

The per-cell time is optimistic for kids. The Oyun Parkı turn is: a child walks to the board, seat spin, TTS, a 3-4 s options delay, 10 s talk, boards plus TPR, reveal, then for teams that missed a hint, a second talk and second boards, then the class echoes twice. That is about 100-140 s, not 60-80. A 4×3 board with 2 interludes, the opening practice chest and Big Treasure comes to about 28-35 min, not 15-18.

The setup time is also optimistic in class. Dragging categories, six emblem/colour/motto picks in Arena (10 s is not enough for 13-year-olds to agree), printing A/B/C cards, and handing out boards and markers adds up to about 5-8 min of dead time at the start of a 40-minute lesson.

The two response channels clash. Mini-whiteboards and A/B/C TPR (stand, sit, hands up) run at the same moment for 28 kids in narrow Turkish desk rows. It gets loud, desks bang, and the teacher cannot check both. Whoever moves first on TPR also gives the answer away to the teams still writing.

Kids have no strategy to play. With no picker's bonus and everyone answering every cell, choosing a chest does not matter, so the walk-up tap is dead time and a queueing fight ('I want to tap!'). Once the category choice is irrelevant, the game is a sequential class quiz, which overlaps heavily with /sinif-oyunu.

The Arena streak multipliers (x1.5 at 3 in a row, x2 at 5) build a runaway leader. Every team answers every cell, so the strongest team is also the most likely to hold a streak, and its gains compound every turn. That works against the Slipstream comeback and the claim that no team falls hopelessly behind.

Hint costs are unfair in the all-answer mode. One H press lowers the value 'for everyone', so a team that already knew the answer loses points because another team struggled. It also opens arguments over who asked for the hint.

'Gift a star to a team you tap' (Mystery Chest) and the Arena Glitch cells ('Steal 5 from a tapped team') create social targeting among 10-14 year-olds. Friend groups gift to friends, the same unpopular team gets stolen from, and the teacher has to referee it.

The İtiraz card is a noise trap with teens. With 30 s arguments and one card per team, 13-year-olds will challenge every close call. At the A levels the arguing happens in Turkish, which adds teacher load without adding English. It works with adults.

The Final Bet logistics do not scale. Six teams write secret wagers, and the teacher has to collect and type them privately. Without a phone remote that means walking around the room, reading the backs of whiteboards, and typing on a board everyone can see. That is 2-3 min of dead time, and the secrecy leaks.

The seat spinner assumes teams of exactly 1-5. With 28 students in 6 teams (a mix of 4s and 5s) plus absences, it will land on 'seat 5' in a team of 4. It also cannot handle a student who refuses to write or to speak.

The 'Say it!' cells single out one child to pronounce a word in front of 28 peers, with the teacher judging publicly. That is anxiety-inducing for 10-12 year-olds, and the 'Which did you hear?' step for the other teams adds another response round to the turn.

The game is not robust to bell and network failures. It has no explicit 'Kaydet, sonraki derste devam' (save the mid-board state and resume next lesson). LLM generation during class depends on school internet and the rate limit, and TTS on a Pardus or Windows board PC often has no English voice.

The teacher faces far too many options. The teacherControls list runs to about 25 dials (answer mode, buzzer lock, negatives, Comeback, harshness, picker %, wager caps, reveal order and more). A teacher preparing between lessons will not configure all of that, and wrong combinations (for example negatives on plus Comeback Strong) produce odd games.

The spec covers features, not what happens in a real room. It does not say what to do with a late team, a merged team, an absent student, or adding and removing a team mid-game. Evening adult classes very often have latecomers arriving 10 minutes in.

Adults may find mini-whiteboards childish, and 10 adults make only 2-3 teams, so a 5×5 board gives each team 8-12 picks. That is fine, but at 60-80 s per cell plus a Double Board round the lesson overruns easily. In adult classes the teacher can usually just hear the answers, so the fixed huddle-then-boards ritual feels slow.
fixes: Design touch-first: dock a large 'teacher bar' along the bottom of the board, reachable by a short adult. It needs Reveal, team chips (tap = correct, preset to 'all correct' so the teacher only deselects), Hint, Undo, Pause and Final buttons, with at least 64 px targets. Tapping a cell opens it. Keep the keyboard shortcuts as an extra for laptops, and never require typing a cell code.

Treat a single screen as the primary mode. Answers, the double-cell location and wagers stay hidden behind a 'göz' long-press peek that the teacher holds with their body blocking the view. Build the phone remote on Supabase realtime as phase 2 and make sure nothing depends on it.

Cut marking time: tell teams to hold boards up in the same left-to-right order as the on-screen chips (show the chip order as a seating map). Allow 'answer-card mode' at A levels (A/B/C/D cards only, instantly readable across the room) instead of written boards. Show an 8 s 'boards up' hold timer so the teacher scans once.

Pick ONE response channel per turn: either team boards/cards, or whole-class TPR, set per category. TPR comes only after boards are down, as a reinforcement echo. Use seated TPR (point, thumbs, fingers 1-3) rather than stand/sit in crowded rooms.

Re-time the kids variant honestly. Drop the walk-up tap (the picking team calls the chest from its seat and the teacher taps), limit the second-try hint to one quick retry with a 5 s talk, and base the lesson-fit estimate on measured per-cell time from the class profile. Start it at about 110 s per cell for Oyun Parkı and about 75 s for Stüdyo.

Give kids a reason to pick: the picking team wins a small cosmetic reward (it places its mascot flag on the chest, and the island map shows the flags), or choosing a harder chest gives the class a bonus sticker. Otherwise, route Oyun Parkı to the /sinif-oyunu engine as a 'category board' skin and keep this game's real identity for Arena and Stüdyo.

Replace the Arena multipliers with a flat streak bonus (+50 at 3, +100 at 5) or a purely cosmetic 'COMBO' badge. Cap how many points any bonus can add per turn, and check in simulation that the gap between teams stays within one or two top-cell values.

Change how hints work in all-answer mode: the first boards-up is always at full value, and hints unlock only a second chance, at one step lower, for the teams that missed. No team is ever penalised for another team's hint.

Remove targeting from anything the kids or teens choose: 'Gift a star' becomes 'Every team +1 star'; Glitch 'Steal' becomes 'the leader gives 1 star to the bank' or is cut from Arena. No mechanic should let students pick another team to hurt or favour.

Limit İtiraz: Stüdyo only by default, opt-in for Arena, a 20 s window, English required at B levels, and a lost challenge costs the card. At A levels, use the 'Yakın' teacher-accept instead of a student challenge.

Make the final work on one screen: use the whiteboard itself as the secret wager (teams write it in a corner, fold or cover it, and reveal it together at the end). The teacher then enters only revealed wagers during the lowest-to-highest reveal, so nothing has to be typed privately. Offer a 'no-wager final' as the one-tap default for classes of 5-6 teams.
Seat spinner: set each team's size at setup (2-6) and allow 'this seat is absent / pass' with one tap. Any student can 'pass the marker' once per game without penalty.
'Say it!' for kids becomes a choral cell: the whole picking team says it together, then the class echoes. Individual speaking is opt-in for Arena and Stüdyo only.

Add a 'Tahtayı kaydet / sonraki derste devam' function that auto-saves after every scoring event, with a one-tap resume. Require boards made from a prompt to be generated and saved before class (prep flow at home) with offline caching of the whole board. Pre-render the TTS audio at generation time or fall back to 'Öğretmen okur'.

Hide the dials behind three presets per audience ('Hızlı', 'Standart', 'Turnuva') plus a one-line summary. Put the advanced dials in a collapsed 'Uzman ayarları' panel with validation that blocks contradictory combinations.
Allow adding, merging or removing a team mid-game. A late team starts at the current median score with a 'Yeni geldi' label, and adults can join an existing team with one tap.
For adults, add an 'Hızlı' flow: optional spoken answers from the spokesperson instead of whiteboards, a 10 s talk, and a 4×4 default for 30 minutes. Keep the whiteboards as the 'fair mode' toggle.

Cut the scope for the MVP: all-answer mode, touch bar, double cell, no-wager final, heat map and Kaçırılanlar. Buzzer, phone pads, İtiraz, Glitch cells, the Double Board round and stat awards come in phase 2.

issues: Low language density. At 60-80 s per cell, a 5x5 board covers only about 25 items in 30 minutes, and each item is answered once by one writer per team. Most students spend most turns watching. For A-level groups that is far less practice than Kahoot or Baamboozle.

Team talk has no language target. At A1-B1 the 10-20 s huddle will run almost entirely in Turkish. 'Herkes cevaplar' then yields one written word per team, not speaking. The skills list says 'speaking (team talk)' but nothing in the design produces it.

The A1 Genç ladder has no production. Picture, then 3 options, then A/B/C cards or TPR is recognition only. Every category in Treasure Island becomes the same picture quiz with a different flag, so the category-as-strategy idea shrinks to 'which animal set'. Nobody says or writes the word unless the class misses (echo only after a miss).

Mini-whiteboard writing at 9-10 years old with A1 is unrealistic for the 'spell' and open templates. Many of these children barely write English, and the spelling rows at 100-200 would stall a turn or make the stronger speller always write, whatever the spinner picks.

The difficulty ladder rests on data that does not exist. The grammar_mcq banks have no per-item difficulty, so 'ranked by per-item difficulty' is invented. CEFR bands in words.js only cover vocab-answer items. Gap, error, order, question and tf items have no reliable difficulty signal, so the validator's 'reorder if not rising' is mostly guesswork, and ladders won't rise in grammar categories.

Teacher prompts will be gutted for the young groups. The rule 'A1/A2 Genç items need an imageKey or are dropped' will delete most LLM output for abstract MEB units (e.g. 'Friendship', 'Feelings', 'Daily routines' verbs). The self-hosted SVG set cannot cover open prompts, so boards come back half-empty with no explanation.

B2 Genç and adult trivia drifts toward general knowledge. 'Numbers & trivia', estimation tiebreaks and the concrete B2 Genç topics (Planets, Natural Forces, Science) reward world knowledge over English, and the LLM will happily write fact questions ('How many moons...'). For 12-year-olds, number estimation is also a pure guess.

Adult A1 gets the full Stüdyo stack: wagers, İtiraz with a 30 s argument, question-form and Double Board rounds. The rules exceed what the language can carry. İtiraz in Turkish at A levels becomes a Turkish debate, and the question-form rule is gated to B1+ but the wager/Final Bet explanation is English-only on the student screen.

Arena skin with A1 content (13-year-old A1): 'Fix the glitch', 'Make the question' and LGS context categories are listed as Arena defaults, but they are B1-level formats. Nothing ties Arena categories to the level profile, so an A1 Arena class could be served B1 templates.
'Which one did you hear?' minimal pairs and 'Say it!' judged by the teacher are subjective and slow with 6 teams. Hand signals for other teams duplicate the board-up moment.

Build size is L+ and several subsystems (BroadcastChannel second window, QR phone remote, phone buzzers, heat map, Material Maker export, lesson-fit learning, topic index) are not about level fit, but they pull effort away from the content validator the level fit depends on.
fixes: Raise practice density in every cell with a mandatory 'Everyone says it' beat after the reveal: the whole class chorally reads the answer or the example sentence (TTS model first). In Oyun Parkı also add 'point and say' for the picture. Optionally allow 'mini-set' cells at A levels (2-3 fast items per cell, shown as one chest).

Give team talk a language job. Show a 2-3 phrase scaffold on the huddle screen per level ('I think it's...', 'Are you sure?', 'Let's write...'). In Arena and Stüdyo add an optional 'English-only huddle' bonus that the teacher toggles per team.

Build a production rung into the A1 Genç ladder. 1 star is picture then choice. 2 stars is picture then say it (chorus plus picked seat). 3 stars is picture then letter tiles or a first-letter gap on the board. 4 stars is picture then write or say the word with a short phrase ('a red apple'). Keep the A/B/C cards as the safety net.

For Oyun Parkı, replace free writing with printable letter-tile strips or 'circle the right spelling' cards on 'spell' cells. Allow whiteboards to show a drawn picture or number instead of a word. The spinner must pick the writer and the design must not let a sibling write for them.

Make the ladder deterministic by FORMAT, not by an estimated difficulty score. Each rung maps to a template tier (e.g. recognize, then choose, then produce a word, then produce a phrase or fix). Use the CEFR band only as a secondary check for vocab answers. Tag grammar_mcq items once, offline, with an easy/mid/hard field instead of claiming per-item difficulty.

For young groups, let emoji and a curated icon fallback count as a picture. Have the LLM prompt demand concrete, picturable items, and show the teacher '3 item çıkarıldı: resim yok' with one-click regenerate. Warn up front when the prompt topic is abstract for A1/A2 Genç.

Add a 'language, not trivia' validator rule: every clue must test a word, form or structure, and the answer must be a lexical item from the level band, not a fact. Make tiebreaks language-based (e.g. 'How many letters in...', 'Write the longest word from the category in 20 s'). Drop number estimation for Genç groups.

Add a level gate on the Stüdyo rule stack. At A1/A2 adults: wager on, but with Turkish rule text on the student screen allowed; İtiraz off by default; Double Board off. Keep İtiraz and the question-form rule for B1+.

Filter category templates by LEVEL first and audience second. Arena category defaults must come from the level profile's whitelist, so a 13-year-old A1 class gets 'Picture → word', 'Opposites' and 'Yes/No' in neon, not 'Fix the glitch'.

Simplify pronunciation cells: 'Which did you hear?' for all teams with A/B cards (one simultaneous response), then a chorus echo. Drop teacher judging of individual Say it! performance at A levels to avoid singling out a child.

Scope phase 1 as board, whiteboards, hint ladder, one double cell, final and the three skins with the level-tiered template ladder. Defer phone buzzers, the QR remote, Double Board and lesson-fit learning to phase 2. Share the team, score and spinner engine with /sinif-oyunu.

reviews.mergeWith: Share its engine with /sinif-oyunu (the Baamboozle-style tile board) as a sibling board type. Keep it a separate game in the menu.
issues: The scope is XL, not L. It has three skins, three answer modes, buzzers on laptop keys and on phones, a second window over BroadcastChannel, a phone remote over QR, wagers, İtiraz cards, a hint ladder, a Say it! variant, 14 templates, a second round, tiebreaks, a lesson-fit timer that learns, a heat map and a Material Maker export. The v1 cannot ship all of that and stay polished.

The phone remote and phone buzzers need a realtime relay. Vercel serverless functions cannot hold websockets, so this needs Supabase Realtime channels plus pairing, reconnection and latency handling. For buzzers, latency fairness across phones on school Wi-Fi is a real problem. This is the riskiest piece, and it serves the smallest audience (adult private groups only).

Duplication risk: under the skin, a Jeopardy board is the same object as the /sinif-oyunu tile board (a grid of cells, team scores, reveal, mark). Other candidates in the suite, such as a Baamboozle or quiz-show game, will also be 'a grid of point tiles'. The distinction (visible categories and rising values, so choosing where to play is the strategy) is real but thin. It is also weakened here, because in 'Herkes cevaplar' every team scores every cell.

The default 'Herkes cevaplar' mode dilutes the core strategy. If every correct team gets the value, picking a 500 cell helps rival teams as much as your own team, apart from the 20% picker bonus. Board choice then barely matters, and the game becomes 'PowerPoint Jeopardy with slide order chosen by students'. That is fine for learning but weaker as a game.

In whiteboard mode the software never sees what students write, so the 'Yakın' Levenshtein flag in the teacher window has no input. It only works in phone mode. The spec describes it as a general feature.

Keyboard conflicts. F is fullscreen but also column F on a 6×5 board. M is mute and also a buzzer key. A/Z/L/Q/P buzzer keys collide with typed cell codes such as 'A3'. 'I plus team number' collides with typed codes. On a Turkish Q keyboard, Shift+digit produces punctuation ('Shift+2' gives an apostrophe), so key handling must use e.code rather than e.key.

Smartboards: many classroom smartboards are touch-only with no keyboard nearby. The whole marking flow is designed around keys (R, 1-6, 0, Enter, H, S). Without a full touch teacher dock, the game is unusable on the typical Turkish MEB smartboard.

Arena scoring stacks too many modifiers: streak multipliers of x1.5 and x2 on top of all-teams scoring, the picker's bonus, Slipstream, the trailing team picking first, capped wagers, hint step-downs and Glitch cells. The streak multiplier directly feeds a runaway leader, which contradicts the spec's own 'strong teams dominating' mitigation. Teachers will not be able to explain the scores.

The A1/A2 Genç rule 'items without imageKey are dropped' means LLM prompt boards for kids will lose most of their items unless a large, curated picture library already exists. The LLM cannot make images. Building a self-hosted SVG picture set is a big asset cost that the spec does not budget for.

LLM validity. Difficulty from the words.js band works only for single-word vocab answers. It is meaningless for grammar, error, question or order items, so 'reorder the ladder' will be noisy. LLM-generated number trivia for tiebreaks is a hallucination magnet. 'The final aims for about 50% success' cannot be checked. 'Answer never appears in another clue' and 'answers unique across the board' will force many regenerations on narrow topics.

Pacing for 9-11-year-olds: 60-80 s per cell, with a teacher reveal and marking every time, leaves long low-action gaps for children. A 4×4 board of about 25 minutes is at the edge of their attention span, even with interludes. The core loop (read, huddle, write, reveal) is a quiz, not play, so teenFit sits below adultFit.

Asset load is under-specified. It needs Gogo the parrot (animated: landing, gasp, sleep, dance), a chest and treasure set, an island map, a ship animation, Arena emblems, the gold foil stamp, and three SFX packs of about 25 sounds each, plus a self-hosted Andika font. Recorded audio files would bloat the page.

Web Speech TTS availability varies. Smartboard Android builds and some Windows installs lack a good en-US voice, and the 0.8x rate sounds robotic on some engines. The 'Say it!' model audio relies on this.
Seeded-RNG placement of the double cell 'so it cannot be disputed' is engineering for a problem that does not exist in a classroom.
The lesson-fit timer 'learns this class's average seconds per cell'. That is a stateful feature with little payoff for the v1.
fixes: Ship an MVP in three phases. P1: a single screen; 4×3 to 6×5 boards; Herkes cevaplar plus Sıra with one steal; a touch-and-keyboard teacher dock; the reveal with its why/example/IPA; the double cell (a wager in Stüdyo, a Green treasure for kids); Final; all three skins; the built-in library plus an LLM generator with a validator. P2: the second window over BroadcastChannel (cheap, no server); hints; İtiraz; the heat map with the Kaçırılanlar export. P3 only if there is demand: the phone remote, phone buzzers over Supabase Realtime, a second round, the learning lesson-fit timer.

Restore the strategy in Herkes cevaplar. The picking team earns the full value; other correct teams earn half, or a fixed 'support' value. Alternatively, keep all-full scoring but make the picker's bonus the double cell's exclusive domain. Put the rule in the teacher's rule card in one line.

Build it as a board type inside the /sinif-oyunu engine, sharing teams, scores, the spinner, undo, sound and the reveal card. Differentiate it by the visible category headers, the ladder values, the history dots and the Final. Do not also ship a separate generic 'quiz board' candidate.

Keyboard map: select cells with the digits 1-6 for columns and then 1-5 for rows (or by clicking). Move fullscreen and mute to F11 and a dock button, or to Ctrl-chords. Make buzzer keys live ONLY while a clue is open in Buzzer mode and disable every other letter shortcut in that state. Use KeyboardEvent.code everywhere.

Add a persistent, collapsible, touch-first teacher dock on the projected screen: Reveal, team chips that are tap-toggles, All, Apply, Hint, Spin, Undo, Final. Hide the answer until Reveal. Make every keyboard shortcut optional.
