Arena scoring: drop the streak multiplier, or make it a flat +1 step instead of x1.5/x2, and cap it. Keep at most 3 scoring modifiers on at once, and have the setup screen show a live 'score rules' summary line.

Kids' pictures: use a self-hosted emoji set (Twemoji/Noto, subset to about 600 glyphs as SVG sprites) keyed by a curated kids' topic index, and force the LLM to pick answers FROM that index for A1/A2 Genç (a constrained vocabulary list goes into the prompt). The validator then checks membership instead of dropping items afterwards.

LLM contract: a JSON schema with strict types per template. Let the code compute difficulty for vocab only; for other item types, trust the order the LLM emits plus a length heuristic. Take tiebreaks from a curated local bank of about 40 well-known numbers, never from the LLM. Drop the 50% target claim. Put a regenerate-cell button and inline editing up front, since the teacher is the real validator.

Kids' pacing: a 4×3 default board; option cards auto-appear after 3 s; every clue has a whole-class TPR moment; the reveal plus the chest animation takes 3 s or less; auto-advance to the next picker. Target 40-50 s per cell. Add a 'hızlı mod' where the teacher only taps 'Sınıf doğru' for single-choice items.
Remove the Levenshtein flag from whiteboard mode and keep it for phone mode (P3). In whiteboard mode, show the accept[] list on the teacher side instead.

Sounds: synthesise every SFX with WebAudio (marimba, synth blip and piano from oscillators plus envelopes), which costs zero asset bytes. Budget Gogo as one SVG with 4 CSS-animated poses. Target under 250 KB gzipped JS+SVG per game, not counting the font.
TTS: detect voices at setup. When no en-* voice exists, switch to 'Öğretmen okur' and show a banner. Mark 'Say it!' as needing either TTS or a teacher model.
Replace the seeded-RNG theatre with a random placement shown in the teacher view, with a 'yeniden yerleştir' button.
Replace the learning lesson-fit timer with a static estimate (cells × seconds per cell for the mode) plus an 8-minute warning that offers 'Final'e geç'.

catalog.rankReason: The teacher's Jeopardy and the best adult quiz (8.3). Build it as a sibling board format on c01's shell: one engine, but its own hub card, so it costs little. It is single-screen first, with a touch teacher bar and a long-press 'göz' peek. The picking team gets full value and other correct teams get half. A mandatory 'Everyone says it' echo follows every reveal, huddles get phrase scaffolds, and a 'What's the question?' category is included. The phone remote and phone buzzers wait for the realtime decision.

catalog.name: Tik Tak Bomba (Hot Potato Word Chain)
catalog.familiarAs: Pass the Bomb / Hot Potato (Sıcak Patates)
catalog.oneLiner: A category, letter chunk, rhyme or sentence frame appears and a hidden fuse starts ticking. The class passes a real soft object (or the on-screen bomb jumps from team to team), and each holder says one new valid word before passing it on. When it goes off, adults take a burnt-toast penalty card, Arena teams miss the survival bonus, and kids get to pick the next balloon. Nobody is ever out.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 40 s, teacher). The summary line reads e.g. '6-A · A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · 10 dk · Değiştir'. The teacher picks four things.
(a) PASS MODE:
- ÇEMBER: a circle or U-shape; one soft object passes hand to hand.
- SIRA: fixed rows of 24-40 students. Each row is a team with its own object passed seat to seat, and the on-screen fuse jumps from row to row.
- EKRAN: 2-6 teams. The bomb lives on the screen and jumps from team to team. Inside a team the speaking turn moves seat to seat.
(b) PROMPT KIND:
- Kategori ('Animals')
- Harf parçası ('words with SH')
- Kafiye ('rhymes with CAT')
- Son harf zinciri: the next word starts with the last letter of the previous one, optionally inside a category.
- Cümle: one sentence on a frame, B1+.
(c) CONTENT: a built-in deck, or a free-text prompt (Turkish is fine) for the LLM, previewed before play.
(d) LENGTH: Isınma (5 fuses, about 6 min) or Maç (3 rounds x 2-3 fuses, 12-15 min).

PRACTICE. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo runs a 25 s demo fuse that never scores: Gogo says 'Cat!', passes to an on-screen friend, the balloon pops and everyone claps. Arena and Stüdyo show a three-line rule card instead.

ONE FUSE (the turn):
1. The teacher taps 'Yeni tur' (Space). The prompt card flips in and is read aloud (0.8x for kids) or gets a speaker button. A reading beat of 2-4 s (the options-delay dial) comes before the fuse lights.
   Oyun Parkı adds a 15 s 'Warm-up with Gogo': the class says 3 example words together with their pictures. Those 3 stay pinned as 'free words' anyone may use, a safety net for kids who freeze.
2. The fuse lights with a hidden random length taken from the range: Park 40-90 s, Arena 25-60 s, Stüdyo 20-60 s, and x1.5 for sentences.
   'Adil fitil' means it can never end in the first 15 s, and in EKRAN/SIRA never before 3 passes or on the same team twice in a row. The tick is steady and speeds up only in the last 10 s; 'Tam gizli' keeps it steady to the end.
3. The holder says ONE new valid word (or sentence) and passes. The teacher is the judge and uses single keys:
   - Space, or a presenter clicker's forward key = valid word. A spark runs along the fuse, and the word jar fills or the team scores.
   - R = 'Repeat!'. A soft two-note 'already!' plays and the holder must say another word. The fuse keeps burning, so the lost time is the only cost.
   - H = Help (the hint ladder).
   - T = pause. B = bang now. Z = undo.
   The live list is optional. The teacher types and autocomplete comes from the category members; Enter adds a chip. Duplicates are caught automatically and the original chip wiggles. Words outside the pack are accepted but marked with a dot for the review. The chunk is highlighted inside the chip ('fiSH'). In chain mode the last letter grows and slides over to become the next target letter.
4. EKRAN/SIRA only: each holder has a shot clock (Park 10 s, Arena 5 s, Stüdyo 6 s). Its ring is in the team colour and is never red.
   If time runs out, the bomb simply moves on and nobody loses points. In Arena the streak breaks, and with Yellow opted in the next team may steal +1 with one word.
5. BANG / POP / OVERLOAD: at most 2 s of effect, then 'Freeze!' and the object stays where it is. The screen never names the holder; the object identifies them.
6. What happens next depends on the skin:
   - Oyun Parkı: the holder becomes 'Gogo's helper'. They pick the next picture category from 3 cards and, with the teacher, read out a Silly card that the WHOLE class performs (e.g. flap like Gogo and say the last word twice).
   - Arena: every other team gets +3 'Survive'. The holding team's streak breaks and it gains nothing; it never goes minus.
   - Stüdyo: the holding team takes a burnt-toast card. The holder may try a Defuse: 3 new words in 10 s, or one sentence with the target structure. Success scrapes the toast off, and each team has 2 defuse kits per game.
7. A 15 s review: a word cloud of the tapped or typed words, plus 3 'Words nobody said' from the category members, read aloud by the speech voice (TTS). Kids repeat each word twice after Gogo. Adults just see them, and the words go to 'Kaçırılanlar'.
8. Next fuse. Park changes the category every fuse, because the vocabulary is small. Arena and Stüdyo play 2 fuses per category, so the easy words run out and the pressure climbs.

HINT LADDER:
- Park (free): a strip of 4 pictures of unsaid members, then the first letter while Gogo says it slowly, then Gogo whispers the whole word.
- Arena: the first letter (1 pt), then a two-word choice strip (2 pts). A score never goes below 0.
- Stüdyo: a teammate may whisper once per fuse for free. Any further silent pass costs a 'half toast', and two halves snap into one.

SCORING AND END:
- Park is cooperative. Each fuse earns 1-3 stars against a par of new words scaled to fuse length and class size (par is about fuse seconds / 6). If nothing was tapped, the fuse earns 2 stars, and stars never go down. In team mode, teams collect stickers per word.
  At the end every team gets a title: Brave Speakers, Super Listeners (fewest repeats) or Best Helpers (most whispers given). The class album gets a 'Pop Party' sticker, and Gogo says goodbye while the class says its 3 favourite words.
- Arena: +1 per valid word. The combo is x1.5 at 3 and x2 at 5 successful turns in a row, based on accuracy only, plus +3 Survive.
  The finish is a podium with emblems plus stat awards: Longest chain, Clean sheet (never overloaded), Clutch and Comeback. There is never a last place.
- Stüdyo: the fewest toasts wins. A tie goes to a 20 s 'Sudden fuse' duel between the tied teams. Options: a final 'Double fuse' where toasts count double, and 'Bahis', a wager of 1-3 toasts that the team will not hold the last bomb.
  Then the full tally and 'Kaçırılanlar' (unsaid crib words, repeats, challenged words and flagged sentences), ready to copy or print as homework.

VARIANTS:
- CÜMLE (B1+): the holder says a full sentence on the frame ('I've never...'). Any grammatical, meaningful sentence counts. For adults the teacher flags errors with E, and they appear later in the review with a one-line 'why', never during the fuse.
- CHALLENGE (Stüdyo): another team calls 'Challenge!' on a doubtful word. T pauses and the teacher decides, with the crib and words.js match shown if the word was typed. A failed challenge costs the challenger a toast, in Standart only.
- SON HARF ZİNCİRİ: dead-end letters (q, x, z, and y at A levels) automatically become 'any letter'.
catalog.playerSetup:
A whole class of 8-40 on one projector, in one of three pass modes:
- ÇEMBER: a circle or U-shape of up to about 20. One soft object is passed from person to person; tables can form teams for the tally.
- SIRA: the default for fixed Turkish classroom rows of 24-40. The 3-6 rows are the teams; each row passes its own object seat to seat, and the screen bomb jumps from row to row.
- EKRAN: 2-6 teams of 4-8 anywhere in the room. The screen bomb jumps from team to team, and the speaker rotates by seat order inside the team.
Nobody is picked by name: the object or the seat order chooses the speaker, and tallies are kept per team, never per student.
catalog.contentShape:
The game consumes FUSE CARDS that code builds from pack items:
{id, kind: 'category'|'chunk'|'rhyme'|'chain'|'sentence', label, labelTr, imageKey?, crib[], minValid, fuse: [min, max]}

1. category-list (the main type). Fields: label (4 words or fewer, EN), labelTr, media.emoji / imageKey (required in Oyun Parkı), open (collocation-style sets the teacher judges), members[8-40] {text, alt[], level (computed), tr}, byLetter, minPerLetter (for the first-letter and last-letter chain modes), multiWord (B2 and adults).
   - Feasibility gate: at least max(12, 0.6 x class size) members at or below the group's word band. Open sets need 10 or more example members for the crib.
   - The members feed the live-list autocomplete, the duplicate check, the kids' picture strip, the printable crib and the 'Words nobody said' review.
2. vocab (secondary). It provides picture hints (media.emoji), defTr for the crib, TTS, and the source words for computed chunk prompts.
   - CHUNK cards are built by code, never by the LLM: {chunk: 'sh', position: 'any'|'start'|'end', count, examples[6]}, counting words.js words in the band (grep-built index).
   - A chunk is offered only if count ≥ 20 (A2), 30 (B1) or 40 (B2). A1/A2 Genç chunk cards also need 2 picturable example words.
3. sound, kind 'rhyme'. Fields: a, ipaA, key, tipTr. These make 'Rhymes with CAT' prompts with an audio model. Members come from the pack's rhyme set.
4. speaking-prompt, mode 'jam', for the Cümle variant (B1+, optional at A2). Fields: prompt (the frame, e.g. 'I've never ___'), starters[≤3], useful[≤5], target ('unit:b1-05'), secs (the fuse minimum).
5. chance-card: the bang deck.
   - Park 'Silly cards' are whole-class TPR tasks with textTr for A1 Genç and amount 0.
   - Arena 'Glitch cards' (Reverse, Double core) are Green by default; Yellow cards (Steal, Swap order) are opt-in.
   - Stüdyo 'Forfeits' (spell the last word, use it in a sentence, defuse) are Green/Yellow; Red cards (Virus: a second bomb) are opt-in.
   - Fields: kind, task ('speak'|'act'|'spell'|'sing'), text, amount, secs.

LLM generation: a free-text prompt such as 'mutfak, 5. sınıf' returns category-list items (label, labelTr, emoji, members with tr, open, multiWord), 3-6 sentence frames and optional chance cards.
- Code then computes levels from words.js, runs the teenSafe filter, drops unpicturable categories for A1/A2 Genç, and enforces the word caps.
- If a category is too narrow, code suggests widening it ('Çiftlik hayvanları dar kalıyor: Hayvanlar yapalım mı?').
catalog.adultVersion:
'Tick-Tock' (Stüdyo).

LOOK: an editorial quiz-night card on cream or on the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, system sans, no mascot and no voice lines. Three skins, one tap apart:
- Retro Bomb: a cartoon black bomb whose fuse spark crawls at a randomised speed, so nobody can read it as a clock, with a 0.3 s camera shake at the bang.
- Toaster: the tick is the toaster's timer; the bang is a DING and a burnt slice flies onto the holding team's plate.
- Sıcak Patates: a steaming potato that glows orange.
The default skin can be set per class.

SOUND: a woodblock tick that goes from 60 to 150 bpm in the last 10 s, a piano sting, and no music by default.

RULES:
- Individual or team pass. Each holder says one new word or sentence.
- The holder at the bang takes a toast for their team. The fewest toasts after 5-8 fuses wins.
- One free teammate whisper per fuse. After that, a silent pass costs a half toast.

ADULT EXTRAS:
- Defuse: 3 more words in 10 s, or one sentence with the target structure; 2 kits per team.
- Challenge!
- The sentence variant with target structures: present perfect 'Have you ever...?', second conditional 'If I won the lottery, I'd...', past continuous excuses 'I was ... when ...'.
- The last-letter chain, a Double final fuse, and the optional Bahis wager.

HARSHNESS: Green + Yellow by default (Reverse direction, Skip, Swap turn order). Red is opt-in and adds Virus: a second bomb joins the final fuse, so two objects circulate.

PROMPTS: life and work topics (things in an office, reasons to call in sick, things you do at an airport, job-interview verbs); collocations (things you can MAKE / DO / TAKE); phrasal verbs with UP/OUT; word formation (-tion, -ment, un-); colour idioms from idioms.js; word families.

REVIEW: 'Kaçırılanlar', with an optional Turkish gloss (it can be switched off for immersion classes). Adults see English on the student screen and Turkish in the teacher chrome.
catalog.teenVersion:
There are two stripped rulesets, both with Nazik on. The group label never appears on screen.

OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11; default for A1 and A2 Genç): 'Gogo's Balloon'.
LOOK AND SOUND:
- Cream background, warm bright colours, rounded shapes, an Andika-type font, and animal team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit).
- On screen, a balloon slowly inflates with a soft rising stretch-squeak. It wobbles more near the end but never turns red.
- At the POP, the balloon bursts into a 2 s shower of the pictures of the words the class actually said. Gogo catches one in its beak and says it, and the class repeats it twice.
- There is no bomb imagery anywhere. The sounds are a marimba tick and a marimba glissando pop, with no buzzers.
- The object is a soft toy (a Gogo plush, or the printable paper balloon), with a 'pass, don't throw' pictogram.
THREE RULES (the teacher reads them from a Turkish card with pictograms in 20 s, and Gogo demos them):
1. Say a word, pass the balloon.
2. Stuck? Say 'Help!': a friend whispers, or Gogo shows pictures.
3. POP! Everyone does the Silly card.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM THE ADULT GAME:
- The pop is a privilege, not a penalty: the holder becomes Gogo's helper and picks the next picture category.
- Scoring is cooperative. The class fills a word jar and earns 1-3 stars per fuse; stars never go down. In team modes, each team gets stickers per word.
- There is a whole-class moment in every turn: the warm-up chorus (3 free words), the optional Parrot Echo (at A1 the class echoes each word once, which is Gogo's own trick), the Silly card at the pop, and the choral 'Words nobody said'.
- A repeat gets a soft boing and 'New word, please!', never a penalty.
- The timer ring is off; the balloon is the clock. Fuses last 40-90 s, and the shot clock is 10 s in team modes.
- Prompts are a big picture plus 0-4 words ('Animals', 'In my bag'), and letters are read aloud.
PACING: 3 rounds of 2 fuses each, with a 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler in between (about 12-15 min). Isınma is 3 fuses in 5 min. Gogo sleeps on the pause screen with the balloon tied to its foot.

ARENA (ages 12-14; default for B1 and B2 Genç; suggested for grade 6+ or when 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor' is ticked): 'Overload Challenge'.
LOOK AND SOUND:
- Dark navy with neon team colours, a condensed display font, and geometric emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond).
- In 10 s, each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
- The bomb is an energy core that charges in the holding team's colour and flickers in the last 10 s. At overload the screen glitches for 0.4 s (an RGB split and a synth 'bzzt').
- No weapon imagery, no mascot, no pastels.
THREE RULES:
1. Your team says one valid word within 5 s, then the core jumps.
2. One Help per round: the first letter, or a two-word choice strip. It costs 1-2 points and never takes a score below 0.
3. Overload: every other team gets +3 and your streak breaks.
SCORING: +1 per word; the combo is x1.5 at 3 in a row and x2 at 5. A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('CHAIN x5', 'CLUTCH!', 'SAVED!'). Steal is opt-in (Yellow). The end is a podium plus stat awards, with no last place and no individual names.

CONTENT FOR BOTH:
- The teenSafe filter applies: no brands, dating, alcohol, horror, office or salary.
- Topics follow YLE and the MEB units, e.g. 5. sınıf 'My Town', 7. sınıf 'Wild Animals', 8. sınıf 'In the Kitchen'.
- B2 Genç means richer concrete language (things in a science lab, -ous adjectives, sports verbs), not abstract debate.
catalog.levelTuning:
Level (the word band and the prompt kinds) is independent of the skin.

A1 and A1 Genç:
- Category prompts only, one word, concrete picturable sets with 20 or more A1 members: colours, animals, food, clothes, body, classroom, family. Adults also get drinks, jobs, and days and months.
- For A1 Genç the prompt is a picture plus 0-4 words. Every member needs an imageKey, and the Help strip shows 4 of them. Read-aloud at 0.8x and Parrot Echo are on.
- Bonus 'Number potato': count by 2s, 5s or 10s.
- No chunk, chain or sentence modes.
- Fuse: Park 40-90 s, adults 30-60 s.

A2 (caps: A2 Genç 8 words, A2 15):
- Broader categories: places in town, jobs, sports, weather, daily-routine verbs, adjectives for people, things that are round.
- First-letter categories ('animals starting with B').
- Picturable chunk prompts with 2 example pictures ('ee': tree, bee; 'sh': fish, shoe), shown only if 20 or more A1-A2 words contain the chunk.
- Rhyme prompts with an audio model ('rhymes with CAT').
- Adults may try the last-letter chain inside a category.
- Fuse: Park 40-90 s, Arena 30-60 s, Stüdyo 25-60 s.

B1 (caps: B1 Genç 14, B1 25):
- Spelling and chunk prompts ('OUGH', 'PH', '-ful'; at least 30 words in the band), irregular past forms, -ing words, verb + noun collocations ('things you can MAKE'), and phrasal verbs with UP (concrete ones for Genç: pick up, clean up, give up).
- The last-letter chain.
- The Cümle variant, on frames from the group's grammar whitelist ('I've never...', 'Yesterday I...', 'You should...').

B2 (caps: B2 Genç 20 on concrete topics only, B2 40):
- Word families and suffix hunts (-tion, -ment, -ous, un-/dis-; at least 40 words in the band).
- Collocations with take, do, make and have.
- Lateral categories ('things that can be broken').
- A synonym chain ('big': huge, enormous, vast).
- Idiom families from idioms.js (adults only).
- Multi-word members.
- Cümle with a target structure (second conditional, passive, relative clauses).
- Fuse: single words 20-45 s (faster retrieval), sentences 40-90 s.

MIXED ABILITY:
- Kolay / Orta / Zor shifts the member band mix (e.g. A2-Kolay cribs and accepts 60% A1 words), adds 10 s to the minimum fuse on Kolay, and changes the number of free Helps.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one level without changing the skin.
- The feasibility gate re-checks each category against the class size and suggests widening it or switching to EKRAN mode.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 5-15 (Isınma 5-8 min, Maç 12-15 min, Oyun Parkı with stirrers up to 20 min)
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP:
- Pass mode (Çember / Sıra / Ekran) and a team count of 2-6.
- Prompt kind: Kategori, Harf parçası, Kafiye, Son harf zinciri or Cümle.
- Content: a built-in deck by level, topic or MEB unit, or a free-text LLM prompt with a preview where members can be removed or edited before play.

FUSE:
- A fuse-range slider (15-120 s) with per-skin defaults.
- 'Adil fitil': a minimum of 15 s or 3 passes, and never the same team twice in a row.
- 'Tam gizli' (no acceleration) and a manual bang.
- Shot clock on/off and its length.
- The number of fuses and rounds, or the lesson-fit length (Isınma / Maç).

LOOK AND AIDS:
- A skin override per class: Balloon, Core, Retro Bomb, Toaster or Sıcak Patates.
- Live list (type or tap only), Parrot Echo, and the warm-up with 3 free words.
- Hint ladder and number of Helps; toggles for Turkish labels and the Turkish gloss.

RULES AND DIALS:
- Switches for Defuse, Challenge, Double fuse, Bahis, Steal (Yellow) and Virus (Red).
- The harshness and Comeback dials (Light: the trailing team picks the next category).
- Kolay / Orta / Zor and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- Volume, the thinking loop, reduced motion, and the 'Öğretmen okur' fallback.

KEYS AND CLICKER:
- Space / PageDown = valid word; R / PageUp = Repeat!; H = Help; T = pause; B = bang; N = next team; E = flag an error for the review; Z = undo the last tap.
- Any tally can be corrected.

Everything is saved in the local class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').
catalog.delightDetails:
SOUND:
- The tick is an instrument, not a beep: a marimba tick for kids, a synth pulse for Arena and a woodblock for adults. It speeds up only in the last 10 s.
- Every valid-word tap gets a small answer (a fuse spark, a balloon squeak or a core hum), so the class hears its progress.

FUSE AND BANG:
- The fuse graphic misleads on purpose: its spark crawls at a random speed, so nobody can count down from the picture.
- Kids' POP rains down stickers of the words the class actually said. Gogo catches one and says it, and the class repeats it.
- Adults' Toaster skin: the timer ticks, DING, and a burnt slice flies onto the team's plate. Two half toasts snap together into one.
- After every bang the whole room plays 'Freeze!'. The room finds the holder, never the screen.

SCOREBOARD AND CHIPS:
- The scoreboard is part of the joke: toast stacks, balloon stickers or core charges sit as icons on each team panel.
- The Arena commentator strip appears at most once per turn: 'CHAIN x5', 'CLUTCH!' for a word in the final 3 s, 'SAVED!' after a Help.
- Live-list chips highlight the chunk (fiSH, TRee). In chain mode the last letter grows and slides over to become the next target letter.
- A repeat wiggles the original chip with a soft two-note 'already!' instead of a buzzer.

REVIEW AND EXTRAS:
- The end-of-game word cloud sizes words by how early they were said.
- 'Words nobody said' becomes the one-tap review homework.
- The printable kit: a foldable paper bomb, balloon and potato; the Silly and Forfeit decks; a teacher crib card per category.
- Pause screens: Gogo sleeps with the balloon tied to its foot; the Arena core cools down in the team colours.
- Reduced motion turns every effect into a static stamp (POP, OVERLOAD, DING).
catalog.risks:
- WEAK STUDENTS FREEZE AND GET LAUGHED AT. Help is always one word away (a whisper or the picture strip). Park turns the pop into a privilege, Arena and Stüdyo count teams rather than people, the screen never names the holder, and no fuse is shorter than 15 s.
- NOISE AND CHAOS WITH 35-40 STUDENTS. SIRA mode keeps the objects inside rows, 'Freeze!' gives a hard stop after every bang, and T pauses.
- PHYSICAL SAFETY. Soft objects only, a 'pass, don't throw' pictogram, and no running.
- BOMB IMAGERY. It can be sensitive in Turkish schools, especially after news events. The bomb exists only as one adult skin: kids see a balloon, Arena sees a core, and any class can default to Toaster or Sıcak Patates.
- WORD VALIDITY IS JUDGED LIVE AND IS FUZZY. Treat it as a warmer, not a graded game. Doubtful words are marked in the review, and Challenge is for adults only.
- THE TEACHER CANNOT TAP, TYPE AND WATCH AT ONCE. The live list is optional, a presenter clicker covers the essentials, and Park scoring works with zero taps (2 stars by default).
- THE HIDDEN FUSE CAN FEEL UNFAIR. 'Adil fitil' and Comeback Light stop the same team being caught again and again.
- CHUNK PROMPTS CAN BE INFEASIBLE AT LOW LEVELS. Code computes them from words.js with thresholds; the LLM never invents counts.
- LLM CATEGORIES CAN BE TOO NARROW OR UNSAFE FOR KIDS. The feasibility gate, the teenSafe filter and the preview before play catch this.
- NO ENGLISH TTS VOICE. The 'Öğretmen okur' mode shows the words large for the teacher to read aloud.

issues: SIRA mode is logically contradictory. If every row passes its own object at the same time, 5 rows speak at once and the teacher cannot judge or tap any of them. If only the row with the on-screen bomb passes, the other 4/5 of the class sit idle. Either way the default mode for 28-40 students breaks in minute 1.

Park incentive inversion. When the pop is a privilege (you become Gogo's helper and pick the next category), 10-year-olds will hold the balloon on purpose, stall or refuse to pass. Within two fuses the stall becomes the game and the rest of the class shouts.

Smart-board reality. Turkish MEB boards are touch screens, usually on Pardus with no keyboard. Most teachers stand at the board without a presenter clicker, and a clicker only has forward/back anyway. The design relies on keys (Space/R/H/T/B/N/E/Z) plus typing into the live list. That is not operable while standing, touching the board and watching 28 kids.

Teacher cognitive load during a fuse is too high. Per word, the teacher hears the word over the noise, judges it, taps it, watches for repeats (R), offers Help (H), and optionally types. On top of that come the 5-10 s shot clocks that the teacher's own tap latency can blow. With 28 kids at about one word every 4-6 s, the teacher becomes a bottleneck and fairness depends on reaction speed.
The shot clock punishes the teacher's latency. An Arena 5 s clock that expires before the teacher taps breaks a team's streak or opens a steal for something the students did right.

Orthographic prompts are played orally. For 'words with SH', 'OUGH', 'ee' and last-letter chains, spelling is not audible (sugar/shoe, knife ends in e, 'bee' vs 'bea-'), so the teacher cannot verify them without typing or asking for spelling. Every such check costs dead time and disputes.

Hearing the holder in a 28-child room is hard. One quiet child says one word while others whisper help and the tick plays. Validity and repeat judgements become guesses, and the loud kids effectively answer for the quiet ones.

Low individual speaking share. A 12-15 min Maç gives about 60-80 word turns, so each of the 28 students speaks about 2-3 times, mostly single words. The whole-class moments help, but the talk ratio is modest. A strong student inside a team (EKRAN) whispers answers for everyone, and the 'free whisper' legitimises this.
The 3 pinned free words let Park kids repeat 'cat, dog, fish' forever. The safety net becomes the default answer and retrieval practice collapses.

Fairness leaks. 'Never the same team twice in a row' and 'never before 3 passes' are learnable: the just-hit team knows it is safe and plays slack. Arena +3 Survive to every other team is pure luck, and with 6 teams it moves 15 points per bang, which outweighs skill. Combo multipliers let strong teams run away.
Stopping at any moment is underspecified. There is T for pause, but no single 'Bitir' button that gives a fair summary mid-round (stars and podium when the bell rings at minute 9).

Adults. The feature list (Defuse, Challenge, Bahis, Double fuse, Virus, half toasts, three skins, Toaster jokes) is far heavier than what 10 adults need from a 6-minute warmer. Setup and rule explanation will eat into the time, and the adult group may find the pass-the-object ritual childish unless it is framed as a quick-fire warmer.
Setup is not 40 s the first time. There are 4 decisions, each with sub-dials, plus an LLM preview/edit. Only a saved class profile with one-tap 'same as last time' makes it realistic.

Offline and TTS fragility. MEB boards often have flaky internet and no English Web Speech voice on Pardus/Chromium. The LLM content, 'Words nobody said' TTS, Gogo lines and read-aloud all fail silently at the worst moment.

Build size is understated as M. It has 5 prompt kinds, 3 audience rule sets, 5 skins, a chunk index built from words.js, a live list with autocomplete, hint ladders, a print kit and 6+ optional rules. That is realistically L.
fixes: Redefine SIRA: ONE object and ONE active row at a time. The on-screen bomb shows which row is live, and the object passes seat to seat inside that row, then crosses to the next row after N words or at the 'jump' cue. Give idle rows a job each turn: they are the 'Repeat police' (they raise a hand on a repeat) or they echo each valid word, so they are not dead time.

Kill the stall incentive in Park. The helper role rotates by a fixed on-screen order (row or mascot), not by who holds the balloon at the pop. The pop only triggers the whole-class Silly card. In addition, the holder must pass within the shot clock or the balloon auto-hops (the screen moves it).

Touch-first teacher UI. Put three huge bottom-edge buttons within reach of a standing adult: ✓ Kelime / ↺ Tekrar / ? Yardım. Add a small tray for pause, bang, undo and end. Keep keys and the clicker as secondary. Optionally add a phone remote via a QR code (same Wi-Fi not required, use Supabase realtime).
Make the shot clock teacher-safe. It pauses automatically when the teacher touches the judgement tray and restarts after the tap. Default it OFF in Park and SIRA, and in Arena use 7 s.

Zero-judgement default. Stars and scores work without any taps, the live list is off by default in Park, and a 'Sadece sayaç' mode just counts ✓ taps. Validity disputes go to the review, never mid-fuse.

Restrict orthographic prompts (chunks, last-letter chain) to EKRAN mode with typed entry or mini whiteboards, or to the adult/Arena rulesets with the live list forced on. For oral Park play, use only category and rhyme (sound-based) prompts.
Unlock free words only after a Help call (Gogo shows them), and allow each one once per fuse.

Hide fairness constraints from students (never show pass counts) and randomise within them. Change Arena Survive from +3 to every other team into +2 for the team that passed the core on (only 1 team gains). Cap combos at x1.5, and let the Comeback Light dial default ON for kids' teams.
To stop domination, show a speaker badge rotating by seat in EKRAN. A whisper is allowed only when the speaker says 'Help!' and counts as the team's Help.

Add a 'Bitir' button always visible in the tray. It ends the current fuse without penalty and goes straight to stars/podium and 'Words nobody said'. Also add a 'Son tur' soft landing (one final 30 s fuse).

Ship a lean adult default: toasts plus Challenge only. Put Defuse, Bahis, Double fuse and Virus behind a single 'Parti modu' toggle. Frame it for adults as a 2-minute quick-fire warmer (Isınma 3 fuses), with EKRAN or Çember passing and no toast skin jokes unless chosen.
Add 'Aynı ayarlar' on the class profile. First screen: one tap to replay the last configuration with a new category; the other dials go behind 'Değiştir'.

Cache built-in decks and audio offline (service worker, pre-rendered TTS mp3s for crib words and Gogo lines). Detect missing English voices at setup and auto-switch to 'Öğretmen okur'. The LLM needs network, so warn before class, not during it.

Re-estimate as L, and cut version 1 to Kategori plus Kafiye, Çember and EKRAN plus the fixed SIRA, and 3 skins (Balloon, Core, Potato). Add chunks, chain, Cümle, Toaster/Bomb and the print kit in version 2.

issues: PERVERSE INCENTIVE IN OYUN PARKI: the pop makes the holder 'Gogo's helper', who picks the next category and leads the Silly card. Children aged 9-11 will stall or hold on to the balloon to get the pop. The game then rewards not speaking, which is the opposite of its learning goal.

A1 GENÇ RETRIEVAL CEILING: an A1 child can produce only about 8-15 words for most categories. In a class of 30, the category runs dry within the first dozen passes, so later holders are left with repeats or the 3 free words. The par of 'fuse seconds / 6' ignores class size and vocabulary exhaustion. A1 kids who barely read are fine on the input side (pictures, read-aloud), but the production demand of recalling a new word under a ticking clock is the hardest possible task for them. The design leans on the strong kids.

LOW TALK TIME PER STUDENT: in ÇEMBER or SIRA only the holder speaks, so in a 10-minute game with 35 students most students say 0-2 words. The whole-class moments (warm-up chorus, Parrot Echo, Silly card, choral review) carry most of the learning. In Arena and Stüdyo those moments are thinner: they have no chorus, and adults only 'see' the review.

THE REPEAT CHECK DEPENDS ON TYPING: automatic duplicate detection needs the teacher to type the words, which they cannot do while judging, tapping and managing 35 students. Without typing, R relies on the teacher's memory, so repeats pass unnoticed. Repeats are the main validity failure in this genre.

SIRA MODE IS UNCLEAR: every row has its own object, but only one screen bomb is live. The design does not say what the idle rows do, or whether their objects move. If they don't, 4-5 rows sit idle, and in a Turkish class of 40 that means noise.

ARENA OVERLOAD SWING IS TOO BIG: +3 to every other team means a 5-team class gains +12 against one team per bang. That outweighs the words a team scored, so the hidden-random fuse, rather than language, decides the podium.

TOO MANY DIALS: 5 prompt kinds x 3 pass modes x 5 skins x about 15 switches, with 9 keyboard keys. The 40 s setup is unrealistic the first time, and the E, Z and N keys will be forgotten mid-game. Build size M is an underestimate; this is L.

HIGHER-LEVEL MODES ARE HARD TO JUDGE LIVE: in Cümle at B1 Genç (spontaneous sentences under a fuse), in synonym chains, and with lateral categories ('things that can be broken'), validity turns into teacher arbitration. Kids argue, and the pace dies. The Challenge rule exists only for adults, so in teen classes these disputes have no procedure.

RHYME AND CHUNK PROMPTS AT A2 GENÇ: Turkish learners read phonetically. Rhyme sets for 'cat' within A1-A2 bands are small (hat, bat, rat, mat, sat) and mostly unpicturable. 'ee'/'sh' spelling chunks are a reading and spelling task that only looks like speaking, and the listening check (did they say a word containing 'sh'?) is ambiguous: sh vs ch, fish vs 'fiş'.

LLM PICTURE COVERAGE: Park requires an image for every member, but no image library exists, so this really means emoji. A teacher prompt such as 'mutfak, 5. sınıf' produces members like spatula, sink, kettle and cupboard, which have no clean emoji. Multi-word LLM members, and LLM members outside words.js, get no computed level. The level gate then leaks.
ADULT DEFAULT SKIN: Retro Bomb is listed first. In Turkish state-school contexts even adult classes (public education centres, workplaces) can find bomb imagery tasteless after news events.

ADULT A1: passing a potato while saying 'apple' can feel juvenile. The Stüdyo look covers the visuals, but the A1 adult prompt list (colours, animals) reuses kid categories rather than adult-life sets.
fixes: Remove the holder privilege in Park. The pop triggers a whole-class Silly card, and the 'helper' is the NEXT holder (the student who says the first word after the pop) or a rotating 'Gogo's helper' badge that the teacher assigns before the fuse. Holding on to the balloon must never be attractive.

At A1 Genç, make the default prompt a 'Picture potato': the screen shows a rotating picture wall of 12-16 category members, and the holder names ANY picture, including ones already said. Recall with a picture cue replaces free recall. Unlock free recall (no pictures) as 'Süper mod' at A2 Genç. Scale par by min(fuse/6, feasible members x 0.7).

Replace live typing with a TAP GRID on the teacher screen (or a phone remote): the crib members appear as chips, one tap marks a word as said, dims the chip and catches repeats automatically, and an 'other' key covers words outside the crib. This makes the automatic repeat check real without a keyboard.

Define SIRA properly: all rows pass their own objects SIMULTANEOUSLY, each row with its own category and one shared fuse. Or run a 'relay' where idle rows chorally echo each valid word (Parrot Echo for all skins). Every turn should give every row a job.

Add a whole-class echo beat to Arena and Stüdyo too: an optional 'Echo' key after every 3rd valid word, where the class repeats it, and a choral or read-aloud review of 'Words nobody said' at every age.
Cut the Arena overload bonus to +1 per other team (or +2 split). Alternatively, the overload freezes the holding team's multiplier only, so word count decides the podium.

Ship three presets per skin (Hızlı Başla / Standart / Tam kontrol) and hide the 15 switches under 'Gelişmiş'. Keep the clicker to three actions: forward = valid, back = repeat, black-screen key = pause. Re-estimate the build as L.

Gate sentence mode (Cümle) and the lateral and synonym modes to Stüdyo B1+ and Arena B2 Genç only, with a teen 'Hakem kartı' rule: the teacher's word is final, and a doubtful answer counts as half, never as nothing.

Treat chunk and rhyme prompts at A2 Genç as a LISTENING variant: the screen reads a word, and the class shows a thumbs-up if it has the sound. Or drop them from the Park defaults; keep chunks from B1 Genç.

LLM pipeline: in Park, drop members with no emoji or imageKey, and re-run the feasibility gate after the drop. Mark members that are not in words.js as 'level unknown' and exclude them from the level-capped crib unless the teacher approves them in the preview.
Make Toaster the default Stüdyo skin and Sıcak Patates the default for MEB or state-school profiles. Retro Bomb stays opt-in.
Add an adult-life A1 pack (things in a supermarket, things in your bag, things at a hotel, drinks at a café) so A1 adults do not get the kids' categories.

issues: Scope is badly over-specified for what is really a 'category plus hidden timer plus teacher clicker' game. 3 pass modes x 5 prompt kinds x 5 skins x about 12 rule switches (Defuse, Challenge, Bahis, Double, Virus, Steal, Comeback, Kolay/Orta/Zor, and more) turns a size-S warmer into a size-L settings maze. The 40 s setup target is not credible with this many switches, and each extra switch is another state-machine branch to test on a projector.

Most of the game happens off-screen: the object, the speaking and the judging. The screen shows a prompt, a fuse and a tally. Without strong fuse/pop art and sound it will feel like a stopwatch with a skin, and the polish budget has to go into those 2-3 moments rather than into options.

The teacher's input load is unrealistic. At a 2-4 s cadence the teacher has to press Space per word, R for repeats, E for flags, and also type live-list chips, all while listening to 30 kids. The live list with autocomplete will almost never be used live, yet it drives the duplicate check, the word cloud, 'Words nobody said', Park stars and the Arena combos. Without taps, most of the scoring and review features have no data.

SIRA mode is confusing. Each row has its own object, but only one row is 'hot' on screen, so 4-5 rows sit idle about 80% of the time, which breaks the 'whole-class moment every turn' rule. And if every row passes at once, the single screen fuse cannot attribute the bang.

In ÇEMBER mode the software cannot know who holds the object, so 'Adil fitil' (not the same team twice, at least 3 passes) cannot be enforced there. Only the 15 s minimum works, which the spec never says.

Park scoring is incoherent. The star par (fuse seconds / 6) needs taps, the default is 2 stars with zero taps, and stars never drop. So stars carry no information, and kids will notice that the reward is random.
Arena's combo of x1.5 on +1 gives fractional scores. Kids' scoreboards should be integers.

Park picture support: the spec says every member needs an imageKey, but the emoji set covers only a few hundred concrete nouns. That rules out adjectives, verbs, chunks and many MEB-unit words, and LLM-generated members will often be unpicturable. There is no fallback defined (e.g. drop the member, or show a text-only chip).

LLM validity: category membership is easy for an LLM, but members are only lemmatised against words.js. Multi-word members, plurals, US/UK variants and 'open' sets need a normaliser, and hallucinated obscure members pollute the crib and the 'nobody said' review (it will surface odd words like 'aardwolf').

Chunk/rhyme indexes: words.js is 1.4 MB and must never ship to the client. The chunk and rhyme counts need a build-time precomputed index, but the spec says 'grep-built' without naming the build step. A good rhyme set also needs pronunciation data. IPA is in words.js, but rhyme matching on IPA needs parsing, and spelling-based rhymes fail (do/go).

TTS risk: MEB smartboards run Pardus/Chromium-class browsers, where English speechSynthesis voices are often missing or robotic. The kids' flow leans heavily on audio (Gogo says words, read-aloud at 0.8x, choral repeats). 'Öğretmen okur' is a fallback that changes the kids' experience.

Naming and imagery: the hub card title 'Tik Tak Bomba' puts bomb imagery on the homepage and in the kids' game list, even though the design itself avoids it for kids. The Retro Bomb skin with camera shake is a needless institutional risk in Turkish schools, and it duplicates Toaster and Potato.

Art load: the Gogo mascot animations (demo, catching a word, sleeping), the balloon inflation and pop shower, the Arena core with an RGB glitch, the bomb, the toaster with a flying toast, and the steaming potato come to 5 animated props plus a mascot. That is the bulk of the build risk.

It overlaps other likely candidates: the Just a Minute / speaking wheel (the Cümle variant is basically JAM), İsim-Şehir STOP (category-list retrieval), a Word Chain / Kelime Zinciri candidate (last-letter chain), and Hot Seat/Taboo timers. The unique core is the hidden-fuse pass mechanic, not the prompt kinds.

Arena's 'Survive +3 to every other team' can flip standings from pure fuse luck. With 5-6 teams, one bang hands out +15 total, which dwarfs the +1-per-word skill scoring and makes words feel pointless.
The tick accelerating in the last 10 s is a genre convention, but it gives away the end of a 'hidden' fuse. 'Tam gizli' fixes this, but it's a switch nobody will find.
fixes: Cut v1 to this minimum feature set: a prompt card (Kategori, plus Harf parçası from B1); a hidden fuse with a 15 s minimum; 3 skins (Balloon for Park, Core for Arena, Sıcak Patates/Toaster for Stüdyo); keys Space (valid), B (bang), T (pause), Z (undo), N (next team); a team tally; a 15 s review of 'Words nobody said'; built-in decks (about 20 categories per level); and LLM category-list generation with a preview. Defer Defuse, Challenge, Bahis, Virus, Double, Steal, Comeback, the live-list autocomplete, the E error flags, rhyme mode, the chain and Cümle to v2 behind a single 'Gelişmiş' drawer.
Rename the hub card to 'Sıcak Patates' (EN: Hot Potato) and delete the Retro Bomb skin. Keep Toaster as an adult easter egg. Bomb imagery then never appears on the homepage.

Reduce pass modes to 2. ÇEMBER: one object, individual play, fuse only. EKRAN: the screen token jumps team to team. For fixed rows, rows are EKRAN teams: only the hot row speaks, and the other rows do a whole-class 'echo' of each accepted word (a clap or repeat). That makes the whole-class moment real and removes the multi-object ambiguity.

State plainly that 'Adil fitil' works only in EKRAN. In ÇEMBER it means only the 15 s minimum plus a 'bang cannot land within 4 s of the previous bang holder's pass' heuristic. Better still, drop the promise there.

Make the core loop work with ZERO typing. The optional live list becomes tap-a-chip from the crib grid (the teacher taps a word they heard, with no keyboard). Scoring counts Space taps only. The word cloud and 'nobody said' fall back to the crib when no chips were tapped.
Park scoring: drop the par formula. Every POP adds one sticker to the class album, and every Space tap drops a pebble into the word jar. The jar fills visibly and the album is the reward. No stars.
Arena: integer scores only. +1 per word, a streak of 3 or more gives +2 per word, and an Overload gives +1 (not +3) to every other team, so skill outweighs fuse luck.

Picture pipeline: a curated emoji/SVG map (about 400 concrete nouns) keyed by words.js lemma. A category is Park-eligible only if at least 12 members map to a picture. LLM-proposed members without a picture are kept for adults and dropped for Genç, and the preview shows the count ('18/24 resimli').

LLM validation: a JSON schema; lowercasing and lemmatisation; a match against words.js for level (unmatched members become 'dot' members, and at most 30% are allowed); the teenSafe word list; a deduplicate pass; the feasibility gate at max(12, 0.6 x class) members; a single retry with a 'widen category' instruction on failure; and a teacher preview with delete. Ship precomputed JSON for the chunk index and a curated rhyme family list (not IPA-derived) at build time. Never load words.js client-side.

Audio: synthesise the ticks, marimba, pop and zap with WebAudio (no asset files). Treat TTS as optional enhancement: probe `speechSynthesis.getVoices()` for an en-* voice at setup, and if there is none, default to 'Öğretmen okur' with big word cards, while Gogo's lines become speech bubbles.

Put the polish budget into three moments: the fuse (a non-linear spark crawl, rising pitch), the pop/overload (a 1.5 s signature animation plus 'FREEZE!' stamp) and the review (a word cloud). Use one mascot with 3 poses (idle, cheer, sleep) as SVG, not frame animation. Reduced motion becomes a static stamp.
Default 'Tam gizli' ON for Arena/Stüdyo, or make the acceleration start at a randomised 6-14 s rather than a fixed 10 s, so the end stays hidden.
Put all setup on one screen with 3 big choices (mod, içerik, süre) and defaults from the class profile. That hits the 40 s target.

Merge the Cümle variant into the Just a Minute/speaking-wheel candidate, and the last-letter chain into any Word Chain candidate. If those candidates are dropped, keep them here only as v2 prompt kinds sharing the same fuse engine.
Reuse the fuse engine as a shared module (a hidden random timer, tick, bang hooks) for other games (Hot Seat, Taboo rounds). That spreads the build cost.

catalog.rankReason: An M-size speaking-fluency stirrer that works for 9-year-olds and adults and breaks up the quiz games. It ships as 'Sıcak Patates', so no bomb imagery appears on the homepage. The rules: one object and one active row at a time, a hidden fuse of at least 15 s, Kategori prompts plus Harf parçası from B1, and a picture potato wall at A1 Genç. In Oyun Parkı the holder gets no privilege: the pop triggers a whole-class Silly card and the helper badge rotates, which removes the stalling incentive.

catalog.name: Gogo Diyor ki! / Ayağa Kalk (Simon Says, Stand Up If, Four Corners, Opinion Line)
catalog.familiarAs: Simon Says, 'Stand up if...', Four Corners, Opinion Line / human spectrum (TPR games)
catalog.oneLiner: The whole class answers with their bodies (stand, sit, point, mime, move to a corner or along a line) while the screen calls commands, statements or questions, and a trap phrase keeps everyone listening.
catalog.howItPlays: The teacher picks 1-3 round types, 2-4 minutes each. (1) COMMANDS: TTS (or the teacher, in 'Öğretmen okur' mode) gives a command from the pack ('Touch your nose', 'Walk like a penguin', 'Show me something blue'). The action picture appears 1.5 s after the audio, so listening comes first. Students obey only when the command starts with the trap phrase. Traps start at 1 in 5 and rise to 1 in 3. (2) STAND UP IF / TRUE-FALSE: a tf item or a survey line. Stand = true (or 'I have'), sit = false, hands on head = not sure. At the reveal, the class repeats the correct sentence twice. (3) FOUR WALLS: an mcq whose options map to the four walls (or 1-4 fingers when the room is tight). Pairs consult for 10-20 s, then everyone points or moves. (4) OPINION LINE (B groups): the window side is 'strongly agree' and the door side 'strongly disagree'. The seat spinner picks 2-3 students to justify, using the starters on screen. Then 'Changed your mind? Move!'. The class plays against the game, not against each other. The teacher taps a 3-level estimate (1 Everyone / 2 Most / 3 Some), which fills a class meter. Nobody is ever out. The last round is always a calming 'sit down if...' sequence that ends with everyone seated.
catalog.playerSetup: Whole class at once (up to 40). Optionally, desk rows act as teams with row captains. A seated-only filter suits fixed desks.
skills: grammar (imperatives, can, present perfect 'have you ever', conditionals)
catalog.adultVersion: Stüdyo 'Stand Up If / Opinion Line', with no Simon Says trap. 'Stand up if you have ever...' (present perfect) is followed by a spinner-picked 'When was that?' (past simple). This builds a class-report moment ('About half of us have...') that can feed c21. Four Walls reviews mcq items after a 20 s pair consultation. The Opinion Line runs debate prompts with useful language on screen ('I see your point, but...'). There are no scores by default. The seated business-class variant uses fingers or colour cards. The editorial look has no mascot.
catalog.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Gogo Says!' has three rules, all shown as pictograms: (1) Listen for 'Gogo says'. (2) No 'Gogo says'? Freeze! (3) Everybody plays. Students caught by a trap strike a funny freeze pose (statue, robot, tree) for 3 s and stay in, so there is no elimination. Gogo sometimes gets a trap wrong himself ('Oops!'). Command sets follow the units: body parts, actions, animals ('Hop like a frog'), colours, classroom objects, feelings. Audio plays at 0.8x, stars go into the class jar, and a score never goes down. ARENA 'Captain's Orders / Reflex Sync' has no parrot and uses a neon COMMAND strip. Gaps shrink to 2 s. Commands have several steps ('Clap twice, then touch your left shoulder') and include left/right, memory commands ('Do the last two again'), and a 'Squad Sync %' per row. The combo builds on 'Everyone' ratings. 'Stand up if...' uses safe, cool prompts (can do a handstand, has been to Kapadokya). It is framed as a reflex challenge, not a kids' game.
catalog.levelTuning: A1 / A1T: one-verb commands with body parts, colours and numbers; picture support; 'Stand up if you have a cat'. A2 / A2T: two-step commands with and/then, prepositions ('Put your pen on your book'), adverbs (slowly, quietly), 'Stand up if you can...' and 'if you like...'. B1 / B1T: conditional commands ('If you're wearing black, touch your head'), present perfect surveys, sequence commands, Four Walls with context mcqs. B2 / B2T: relative clauses and double conditions, an opinion line with justification and concession, and a persuasion round ('Convince two people to move'). Screen text follows the word caps; commands are mostly audio.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 3-10 as a warmer, brain break or settler; 15 as a full set
catalog.contentShape: A new 'command' item: {text, verb, bodyPart?, picture, seatedOk (bool), movement ('none'|'hands'|'stand'|'walk'), trapAllowed}. It is generated from vocab items with actable=true plus command frames. tf items with about='picture'|'sentence-correct'. survey / speaking-prompt with mode 'survey' or 'opinion' for 'Stand up if' and the opinion line. mcq for Four Walls. A curated safe-topic list decides which 'Stand up if' prompts are allowed.
catalog.delightDetails: Listening comes first: the picture follows the audio. The teacher panel has a 'mirror' hint because left and right flip when the teacher faces the class. A 'Sleepy Gogo' settler slows and softens the commands until heads are on arms. Every card carries a seated-safe icon. At the end, a class map of the adult survey results turns into review sentences in Kaçırılanlar. The trap phrase can be personalised ('Captain says', 'Teacher says').
catalog.teacherControls: Trap rate, speed, seated-only and hands-only filters, round-type toggles, the 3-level class estimate keys, repeat audio, Öğretmen okur, safe-prompt list editing, row-teams toggle.
catalog.risks: Noise and crowding in classes of 35-40: seated-only is the default for public schools. 'Stand up if' can expose personal facts: only curated safe topics are allowed (never family, religion, money, health or body), and teenSafe applies. Judging a whole class is fuzzy, so the game uses estimates and never scores individuals. 13-year-olds may find Simon Says childish, which the Arena reframing addresses. Students with limited mobility get a hands-only equivalent for every command.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (the TPR response mode is only assumed, not built)

issues: AUDIO FAILURE IS THE #1 BREAK POINT. Turkish public-school smart boards (MEB/FATIH Android boards) often have no English TTS voice or a robotic one, and their speakers are drowned by 28 kids. A 'listening first' game dies when minute 1 is a silent or garbled command. Browser TTS at 0.8x also sounds worse, not clearer.

The per-item 3-level class estimate (1/2/3) is the teacher's biggest cognitive load. They have to watch 28 bodies, spot trap-fallers, manage noise and tap a key every 5-8 s while standing away from the board. They will either stop rating (so the meter becomes meaningless) or stop teaching. 'Squad Sync %' per row multiplies this by 4-6 rows and is not doable by one person.

Four Walls with 28 kids physically moving means 60-90 s of chaos per item in a room with fixed double desks and bags in the aisles. That gives about 4 items in 10 minutes plus a real safety and noise complaint from the next classroom. Even the finger fallback breaks down: kids copy the strongest pupil's fingers (herd answering), so the reveal measures who the leader is, not comprehension.

Herd effect across all round types. In Stand Up If and True/False, weaker listeners simply watch the fast kid and follow half a second later. The design never forces an independent response, so one strong student effectively answers for the room, and the class meter rewards it.

Opinion Line creates dead time: 2-3 justifiers speak while 25+ stand idle. With 12-14 year-olds, standing idle turns into chatting within 20 s. It is also physically impossible in rows ('window side to door side' means climbing over desks).

Trap-catching is unenforceable and invites arguing ('I didn't move!', 'He moved!'). The funny freeze pose is good, but nothing tells the teacher who to point at. With no individual consequence, some 11-year-olds will deliberately fall for traps to do the funny pose, and the trap stops working as a listening check.

Settling back down is where lessons are lost. The design has a calming 'sit down if' finale, but no mid-game 'freeze and silence' control. If the class boils over at minute 4, the teacher needs a one-tap calm-down that isn't the end of the game.

Safety and cultural limits on LLM-generated commands. Free-text prompts can yield 'touch your partner's shoulder', 'hug', 'jump on your chair', 'close your eyes and spin' or dance moves. In Turkish schools, cross-gender contact and anything that looks like a religious gesture or dance are sensitive, and climbing furniture is a liability. The item schema has seatedOk and movement flags but no noContact or noFurniture guarantees.

'Stand up if' prompts are unverifiable and socially risky even with safe topics. 'Stand up if you have been to Kapadokya' quietly exposes which kids' families travel (money), and 'if you have a pet' can too for poorer students. A safe list keyed to family, religion, money, health and body misses travel, possessions and phones.

Adult fit is narrow. 10 adults after work will do Opinion Line and 'Stand up if you have ever...' as a 5-minute warmer at most. Simon Says is gone, Four Walls with 10 people is fine but thin, and there is no scoring, so it isn't a full game for adults. It is really a warmer tool, and it competes with a discussion card deck.

Setup time: choosing 1-3 round types, trap rate, speed, filters and a pack before starting takes too long for a 3-minute brain break. It has to be one tap from the homepage or teachers won't use it spontaneously.

Left/right: the mirror hint is on the teacher panel, but the screen itself shows the picture un-mirrored to a class facing the board. For a class facing the screen that is correct, yet the teacher demonstrating while facing the class shows the opposite. The Arena left/right commands will cause genuine disputes.
fixes: Ship pre-recorded human audio (two voices, natural speed plus a slow take) for every built-in command and every trap phrase. Use TTS only for LLM-generated content, and run a 5-second audio check on game start ('Can you hear Gogo? Thumbs up!'). If no English voice is found, auto-switch to Öğretmen okur with a large-print command shown only on the teacher's view.

Make the class estimate optional and coarse. By default, rate only once per round (every 5-8 items) with 3 big on-screen buttons plus keys 1/2/3. Support a presenter clicker (PageDown = next, B = blackout/freeze). Drop per-row Squad Sync ratings, or rate only the one row the spinner spotlights that turn.

Add a 'reveal on the beat' mechanic against the herd effect: a 3-2-1 countdown with 'eyes closed, show your answer' (fingers or arms up/down) on Gogo's 'NOW!'. Answers are simultaneous, so copying is impossible. For True/False, use 'thumbs up/down on your chest' hidden answers revealed together.

Replace walking Four Walls in public-school mode with 'Four Corners of the Desk' or finger/colour-card answers. Keep walking only as an opt-in for small classes (under 16) and adults, with a 'mover rows' option where one row walks per item while the others answer with fingers.

Rework Opinion Line for rows: 'Opinion Arms' (arms high = strongly agree, down = strongly disagree), or have only one row stand and form the line at the front. Pair-talk for 20 s before any justification so everyone speaks, and then the spinner picks the speakers.

Make traps self-policing and fun, not disputed: after a trap Gogo shows 'Did you move? Show me your statue!' and whoever honestly moved poses. Add a 'Honesty Star' to the class jar when many admit. Cap trap poses to one per 3 traps so deliberate falling loses its payoff.
Add a global 'Freeze & Breathe' button (key F): the screen goes calm blue, Gogo whispers 'Freeze... breathe in... breathe out', then play resumes. Keep the final settler sequence as it is.

Hard-constrain the command generator with a whitelist of verbs and body parts. Forbid contact with others, furniture climbing, spinning with eyes closed, dance, prayer-like or religious gestures, and anything touching the chest, hips or face of others. Post-filter LLM output against a banned-pattern list, and tag every item with a movement level plus noContact=true, shown as an icon.

Extend the safe-prompt list to exclude travel, possessions, devices, holidays and family activities that proxy wealth. Default kid prompts to preferences and abilities ('Stand up if you like pizza / can whistle'), which are costless to reveal and fun.
Add a zero-config 'Hızlı Mola' button that starts a 3-minute seated brain break with the class's current unit, trap rate 1/5 and the settler at the end. Keep full configuration behind 'Ayarlar'.

Show a small mirrored 'teacher's view' silhouette on the teacher panel only. On the board, use L/R arrow badges plus a coloured wristband convention (the left hand is always the blue side on screen), so left/right commands can be checked without argument.

Position it honestly for adults: market the Stüdyo version as a 5-8 minute warmer or icebreaker ('Find someone who / Stand up if / Opinion Line') that feeds the class-report sentences. Don't count it as one of the 10 'proper' games for adult groups; count it as a kids' and teens' core game and an adult warmer utility.

issues: Four games sit under one name, and each fits a different band. Commands fit A1-A2 kids. Stand Up If fits A2-B1 of any age. The Opinion Line fits only B1-B2. The group chip does not decide which rounds appear, so an A1 Genç teacher can switch on an Opinion Line that the class cannot use, and a B2 adult teacher sees a Simon Says round.

The design says A1 kids who barely read can play, but that holds only for COMMANDS. Stand Up If shows a tf sentence, and Four Walls maps 4 text mcq options to the walls. A 9-year-old A1 cannot read 4 options in 10-20 s. Nothing says tf and mcq items are read aloud or shown as pictures for Oyun Parkı.

B1-B2 command language is artificial. 'If you're wearing black, touch your head' and relative-clause double conditions are logic puzzles, not B2 practice. For B2 adults, the Commands round is dead weight and a bit babyish.

A1-A2 adults (Stüdyo) have almost no content that fits their level. Commands are dropped as childish. The Opinion Line is B-only. What is left is Stand Up If with 'have you ever', which is A2+ grammar. A1 adults end up with nothing but a thin tf round.

Almost no production at A1-A2. Students only listen and move. The only speaking is the chorus repeat and the B-level justification by 2-3 spinner-picked students, so 37 of 40 students never produce language.

LLM content is unrealistic for the command type. Many teacher prompts are not actable, e.g. 'past simple irregulars', 'environment', 'LGS 8. sınıf ünite 3'. An LLM will produce commands like 'Recycle a bottle' or 'Mime global warming' that cannot be done at a desk, or it will quietly fall back to tf. Fields like movement, seatedOk and trapAllowed are easy for an LLM to get wrong.

Built-in content is weaker than it looks. words.js has no 'actable' flag and no pictures. The claim 'generated from vocab items with actable=true plus command frames' implies curating a command bank and drawing action pictures (hop like a frog, walk slowly), and that asset cost is not counted in buildSize M.

Stand Up If exposes personal information at every level. Even 'has been to Kapadokya' or 'have a cat' marks out poorer children in Turkish public schools (travel, pets, phones). The safe-topic list needs to exclude anything about possessions or travel for Genç groups, not only family, religion, money and health.

Opinion Line prompts from the LLM for B1-B2 Genç risk controversial topics, and this is a public MEB school context. The same goes for adult debate prompts. Nothing requires filtering them or having the teacher approve them before play.

Arena: many 12-14-year-olds are self-conscious, and standing up alone or being picked out by the spinner to justify in front of the class raises affective filter. The 'Squad Sync %' comes from the teacher's fuzzy 3-key estimate, so a teen can see it as unfair.

In Oyun Parkı, raising the trap rate to 1 in 3 makes it frustrating for 9-year-olds. The funny freeze pose works, but a high trap frequency turns the game into a trick instead of a comprehension check.

Measuring learning is weak. The class meter is a teacher estimate, so the Kaçırılanlar review has no data on which item was missed, except for Four Walls and tf, where the teacher could tap the correct share.
fixes: Gate round types by level and audience. Oyun Parkı A1-A2: Commands plus picture Stand Up If only. Arena: Commands (multi-step) plus Stand Up If plus Four Walls, with the Opinion Line only at B1-B2. Stüdyo: no Commands by default. Stand Up If, Four Walls and Opinion Line, plus a 'Find someone who' follow-up. Show the locked rounds to the teacher with a one-line reason and let them override.

Read every tf and mcq item aloud with TTS in Oyun Parkı and for A1 of any audience. Four Walls for A1-A2 kids uses picture options (4 pictures, one per wall), with words only as a secondary label. Cap on-screen tf text at the level word cap and speak it twice.

Replace the B1-B2 Commands with 'Mime and guess'. The screen privately shows a B-level phrasal verb, idiom or collocation to one row. The row mimes it, and the class must say the full sentence. This keeps TPR and adds production.

Add a proper A1-A2 Stüdyo round, 'Stand Up If: present simple', with work, routine and preference prompts ('Stand up if you drink tea in the morning'). Follow it with a spinner-picked 'How often?' or 'Why?' answered with sentence starters.

Build in production at every level. (a) A Chorus Echo: the class says the command back before they act. (b) A 'Be Gogo/Captain' turn: a student reads the next command card aloud (picture plus word support at A1). (c) A pair 'turn and tell' of 10 s after every Stand Up If reveal ('I have a cat. You?').

Ship a curated built-in command bank of about 300 items. Give each one a picture, movement, seatedOk and CEFR band, and map it to the MEB unit themes. For LLM prompts, classify the topic first. If the topic is not actable, route it to Stand Up If tf, Four Walls mcq or Opinion items, and say so to the teacher ('Bu konu komut için uygun değil, Doğru/Yanlış turu hazırlandı'). Validate the command fields against a verb whitelist and send only commands that pass it to TTS.

Extend the safe-topic list for Genç groups: no possessions, travel, pets, devices or family situations. Prefer abilities, preferences, school life and imaginary 'would you' prompts. Show every generated 'Stand up if' and Opinion prompt in a preview so the teacher can approve or remove it before class.

Arena anonymity options: fingers or colour cards instead of standing, and an Opinion Line that can run as a row-level vote where a row captain justifies. The spinner has a 'pass to partner' option. Show Squad Sync as a class-wide meter, not ranked per row.
Cap the Oyun Parkı trap rate at 1 in 4, and add a 'Gogo slow-mo' repeat after every trap so the missed phrase is heard again.
Let the teacher tap the share of correct responses on tf and Four Walls items (a quick 3-level key per item). This gives Kaçırılanlar item-level data on what to review, beyond the class meter.

Rename the entry to what it is on each skin: 'Gogo Says!' (Oyun Parkı), 'Reflex Sync' (Arena), 'Stand Up If / Opinion Line' (Stüdyo). That way adult teachers do not skip it as a kids' Simon Says game.

issues: The screen does very little. The game happens in the room, so on the projector it risks looking like a slideshow with TTS (a card, a picture, three estimate buttons). Without strong screen-side feedback (animated caller, countdown, freeze reveal, sync meter), it will not read as a 'proper game' next to Baamboozle-style candidates.

There are too many round types for one game. Four Walls is an MCQ quiz answered with your body, which duplicates every MCQ candidate and the existing /sinif-oyunu. Opinion Line overlaps the speaking/debate candidates (Would You Rather, Just a Minute, spinner games). Four modes means four UIs, four rule cards and four sets of teacher controls for an M-sized build, so it is really L.

TTS is the biggest technical risk. Classroom smartboards (Windows boards, Android panels, school PCs) often have no English voice, a robotic one, or none offline. speechSynthesis rate/voice choice is inconsistent across browsers, and 0.8x on a bad voice hurts listening-first. The core rule (audio first, picture 1.5 s later) collapses when audio fails.

The picture assets are heavy and do not scale with LLM content. The built-in command sets need about 150-250 consistent action pictograms (body parts, animal moves, prepositions, feelings) in two or three skins. Free-text LLM packs will produce commands no picture exists for, so 'picture support for A1' silently disappears for custom content.

'command' is a new item type outside the 22 shared ids. That adds schema, validator, generator prompt and editor work. Trusting the LLM to set seatedOk/movement/trapAllowed is unsafe: it will mark 'jump three times' as seatedOk or produce 'walk to the door' in a 40-seat room.

Safety contradicts itself. The Arena examples 'has been to Kapadokya' (travel means money/SES) and 'can do a handstand' (physical ability/body) break the stated never-money/body/health rule. 'Have a cat' and present-perfect 'have you ever...' prompts leak SES and family circumstances. LLM-generated 'Stand up if' prompts will drift into these areas unless the curated list is a hard allowlist.

Removing elimination removes Simon Says's tension. With freeze-pose-and-stay-in, nothing is at stake except the class estimate, which is a vague teacher tap. The 'class plays against the game' meter needs a clearer target or the trap loses meaning after 2-3 minutes.

The teacher input load is too high for a whole-class TPR game. A 3-level estimate every turn, per-row Squad Sync % in Arena, a spinner, and repeat/mirror controls, all while the teacher is watching 40 bodies, is not realistic. Per-row sync needs one tap per row per turn.

The adult version is an activity, not a game. Stand Up If and Opinion Line are good warmers but have no scoring by default, no arc and no win state, and Simon Says is removed. Adults will see it as a teacher tool. That is fine, but it should not be counted as one of the '10 proper games' for Stüdyo.
The Kaçırılanlar class map built from survey results rests on estimates ('about half'), not data. Review sentences generated from fuzzy taps can state false facts about the class.
fixes: Cut to two core modes: (1) Gogo Says / Captain's Orders (commands with the trap) and (2) Stand Up If / Opinion Line (one mode with an agree-disagree spectrum toggle for B levels). Remove Four Walls as a round and make 'physical answers' (4 corners/fingers, stand/sit for T/F) a global answer-mode setting that any MCQ/TF game can switch on. This keeps the build honestly M.

Make the screen carry the game. Use a big animated caller (Gogo the parrot in Oyun Parkı, a neon COMMAND strip with a glitch-in in Arena), a visible 3-2-1 beat, and a trap reveal ('Gogo didn't say it!' with the freeze pose card spinning in). Add a Class Power bar that fills toward a round goal (e.g. 8 'Everyone' ratings) and unlocks a celebration or a new freeze pose. Give it one clear win condition per round.

Audio: pre-render MP3s for all built-in command packs (a neural TTS at build time, including a 0.8x version) and ship them as static assets, about 1-2 MB per pack and lazy-loaded. Use browser TTS only for LLM packs, with a voice check on setup. If no English voice is found, switch automatically to Öğretmen okur and show a large text card for the teacher. Add a 'test sound' button on the setup screen.

Pictures: build a fixed icon library of about 120 pictograms keyed by verb × bodyPart/animal/colour/object, drawn as SVG sprites that are re-coloured by skin. Constrain the LLM to output commands only from that controlled vocabulary (verb and object ids plus a free-text wording). The validator rejects anything that is not in the library, so every generated command has a picture. B-level conditional commands can go text/audio-only by design.

Do not add a new top-level type. Model commands as vocab items with actable:true plus a small 'command' frame {verbId, objectId?, steps[], condition?}. Derive seatedOk and movement from a hand-written verb table (touch/point/clap = seated; hop/walk/jump = stand/walk), never from the LLM. Drop any command whose derived movement is above the room setting.

Make 'Stand up if' prompts a hard allowlist of templates: likes/preferences, today/this morning, can-do school-safe skills (whistle, snap fingers, say the alphabet backwards), opinions about neutral topics. Ban travel, possessions, pets, family, abilities tied to the body, health, religion, money and appearance beyond clothing colour. Change the Kapadokya and handstand examples. The LLM may only fill slots in allowlisted templates, and a Turkish/English deny-list plus a teenSafe check runs after generation.

Cut teacher input to one tap per turn: a single 3-key estimate (1/2/3 on keyboard, big buttons on the smartboard or phone presenter view), with a 'skip rating' default after 5 s. Drop per-row Squad Sync unless row-teams mode is on, and even then rate only the row the spinner picked. Add a keyboard/clicker map (space = next, R = repeat, M = mirror) so the teacher can run it from a presenter remote.

Add stakes without elimination. In Arena, a streak of 'Everyone' ratings multiplies Class Power and a trap caught costs streak, not points. In Oyun Parkı, traps are the fun part: caught students do the pose and Gogo does it with them, and the class jar still only goes up. Escalate the trap rate visibly ('Gogo is getting sneaky!') so tension rises over 3 minutes.

Adults: position it as 'Stüdyo Isınma' (warmer toolkit). Present-perfect Stand Up If, then a spinner-picked 'When/where was that?' follow-up, then an Opinion Line with concession starters. Do not count it among the headline adult games, and keep a seated fingers/colour-card mode as default.

Base the survey summary in Kaçırılanlar on language, not data. Produce sentence frames ('Most of us / Some of us / Nobody...') filled from the teacher's 3-level taps, labelled as estimates, with no invented numbers.

Default public-school settings: seated-only on, hands-only equivalents auto-substituted, walking commands off. Show a mirror-hint toggle for left/right in the teacher view. Include the calming 'sit down if...' closer as a fixed last screen with softer music, and no score animation.

catalog.rankReason: Fills the critics' first gap: there is no TPR/movement game, yet it is the default warmer and brain break for 9-11s and the cheapest whole-class response. M build with two modes: Gogo Says / Captain's Orders (commands with a trap) and Stand Up If / Opinion Line (a spectrum at B levels, which is how adults come in). It needs pre-recorded audio for every built-in command and trap phrase, a coarse once-per-round class estimate, and a big animated caller so the screen carries the game. Adult appeal is low (5.3), so for adults it is pitched as the Opinion Line.

catalog.name: Hafıza Kartları (Memory Match)
catalog.familiarAs: Memory / Pairs / Concentration (Wordwall Matching Pairs, Baamboozle+ Memory)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams take turns turning over two numbered cards to find language pairs: picture and word, word and meaning, EN and TR, verb forms, collocation halves or idiom and meaning. The class says every card aloud as it flips, and a match only pays in full when the team uses the pair ('Say it' / 'Lock it' / 'Use it'), so a calm memory game becomes a steady stream of speaking.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (teacher, about 60 s, Turkish chrome)
1. Choose the group chip and a topic: a built-in category, or a free prompt such as 'mutfak eşyaları, 4. sınıf'.
2. The pair type is suggested from the level and can be changed (Resim–Kelime, EN–TR, Kelime–Tanım, Kolokasyon, Fiil halleri, Deyim–Anlam, Zıt anlam, Kafiye, Soru–Cevap, Kelime ailesi).
3. The lesson-fit timer proposes the grid and the number of rounds, e.g. '12 kart × 3 tur ≈ 18 dk'. Its estimate is turns ≈ 2.2 × pairs for kids, 2.0 × pairs in Arena and 1.8 × pairs for adults, at about 25 / 30 / 40 s per turn.
4. Pick 2-6 teams. The summary line reads 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 18 dk · 12 kart · Resim–Kelime', with a 'Değiştir' link.
5. The validator runs before the deal and reports its result, e.g. '12 çift hazır · 2 belirsiz çift çıkarıldı'.

0. PRACTICE (Oyun Parkı only, unscored, 20-30 s). Gogo the parrot plays a 4-card demo: he flips, says the word, the class echoes, he finds the pair and says 'It's a pair! Say it!'.

1. DEAL. Cards fly into a numbered grid in order, with soft ticks. The deal takes 2 s or less and can be skipped. For B groups there is an optional coordinate mode (A1-E6, Battleship-style), which practises the alphabet.

2. LOOK AND SAY (preview; default ON for kids at 8 s, ON in Arena at 5 s, OFF for adults). Every face is shown and read by TTS (0.8x for A1/A2 Genç), and the class echoes each word. Then all cards flip down with one whoosh. This makes the grid a vocabulary drill before the memory play starts, and it removes the first team's blind-start disadvantage.

3. TURN.
- Kids and Arena: the seat-number spinner picks the picker inside the active team. Adults: the rotating spokesperson picks. Nobody is ever named.
- The picker calls a number in English ('Number seven!'). The teacher taps the card or types 7 + Enter, or a student taps the interactive board ('Tahtaya gel').
- The card flips (350 ms) and spotlight-zooms to the centre at the prompt font floor, so the back row can read it, while TTS reads it aloud. The whole class echoes it (kids), then it shrinks back to its slot.
- The team may huddle (10 / 15 / 20 s, 'Team talk'), then calls the second number.
- Conflict resolved: the raw idea had teams call both numbers at once. Calls are now sequential, because in a real class the first card is language input and the second call is a genuine memory decision. Calling both blind survives as an optional risk play ('Double Down' / 'Call both').

4a. MATCH. The two cards glide together with a magnetic 'click', glow in the team colour with the team emblem or mascot stamped on them (colour plus shape, safe for colour-blind students), and fly to the team's tray.
- Points: kids get 1 star; Arena gets +10 (× combo); adults get +10.
- LANGUAGE STEP:
  - Kids 'Say it!': the team says the word or a frame together, e.g. 'It's a frog!'. For actable items, the whole class stands and acts it. Reward: a sticker.
  - Arena 'Lock it': within 30 s, say it plus the round's check (a sentence frame, the other form, spell it, or the opposite). Reward: +5, and the streak grows.
  - Adults 'Use it': a natural sentence with the pair. The teacher taps ✓ / ✗ / 'Tekrar'. Reward: +5.
- WRONG LANGUAGE STEP:
  - Kids: a soft 'boing', then a second try with a free hint (picture, then first letter, then listen again). If it is still wrong, Gogo says it, the class repeats it twice, and an effort star goes to the class album. The pair's star stays with the team.
  - Arena: the streak breaks, and the team keeps the pair and its 10. If the teacher has opted in to mild steals, the next team in turn order may answer for the +5; otherwise the class says the model answer together.
