Show the class profile name in huge type with the hero roster on the resume screen (teacher-only confirm) to prevent loading the wrong class. Add a 'bugün eksik' toggle that lends an absent team's hero to its members, and export or import the save as a short code.

Limit dominance: the spinner also picks the WRITER (not just the speaker) each node, rotating the pen. Magic sentences must be said by a spun seat, not by a volunteer. Voting uses per-team counts (one vote per team, reason first) at all levels in large classes, not the head-count majority. Steal eligibility goes to the team with the fewest steals so far, not the next in rotation. Cap the Stüdyo wager at 25%, or turn it into a co-op 'party wager' on boss HP.

Offer an adult 'Hızlı başlangıç' preset: no pre-teach (or a 30-s glossary card), heroes auto-dealt, magic sentences replaced by a quick 'say the frame' or off, and Talk nodes and Yol Ayrımı forks up front. Label the dice and rituals 'isteğe bağlı' in Stüdyo.

Solve TTS in advance: pre-render audio for all built-in adventures and pre-teach words (static MP3s shipped with the pack), and for LLM packs use a server-side TTS render cached per pack. Show a clear red 'Ses yok, öğretmen okur' banner in setup before class, not mid-lesson.

Add a per-section shuffle for replayability (fork outcomes, boss phase items and ending conditions are reseeded per class profile) and 2-3 skins per audience at launch, so parallel classes cannot spoil each other.

Re-phase the build. Ship Yol Ayrımı first as its own lightweight game (scene, comprehension gate, vote, ending gallery). It covers adults and kids well with low teacher load and could count as a separate game in the 10-game suite. Then build the Quest map: v1 linear with gate, chest and boss, one currency, phone remote, 'Zil çaldı'. Talk nodes, shop, events and campaigns come later.

issues: A1 Genç pre-readers are still expected to read. Fork labels are full sentences ('The bridge is short but old.'), Yol Ayrımı comprehension gates are about scene text, Puzzle Door riddles have 3 text clues, and typewriter text is the default. With a 0-4 word panel cap, a 'gate about the text' has almost nothing to test, so the gate becomes a guess.
Typewriter reveal hurts early readers. The text arrives slower than the 0.8x read-aloud, and it breaks the link between the word they see and the word they hear.

The picture requirement in Oyun Parkı clashes with the built-in sources. grammar_mcq_* items are text-only sentence MCQs, and words.js has no images. Emoji only cover concrete nouns, so after 'items that cannot be pictured are dropped' a grammar-topic pack (for example 'present continuous') or an abstract free prompt leaves picture gates nearly empty. The run then fails or falls back silently.

A free Turkish prompt such as 'hayvanlar ve present continuous' must produce up to 20 item types plus a coherent narration layer, per level and per audience. That is the least reliable path in the whole suite. Types like lock, case, roleplay and sound at A1 Genç are unrealistic for the LLM to get right, and the validator's words.js band check cannot judge grammar or naturalness.

Most of the time does not go to language. Per node there is a scene, a spotlight spin, a question, a huddle, boards, a reveal, a die roll, loot, an Echo and the meter, and on top of that come map turns, votes, the pre-teach and heroes. In a real class a node takes 4-5 min, not 3, so 20 min yields about 3 challenges per team. The ceremony (dice tumble, loot rarity, fanfares) competes with retrieval time.

Individual production is thin. Only the spotlight student speaks, once per node, and with 6 teams × 7 nodes each student may speak aloud once or not at all. Most output is board-writing or holding up A-D cards. On Talk nodes only one team talks while the other 5 teams wait.

Talk nodes at A1 Genç and A2 Genç put one 9-year-old on the spot to perform a line to the teacher-as-NPC in front of 30 peers. That is high affective load for this age, even with the Weak-to-model-to-repeat safety net.

The adult 'magic sentence' ritual ('I'm going to show my press card') and the hero powers can feel infantilising for A1-A2 adults in a corporate or university class. The Stüdyo skin fixes the visuals but not this ritual.
B2 Genç is promised 'concrete topics, not abstract debate', yet the boss's phase 3 at B2 is a debate or accusation duel. The rule is not split by audience.

B2 adult challenges are mostly 'MCQ with harder items'. The inference and word-formation items depend on content the banks don't have (grammar_mcq has no word formation, and readings_* may lack inference items), so B2 risks feeling like A2 with longer text.

Oyun Parkı all-answer assumes printed A-D picture cards, one set per team or per student, and TPR mapping (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C) collapses at 4 options. A1 Genç should never see 4 options anyway, but the challenge spec allows 3-4 at A2.
The adventure log at A1 Genç is 5 sentences of text that the children cannot read. The keepsake misses its audience.

Minimal-pair listening gates at A1 Genç depend on browser TTS quality. Many school PCs have a poor en-US voice, and on the 'Öğretmen okur' fallback the teacher gives the answer away through articulation.

The setup and dial surface is very large for 8 groups × 3 audiences × 4 lengths. A teacher who picks A1 adult + Arena or B2 Genç + Oyun Parkı can reach combinations nobody has tuned (for example a d20 with 0-4 word panels).
fixes: For A1 Genç (and optionally A2 Genç), add a 'pre-reader' profile. Fork choices become 2 picture cards with an audio label and no sentence text. Comprehension gates become listen-and-point picture questions ('Where is Gogo? Point!') about the spoken narration, not the on-screen text. Puzzle Door is letter tiles or picture-riddle only, with no 3-clue text riddles. Typed answers never appear.
Replace typewriter text with read-aloud plus word-by-word karaoke highlighting whenever the audience is Oyun Parkı or the level is A1. Keep typewriter only for Arena B1+ and Stüdyo.

Add a picturability check at pack build time. If fewer than about 70% of the gate items for an Oyun Parkı run have an emoji or imageKey, warn the teacher in the preview ('Bu konu resimle zor anlatılır') and offer auto-switch options: listen-and-choose, TPR 'act it' items (actable=true), or a sentence-level picture scene ('The cat is sleeping' shown with emoji compositions) for grammar topics like present continuous.

Cap the item types per level and audience in the generator: A1 Genç gets vocab-picture, sound (only if a good voice is detected), tf-listen, pair (emoji) and order (chunk tiles); A2 adds gap-with-bank and mcq; B1+ unlocks error, qa, riddle and roleplay. The LLM is asked only for these types, which raises reliability. Keep 'Sadece sorular' as the only one-click LLM path for Genç groups until the story layer passes validation often in testing.

Budget time honestly. Size the map at 4 min per node, not 3 (20 min = 3-4 nodes + mini-boss). Make the dice roll auto-resolve in under 1 s after the first two rolls. Merge Echo, loot and meter into one combined reward animation of at most 2 s. Show a 'dil süresi' ratio in teacher analytics to catch drift.

Raise individual output. On Talk nodes every team rehearses the line in pairs for 30 s ('everybody practises, one performs'), and the teacher can tap 'another team performs too' for a shared bonus. At Camp, add a pair drill ('ask your partner the lost word'). Make the magic sentence a whole-team chorus, not one person.
For Oyun Parkı Talk nodes, add a 'team chorus' option in which the spotlight team says the formula together, then optionally one volunteer. Never require an individual solo at A1 Genç or A2 Genç.

In Stüdyo, rename magic sentences to 'Power lines' and frame them as in-role functional language ('Let me handle this.'). Add an 'Adult classes: skip power rituals' toggle, on by default at A1 and A2 corporate settings, in which powers fire with a click.
Split the B2 boss phase 3 by audience: Stüdyo gets a debate or dilemma, Arena B2 Genç gets an evidence-based accusation or problem-solving explanation on concrete topics only.

Give B2 real B2 work. Generate word-formation, collocation and inference items from words.js families and readings_* texts (derive rules plus LLM with a validator). Require at least 30% production items (qa typed, error without highlight) at B2, and make the Adventure Log rewrite a follow-up writing task.

Make the printing kit part of setup: per-team A/B (A1 Genç) or A-D picture answer cards, and the colour/shape team banners. Force 2 options at A1 Genç and at most 3 options with TPR in Oyun Parkı, falling back to cards for 4.
For Oyun Parkı, render the Adventure Log as a 4-6 panel picture strip with one short caption each, read aloud by Gogo. The text log is for the teacher or print.

Before offering sound gates, run a TTS voice check. If no good English voice is found, disable minimal-pair gates and substitute picture listening via teacher read-aloud, where giving the answer away does not matter.

Lock the audience/level combinations to tuned presets (Oyun Parkı only for A1 Genç and A2 Genç; Arena for any Genç group; Stüdyo for adults) and hide cross-audience overrides behind 'Gelişmiş'. Test the 8 default presets before shipping any others.

Ship v1 with the three strongest configurations only: Oyun Parkı A1 Genç and A2 Genç (Gogo and the Lost Colours), Arena B1 Genç (Mystery Academy), Stüdyo A2-B1 ('Kayıp Bavul'). Add Yol Ayrımı and LLM stories after classroom trials. Consider sharing the Yol Ayrımı engine with any separate Crossroads or Treasure Map candidate rather than building it twice.

issues: Scope is not one game, it is three or four: a branching-map RPG, a story-only CYOA (Yol Ayrımı), a mystery/case game (Grand Hotel, Office Mystery, Mystery Academy use pack.frames.case) and a mini-game host (Chest = match/sort/unjumble/odd, Puzzle Door = riddle/hangman/lock). 11 node kinds x 3 audience rule packs x ~20 content types means about 60+ distinct screen states. Even phased, v1 as written (gate + npc + chest + boss + kids ruleset + 3 skins) is L-XL on its own. It is the highest-risk item in the suite.

Duplication with other likely candidates. Puzzle Door spell-it is Hangman; the Chest mini-games are Memory/Group Sort/Unjumble; the case frame and the accusation boss are the 'Kim Yaptı?/Alibi' mystery game; Yol Ayrımı is a standalone CYOA game; the boss is a Gimkit-style boss battle. If those ship separately, the suite builds them twice or they drift apart visually and in their rules.

The core loop risks being 'MCQ quiz with a map skin'. About 70% of nodes are Challenge gates (mcq/vocab/gap), and the map only changes which question comes next. Unless forks, loot and hero powers visibly change later play, adults will see it as a Kahoot with extra clicks.

The pacing numbers are optimistic. One node runs scene typewriter, spotlight spinner, delayed options (2-4 s), huddle (10-20 s), all-write, reveal, teacher Doğru/Yanlış per board, a dice animation, Echo awards and meter fill. With 5-6 teams judged by hand, that is realistically 4-5 minutes, not 3. A 30-minute Bölüm with 7 nodes plus a boss will overrun, and the pre-teach and hero steps add another 4 minutes.

The kids checklist passes on paper but not in practice. The 3-rule card hides extra systems: hero powers with magic sentences, the backpack with 5 item types, the shop with a shared purse, chests, events and Echo stickers. 9-year-olds will not track them. The teacher will, and gets overloaded.

Teacher cognitive load is heavy. The GM panel needs about 30 buttons, the keyboard map has 14 keys, plus speaking judgement with a checklist, TPR vote counting and a real-die entry. On a single-screen setup (the common Turkish classroom case: one laptop mirrored to a projector or smartboard) the GM overlay shows the answers to the class.

Keyboard collisions: A/B/C for fork choices clash with B = Boss and S = Skip if a fork ever has more than 3 options, and Y/N and 1/2/3 overlap in meaning across node kinds. Letter shortcuts are also unusable on a touch smartboard.

Art and asset load is the hidden cost. Three skins each need a map (with per-region colour flood or district lighting), hero portraits with 3 expressions, 3-4 bosses with phase states, creature idles, and loot icons. Some built-in adventures (London, Grand Hotel, Startup, Museum, Stranded, Office, Dragon Riders, Cyber City, Space Station, Gogo, Dragon Egg, Space Puppy, Animal Island) need their own backgrounds. That is 13+ adventures: not shippable with polish.

LLM reliability: the item layer is fine (it reuses validated types), but the narration layer across 7-10 nodes with a word cap per panel, a lexical band per level, a teenSafe blocklist and outline consistency will fail often at A1 Genç (0-4 words per panel is barely narration). The fallback template lines will make generated stories read as patchwork. The words.js band check will also flag proper nouns and skin words (dragon, receptionist) as off-band.
The word-band check against words.js (1.4 MB) cannot run client-side. It needs a server-side validator or a precomputed compact lemma-to-band map, otherwise the build ships a large bundle.

Adults: the fantasy/RPG framing plus d20 loot fits some adult classes poorly. The Stüdyo skins (London, Grand Hotel) are good but are effectively a different game (a scenario simulation). The dice add ceremony without meaningful decisions, since the roll only sizes gold that buys the same 5 items.
Echo and Inspiration, team XP, the shared purse, party hearts and the Quest Meter make 5 overlapping currencies in Arena and Stüdyo. A classroom only reads 1-2 on a projector.

TTS: speechSynthesis on Turkish-locale Windows school PCs often lacks a good en-GB/en-US voice, and Chrome's online voices need a network connection. Gogo 'reads every panel at 0.8x' and is central to A1 Genç (0-4 words per panel), so a missing voice breaks the kids mode, not just a convenience.
Save and resume across lessons on a shared school PC with localStorage is fragile. Cloud sync depends on teacher login, which many teachers skip in class.

Silent-signal votes (corners, stand/sit) and the 'teacher taps majority' step are fine, but the VETO, the Comeback tie-break, reasons-before-vote and the hard-path diff shift add rules to each fork that most teachers will switch off.
fixes: Split it. Ship 'Büyük Macera' as the map RPG only. Make Yol Ayrımı its own lightweight game (scene -> gate -> vote; about an M build that reuses the scene renderer), and move the case/mystery frame (Grand Hotel, Office Mystery, Mystery Academy) into the mystery candidate (Kim Yaptı?). Cross-link them as 'Macera ailesi'.

Build a shared 'challenge widget' library for the whole suite (mcq, gap, match-4, sort-2, unjumble, spell-tiles, error-tap, tf-fix, lock) with one API: render(item, audience) -> Promise<result>. The RPG, Hangman, the Baamboozle board and Jeopardy then all consume it. The RPG's Chest and Door become thin wrappers, which kills the duplication.

A real v1 MVP: a linear 5-7 node map with only Challenge, Talk, Chest, Camp and Boss; ONE skin per audience (Gogo and the Lost Colours, Cyber City, Kayıp Bavul London); no shop, no events, no backpack, no powers except one per team; a d6 reward for kids and no dice for adults (show a 'loot card' instead). Add forks in v1.5, because forks are the core differentiator. Shop, events, campaigns and LLM stories come in v2+.

Make forks matter mechanically so it isn't a skinned quiz. Each path changes the NEXT node's kind and skill (Talk vs Puzzle), the difficulty and the visible reward, and at least one fork per chapter unlocks a different ending panel. Show the consequence on the map immediately (e.g. the bridge path skips Camp).

Re-time from real measurements: budget 4 min per node with 4 teams and 5 min with 6; cap teams at 5 by default; auto-skip the typewriter for adults; make Echo automatic for engine-checked items. Let the live estimate auto-compress, e.g. shorter huddles and a skipped Camp, when behind schedule, rather than relying only on 'Boss'a geç'.

Kids: cut hero powers down to Gogo's prompted one-liners (the powers auto-trigger when Gogo cues them, so there is no choice), and drop the shop and backpack from Oyun Parkı entirely. Loot is purely cosmetic (colour splash plus sticker). That keeps the 3-rule card honest.

Collapse currencies. Party level: Quest Meter plus hearts (hearts not shown in Oyun Parkı). Team level: exactly one (stars, XP or points). Gold and the shop should apply only to Stüdyo and Arena, and only in v2.

GM input: provide a phone or second-tab presenter view via BroadcastChannel/URL pairing when available. For single-screen setups, make answers hidden by default behind a hold-to-peek key, and add a large on-canvas touch bar (Doğru / Yanlış / Great-Good-Weak / Next) for smartboards. Keep keyboard shortcuts but remap: fork choices = 1/2/3 only in fork state, Great/Good/Weak = 1/2/3 only in Talk state (state-scoped keys), Boss = Shift+B, Skip = Shift+S.

Art strategy: one illustrated SVG map per skin, built from named region paths, so the colour flood is a CSS filter/fill transition per region (grayscale -> colour) and the Arena district light-up is a stroke glow on the same paths. Hero portraits as layered SVG (base plus 3 mouth/eye states). Bosses as a 3-state SVG. Twemoji/OpenMoji (self-hosted, licensed) for item pictures. Target under 400 KB of art per skin, lazy-loaded.
Sound: about 12 short self-made or CC0 cues per skin (marimba / synth / woodblock), lazy-loaded, muted by default in Stüdyo. The dice sound and roll must be under 1 s.

LLM: generate narration node-by-node with the full outline in context but a strict JSON schema per node ({panels: string[<=3], choices[{label}]}); validate caps and the blocklist client-side and the band server-side with a precomputed lemma-to-CEFR map (a few hundred KB, gzip) plus a per-skin allowlist of story nouns. Retry once per failing node with the violation listed, then fall back to the template. For A1 Genç, skip LLM narration entirely and use template picture-panels.

TTS: detect an English voice at setup, warn in Turkish, and offer pre-rendered MP3 narration for the built-in adventures (at minimum the kids ones, since Gogo depends on it); generated stories fall back to 'Öğretmen okur' with a larger teacher-script font in the GM view.

Adults: reframe Stüdyo as 'Senaryo' (a real-life mission sim) and drop the d20. A right answer reveals a loot/perk card; Talk nodes use Great/Good/Weak mapped directly to Success / Success at a cost / Complication with no roll (or the roll as an opt-in). Fantasy remains available but is not the default.

Save: export/import the class profile as a short code or JSON file and a QR code; keep localStorage as the primary store and use cloud sync only when logged in; store the run log compactly (item ids, not text).

Validation fixtures: ship each built-in adventure as a static JSON pack that goes through the same validator in CI (graph reachable, at least one win ending, caps met, slots fillable from the built-in banks for every level), so regressions surface before class.

catalog.rankReason: Requested (RPG), but the most ambitious game and the weakest on logistics (6). It ships last in the first wave and only as the map RPG: fog map, one power per hero team, class votes, a co-op boss, and 'a right answer always succeeds; dice only set the size of the reward'. Size maps with a measured clock (4.5 min per node for Genç, 3 for adults) and get the first scoring moment on screen before minute 3. A1 Genç get a pre-reader profile (picture fork cards with audio); low levels get karaoke read-aloud instead of typewriter text. Challenges come from the shared widget library. The case frame moves to c26, Yol Ayrımı becomes a later light game, and c25's Komut Modu can join it later.

catalog.name: Hız Avı (Swat & Spot Speed Race)
catalog.familiarAs: Slap the Board / Whack-a-Mole / Balloon Pop / Dobble (Spot It!)
catalog.oneLiner: A fast listening-and-looking race on the projector. In 'Avla!' one runner per team races to touch or call the floating balloon, fish or word that matches a spoken or shown clue. In 'Eşini Bul!' runners race to name the one picture or word that two Dobble-style cards share. After every find, the whole class says the word together.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 60 s)
The teacher picks a pack: a built-in topic, or a free-text prompt that the LLM turns into items. The setup screen shows one summary line, for example 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk · Değiştir'. The teacher then chooses three things.

1. The match recipe:
- Kids: Avla! → Eşini Bul! → Avla!
- Arena: Avla! → Eşini Bul! → Hızlı Seri
- Stüdyo warmer: one round of either mode. Full match: 3 rounds.

2. The race style. The game suggests one from a setup question: 'Etkileşimli tahta var mı? Sınıf kalabalık mı?'
- 'Söyle' (the default): runners stand up at their desks and call the item's number AND its word, e.g. 'Seven, giraffe!'.
- 'Tahtaya dokun': a duel with at most 2 runners at the board. A tape line sits two steps from the board, and the rule is walk, don't run. On LCD smart boards runners use an open palm. Soft foam swatters are allowed only on a projector wall or whiteboard.
- 'Masadan': the calmest style. Everyone stays seated, the runner raises the team paddle and says the answer.

3. The teams: 2 to 4. The game offers printables: number cards 1-8, team paddles, and a call list for 'Öğretmen okur' when there is no English voice.

PRACTICE
Gogo, the parrot (kids), or a 2-clue 'Warm-up' (Arena/Stüdyo) plays 2 clues that don't score.

MODE A: AVLA! (SWAT). One clue takes about 20-30 s; a round is 8-12 clues.

1. Runners. The seat spinner picks one seat number per racing team, e.g. 'Fox #5 vs Panda #12'. Nobody is ever picked by name.
- In 'Söyle' and 'Masadan', every team races on every clue.
- In 'Tahtaya dokun' with 3-4 teams, two teams duel on a round-robin schedule and the others form the Tribune.
- Rotation: no seat runs twice until every seat in that team has run. Absent seats are skipped.

2. Ready. 6-16 items drift slowly: balloons, fish, moles, radar blips or paper slips. Each carries a big number plus a colour-and-shape badge, so it works for colour-blind students. Runners put their hands on their heads ('Hands on heads!'). The items look glassy and locked.

3. Clue. The clue is spoken by TTS and shown on screen. It can be:
- a picture or an audio word
- an easy definition, or a Turkish word
- a gap sentence
- a relation: 'past of GO', 'opposite of HOT', 'rhymes with BEAR'
- a category: 'Find a fruit!'
- a 3-part riddle, read one part every 4 s
- 'Which sentence is wrong?' with 4 floating sentences
- a minimal pair: 'ship' is heard and ship/sheep/chip/cheap float

The items stay locked until the clue has finished and the options delay has passed (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s). Then a chime plays and 'GO!' appears. This means nobody wins by guessing before the clue is over, or because of TTS lag. In touch mode the items FREEZE at GO, so no child chases a moving target.

4. Race and input. The teacher enters the item first, then the team: click or tap the item (or type its number; two digits within 0.5 s for 10-16), then press the team key (Q/W/E/R) or tap the team's colour chip. On a touch board, the touched item pops and colour chips appear beside it for the runner to tap. Two team keys within 1 s means a PHOTO FINISH: both teams score and a 1.5 s slow-motion replay plays. U undoes the last award.

5. Correct. The item's effect depends on the skin:
- a balloon floats up with a star into the team's basket
- a fish swims into the team's bowl
- a mole waves hello and ducks
- Arena: a 'LOCKED' stamp
- Stüdyo: the slip flips to show IPA, the TR gloss and the example

TTS says the word, and the class echoes it: 'Say it twice!'. This is always on for kids and a toggle for everyone else. A new item drifts in, so the choice never gets easier as the round goes on.

6. Wrong. A soft boing plays and the item shrugs.
- Kids: a 2 s 'dizzy' wobble, then the runner may try again. Nobody is out.
- Arena/Stüdyo: that runner is locked for this clue and the others keep racing. This is the natural steal, and the first team loses nothing. Stüdyo has an optional −1.

7. Stuck. Hints arrive automatically and are free in every mode, because a hint bought by one team would also help the rival runner.
- Kids: at 6 s the clue plays again; at 10 s the first letter appears and the target wiggles; at 15 s Gogo flies to the target and says it, the class repeats it twice, and both runners get an effort star (it goes to the album).
- Arena: at 8 s the first letter; at 12 s 50:50 (half the wrong items fade); at 16 s a gapped example; at 20 s the reveal.
- Stüdyo: at 10 s the definition or example; at 15 s the TR gloss (it can be switched off); at 20 s the reveal plus a one-line 'why'.

8. Everyone else answers every clue.
- Kids: on GO, seated students point at the item from their seats, or show the number with fingers or number cards.
- Arena: each seated team writes the number (A levels) or the word itself (B levels, which practises spelling) on one mini-whiteboard and holds it up at 'Boards up!'.
- Stüdyo: pairs jot the answer down.
- The teacher then taps 'Sınıf ✓' or the team chips.

MODE B: EŞİNİ BUL! (SPOT). One card pair takes about 15-25 s; a round is 8-10 pairs.

1. Two big cards deal in. Kids' cards slide in upright or tilted by 10° at most; Arena and adult cards spin in. Each card has k symbols, and exactly one symbol is on both.

2. Runners race to SAY the shared item in English.
- Kids: saying the full frame 'It's a banana!' earns a bonus feather star.
- B1 and above: an optional 'Say it in a sentence' bonus, e.g. 'There's a key on both cards.'

3. The teacher clicks the item the runner named (on either card), then the team. The teacher doesn't need to find the match; the game checks it.
- Correct: the item glows on both cards, a line in the team colour connects the two, and TTS says the word.
- Wrong: the same rules as in Avla!.

4. Stuck:
- Kids: at 8 s both copies shimmer; at 12 s Gogo points to them.
- Arena: at 10 s half the non-matching symbols fade.
- Adults: at 15 s the first letter appears.
- Everyone: the reveal comes at 20 s.

Variants:
- 'Merkez Kart' (Dobble's Poison Well, renamed): whole teams play instead of runners. Each team has its own card around a centre card that flips every round, and each team's card shares a different single item with the centre. Teams huddle (kids 10 s, Arena 15 s, adults 20 s), then a rotating spokesperson says the answer. The first correct team gets +2 and every other correct team gets +1, so every team can score.
- 'Çapraz' (A2 and above): card A shows words and card B shows pictures, TR glosses, past forms, IPA or idiom halves. Exactly one pair connects.

MODE C: HIZLI SERİ (Arena/Stüdyo finale only)
The same runners play 5 clues back to back. A wrong call sits that runner out for the next clue. There is no speed bonus. Stüdyo teams may wager before the series.

SCORING
Speed decides WHO scores, never HOW MUCH. There are no time-based points.
- Oyun Parkı: winning a race = 1 star; a photo finish = both teams. The frame bonus is 1 feather star. Gogo's reveal gives effort stars to the class album. Each time most of the seated class got it right, a balloon goes into the shared class jar. Stars never go down.
- Arena: a race win is +3 and a correct tribune board is +1. A clean streak gives a combo of ×1.5 at 3 and ×2 at 5. The streak counts accuracy only, and a false call breaks it. Scores have a floor of 0.
- Stüdyo: a win is +2, a tribune answer +1 and a sentence bonus +1. The −1 for a false call is optional.
- Power cards: once per round, a golden item is the target. The team that wins it draws a card:
  - Kids get Green cards only: Gift a star to a team you tap, Everyone +2, Double next, Brain break with Gogo.
  - Arena adds Yellow cards when the teacher opts in: Steal 5 (capped at that team's score), Pick the next duel pairing.
  - Stüdyo uses Green and Yellow by default, and Red only when the teacher opts in.
- Comeback (Light): the last team gets +1 Slipstream when it wins a clue, and the trailing team picks the next round's clue type or skin.

BETWEEN ROUNDS
- Kids: a 45 s stirrer ('Stand up if you popped a balloon! Jump twice!') or a 60 s settler ('Close your eyes. What was on balloon 3?'). The settler recycles the round's words.

FINALE
- Kids: every team gets a title, the jar releases its balloons, and a sticker goes into the album.
- Arena: a podium plus stat awards.
- Stüdyo: full scores plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' list.
catalog.playerSetup:
2-4 teams; a class split into two halves is the kids default. One runner per team per clue, picked by the seat-number spinner and rotating through every student before anyone runs twice. In 'Tahtaya dokun' at most 2 runners are at the board (a duel, round-robin with 3-4 teams while the others form the Tribune). Everyone who isn't running answers every clue: pointing or fingers (kids), one mini-whiteboard per team (Arena), pair jotting (Stüdyo). 'Merkez Kart' is a whole-team mode: huddle, then a rotating spokesperson answers. Works for 12-40 students.

Inclusion options:
- 'Buddy run': two students run together.
- Per-seat 'hep masadan': a student who can't or won't come forward always competes by call-out from their seat.
- An optional private 'denk eşleşme' tier: the teacher marks seats into three tiers so the spinner matches runners of similar confidence. It is never shown on screen.

Nobody is picked by name, and the group label never appears on the student screen.
skills: speaking (short frames: 'It's a...!', 'Say it in a sentence')
grammar forms, collocations and error spotting
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Rapid Recall' (Avla!) and 'Spot the Twin' (Eşini Bul!)

LOOK AND SOUND
- An editorial quiz-night look: cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, with a system sans font.
- Items are paper slips, luggage tags (travel packs) or letter tiles drifting on a desk-like surface.
- No mascot and no voice lines. The caption strip is neutral: 'Round 2 · Travel'.
- Sounds: woodblock and piano, 1 s or less. Music is off.

RULES
- The default race style is 'Söyle': the runner stands up at the desk and says the word, and the number is only a backup. Most adults prefer this to walking to the board.
- A rotating spokesperson, with pair consultation for the tribune point.
- A wrong call locks the runner for the clue; the −1 is optional.
- After every find, the slip flips to show IPA, the TR gloss and an example sentence.
- A missed item gets a one-line 'why' (whyTr).
- Optional 'Say it in a sentence' bonus (+1) with a personal sentence, e.g. 'I made a mistake at work yesterday.'
- The finale can be a Hızlı Seri with a wager: teams bet up to half their score before their runner's 5-clue series.

ADULT CLUE TYPES (beyond pictures and definitions)
- Collocation gaps: 'make a ___', where only 'mistake' on screen fits and the distractors are guaranteed wrong.
- A phrasal verb from its definition.
- Synonyms, and register: 'the formal word for GET' → obtain.
- Word families: 'the noun of DECIDE'.
- Error spotting: 4-6 sentences float and one is wrong; the reveal underlines the error span and shows whyTr.
- Minimal-pair listening: TTS says 'full', and full/fool/fall/foul float.
- -ed endings: 'Find the /ɪd/ one'.
- Stress patterns and silent letters.

SPOT FOR ADULTS
- Word-only cards with mixed typefaces and rotations of 30° or less, so the words stay readable. This is harder than it sounds.
- Look-alike decoys: quiet/quite, lose/loose, advice/advise.
- Cross-match cards: word ↔ IPA, verb ↔ past form, idiom half ↔ idiom half (B2), word ↔ TR (A2).

CONTENT
Built-in adult packs: travel and airports, food and restaurants, job interviews, complaints, small-talk chunks, phrasal verbs, make/do/take/have collocations, confusing words, irregular verbs, minimal pairs.

TIMING
A 5-8 minute warmer, or a 20-30 minute match with the Kaçırılanlar review at the end: every word nobody found before the hints, with IPA, TR and an example, and a one-click 'Bu kelimelerle tekrar oyna' for the next lesson.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two different skins with different rule packs. Level and skin stay independent.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1/A2 Genç): 'Pop Party' (Avla!) and 'Gogo's Twins' (Eşini Bul!)

Rules: 3 rules on a Turkish rule card, each with a pictogram, explainable in 20 s:
1. Hands on heads, listen to Gogo.
2. On GO, touch it or say it, gently.
3. Everybody points and says it twice.

Visuals:
- A warm, bright palette on cream, big rounded items, and an Andika-type font at a 6vh floor.
- 6-8 items at most, so the labels stay big.
- Item skins:
  - Balloon Party (the default): a popped balloon floats up with a star into the team's basket.
  - Aquarium: the fish swims into the team's bowl and blows a bubble heart.
  - Peek-a-boo Garden: moles in tiny hats wave hello and duck back down.
- The pointer is Gogo's feather, never a fly swatter hitting animals.
- Team mascots: panda, fox, lion, frog, and so on.

Gogo the parrot:
- demos a 2-clue practice round
- says 'Ready? Hands on heads!'
- repeats every word like a parrot, which models the choral echo
- flies to the answer when the board is stuck
- sleeps on the pause screen

Checklist:
- No elimination: a wrong touch is a 2 s dizzy wobble, then another try.
- No score below zero: stars only.
- A whole-class response every turn: pointing from seats, then the echo twice.
- Non-violent failure: a wrong balloon just boings, and nothing bursts on a mistake.

Other rules:
- Audio clues are read aloud automatically at 0.8x, with a picture on every item.
- No timer by default; when switched on, it is a calm 40 s ring with a marimba chime.
- Pacing: 3 rounds of 3-5 minutes with a stirrer or settler between them, 15-20 minutes in total.

Endings: every team gets a title: Eagle Eyes, Super Listeners, Best Echo, Bravest Guessers, Best Helpers. The class jar releases all the balloons with the words of the day, and the album gets a sticker.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1/B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç group in grade 6+): 'Signal Hunt' (Avla!) and 'Twin Scan' (Eşini Bul!)

Visuals:
- Dark navy with neon accents in the team colours, a condensed display font at a 5vh floor, and 8-12 items.
- The items are blips on a slow radar sweep. A correct call gets a lock-on reticle and a 'LOCKED' stamp in the team colour.
- Twin Scan cards are holo-panels, and a laser line connects the match.
- In 10 s, teams pick an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.
- No mascot. A commentator strip shows at most one line per turn: 'CLEAN STREAK x3', 'PHOTO FINISH!', 'CLUTCH!'.

Rules:
- Framed as a 'Match'.
- A wrong call locks the runner for the clue while the others race on.
- Seated teams write the answer on a mini-whiteboard for +1.
- An accuracy combo: ×1.5 at 3, ×2 at 5. Scores have a floor of 0.
- A 30 s ring in neutral white.
- Opt-in 'Glitch' distraction: a 2 s blur wave with no flashing, disabled under reduced motion. This is the teen-favourite jellyfish from Fishing Frenzy.
- Opt-in Yellow cards.
- Hızlı Seri as the finale.
- Pacing: 3 rounds of 5-7 minutes.

Endings: a podium and stat awards (Longest clean streak, Sharpest tribune, Comeback, Clean sheet). Never a 'last place', and never any cartoon animals or 'Good job, superstar!'.

CONTENT
All Genç groups run through the teenSafe filter. Topics follow YLE (animals, food, classroom, body, clothes, toys, weather, sports, home, transport, colours and numbers) and the MEB unit mappings, with a picture for every item. B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics: synonyms, word families and minimal pairs, not abstract register.
catalog.levelTuning:
All the numbers below are defaults. A 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' dial inside each group shifts them:
- ±2 items
- motion speed
- decoy similarity: at Zor, look-alike or sound-alike decoys such as three/tree, bear/pear, quiet/quite
- Spot rotation and size variance: at Kolay, the shared item has the same size on both cards

'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one full level.

A1
- Genç (0-4 words on screen):
  - Avla!: 6 picture-only balloons with numbers. The clue is the audio word at 0.8x, with an optional 'show the word' reading support, or 'Find a fruit!' / 'Find the red one!'.
  - Spot: 4 upright pictures per card, picture ↔ picture.
  - Frame: 'It's a ___!'.
- Adults (10 words or fewer):
  - 8 items with a picture and the word.
  - Clues: audio, a picture (words float), a TR word.
  - Spot: 5 symbols, with picture ↔ word cross-match.

A2
- Genç (8 words or fewer):
  - 8 items with a picture and a word label.
  - Clues: easy definitions ('It has a long neck.'), opposites, 'past of GO', categories.
  - Spot: 5-6 symbols, picture ↔ word cross-match, and the 'Renk & sayı' variant, where the shared item must be said with its number and colour ('two red apples!'). It needs tinted SVGs.
- Adults (15 words or fewer):
  - 10 word items.
  - Clues: defEasy, TR, simple gap sentences, past forms.
  - Spot: 6 words, or word ↔ TR cross-match.

B1
- Genç (14 words or fewer):
  - 10 word items, pictures optional.
  - Clues: gap sentences, 3-part riddles, irregular past forms, word families.
  - Spot: 6 words tilted up to 15°, verb ↔ past cross-match.
  - Tribune boards write the word, not the number.
- Adults (25 words or fewer):
  - 12 items.
  - Clues: gap sentences, collocations, phrasal verbs from definitions, riddles, -ed endings.
  - Spot: 8 words in mixed fonts, with the 'Say it in a sentence' bonus.

B2
- Genç (20 words or fewer, concrete topics):
  - 12 items.
  - Clues: synonyms and antonyms, word families, minimal pairs (live/leave), rhymes, stress, error spotting with 4 short sentences.
  - Spot: 8 words, look-alikes, word ↔ IPA.
- Adults (40 words or fewer):
  - 12-16 word items, or 4-6 sentence items.
  - Clues: register swaps, synonyms, collocations, error spotting with the span highlighted, minimal-pair listening, silent letters, stress patterns.
  - Spot: 8 words with full rotation, word ↔ IPA, idiom halves.

Font floors (6/5/4.5vh) are what cap the item count on a 16:9 projector. A long clue is split into two cards rather than shrunk.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 5-25 (warmer: one 5-8 min round; Oyun Parkı match: 3 rounds, 15-20 min; Arena: 3 rounds, 15-21 min; Stüdyo: 20-30 min full match)
catalog.contentShape:
Code builds two runtime lists from the pack.

(1) Avla! TARGETS

Each target has these fields:
- id
- srcType
- label: what floats. A term of 3 words or fewer; a full sentence only for error items, within the group cap.
- media: emoji or SVG imageKey. Required for A1/A2 Genç, where unpicturable items are dropped.
- speak: the TTS text.
- accept[]: the term plus alt[].
- clues{}: any of
  - audio
  - picture
  - defEasy, def, defTr
  - gap: from vocab.gap, gap.text or an mcq stem with fmt gap/collocation
  - rel: 'past of GO' (pair rel past), 'opposite of HOT' (ant), 'means BIG' (syn), 'rhymes with BEAR' (sound rhyme), 'the noun of DECIDE' (vocab.family)
  - cat: the category-list label, e.g. 'Find a fruit!'
  - riddle[3]: hard to easy
  - sound: minimal-pair audio, or the /t/ /d/ /ɪd/ key
- confusables[]: ids that must never float together with this target.

How each item type feeds the game:
- vocab: every clue kind.
- pair: relation clues, and the Spot cross-match.
- sound: minimal-pair, -ed, stress and rhyme rounds.
- category-list: 'Find a ___'. Only one member of that list floats; the fillers come from other lists.
- riddle: clues read one every 4 s.
- error: 1 wrong sentence plus 3-5 correct 'right' sentences taken from other error items. The reveal highlights the span.
- gap / mcq: sentence rounds, where the floats are the bank or options (4-6).

The screen shows the target plus fillers drawn from the same pack, never including its confusables. Code computes confusables from four sources:
- the same image
- alt[] and homophones (pear/pair on audio clues)
- synonyms on defEasy/TR clues, and gap.alsoOk
- shared category membership

For LLM-generated packs, one extra pass asks 'could any other on-screen item also answer this clue?'. The teacher preview flags anything the checks were unsure about.

(2) Spot SYMBOLS

Each symbol is {id, label, media?, ipa?, pairKey?}.

Every round is generated fresh: code picks one shared symbol plus k−1 and k−1 other symbols, with no other overlap between the cards. A pair of cards therefore needs only 2k−1 symbols (15 for k=8), not a full 57-card Dobble deck. For variety, the pack needs at least 3 times that.

Constraints:
- The shared item never sits in the same position on both cards.
- At Orta and Zor, it also appears at a different size on each card.

Cross-match cards put pair.a on card A and pair.b on card B, and code checks uniqueness within pair.set. The allowed relations are tr, emoji, past, ant, def, sound/IPA and idiom half. syn and colloc are allowed only after the LLM uniqueness pass and the teacher preview.

Merkez Kart needs k + teams×(k−1) symbols per round, e.g. 21 symbols for 4 teams at k=5.

MINIMUMS
- Avla!: 8 targets for kids and 12 for Arena/Stüdyo. The ideal is 16-40.
- Spot: 12 symbols at k=4 and 24 at k=8.

VALIDATION
- Word caps per group are enforced on clues and float labels.
- teenSafe.
- The CEFR band is taken from words.js.
- IPA comes only from words.js.
- No duplicate images.
- A generated pack that is too small is topped up from the built-in topic nearest to it.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- The pack: a built-in topic or a free-text prompt (Turkish is fine), then a preview of every clue, answer and confusable warning, where items can be edited or removed.
- The summary line with 'Değiştir': skin, rule pack, timer, minutes. The result is saved to the class profile.
- The match recipe: which mode each round uses (Avla! / Eşini Bul! / Merkez Kart / Hızlı Seri), and the lesson-fit minutes (5/10/15/20/30), which size the rounds.
- The race style (Söyle / Tahtaya dokun / Masadan).
- 2-4 teams, the class size, absent seats, buddy-run seats, 'hep masadan' seats, and the optional private tiers.

AVLA!
- Item count (6-16)
- Motion: Durgun ızgara / Yavaş / Orta / Hızlı. The OS reduced-motion setting forces the static grid. In touch mode items freeze at GO; a 'Hareketli hedef' override exists for call-out only.
- The item skin
- Labels: number, colour, shape
- A clue-type mix with checkboxes and per-group defaults
- The options delay

EŞİNİ BUL!
- Symbols per card (4-8)
- Rotation and size variance
- The cross-match relation
- Auto-advance on/off

RULES
- The wrong-call rule: dizzy retry / lock for this clue / lock for this clue and the next
- The optional −1
- Each hint step on/off, and the TR gloss off for immersion classes
- Choral echo on/off
- The frame and sentence bonuses
- The golden item and the Harshness level (Green / Yellow / Red)
- Comeback (Off / Light / Strong)
- The Glitch distraction (Arena opt-in)
- Timer: off / 30 / 40 s, +10 s, 'Süresiz'

KEYS
- Item number or click → team key Q/W/E/R. Two team keys within 1 s = tie.
- U: undo the last award
- Space/→: next clue
- L: listen again
- H: next hint now
- T: pause
- 'Bu da olur': accept an unexpected valid answer and flag the item for review

PRINTABLES
- The call list (the seeded order matches the game, for 'Öğretmen okur')
- Number cards 1-8
- Team paddles
- A floor-line reminder

The team setup and the class profile should be shared with /sinif-oyunu and the other games.
catalog.delightDetails:
KIDS (OYUN PARKI)
- Balloon strings sway. A popped balloon floats up and a star flies to the team's basket at the screen edge. The pop is a soft marimba 'plip', never a bang, for noise-sensitive children.
- Aquarium fish swim into the team's bowl and blow a bubble heart. Garden moles wear tiny hats and wave before ducking.
- Gogo bobs to the rhythm on the top edge, parrots every word so the class echo has a model, and sleeps with 'zzz' on the pause screen. On a pause, the balloons also stop in mid-air.
- The class jar slowly fills with balloons. At the finale it opens, the balloons float up, and each one carries a word the class found.
- The settler 'What was on balloon 3?' recycles the round's words.

PHOTO FINISH (all skins)
A 1.5 s slow-motion replay with a soft camera flash, and both teams score.

ARENA
- A radar sweep, a lock-on reticle in the team colour, a flame on a clean streak, and a 'CLUTCH!' line when a trailing team takes a golden item.

SPOT
- Cards deal in like a dealer shuffling. Symbols wiggle a little. The winning symbol glows on both cards, joined by a line in the team colour.
- In 'Renk & sayı', the matching apples bounce together.

STÜDYO
- The slip flips over like an index card to show IPA, TR and an example.
- A quiet woodblock tick.
- Kaçırılanlar comes with 'Bu kelimelerle tekrar oyna'.

RUNNERS
- Runner tags show the seat number inside the team emblem.
- A rotation strip shows who has run, so students see it is fair.

LEARNING FEATURES DRESSED AS FUN
- 'Say it twice!' echo, 'It's a ___!' feather stars, and tribune boards that make seated teams spell the word.

KEPT AND CUT FROM THE RAW IDEAS
- Kept: the ambient 'look at me' wiggle.
- Cut: items that dodge before being hit. On a touch board they make children chase items.
catalog.risks:
PHYSICAL SAFETY
Rushing to the board, collisions, and slapping an expensive LCD board.
- Default to 'Söyle' in crowded rooms.
- 'Tahtaya dokun' allows at most 2 runners, a tape line two steps back, walk-don't-run, hands on heads until GO, and items that freeze at GO.
- Open palm only on LCD panels; foam swatters only on a projector wall.

SPEED FAVOURS CONFIDENT STUDENTS
- Strict seat rotation, buddy runs, and the private matching tiers.
- Tribune points and the class jar make seated answers count.
- There are no speed points: speed decides who scores, not how much.
- Kids get no lockout, just retries.

AMBIGUOUS ITEMS
Two valid answers on screen, synonyms, homophones, or pictures that could be read two ways (bear/teddy).
- The confusables list, the LLM uniqueness pass, the teacher preview, the curated SVG set, accept[] alternatives, and 'Bu da olur'.

ADJUDICATION
Noise and disputes over who was first.
- The item-then-team input, the generous photo-finish rule, undo, and the rule 'the teacher's call is final'.
- In 'Söyle' the runner must say the WORD, not only the number.

TTS
Missing voices or lag.
- Items stay locked until the clue finishes.
- Without an English voice, 'Öğretmen okur' uses the printed call list.

MOTION
Motion sickness and photosensitivity.
- The static grid, and the reduced-motion setting is respected.
- Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.
- The Glitch is opt-in for Arena only.

OVEREXCITEMENT IN KIDS
- The 'Hands on heads!' reset, the 45/60 s settlers, and a fixed round length.

UNEVEN TEAM SIZES
Students in small teams run more often. Show the rotation strip.

SMALL GENERATED PACKS
The validator tops the pack up from the nearest built-in topic.

12-13-YEAR-OLDS
They reject cartoon visuals. Arena is auto-suggested for grade 6+, and the group label is never shown.

issues: WHOLE-CLASS RESPONSE LEAKS THE ANSWER. In Oyun Parkı, seated students point at the item or show fingers 'on GO', at the same moment the runners race. The fastest pointers therefore give the answer to their runner. With 14 kids per half, the race becomes 'who copies the loudest teammate', which defeats the seat rotation and the fairness design.

ADJUDICATION IN 'SÖYLE' IS UNREALISTIC WITH 28 KIDS. Up to 4 runners shout 'Seven, giraffe!' at once while 24 seated kids also call out. The teacher cannot reliably hear who was first, who said the right number, or whether the word matched. The 1 s photo-finish window hides this with 2 teams but not with 3-4. Disputes ('We said it first!') will happen on most clues and cost 10-20 s each.

SPAM GUESSING IN KIDS MODE. There is no lockout and only 6 items. A runner in 'Söyle' can call 'One! Three! Five!' faster than the teacher can reject each call, and the 2 s dizzy wobble only works if the teacher logs every wrong call. Most calls go unlogged, so the kid who guesses fastest wins, not the kid who listened best.

TEACHER INPUT CONFLICTS WITH TEACHER POSITION. Q/W/E/R, U, H, L and Space need the laptop. 'Tahtaya dokun' and classroom management need the teacher at the board or walking the aisles. No remote or on-screen control bar is specified, so the teacher shuttles between desk and board on every clue. The flow is item click, then team key, plus undo, plus 'Sınıf ✓' on every clue: 3-4 inputs per clue, about 30 inputs per round, under noise.

SEAT-NUMBER LOGISTICS ARE UNDERESTIMATED. 'Fox #5' only works if every child knows their team AND their per-team seat number. In a public school with rows of pairs, absentees and kids swapping seats, first-time setup takes 5-8 minutes: numbering, printing tags, entering absent seats. That is not 60 s. After that the classes move rooms or seats change.

PROXIMITY UNFAIRNESS IN 'TAHTAYA DOKUN'. A back-row runner in a narrow Turkish classroom walks 6-10 m past bags and desks, while a front-row runner takes 2 steps. The rule 'Items freeze at GO' does not fix this. Walk-don't-run makes the gap bigger.

TOUCH-BOARD HARDWARE REALITY. Many MEB FATİH boards register multi-touch badly or treat a palm as several touches. Two kids touching at once can pop the wrong item. After a pop, both runners are right there and either one can tap the team colour chip. The disputed chip tap will cause arguments.

MINI-WHITEBOARDS ARE AN ASSUMPTION. Most Turkish public-school classes don't have a set of them. Checking 3 team boards for +1 each clue adds 5-10 s of teacher reading per clue, and 'Sınıf ✓' ('most of the class got it') is a subjective call the teacher has to make 30 times.

SPOT READABILITY AT DISTANCE. Two cards of k=8 word symbols with rotation and size variance, at a 4.5vh floor, are hard to read from the back row of a 9 m classroom with a washed-out projector. Merkez Kart puts 4 team cards plus a centre card (about 21 symbols) on one screen. That fails outright on a typical 2.5 m projection.

HIZLI SERİ SPOTLIGHTS ONE STUDENT. One runner faces 5 clues in a row in front of peers, with the whole match riding on it and an optional wager for adults. For shy 12-14 year-olds this is the anxiety moment the rest of the design works hard to avoid. A weak runner drawn by the spinner can lose the match for the team, which feels unfair.

SCORING SCALE BUGS. In Arena, a +3 win with ×1.5 gives 4.5 points, so fractions appear on screen. The ×2 combo at a 5-streak rewards the team that is already winning, which works against the Slipstream comeback. 'Steal 5' is on a different scale from +3/+1. A team that falls behind in a 2-team kids game has no visible way back beyond +1.

NO 'STOP NOW' PATH. Rounds are fixed at 8-12 clues and there is a finale sequence. When the bell rings mid-round or the principal walks in, the teacher needs one tap to go to the finale and save the Kaçırılanlar list, and the design never states this.

TEACHER SETUP OVERLOAD. The controls list has about 40 settings: recipe, race style, motion, skins, clue mix, delays, wrong-call rule, hint steps, harshness, comeback, glitch, tiers, buddy seats. It will intimidate a teacher who has 3 minutes of break between lessons. The summary line helps, but the preview-and-edit step for LLM packs adds another 1-2 minutes.

SCOPE. Three modes plus Merkez Kart, Çapraz, Renk & sayı, 3 skins × 3 item skins, power cards, photo-finish replay, Glitch, tiers and printables make this an XL build. The core loop (Avla! in Söyle mode with rotation) risks shipping late or unpolished.

ADULT FIT. With 10 adults (2-3 teams of 3-5), each adult runs roughly every third or fourth clue and sits idle in between, apart from pair jotting. The racing is a good 5-8 minute warmer, but a 20-30 minute adult match drags. Adults also tend to call answers out of turn, which breaks the runner rule.
fixes: SEQUENCE THE WHOLE-CLASS RESPONSE. Keep seated students on 'Hands on heads / lips zipped' until the award. The class then points and echoes AFTER the find (the 'Say it twice' moment). In Arena, boards go up after the award too, and they score only if the board was written before GO+3 s (the teacher says 'pens down'). Any seated call-out during the race gives the point to the other team. That is one rule, shown as a pictogram.

DEFAULT TO 2-TEAM DUELS IN 'SÖYLE' FOR LARGE CLASSES. With more than 20 students, use 2 runners per clue even in Söyle, rotating team pairings. Show the runners' seat tags big on screen so the teacher listens to exactly 2 voices. Add a 'Numarayla' kids option where the runner holds up a number card instead of shouting, so the teacher can judge first visually.

ONE ANSWER PER RUNNER PER CLUE IN KIDS MODE. Replace unlimited retries with 'one wrong call → Gogo gives you a hint card, then one more try'. That is 2 attempts, which stops spam guessing and is still not elimination. If both runners miss twice, Gogo reveals it and both get an effort star.

TEACHER REMOTE. Add a phone remote page (a QR code on the setup screen, same session) with big team buttons, undo, next, hint and pause. Also add a thin on-screen control rail at board height for smart boards, and simplify the award to one tap: the team chip on the winning item. Drop the per-clue 'Sınıf ✓' in kids mode, or make it an automatic jar balloon on every 3rd clue.

SEATLESS RUNNER PICKING. Offer 'isim kartı yok' mode: the spinner shows a team-coloured number that matches printed numbered lanyards or desk stickers, handed out once and kept in the class profile. Or offer an 'el kaldıran değil, sıradaki' row-based rotation (row 1 left seat, row 1 right seat ...) that needs no numbering. Target a real setup time of 2 minutes the first time and 20 s after that.

EQUALISE DISTANCE IN 'TAHTAYA DOKUN'. The next duel's runners walk up during the current reveal and wait at the tape line, so every race starts from the line. State this rule plainly: 'Sıradaki koşucular çizgide bekler.'

TOUCH SAFEGUARDS. After a touch pops an item, show the team chip for the runner who stands on that side (left and right halves of the board are assigned per team). Or let the teacher confirm with the remote. Offer a 'dokunmatik güvenilmez' toggle that makes the board display-only while the teacher inputs.

MAKE TRIBUNE BOARDS OPTIONAL. The Arena default is 'fingers/number cards' for A levels. Mini-whiteboards are an opt-in, and printable A4 dry-erase sleeves can stand in for them. Score tribune answers per team with one tap ('Tribün ✓'), not per board.

SPOT PROJECTION LIMITS. Cap k by a measured 'room size' setup question (small/medium/large). Large rooms get k≤6 and pictures, words at a 6vh minimum. Merkez Kart is allowed only on screens flagged as large or with at most 2-3 teams, where it shows one team card at a time in turn.
RECAST HIZLI SERİ AS A TEAM RELAY. The 5 clues go to 5 different teammates in rotation. Or allow a 'buddy' pair. The wager is Stüdyo-only and capped at a third of the score.

FIX THE SCORING. Arena: win +2, tribune +1, streak bonus +1 flat at 3 and at 5 (whole numbers, not multipliers). Steal cards take 2 points, capped. Comeback 'Light' applies from the start of round 2. Kids: stars only, and the finale shows titles rather than ranks. Keep 'speed decides who, not how much'.
ALWAYS-AVAILABLE 'BİTİR' BUTTON. It jumps straight to the finale (under 20 s) and auto-saves the Kaçırılanlar list and the rotation state, so the next lesson resumes the rotation where it left off.

THREE PRESETS PLUS 'GELİŞMİŞ'. Setup opens on three presets: 'Hızlı ısınma 5 dk', 'Sınıf maçı 15 dk' and 'Tahta düellosu'. All other dials sit behind 'Gelişmiş'. LLM packs show a 10-item quick preview with only the flagged items expanded.

PHASE THE BUILD. v1: Avla! in Söyle and Masadan modes, 2 skins (kids balloons, Arena radar; Stüdyo as a theme of Arena), rotation, auto-hints, undo, finale and Kaçırılanlar. v2: Eşini Bul! plus Çapraz. v3: Merkez Kart, power cards, Glitch, Renk & sayı, photo-finish replay.

ADULTS. Position Stüdyo as a 5-10 minute warmer by default. In the full match, make every clue a race for all teams at once in 'Masadan' mode, where each team writes the answer on paper and the first raised paddle is checked, so all 10 adults are active on every clue instead of 1 runner per team.

issues: Best fit is A1-A2 young learners. Listen-and-point to a picture needs no reading and has real listening value. The fit gets steadily worse at higher levels: for B2 adults, recognising one word on a floating slip is well below their level and feels like a warmer at best. Only the error, collocation and register clues are B2-worthy, and the default clue mix does not make them the default.

The kids' 'dizzy retry, nobody out' rule turns into brute force. With 6 items and unlimited retries after 2 s, a runner who does not know the answer can tap or call items until one is right, and still wins a star over a runner who hesitated. Speed plus retries rewards guessing, not listening.

In 'Söyle' mode with 2-4 teams all calling at once ('Seven, giraffe!'), the teacher has to judge who was first and whether the word was said, in a noisy room of 30 or more children. Pressing the item and then the team key is fast for one call but not for two nearly simultaneous calls. The rule '2 team keys within 1 s = photo finish' depends on the teacher's keyboard speed, not on the students, so ties will be recorded wrongly or missed.

The language output per clue is thin. At A levels the whole tribune answers by number or pointing (no English). The runner says one word. The only production for everyone is the choral echo. For adults and B-level teens, most clue types produce recognition, not recall. Eşini Bul! with word-only cards (adult 'mixed typefaces, 30° rotation', look-alikes) is mainly a visual-search test: the hard part is scanning, not language.

Moving text hurts readers. Floating or drifting sentence items (error spotting with 4-6 sentences, gap options) at a 4.5-5vh font floor on a projector are hard to read while they move, and the reading-speed gap between students decides the winner. A1 adults, who read slowly in English, are hit hardest.

Some clue types don't suit their groups. Word ↔ IPA Spot for B2 Genç is wrong, because Turkish 12-13-year-olds are not taught IPA. 'Rhymes with BEAR' and stress-pattern clues for kids depend on TTS producing an isolated word clearly. The minimal-pair clue ('ship' vs sheep/chip/cheap) depends on browser TTS vowel quality, which is unreliable for single isolated words, especially at 0.8x.
Relation clues for A2 Genç ('past of GO', 'opposite of HOT') are meta-language that 9-10-year-olds may not know in English, and they add reading. They need a pictogram or Turkish frame.

The LLM path is weak for the groups that need it most. A1/A2 Genç require a picture on every item, but the LLM can only choose emoji or keys from a curated SVG set. A teacher prompt like 'my town, places, directions' or 'MEB 5. sınıf Unit 4 daily routines' produces many unpicturable items, which get dropped. The top-up from the 'nearest built-in topic' then silently swaps in off-topic words, so the teacher gets a different lesson than they asked for.
'Renk & sayı' ('two red apples') needs tinted SVGs and counted items, which is a content-art dependency the LLM cannot supply. It is only viable with built-in art.

Teacher setup is too complex for a quick warmer. There are 3 modes, 3 race styles, 8+ clue types, hint ladders per skin, power-card harshness, comeback, glitch, tiers and printables. The one-line summary helps, but the clue-type mix per level is where teachers will get it wrong, for example by leaving IPA or register clues on for a teen group.
In Arena, B-level tribune boards write the word while A-level boards write the number, so a 13-year-old A1 class spends the tribune time writing digits, with no language practice.

Adult appeal: slap-the-board plus power cards and golden items can feel juvenile to B2 professionals unless it is framed as a short 5-8 minute review warmer. As a 20-30 minute 'full match' it will outstay its welcome for adults.
fixes: Stop the kids' brute force. Allow a retry only after every other racing team has had one attempt, or cap it at 2 attempts per runner per clue. On a wrong item, that item turns grey for that runner. If the runner guesses more than 2 items within 3 s, no star (a 'Slow down, listen!' nudge).

Default kids 'Söyle' to at most 2 racing teams per clue (a duel) plus the whole-class point-and-say. Show a big on-screen 'WHO WAS FIRST?' pair of chips for the teacher. Replace the key-timing photo finish with an explicit 'Berabere' button (B), so a tie is the teacher's decision, not their keyboard speed.

Add a production step that scales with level after every find. Kids A1: 'It's a ___!' as a whole class. A2 Genç: 'I can see a ___' or a colour + noun. B1: the winning team's next runner makes a sentence with the word within 10 s for +1. B2 adults: collocation or sentence with a register constraint. Make it on by default from B1, not an optional bonus.

Make the Durgun ızgara (static grid) the DEFAULT for any item carrying text (A1 adults and up, and all sentence items). Keep drift only for picture-only kids items. Error and gap sentences never move and never rotate.

Tier the clue mix by default and hide unfit types. No IPA and no register clues for any Genç group. Relation clues for A2 Genç come with a pictogram (a clock-back arrow for past, a see-saw for opposite) or a Turkish frame ('GO'nun geçmişi?'). Stress and minimal-pair clues are allowed for kids only if pre-recorded audio exists (not TTS). Otherwise mark them 'Öğretmen okur'.

For B1+ adults and teens, make sentence-level clue types the default (collocation gap, error sentence, word family, phrasal verb from definition). Keep single-word picture or TR clues as a Kolay option only.

Replace adult word-only Dobble with the cross-match version by default (word ↔ definition snippet, verb ↔ past, collocation halves), so the shared item must be understood, not just spotted. Keep a rotation cap of 15° for text.

LLM path: before generating, show which items can be pictured for picture-required groups. If fewer than 8 remain, ask the teacher ('Resimsiz öğeler çıkarıldı: 11/20. Kelime etiketiyle oyna / yerleşik konudan tamamla?') instead of topping up silently. Any topped-up item is visibly tagged in the preview.
In Arena with A-levels, the tribune writes the WORD with its first letter given (a scaffolded spelling), or picks from a Turkish-to-English printed strip, never a bare number.
Ship a 'Hızlı başla' preset per group (clue mix, mode recipe, race style chosen) with one toggle row. Move tiers, glitch, harshness and comeback into an 'Gelişmiş' drawer.

For Stüdyo, frame the default as a 6-10 minute review warmer that ends with Kaçırılanlar. Make the 30-minute match opt-in, and drop golden items and power cards by default for adults unless the teacher turns them on.
Build a curated SVG and emoji set mapped to the YLE and MEB grade 2-8 word lists first, because this game's kids version is only as good as its picture coverage.

issues: Scope is XL, not L. As specced this is two games in one (Avla! and Eşini Bul!), plus Hızlı Seri, Merkez Kart, Çapraz, Renk & sayı, 6+ item skins (balloon, aquarium, garden, radar, slips, luggage tags), 3 audience skins, power cards in 3 harshness tiers, comeback modes, Glitch, class jar, album, stirrers and settlers, a slow-motion replay, a seat-tier matcher and printables. That is realistically 7-9k LOC plus a large art set. The polish will spread thin and the result will feel like a settings panel with a game attached.

'Photo finish' and its 1.5 s slow-motion replay are fake. In every race style except a true touch duel, the game only knows when the TEACHER pressed the keys. Pressing two team keys within 1 s measures the teacher's reflexes, not the runners, and there is nothing to replay. Students will notice it replays the teacher's clicks.

Touch mode cannot attribute a touch to a team. With one shared field, 'item pops, then the runner taps their colour chip' lets either runner claim it, and the second runner's touch lands on a popped item. Many Turkish FATİH boards are IR-frame boards with weak multitouch, and on a projector wall with foam swatters there is no input at all. So the flagship 'slap the board' mode silently falls back to teacher judgment.

In 'Söyle' with every team racing on every clue, 30-40 students shout at once in a loud room. Deciding who was first rests entirely on the teacher's ear. The game adds adjudication UI but no real adjudication, which is where disputes will come from.

Item-then-team input (click item, then Q/W/E/R) costs about 1.5-2 s per award and assumes a keyboard. At a smartboard there is no keyboard, and typing two digits within 0.5 s is fragile on touch. The 'teacher enters item first' step is also redundant in Söyle mode, where the target is known and the only real question is which team.

Riddle clues contradict the lock rule. If items stay locked until the whole clue has been read (3 parts × 4 s + the options delay), a riddle round is roughly 15 s of waiting, and the 'guess early on hard-to-easy clues' tension riddles exist for is gone.

Floating sentences (error / gap / mcq rounds) are unreadable while they move on a projector at 4.5-5vh, and 4-6 sentences cannot drift without overlapping. Those rounds are also just an MCQ with moving options, which duplicates every quiz candidate and dilutes this game's identity (a fast find-the-word hunt).

Relying on emoji for pictures is a real risk. School boards run Pardus/Linux or old Windows, where colour emoji are missing or look inconsistent. 'Renk & sayı' needs recolourable monochrome SVGs. The kids' A1/A2 versions depend on a consistent curated picture set of about 300-500 icons, and that asset is not budgeted.

TTS risk is underplayed. Web Speech often has no en-US/en-GB voice on Pardus/Chromium boards, and minimal-pair rounds (ship/sheep, full/fool) make no sense with a poor or robotic voice. 'Öğretmen okur' with a printed call list breaks the seeded screen order the moment the teacher skips or undoes something.

LLM uniqueness is the hardest content problem, and it is only described vaguely. The on-screen set is built at runtime, so a per-screen 'could another item answer this?' pass can't run at game time. Without a precomputed conflict matrix, the teacher preview cannot show real conflicts. Relation clues ('means BIG', 'the noun of DECIDE') and category clues are exactly where an LLM produces two valid answers.

The setup and teacher controls are too many for a 60 s setup: about 40 toggles. Even a detail-loving teacher won't configure them in a live lesson, and the defaults will do all the work, so most of these controls are dead weight to build and test.
Performance on weak board PCs: 16 drifting SVG items with sway, shadows, blur (Glitch), particle stars and a radar sweep can drop frames on low-end hardware. Janky balloons read as cheap.

Some of this duplicates other likely candidates. Eşini Bul! overlaps Memory/Match and Bingo on the 'pair' type, and the Hızlı Seri wager overlaps the Jeopardy/Millionaire finales. The unique core is Avla! (the listen-and-find swat race) and the Dobble-style twin spot.
Dobble with words and no pictures (adult Spot) is mostly a visual word search. Look-alike decoys make it harder, but it is weaker than the picture version and may feel like homework.
fixes: Ship in phases. MVP (size L, about 3k LOC): Avla! with 3 skins (one item skin per audience: balloons, radar blips, paper slips), Eşini Bul! as the second round type (picture and word cards, plus cross-match only for tr/emoji/past), the rotation strip, echo, hints, and scoring as specced. v2: Merkez Kart, Hızlı Seri with wager, power cards, and the extra item skins (aquarium, garden, luggage tags). Cut Glitch, the seat tiers and the album from v1.

Make the touch duel real with a mirrored split screen. In 'Tahtaya dokun', the left half belongs to team A and the right half to team B, each with the same items in a different shuffled layout. The first correct touch on your own half wins and the touch time is recorded. This gives true photo-finish detection (touches within 150 ms) and an honest replay of the recorded touch points. For projector walls with foam swatters, label the mode 'Öğretmen hakem' and drop the replay.

Replace the fake photo finish in Söyle/Masadan with an explicit 'Berabere' button (both teams score) and a short tie sting, with no slow motion. Keep the slow-motion replay only where real touch timestamps exist.

Invert the input when the target is known: the game already knows the right item, so the teacher only presses the team (a big on-screen chip or Q/W/E/R). Clicking an item is needed only to mark a WRONG call ('which did they say?') or 'Bu da olur'. Add a docked, auto-hiding control bar with big team chips for smartboards. Drop the two-digit typing timing and use a numeric keypad popover instead.

Change Söyle so it cannot become a shouting match. Race 2 teams per clue on a round-robin, with the other teams on tribune boards, or run 'paddle first, then speak' (Masadan): the first paddle up gets the call and the teacher taps that team. Say in the rule card that the teacher's call is final.
Unlock riddles after part 1, while parts 2 and 3 keep arriving, and give points for early correct calls in the kids' star currency only as a feather bonus. Or move riddles out of Avla! entirely.

Show all sentence content (error, gap, mcq) as a static 2×2 or 2×3 grid of slips that settles on GO, never drifting. Limit gap/mcq rounds to single-word answers so the game stays a word hunt and does not become a moving quiz.

Budget a picture asset set: a self-hosted, licensed SVG subset (OpenMoji CC BY-SA or Twemoji CC BY 4.0, with credits) of about 400 YLE/MEB concepts, one sprite sheet with monochrome variants for 'Renk & sayı'. Never depend on system emoji. Map words.js lemmas to imageKeys so built-in and LLM packs share the same pictures.

Improve TTS. At build time, pre-generate MP3/OGG audio for the built-in packs' words and the minimal-pair sets, served from a CDN or Supabase Storage and lazy-loaded per pack. Use Web Speech only as a fallback for LLM packs. Test for an English voice at setup, and hide sound and minimal-pair clue types when none is available. Make 'Öğretmen okur' show the next clue on a presenter/phone view, or as a small hidden-until-hover strip, instead of a printed list that falls out of sync.

Handle uniqueness once per pack. The LLM returns, for every item and every clue kind, 'otherItemsThatAlsoFit: [ids]'. Code merges this with deterministic checks (same imageKey, category co-membership, words.js alt forms, a homophone list) into a conflict matrix. The runtime screen picker samples fillers only from non-conflicting items, and the teacher preview lists the conflict pairs with a one-click fix (remove the clue or remove the item). Validate the JSON schema strictly (Zod), clamp word caps in code, and drop items whose CEFR band from words.js is above the group.

Collapse setup to the summary line plus 3 visible choices: recipe, race style, teams. Everything else goes behind 'Gelişmiş' and is saved per class profile. Share the team, profile and seat-rotation module with /sinif-oyunu (game-classroom.mjs) rather than building new ones.

For polish on weak hardware, use one SVG layer moved with CSS transforms (translate3d), no animated filters or box-shadows, and at most 12 items for kids and 12 for Arena at 16:9. Keep a 'Durgun ızgara' fallback that triggers automatically when frames drop below 40 fps. Synthesize the ~15 SFX with WebAudio (marimba plip, woodblock, chime, boing) so there are no audio asset downloads.

Make adult Spot mainly cross-match (word ↔ TR / past / IPA / idiom half) rather than word ↔ same word, and position adult Avla! as a 5-8 minute warmer by default. The adult fit depends on Rapid Recall being brisk and understated.

Add real QA: a seeded deterministic mode, so the call list and the replays of a match are reproducible, and a headless test that generates 500 random screens per built-in pack and asserts that every screen has exactly one valid answer and every Spot pair has exactly one shared symbol.

catalog.rankReason: Slap the board / balloon pop (teen 8.3), excellent listening for A1-A2 kids but thin for adults (6). First game of the next wave. It needs a real mirrored split-screen touch duel instead of the fake key-timing photo finish, and 2-team duels in Söyle for large classes. Seated students stay 'hands on heads' until the award, and retries are capped. MVP: Avla! with one item skin per audience, and Eşini Bul! as round 2.

catalog.name: Cümle Mezadı (Grammar Auction)
catalog.familiarAs: Grammar Auction (classic ELT game; Languago roadmap G06)
catalog.oneLiner: Teams spend a budget on sentences they think are correct. After the gavel falls, the forgeries are exposed, and teams earn value back by fixing them. The lots are built automatically from Languago's grammar MCQ banks: the stem plus the key is an original, and the stem plus a learner-error distractor is a forgery. This makes it the suite's error-correction and confidence-calibration game.
catalog.howItPlays:
CORE LOOP (the same spine in all three skins; the skins change the rules, see the adult and teen fields).
0 SETUP (teacher, 1-2 min, before class). Pick the group chip. The summary line reads, for example, 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · Canlı mezat · 12 lot · 30 dk'. Then pick the content: grammar units (multi-select, 'Son 3 üniteyi karıştır'), a built-in category ('Past simple irregulars', 'Present perfect vs past', 'Comparatives', 'Conditionals', 'Articles & quantifiers'), an existing pack, or a free-text prompt such as '6. sınıf, past simple düzensiz fiiller, futbol temalı'. The engine builds the lots and opens the LOT LIST. Each row shows the sentence exactly as the class will see it, O/X, the fix, the Turkish why and the source. The teacher can edit a lot, flip it (original <-> forgery), swap the distractor, reorder, regenerate, or tap 'Emin değilim'. That button removes the lot and denylists that stem plus distractor for good. Optional printouts: team paddles (colour, emblem or mascot, number), one lot catalogue per team, 0-3 coin fans for kids, and the teacher's auctioneer phrase card.
1 PRACTICE LOT (unscored, 20-30 s). One original and one forgery, demoed by Gogo (kids), by a 'Warm-up lot' (Arena) or as 'Lot 0' by the teacher (adults).
2 CATALOGUE PREVIEW (Stüdyo 2-3 min, Arena 90 s, none for Oyun Parkı). All lots appear in a numbered list. Teams whisper and write a tick or cross and a maximum price on their printed catalogue (adults consult in pairs).
3 EACH LOT. The lot card slides in (onto an easel, a market stall or as a card drop). Every lot has a speaker button; A1/A2 Genç get automatic read-aloud at 0.8x. There is an individual prediction first, then Team talk (10/15/20 s), then 'Boards up!'. How teams bid depends on the mode:
- LIVE (adult default): the opening bid is 100 and raises are 50. A team raises its paddle and calls the amount in English. The teacher taps that team's paddle button (+step) or types the amount. A 10 s 'Going once... going twice...' strip restarts on every new bid. Then the gavel: 'SOLD to The Espressos for 350!'.
- SEALED (Arena default, adult option): every team writes its bid on a mini-whiteboard and all boards go up together. The highest bid owns the lot. A tie gets one overtime raise; if teams are still tied, the lot is shared (each pays, each gets its value).
- SHELLS (Oyun Parkı): coin cards 0-3; every team that pays gets its own copy.
The wallet updates instantly. A team can never bid more than its wallet or hold more lots than the cap, ceil(lots/teams)+1. Unsold lots go to the storeroom (Depo, or Gogo's bag for kids).
4 CLASS VOTE before every reveal, as a whole-class response: thumbs up or down (adults, can be switched off), VALID/GLITCH on the boards (Arena), stand for Treasure and sit for Trap (kids).
5 REVEAL. After each lot in Park and Arena. In Stüdyo it comes at the end by default, as the 'Ekspertiz' (appraisal), so that early reveals don't hint at later lots. Originals get a gold frame or a shine badge. Forgeries crack exactly at the error span.
6 FIX (the teaching moment). The owner commits its fix first: the spokesperson or spinner seat says it, or the team holds up its board. While that happens, every other team writes its own fix. The teacher then taps 'Show fix'. The right words are inked over the struck-through span, with any alsoOk repairs listed, and the teacher taps tick or cross for the owner. Fixes that change the meaning don't count. If the owner misses, every other team with a correct board gets the open-restoration/steal bonus, and the owner loses nothing more. The one-line rule appears (whyTr of 90 chars or fewer; whyEn at B levels), and the class says the correct sentence together (twice with kids).
7 SALVAGE (Stüdyo and Arena). Unsold forgeries come up in a quick batch; all teams write fixes at once, and each correct fix is worth +50. Unsold originals get a 'Nobody trusted this one!' beat: why did it look wrong?
8 FINALE. A collection screen (framed paintings, a trading-card binder or a treasure chest), awards, the calibration report and 'Kaçırılanlar'.
SCORING (one idea behind every skin). Each team has two counters. The WALLET is spending money, so it only goes down (except for gifts). The SCORE only ever goes up:
- An original is worth 2x the price paid.
- A fixed forgery is worth 1x the price (the money comes back as value).
- An unfixed forgery is worth 0.
Unspent money scores nothing and only breaks ties. That kills the 'buy nothing and keep 1000' exploit, and it makes the bid size express how confident the team is (the G06 calibration goal). Brakes: the lot cap, and Comeback Light (the trailing team picks the next lot from the catalogue; +50 Slipstream when the last team fixes a forgery). The classic tekhnologic scoring is available as an option, 'Cümle puanı': 1 point per original or fixed forgery, with money left as the tiebreak. There are no speed points anywhere. Nobody is picked by name: kids and Arena use the seat-number spinner, and in adult classes the paddle holder is the spokesperson (the paddle passes left after every lot).
catalog.playerSetup: 2-6 teams (4 is ideal) of 3-6 students. In crowded state-school classes of 30-36, use 6 teams of 5-6. One projector, with the teacher at the laptop (keyboard or touch). Each team gets a printed paddle (team colour plus a shape emblem or a kids' mascot, and the team number) and a mini-whiteboard or A4 paper with a marker. Kids also get a 0-3 coin fan (or use fingers). Seats in each team are numbered 1-6 for the spinner. Adults consult in pairs during the catalogue preview and rotate the spokesperson with the paddle.
catalog.contentShape:
LOT (built at run time; one lot per stem, so a game never shows both versions of the same stem): {lotNo, show ('original'|'forgery'), text (what the class sees), right, wrong?, span [start,end) of the slot in the shown text, fixes (right plus alsoOk[], e.g. "She's lived" / "She has lived"; at B1+ also a different valid repair such as changing the time word), errorType (from the error-item list), target (e.g. 'present perfect vs past simple'), unit ('b1-01'), whyTr (90 chars or fewer), whyEn?
