(B groups), media.emoji or imageKey (required in A1/A2 Genç, where the picture can be the evidence: two cats vs 'two cat'), diff (1-3), ctx? (a two-line dialogue for B2 near-miss lots), fixBank[2-3]? (kids and A groups: the right word, the distractor and one more), source ('mcq'|'gap'|'tf'|'error'|'llm')}. The slot sits in the same place in both versions, so underlining it never gives the answer away.
SOURCES:
(1) grammar_mcq_* (built-in). The original is q with ___ replaced by options[a]. The forgery is q with options[k≠a], where k is the most typical learner error. whyTr is why[k] when it is specific. The generic pattern "'X' seçeneği bu cümle için gramer açısından uygun değil" is detected by regex and replaced with the unit's rule line from grammar_*.js, or with an LLM rule card cached per unit and distractor, which the teacher can edit. Meta stems whose options are whole sentences ('Which present perfect form is correct?') give lots directly: the key is an original and the distractors are forgeries. Two-blank stems, stems over the word cap and stems outside the word band are skipped.
(2) gap items: answers[0] versus bank minus answers.
(3) tf items with about='sentence-correct' and a fix. The span is computed by diff, and the item is dropped unless the difference is one contiguous chunk of 3 tokens or fewer (5 for B2 word order).
(4) error items from packs or the LLM: {wrong, right, span, errorType, whyTr, unit?}, for example {"wrong":"Our team winned the match yesterday.","right":"Our team won the match yesterday.","span":[9,15],"errorType":"tense","target":"past simple irregular","whyTr":"win düzensizdir: geçmiş hali won."}.
VALIDATION:
- Exactly one error, and the right version passes an LLM grammaticality check.
- A forgery is rejected if ANY reading of it is grammatical. For example, 'I ___ tired' with 'was' instead of 'am' is rejected; a tense swap with no time anchor is rejected.
- Word caps: A1 Genç 4, A2 Genç 8, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40 (sentences are normally 20 words or fewer). A words.js band check applies too.
- For Genç groups: the teenSafe filter (no boss, salary, smoking, alcohol or dating), and only syllabus modules tagged primary/middle essential or recommended in cefr_grammar_syllabus.json.
- Mix: 30-60% forgeries (default 50), never more than 3 originals or 3 forgeries in a row, at least 3 errorTypes in a mixed set, and capital or spelling errors only when the teacher targets them.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'The Auction House' (Mezat Evi).
LOOK: an editorial quiz-night auction catalogue. Cream paper (or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme), serif lot numbers, each sentence hung on an easel as a small painting, a wooden gavel, woodblock and piano sounds, and a prompt font of at least 4.5vh. There is no mascot and no voice line, just a neutral caption: 'Lot 7 of 12 · Past vs Present Perfect'. The theme is originals versus forgeries. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').
RULES:
- Budget 1000; 12 lots (8-10 at A1); lot cap 4.
- A 2-3 min catalogue preview with the printed catalogues.
- LIVE auction: opening bid 100, raises of 50 (100 at A1-A2 to keep the numbers easy), and a 10 s going-once strip that restarts on every bid.
- Bids must be called in English. If a team calls one in Turkish, the teacher just waits: 'In English, please?'.
- Following the no-voice dial, the teacher is the auctioneer, reading from an on-screen phrase strip: 'Do I hear three hundred?', 'Any advance on two fifty?', 'Fair warning...', 'SOLD!'. An opt-in English TTS auctioneer is there for number listening practice. At A1-A2 the digits are also shown in words ('three hundred and fifty').
EKSPERTİZ (at the end):
- Lots flip one by one, and a loupe sweeps across each painting.
- An original gets a gold frame and pays 2x.
- A forgery cracks at the error. The paddle holder has 20 s to restore it aloud or on the board, which gets 1x the price back. A one-sentence rule explanation earns +100 in English at B1-B2, or +50 in Turkish or English at A1-A2. If the owner misses, every other team with the right fix gets +50 (open restoration).
- Then comes the Depo salvage.
- Hint ladder while restoring: rule name, then an example, then the Turkish gloss; each step lowers the refund by 10%. The Turkish gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
OPT-IN SPICE (Harshness Yellow/Red):
- Final lot: the last original pays 3x; on by default at B1-B2.
- All-in, once per game: the whole wallet on one lot; an original pays 2.5x.
- Sealed envelope bids.
- Flash lot (B2): the sentence shows for 5 s, then only its number.
- Audio lot: heard, not seen.
- Forgery penalty (Red, off by default): an unrestored forgery takes 25% of its price off the score.
ENDING: the scores roll up with a 0.6 s chime. Each team has a Collection wall: gold-framed originals, restored forgeries with a small brass 'Restored' plaque, and unrestored ones stamped FORGERY. The awards are Best Investor (best value-to-price ratio), Keen Eye and Master Restorer. The Güven karnesi shows each team's average price for originals against forgeries ('You paid 310 for originals and 140 for forgeries: well calibrated'). 'Kaçırılanlar' lists every forgery with its fix and rule, plus the originals nobody trusted, and exports as a Fix-it worksheet or a Languago practice set. Teacher chrome is in Turkish; the student screen is in English.
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (9-11; the default for A1/A2 Genç): 'Treasure or Trap?' Gogo the parrot runs a sentence stall at a friendly island market (no swords, no cannons).
LOOK: cream background, warm bright colours, rounded cards, an Andika-type font at 6vh or more, and team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit). Every lot is a short picture sentence, such as 'The cat is under the table' with cat and table stickers. At A1 the picture is the evidence: 'Look! One cat or two cats?'. Gogo reads each sentence twice at 0.8x.
THREE RULES (Turkish rule card plus pictograms, 20 s):
1) Treasure or Trap? Everybody stands for Treasure and sits for Trap. After 10 s of team talk, each team shows a coin card with 0, 1, 2 or 3 coins.
2) Treasure: your coins turn into double gems (1 coin = 2 gems).
3) Trap: every team fixes it together, and a right fix = 1 gem.
DETAILS:
- 10 coins in a pouch. Bids are only 0-3 and the app does the counting.
- Every paying team gets its own copy, so there is no bidding war, no ties and no rich team buying everything.
- Reveal after every lot. Treasure: the card gets a 'Shiny sentence!' badge, gems pop into the chest, and the class says the sentence twice with Gogo.
- Trap: a cheeky crab holds up the wrong word. After 3-4 s, 2 fix cards (A1) or 3 (A2) appear, numbered and coded by colour and shape, and teams hold up fingers. The seat spinner picks who shows.
- If a team is wrong: a soft 'boing', a free hint (picture, then first letter, then listen again) and a second try. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album. The crab happily swaps the word and scuttles away.
- Gems never go down; coins are only spending money.
PACING: 3 voyages (islands on a sea map) of 2-3 lots each. Between voyages come a 45 s 'Gogo says' stirrer (quick stand/sit sentences, unscored) and 'Gogo's Gift': +2 coins for every team, and a picture rescue question worth 2 coins for any team at 0. The timer is off by default (a calm 40 s ring when on). 6-9 lots, 15-25 min.
ENDING: every team gets a title (Treasure Hunters, Super Fixers, Brave Buyers, Careful Captains, Sharp Eyes), the chest opens, confetti falls in team colours and shapes, and the class album gets a 'Treasure Map' sticker.
Kids checklist: 3 rules, pictograms, no elimination, nothing below zero, a whole-class vote plus a shared fix or choral repeat every turn, and non-violent failure imagery. It passes.

ARENA (12-14; the default for B1/B2 Genç and suggested for any Genç class in grades 6-8): the 'Glitch Market' Challenge.
LOOK: dark navy and charcoal, neon team colours, a condensed display font at 5vh or more, and short synth blips. Sentences drop as holographic trading cards. Wrong ones are GLITCH cards, where the error word flickers with an RGB split; fixes get stamped PATCHED. In 10 s, teams pick an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.
RULES (English rule card with a Turkish toggle):
1) On every lot, all teams write VALID or GLITCH plus a bid (0-400, in steps of 100) on their board, and the boards go up together.
2) The highest bid owns the card (a tie gets one overtime raise, then the card is shared). VALID pays 2x the bid. GLITCH: patch it in 20 s for 1x the bid. If the owner misses, every other team with the right patch steals +50, and the owner loses nothing more.
3) Every right call scores +50, with a combo of x1.5 at 3 in a row and x2 at 5 (accuracy only).
DETAILS:
- 1000 credits. Spend-or-lose: unspent credits only break ties. The score floor is zero, and the card cap is ceil(lots/teams)+1.
- A 90 s catalogue preview, then 10 lots in 3 rounds.
- A 30 s board timer in the team colour.
- A commentator strip at most once per turn ('CLEAN CALL', 'COMBO x2', 'CLUTCH PATCH', 'STEAL').
- The last lot is the 'Legendary Drop', where VALID pays 3x.
- Patch hints cost credits but never take a team below zero: Scan (highlight the slot) 50, a 50:50 two-word bank 50, a gapped example of the rule 100.
ENDING: a podium for the top 3, plus stat awards for everyone (Sharpest Eye = longest call streak, Best Investor, Patch Master, Clean Sheet = never bought a glitch, Comeback). There is never a last place.
FOR ALL GENÇ GROUPS: no all-in, wagers or double-or-nothing, and teenSafe topics only (school, sport, games, animals, holidays, science facts).
catalog.levelTuning:
A1 (adults) and A1 Genç
- Grammar: be (am/is/are), have got/has got, a/an, plural -s, this/these, can, there is/are, possessive adjectives, and in/on/under with a picture.
- Forgeries are one visible word ('She are happy', 'It's a apple', 'He can swims').
- Kids: 6 lots of 3-4 words, with a 2-card fix bank.
- Adults: 8-10 lots of 10 words or fewer. The fix is chosen from 3 options or said aloud, the Turkish why is always on, and bids go up in 100s.
- About 50% forgeries and no near-miss originals.

A2
- Grammar: present simple vs continuous, don't/doesn't, past simple regular and irregular ('goed', 'did went'), comparatives and superlatives ('more big', 'the most cheap'), much/many, going to, frequency-adverb position, object pronouns.
- Sentences of 8 words or fewer for kids and 15 or fewer for adults.
- Kids fix from a 3-card bank; adults fix aloud or on the board.
- Adults switch to raises of 50 once they are comfortable with the numbers.

B1
- Grammar: present perfect vs past simple ('I have seen him yesterday'), for/since, will vs going to, first and second conditional forms ('If it will rain'), gerund vs infinitive ('enjoy to swim', 'looking forward to see'), used to, relative who/which, simple passive.
- 10-14 words (up to 25 for adults). Fixes are written on boards.
- The explain-the-rule bonus moves to English.
- Near-miss originals appear: sentences that look wrong but are right ('Who did you go with?'). Up to 55% forgeries.

B2
- Grammar: mixed and third conditionals, wish/if only + would, reporting-verb patterns ('suggested me to apply'), passive reporting ('He is said to have left'), articles and uncountables ('the informations'), make/do collocations, inversion ('Hardly I had sat down'), causative have/get, reported speech.
- Up to 20 words, with an optional two-line context dialogue.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics, with no abstract debate and no register lots.
- Adult B2 adds Flash and Audio lots and subtler near-miss originals. Alternative repairs count, with the teacher judging.

KOLAY / ORTA / ZOR inside each group
- Kolay: the slot is softly underlined on every lot (originals too, so the underline never gives the answer away), there is always a fix bank, 40% forgeries, and the word mix sits one band lower (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words).
- Orta: one magnifier per team per round.
- Zor: no highlight, written fixes, 60% forgeries and more near-miss originals.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the grammar and the word band by one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-35 (Oyun Parkı 15-25, Arena 20-28, Stüdyo 25-35). The lesson-fit timer sizes the lot count, and 'Hızlı ekspertiz' reveals any remaining lots in one batch when time runs short.
catalog.teacherControls:
CONTENT
- Unit multi-select from grammar_a1..c1 ('Son 3 üniteyi karıştır'), built-in categories, MEB grade and unit presets for Genç groups, pack import, or a free-text prompt in Turkish or English that goes to the LLM.
- Lot count (6-16, suggested by the lesson-fit timer), forgery share (30-60%), and near-miss originals on or off (B1+).
- The lot editor: edit, flip original/forgery, swap the distractor, reorder, lock the order, regenerate, and 'Emin değilim' (remove and denylist).
- Turkish why on or off, and whyEn at B levels.

RULES
- Bid mode: Canlı, Kapalı zarf or Sabit 0-3.
- Budget, opening bid, step and lot cap.
- Scoring: Koleksiyon değeri (default) or classic Cümle puanı.
- Reveal timing: after each lot, at the end, or at half-time.
- Class vote on or off.
- Correction refund, explain bonus (and its language) and open restoration/steal, each on or off.
- Hint level: slot highlight always / once per round / off.
- Modifiers: Final lot, All-in, Flash lot, Audio lot and Forgery penalty (adults only); Comeback Off/Light/Strong.
- Timers (+10 s, Süresiz) and the auctioneer TTS on or off.

LIVE CONTROL (keyboard and touch)
- Big paddle buttons per team with +step chips.
- 1-6 selects a team, Up/Space adds a step, Down takes one back, typing digits enters an exact amount, and Enter is SOLD.
- G restarts the going-once strip, U undoes the last bid or sale ('Satışı geri al' refunds it), S skips the lot, T pauses, R reveals, and Y/N judges a fix.
- Manual score correction.
- 'Hızlı ekspertiz'.

PRINT
- Paddles, catalogues, coin fans, the auctioneer phrase card, and the Kaçırılanlar Fix-it worksheet.

PROFILE
- Everything is saved in the local class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').
catalog.delightDetails:
GAVEL AND SALE
- The gavel 'bang' drops a big SOLD stamp in the buying team's colour, and its paddle pops up.
- 'Going once... going twice...' fills three dots with three woodblock ticks, which speed up in a bidding war (3 or more raises in 10 s).
- The wallet wobbles when a bid passes half of it ('Fair warning!').

REVEALS
- Adults: a loupe sweeps the painting; a forged word gets a hairline crack, and the restoration writes the fix in ink.
- Kids: Gogo pecks the suspicious word and it wobbles, and the treasure chest lid pops open.
- Arena: GLITCH cards flicker with an RGB split, and patching them stamps PATCHED.
- Every reveal carries a one-line rule in the tone of that skin.

AROUND THE GAME
- Bids are called in English numbers (with the number in words at A1-A2), so the auction doubles as number practice.
- The trailing team 'picks the next lot from the catalogue'.
- Undo plays a reverse-gavel animation.
- The kids' sea map moves the ship island by island, and Gogo's Gift arrives as a 2 s coin rain.
- Arena shows a neon combo bar, and the team emblem pulses on a streak.

FINALE
- Collection walls: gold frames and brass 'Restored' plaques (adults), a holo card binder (Arena), or a treasure chest of shiny sentences (kids).
- The Güven karnesi calibration chart, and a 'weakest structures' strip for the teacher, grouped by errorType.
- Confetti in team colours and shapes only at the kids' finale.
- Reduced motion replaces every effect with a static stamp. Colour is never the only signal: O/X stamps and shape emblems always appear.
catalog.risks:
AMBIGUOUS FORGERIES. Some distractors are grammatical in another reading ('I was tired'). Mitigations: the adversarial LLM check, the rule list (no tense swaps without a time anchor), the teacher preview, and 'Emin değilim' with a permanent denylist.

SEVERAL VALID FIXES. Mitigations: the alsoOk list, teacher judgement, and rejecting any fix that changes the meaning.

WEAK 'WHY' TEXT. The bank holds hundreds of generic 'why' strings that teach nothing. Mitigation: regex detection and replacement with unit rule lines or cached LLM rule cards.

ABOVE-LEVEL STEMS. Some A1 stems are above level ('Do you know where my keys ___?'). Mitigation: the word caps and the words.js band check drop them.

LOUD BIDDING CHAOS. Mitigations: paddles, one call at a time, the teacher entering every bid, the sealed and shells modes, and keyboard control.

RUNAWAY RICH TEAM OR HOARDING. Mitigations: the lot cap, unspent money scoring zero, and the trailing team picking the next lot.

GAMBLING FEEL FOR MINORS. Mitigations: no wagers or all-in for Genç groups, kids get fixed 0-3 'sure-coins' and gems that never drop, and teenSafe topics.

ARITHMETIC LOAD. Mitigations: the app does all the maths, with round steps at A levels.

TIE DISPUTES. Mitigation: one overtime raise, then the lot is shared; never who was fastest.

TIME OVERRUN. Mitigations: the lesson-fit timer and 'Hızlı ekspertiz'.

TEACHER SEEING ANSWERS EARLY ON ONE SCREEN. Mitigation: teams always commit their fix before 'Show fix', and the answers appear only in the pre-class lot list.

WEAK PUBLIC-SCHOOL CLASSES. Mitigations: Kolay, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.

issues: ADULT RUN (10 adults, 3 teams, Stüdyo): about 1 min setup, 2-3 min preview, then 12 live lots at roughly 70-90 s each (team talk, calls, a going-once strip that restarts on every bid), which comes to about 17 min. Ekspertiz then needs about 60 s per lot (loupe, 20 s restore, open restoration, rule line), which is another 12 min, plus salvage and the finale. That totals 35-40 min, over the stated 25-35. More importantly, if the class runs over or the bell rings, the whole payoff is lost. The end-only reveal means you cannot stop the game at any moment.

END-ONLY REVEAL IS WEAK TEACHING. By lot 12, adults have forgotten why they bought lot 2. Twelve restorations in a row are dead time for the 2 teams that don't own the lot, and they only get a +50 open-restoration chance. The feedback comes 20+ min after the decision.

TEACHER LOAD IN LIVE MODE. The teacher is auctioneer, reading the phrase strip, entering every bid (typed amounts or +step), restarting the going-once strip, judging fixes, and judging open-restoration boards, all at once. The laptop keyboard shortcuts (1-6, Space, Enter, G, U, Y/N) tie the teacher to the desk. On a smart board they are useless, because there is no keyboard at the board.

ARENA DATA ENTRY IS HEAVY. Rule 3 (+50 per right call, with combos) means that on every lot the teacher must record every team's VALID/GLITCH call as well as the bids. For 6 teams that is up to 12 inputs per lot, plus steal ticks for 5 boards. With 28 kids waiting, each lot's scoring can take 30-60 s of dead time while the teacher walks the room reading whiteboards.

ARENA SEALED BIDS COLLAPSE TO TIES. Bids run 0-400 in steps of 100, so there are only 5 values, and confident teams will all bid 400. The overtime raise can't go above the 400 cap, so it is undefined. Many lots end up shared. That multiplies the owner fixes the teacher has to judge and blurs who the owner is for steals.
ARENA DOUBLE-COUNTS THE VOTE. The class VALID/GLITCH vote (step 4) and the call written on the boards (rule 1) are the same decision made twice, which is another 10-15 s per lot for nothing.

ARENA COMBO MULTIPLIERS (x1.5 at 3 in a row, x2 at 5) reward the team that is already strongest. With only 'Comeback Light', a weak 6th team in a mixed-ability public-school class falls hopelessly behind by round 2 and disengages. The lot cap does not limit call points.

OYUN PARKI: TWO CURRENCIES AND TWO DECISIONS PER LOT. Kids stand or sit individually, then the team agrees on 0-3 coins, while coins and gems are different things and treasure doubles. For 9-10-year-olds that is more than '3 rules in 20 s' in practice. Expect teams to spend all 10 coins by lot 3-4, because unspent coins are worthless and nothing tells them to save. After that they sit out bidding until Gogo's Gift.

OYUN PARKI TRAP FIX IS UNCLEAR FOR 6 TEAMS. 'Every team fixes it together, fingers up' is fine, but the spinner then picks one seat per team. Checking 6 finger answers, running hint ladders and second tries for each wrong team, and choral repeats twice means one trap lot can take 2-3 min. With 28 kids, the stand/sit plus choral repeat every lot gets noisy by lot 6.

ONE STRONG STUDENT CAN DOMINATE. The catalogue preview and team talk let the strongest student decide every tick and every bid, and the individual prediction is never recorded or checked. The spinner only spreads who fixes, not who decides. In adult live mode, the loudest person on the paddle drives the bidding war.

PRINT DEPENDENCY. Paddles, per-team catalogues, coin fans and phrase cards take 10+ min of prep and photocopies, which are often rationed in state schools. Mini-whiteboards for 6 teams are not a given. The design assumes print, and the no-print path is not specified.

The Stüdyo catalogue preview shows all 12 sentences at once on paper. Teams that finish early do nothing for 2 min, and the paper makes it easy to eavesdrop on another team's ticks in a small adult room (a minor issue).

Replayability depends on the bank. There are about 22 MCQs per unit and 12 lots per game, and 'one lot per stem' is per game only. Replaying the same unit next week repeats stems unless used stems are tracked in the class profile.

The session length claims ignore transition time: explaining the rules, forming teams, handing out paddles and boards. With 28 kids that is 4-6 min before lot 1, so Oyun Parkı's 15-25 min is really 25-30.
fixes: Make Stüdyo's default reveal 'every 4 lots (mini-Ekspertiz)' rather than all at the end. Keep the end-only reveal as an option. Show a persistent 'Kalan süre / kalan lot' estimate, and have 'Hızlı ekspertiz' auto-suggest itself at T-8 min so there is always a reveal before the bell.

Add a phone remote. The teacher opens a QR link on their phone and gets the paddle buttons, SOLD, undo, reveal and Y/N, so they can run the auction standing among the students. Also give the smart board a large touch control bar (team paddles along the bottom edge, an oversized SOLD button). Keep the keyboard shortcuts only as a bonus.

In live mode, automate the auctioneer role: the going-once strip runs itself after 8 s of no taps, and the phrase strip highlights the next line to read. Then the teacher's only job per bid is one tap on a team paddle.

Arena scoring entry: after 'Boards up', show a single grid. One tap per team cycles the bid (0/100/200/300/400), and a second row toggles V/G. Better still, drop per-team call points and keep only 'owner outcome plus steal', so the teacher enters about 1 bid and 1-6 steal ticks. Steal checking works as: teams hold boards up and the teacher taps the correct teams from the front, with no walking round.
Arena ties: allow bids up to 500 (or 0-1000 in steps of 100), or break ties by the fewest cards owned so far. Never share unless teams are still tied after that, so that there is one clear owner.
In Arena, merge the class vote into the board call and remove the separate step 4.

Replace Arena's streak combos with a flat +50 per right call, capped at something like 3 teams per lot. Or make the comeback 'Strong' by default for Genç: the trailing team picks the lot and gets a 1.5x refund. A 6th team must be able to catch up in the last round.

Simplify Oyun Parkı to one currency. For example, drop the gems and put coins in the chest: a Treasure returns 2x the coins, a fixed Trap returns the coins (+1). Show a coin pouch with a gentle 'save some!' nudge once coins drop below 4, or give a 3-coin refill per voyage. Remove the individual stand/sit when coin fans are in use, or keep only one of the two.

Oyun Parkı trap pacing: all teams hold up fingers at once, and the teacher taps the teams that are wrong in one screen. One shared hint and one shared retry, not per team. Choral repeat once, twice only on the final lot. Cap each trap at 60 s.

Anti-dominance: ban the spokesperson from deciding. Before team talk, each member shows thumbs up or down privately, and a rule says the team must go with the majority, or the spinner picks the decider for that lot. In adult live mode, the paddle rotates every lot and only the paddle holder may call bids.

Ship a fully no-print path as the default: on-screen catalogue, fingers for coins (0-3), A4 paper or notebooks instead of whiteboards, team colours on screen instead of printed paddles. Print should be an optional upgrade, and the setup screen should say which mode needs which materials.
Store used stems per class profile, with a 'Daha önce görülmeyenleri öncelikle' default and 'Kaçırılanlar tekrar' as a replay mode, so repeat sessions feel fresh and double as review.
Budget 3 min into the lesson-fit timer for the rules and team formation. Offer a 'Hızlı başla' that skips the practice lot and preview when the class has played before (the class profile remembers).

Adult preview: have teams mark prices on their own copy but hide the catalogue after the preview on screen. Or skip the paper catalogue and let the preview be 90 s on screen with lot numbers, to cut dead time.

issues: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the A1 Genç word cap is 4, but the flagship kids example 'The cat is under the table' has 6 words, and in/on/under-with-picture sentences need 5-6 words. At a cap of 4 the built-in A1 MCQ banks will yield almost no lots, because most stems are 6-10 words. The A1 Genç pool will be starved, or the LLM will keep drafting sentences that get rejected.

A1 GENÇ IS MOSTLY GUESSING. Grammaticality judgement is a metalinguistic skill that 9-10-year-old A1 learners barely have, and many cannot decode the sentence yet. Stand/sit votes then become social copying of the strongest reader. The picture only works as evidence for plurals and prepositions; it gives nothing for 'She are happy' or 'He can swims'. Read-aloud helps decoding but not the judgement itself.

OVEREXPOSURE TO WRONG FORMS FOR KIDS. A 50% forgery share means half of what A1/A2 children see and hear read aloud twice at 0.8x is incorrect ('Gogo reads each sentence twice'). With young learners who acquire by imitation, hearing 'She are happy' repeated before the reveal works against the input goal.

PRODUCTION IS THIN AT EVERY LEVEL. The fix is usually one token picked from a 2-3 card bank (kids, A groups), so the learning event is recognition, not production. Kids say only the choral repeat. Most spoken English from adults is bid numbers, not grammar.
10 s TEAM TALK IS TOO SHORT for A2 Genç and for A1-A2 adults to read an 8-15-word sentence, reach agreement and pick a coin value. Weak public-school classes will default to 0 or 3 at random.

ARENA IS OVERLOADED FOR 12-YEAR-OLDS. On top of a 3-rule card it adds sealed bids 0-400, a VALID/GLITCH call, a +50 accuracy score with combo multipliers x1.5/x2, steals, an overtime raise, shared cards, a lot cap, 3 hint purchases with different prices, the Legendary Drop at 3x, and spend-or-lose. That is far beyond the 20-second explanation, and it rules out an A1/A2 Genç class in grades 6-8 that is moved to Arena by the MEB-grade suggestion.

B2 GENÇ GRAMMAR LIST IS NOT AGE-SAFE. Inversion ('Hardly had I'), passive reporting ('He is said to have left'), reporting-verb patterns and wish + would are listed for B2 generally. The teenSafe/syllabus filter covers topics and module tags, but the designer text implies these structures reach 13-year-olds, where they read as abstract and adult.

STÜDYO END-OF-GAME EKSPERTİZ DELAYS FEEDBACK by 20-30 minutes. At A1-A2 adult level, learners will have forgotten why they bid on lot 3, so the fix moment loses its noticing value. Twelve restorations at 20 s each plus explanations at the end also blow the time budget.

'MOST TYPICAL LEARNER ERROR' HAS NO DATA SOURCE. The grammar_mcq banks carry options and why[] strings but no error-frequency tag, so choosing k is either arbitrary or needs an LLM call per stem. Some distractors are implausible errors no Turkish learner makes, which gives easy, non-diagnostic forgeries.

LLM PROMPT PATH IS BRITTLE AT LOW LEVELS. A Turkish prompt such as '6. sınıf futbol temalı past simple' must produce many sentences that satisfy the word cap, the band and exactly one error, and pass an adversarial 'no grammatical reading' check. An LLM checker is unreliable at exactly the tense-swap and article cases. Yield per call may be low, and the teacher preview becomes the only real safeguard.
KIDS 'BETTING' FRAME: coins in, doubled gems out is still a wager mechanic for 9-year-olds, even without all-in. Some Turkish parents or administrators may object to the 'bid your coins' framing.

BABYISHNESS RISK IS LOW FOR ADULTS (the auction-house frame is strong). The A1 adult rule set (3-option fix, Turkish why always on) is fine, but 8-10 lots of 'She are happy'-level sentences can feel trivial to false-beginner adults.
fixes: Raise the A1 Genç cap to 6 words (A2 Genç 10). Pre-compute per-group lot yield from the banks at build time, and show 'Bu seviyede X lot var' in setup.

In Oyun Parkı A1, make the default an audio-plus-picture contrast. Show the picture and Gogo says two versions ('One cat or two cats? — two cat / two cats'), and kids pick which one Gogo should keep. Restrict A1 Genç forgeries to picture-verifiable error types (plural -s, a/an, in/on/under, this/these, is/are with a picture of one vs many).

Lower the default forgery share for Genç groups to 30-40%. Never read a forgery aloud twice: read it once, and read the corrected version twice after the reveal. Keep the choral repeat on the correct form only.

Add a production step: after each fix, the owner team (B1+) or the class (A levels) produces one NEW sentence with the same structure ('Now make your own'), with an optional quick judge tick. At B levels, drop the fix bank on Orta/Zor and require a written board fix.
Set team talk defaults to 20 s for A1-A2 and all Genç groups (15 s B1+ adults), with a +10 s key.

Split Arena into 'Arena Lite' (the default when an A1/A2 Genç class is moved to Arena by grade). Lite drops combos, hint prices and the overtime raise, and uses sealed bids of 0/100/200/300 only. Keep the full Arena for B1-B2 Genç. Put the 3 rules on the card and move the extras to a 'Pro kurallar' toggle.

Add an explicit Genç grammar denylist: no inversion, passive reporting, reporting-verb patterns, wish/if only + would or mixed conditionals. B2 Genç should mean concrete-topic present perfect, conditionals 1-2, passives and relative clauses.

Make the default Stüdyo reveal at half-time for A1-A2 adults (after each block of 4 at A levels), and keep end-of-game Ekspertiz as the B1-B2 default. Use 'Hızlı ekspertiz' batch fixes for the lowest-value lots.

Add a Turkish-L1 error-type priority map per unit (e.g. article omission, 3rd-person -s, did + past, 'more big', 'since 3 years'). Use it to pick k, and fall back to a one-time cached LLM ranking per stem stored with the bank.

For LLM packs, generate error items in the {wrong, right, span, errorType} format with a constrained template per errorType and a deterministic check (single contiguous diff within the cap, band check). Run the LLM ambiguity check only as a flagger, show flagged lots in amber in the lot list, and over-generate by 1.5x.
Reframe the kids' economy as 'confidence stars' (0-3 'how sure are you?'). The app gives gems for right calls and does not show coins being spent, so there is no betting vocabulary in Oyun Parkı.

For A1 adults, add a 'Mezat Plus' content option: two-slot lots, or lots mixing A1 grammar with A2 vocabulary, so false beginners are not bored. Keep the auction-house skin, which already avoids babyishness.

issues: SCORING IS BROKEN FOR CALIBRATION. The rules are: original = 2x the price, fixed forgery = 1x the price, unspent money = 0. So every purchase scores 0 or more, and buying a forgery you can fix is pure profit. The dominant strategy is 'spend everything and max-bid every lot up to the cap', which destroys the G06 confidence-calibration goal the card claims as its reason to exist. The Güven karnesi will report calibration that the incentives never asked for. The only downside is the opt-in Red penalty.

THE KIDS SKIN IS NOT AN AUCTION. In 'Treasure or Trap?' every paying team gets its own copy for 0-3 coins, so it is a confidence-weighted true/false plus a fix. That is close to any T/F or 'Fix it' candidate, and to Kahoot-style wagers. It is defensible pedagogically, but the suite should know that the auction identity lives only in Stüdyo and Arena.

THE KIDS VARIANT HIDES ITS RULE COUNT. It is billed as 3 rules, but a single lot asks for four physical response formats (stand/sit vote, a coin card, fingers for the fix bank, the seat spinner), plus hints, a second try, effort stars, Gogo's Gift, a rescue question, voyages and a stirrer. At 9-10 that is more than the 20 s explanation budget. Coins also run out: 10 coins, bids of up to 3 and 6-9 lots, with Gift top-ups needed to paper over it.

ARENA DATA ENTRY. Every lot needs, for each of up to 6 teams, a VALID/GLITCH call plus a bid from 0 to 400, and on top of that a combo tracker, a steal and a patch. Unless the input is a very fast grid, the teacher spends 30-45 s per lot typing, and the energy dies. The spec also runs two parallel scoring systems (bid value and +50 per call with a combo multiplier), which is hard to read on a projector for 12-year-olds.

STÜDYO TIME BUDGET. 12 live lots at about 60-90 s each, plus an end Ekspertiz of 12 x (loupe + 20 s restore + open restoration + rule), plus the Depo salvage, comes to 35-45 min. The stated 25-35 is too optimistic. Batching every reveal at the end also moves the teaching moment to the last 10 minutes, where the bell will cut it off.

LOT GENERATION FROM THE MCQ BANKS IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS. The 'most typical learner error' distractor has no data behind it: many distractors are not learner errors (for example 'ago'/'during' in for/since items). Some forgeries are borderline-grammatical or change the meaning rather than break the grammar ('They have lived here from last March', 'until 2020'). The 'any reading grammatical' rule cannot be decided with regex and is only as good as DeepSeek run as a judge.

WEAK WHYS ARE A CONFIRMED A1 PROBLEM, not a hypothetical one. I checked the banks: grammar_mcq_a1.js has 333 generic 'gramer açısından uygun değil' strings, and A2-C1 have none. The B1 'why' strings are specific but verbose (well over 90 chars, with a 'Yanlış: ...' prefix), so they need trimming, not just regex replacement.

LLM SPANS WILL BE WRONG. The error-item schema asks the model for character offsets ('span':[9,15]). LLMs miscount character offsets often, so the crack or underline animation lands on the wrong letters, which is a visible polish failure.

SCOPE CREEP. There are 3 bid modes, 2 scoring systems, 3 reveal timings, 6 opt-in modifiers, a hint ladder with % refunds, Comeback Off/Light/Strong, TTS, print sets, Flash lots and Audio lots. The teacher controls are a settings maze, and each combination is a test path. As written this is XL, not L.

RUNTIME TTS RISK. Web Speech English voices vary widely on school Windows PCs and smartboards (some have no en voice, or only a robotic one). Kids' A1/A2 read-aloud is billed as core ('Gogo reads each sentence twice'), so an unreliable voice breaks the kids skin.

ART AND ASSETS DEBT. Gogo the parrot and the crab (several poses: peck, hold word, scuttle), 6+ animal mascots, an easel and frames, a crack overlay, a loupe, holo cards with an RGB-split glitch, a sea map with a ship, a treasure chest, and picture evidence (emoji/imageKey required at A1/A2 Genç, where 'two cats' needs an image that really shows two). That is three separate art directions for one game.
fixes: Change the default value formula so risk is real. Unspent money scores 1x (it is 'kept capital'). An original pays 2x (profit = price), a fixed forgery refunds 0.5x (a loss of 0.5x the price), and an unfixed forgery pays 0 (a loss of the full price). Buying then only pays off when the team really believes the sentence is right, so calibration becomes the winning skill. Keep the hoarding brake as a minimum-purchase rule (each team must own at least ceil(lots/teams)-1 lots, or unsold lots are force-assigned at the opening bid), not as 'cash is worthless'. Simulate it with a 50-line script before tuning the multipliers.

Build ONE engine with bidMode as a parameter (live | sealed | shells) and a shared Lot model, reveal pipeline and finale. Ship in phases. MVP (M-sized): Stüdyo Live with per-lot reveal as the default (end-Ekspertiz as an option), plus Arena Sealed. Phase 2: the Oyun Parkı skin. Cut for v1: All-in, Flash, Audio lot, the hint-ladder % refunds, Comeback Strong, half-time reveal and the TTS auctioneer. Put the rest under 'Gelişmiş'.

Arena and sealed input: a one-screen entry grid where each team row has 2 big toggles (V/G) and 5 bid chips (0/100/200/300/400) with smart defaults, so 6 teams take about 12 taps and under 15 s. Keyboard: team digit, then v or g, then a bid digit. Drop the separate +50-per-call combo system, or fold it in as a small 'Keen Eye' side meter that never changes the score, so there is one score for teens to read.

Kids: keep only 2 response formats per lot, a coin card for Treasure/Trap confidence and fingers for the fix. Drop stand/sit (or make the coin card itself the stand-up moment). Merge Gogo's Gift and the rescue question into one automatic '+2 coins between islands'. Give kids a fixed 12-coin pouch sized to lots x 1.5 so they can't run dry. Be honest in the suite matrix that this skin is 'Treasure or Trap', a confidence T/F variant, and don't also ship a separate kids T/F-sort game.

Content pipeline: precompute an OFFLINE curated lot bank. A node script walks grammar_mcq_*: it picks the forgery distractor by a rule table per unit (agreement, form or verb-pattern errors preferred; semantic distractors like ago/during excluded), asks the LLM for a 90-character whyTr and the rule card once per unit x distractor, and adds an adversarial 'is any reading grammatical?' check. The output is lots_a1..b2.json, which the teacher reviews once in bulk. Runtime LLM calls are used ONLY for free-text prompts, and those go through the same validator plus the teacher's lot list.

Never trust LLM offsets. Ask for wrong and right sentences only, compute the span with a token-level diff on the server, and reject anything that is not a single contiguous chunk of 3 tokens or fewer. Also run the same checks in code: word caps, the words.js band, a teenSafe keyword list, and one error = one diff chunk.
Fix the A1 whys first: generate 90-character Turkish rule lines for the 333 generic A1 'why' strings offline, and trim the B1-B2 'Yanlış: X bu boşlukta...' boilerplate to the substantive clause.

Time: default Stüdyo to 10 lots with per-lot reveal (or reveal at half-time) and measure. Show a live 'kalan süre / kalan lot' estimate, and have Hızlı ekspertiz auto-offer when the projected time exceeds the lesson slot.

Audio: ship pre-generated MP3s for built-in lots at A1/A2 Genç (a small, cacheable set produced by a build script with a good TTS voice). Use Web Speech only as a fallback for LLM lots, and show a speaker-off state gracefully.

Assets: one shared SVG sprite sheet. Gogo in 4 poses and the crab in 2, made as simple flat vector art. Frames, crack and loupe are drawn with CSS/SVG, and the glitch is a CSS text-shadow RGB split. Use emoji for A1 picture evidence, and allow ONLY lots whose evidence is emoji-representable (count and position with 1-3 objects). About 8 sounds in total, shared across skins with a pitch or filter change (gavel/woodblock, tick, sold, crack, shine, patch, soft boing, chime), self-hosted and under 150 KB.

Polish priorities that make it feel like a game rather than a skinned quiz: the gavel slam with the SOLD stamp in the team colour; the going-once strip accelerating in a bidding war; the crack landing exactly on the diffed span, then ink restoration; the collection wall finale; the calibration chart. Build these five before any modifier.

Smartboard: every control at least 64px, no hover-only affordances, and the undo sale always visible. The presenter view (optional) shows the O/X and the fix to the teacher, so the teacher can run the auction without having to memorise the lot list.

catalog.rankReason: The best adult score in the suite (8.7) and the only error-correction game. Its content is almost free: stem+key from the grammar MCQ banks is an original, stem+distractor is a forgery. Fix the scoring so risk is real (unspent money keeps 1x, a fixed forgery refunds 0.5x) and reveal per lot or every 4 lots. Raise the A1 Genç cap to 6 words and use an audio-plus-picture contrast for kids. Teen appeal is low (6), so it comes after the first wave.

catalog.name: Kelime Oyunu: English Edition
catalog.familiarAs: Kelime Oyunu (tv2 word show)
catalog.oneLiner: The Turkish TV word show adapted for class. Teams climb a ladder of hidden words that run from short to long. Each word is a row of blank tiles with an English clue, each team races its own clock, and every letter a team buys lowers that word's value.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 1 min).
- The teacher picks the group chip and a content source: a built-in topic (e.g. Food, Jobs, MEB 7. sınıf Environment), a free prompt (Turkish is fine, e.g. '6. sınıf spor ve hobiler kelimeleri'), or a pasted list of the teacher's own words (the LLM only writes the clues).
- A summary line shows the settings, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 4:00/takım · 30 dk · Değiştir'.
- A preview grid shows every ladder with its answers. The teacher can swap a clue (S) or a word (W, same length, taken from the reserve) before projecting.
- Teams (2-4) get a name or emblem, one mini-whiteboard and a marker. A seat-number spinner assigns spokespeople, so nobody is ever picked by name.
- A 'Deneme kelimesi' practice word (not scored) demonstrates the flow. In Oyun Parkı, the mascot Gogo demonstrates it.

THE SCREEN.
- Left: the ladder, one row per word, grouped by length. The TV profile is 4,4,5,5,6,6,7,7,8,8,9,9,10,10. 'Kısa 10' and 'Mini 8' are shorter profiles for shorter lessons.
- Each row has one blank tile per letter and a value chip (letters × 100).
- A length ribbon with a climber marker shows progress.
- Centre: the clue in large type, with a speaker button and the tile pattern (e.g. '5 letters: L _ _ _ _').
- Right: each team's clock and score.
- Bottom: an auto-hiding teacher strip (ANSWER / LETTER / PASS / ✓ / ✗), large enough to tap on a FATİH interactive board.

MODE A 'Sırayla (TV-klasik)'. This is the Stüdyo default. Each team plays its own ladder against its own clock. All ladders have the same lengths and balanced difficulty.
1) The row lights up and the clue is read aloud (by TTS or the teacher). The clock starts after a reading grace of 2 s (adults), 2.5 s (Arena) or 3-4 s (kids).
2) The active team talks. The spinner has already chosen this word's spokesperson. Every other team silently writes its guess on its board (the 'gölge tahmin', or shadow guess).
3) The spokesperson says 'Answer!' and the teacher presses SPACE (or the clicker). The clock freezes with its own 'stopped' sound, and an answer window opens (10 s for adults and Arena, 15 s or off for kids).
4) The spokesperson says the word, and spells it if spelling mode is on.
   - The teacher presses Y: the remaining hidden tiles flip gold and roll up into the score (hidden tiles × 100).
   - The teacher presses N, or the window runs out: 'BOARDS UP!'. Every shadow team with the right word gets half the value. The active team loses nothing, except under the optional adult 'TV kuralı' (wrong = minus the current value).
5) 'Buy a letter' (L): one hidden tile flips and the value chip ticks down by 100 while the clock keeps running. Adults get a random tile, as on TV. Kids get the most helpful tile: the last letter, then vowels.
6) 'Pass' (P): the word slides into a Pass tray and comes back after the last row if time remains. Shadow boards stay down.
7) The turn ends when the ladder is done or the clock reaches 0. The word in play then goes to boards-up, and the next team starts its ladder.

MODE B 'Düello (satır satır)'. This is the default in Oyun Parkı and Arena, and for 2 teams in any audience.
- One shared ladder in which each length row holds one word per team, so every team plays the same lengths.
- Teams alternate word by word. Each team's chess clock runs only during its own word.
- On a wrong answer, the other teams show their boards immediately for half value.
- Every team gets a turn every 1-2 minutes, so nobody waits 4 minutes.

MODE C 'Sınıf Rekoru'. The whole class is one team playing against the clock and its own saved record. It suits small classes, private lessons and warm-ups.

AFTER THE LADDERS.
- Optional 'Kapış turu' (Arena and adults, at most 6 words). Passed and unplayed words return one at a time. All teams write for 15 s, then boards up, and every correct board scores half value.
- Then the final word, which differs by audience: adults bet a secret wager, Arena plays the 'Final Climb' for double value, and kids solve Gogo's co-op 'Big Word'.

RECAP (2-3 min): 'Merdiven turu'.
- The ladder lights up row by row, each word in the colour of the team that found it (grey if no team did).
- The teacher clicks through the words. Each one shows its IPA with the stress marked, audio, the Turkish gloss and an example sentence, and the class echoes it (twice for kids).
- End screens follow the audience (see the versions). Adults also get the 'Kaçırılanlar' list.

SCORING SUMMARY.
- Adults: points = hidden tiles × 100. Stickers for kids and combos for Arena are described in the versions.
- There are no speed points in any mode. The clock is a budget, not a bonus.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Teams: 2-4 teams of 4-9 students (a class of 20-36). Each team has one mini-whiteboard and a marker.
- Modes: Düello for 2 teams (half the class against half), or row by row for 3-4 teams in Oyun Parkı and Arena. Sırayla (TV-klasik) suits 2-4 teams of adults. Sınıf Rekoru makes the whole class one team, which fits small groups and 1-to-1 lessons.
- Roles rotate with the seat-number spinner for every word: a spokesperson for the active team and, at B levels, a 'board writer' on each shadow team. Adults may use pair consultation inside the team.
- The teacher hosts and judges from the laptop, the clicker or the board strip.
skills: vocabulary retrieval from definitions (meaning to form)
reading and listening to English clues and definitions
speaking: spoken answers, team talk in English, pronunciation echo in the recap
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO 'Kelime Oyunu: English Edition'. It is faithful to the TV format and fits a real 40-minute lesson.

LOOK AND SOUND
- Editorial quiz-night style on cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. Tiles look like letterpress blocks. System sans font.
- No mascot and no voice lines, only a neutral caption ('Round 2 · Travel').
- Woodblock and piano sounds, each at most 1 s. Music is off.
- Teacher chrome is in Turkish. The rules screen opens with 'Kelime Oyunu'nu bilirsiniz: …' in a single sentence, then lists the three classroom differences: shadow boards, steals and hints. Student-facing text is English.

RULES
- Ladder profiles: TV 14 (4-10 letters, 2 of each length), Kısa 10 (4-8) or Mini 8.
- Clock: 4:00 per team by default, 3:00 for 'Hızlı', or Süresiz. The answer window is 10 s.
- Word value: hidden tiles × 100. Each bought letter costs 100.
- Hint ladder (the definition is always the clue): a gapped example sentence (−100), then the Turkish gloss (−200). The teacher can switch the gloss off for immersion classes.
- Wrong answers score 0 by default. The optional 'TV kuralı' deducts the current value (optional negatives).
- Spelling: from B1, words of 8 or more letters must be spelt. At B2, spelling always counts, and a misspelt word earns half value. In 'Canlı heceleme', letters appear in the tiles as the teacher types what the spokesperson spells.
- Shadow boards and half-value steals are on.
- Kapış turu is optional.
- 'Final Kelimesi' (secret wager):
  - Each team writes a wager on a slip of paper: up to half its score, or up to 500 if it has 0.
  - A long word appears: 11-12 letters at B2, 9-10 at B1, 8 at A2, 7 at A1.
  - One letter flips every 5 s for 30 s, then boards up.
  - A right answer wins the wager and a wrong one loses it. Because the wager is at most half the score, no score can drop below zero.
- Luck and harshness: Green and Yellow are on by default, but this game uses only one optional 'Altın kelime' (Double), announced when it appears. Red cards are opt-in and are not used here.
- Comeback: Light. When the trailing team answers correctly it gets a +100 Slipstream bonus, and it chooses the theme of the next ladder when a pack has several.

TEAM TALK
A strip of phrases keeps the huddle in English: 'Could it be…?', 'It's got seven letters, so…', 'Let's buy a letter.', 'I'm not sure how to spell it.'

CONTENT
- Life and work categories: travel, job interviews, workplace, health, shopping and money, housing, small talk, complaints, technology.
- 'YDS/YÖKDİL kelime' packs come from the AWL words in words.js, with cloze clues such as 'The company plans to ___ 50 new staff.' → HIRE.
- Free prompts work as well, e.g. 'hemşirelik öğrencileri için hastane kelimeleri'.

ENDING
- A 0.6 s chime and the scores rolling up.
- The full scoreboard and a modest finale.
- Stat cards: 'En uzun kelime: ENVIRONMENT', 'Harf almadan bilinen: 6', 'En iyi kapış'.
- The 'Kaçırılanlar' list (word, IPA, Turkish gloss, example) can be copied, printed or sent to the Material Maker as a follow-up worksheet.

PACING
- 4 teams × 4:00 plus overhead: about 25-30 min.
- 2 teams in Düello: 15-20 min.
catalog.teenVersion:
Levels and skins are independent: a 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena visuals with A1 picture clues, and a 9-year-old B1 class keeps Oyun Parkı.

(a) OYUN PARKI, ages 9-11: 'Letter Box' ('Harf Kasası' in the teacher chrome)
This is a stripped ruleset that passes the kids checklist.

THREE RULES
Turkish rule card for the teacher, pictograms for the class. It can be explained in 20 s.
1) Look and listen (eye and ear icons).
2) Talk with your team, then say 'Answer!' (speech bubble).
3) More letters, smaller sticker (gold → silver → bronze). Every word you find still gets a sticker.

HOST
- Gogo the parrot demonstrates a practice word (25 s, not scored).
- It reads each clue at 0.8x and holds the free first letter in its beak before dropping it into the tile.
- It says the answer after a miss, and it sleeps on top of the ladder when the game is paused.
- As each tile flips, the letter's English name is spoken ('Bee!', 'Jay!'), which practises the A/E/I and G/J names that Turkish children mix up.

CLUES
- A self-hosted SVG picture plus at most 4 words (A1 Genç, e.g. 'big · grey · animal') or 8 words (A2 Genç, 'It is a big grey animal.').
- Lengths are 3-5 at A1 and 3-7 at A2. The first letter is always free.
- The hint ladder is free: picture, then first letter, then listen again. An extra bought letter only downgrades the sticker.

STRUCTURE
- Row by row, with every team getting 1 word per turn.
- Three rounds: short words (3-4 letters), middle words (5) and long words (6-7), each 3-5 min.
- Between rounds there is a 45 s stirrer ('Sky-write the longest word with your finger!') or a 60 s settler ('Trace it on your desk, say each letter').
- No clock by default. The optional clock is a calm 5:00 ring that never turns red and ends with a marimba chime.

WHOLE-CLASS MOMENT, EVERY WORD
- A1 Genç: Gogo says 'Stand up if you know it!', then everyone says the word twice with an action (an animal sound, a mime).
- A2 Genç: the other teams write on their boards. Spelling is judged leniently, and a correct board earns a helper sticker, which counts toward the Best Helpers title.

SCORING
- Stickers drop into each team's box: gold (no bought letters) = 3 stars, silver (1-2 letters) = 2, bronze (3 or more letters, or a second try) = 1.
- Stars never go down. There are no steals, no wagers and no minus points.

WRONG ANSWERS
- A soft 'boing', the next letter flips free, and the team tries again.
- If it is still wrong, Gogo says the word, the class repeats it twice, and the team earns an effort star for the class album.
- Failure imagery is never violent: tiles just wobble, and Gogo shrugs.

FINALE
- A co-op 'Big Word': Gogo flips a letter every 8 s, and all teams whisper and write together.
- When the class solves it, confetti falls in the team colours and shapes (at most 2 s).
- Every team gets a title: Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers (most words with no bought letters) or Super Spellers. A sticker goes into the class album.

CONTENT AND LENGTH
- YLE-style and MEB-unit topics with pictures: animals, food, school things, body, clothes, toys, weather, family, and MEB 5 Health or Life in Nature. The teenSafe filter is always on.
- 15-25 min in total.

(b) ARENA, ages 12-14: 'Word Climb'

LOOK AND SOUND
- Dark navy with neon accents in the team colours, LED-panel tiles and a condensed display font.
- In 10 s, each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.
- The framing is 'Match' and 'Challenge'. No animals, no talking mascot, no pastels.
- English rule card with a Turkish toggle. Synth blips of at most 1 s, and an optional quiet thinking loop.

RULES
- Row-by-row Düello with a 3:30 chess clock per team. The ring is in the team colour, and a word solved in the last 10 s triggers a 'CLUTCH!' caption.
- Each bought letter costs 100.
- Hint ladder: first letter (−100; free with A1/A2 content), then a gapped example (−100), then 'Two options' (the word against a same-length decoy; the value halves).
- Combo: x1.5 after 3 correct answers in a row, x2 after 5. A pass freezes the streak and a wrong answer breaks it. The combo counts accuracy only, never speed.
- Wrong answers: the other teams steal by boards-up for half value, and the first team loses nothing. The score floor is zero.
- Point steals (the Yellow harshness level) happen only if the teacher opts in.
- A commentator strip appears at most once per turn: 'CLEAN CLIMB', 'COMBO x2', 'CLUTCH!'.
- Kapış turu is optional.

FINALE
- 'Final Climb': one long word, all teams write, and a correct board scores double value.
- A podium, plus stat awards so that every team is named somewhere: Longest streak, Cleanest climb (fewest letters bought), Comeback, Best steal. There is never a last place and no student is named.

CONTENT AND LENGTH
- Richer language on concrete teen topics: sport, games, tech, environment, school life, travel, food. Never adult domains.
- 3 teams: about 15-20 min.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Lengths 3-6 (A1 Genç 3-5): concrete nouns, colours, very common verbs and adjectives.
- Clue: a picture plus 4 words or fewer (Genç), or a 'It's a…' clue of 10 words or fewer with an optional free picture (adults).
- The first letter is free, and later letters pick the most helpful tile.
- The Turkish gloss costs only 100 for adults.
- Answers are spoken only (no spelling), with a 15 s answer window. Mini 8 ladder.

A2
- Lengths 4-8 (A2 Genç 3-7).
- Simple definitions of 15 words or fewer, e.g. 'a place where you buy medicine' → PHARMACY. A2 Genç: 8 words or fewer, with a picture.
- The first letter is free. The Turkish gloss costs 200. Spelling is off. Kısa 10 ladder.

B1
- Lengths 4-10 (B1 Genç 4-8).
- Definitions plus gapped sentences, e.g. 'I can't ___ this box. It's too heavy.' → LIFT. 25 words or fewer (B1 Genç: 14).
- The first letter is paid, and spelling is required on words of 8 or more letters.
- The Turkish gloss costs 200. Adults use the TV 14 ladder.

B2
- Lengths 5-10 plus a bonus 11-12 row or final word (B2 Genç 5-10).
- Clue types: synonym, antonym, collocation, cloze and word family, e.g. 'the noun of decide' → DECISION.
- The hard cap is 40 words, but aim for 25 or fewer (B2 Genç: 20, concrete topics).
- Turkish hints are off. Spelling always counts, and a misspelt word earns half value.
- Optional phrasal row with a fixed gap tile (GIVE_UP).

ALL LEVELS
- The Kolay/Orta/Zor dial shifts the word-band mix (e.g. B1-Kolay = 60% A2 words), shortens lengths by one and makes the first letter free.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops a whole level without changing the skin.
- Clue text is capped by the group caps (A1 Genç 0-4, A2 Genç 8, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40). The generator aims for about 60% of the cap, and a clue that is too long gets a shorter clue type, never a smaller font.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 10-35 (Mini ladder warm-up 10; Oyun Parkı 15-25; Arena 15-25; Stüdyo 20-35)
catalog.contentShape:
One ladder pack lives in pack.frames.ladder: {profile: [lengths], mode, perTeam, finalId?, reserve: {length: [itemIds]}}. Code builds it from answerable items.

FIELDS EACH RUNG NEEDS (from vocab)
- answer = term: letters a-z only, single word. Its length is the tile count. The spelling follows the class profile's UK/US setting, and the other spelling is accepted aloud through alt[].
- Clue registers, chosen by audience:
  - media.img from the self-hosted SVG set (required for A1/A2 Genç; emoji appears only in the teacher preview);
  - clueEasy from defEasy;
  - clueDef from def (B groups);
  - clueGap from gap.text with ___ (B1+; the tiles show the exact form the gap needs, and A/Genç groups never get inflected answers);
  - clueFamily/clueSyn from family[] and synonyms (B2).
- defTr: the paid Turkish hint and the teacher's check.
- example: used in the recap and for the gapped-example hint.
- ipa (only from words.js, hidden if missing) and syll.
- alsoOk: other same-length words the teacher may accept.
- CEFR band and frequency rank, for balancing ladders.
- teenSafe flag.
- The computed hangman flag gives eligibility (letters only, 3-12).

qa ITEMS
Usable when answerKind='word' and accept[0] is letters only. The clue becomes the clue, accept[] becomes the accepted list, and hintTr becomes the Turkish hint.

riddle ITEMS
clues[3] (hard to easy) become 'Gogo's clues' for kids and hint rungs for others. The next clue costs the same as a letter, and answer fills the tiles.

BUILT-IN PATH
- words.js (w, p, d, e, i, t) is filtered by band, length, part of speech (mostly nouns for kids), category tags and teenSafe.
- Oxford definitions often break the caps (elephant runs to about 35 words), and words.js examples are often fragments ('herds of elephants'). So built-in categories ship with a pre-generated, validated clue bank that works offline.

FREE-PROMPT AND OWN-LIST PATH
The LLM returns vocab items under the merged AudienceProfile. Code then:
- computes lengths and fills the rows;
- deals balanced ladders round-robin by band and frequency;
- keeps one reserve word per row;
- validates each clue: no answer stem or family member in the clue, the word cap, at least 90% of clue words within the level band, and an ambiguity check (a same-length, same-initial alternative forces a rewrite).
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Mode (Sırayla / Düello / Sınıf Rekoru) and teams (2-4).
- Ladder profile (TV 14 / Kısa 10 / Mini 8 / custom lengths) and length range.
- Clock per team (Süresiz, or 2:00-6:00), answer window (5-20 s or off) and reading grace.
- Letter cost (50/100), the free-first-letter toggle and the reveal order (random or most helpful).
- Turkish hint on/off and its cost.
- Spelling: off / 8 or more letters / always / live spelling.
- Wrong-answer penalty: 0, or 'TV kuralı' (adults only).
- Shadow boards on/off, and steal value (half / full / off).
- Kapış turu on/off and its maximum number of words.
- Final: off / wager / Final Climb / Big Word.
- Altın kelime on/off, and Comeback (Off / Light / Strong).
- UK/US spelling, Kolay/Orta/Zor, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- Lesson minutes: the lesson-fit sizing picks the ladder length and the clock.
- Audience overrides (skin, rule pack, any dial), saved to the local class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').

PREVIEW
- Shows all answers.
- Swap a clue: cycles picture / easy / definition / gap.
- Swap a word: same length, from the reserve.
- Edit a clue inline, and lock the pack.

IN-GAME KEYS
- SPACE: Answer (stops the clock). Y: correct. N: wrong.
- L: buy a letter. H: next hint. P: pass. R: read aloud.
- S: swap the clue. W: swap the word (only before any letter is bought).
- A: accept an alternative answer (it is logged to the class profile, so later games accept it automatically).
- U: undo the last judgement. E: edit a score.
- + / −: 10 s. T: pause. B: blank the screen.
- Esc: teacher panel. ?: key legend.

OTHER INPUT
- Presenter clicker: PageDown = Answer or next, PageUp = buy a letter, B = pause.
- A touch strip for interactive boards.
- Optional teacher console: a second window on an extended display shows the answer, Turkish gloss and next word while the projector shows only the game. A printable answer sheet is the fallback.
catalog.delightDetails:
TILES AND SOUND
- Tiles flip with a sound per skin: marimba plink, synth tick or woodblock clack.
- Kids hear each letter's English name as its tile flips.
- A distinct 'clock stopped' sound for each skin (a bell ding, a mag-lock clunk, a woodblock knock), with the digits freezing and dimming.

CORRECT ANSWERS
- Unbought tiles glow gold one by one and fly into the score with '+800' rolling up.
- Kids hear a sticker clink into their team's box (2 s or less).
- A 'Harf almadan bildi!' stamp (Stüdyo), 'CLEAN CLIMB' (Arena) or a gold sticker (kids).

BUYING, PASSING AND THE CLOCK
- When a letter is bought, the value chip ticks down (800 → 700) with a small dip. That tile keeps a slightly different shade, so the recap shows how each word was cracked.
- A length ribbon with a climber marker (a flag, or Gogo hopping up the rungs).
- Passed words sit tilted in a Pass tray and whoosh back later.
- The last 10 s pulse softly (never red for kids).

LANGUAGE AND SPELLING
- The tile count is shown as an explicit hint ('5 letters: L _ _ _ _'), which quietly settles synonym ambiguity.
- A team-talk phrase strip (B groups) keeps the huddle in English.
- Live spelling fills the tiles as the teacher types what the team spells.
- The recap marks the stressed syllable in the IPA and underlines tricky letters (silent or double) from B1.

HOST, RECORDS AND ENDINGS
- Gogo's practice word and nap on the pause screen (kids).
- 'New class record!' banner in Sınıf Rekoru.
- The final ladder lights up row by row in the team colours, followed by stat cards ('En uzun kelime: ENVIRONMENT', 'Harf almadan: 6', 'En iyi kapış').
- Kids: a titled sticker for every team and a page in the class album.
catalog.risks:
CLUE QUALITY
- Oxford definitions in words.js are often far over the caps (elephant runs to about 35 words), and its examples are often fragments. Fix: a curated clue bank for built-in topics, the validator, and live swaps (S/W).
- Clues with several valid answers (big/large, shop/store). Fix: the tile count and first letter usually settle it; add an alsoOk list, the A key, and a validator flag for same-length, same-initial alternatives.
- Answer leaks (the stem or a family word inside the clue). Fix: a stem and family[] check.
- Narrow topics cannot fill the long rows (colours has few 9-10 letter words). Fix: the ladder profile shrinks automatically with a Turkish warning, or borrows from a neighbouring category. Rows are never padded with off-level words.
- Inflected answers in gap clues (hired vs hire). Fix: the tiles show the exact form, and adults at B1+ see a '(verb, past)' tag.
- UK/US spelling changes the tile count (colour/color). Fix: a class-profile setting, with the other spelling accepted aloud.
- LLM IPA can be wrong. Fix: take IPA only from words.js.

CLASSROOM DYNAMICS
- Idle teams during a 4:00 TV-klasik turn. Fix: shadow boards and half-value steals, and kids and Arena default to short row-by-row turns.
- Shouted answers. Fix: boards only; a shouted answer voids that team's steal, and kids see a 'Shh, boards!' pictogram.
- Clock pressure on shy or weaker students. Fix: the reading grace, Süresiz, no clock for kids, and never any speed points.
- Spoken versus spelt answers. Fix: lenient judging of spoken answers at A levels, with spelling only from B1 and flagged per word.
- One team gets a harder ladder in Sırayla. Fix: deal words by band and frequency, with the same length profile for every team.

PRACTICAL
- No English TTS voice on the machine. Fix: 'Öğretmen okur' (the teacher reads).
- The answer must not show on the projector. Fix: the teacher console or a printed key.
- 'Kelime Oyunu' is a TV brand. Use it only descriptively in the teacher chrome. Copy no logo, jingle or set design, and title the student screens 'Word Show', 'Word Climb' or 'Letter Box'.
- Children may not know the show, so the Turkish rule card and pictograms carry the explanation.
- Genç packs must always pass teenSafe.
sources: https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelime_Oyunu (format reference, from the raw idea; the show's exact rules were not verified, so this is a classroom adaptation)
C:/lg/src/data/words.js (entry fields w, p, d, e, i, t: word, part of speech, Oxford definition, example, IPA, Turkish; checked with grep)
C:/lg/src/lib/game-classroom.mjs and src/pages/sinif-oyunu.astro (existing team and projector board to reuse for teams, keys and projector layout; not re-read for this design)
C:/lg/src/pages/api/materials/generate.ts (LLM endpoint with rate limiting for free-prompt packs)
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Share one word-tile engine with Hangman, but keep both games (the Hangman 'Word Vault' adult variant must stop using definition clues so the two stay distinct)

issues: SETUP TIME IS UNDERSTATED. The '1 min' only holds for a locked built-in pack. With a free prompt, the teacher waits for the LLM and then reviews a TV-14 preview. That is 14 words × up to 4 ladders, about 56 answers plus clues and reserves, so 3-6 minutes, done in front of the class if not prepared at home. Handing out boards and markers, naming teams and picking emblems (Arena gives each team 10 s) add 2-3 minutes more.

FREE PROMPTS BREAK THE KIDS PATH. A1/A2 Genç require a self-hosted SVG picture, but an LLM prompt like '6. sınıf spor ve hobiler' will return words that have no SVG. The spec never says what happens then (drop the word, fall back to a text clue, or use the emoji the kids never see). The built-in 'curated clue bank' is also a large content-production job that the 'M' build size hides.

SIRAYLA (TV-KLASİK) WITH 4 TEAMS IS 12 MIN OF WAITING PER TEAM. Shadow boards engage one writer per team, not the other 6-8 students. It fails with kids, and it is still weak with adults at 3 teams (8 idle minutes). It also cannot stop fairly partway: if the bell rings during team 3's ladder, team 4 never played. Lesson-fit sizing only helps if the teacher sets the minutes correctly and nothing interrupts (announcements, a late start, discipline).

ONE BOARD PER TEAM OF 7-9 MEANS ONE STUDENT DOES THE WORK. The strongest student grabs the marker, and the rest watch. The spinner rotates the spokesperson and (at B levels) the board writer, but the huddle is still dominated by one or two students. In Oyun Parkı nothing rotates the board writer at all. Many Turkish public-school classes also have no mini-whiteboards, and the spec has no fallback.

SPINNER DEAD TIME. A seat-number spin before every word adds 5-10 s × roughly 24-40 words, so 3-5 minutes of spinning per lesson. It is also another click the teacher has to make. Students may not remember their seat numbers, and seats change.

TOO MUCH FOR THE TEACHER TO DRIVE. There are about 20 hotkeys (SPACE/Y/N/L/H/P/R/S/W/A/U/E/+/−/T/B/Esc/?), and the teacher is standing at a touch board away from the keyboard. The touch strip only shows ANSWER/LETTER/PASS/✓/✗, so hint, undo, accept-alternative and pause are keyboard-only while the teacher is at the board. 'Canlı heceleme' asks the teacher to type letters on an on-screen keyboard while listening to a child spell in a noisy room, which is not realistic.

THE TEACHER CANNOT SEE THE ANSWER. FATİH boards are almost always single-display, so the 'teacher console on an extended display' does not exist there. The printed answer sheet is the only fallback, and it has to be regenerated whenever the teacher swaps a word or clue (S/W), so it goes out of date as soon as they do. Without the answer, the teacher cannot judge alternatives such as big/large quickly.

THE 'SPACE ON ANSWER!' HANDSHAKE FAILS IN NOISE. With 28 children, the teacher misses the moment, hears 'Answer!' from the wrong team, or two teams shout at once. The 10-15 s answer window then runs out while the teacher is still sorting out who spoke.

SHOUTING RUINS THE ACTIVE TEAM'S WORD. The rule 'a shouted answer voids that team's steal' needs the teacher to tell which of 3 teams shouted, which is impossible in a loud room. It also does nothing for the active team, whose word was just given away.

OYUN PARKI HAS NO CLOCK BY DEFAULT, SO IT DRAGS. A team of hesitant 10-year-olds can deliberate for 90 s or more while three teams wait. The wrong answer → free letter → retry → Gogo says it → class echoes twice sequence, plus a letter name spoken at every flip, can run 60-90 s per word. With 4 teams × 3 rounds × 1 word per turn, the 15-25 min estimate is likely exceeded, or the game ends with only 2 rounds played.

'STAND UP IF YOU KNOW IT!' IS A CLASSROOM-MANAGEMENT HAZARD with 28 lively kids. It creates noise and chairs scraping every word, and the teacher then has to settle the class again before the next clue. Doing it every word is too often.

DÜELLO FAIRNESS DEPENDS ON EACH WORD'S DIFFICULTY. Every team gets a different word of the same length, so one team's CLOUD against another's SCARF can feel unfair to kids, who notice immediately ('Their word was easier!'). The band and frequency balancing is invisible to them.

A TEAM CAN STILL FALL HOPELESSLY BEHIND for adults and Arena. Steals pay half value and the Arena combo multiplies the leader's score, so a snowball is possible. Slipstream's +100 is tiny next to a x2 combo on an 800-point word. Arena's 'no last place' podium still shows the ranking.

STICKER TIERS STILL RANK THE KIDS. Gold, silver and bronze per word are fine, but a team that keeps getting bronze sees it. The effort star goes to the 'class album', not the team, so the weakest team's box stays visibly emptiest.

THE RECAP COMES LAST AND WILL BE CUT BY THE BELL. The 2-3 min 'Merdiven turu', where most of the learning (pronunciation echo) happens, sits after the finale. In real 40-min lessons it is the first thing lost.

SCOPE CREEP HIDES THE REAL BUILD SIZE. There are 3 modes, 3 skins, 3 finals, Kapış, combos, a commentator, Altın kelime, Comeback, live spelling, TV kuralı, alternative logging and stat cards. That is L/XL, not M, and each option is another setup decision for the teacher.

IT OVERLAPS WITH HANGMAN (Word Vault: category plus definition clue, reveal letters, 6 misses) and with Jeopardy/qa games. The distinct hook is the clue → word ladder with letter buying and team clocks. That hook should be kept sharp, or the suite ends up with two 'guess the hidden word from tiles' games.
fixes: MAKE DÜELLO THE ONLY DEFAULT FOR EVERY AUDIENCE WITH 3 OR MORE TEAMS. Keep Sırayla as an adult-only option for 2-3 teams, and show a Turkish warning: 'Her takım ~X dk bekler'. When the teacher stops the game, end on a completed round only: an 'Oyunu bitir' button finishes the current round so every team has had the same number of turns, then goes straight to the recap.

ADD A 'SHORT RECAP FIRST' OPTION. Put a 60-s pronunciation echo of the words the class missed before the finale, or make the recap a separate 'Tekrar' button reachable from the pause screen at any time. Also offer the Kaçırılanlar list as a QR code or printout for kids' homework.

REPLACE THE PER-WORD SPINNER. Assign speaking order once at setup (team members number off 1-9, and the screen shows 'Konuşmacı: 3' next to the team name, advancing automatically each turn). Use the spinner only when the teacher chooses to. The board writer rotates the same way, including in Oyun Parkı, so the marker moves around every student.
ADD A NO-WHITEBOARD FALLBACK. Offer A4 in plastic sleeves, notebook pages held up, or a first-letter hand-sign mode for A1 kids. Say in the setup screen what is needed ('Takım başına 1 tahta/kağıt').

CUT THE TOUCH STRIP TO 4 BIG BUTTONS PER TURN: ✓ Doğru, ✗ Yanlış, Harf ver, Geç. Put a long-press 'more' menu behind them (ipucu, geri al, kabul et, duraklat). Drop the 'Answer!' SPACE freeze step for kids and Arena: the clock (if any) stops when the teacher taps ✓/✗. Remove live spelling from touch mode entirely; the teacher just judges the spelling with ✓ or ½.

SOLVE ANSWER VISIBILITY FOR SINGLE-SCREEN CLASSROOMS. (a) Add a phone companion: the teacher's phone opens a page by QR/code that shows the current answer, the Turkish gloss and alsoOk words, with no install. (b) Add a 'hold to peek' corner that shows the answer in small grey type only while the teacher holds it. (c) Regenerate the printable key whenever the pack is locked, and number the words so a swap shows as 'W7 → yedek'.

HANDLE SHOUTING FOR THE ACTIVE TEAM. If an answer is blurted by another team, the teacher taps 'Söylendi', the active team gets full value, and nobody steals that word. It needs no identification of who shouted, and it quickly teaches silence.

GIVE OYUN PARKI A SOFT PER-WORD TIMER. Use a 45-60 s sand-timer picture that never turns red and that the teacher can extend. After it runs out, the teacher taps 'Birlikte bulalım' and Gogo gives letters until the word is solved. Allow only one retry, and speak letter names only for the free letter and bought letters, not in the recap animation. Cap each round at 1 word per team × 3 rounds, with round 3 optional.
REPLACE 'STAND UP' WITH SEATED WHOLE-CLASS RESPONSES: thumbs up, mouthing the word, finger-writing the first letter in the air. Use stand-up only in the 45-s stirrer between rounds, not every word.

MAKE DÜELLO FAIRNESS VISIBLE. Deal each row as a matched pair or triplet from the same frequency band, and let the teacher silently swap a word (W) before it is shown. Optionally, all teams in a row get the SAME clue category (e.g. all animals) so the rows feel equal. For kids, consider every team trying the same word, with boards written simultaneously, and scoring in parallel instead of alternating.

STRENGTHEN THE COMEBACK FOR ADULTS AND ARENA. Cap the combo at x1.5, scale Slipstream to the current word value (e.g. +25%), and let the trailing team choose the next row's length. For kids, effort stars go into the TEAM's box as well as the album, so no team's box looks empty.

SHIP FOUR PRESETS INSTEAD OF A WALL OF DIALS: 'Hızlı ısınma (10 dk)', 'Tam ders (35 dk)', 'Yarışma gecesi (yetişkin)', 'Oyun Parkı'. Hide the full dial table behind 'Gelişmiş'. Keep Kapış, Altın kelime, TV kuralı and live spelling out of v1 and re-scope the build as L.

DEFINE THE FREE-PROMPT PICTURE FALLBACK FOR A1/A2 GENÇ. Pick only words that have an SVG in the set, and fill any gaps with built-in words from the same topic, with a Turkish notice. If fewer than 8 words have pictures, offer 'Resimsiz oyna (öğretmen okur)'.

SHOW A REALISTIC SETUP ESTIMATE, and let the teacher prepare and lock a pack at home and open it later from 'Hazır paketlerim' in one click. Pre-assign teams and emblems automatically, with renaming optional.

DIFFERENTIATE THE GAME FROM HANGMAN IN THE SUITE: the ladder, team clocks and letter buying are Kelime Oyunu's own identity. Make sure Hangman stays letter-guessing only, with no definition-to-word ladder, so the two games do not blur.

issues: Kids path breaks on free prompts. A1/A2 Genç requires a self-hosted SVG picture for every rung, and the LLM cannot make pictures. So a prompt like '4. sınıf meslekler' only works for words already in the SVG set. The design never says what happens when a generated word has no picture: is it dropped, is the rung shown without a picture, or is it an emoji? That leaves hard requirement (b) unmet for the youngest groups.

A1 Genç who barely read are really playing picture naming. With a picture, a free first letter and TTS, the tile row is decoration. Children who can't decode get nothing from the letters, and children who can find it trivial. The core mechanic, where letters make the word cheaper, has almost no learning bite at this level.

The kids variant ('Letter Box') is very close to the kids Hangman ('Balloon Rescue'). Both have picture hints, letter tiles revealed one by one, letter names spoken aloud and no elimination. In a 10-game suite, the two feel like the same game twice for Oyun Parkı classes.

At A1 and A2 adult level, the Turkish gloss hint (100 or 200) is cheaper than it is worth. Once teams learn this, they buy the gloss first, and the game turns into Turkish-to-English translation instead of recall from an English definition. That cuts the English reading and listening input the game is built on.

Shadow boards ask A1 and A2 kids to write whole words under time pressure. Lenient spelling is mentioned, but nothing defines 'lenient' (is FOKS for FOX ok?). Without a rule, teachers judge inconsistently and children argue.

Production is thin. Each turn is one spoken single word, with spelling from B1. The team-talk phrase strip exists only for B groups. Adults at A1 and A2 and all the kids huddle in Turkish, so apart from the recap echo, spoken English per student per minute is low.

The B2 clue types (word family, antonym, 'the noun of decide') are metalinguistic. B2 Genç keeps them 'concrete', but 12-13-year-olds at B2 still stumble on 'the noun of…' prompts that assume grammar terms they meet in Turkish, not in English.

In Sırayla with 4 teams × 4:00, the shadow teams write a guess for every word for 12 minutes. Steals only pay when the active team is wrong, so a strong active team means long stretches with no reward. Adults disengage too; the design only fixes this for kids and Arena.

LLM clue validation depends on '90% of clue words within the level band'. That needs lemmatised lookup against words.js (words.js stores lemmas, so 'buys' and 'bigger' will fail). The ambiguity check also needs a same-length, same-initial word list for each level. Neither is specified, and without them free-prompt clues at A1 will be over-level or ambiguous.

Narrow free prompts, and teacher-pasted lists above all, won't fill the length profile (e.g. 8 words, all 5-6 letters). Shrinking the profile automatically is fine for Mini 8, but the 'short to long ladder' progression, which is the game's identity, falls apart.
Arena's 'Two options' hint (the word against a decoy) turns a recall game into recognition. For weak 12-14 classes it becomes the default path, and the value only halves, so it is still worth taking.

The dial set is huge (about 25 settings). Level fit depends on the right combination (spelling, gloss cost, first letter, window, lengths). A teacher who changes one dial can easily produce a mismatched setup, such as B2 spelling with A1 Genç content.
