Letter names ('Bee', 'Jay') are good for kids, but Turkish adults at A1 and A2 have the same A/E/I and G/J confusion. Live spelling at B1 adult level assumes letter names they may never have been taught, and the adult version gets no letter-name support.
fixes: Add a 'picture available' gate for Oyun Parkı. On free prompts, the generator may only pick words that exist in the SVG index. When too few match, show a Turkish warning ('Bu konu için 6 resimli kelime bulundu') and offer to fill the rest from the nearest built-in picture category. Never ship a picture-less rung to A1 Genç.

For A1 Genç, make the letters matter. Once the word is named, the class chants the spelling while the tiles flip ('F-O-X!'). Or add an optional 'Harfi bul' step where the team must find the missing tile letter on a 3-letter choice strip. Then the tiles carry letter-sound learning instead of decoration.

Separate the kids variant from Hangman. Lean on the ladder and length progression (the climb, words growing longer, a sticker per rung) and the free-reveal-then-sticker-downgrade economy, and keep failure imagery off the letters entirely. Better still, share the Letter Box renderer with Balloon Rescue and give each game a distinct loop: Hangman is guessing letters, Kelime Oyunu is naming the whole word from a clue.

Gate the Turkish gloss. It unlocks only after one bought letter or the example hint, and it costs half the current value rather than a flat 100 or 200. Track gloss use and show it in the recap so the teacher sees whether the class is relying on L1.

Define lenient spelling for kids' boards: accept any spelling with the right letter count ±1 and the first and last letters correct, or a phonetic match. Show the correct spelling next to their board on boards-up, so every steal is also a spelling correction.

Make a phrase strip for every audience: pictogram phrases for kids ('I know!', 'Is it…?', 'Letter, please!') and an A-level adult strip. Have the spokesperson answer in a frame ('Is it a fox?' / 'It's a fox.') and, at A2+, add an optional one-sentence bonus (+100 for using the word in a sentence) so the game produces more than single words.
Restrict B2 Genç clue types to synonym, cloze and collocation. Keep word-family and antonym clues for adults, or phrase them in plain English ('decide → a ___ (noun)', with an example).

Make Düello the default for 3-4 adult teams too, and keep Sırayla as the 'TV-klasik' option for 2 teams or a short clock (2:30). Or add a shadow-team 'bonus board' for every word (a small +50 for a correct shadow guess even when the active team is right), so shadow work always pays.

Specify the validator: lemmatise clue tokens (strip -s/-es/-ed/-ing/-er/-est plus a list of irregulars) before the words.js band lookup. Keep a per-level function-word whitelist. Build the ambiguity index from words.js filtered to the level band plus one level.

For short own lists, offer a 'Karışık' profile that orders the ladder by difficulty (band and frequency) instead of length, and says so in the setup summary. Keep the short-to-long ladder only when the pack supports it.
Offer Arena's 'Two options' only from the second hint, cut the value to 100 flat, and break the combo when it is used, so recall stays the main path.

Replace the free-form dials with level presets that bundle the right settings for spelling, gloss, first letter, window and lengths, plus an 'Advanced' drawer. If a changed dial conflicts with the group (e.g. spelling 'always' with A1 Genç), show an inline Turkish note.
Put the letter-name audio on tile flips in every skin, off by default for B2. Add a one-screen English alphabet warm-up before Canlı heceleme at A2 and B1 adult level.

reviews.mergeWith: Share one word-tile engine with Hangman, but keep both games (the Hangman 'Word Vault' adult variant must stop using definition clues so the two stay distinct)
issues: Build size is L, not M. There are 3 modes × 3 audiences, 4 finales (wager, Final Climb, Big Word, Kapış), combo, comeback, Altın kelime, 4 spelling modes, live spelling, a second-window console, alt-answer learning and about 25 setup dials. Each one is small, but together they multiply the QA matrix (mode × audience × finale × team count) far beyond one M-sized island. Sırayla with 4 teams and wagers is the riskiest part, and it is the least used in class.

It overlaps with Hangman. The adult Hangman variant 'Word Vault' (category plus definition clue, optional wager) is almost this game without the clock. If both ship as specced, a teacher sees two 'reveal a hidden word from a definition' games in the menu.

The kids path needs a big self-hosted SVG picture library (hundreds of concrete nouns across animals, food, school, body, clothes, toys, weather, family and MEB units). That is the single largest asset cost in the design. Free prompts ('6. sınıf spor ve hobiler') cannot produce pictures, so the A1/A2 Genç free-prompt path breaks, or quietly falls back to text clues that kids cannot read.

The LLM cannot be trusted to count letters or to match a length profile. A 14-rung ladder × 4 teams needs about 56 words at exact lengths plus one reserve per row, about 70 words, from a single topic. Narrow topics or kids' 3-5 letter bands run dry, and 9-10 letter rows are especially hard at A1/A2.

The ambiguity check ('a same-length, same-initial alternative forces a rewrite') has no data source. words.js has no synonym graph, so code cannot detect that 'a place where you buy things' also fits STORE/SHOP. As specced, the check cannot be implemented.

The band check ('90% of clue words within the level band') fails on inflected forms and on words missing from words.js (names, plurals, -ing). It needs lemmatisation, or it will reject good clues and pass bad ones.

Judging shadow boards is the hidden bottleneck. After every wrong answer the teacher must read 2-3 boards across a room and enter which teams were right. The spec gives Y/N keys but no fast per-team steal input, so each boards-up moment costs 15-20 s of fiddling.

The answer can leak on the projector. Most Turkish classrooms mirror the laptop to the FATİH board, so the preview grid, the swap UI and any 'check the answer' view show on the wall. A second-window console needs an extended display, which many classrooms don't have.

Spoken letter names ('Bee!', 'Jay!') through Web Speech are unreliable. Many voices read a single 'a' as the article /ə/ or read 'g' oddly, and Turkish machines often have no English voice at all. The core A/E/I and G/J teaching feature would then silently fail.

Gogo the parrot is a per-game mascot, but the suite already defines animal team mascots for Oyun Parkı. A second recurring character for this one game adds animation-rig cost (demo, beak-drop, nap, shrug) and fragments the brand.

Oyun Parkı barely needs the TV format. With a picture, a free first letter, no clock, no steals and 3-5 letters, it becomes picture naming with tiles. That passes the kids checklist, but most of the Kelime Oyunu tension (the clock budget and the value dropping as letters are bought) disappears. Only the sticker downgrade is left, so teen fit is weaker than adult fit.
The Arena 'Two options' hint needs a same-length decoy for every item, which is an extra generated field and another validation path that the content shape doesn't list.

Live spelling (the teacher types while the student spells), the custom-length profile, the Altın kelime, the Comeback settings and the Kapış turu are polish features that the first release doesn't need. Each one adds state to undo (U) and to score editing (E).
Too many teacher dials. About 25 settings on the setup screen overwhelm a teacher who has 1 minute before class, even with the summary line.
fixes: Cut v1 to a clear minimum: Düello (the default everywhere) plus Sınıf Rekoru; one finale per audience (adults: wager, Arena: Final Climb, kids: Big Word); the Mini 8 and Kısa 10 profiles; buy-letter, pass, hint ladder, shadow boards with half-value steals, the recap, and undo. Sırayla (TV-klasik), Kapış, Altın kelime, Comeback, live spelling, custom lengths and the 'Two options' hint move to v1.1. This keeps the build honestly at M.

Build one shared word-tile component (flip animation, value chip, reveal-order policy, per-skin SFX) used by both Hangman and Kelime Oyunu. Differentiate the games clearly. In Hangman the class guesses letters, and the clue is only a category or picture. In Kelime Oyunu, the teams get a definition, can buy letters and play against a clock budget. Remove definition clues from Hangman 'Word Vault'.

Pictures: adopt one self-hosted icon set suite-wide (for example a curated OpenMoji subset, committed as SVG sprites, with CC BY-SA attribution) instead of bespoke art. For the A1/A2 Genç free-prompt path, have the LLM choose only from the list of pictured words (pass the keys in the prompt), and let code drop anything without a picture. Warn in Turkish if fewer than 8 remain.

Generation contract: ask the LLM for about 2.5× over-generation with a target length band, never exact lengths. Code computes the lengths, deals the rows, drops mismatches, and shrinks the profile automatically (Mini 8 fallback) with a Turkish warning. Never let the LLM decide the tile count.

Replace the impossible ambiguity check with a blind-solve validator. A second, cheap LLM call gets only the clue, the length and the free letters, and must answer. If its answer differs from the target, flag the clue for rewrite, or move the answer into alsoOk if it is a true synonym. Also run a code stem check (answer, its first 5 chars and the family[] entries must not appear in the clue), a word cap after lemma-stripping, and a check that the answer is letters only, 3-12 long.

Band check: lemmatise with a small suffix stripper (-s, -es, -ed, -ing, -ly) before looking up words.js, and treat unknown tokens as out-of-band only when they are over 6 letters. Log the result as a warning, not a hard rejection, for adults.

Ship the pre-generated, validated clue bank for every built-in topic as static JSON, so the core game works offline and needs no LLM calls during class. The free-prompt path should show the preview with a validator badge for each clue (✓ / ⚠).

Steal input: after 'BOARDS UP', show the team chips large at the bottom (touch) and map the keys 1-4 to toggle each team as correct, with Enter to confirm. The whole boards-up step should take about 5 s of teacher input.

Answer privacy: default to a 'Projektör modu' in which the preview grid and answers need hold-to-peek (press and hold, blurred by default), with a small answer chip that shows only while a key is held. Offer a phone QR 'Öğretmen kumandası' (BroadcastChannel is not enough across devices, so keep the printable answer sheet as the guaranteed fallback), and let the second window be optional.

Letter names: ship 26 prerecorded letter-name clips per skin voice (under 150 KB total as Opus/MP3), and never use TTS for single letters. Use TTS only for clues, and detect a missing English voice at setup to switch to 'Öğretmen okur' automatically.
Drop Gogo as a game-specific host. Use the suite-wide Oyun Parkı host or the team animal mascots, with one reusable SVG rig (idle, cheer, shrug, sleep) shared across all kids skins.

Give the kids variant real game tension without harshness: a visible 'sticker meter' that shrinks from gold to silver to bronze as letters are bought, a Gogo/host 'Letter Box' that opens with a sound, and team-alternating rows with an optional class-wide sand timer that only affects the sticker colour. Keep the checklist intact.

Synthesise all short SFX (plink, tick, clack, clock stop, chime) with WebAudio per skin, so there are no sound assets beyond the letter-name clips. Tile flips use CSS 3D transforms, and the score roll-up uses requestAnimationFrame. Honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Setup UX: show only 3 visible choices (content source, mode and the lesson-minutes slider). Everything else sits behind 'Gelişmiş' and is driven by audience presets plus the saved class profile.
Content shape: add optional 'decoy' only when the v1.1 Two-options hint ships. Use media.icon (a key into the shared icon set) in place of media.img, so validation is a simple set membership test.
Keep the TV brand only in the Turkish teacher chrome. Student screens say 'Word Climb', 'Letter Box' or 'Word Show', as already planned.

catalog.rankReason: Kelime Oyunu, the tv2 show adults know (8.3), an M build on c03's word-tile component. Düello is the default for 3+ teams. Kids' free prompts go through a 'picture available' gate, and A1 Genç chant the spelling. There is one finale per audience. It is next wave only because c03 fills the reveal-a-word slot first.

catalog.name: Şifre Kır (Class Codebreaker Wordle)
catalog.familiarAs: Wordle / Flippity WordMaster, with a Blooket Crypto Hack flavour
catalog.oneLiner: Teams take turns guessing the topic's secret word on one big Wordle grid and read the green, yellow and grey tiles together. A free clue appears after row 4. Teams score for every new green and for cracking the word in fewer rows. Every crack ends on a word card with a picture, the sound and a sentence, so the letter logic always lands on meaning.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 1 min). The teacher opens the class profile (e.g. '6-A · A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk'). They then pick a built-in topic (YLE/MEB units for kids, life and work tasks for adults) or type a prompt ('okul eşyaları, 5. sınıf' / 'job interview B1'). The builder keeps a word only if it meets all of these:
- a single word using only a-z
- length in the group's range
- in the guess dictionary
- passes teenSafe for Genç groups
- has a picture for A1/A2 Genç
The setup screen shows the secret list with a 'Değiştir' button on each word. The list disappears the moment 'Başla' is pressed. The lesson-fit timer sets the number of words (about 3-4 min per word).

ONE WORD (Relay mode, the default)
1. FRAME. The screen shows:
   - the grid: word length × 6 rows (7 in Oyun Parkı)
   - a caption ('Round 1 · Animals · 5 letters')
   - the letter keyboard
   - a team strip with an arrow on the active team
   The starting team rotates every word so nobody always guesses blind. An optional warm-up row lets the game (Gogo in Oyun Parkı) play one random valid word first, so row 1 already gives information.
2. TEAM TALK (10/15/20 s by mode), then 'Word up!'. The seat-number spinner picks the speaker in the active team, so nobody is ever named. The speaker spells the guess in English letter names ('B-R-E-A-D'). The teacher or a rotating student typist types it, and the class sees the row before Enter.
3. CHECK. If the word is not in the dictionary, the row wobbles and shows 'Not in the word list'. No row is used and the team tries again. Shift+Enter lets the teacher accept the word and adds it to the class dictionary. In Hard mode, a guess that ignores a revealed green or yellow is refused with a one-line reason.
4. FLIP. The tiles turn one by one, 250 ms apart. In Oyun Parkı the letter names are read aloud.
   - Green with a tick: right letter, right place.
   - Yellow with arrows: the letter is in the word but in the wrong place.
   - Grey with a dot: the letter is not in the word.
   Repeated letters follow Wordle's exact rule: greens are marked first, and yellows only up to the number of unmatched copies in the secret. The keyboard keeps the best colour seen for each letter.
5. WHOLE-CLASS MOMENT (every turn, all modes). Before the flip, the non-active teams predict the number of greens with their fingers (+1 for an exact call in Arena and Stüdyo). After the flip, they copy the row onto their paper or mini-whiteboard grid. In Oyun Parkı everyone spells along with Gogo, then gives thumbs up or down for each picture card that still fits.
6. SCORE AND PASS. The guessing team gets +1 discovery point for each letter it turns green for the first time. The arrow then moves to the next team.
7. CLUES. After row 4 a free clue appears automatically (the picture, or the definition at B levels). Earlier hints are free in Oyun Parkı and cost points in Arena and Stüdyo (see the versions).
8. CRACK. The solving team gets crack points = 7 − row (row 1 = 6, row 6 = 1). The tiles do a bounce wave, then the Word card opens:
   - the picture
   - the word with a speaker button and the IPA
   - an easy definition
   - the example sentence with the word highlighted
   - the Turkish gloss (toggle)
   The class repeats the word twice. In Arena and Stüdyo, any team can earn +1 by using the word in a correct sentence ('Use it!').
9. NOT CRACKED after the last row: 'Last chance'. Every team writes one final guess, then 'Boards up!'. Each correct board scores +1, then the word is revealed. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo 'has the key': the chest opens anyway and the class chants the word.
10. BETWEEN ROUNDS (2-3 words per round): the scoreboard, then a 45 s stirrer. Examples: 'Air spelling' (write the last word in the air with big arm letters) or 'Spell it backwards'.

END. Each mode has its own ending. The class also gets a share grid (coloured squares only, no letters) and the review list.

OTHER MODES
- 'Sınıf vs Kilit' (co-op). Table groups take rows in turn, but the whole class chases one target (e.g. crack it in 4 rows) and earns 1-3 class keys. It is ideal as a 3-4 min 'Günün şifresi' lesson starter or closer.
- 'Düello' (Arena and Stüdyo; 2 teams or two halves of the class). Two grids sit side by side with the same secret, and the teams alternate rows. You see your own letters but only the colours of the opponent's rows, so reading their pattern is part of the deduction. The first team to crack the word wins it. If the team that moved first cracks it, the other team gets one equaliser row; if both crack, both score.

TEACHER KEYS
- Enter: submit
- Backspace: delete a letter
- Shift+Enter: accept the word
- U: undo the last row (for typos; also removes its points)
- H: hint
- C: clue now
- R: reveal
- S: skip or swap the word
- P (hold): peek at the secret for 1 s in the teacher corner
- T: pause
- +: add 10 s
- N: next word
catalog.playerSetup:
Relay (default): 2-6 teams of 3-6 students. Four teams is the sweet spot on a 6-row grid, since each team gets about 1-2 rows per word. Inside each team:
- a speaker picked by the seat-number spinner (never by name)
- team talk before every guess
- optionally, one printed A4 team grid per team to shadow the game
Sınıf vs Kilit: the whole class is one side, and table groups take rows in turn.
Düello: 2 teams or two halves of the class.
One device drives the projector. The teacher types, or a rotating student typist sits at the keyboard; the typist is never the speaker.
skills: speaking (spelling aloud, team talk, Use it! sentences)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO · 'Puzzle Page' (Bulmaca Sayfası)

LOOK. An editorial newspaper puzzle page: cream paper, serif capital tiles, thin rules, and the round and topic in small caps. The dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme is an alternative. The UI uses the system sans. There is no mascot and there are no voice lines; the only caption is neutral ('Round 2 · Travel · 6 letters'). Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs', 'Past Perfect Strangers').

CONTENT. Life and work tasks: travel, job interviews, complaints, money, health, small talk (e.g. FLIGHT, REFUND, SALARY, INVOICE, COMMUTE). Word lengths:
- A1 adults: 4-5 letters
- A2: 5
- B1: 5-6
- B2: 6-7

RULES ON TOP OF THE BASE GAME
1. Scoring: crack points (7 − row) plus +1 for each new green. Optional negatives stay off by default.
2. 'Call it' (wager). Once per word, a team may declare 'Final answer' before Enter. If it is right, the crack points are doubled. If it is wrong, the team loses 2 (only when negatives are on; otherwise 0), and the row is used either way.
3. Hard mode: on by default at B2, optional elsewhere. Revealed greens must stay in place and yellows must be reused.
4. Hint ladder, bought by the active team on request:
   - definition: −1
   - gapped example: −1
   - Turkish gloss: −2 (can be switched off for immersion classes)
   The automatic clue after row 4 is the definition only, with no picture.

MORPH ROUNDS (B1-B2). The secret is a form, not a lemma, and the clue names the operation:
- 'past of THINK' → THOUGHT
- 'plural of CHILD' → CHILDREN
- 'noun of DECIDE' → DECISION (8 letters, B2 Zor only)
- 'adverb of CAREFUL' → CAREFULLY is too long, so the builder picks QUICKLY-length words instead
These are built from gap items that have a base word and from the words.js family data. Grammar is practised through spelling.

'USE IT!' After each crack, any team can earn +1 with a correct sentence using the word. The teacher judges, and a model sentence is on the card.

'HACK' (optional; Yellow harshness; from Blooket Crypto Hack). After cracking a word, the team may answer one bonus MCQ from the pack.
- Right: take 2 points from a team it taps, capped at that team's score.
- Wrong: nothing happens.

DUEL mode is available for two-team classes.

WHO ANSWERS. A rotating spokesperson, with pair consultation inside the team during the 20 s huddle. An answer timer of 30 s is optional.

SOUND. Woodblock tile clicks and a soft piano chord on a crack (0.6 s), with the score rolling up. Music is off.

PACING. Rounds of 3 words (8-12 min each), 2-3 rounds, 20-35 min in total. The last word is the 'Final Cipher': a 7-letter word with crack points doubled.

ENDING
- full scores
- per-team stats (average rows per crack, greens found, Call-its landed)
- the share grid
- the 'Kaçırılanlar' list: each missed or late word with its definition, example and the row it fell on, exportable to the word notebook or flashcards
catalog.teenVersion:
There are two skins with genuinely different rules. The audience mode picks the skin; the level stays separate.

OYUN PARKI (9-11) · 'Treasure Lock' (Hazine Kilidi)

LOOK. A cream background with warm bright colours. A big wooden treasure chest whose brass lock is the grid. Rounded tiles with lowercase letters in the Andika-type font. Animal team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit). Gogo the parrot sits on the chest, taps each tile with his beak as it flips, and reads the letter names at 0.8x speed.

RULE CARD. In Turkish for the teacher to read, with three pictograms; it takes 20 s:
1. Pick a picture or say a word.
2. Spell it together. Green tick = right place, yellow arrows = move it, grey = not in the word.
3. Open the chest. Every helper gets a star.

PRACTICE ROUND. Gogo plays one 25 s word that does not score. The secret is 'frog': he tries 'fish', the f turns green, he tries 'frog', and the lid pops.

PICTURE BANK. 6 cards at A1 Genç, 8-9 at A2 Genç. They show topic words with the same number of letters, and the secret is among them. A team guesses by tapping a card or by saying any real word.
- After each flip, the class gives thumbs up or down for each remaining card ('Does it fit?').
- At A1 Genç, cards that no longer fit fade by themselves after the vote.
- At A2 Genç, the teacher taps them out as the class calls 'Out!'.

WHOLE-CLASS RESPONSE every turn: everyone spells the guess with Gogo while the tiles flip, then comes the thumbs vote.

CLUES (all free)
- after row 2: Gogo says the first sound ('It starts with /f/')
- after row 3: the first letter appears as a ghost tile
- after row 4: Gogo reads the picture sentence ('It's green. It can jump.')

WORDS AND GRID. 3-4 letters, 7 rows, and no repeated letters at A1 Genç. The keyboard is in ABC order with big keys.

TIMERS. No timer by default. If it is switched on, it is a calm 40 s ring that never turns red, with a marimba chime at 0. Team talk lasts 10 s.

SCORING
- The team that opens the chest gets 2 stars.
- Every team whose guess found a new green that word gets 1 helper star.
- Stars never go down. There are no steals and no speed points.
- If all 7 rows pass, 'Gogo has the key!': the chest opens anyway, the class chants the word twice, and every team gets an effort star for the class album.

WRONG WORDS. Gogo tilts his head ('Hmm, is that a word?'). The team tries again and no row is lost.

CELEBRATION. At most 2 s: the lid pops, stickers fly out and Gogo dances. Confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale.

SOUND. Marimba notes that climb with each green and a soft wooden tok for grey. No buzzers.

PACING. 3 rounds of 2 words (3-4 min each), 15-20 min in total. Between rounds there is a 45 s stirrer: 'Air spelling' with big arm letters, or 'Letter bodies' (make the first letter with your body).

ENDING. Every team gets a title: Sharp Eyes (most greens), Best Spellers, Super Helpers or Brave Guessers. The class album gets a sticker page with the pictures of the cracked words.

KIDS CHECKLIST: 3 rules; explainable in 20 s with pictograms; no elimination; no score below 0; a whole-class response every turn; the only 'failure' is Gogo opening the chest.

ARENA (12-14) · 'Cipher Grid'

LOOK. Dark navy or charcoal, with neon cells in the team colours and a condensed display font in capitals. Geometric emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond). No mascot and no pastels. Every game is framed as a 'Match'. In 10 s, each team picks its emblem, its colour and a 3-word motto ('No letter left').

RULE CARD. In English, with a Turkish toggle:
1. One real word per turn.
2. Green = LOCKED, yellow = SIGNAL (wrong slot), grey = NOISE.
3. Fewer rows = more points. New greens score, and streaks multiply.

WORDS AND GRID. 5 letters at B1 Genç and 5-6 at B2 Genç, with 6 rows. An A1/A2 Genç class moved to Arena (grade 6+) keeps 4-letter words, the picture bank and read-aloud, in Arena styling.

TIMERS. A 30 s answer ring in the team's colour, and 15 s of team talk.

WHOLE-CLASS RESPONSE every turn. The non-active teams flash fingers for the number of greens they predict (+1 for an exact call) and track the grid on mini-whiteboards.

POINTS
- +1 for each new green
- crack = 7 − row
- 'Signal streak': a team that scores on 3 of its turns in a row gets x1.5, and 5 in a row gets x2 (based on accuracy only)

HINTS. They cost points but never take a score below 0:
- first letter: −1
- 'Scan' (a 50:50 on the keyboard): greys out half of the untried letters that are not in the word, −1
- gapped example sentence: −2
The definition after row 4 is free.

STEAL BY ANSWERING ('Intercept'). From row 4 on, when the active team misses, the first team to raise its emblem card gets one spoken guess in 10 s. If it is right, that team cracks the word. If it is wrong, nobody loses anything.

YELLOW HARSHNESS (opt-in). 'Hack': after a crack, the team answers a bonus MCQ to take 3 points from a team it taps. The amount is scaled down from the standard 5 because this game's points are smaller, and it is capped at that team's score.

DUEL mode is available for two-team matches.

COMMENTATOR STRIP, at most once per turn: 'SIGNAL x3', 'CLEAN CRACK' (a crack on row 1-2), 'CLUTCH' (a crack on row 6).

CELEBRATION. A crack plays a 1.2 s 'DECRYPTED' glitch plus a synth sting. Each cracked word becomes a badge inside the team's emblem.

PACING. Rounds of 2 words (5-7 min each), 3 rounds, 20-25 min in total. Interludes are optional.

ENDING. A podium plus stat awards: Longest streak, Clean crack, Scout (most greens) and Comeback. There is never a last place. The class share grid closes the match.
catalog.levelTuning:
Two dials sit on top of the level:
- Kolay/Orta/Zor shifts the word length by −1/0/+1, sets the word-band mix (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words) and sets the picture bank size.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole profile by one level.

GENÇ GROUPS
- A1 Genç: 3-4 letters (cat, fish, cake, frog). A1 YLE/MEB picture words only, and no repeated letters in secrets. 7 rows. A picture bank of 6 that fades by itself. Lowercase tiles and an ABC keyboard. Letter names are read at 0.8x. Clues are pictures and sounds, 0-4 words ('It's green.').
- A2 Genç: 4-5 letters (horse, apple, train). 7 rows. The picture bank has 8-9 cards (or is off), and the class crosses cards out. Repeated letters are allowed, with a '×2' tip on the Word card. Clues are 8 words or fewer ('It lives in the sea.').
- B1 Genç (Arena by default): 5 letters, 6 rows, no picture bank. Clues are 14 words or fewer, and hints cost points. A first taste of Morph rounds with a few irregular pasts (WROTE, SPOKE).
- B2 Genç: 5-6 letters of richer concrete vocabulary (PLANET, ISLAND, CASTLE, INSECT). Clues are 20 words or fewer. Riddle clues (3 steps, hard to easy). Morph rounds use pasts and comparatives (BIGGER). Never abstract debate words.

ADULT GROUPS
- A1: 4-5 letters from the A1 band, with no repeated letters by default. 6 rows, and the warm-up row is on. Clues are 10 words or fewer, with an optional picture, and the TR gloss is available.
- A2: 5 letters (mixed 4-6), from the A1-A2 band. Repeated letters are allowed. Light Morph rounds: irregular pasts (BOUGHT, TAUGHT) and plurals (BOXES).
- B1: 5-6 letters from the B1 band, including word families. Hard mode is optional. The clue is the definition (25 words or fewer). Morph rounds: irregular pasts, comparatives and -ly adverbs.
- B2: 6-7 letters (8 at Zor), from the B2 band. Hard mode is on. The clue is the definition only (40 words or fewer, no picture). Morph rounds use word-family changes (DECISION, ABILITY). Riddle clues, 'Call it' and the Final Cipher are all in play.

GUESS DICTIONARY. Kids' groups accept any real word but steer guesses through the picture bank. The adults' strict mode accepts words.js lemmas, generated inflections, irregular forms, UK/US spellings and the class dictionary.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 3-4 for a single 'Günün şifresi' warm-up word · Oyun Parkı 15-20 · Arena 20-25 · Stüdyo 20-35
catalog.contentShape:
SECRET WORDS come from 'vocab' items with form='word'. The fields used:
- term: a-z only; code computes the length and whether letters repeat
- media.emoji or media.img: required for A1/A2 Genç; also used on the Word card
- defEasy or def: the automatic clue, capped at the group's word limit
- defTr: the TR gloss hint
- example and gap: the gapped-example hint and the Word card
- ipa, syll
- family[]: Morph rounds at B levels
- concrete

OTHER ITEM TYPES
- 'gap' items with a base and a one-word answer feed Morph rounds. The secret is answers[0][0] (e.g. THOUGHT); the clue is 'past of THINK' or the gap sentence.
- 'riddle' items give the optional 3-step clue ladder. The answer must be one word of a valid length.
- 'category-list' members supply same-length decoys for the picture bank, plus the topic label and emoji for the round caption.
- 'mcq' items are used only for Intercept/Hack bonus questions and Last-chance tiebreaks.

COMPUTED PER PACK: a byLength index, hasRepeat, the CEFR band from words.js, inDictionary and teenSafe.

LLM PATH. The teacher's prompt (possibly in Turkish) returns vocab and riddle items. The model never counts letters or sets lengths; code does both. If too few words fit, the builder widens the length by ±1 and tells the teacher, e.g. '5 harfli yalnızca 4 kelime bulundu; 4 ve 6 harfliler eklendi'.

GUESS DICTIONARY. Built once, about 20k forms, gzipped to roughly 50-100 KB. It contains:
- words.js lemmas
- generated inflections: -s/-es/-ies, -ed/-ied, doubled consonants, -ing, -er/-est
- irregular forms from the grammar banks
- UK/US variants
- the class dictionary (words the teacher accepted)
Proper nouns, abbreviations and a blocklist are removed.

A pack is playable when it has at least 6 secret-ready words in the group's length range (at least 4 with pictures for Oyun Parkı).
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP (saved in the local class profile)
- Mode: Relay / Sınıf vs Kilit / Düello
- Content: topic or free prompt; the word count, or lesson-fit minutes
- Word length: automatic by level, a fixed 3-8, or mixed
- Rows: 5-8
- Repeated letters: on/off
- Morph rounds: on/off
- Picture bank: off / 6 / 9 cards; cards fade by themselves or the teacher taps them out
- Warm-up row: on/off
- Dictionary: strict with teacher override; loose (any real-looking word, for very young classes); or topic-only
- Hard mode
- Clues: the automatic clue appears after row 2-5 or never; the clue type is picture, definition, gap sentence or riddle
- Hints: the hint ladder and its costs; the TR gloss on/off
- Timing: Süresiz / 30 / 40 / 60 s with +10 s; huddle length
- Scoring: discovery points, green-count calls, 'Call it', negatives, 'Use it!'
- Intercept on/off
- Harshness: Green / Yellow / Red (Hack needs Yellow or higher)
- Comeback: Off / Light / Strong. At Light, the trailing team picks the next topic card, and its crack earns +2 Slipstream.
- Display: lowercase or UPPERCASE tiles; ABC or QWERTY keyboard; letter-name audio; reduced motion; colour-blind palette; sound and music

WORD LIST (setup screen only; it disappears at Başla)
- Preview, reorder or swap any word.
- Add your own words. They are validated live: 'not a-z', 'not in dictionary', '9 letters: too long'.

IN GAME
- Keys: U undo the last row, Shift+Enter accept a word, H hint, C clue now, R reveal, S skip, P hold to peek, T pause, + add 10 s, N next word.
- Manual point adjustment with +/- on each team chip; never below 0 in Nazik mode.
- A 'Teacher panel in a second window' option for dual-screen setups, so the secret never appears on the projector.
catalog.delightDetails:
- The classic staggered tile flip, with sound matched to the mode: marimba notes that climb with each green (Oyun Parkı), synth blips (Arena), woodblock (Stüdyo). On a crack the row does a bounce wave.
- Letter names spoken in English as the tiles flip. This targets Turkish learners' typical E/I, A/E, G/J and Y/W mix-ups, and a small 'letter names' strip sits on the pause screen.
- Shapes as well as colours on tiles and keys: a tick for green, arrows for yellow, a dot for grey. The keyboard keeps a colour map, and kids get an ABC-order keyboard with big keys.
- Ghost tiles: the first-letter hint appears as a faint letter in the next empty row.
- Picture-bank cards fade softly and slide aside. A card sparkles when the class correctly calls it 'Out!'.
- Gogo perches on the chest, taps each tile with his beak, tilts his head at non-words, 'has the key' when a word goes unsolved, and sleeps on the lock on the pause screen. The Arena pause screen reads 'SIGNAL LOST'.
- Arena details: the 'DECRYPTED' glitch, a commentator strip at most once per turn, team emblems and mottos, and each cracked word stamped as a badge inside the team's emblem.
- The Word card after every crack: picture, sound, IPA, definition, and the example sentence with the word highlighted. A '×2' tip appears when the secret has a double letter.
- 'Nasıl çözdük?': a row-by-row replay of the solving path after each word.
- The class share grid: the game summarised in coloured squares only, with no letters. It can be printed for the class album or the board ('7-B · 6 words · 23 greens').
- A printable A4 team sheet with 6 blank rows and an alphabet strip for crossing letters out. Kids colour it with green and yellow crayons, which keeps every student busy.
- Turkish keyboard care: the I key's 'ı' is mapped to i, letters are uppercased in the en-US locale so 'i' never becomes 'İ', and ş ğ ç ö ü get a gentle 'English letters only'.
- A teacher Undo for typos, which also takes back any points from that row.
- Reduced motion swaps every flip and burst for a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
1. Letter logic without meaning. Every crack ends on the Word card, with choral repetition and 'Use it!'. Kids choose words from pictures. The review list feeds the word notebook.

2. Later teams inherit earlier teams' information. The starting team rotates each word, the warm-up row gives row 1 information, and +1 per new green rewards informative early guesses. Duel mode handles two teams.

3. One strong speller runs the team. The spinner picks the speaker, the typist is a different student, and team talk comes before every guess.

4. Dictionary gaps ('HOUSES is a word!'). The dictionary accepts lemmas, generated inflections, irregular forms and UK/US pairs. The teacher override is saved in the class dictionary. A rude guess gets the same neutral 'Not in the word list' and never appears on the grid.

5. Turkish keyboards and locale. The I key types 'ı', and uppercasing in the Turkish locale turns 'i' into 'İ'. The fix is to normalise to en-US and map ı and İ to i and I.

6. The secret leaks on the projector. The list vanishes at Başla, peeking is hold-to-show, and a second-window teacher panel is offered.

7. Colour-only feedback fails about 8% of boys. Shapes are on by default, and a colour-blind palette is available.

8. Repeated-letter feedback confuses beginners. A1 secrets have no repeats, colouring follows Wordle's exact rule, and the Word card shows a '×2' tip.

9. The game runs slow with 6 teams. Recommend 4 teams, and use 2-3 words per round, the lesson-fit timer and the automatic clue.

10. LLM content errors. Code, not the model, computes the length and checks the dictionary, the CEFR band and teenSafe.

11. Weak alphabet knowledge among 9-year-olds. The game offers the picture bank, spoken letter names, the ABC keyboard and free clues.

12. Scope. Duel mode and Morph rounds can ship in a second pass without changing the core.
reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Hangman (share the word-guess family, content packs and Word card; keep as separate game)

issues: MINUTE-BY-MINUTE PACE IS UNDERESTIMATED. One Relay turn with 28 kids runs: spinner (5 s), team talk (10-15 s), the child spelling aloud in English letter names (15-30 s, with E/I, A/E, G/J and Y/W slips and restarts), typing plus a read-back, finger predictions from 3 other teams (10 s), a flip with every letter read at 0.8x (about 4-5 s), a thumbs vote per remaining picture card (15-20 s), then copying the row onto paper. That is 60-90 s per row. A 5-row word is 5-7 min before the Word card and choral repetition, not 3-4. The 15-20 min Oyun Parkı plan (6 words) will really fit 3-4 words.

ONLY ONE CHILD IS ACTIVE AT A TIME. In a 7-child team, one speaks and the rest wait. For the other 21 students the 'whole-class moment' is finger-counting and copying the row. Copying is quiet busywork for some kids and a chance to chat for most. Once the class has lost the thread, the thumbs vote on each picture card turns into noise.

TURN ORDER DECIDES WHO SCORES. Wordle information builds up, so the team that gets row 3-5 usually cracks it, and crack points (up to 6) dwarf the +1 per green. Rotating the starting team only evens this out over many words, and a 15-20 min kids game has just 3-6 words. With 4 teams and 6 words, some teams never hold the 'good' row. Kids see the win as random: 'they only won because it was their turn'.

THE PICTURE BANK MAKES KIDS' ROUNDS TRIVIAL, OR IS HARD TO BUILD. With 6 same-length cards that fade by themselves, row 1 or 2 usually leaves 1-2 cards, so the deduction collapses into picking a picture. Building 6 picturable, same-length, no-repeat 3-4 letter A1 words per topic is also hard (a 'school things' topic: pen, bag, ruler, book, desk...). The builder will often widen the length and break the 'same length' logic.

DUEL MODE CANNOT WORK ON ONE SHARED SCREEN. 'You see your own letters but only the colours of the opponent's rows' is impossible when both halves of the class look at the same projector. Either both teams see everything, or the mode needs devices.

THE SECRET LEAKS ON A PUBLIC-SCHOOL SMART BOARD. On a MEB board, the board is the teacher's only screen. The setup list with 'Değiştir' buttons is shown in front of the class (teachers set up after the students arrive), a 'P hold to peek' on the board is seen by 28 kids, and a 'second-window teacher panel' needs hardware almost no Turkish classroom has.

THE TEACHER CONTROLS ASSUME A KEYBOARD. U, H, C, R, S, P, T, +, N and Shift+Enter mean nothing to a teacher standing at a touch board, or holding a wireless clicker in an adult class. Rotating a student typist onto the board brings kids crowding to the board, adds 20-30 s per turn, and adds typos (so more Undo).

ARENA SCORING IS OVERLOADED FOR CLASSROOM BOOKKEEPING. It stacks new-green points, crack points, the x1.5/x2 streak multiplier (which produces fractions), exact-green calls, three priced hints, Intercept, Hack, Comeback Slipstream, Use it! and commentator strips. The teacher cannot explain or check why a team has 17.5, and 13-year-olds will argue about every point.

INTERCEPT REWARDS SPEED AND CAUSES CHAOS. 'The first team to raise its emblem card' leads to disputes over who was first, shouting, and the strongest, fastest kid dominating. It clashes with Nazik mod, and Arena keeps Nazik mod on.

SPELLING WITH LETTER NAMES IS A HIDDEN BARRIER. Many Turkish 5th-6th graders do not know English letter names reliably. They will spell in Turkish ('be-re-e'), and the teacher has to decide on the spot whether that counts. Weaker kids then avoid being picked by the spinner, which is the opposite of the goal.

PART OF THE WHOLE-CLASS MOMENT NEEDS MATERIALS. Mini-whiteboards and printed A4 grids per team are rare in public schools. 'Boards up!' for the last chance assumes every team has a board and a marker.
SIX TEAMS BREAKS IT. With 6 rows and 6 teams, each team gets about 1 row per word, waits 5 turns, and loses interest. The game allows it and recommends against it, but a crowded class will choose it.

ADULTS: Wordle is a solo puzzle many adults already play on their phones. With 10 adults in 2-3 teams, handing over the turn is slower than a pair solving it on paper, and strong solvers get impatient during others' turns. The adult features (Morph rounds, Call it, the Kaçırılanlar list) are good, but a 20-35 min session is too long for this mechanic. Adults tire of it after about 4-5 words.

IT OVERLAPS WITH HANGMAN. Hangman's Arena skin is already 'Code Breaker', a vault with laser locks, while this game's Arena skin is 'Cipher Grid'. Two spelling-deduction games with the same hacker/vault theme in one suite will look like duplicates to the teacher and to the students.

THERE ARE TOO MANY TEACHER CONTROLS. About 20 setup dials (dictionary modes, clue row, clue type, hint costs, harshness, comeback, keyboard layout...) is a lot to face with 28 kids waiting. The saved class profile helps only from the second use onwards.

THE DICTIONARY REJECTS CHILDREN'S GUESSES. 'Not in the word list' followed by 'try again' can loop: a child offers three misspelled words in a row while the class waits. That means dead time, and public embarrassment for the speaker.
fixes: Plan with honest numbers. Budget 5-6 min per word in Oyun Parkı and 4-5 in Stüdyo, and let the lesson-fit timer compute the word count from those figures. Make Oyun Parkı 2 rounds of 2 words (about 20 min). Make 'Günün şifresi' (co-op, 1 word) the headline use case on the menu.

Make the co-op mode 'Sınıf vs Kilit' the default for Oyun Parkı. The whole class is one side, and the competition moves to 'class keys vs the lock'. This removes the turn-order luck, which is the core fairness flaw for kids. Keep team Relay as an Arena/Stüdyo option.

In Relay, cut crack points sharply: a flat +2 for the crack, and +1 for each new green, grey elimination or yellow placement. Alternatively, split the crack points between the cracking team and the team whose previous row gave the most new information. At minimum, show a 'row luck' note and rotate the starting team within the round, not only between words.

Replace the per-card thumbs vote and the copying onto paper with one snappy whole-class action per turn: 'Show me 1-5 fingers: how many greens?' before the flip. After the flip, one choral 'Out!' for the eliminated cards, which the teacher taps once and which then fade. Make the A4 grid an optional printable for early finishers, not something the turn depends on.

Make the picture bank a hint, not the default. It starts hidden and appears after row 2 (A1 Genç) or row 3 (A2 Genç), with 6 cards of mixed lengths so the letter count still matters. Require the builder to find at least 6 picturable topic words; otherwise it says so and switches to 'Clue mode' instead of silently widening the length.

Let the guess be given by tapping a picture card or by a teacher-typed word. Accept Turkish-alphabet letter names without penalty in Oyun Parkı. Add a 20 s 'alphabet song strip' pre-teach at the first launch of each class profile, and let the speaker pass to a partner ('Phone a friend') once per word, with no penalty.

Drop Duel mode, or redesign it to show everything on the shared screen: two grids with the same secret, all letters visible, teams alternating. That is simply a race and needs no hidden information. Hidden-info Duel can come later as a device mode.

Build for one screen. The setup word list is blurred by default and shown only while held. Starting 'Başla' in 'projector-safe' mode hides everything. Peek moves to the teacher's phone through a QR companion page (secret, skip, reveal, +/- points), which also works as a clicker for adult classes. Drop the second-window panel as the main solution.

Put a touch-first teacher dock on screen: a small, collapsible corner bar with Undo, Clue, Reveal, Skip, Pause and Next, and 2-tap confirmation for the destructive ones. Keep the keyboard shortcuts only as extras for projector plus laptop. By default the teacher types, not a student at the board.

Simplify Arena scoring to three sources: new greens, crack points on a smaller scale, and a streak shown as a flame counter that adds +1 instead of multiplying. Remove Hack and green-count bets from Arena by default. The whole score should be explainable in one sentence.

Replace Intercept's first-to-raise race with 'Boards up': every non-active team writes one guess, all are revealed at once, and each correct team gets +1. That is fair, silent, whole-class and consistent with Nazik mod.

Differentiate from Hangman. Give Arena here a non-heist theme (e.g. 'Signal / satellite decoding' or 'Lab analysis'), or have Hangman Arena drop 'Code Breaker'. In the game menu, pitch this game as the '3-minute lesson starter' and Hangman as the 'party round'.
Reduce setup to three visible choices (Topic, Mode, Minutes) plus an 'Ayrıntılar' drawer. Ship presets per audience mode so the first launch takes under 60 s.

Add a dead-time guard. After 2 rejected non-words in a row, show 'Try a picture card?' in kids' modes, or auto-accept any plausible spelling in the 'loose' dictionary. Never say the rejected word aloud.

For adults, cap sessions at 15-20 min or 5-6 words, offer a 'pairs on paper' parallel variant where every pair solves and the screen reveals the answer, and keep Morph rounds and the Final Cipher as the highlight.

issues: A1 Genç (9-10, barely reading) is the weakest fit. Wordle's core skill is orthographic deduction: you have to recall English spelling and know the English letter names, and Turkish kids at A1 often don't know those yet (E/I, A/E, G/J, Y/W). The 'yellow = right letter, wrong slot' idea is abstract for a 9-year-old. The picture bank rescues the game, but it also turns it into 'pick 1 of 6 pictures by elimination', so the letter logic mostly disappears and many turns become picture taps with no spelling.

With a 6-card bank of 3-4 letter words, one or two flips usually leave a single card, so the 7-row grid and the ghost-tile/first-sound clue ladder are oversized. The word is often cracked on row 2-3 by elimination, not by spelling, and the 'helper star per new green' rewards luck.

The language learning is mostly spelling and form. During guessing, students retrieve any English word of the right length ('BREAD' in a Travel round), so what gets practised is off-topic word recall, not the topic vocabulary. The meaning work is packed into the Word card at the end, which takes about 20 s of each 3-4 minutes.

Engagement per student is low. With 4 teams on a 6-row grid, each team produces 1-2 guesses per word, and the non-active teams' 'predict the number of greens with fingers' is a thin, numeric, non-linguistic task. Copying the row onto a whiteboard is clerical work. For adults, a 30-minute session can feel slow.

The dictionary has a correctness risk: generated inflections (-s/-es/-ies, -ed, doubled consonants, -er/-est) will accept over-regularised non-words (CHILDS, GOED, BADDER, FUNNER) unless they are checked against a real word list. Accepting those actively teaches errors. It can also reject real forms missing from words.js (proper-ish common words, compounds, slang teens know).

The picture requirement for A1/A2 Genç is hard to meet from LLM prompts. Emoji coverage for MEB/YLE topics is patchy: an 'okul eşyaları' prompt yields ruler, eraser, rubber and sharpener, most of which have no emoji. The 'at least 4 with pictures' playability rule will fail often, and the fallback is unspecified.

The MEB and topic vocabulary for Genç groups contains many words outside the 3-5 letter a-z single-word window (pencil case, T-shirt, sharpener, grandmother). The length filter silently drops the most curriculum-relevant items and keeps short generic ones, so the round no longer matches the unit being taught.

B2 adults: 6-7 letter secrets with Hard mode on and 6 rows, split across 4 teams, give a high failure rate. Each team sees one row and must deduce from other teams' guesses; with 7 letters the game often ends in 'Last chance', which is anticlimactic.

Morph rounds are the best language payoff for B levels, but the spec is self-contradictory (DECISION is 8 letters, and CAREFULLY is 'too long, so pick QUICKLY-length words'). There is no rule for the clue when the base itself reveals most letters: 'past of THINK' leaves only OUGHT to deduce, which is trivial.
The Arena 'Signal streak' multipliers (x1.5) on small integer scores produce fractions. Streaks also depend on turn order and luck, not on language.

Rule load for adults and Arena is heavy: discovery points, crack points, Call it, green-count calls, Intercept, Hack, streaks, hint costs, Use it!. The actual language moments (Use it!, the Word card) are worth the least, while letter luck is worth the most.
It overlaps with Hangman in the suite (both are letter-guessing spelling games). Without a distinct learning goal it adds breadth, not pedagogy.

Some Turkish-L1 specifics are missing: the phonics mismatch (Turkish spelling is phonemic, so kids spell by sound: 'FİŞ' for fish, 'KAT' for cat) is not addressed in the feedback. Wrong vowels are the most common error and get only a grey dot, with no teaching moment.
fixes: A1 Genç: replace free deduction with a 'Picture Wordle' variant. The team must SPELL the chosen picture card aloud with Gogo, letter by letter, before it is submitted (tap the card, then the class spells it chorally while the tiles fill). This keeps spelling practice even when the guess comes from the bank. Add a 'sound-it-out' mode where tiles flip with the phoneme, not the letter name, and a teacher toggle for letter names vs sounds.

Size the kids' bank and grid together: 6 cards means 4 rows, 9 cards means 5 rows. Add 1-2 same-shape near-miss decoys (cat/cap/car) chosen by code for maximum letter overlap, so every row actually needs letter reading rather than picture elimination.

Add a 'Topic-only' guess rule (on by default for Genç and optional for adults): valid guesses must come from the pack's category-list and vocab items, shown as a word wall at B levels. Guessing then becomes on-topic lexical retrieval, and every guess recycles target vocabulary.

Make the whole-class moment linguistic: non-active teams write on their whiteboards which topic words still fit (or one candidate word) before the reveal, and score +1 if a board holds the secret. Drop the green-count finger prediction or keep it only as an Arena extra.

Dictionary: accept generated inflections only when they also appear in a bundled real-word frequency list (e.g. a SCOWL/wordfreq top-40k); give irregular lemmas' regular forms (CHILDS, GOED) a teaching reject message ('child → children'). Keep the teacher override.

Picture fallback: allow a curated self-hosted icon set per YLE/MEB topic (not emoji only). If pictures are still missing, let the teacher snap or upload an image or switch that word to a spoken-clue card. State the fallback in the builder ('3 kelimenin resmi yok: sesli ipucuna geçildi').

Curriculum fidelity: for Genç groups, show the dropped unit words at setup ('pencil case: 2 kelime, atlandı') and route multi-word and long items into the Word card review list, so the unit's key words still appear even if they cannot be secrets.
Balance B2 adults: default to 6 letters and 7 rows with 4 teams, or suggest Düello. Make the automatic definition clue appear after row 3 at 7 letters. Move 7-letter words to the Final Cipher only.

Clean up Morph rounds: cap secrets at the group's max length, drop the spec's contradictory examples, and choose operations where the form change is the puzzle (irregular pasts, plurals, suffix changes). Show the base word as the clue but score only the letters that differ from the base, so it isn't trivial.

Re-weight scoring towards language: 'Use it!' worth 2 (Stüdyo) and a mandatory class sentence at A levels. Replace the x1.5 streak with an integer +1 streak bonus, and cut Hack from Arena defaults (keep opt-in in Stüdyo only).

Differentiate from Hangman: position Şifre Kır as the deduction and spelling-pattern game at A2+/Arena/Stüdyo, and recommend Hangman's Balloon Rescue for A1 Genç. Alternatively, share one letter-game engine with both as modes, so the suite doesn't carry two near-duplicates.

Add L1-aware feedback: after each word, a 'Tuzak harf' tip when the class misplaced a typical Turkish-learner confusion (vowel letter names, c/k, silent e, double letters), and the pause-screen letter-name strip read aloud on tap.

reviews.mergeWith: Hangman (share the word-guess family, content packs and Word card; keep as separate game)
issues: The core is cheap and low-risk: a grid, a keyboard, the exact Wordle scoring algorithm, a tile flip in CSS and the Word card. It could be a strong S/M game. The written design is not that, though. It stacks Relay, co-op, Duel, Morph rounds, Call it, Hack, Intercept, signal streaks, green-count bets, a picture bank, a warm-up row, hard mode, a hint ladder, comeback, a commentator, a share grid, a replay and a printable sheet. It also has three skins, each with different timers and scoring. At that scope it is a real L. The build and QA cost sits in the combinations of all these dials, not in the Wordle core.

Duel mode breaks on one projector. 'You see your own letters but only the colours of the opponent's rows' cannot work when both teams share one screen, and the speaker spells each guess out loud to the whole room. The hidden-information premise disappears.

Relay scoring is mostly turn luck. Every team sees every row, so the team whose turn comes when the information is enough to solve collects the crack points (7 − row, up to 6). Crack points are also lowest on late rows, which are exactly when a solve is most likely. +1 per new green is too small to balance this. With 4-6 teams, a team's score depends on its seat in the rotation more than on its deduction.

The guess dictionary is the biggest technical risk. Rule-based inflection of words.js lemmas over-generates non-words ('childs', 'runned'), while irregulars and common words outside Oxford 5000 (e.g. 'pizza', names of foods and brands) are missing. A rejected 'HOUSES' in front of a class breaks trust. The dictionary is also 50-100 KB gzipped plus a blocklist, so it must be built at build time and lazy-loaded, not computed in the browser from the 1.4 MB words.js.

Rude or blocklisted guesses cannot really be 'never shown'. The speaker says the letters aloud and the typist types them before Enter, so the row is visible while it is being typed. Only a filter before any tile renders, together with a neutral wobble, prevents the grid from showing it.

Pictures for the A1/A2 Genç secrets and for the picture bank decoys are a real asset cost. Emoji render inconsistently or are missing on the school smartboards common in Turkey (older Android boards, Windows Segoe glyphs), and several YLE words have no emoji at all. LLM-generated words for kids will often have no picture, and then the pack fails the 'at least 4 with pictures' check.

The audio depends on speechSynthesis, which is unreliable on classroom smartboards (en-US voices are often missing on Turkish Windows and Android installs). Both letter names at 0.8x and word pronunciation need a fallback.

The kids version is heavier than the checklist claims. It adds helper stars, a picture-bank vote on every card after every flip, three clue stages, a spinner, team talk and a copy-the-row step. A thumbs vote on 8-9 cards after each flip takes about 30-60 s per turn. Yellow ('in the word, wrong place') is abstract for 9-year-olds. With a 6-card bank and 3-4 letter words, the game quickly becomes 'pick a picture', so letter deduction is barely used.

Pacing is optimistic. Each turn has a spinner, 10-20 s of talk, spoken spelling, typing, green predictions, a flip, copying the row and scoring. That is roughly 45-70 s, so a 5-row word with 4 teams takes 4-6 min, not 3-4 min.
The green-count prediction (+1 for an exact call) makes the teacher track several teams' finger counts on every turn. That bookkeeping will be skipped in practice.

Morph rounds are underspecified and partly incoherent. The 'CAREFULLY is too long, so pick QUICKLY-length' example shows that family data does not reliably produce valid lengths. Irregular forms also need a separate source; words.js family data is not verified.

It overlaps with Hangman: both are spelling guessing games with a secret word, and Hangman's Arena skin is literally 'Code Breaker' with a vault. Two vault or cipher themed word-guessers in one suite will feel like duplicates.

LLM content is actually the most reliable part here. The model only proposes words and code filters them. However, the LLM's easy clues and definitions can contain the secret word or its stem, or exceed the word caps. They need validation just as the words do.
fixes: Ship an MVP in two phases. Phase 1: Relay plus 'Sınıf vs Kilit' co-op (the 'Günün şifresi' warm-up); Wordle scoring with shapes; three skins; picture bank for Oyun Parkı; the automatic clue plus one hint; the Word card; teacher keys U/Shift+Enter/R/S/N; a second-window teacher panel over BroadcastChannel; the share grid. Phase 2: Morph, Call it, Intercept, Hack, streaks, the commentator and the printable sheet. Cut green-count betting as a scored mechanic and keep it as an unscored 'fingers up' moment.
Remove Duel or redesign it for one screen. Either (a) both teams see everything and simply race on separate grids with the same secret, or (b) drop it entirely. Do not ship hidden-letter Duel.

Fix Relay scoring so it rewards information rather than position. Option 1: a flat crack bonus (+3), keep +1 per new green, and add +1 per new yellow. Option 2: make co-op the default for kids and use Relay only in Arena and Stüdyo. Either way, the starting team keeps rotating.

Build the dictionary offline with a Node script run at build time: words.js lemmas plus a curated irregular-forms table plus a hand-checked list of the top ~10k frequency words (not generated inflections alone). Ship one sorted .txt.gz per word length, lazy-fetched on game start (about 20-60 KB each), and binary-search it. In the kids groups use the 'loose' mode by default, where the picture bank and any a-z word the teacher accepts are valid.
Check every guess against the blocklist before any tile renders. While typing, show the letters in a neutral 'pending' row and clear it on a blocklist hit.

Commission or source one shared, licensed SVG icon set (about 300-400 YLE/MEB concrete nouns) that all the games use. Give kids secrets only from words that have an icon; the builder should reject LLM kid words that have none and tell the teacher. Use emoji only as a fallback, and never for secrets.
Record the 26 English letter names (about 60 KB of Opus/MP3) and ship them. Use speechSynthesis only for word audio, with IPA plus a 'repeat after the teacher' fallback when no English voice exists.

Simplify Oyun Parkı. No yellow at A1 Genç: show only green or grey plus picture elimination, and add yellow ('it's in the word!') at A2 Genç. Replace the per-card thumbs vote with a single class call ('Which pictures are out?'), and let the game fade the cards automatically. Make it co-op against the lock by default, with helper stars only as decoration.

Re-estimate pacing at about 5 min per word with 4 teams. Set the lesson-fit timer to 4-5 min per word, make the automatic clue after row 3 the default for kids, and make copying rows onto paper an optional printout, not a step on every turn.
Validate LLM clues as well: reject any clue that contains the secret, a shared stem of 4+ letters, or more words than the group's cap. Regenerate or fall back to the words.js definition.
Make Morph rounds a curated static table (irregular pasts, plurals, comparatives with lengths precomputed), not a runtime derivation from family data. B2 word-family items only if they are verified.

Separate it from Hangman. Give it non-vault skins (e.g. Oyun Parkı treasure chest, Arena 'signal grid'/radar, Stüdyo puzzle page) and move the 'Code Breaker'/vault theme away from one of the two. In the hub, present both under one 'Kelime Tahmin' family, with shared content packs and a shared Word card component.

Share components: build the Word card, the team strip, the timer ring, the teacher panel and the second-window sync once, and reuse them across the suite. Game-specific work here then comes down to the grid, the evaluator, the keyboard and the skins, which keeps it a real M.

catalog.rankReason: Wordle, an M build on the shared word-tile component (adult 7.7, weak for A1 Genç). Ship Relay plus the co-op 'Sınıf vs Kilit' (as the 'Günün şifresi' warm-up), Picture Wordle for kids, near-miss decoys, and an honest 5-6 min per word. Drop the hidden-letter Duel, which cannot work on one screen. A cheap follow-on to c03.

catalog.name: Gizli Ajan Kelimeler (Spy Words)
catalog.familiarAs: Codenames (Codenames Pictures for the kids' picture board, Codenames Duet for the co-op mode)
catalog.oneLiner: Two (or three) teams race to find their secret agents on a 4x4 to 5x5 grid of pictures or words. Their only guide is a clue from their spymaster, who sees the secret key on a phone at the front (or, at A1, a clue from the HQ radio). They must avoid the single trap card.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (2-3 min, teacher)
1. The teacher picks a built-in topic or types a free prompt (Turkish is fine). The game builds a board from 3-5 word clusters plus bridge words and shows it on the projector. Card codes are 1-16 for kids and A1-E5 for Arena and Stüdyo. Before the first clue, the teacher can long-press any card to Swap it, for example an unknown word or an ambiguous picture.
2. THE KEY IS NEVER DRAWN ON THE PROJECTOR. 'Anahtar nerede?' has five routes:
   (a) Ajan masası (default). The teacher's phone opens languago.site/ajan and enters the 4-digit table code shown on the projector (the words are public anyway). The phone generates the key and shows a 5-character key code. The teacher types that code into a masked field on the projector (students see only •••••), so both devices now compute the same key. The phone goes on a stand on the teacher's desk, and BOTH spymasters stand behind it facing the class, like the shared key card in the board game.
   (b) The spymasters' own phones (adult classes), using the same table code and key code.
   (c) A second screen (non-mirrored laptop window).
   (d) Printed, laminated key cards for phone-free schools. There are 24 patterns, each usable in 4 orientations. The teacher types the card number and its rotation.
   (e) No key at all: HQ/Gogo mode, where the app itself is the spymaster.
3. Key sizes (the starting team has one extra agent; starters alternate between boards):
   - 5x5: 9 / 8 / 7 civilians / 1 trap.
   - 5x4: 7 / 6 / 6 / 1.
   - 4x4: 6 / 5 / 4 / 1.
   - 3 teams on 5x5: 7 / 6 / 6 / 5 / 1.
   The key border colour shows which team starts.
4. Teams sit in cells of 4-5 around a mini-whiteboard. The seat-number spinner picks the spymaster for the board, and the Captain rotates every clue. Nobody is picked by name.

TURN
1. CLUE. The spymaster says the clue aloud in the style set by the level:
   - Describe ONE card: 'It's yellow. Monkeys love it.' The number is always 1.
   - Category + number: 'Animals, 2'.
   - One word + number: 'Cold, 3'.
   Spymasters keep a poker face: no pointing, no Turkish, no word that is on the board. The teacher types the clue in the teacher bar, or only taps the number pips for spoken-only kids' play. The validator checks it.
   The projector plays a spy-radio crackle and types 'INCOMING · COLD · 3' with 3 empty agent silhouettes. If the clue timer runs out, the spymaster gets one +10 s. After that, HQ gives an automatic safe clue (a category label with number 1), so the game never stalls.
2. TEAM TALK. The first pick gets a longer discussion (kids 60 s, off by default; Arena 45 s; adults 60 s). Later picks use the huddle dial (10 / 15 / 20 s).
   - A phrase strip is on screen: 'I think it's..., because...', 'Maybe..., but...', 'Let's choose...', 'Let's stop.'
   - Each cell writes its card code, then 'Boards up!'. The Captain goes with the majority.
   - WHOLE-CLASS MOMENT: meanwhile the waiting team writes a Shadow read, the card they think the clue points to.
3. CALL AND FLIP. The Captain says the call sentence for the level:
   - A1: 'The banana, please!'
   - A2: 'We choose the banana.'
   - B1+ (reason rule): 'We choose "bank", because money is in a bank.'
   The teacher taps once to lock the card (a 'Final answer?' ring) and taps again to flip. The two steps prevent smartboard mistaps. Outcomes:
   - Own agent: a pip fills. The team may keep guessing up to number+1 (earlier clues can be used), or say 'Let's stop.'
   - Civilian: the turn ends.
   - Rival agent: the turn ends, and the card counts for the rival.
   - Trap: resolved by the mode's rule (instant loss for adults, the Alarm in Arena, the Sleeping Dragon for kids).
4. Shadow reads are revealed. Matches earn Intel points (Arena) or detective stars (kids). Play passes to the next team.

END
- A team wins when all its agents are found.
- 'Reveal all' then sweeps the whole key across the board.
- DOSSIER DEBRIEF, clue by clue:
  - each spymaster explains the intended link out loud ('I said "cold" because snow and ice are cold'): a short speaking task;
  - the cards the team actually picked;
  - the misread words, with picture, defEasy and TR gloss;
  - the Best link of the game.
  One tap exports the list to flashcards.

SCORING BY MODE
- Kids: stickers and stars that never go down.
- Arena: 10 per agent, with combo and a floor at zero, played as a best-of-3 series.
- Adults: the race, plus an optional 2-3 board campaign.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Default: 2 teams. Alternatives: 3 teams for classes of 24+ at B1 and above, or co-op 'Whole class mission' (the class against a turn limit), which suits A1 and very large classes.
- Each team has 1 spymaster (in Oyun Parkı, a pair of 'spy chiefs' who build clues together) standing at the spy desk.
- Everyone else sits in cells of 4-5 with one mini-whiteboard. Rotating roles per clue, shown on printable badges:
  - Captain speaks the call.
  - Scribe writes the clue and the cell's pick.
  - Checker holds the phrase card and makes sure the cell talks in English.
- The spymaster changes every board via the seat-number spinner. Ex-spymasters become Scribes, because they know the old key and the new one is fresh.
- Class sizes 8-36.
- The teacher referees, flips and types clues. At A1 the teacher can be the spymaster for both teams, which turns it into a listening game.
skills: vocabulary networks: semantic fields, superordinates, polysemy, collocation
speaking: negotiating and justifying (I think... because...)
listening for meaning (spoken clues, HQ radio)
word-formation awareness (B2 root and family rule)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO · 'Codewords' (Kod Adları)

LOOK: an editorial quiz-night style, on cream or on the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. Cards look like index cards, with the word in a big system sans and a small A1-E5 code in the corner. No mascot and no voice lines; captions stay neutral ('Board 2 · Travel'). Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('Flat White' vs 'Cortado', 'The Irregular Verbs').

CLASSIC RULES
- 5x5 word board: 9 / 8 / 7 civilians / 1 assassin; the starter alternates between boards.
- Clues are one word + number at B1+, and 'Describe one' or category + number at A1-A2.
- A team may guess up to number+1. A civilian ends the turn; a rival card ends the turn and helps the rival.
- The assassin means instant loss by default. It can be switched to 'the rival covers 2 cards'.

TIMERS: clue 60 s (45 s at B2), first discussion 60 s, later picks 20 s. 'Süresiz' is available.

SPEAKING
- A rotating spokesperson.
- The reason rule at B1+: 'We're going with bank, because...'.
- The rival team may call 'Illegal clue!'. The teacher rules with the validator's help.

CARD HELP (any board word, never the key): definition, then example, then Turkish gloss. Each step costs 1 point in campaign mode, and the TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.

SCORING: the race decides each board. An optional 2-3 board Campaign scores:
- board win = 3 points;
- +1 for each 'clean link' (a clue of 2 or more found completely in one turn);
- optional −1 for hitting a rival card or the assassin. Negatives are opt-in; otherwise the floor is 0.

B1/B2 EXTRAS
- 3-team board for big classes.
- 'Bid round': the spymasters bid openly ('I can link 4!'). The higher bid gives the clue. Delivering all the cards earns +2; falling short gives the rival one free card.
- B2 constraint cards, drawn before a board: Synonyms only; Collocations only ('heavy, 3' → rain, traffic, bag); Opposites; No nouns.
- Idiom boards: the cards are idioms, and clues work by meaning ('easy, 2' → piece of cake, a walk in the park).
- The official 0 and 'unlimited' clues.
- Red harshness, opt-in: two assassins.

ENDING: full scores and a modest finale, then the Dossier debrief with the 'Kaçırılanlar' list. It shows every card picked wrongly, the clue that misled the team, the definition and the TR gloss, and it exports to flashcards or the Material Maker.

HQ MODE: the app gives the clues from category labels and collocations, for classes where nobody wants to be spymaster yet.
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11, default for A1/A2 Genç) · 'Secret Agents Academy' (Gizli Ajan Akademisi)

LOOK
- A cream board with rounded picture cards from the self-hosted SVG set.
- Word labels are hidden at A1: the picture carries the meaning, and the word appears on flip while Gogo says it. At A2 the labels are shown.
- Animal teams (Panda team vs Fox team).
- Gogo the parrot, wearing a tiny spy hat, is HQ.

BOARD: 4x4 = 16 pictures: 6 / 5 / 4 townspeople / 1 Sleeping Dragon.

THREE RULES on a pictogram card (ear, standing child, sleeping dragon):
1. Listen to the clue.
2. Stand up for your picture. The captain says 'The banana, please!'
3. Find your agents. Don't wake the dragon!

CLUES
- A1: Gogo reads a one-picture description from the riddle clues, 4 words or fewer per sentence, with TTS at 0.8x ('It's yellow. Monkeys love it.').
- A2: a pair of spy chiefs at the spy desk builds the clue with frame cards ('It's ___. It lives in ___. You can ___ it.'). The teacher echoes it aloud.
- The number is always 1.

EVERY TURN
- A 3 s 'Think...' lock.
- Then the Stand-up vote: the teacher spotlights candidate cards one by one, Gogo says each word, and children from BOTH teams stand for their pick. This is the whole-class response moment, and it repeats the vocabulary aloud.

OUTCOMES
- Agent: an 'AGENT FOUND!' stamp and a sticker in the team's Spy File.
- Townsperson: waves 'Hello!', and Gogo gives clue 2 for one more try.
- Second miss: Gogo names the card, everyone repeats it twice, and it flips with an effort star for the class album.
- Rival agent: the agent tips its hat, 'Thanks!', and the card counts for the other team.
- Dragon: it wakes and yawns, the class whispers 'Shhh... sleep, dragon!', and its snore blows over one of the other team's agents. The turn passes. Nobody is out.

PACING AND ENDINGS
- No timer by default; when it is on, a calm 40 s ring and a marimba chime.
- Stars never go down. Mission stars (1-3) come from agents found, no dragon, and English phrases used.
- 3 boards of 5-7 min, with a 45 s 'Spy walk' stirrer between them ('Walk like a spy... freeze!').
- Gogo demos a 2x2 board in 25 s at the start; the demo does not score.
- Ending: 'Mission complete!' for BOTH teams, confetti in team colours and shapes, and a title for every team (Top Agents, Sharp Eyes, Super Listeners, Brave Guessers). The class album gets a spy badge.
- Optional co-op 'Whole class mission': 7 agents and 8 torches (turns) that dim gently. It always ends with 1-3 stars, never a 'lose' screen.

This version passes the kids' checklist: 3 rules, explainable in 20 s with pictograms, no elimination, no score below zero, a whole-class vote every turn, and non-violent failure imagery.

ARENA (ages 12-14, default for B1/B2 Genç and for any Genç class at grade 6+) · 'Undercover Ops'

LOOK
- A dark navy board with neon team colours, dossier cards coded A1-E5 and a condensed display font.
- In 10 s, each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto ('Silent. Smart. Fast.').
- No mascot. A commentator strip appears at most once per turn: 'TRIPLE LINK', 'CLUTCH', 'INTERCEPTED', 'CLEAN SWEEP'.

BOARD: 5x4 = 7 / 6 / 6 civilians / 1 trap; 5x5 is optional.

THE TRAP is 'the Alarm', a laser grid (no violence): the streak resets, the turn ends and one rival agent is auto-revealed. 'Hardcore: instant loss' is opt-in.

CLUES BY LEVEL
- A1/A2: HQ radio or a one-card description.
- A2: category + number.
- B1/B2: one word + number (3 or less; 4 or less at B2 Genç).

TIMERS ON: 45 s clue, 45 s first pick, 15 s for later picks.

WHOLE CLASS: the waiting team writes a Shadow read on mini-whiteboards; a match earns +1 Intel.

POINTS: 10 per agent. The combo is x1.5 at 3 correct in a row and x2 at 5 (accuracy only, never speed), with a floor at 0.

OPTIONS AND FLOW
- Backup hint (the next riddle clue, or 'Scan' to reveal one civilian) costs 1-2 points but never takes a score below 0.
- Yellow harshness, opt-in: 'Intercept'. After a civilian hit, the rival may make one free pick without a clue. The first team loses nothing.
- A best-of-3 series, 5-7 min per board.

ENDING: a podium plus stat awards (Longest streak, Best link with the words it joined, Clean sheet, Comeback, Sharp Readers). No last place, no individual names, and no cartoon animals or pastels.
catalog.levelTuning:
CLUE LADDER (steps up with the level; 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one step without changing the skin)
1. Describe one card, number 1.
2. Category + number, max 2.
3. One word + number, max 3.
4. One word + any number, plus 0 and unlimited clues.

A1
- Kids: a 4x4 picture board with labels hidden until the flip. Gogo HQ or the teacher is the spymaster, so it is a listening game. Clues are A1 riddle descriptions of 4 words or fewer. The Stand-up vote, and free help: listen again, then another clue.
- Adults: a 5x4 board of words with emoji. HQ or the teacher gives 'Describe one' clues of 10 words or fewer. Students start as Captains, not spymasters. Card help with the TR gloss is free.

A2
- Kids: 4x4 pictures with labels. A spy-chief pair builds descriptions from frame cards (8 words or fewer).
- Adults: 5x4 or 5x5. Students give descriptions or category clues ('Animals, 2'). The spy phone shows a Clue helper: the category labels that cover 2 or more of the team's own cards, with any label that also covers the trap greyed out.

B1
- Teens (Arena): 5x4 or 5x5 words, one word + number (3 or less), helper off, reason rule on.
- Adults: 5x5 classic with the reason rule, bridge words appear, and the validator warns about shared stems.

B2
- Teens: richer but concrete words (the teenSafe filter applies; no abstract debate), number 4 or less, root rule on.
- Adults: abstract and polysemous bridge words (spring, fair, bank, match), any number, and 0 or unlimited clues.
  - The validator blocks clues that share a root or family with a card.
  - Extras: constraint rounds (synonyms, collocations, opposites, no nouns), idiom boards, the bid round, and optional two assassins.

MIXED ABILITY
- Word bands come from words.js by level. The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial shifts the band mix (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words), the clue helper and the free hints.

CAPS
- Text caps (0-4 / 8 / 14 / 20 words for Genç; 10 / 15 / 25 / 40 for adults) apply to every HQ clue and phrase card.
- Card words are always 12 characters or fewer.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-40 (4x4 board 5-7 min, 5x4 board 6-8 min, 5x5 board 12-15 min; Oyun Parkı 3 boards ≈ 20 min, Arena best-of-3 ≈ 20-25 min, Stüdyo 2-3 boards ≈ 25-40 min)
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Content: built-in topic or free prompt (Turkish is fine).
- Grid: 4x4, 5x4 or 5x5.
- Card face: picture / word / picture+word / word revealed on flip.
- Teams: 2, 3 or co-op. Starter: random, alternate, or the trailing team.
- Clue source: Gogo/HQ auto, teacher spymaster, or student spymaster.
- Clue style and max number.
- Clue validator: warn / block / off. Blocking Turkish words and exact card words is always on; the validator also checks alt[], family[], plurals and shared stems of 4 letters or more.
- Trap rule for each mode.
- Gadgets (off by default in Stüdyo) with the Harshness level:
  - Green: Radar reveals one civilian; Shield absorbs one civilian hit.
  - Yellow: Jam caps the rival's next number at 2.
  - Red: two traps.
- Comeback: Light = a team 3 or more agents behind gets one free Radar.
- Key delivery: spy desk phone, own phones, second screen, printed key cards, or no key.
- Reason rule on/off. Card-help ladder and TR gloss on/off.
- Timers: clue, first pick and later picks, plus 'Süresiz'.
- Sound and thinking loop.
- Lesson-fit: minutes → number of boards and grid size.

IN PLAY
- Two-step flip.
- U = undo the last flip (restores the turn state).
- Manual flip or reassign.
- +10 s, T to pause.
- 'Kural dışı ipucu' button: in Nazik the spymaster just tries again; in Standard the turn ends and the rival covers one card.
- 'Kabul' to accept a creative clue the validator flagged.
- Swap card (long-press, before the first clue).
- 'Yeni anahtar' (new key, same words) and 'Yeni tahta' (new board).
- Seat-number spinner. Reveal all. End & Dossier.

PROFILE
- Everything saves to the local class profile ('8-C · B1 Genç · Arena · 5x4 · 30 dk'), including the Arena emblems and mottos.
catalog.delightDetails:
SPY RADIO: every clue arrives with a crackle of 1 s or less and types out teleprinter-style ('INCOMING · FRUIT · 3'). Empty agent silhouettes fill in the team colour as agents are found. A clue-history rail keeps every earlier clue on screen for the +1 guess.

FLIPS BY MODE
- Kids: an 'AGENT FOUND!' rubber stamp and a sticker in the Spy File.
- Arena: the dossier slides open to a neon silhouette, 'CONFIRMED'.
- Stüdyo: a quiet colour wash and a pen tick.

CHARACTERS
- Civilians have little personalities (a baker, a postman, a granny waving 'Hello!').
