Cut the MVP to a small first build: the phase runner projector (brief, prep, mission with a pausable sun or bar, twist, report reveal, stamps), print mode, 8 built-in scenarios per audience per A2 and B1 (then expand), the LLM generator with the structural validator and a side-by-side preview with inline editing, role swap, and 3 skins. v2 adds QR, phones, Walkabout, phrase bingo, the Kaçırılanlar handout, Karışık görev and the noise meter. Drop the adult wager altogether.

Assets list for the MVP: 3 skin token sets, a stamp animation per skin (SVG plus CSS), the envelope and seal animation, a mission-meter SVG per skin, Gogo in 4 poses (idle, point, magnifier, sleep), about 12 sounds per skin (the marimba, radio static and phone-ping packs, all CC0 or self-made, under about 400 KB total), and the sticker set. Keep the island under about 150 KB of JS, not counting the stickers, which are lazy-loaded per scenario.

Smartboard and phone input: one 'Sonraki adım' target of at least 120 px, plus keyboard shortcuts (Space, T, arrow keys). Put nothing that matters in the top 15% of the screen, which a short teacher cannot reach on a wall board. Report buttons on phones should be at least 56 px, and the reduced-motion setting should apply to stamps and shakes.

catalog.rankReason: The only game where every student speaks at the same time, which is the biggest talk-time multiplier for classes of 30-40. v1 is projector + print only, with manual squad scores. Round 2 re-rolls the fact table ('Aynı görev, yeni bilgiler'), and A1 Genç get a turn-taking script mode. It needs print packs and a transport decision before it can join the set.

catalog.name: Amiral Battı: Grammar Fleet (Battleship)
catalog.familiarAs: Amiral Battı / Battleship
catalog.oneLiner: Hidden fleets sit on a grid whose rows and columns are word sets. To fire at a square, a team must SAY the sentence or question that square builds ('Did Emre play football last weekend?'). The defenders answer in the matching short form ('No, he didn't!'). Children hunt Gogo's buried treasure on a picture island instead of sinking ships.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (60-90 s). The teacher picks a template, either a built-in grammar unit or a typed prompt, and a mode. The app builds the grid. Row labels and column labels are word sets (pictures for children). Every cell holds a code-built model sentence in the target form. There are three modes.
- 'Düello': 2 teams, 2 identical fleets, classic Amiral Battı. It is the default for Arena and Stüdyo.
- 'Ortak Deniz': 2-4 teams hunt ONE hidden fleet that the app places. It is the default for Oyun Parkı and for any class that wants 3-4 teams.
- 'Çift Pratiği': a printable A4 sheet with two grids per pair. It is an authentic information-gap warm-up in which each student draws their own ships (5-8 min).
Ships are placed randomly and hidden from everyone, including the teacher, and a small 'Öğretmen de bilmiyor' badge says so. Ships never touch, as in Amiral Battı. Rock cells (combinations the validator rejected) never hold ships. Optional 'Kaptan yerleştirir': each captain places their fleet on the teacher's phone in 30 s while the projector shows a curtain ('Don't look!').
A frame strip under the grid shows the target form and the reply frames, for example 'Past simple question: Did ___ ___ last weekend?' and 'Yes, ___ did. / No, ___ didn't.'

PRACTICE (20-30 s, not scored). In Oyun Parkı, Gogo demos one dig on a 2x2 mini island. In Arena and Stüdyo, the teacher fires one demo shot at a sample cell and the class echoes it.

TURN (about 40 s)
1. SPEAKER. The seat-number spinner (Oyun Parkı, Arena) or the rotating spokesperson (Stüdyo) picks who speaks. No one speaks twice until the whole team has had a turn, and nobody is ever called by name.
2. AIM. The team names a coordinate ('C4'), and the teacher taps it or uses the arrow keys. The cell zooms in. Its row label and column label pulse, and the two labels drop into the frame's slots as grey base forms ('she' + 'go').
3. TEAM TALK. A huddle of 10, 15 or 20 s runs while a radar sweep turns. 'The whole team whispers, one says it.' Big teams split into crews of 3-4 to check the sentence. In Arena, every student also writes it on a mini-whiteboard.
4. FIRE. 'Boards up!' The speaker says the sentence aloud. The teacher's phone remote shows the model, every accepted variant and the typical trap ('Did she went'). The teacher taps ✓ (Space) or ✗ (X).
5. ECHO. On ✓, the base forms in the frame morph into the right forms (go becomes went) and the model is read aloud (automatically for children at 0.8x; speaker button for the rest). The whole class echoes it once, or twice with Gogo for children. Before the reveal, everyone predicts: thumbs up for a hit, thumbs down for a splash.
6. SHOT. After a 1.2 s sweep, it is a splash (miss) or a hit. A hit gives NO extra turn, which keeps speakers rotating and turns fair.
7. REPLY ('Telsiz'). The defending team's radio operator answers in the matching short form, read from the result card: 'Yes, he did!' on a hit, 'No, he didn't.' on a miss. In Ortak Deniz and in Oyun Parkı, the whole class shouts the short answer together. In Arena and Stüdyo, a wrong short answer gives the attackers +1. In 'state' cells (true sentences) there is no reply, and the echo is the whole-class moment.
8. SUNK. When the last cell of a ship is hit, its silhouette appears with its name and a 'SUNK!' stamp, and the team scores +3. The cells around it can auto-mark as water (option).

WRONG SENTENCE
- Oyun Parkı: a soft 'boing' and a second try with a free hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo says it, the class repeats it twice and the team gets an effort star. The team STILL digs, so luck is never taken from children, but it earns no sentence star.
- Arena: no shot, and the streak breaks. The other team may 'Intercept' by saying the correct sentence within 5 s, for +1. The attackers lose nothing.
- Stüdyo: no shot. The model and a one-line 'why' (whyTr) appear, with an optional -1.

SPECIAL CELLS (chance-card items, 0-3 per grid, hidden, triggered only by a correct sentence that hits them)
- Green: Message in a Bottle (Everyone +2), Double (the next hit counts double), Shield, Telescope/Sonar (shows how many ship cells lie in a 3x3 area).
- Yellow (Arena opt-in): Steal 5, capped at the other team's score; Swap turn order.
- Red (Stüdyo opt-in): Mine (fix an error sentence in 20 s or lose your next shot); Swap scores.

LEGS AND PACING. Each leg uses a fresh grid and a new target form. For example, Leg 1 uses 'state' cells (affirmative and negative sentences) and Leg 2 uses questions with the reply. Oyun Parkı has 3 islands of 4-5 min. Arena has 2 legs of 6-7 min. Stüdyo has 2-3 legs of 8-12 min. A leg ends when a fleet is gone or its clock runs out. The lesson-fit timer assumes about 40 s per shot and sizes the grid and fleet to match. 'Son Salvo': in the last 3 minutes the speaker aims at 2 cells and must say both sentences, and each correct one fires. This doubles the language and brings the game to a finish.

SCORING. Hit 1, sunk 3, whole fleet +5 (the ESL Kids Games scheme plus a finishing bonus). Language always counts, not only luck:
- Oyun Parkı: a sentence star for every correct sentence, 1 treasure star per chest square, and +2 for opening a full chest. Scores never go down.
- Arena: x10 points (sentence 10, hit +10, sunk +30), multiplied by the accuracy combo (x1.5 at 3 correct sentences in a row, x2 at 5, even when the shots miss). The floor is zero.
- Stüdyo: points, a 'Precision' tally of correct sentences that breaks ties, optional negatives and the Torpedo wager.
The winner is the first team to sink the whole enemy fleet; otherwise points decide when the clock ends.

END. 'Filoları göster' shows the surviving ships as dotted ghosts, and near-misses glow ('one square away!'). Then comes each mode's ending: team titles and an album sticker for children, a podium and stat awards for Arena, full scores and 'Kaçırılanlar' for Stüdyo. 'Kaçırılanlar' lists every sentence that got ✗, with its model and why, for a final choral drill.
catalog.playerSetup: Düello: the class is split into 2 teams, and each team sits in crews of 3-4 for the huddles, so every student talks every turn. Ortak Deniz: 2-4 teams against one hidden fleet (the default for children). Çift Pratiği: pairs with a printed A4 sheet, each student with their own grid and an 'enemy' grid, as a 5-8 minute warm-up or a stand-alone activity for small classes. Speakers rotate strictly: the seat-number spinner for Oyun Parkı and Arena, a rotating spokesperson with 20 s pair consultation for Stüdyo. One team member is the radio operator for replies, and this role rotates too. Big classes (30+): only the speaker's voice counts, whole-class echo and thumbs prediction on every turn, and Arena adds mini-whiteboards for everyone. The teacher runs the laptop or projector and, ideally, the phone remote with the answer key.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Grammar Fleet' (naval plotting table)
LOOK. Editorial quiz-night style: a cream chart paper grid with a thin compass rose and system sans labels, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme. Hits are ink X marks and misses are pencil dots. Sunk ships are stamped silhouettes with pattern fills, so the board is colour-blind safe. There is no mascot and no voice lines, only a neutral caption ('Leg 2 · Present perfect'). Sounds: a soft sonar ping in the huddle, a woodblock 'tock' for a splash, a two-note piano sting for a hit, a low piano chord plus the stamp for 'SUNK', and every chime lasts 0.6 s. Music is off. Ships carry grammar-pun names: HMS Irregular (3), The Auxiliary (3), Past Participle (2), Modal Queen (2), and the singles 'Contraction' and 'Full Stop'. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or puns ('The Irregular Verbs').

RULES. Düello with 2 identical fleets on a 6x6 grid: 2x3, 2x2, 2x1 (12 cells) for 35-40 min, or 1x3, 2x2, 2x1 (9 cells) for 20-25 min. A 7x7 grid is available for long lessons with short labels. The Reply rule is on by default: the defending radio operator must give the right short answer, otherwise the attackers get +1. The rotating spokesperson gets 20 s of pair consultation.
- 'Debrief' (B1-B2, on by default at B2): after a hit, the attackers may ask ONE follow-up wh-question ('Where did he go?'). The defenders improvise a one-sentence answer, and each accurate sentence scores +1. The prompts come from speaking-prompt followUps.
- 'Torpedo' wager: before firing, a team may stake 1-3 points on a cell marked with a bolt. That cell needs a harder transformation: a negative question, a question tag, or the sentence plus a because-clause. If the sentence is correct, the team fires at that cell AND one adjacent cell of its choice and gets its stake back doubled. If it is wrong, the stake is lost.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default. Red (Mine, Swap scores) is opt-in.
- Hints cost points: 1) the rule in one line ('Have + V3'); 2) a model on a DIFFERENT cell; 3) the Turkish gloss of the cell, which can be switched off for immersion classes.
- Wrong sentence: no shot, model plus why, optional -1.

TEMPLATES (adult life and work). Present perfect with ever/never ('Have you ever eaten sushi?'); for/since ('How long has she worked here?' with the reply 'For two years.'); second conditional (rows are if-situations, columns are actions: 'Would you quit your job if you won the lottery?'); passive in 'state' mode with built-in facts ('Tea is grown in Rize.' / 'Coffee isn't grown in Turkey.'); question tags ('You've been to Izmir, haven't you?'); must/have to at work ('Do you have to wear a suit at work?').
B2 adds reported questions, embedded questions, third conditional, causative and the Collocation Minefield (see levelTuning).

END. The full scoreboard with a Precision column, 'Filoları göster', and 'Kaçırılanlar' as a clickable list: each missed sentence with its model, whyTr and a TTS button for a closing choral drill. There is also a printable grid key for homework ('Write 6 sentences from cells nobody fired at').
catalog.teenVersion:
TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT KID RULESETS (the group label is never shown on screen)

OYUN PARKI (9-11, default for A1/A2 Genç): 'Treasure Island / Hazine Adası'
THEME. There are no ships and no explosions. The board is a sunny sand island on a cream sea, with palm trees at the corners and one shared grid (Ortak Deniz). Gogo the parrot wears a tiny captain's hat, and he buried the treasure. Teams are animal crews in bandanas: Panda crew, Fox crew, Lion crew, Frog crew.
- A miss is a friendly surprise: a crab waves, a seashell or a starfish appears, and Gogo says 'Oh, a shell!'.
- A hit shows gold coins peeking out of the sand.
- A complete chest pops open with a coin shower of 2 s or less and a xylophone run.
- There are no horns or buzzers, only marimba 'bloops'.

RULES (3, on a pictogram card; the Turkish rule text is for the teacher to read in 20 s):
1. Pick a square (finger icon).
2. Say it! The team whispers and one says it (speech bubble icon).
3. Right sentence = dig! (shovel and chest icons)
Everything else is automatic.
- Whole-class moments every turn: thumbs-up/down prediction, echoing the sentence twice with Gogo, and the class shouting the short answer ('Yes, it is!').
- No elimination and no negatives. A wrong sentence gets a second try with a free hint; then Gogo says it, the class repeats it and the team still digs.
- Stars never go down: a sentence star per correct sentence, a treasure star per coin square, +2 for a full chest.
- Hints are free: 1) the picture slots in the frame light up; 2) the first word ('Is...'); 3) Gogo says it again slowly.
- The timer is off by default. When it is on, it gives 40 s with a calm ring that never turns red and a marimba chime at 0. Team talk lasts 10 s.

GRID. A 4x4 island (chests 1x3, 1x2, 1x1) or 5x5 (1x3, 2x2, 2x1), with a high treasure rate so children succeed often. Both axes are pictures: colour splashes, clothes, toys, animals, and fictional character cards (Ali, Mia, Ela, Tom).
- Frames are picture-and-word strips such as 'Is it a [red] [hat]?', 'Have you got a [blue] [bag]?' and 'Is the [cat] [under] the box?'.
- 'Can' grids use 'state' mode, so silly combinations become funny true negatives: 'A frog can't sing!'. A child never has to say something false.

PACING. 3 islands of 4-5 min. Between islands: a 45 s stirrer ('Gogo says: stand up if you have a red pencil!', using the grid's words) or a 60 s settler (count the coins together, or colour the chest on the printable).
ENDING. Every crew gets a title (Best Diggers, Super Speakers, Bravest Treasure Hunters), confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale, and the class album gets a 'Treasure Map' sticker. Gogo sleeps on a chest on the pause screen and says 'Ahoy, crew!' and 'Bye-bye, crew!' in the rituals.
CHECKLIST. It passes: 3 rules, 20 s with pictograms, no elimination, no score below zero, a whole-class response every turn, non-violent imagery.

ARENA (12-14, default for B1/B2 Genç and for any Genç class at grade 6+): 'Sonar Strike'
THEME. A dark navy screen with a neon wireframe grid. The 'Match' is Düello between 2 teams. The two fleets are wireframe subs with callsigns (VOLT-3, NOVA-2). A sunk sub 'goes offline' with a glitch dissolve and a synth blip, never with fire. There are no animals, no mascot and no pastel colours. A commentator strip shows at most one caption per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!', 'INTERCEPTED!').
OWNERSHIP. In 10 s each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto, which shows on its team bar.

RULES
- A 30 s turn timer with a ring in the team colour, and a 15 s team talk.
- The spinner picks the speaker, and everyone writes the sentence on a mini-whiteboard, so the teacher can call 'Boards up!' to spot-check.
- Accuracy combo: x1.5 at 3 correct sentences in a row, x2 at 5, even when the shots miss, so skill beats luck.
- 'Intercept': the other team may steal a wrong turn, and the attackers lose nothing.
- Hints cost 1 point with a floor of 0: 1) the first word; 2) 50:50 between two forms ('went / goed'); 3) a gapped model.
- Yellow luck (Steal, Swap order) only if the teacher opts in. 2 legs of 6-7 min, then Son Salvo.
ENDING. A podium plus stat awards (Sharpest Aim = best hit ratio, Longest Streak, Clean Sheet = no hints, Comeback), and never a 'last place'.

CONTENT FOR BOTH. teenSafe is enforced on every axis and cell: no dating, alcohol, violence, brands, money, jobs or office topics. The experiences are child-world ones ('Have you ever ridden a camel?', 'Did you go to the aquarium last summer?').
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Genç (Oyun Parkı, 4x4): only pictures on both axes, 0-4 words on screen, and everything read aloud at 0.8x.
  - Units: a1-12 (colours x nouns: 'Is it a red hat?'), have got ('Have you got a blue bag?'), a1-08 in/on/under ('Is the cat in the box?'), a1-07 ('Is there a ball in the bedroom?'), a1-16 can in state mode ('A fish can swim. / A fish can't fly.').
  - Reply: 'Yes, it is! / No, it isn't!'
- Adults (5x5): word plus emoji labels, max 10 words.
  - Units: a1-01 ('Is she a nurse?'), a1-06 ('Do you live near the station?' / 'Does he work on Saturdays?'), a1-07 with places in town, a1-16, a1-15 ('Is he cooking?').
  - The 'Choice shot' scaffold is on by default at A1-Kolay: the board shows 3 versions ('Does she work? / Does she works? / Do she work?'), built from errorType patterns, and the speaker still has to SAY the right one.

A2
- Genç (Oyun Parkı 5x5, or Arena if grade 6+): pictures plus one-word labels, max 8 words.
  - Fictional character cards x food, sports and places.
  - Units: a1-06/a2-02 ('Does Mia like pizza?'), a2-01 ('Is Ali swimming?'), a2-10 ('Was Ela at the zoo?'), regular past ('Did Tom play tennis?').
- Adults (6x6), max 15 words.
  - Units: a2-03/04/09 past simple (rows = people, columns = weekend activities, with a fixed time phrase from a2-11: 'Did your sister go to the cinema last weekend?'), a2-05 going to, a2-06 comparatives in state mode ('The metro is faster than the bus.'), a2-07 ('Is there any milk in the fridge?'), a2-15 ('Do you have to wear a uniform?').

B1
- Genç (Arena 6x6): word labels with small icons, max 14 words.
  - Units: a2-09 irregular past, going to, b1-12 ('Have you ever ridden a camel?'), a2-16 should in state mode ('You should wear a helmet on a bike.'), comparatives and superlatives.
- Adults (6x6), max 25 words, where the frame names the form but the verb forms are not shown.
  - Units: b1-12 ever/never, b1-01 for/since ('How long has he played the guitar?' with the reply 'For three years.'), b1-06 second conditional (rows = if-situations, columns = actions), b1-08 passive in state mode from built-in fact lists, b1-13 used to, b1-14 tags.
  - Debrief follow-ups are optional.

B2
- Genç (Arena 6x6): richer language on concrete topics, never abstract debate, max 20 words.
  - Units: b1-06/b2-04 ('Would you live on Mars if you could?'), b1-13 used to ('Did you use to collect stickers?'), b2-01 present perfect continuous, b2-09 wish in state mode ('I wish I had a dog.'), b2-16 embedded questions (rows = openers 'Do you know / Could you tell me', columns = museum, station, library).
- Adults (6x6 or 7x7), max 40 words.
  - Units: b2-03 third conditional ('If you had missed the bus, would you have been late?'); b2-05 reported questions in 'report' mode (row = reporter 'My boss asked me' x column = direct question 'Where are you going?' gives 'My boss asked me where I was going.'); b2-16 embedded questions; b2-19 causative ('Have you ever had your car serviced?'); b2-09 wish.
  - The Collocation Minefield (verbs make/do/take/have/pay/catch x nouns): non-collocations are mines. Spotting one ('That's not a collocation, it's do homework') is correct, safe and +1. Saying a sentence with it is ✗.
  - Debrief follow-ups are compulsory after a hit.

DIALS
- 'Kolay': Choice shot on, verb forms shown in the frame, hints cheaper.
- 'Orta': the frame with base forms.
- 'Zor': no frame strip, the target form is only named ('Third conditional question'), and there are Torpedo cells.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' swaps the template list down one level and keeps the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-40 (Oyun Parkı: 3 islands of 4-5 min plus stirrers, about 20. Arena: 2 legs of 6-7 min, 15-20. Stüdyo: 2-3 legs of 8-12 min, 20-40. Paper pair warm-up: 5-8.)
catalog.contentShape:
The grid is a frame at pack.frames.fleet, like story/case/escape.

{ unit ('a2-04'), targetForm and targetFormTr, cellMode, frame (a slot template shown under the grid, e.g. 'Did {R} {C} last weekend?'), replyFrames {yes, no} using {pron}, rows[4-6] and cols[4-6], cells[r][c], fleet, placement }

cellMode is one of:
- 'ask': an open-truth yes/no question that the fleet answers.
- 'state': say a TRUE sentence, adding 'not' when needed.
- 'report': transform a given sentence (B2 reported or embedded).
- 'colloc': the B2 minefield.

rows[4-6] and cols[4-6]: {label, ref (vocab id), media.emoji or imageKey (required for Genç), pron? (he/she/it/they/I, for replies), forms? {s, past, pp, ing}}.

cells[r][c]:
- model
- accept[]: contractions, have got / have, UK/US, optional time phrase, 'ever' placement
- replyYes, replyNo
- tr: Turkish gloss, teacher only
- whyTr: 90 chars or fewer, e.g. 'Did + V1: geçmişi yardımcı fiil taşır'
- trap: the typical error to listen for, e.g. 'Did he went'
- choices[3]?: Choice-shot versions
- flag: 'ok' | 'silly' | 'rock'
- followUp?: B1-B2
- special?: chance-card id

fleet {ships[{len, name}]} and placement are code-only and never come from the LLM.

WHAT FEEDS IT
- vocab: axis words with forms and pictures.
- pair with rel 'qa': question to short answer, used in the Radio Check warm-up and on the reply card.
- gap: the frame and reply slots ('Yes, she ___.').
- mcq with fmt 'gap': Choice-shot versions and a silent fallback mode.
- error: Mine cells and the trap list (errorType aux-question, tense, 3rd-s, word-order).
- speaking-prompt with mode 'ask': Debrief follow-ups.
- chance-card: special cells.

PIPELINE. A built-in template, or the LLM from the teacher's prompt (e.g. 'geçen hafta sonu, spor ve hobiler, past simple sorular'), proposes only the unit, the axes and per-cell plausibility flags. CODE builds every model sentence from the template plus morphology, so the answer key is always grammatical:
- 3rd person -s/-es/-ies;
- irregular past and participle from the a2-09 list and words.js;
- -ing consonant doubling;
- a/an;
- the reply pronoun.

VALIDATOR
- 4-6 unique axis items in one semantic field.
- Every cell contains both axis items, in inflected form.
- A target-form regex per template (e.g. '^Did \w+ <base verb>', '^Have you ever <pp>').
- The word cap for the group.
- teenSafe on every Genç cell.
- Open-truth rule for 'ask' mode: only people or characters x activities, or 'you' x experiences. Common-knowledge facts are moved to 'state' mode, and 'state' facts come only from built-in fact lists, never from the LLM.
- At most 4 rock cells per grid; otherwise one axis item is swapped.
- Verbs without verified forms are dropped.
- Genç groups drop any axis item that has no imageKey.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP. One summary line ('B1 · Stüdyo · Düello · 6x6 · Süresiz · 25 dk') with a 'Değiştir' link. The settings are:
- Mode: Düello / Ortak Deniz / Çift Pratiği PDF.
- Template: the built-in unit list, each shown with an example cell, or a Turkish/English prompt to the LLM.
- An editable grid preview: tap an axis label to swap the word, tap a cell to edit its model or make it a rock, and use 'Yeniden üret' per axis.
- Cell mode: ask / state / report / colloc.
- Grid size: 4x4 / 5x5 / 6x6, plus 7x7 for adults.
- Fleet: auto-sized by the lesson-fit timer, or set by hand.
- Placement: Rastgele / Kaptan yerleştirir.
- Rules and scaffolds: Reply rule, Echo, Choice-shot scaffold, Debrief follow-ups, Torpedo cells.
- Luck and scoring: specials and Harshness level; hint costs; optional negatives; Son Salvo.
- Board options: auto water halo around sunk ships; TR gloss off for immersion.
- Timers: huddle 10/15/20 s, turn 30/40 s, Süresiz.
All choices are saved to the class profile.

IN PLAY
- The phone remote (QR) shows the targeted cell's model, every accepted variant, the trap to listen for and the correct reply. It has big ✓/✗ buttons, the hint ladder, undo and speaker skip. It never shows the fleet, except behind a long-press 'Düzeltme' for manual correction.
- Long-press ✓ means 'Kabul': it counts as correct but logs the sentence to Kaçırılanlar.
- Laptop keys: arrows + Enter to aim, Space ✓, X ✗, H hint, R replay audio, U undo last shot, T pause, + adds 10 s, E ends the leg, F reveals the fleets.
- Manual score and cell correction.
- Change the target form between legs.

AFTER. 'Filoları göster', the 'Kaçırılanlar' list with TTS, and a printable grid key plus blank grids for homework or the next lesson's paper warm-up.
catalog.delightDetails:
- A radar sweep with a quiet ping every 2 s during team talk; for children it is Gogo's telescope swinging across the island instead.
- The frame slots hold grey base forms that visibly morph on ✓ ('go' becomes 'went', 'she' + 'have' becomes 'she has') with a tiny typewriter tick, so the grammar change is SEEN.
- Named ships:
  - Stüdyo: puns such as HMS Irregular, The Auxiliary, Past Participle, and the single 'Contraction'.
  - Arena: callsigns such as VOLT-3.
  - Children: Big Chest, Tiny Chest, Gogo's Snack Box.
- Distinct sink moments per skin:
  - Stüdyo: an ink 'SUNK' stamp with a piano chord.
  - Arena: a neon glitch as the sub goes offline, with a synth sting.
  - Children: the chest pops open with a coin shower.
- A different miss per skin: for children a crab waves, or a shell or starfish appears ('Oh, a shell!'); a sonar ripple for Arena; an ink dot plop for Stüdyo.
- Hits and misses use shapes as well as colours (X, dot, hatched sunk), so the board is colour-blind safe.
- A fairness badge, 'Öğretmen de bilmiyor', which children love.
- Only the targeted grid is shown large, and the grids slide across when the turn passes, so labels stay readable from the back row.
- 'Son Salvo': in the final 3 minutes the grid border pulses and the thinking loop gets slightly faster.
- The fleet reveal shows surviving ships as dotted ghosts and glows near-misses ('one square away!').
- A 'Captain's Log' end card shows each team's best sentence and its longest streak.
- Children: Gogo in a captain's hat, an 'Ahoy, crew!' hello and a 'Bye-bye, crew!' goodbye, and sleeping on a chest on the pause screen.
- Arena teams' mottos scroll on their team bars.
- Axis names come from a mixed Turkish and English fictional name pool, so the class sees Emre and Mia side by side.
- The printable paper version uses the same art and is ink-friendly for the pair warm-up.
- Reduced motion turns every animation into a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- Teacher judgement bottleneck. Mitigations: the phone key lists accepted variants and the trap, Choice shot is available at A1-Kolay, and the 'Kabul' long-press handles near-misses. If the teacher has no phone, the model is still revealed on the board after ✓/✗, and a printable key can be used.
- Only 2 teams means little talk time per student. Mitigations: crew huddles, strict rotation, whole-class echo and prediction every turn, Arena mini-whiteboards, Ortak Deniz for 3-4 teams, and the paper pair warm-up.
- Luck could outweigh language. Mitigations: correct sentences always score (sentence stars, the Arena combo, the Stüdyo Precision tiebreak), and a hit gives no extra turn.
- Truth confusion ('Yes, a fish can fly'). Mitigation: the open-truth rule. 'Ask' cells are only about characters, people or 'you' in the game world, and facts are said only as true 'state' sentences.
- The LLM may state wrong facts. Mitigation: state-mode facts come only from built-in lists.
- Odd or nonsense cells ('The dog plays chess'). Mitigations: 'silly' flags are kept for fun only where they work, and anything else becomes a rock, which the teacher can also set with one tap.
- Morphology errors. Mitigation: code builds the forms, and unverified verbs are dropped.
- Game length (about 40 s per shot). Mitigations: the lesson-fit sizes the fleet, leg clocks, and Son Salvo.
- Violent framing for minors. Mitigations: children never see ships, fire or horns; Arena subs go offline without fire; teenSafe runs on every axis.
- Noise and teammates prompting aloud. Mitigations: the whispered huddle, and the teacher can tap 'Tekrar' so the speaker repeats alone.
- A mirrored laptop would expose the key on the projector. Mitigation: the key lives only on the phone remote.
- Projector readability at 6x6 and above. Mitigations: label font floors and the single large grid. 7x7 is adults-only and needs short labels.
sources: C:/lg/src/data/grammar_a1.js .. grammar_b2.js (unit ids used for templates)

issues: The pacing numbers don't fit together. A turn has speaker spin, aim, a 10-20 s huddle, say, judge, morph and TTS, echo (twice for kids), a thumbs prediction, a 1.2 s sweep and a reply. In a real class of 28 that is 55-75 s, not 40 s. An Arena leg of 6-7 min is only 6-8 shots in total, so 3-4 per team. In Düello with 9-12 ship cells, no fleet is ever sunk. The core Battleship pleasures (finding a ship, reasoning from adjacent hits, sinking it) almost never happen, and the leg ends on the clock with luck-based points.

Ortak Deniz with 4 teams means each team shoots about once every 4 minutes, which is heavy dead time for 10-year-olds. It also has a free-rider problem: team B fires next to team A's hit and takes the sink bonus. Order of play, not language, decides who sinks the chests.

In the 4x4 Oyun Parkı island there are about 6 treasure cells and 3 islands of 4-5 min, so each of 28 children speaks roughly once per 20 min. The spinner rotation guarantees fairness but not talk time. Most of the speaking is choral.

The 'Telsiz' reply in the projected modes has no real information gap. The fleet is hidden from everyone, so the 'defender' reads 'No, he didn't' off the result card. Scoring +1 against the defenders for misreading a card is odd and adds a ruling for the teacher. In Düello it is also unclear who the defending team is answering for.

The smart-board reality clashes with the key-on-phone design. The teacher stands at a touch board, not at a laptop, so the keyboard shortcuts don't help. Phone pairing by QR needs a realtime connection. MEB school Wi-Fi often blocks it, and many teachers won't use their own mobile data. Without the phone, the teacher has to judge by ear with no model, and in Oyun Parkı the auto-read model then reveals it too late to help.

The teacher's cognitive load is very high: specials, a 3-step hint ladder, a 5 s Intercept, Kabul long-press, Torpedo, Debrief, Mine, Swap scores, Son Salvo, combo multipliers, the Reply-rule +1 and optional -1. Standing at the board with 28 children, the teacher can't track the Intercept window, the combo, the wager and the reply penalty at once. Most of these will be switched off after the first lesson, or they will cause disputes.

The Intercept within 5 s causes chaos with 12-14 year-olds. Several students on the other team shout at once, nobody is designated, and the loudest student wins. One strong student ends up dominating.

The Arena combo multiplier (x1.5/x2) plus hit/sunk points creates a runaway leader. Stat awards soften the ending, but mid-game a team 60 points behind with 2 minutes left can't catch up, and teens disengage.
Düello has no last-shot parity. If team A sinks the last ship on its turn, team B, which may be one cell from winning, never gets its equal turn.
Mini-whiteboards are assumed for Arena, but most Turkish public classrooms don't have them. A 'Boards up' spot-check that depends on missing equipment silently fails.

The coordinate call-out is ambiguous. The axes are word sets, so the design needs to say whether kids call 'C4' or 'red hat'. The team names the coordinate but the spinner picks the speaker, which invites a strong student to choose the cell and dictate the sentence.
Setup is quoted as 60-90 s. With the LLM path, the editable preview, rock flags and the settings summary, the first-time setup is more like 3-5 min. Only the built-in template path meets 90 s.
Drill fatigue: one leg is 8-12 turns of the identical structure. That is fine for adults, but kids get bored after about 6 identical 'Is it a ___ ___?' turns unless the axes are varied or funny.
Adults (10 people): 2 teams of 5 means each adult says one sentence every 5-8 minutes. Paper Çift Pratiği gives far more talk time, yet the projected Düello is the default.
fixes: Size the game by realistic time. Budget 60 s per shot (45 s for adults) and let the lesson-fit calculator pick a smaller fleet. In Arena use a 5x5 grid with 1x3 + 1x2 + 1x1 (6 cells) so at least one sink happens per leg, or make legs 10 min and use one leg plus Son Salvo. Show the teacher an estimate at setup: '≈14 atış, 1-2 batış beklenir'.
Cut the per-turn ceremony by audience. Oyun Parkı: echo once, prediction every other turn. Arena: no prediction, and the sweep is 0.6 s. Stüdyo: auto-skip the TTS. Aim for a hard 45 s cycle.

For Ortak Deniz with 3-4 teams, use a SIMULTANEOUS round. Every team gets a picture card (or 2 minutes on the board) to pick its cell and prepare its sentence at the same time, then the speakers fire in rotation. Award sink bonus points to every team that hit that chest, so there is no free-riding.

Make the reply a whole-class choral moment in every mode, drop the +1 against the defenders, and never have one student read a card aloud as 'production'. Keep the real information-gap reply only in Çift Pratiği, and promote that mode as the default for small adult classes (8-12) as a pair round, with the projected Düello as the finale.

Design for the smart board first. Put big ✓/✗/hint buttons on the board itself. Show the teacher's key as a small toggle-able 'öğretmen bakışı' strip, hidden by default, that the teacher peeks at by pressing and holding. Make the phone remote optional, working over plain HTTP polling via Supabase, with a clear fallback message if pairing fails.

Ship three presets instead of a settings wall. 'Sade': hit/sink/sentence points only. 'Standart': plus specials (green). 'Tam': Torpedo, Debrief, Intercept, Mine. Hide everything else under 'Gelişmiş'. Each preset shows at most 3 live mechanics per turn.

Make the Intercept orderly. The other team's next scheduled speaker is the only one allowed to intercept, and they tap a big 'Intercept' button on the board or the teacher taps their team bar. Otherwise, drop the Intercept for classes over 20.

Add a comeback brake in Arena. Cap the combo at x1.5, and give the trailing team a free Sonar after 3 turns in a row behind by more than 30 points. Show the points but not the gap bar until the last minute.
Add last-turn parity. If team A clears the fleet, team B gets its equal final shot, and a tie is decided by Precision.
Offer a mini-whiteboard substitute that works without equipment: 'Deftere yaz, kaldır' with a notebook, or everyone mouths the sentence to a partner. Label the check as optional.

Pin down who says what. The spinner-picked speaker names the cell AND says the sentence. Show both labels AND letter-number coordinates. Kids may come up and tap the cell themselves on the smart board, which is a nice movement break.
Offer a 'Hızlı başla' on the first screen: last class profile plus a built-in template, playable in 2 taps. The LLM path and the grid editor sit behind 'Özelleştir', with honest time expectations.

Fight drill fatigue. Change the cell mode every 5 turns in Oyun Parkı: first 'ask', then 'state' sentences like 'A frog can't sing!', or silly flags. Use island breaks with stirrers (already planned) every 4-5 min without exception.
Stopping and resuming: autosave the grid state to the class profile so a leg cut by the bell continues next lesson, and print the 'Kaçırılanlar' list and blank grid in one click.

issues: A1 young learners who barely read cannot produce 'Have you got a blue bag?' cold. The model audio is only heard after the teacher taps ✓/✗ or on the third hint, so most early turns become fail, then Gogo says it, then repeat. That is a slow, discouraging loop, and the sentence star becomes mostly luck-free failure.

Naming coordinates ('C4') adds a step that does no work. For kids the row and column pictures already identify the cell, and saying 'C4' in English (letters plus numbers) is extra load for A1 kids with no grammar value. The sentence itself should be the aim.

The pacing arithmetic does not close. At about 40 s per shot, an Arena leg of 6-7 min gives roughly 10 shots, 5 per team, on a 36-cell grid with 9-12 ship cells. Fleets will almost never sink, so the 'first to sink the fleet' win condition and the +5 fleet bonus are effectively dead, and the SUNK moment (the main delight) rarely fires. Stüdyo 8-12 min legs on 6x6 Düello have the same problem.

Treating the LLM prompt as a first-class path is overstated. Code-built morphology is realistic for a2-04 past-simple questions, have got, can and colour-noun templates. It is NOT realistic for B2 third conditional, reported questions (backshift, pronoun and time-word shifts), embedded questions, causative or wish without a hand-written generator per template. A teacher prompt that does not map to an existing template (e.g. 'travel phrasal verbs', 'idioms') has nowhere to go.

'state' mode depends on built-in fact lists (passive facts, can/can't animal facts, comparatives). A typed LLM prompt therefore cannot produce state-mode grids, which cuts out a large share of the kid templates and the B1 passive for prompt-driven content. The design never says this to the teacher.

Kids' content is capped by the image library ('Genç groups drop any axis item that has no imageKey'). A teacher prompt like 'deniz hayvanları' may shrink below 4 items per axis, and there is no fallback defined.

The teenSafe list bans jobs and money. Jobs ('Is she a doctor?', a1-01) and prices/shopping are core A1-A2 and MEB grade 5-6 topics for 9-13-year-olds. Banning them removes legitimate curriculum rather than protecting children.

The drill is highly repetitive: one frame, 10-20 near-identical sentences. That is excellent controlled practice at A1-A2 but thin for B2 adults unless Debrief is on. The B2 'Collocation Minefield' is a different task (judgement rather than a transformation drill) bolted onto the same frame, and it muddles the 'right sentence = fire' contract.

Rule overload for the teacher and for Arena teens: Intercept, combo, Torpedo, Debrief, Mine, Swap, Steal, Son Salvo, Kabul, Choice shot, hint costs, the Reply penalty and water halo. The kids checklist passes, but the Arena default still shows 6-7 live rules, and the Stüdyo teacher faces about 20 setup toggles.

The Reply ('Telsiz') is read from the result card, so it is reading aloud, not production. At A1 it is fine. At B1-B2 the defender just reads 'No, he didn't' and practises nothing, yet a wrong reply is penalised, which mostly punishes attention lapses.

In Ortak Deniz there is no opponent, so 'Yes, it is!' shouted by the class after the reveal is echoing, not answering. That is fine, but it is not the information gap that justifies Battleship. For kids the game is a luck hunt with a repeat-after-me gate.

At A1 adult 'Kolay', Choice shot plus the verb forms shown in the frame make the target trivially readable. Production becomes reading one of 3 options aloud, which risks 'just clicking' in spoken form.
Arena mini-whiteboards for everyone in a 15 s huddle is optimistic for A2-B1 teens writing a 7-10 word question, and it creates a writing bottleneck that eats the pace.
fixes: Add a 'Dinle-söyle' aim for Oyun Parkı at A1 and optional at A2: when the cell is aimed, Gogo says the model once at 0.8x, then the crew whispers and the speaker repeats it. At A2 Genç, switch to 'hear it only after a failed first try'. At level up, move to the frame only. This keeps A1 non-readers successful and still gives production.

For Oyun Parkı, drop coordinates entirely. The speaker points at, or the teacher taps, the two pictures, and saying the sentence IS the shot. Keep 'C4' only for Arena and Stüdyo, where it adds strategy talk.

Fix the lesson-fit math. Size the fleet from the expected shots: fleet cells ≈ 35-40% of the grid for kids and 25-30% for older groups, 5x5 by default for Arena and 6x6 only for 25+ min Stüdyo. Let a leg end on 'treasure/fleet found OR clock', and make Son Salvo fire two cells in every turn of the last third, not just the final 3 min. Simulate: each leg should sink at least 2 ships on average.

Make templates the only content source for the grid, and let the LLM only fill axes (people, activities, places) for a chosen template. Show the teacher which templates accept a prompt ('Prompt ile doldurulabilir' badge) and which are built-in only (state, report, B2 transformations). If a prompt does not map to a template, suggest the nearest template in Turkish rather than failing silently.

Ship B2 transformation templates (reported, embedded, third conditional, causative) only when a hand-written, unit-tested generator exists for each. Until then, offer them from curated built-in grids, with the LLM limited to swapping nouns inside verified frames.
Kids' prompt fallback: if fewer than 4 image-backed items survive per axis, fill from the nearest built-in picture set in the same semantic field and tell the teacher which items were substituted.
Relax teenSafe for 9-13: allow jobs, shops, prices and pocket money. Keep banning dating, alcohol, violence and brands.
Move the Collocation Minefield out into its own mode or another game (it fits a Sentence Auction or odd-one-out game better). Keep Battleship to transformation cells.

Cut the default rule sets. Arena default: timer, combo and Intercept only, with Steal, Swap and Torpedo off and listed under 'Ekstra'. Stüdyo default: Reply plus Debrief at B1-B2 only. Group all other toggles under a collapsed 'Gelişmiş' panel with a one-line preset per level.

Make Reply real production at B1-B2. The result card shows only YES/NO (an icon), and the operator must build the short answer ('No, she hasn't.') from the question they heard. Only A1-A2 keep the printed reply.
At A1 Kolay, show the Choice-shot options for 5 s, then hide them before the speaker speaks, so the speaker must hold the form in memory, not read it.
Arena whiteboards: write only the key two words (auxiliary + verb form, e.g. 'Did / go'), not the whole sentence. That keeps it inside 15 s and still gives whole-class accountability.

Add one freer-production beat per leg for B1-B2 (both ages). After a sink, the attackers make one TRUE sentence about themselves with the same form ('I've never ridden a camel.'). Score it +1. This breaks the repetition and is still teenSafe.

issues: Rule surface is far too big for one build. 3 modes x 3 skins, plus Intercept, combo, Torpedo wager, Debrief, Mine, Swap scores, Steal, Sonar, Shield, Double, Son Salvo, Kaptan yerleştirir, Choice shot, 4 cell modes and a printable PDF. That is really an XL build, not L, and every combination needs testing. The risk is a buggy, half-polished game instead of a tight one.

The phone remote is load-bearing: the answer key, accepted variants and the trap live only there. /sinif-oyunu is a single-screen app, so a QR-paired remote needs a realtime channel (Supabase Realtime broadcast or polling), pairing, reconnect handling and school Wi-Fi tolerance. That is its own sub-project, and without it the teacher-judgement mitigation mostly collapses.

Code-built morphology is the right idea and makes the answer key reliable for ask and state templates: do-support, 3rd-s, past, pp, -ing, a/an, reply pronoun. The 'report' mode (backshift, pronoun and time-word shifts, question to statement word order) and embedded questions are much harder to generate correctly by rule. Third conditional plus pronoun agreement across 36 cells will produce subtle errors, such as 'My boss asked me where was I going' edge cases or 'your' becoming 'my'. The 'accept[]' variant lists are also hard to build exhaustively, so teachers will see 'not in list' for correct answers.

Picture axes for Genç need a real icon library: colours, clothes, toys, animals, food, sports, places, character cards. Emoji fallback looks different on a Windows projector, reads poorly at 5x5 from the back row, and many target nouns have no emoji. The rule 'drop any axis item without imageKey' will make LLM-prompted Genç grids fail often, so the free-prompt promise is weak for children.

The LLM prompt path is thin by design (it only proposes a unit plus axes), which is good for validity. But mapping a free Turkish prompt to one of roughly 25 code templates is effectively template selection. Prompts outside the templates (e.g. 'used to at A1', 'phrasal verbs') have no grid form, and the design never says what happens then.

Pacing risk. About 40 s per shot with one speaker means about 15 shots in 10 minutes. On a 6x6 grid with 12 ship cells, the hit rate is 33%, so a Düello leg rarely ends by sinking and usually ends on the clock. That makes 'first to sink the fleet wins' mostly fictional, and points decide. At Oyun Parkı, 4 crews x 40 s means each crew fires about once every 2.5 minutes, which is long for 9-year-olds.

The kids ruleset claims 3 rules but runs a heavy turn loop: spinner, aim, huddle, speak, second try, echo x2, prediction, 1.2 s sweep, and a shouted short answer. It passes the checklist on paper, but the real turn is 50-60 s with lots of teacher taps. The thumbs prediction before the reveal also feels empty for a random hidden fleet (pure guessing, with nothing to learn from it).

Semantic oddity: in 'ask' mode, the truth of 'Did Emre play football?' is decided by where the ships are. That is fine and a classic ESL battleship move, but the design adds 'state' mode, 'silly' flags, rocks and an open-truth validator for it. Each extra mode multiplies the validator and UI work, while the payoff for B1+ adults is small.

Düello with 2 identical app-placed fleets means neither team 'owns' a fleet, so the Reply rule (the defending radio operator answers) is theatre: the answer is read off a result card. It adds time but little language, apart from the short-form drill.

Printable Çift Pratiği is cheap (print CSS), but it is a separate mode with different pedagogy (a student-to-student information gap). It belongs as an export button, not a third play mode in the selector.

Asset list is heavy across 3 skins: an island board, a crab, shells, a chest animation and the Gogo parrot with several poses; a neon wireframe sub set with a glitch shader; an ink-stamp editorial set; three sound palettes of about 8 cues each. Art consistency with the other 9+ games is not addressed.
fixes: Define an MVP and ship that first. MVP: Ortak Deniz plus Düello, 'ask' and 'state' cell modes only, 3 skins, a fixed fleet table per grid size, hit/sunk/fleet scoring, the Arena combo, the Stüdyo Precision tiebreak, the Kaçırılanlar list and the print-CSS export of the grid key plus blank sheets. Defer to v2: Torpedo, Debrief, Mine/Swap/Steal specials, Kaptan yerleştirir, report and colloc modes, and Son Salvo double aim. In v1, keep the specials to 2 green ones: Bottle (+2 everyone) and Sonar.

Make the game fully playable without a phone. Add a laptop 'presenter peek': hold a key (K) to show the model, the accepted variants and the trap in a small corner card that auto-hides on release. Also offer a second-window presenter view over BroadcastChannel for extended displays. Build the QR phone remote as a shared platform service (Supabase Realtime broadcast with a 4-digit room code) that every game reuses, not a Battleship-only feature.

Limit code-built templates to shapes a small morphology engine handles provably: yes/no questions with be, do, did, can, have got, have you ever + pp, is there, going to, and comparative/superlative in state mode. Ship 20-25 hand-reviewed built-in templates with fixture tests (snapshot every generated cell for every template). Make reported and embedded questions and the third conditional hand-authored built-in grids only, not generative.

Replace exhaustive accept[] lists with normalisation rules: contraction expansion, optional time phrase, have/have got equivalence. Keep 'Kabul' long-press as the escape hatch, and show the trap line prominently, since the trap is what teachers really use.

Commit to a self-hosted SVG icon set (OpenMoji-style, one licence, one art style) with an imageKey index covering the noun lists of every Genç template (about 250 icons), shared across all games. For LLM-prompted Genç grids, constrain the axis vocabulary to the icon index in the prompt itself. Then 'drop without imageKey' rarely fires and the output is regenerated rather than silently shrunk.

Handle the prompt-to-template failure honestly. The LLM returns {templateId, confidence} from the whitelist. When nothing fits, the setup shows 'Bu konu Amiral Battı'na uymuyor' and suggests the closest template or another game (e.g. the tile board). Never force a bad grid.

Retune pacing. The lesson-fit sizes the fleet so that about 50% of expected shots hit (a denser fleet, fewer water cells), and the win condition says plainly 'most points when the clock ends'. For Oyun Parkı, cap Ortak Deniz at 3 crews and cut the echo to once plus the shouted reply, targeting a 35 s turn. Replace the thumbs prediction with the Sonar-style 'hot/cold' hint from Gogo after a miss, so prediction has information.
Cut the Düello Reply role to the whole-class shout in all skins, or make it the defending team's crew read-out only when it adds a new form (tags, B1+). This saves about 8 s per turn.
Move Çift Pratiği out of the mode selector into an 'Yazdır' button (A4 pair sheet plus key) on the setup and end screens.

Budget polish where it shows most. The frame-slot morph animation (go becomes went) is the signature moment: build it first and make it great. Give each skin its three key moments (hit, miss, sunk) with one sound each, and reuse one grid renderer (SVG) with skin tokens, so the three skins are theme files rather than three games.

Input: support tap on the projected grid for smartboards, with 64 px or larger hit targets; the 6x6 grid at full height gives roughly 120 px cells at 1080p. Also support arrow keys plus Enter and a coordinate keypad on the remote. Show row and column coordinates (A-F, 1-6) in large type on both axes so students can call shots from the back row.

Distinct from the existing MCQ tile board (/sinif-oyunu) because it is a spoken sentence-production drill. Do not merge it, but reuse sinif-oyunu's team bar, score, undo and projector shell components, so the build shares the team and scoring infrastructure.

catalog.rankReason: Battleship where firing IS saying the sentence: spoken question forms and short answers, a grammar-speaking mix nothing else offers. It needs a grid content frame and a no-phone presenter peek. MVP: Ortak Deniz + Düello, with ask/state cells only. Kids drop coordinates, point at the two pictures and hear a 'Dinle-söyle' model first. It takes c23's Dig site.

catalog.name: Telaffuz Labirenti (Pronunciation Maze & Minimal Pairs)
catalog.familiarAs: Pronunciation maze / minimal pairs / four corners (TYMM curriculum games)
catalog.oneLiner: Hear it, pick it, say it. The class first plays a whole-class minimal-pairs listening round ('Ses Avcısı'). Then teams steer an avatar through a fogged word maze by choosing and saying the words with the target sound, aimed at sounds Turkish speakers mix up (v/w, θ/t, iː/ɪ, æ/ʌ, final d/t, -ed, stress). A tongue-twister finale closes the game.
catalog.howItPlays:
Arc: Duy, Seç, Söyle, Oyna. Students hear the sound before they have to say it. The game runs on one screen, with the teacher at the laptop or the smart board.

SETUP (teacher chrome in Turkish, about 60 s)
- One summary line, e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 15 dk · /iː/–/ɪ/ · Kulak Yolu', with a 'Değiştir' link.
- The teacher picks a contrast from the 'Türk öğrencilerin karıştırdığı sesler' catalog, which has quick chips for the top 8.
- A built-in topic or a free prompt can narrow the word list.
- The teacher picks the audio source, then checks the 'Önizle' list. It shows every word with its IPA, picture and sound class, and any word can be struck out.
- A 5-second sound check plays a test word ('Arka sıra duyuyor mu?'). If the back row cannot hear it, one tap switches to 'Öğretmen okur'.

PHASE 1: SES AVCISI (whole class, 3-4 min, 8 items, no team scores)
1. The pair appears side by side: pictures for kids (sheep | ship), words plus optional IPA for older groups.
2. The app says ONE of the two words (twice for kids), or the teacher reads it from the cue sheet or phone.
3. Answer lock: everyone thinks until '3, 2, 1... Show me!' (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s). Then everyone answers at once, so nobody can copy the fastest student. Ways to answer:
   - A/B cards (colour plus shape)
   - the sound's own gesture: bite the lip for /v/, round the lips for /w/, tongue tip out for /θ/, big smile for /iː/
   - left or right side of the room
   - stand or sit
   - fingers
4. The teacher taps one 'Sınıf ne dedi?' button: Hepsi / Çoğu / Yarı yarıya / Azı. There is no counting; this only feeds the class meter.
5. Reveal: the right twin glows, both words play (target, then contrast) and the mouth-shape animation runs. The class echoes both words with the gesture.
6. If the class split (Yarı yarıya or Azı), the pair comes back 3 items later with the OTHER twin (adaptive re-ask).

The item formats rotate:
- 'Same or different?': two words are heard. A1 starts here.
- 'Which one?': the core format.
- 'Odd one out': three words are heard and students show fingers 1-3 (A2+).
- 'Four Corners': for sounds with 3 or 4 categories (-s /s z ɪz/, -ed /t d ɪd/, stress patterns Oo, oO, Ooo, oOo), with printable corner posters. In a crowded room students point at the posters instead of walking.

STIRRER (45 s, optional): 'Sound Simon'. The host calls out gestures ('Simon says /θ/!'). Nobody sits out.

PHASE 2: LABİRENT (teams, 6-12 min)
The board is a fogged grid. Only the cells next to an avatar are lit and readable. Visited cells stay lit as a trail. The rule strip shows the target sound as a symbol, a mouth icon and one short line within the text cap.

There are two path rules. The contrast chooses one, and the teacher can override it:
- KULAK YOLU (Ear path). Used when the spelling gives the answer away (v/w, θ/t, final d/t), and by default for kids. At every junction, two of the lit cells are twins (vest | west). The app says the one on the path, and the team has to pick it.
- SES YOLU (Sound path). Used when the spelling does not help: book /ʊ/ vs food /uː/, bread vs bead, this /ð/ vs thin /θ/, walked /t/ vs wanted /ɪd/, stress patterns. The team has to find a lit cell that contains the target sound.

A turn:
1. The seat-number spinner picks the active team's speaker. Nobody is named.
2. Team talk (10 / 15 / 20 s). The team whispers the lit words and may use the throat test: with a hand on the throat, /ð z d v/ buzz and /θ s t f/ do not.
3. The speaker points or taps, or calls a direction in English ('Go up! Go left!') while the teacher presses the arrow key. The speaker SAYS the word aloud, and the whole class echoes it.
4. Reveal: the cell flips and the model audio plays at once, so the class hears their attempt and the model back to back. Arena and Stüdyo also see the IPA and the mouth animation. For kids, Gogo parrots the word.
5. The step gets two separate results:
   - CHOICE is automatic: does the word have the target sound or not.
   - CLARITY comes from the teacher's judge buttons: Net / Anlaşılır / Bir daha (keys 1/2/3). Net and Anlaşılır both count; the teacher judges intelligibility, not accent. 'Bir daha' replays the model slowly, the team says it together, then the speaker tries once more. The step goes on either way.
6. The result:
   - Right choice: the avatar moves. In Arena and Stüdyo the team may chain up to 3 steps, and each step is spoken.
   - Wrong choice: the trap cell shows its word and sound ('west = /w/'), stays marked for everyone, and the turn passes.

Special cells (pictograms, a few per board):
- Key: sits on a side branch, so a detour means more speaking.
- Echo: the whole class says the word three ways (whisper, normal, big voice).
- Twin bridge: say both twins in a row ('sheep, ship'); at B1+, in one sentence ('The sheep is on the ship').
- The goal.

A round always ends at the end of a full cycle, so every team gets the same number of turns. The lesson-fit timer sets the maze size.

SETTLER (60 s, optional): 'Sessiz dudaklar'. The teacher mouths one twin silently and the class reads the lips and answers A or B. It calms the room after the Echo cells.

PHASE 3: TEKERLEME FİNALİ (2-4 min)
- A short twister packed with the target sound: 'Vivian's very wet van'; for kids, 'A big bug in a bag'.
- The app plays it, and the whole class says it at three speeds.
- Then each team says it together while the teacher judges Temiz / Neredeyse / Bir daha.
- Every clean attempt is worth the same. There are no speed points; the tempo only earns a badge.

CLOSE (1-2 min)
- A 4-pair Ses Avcısı rematch with the other twins fills the class-only 'Sınıf Ses Ölçeri' (round 1 vs now). The wording is never negative, e.g. 'Kulaklar ısınıyor'.
- The whole trail replays as a 'path chant': every word on the path in rhythm, with the class chanting along.
- Then come the ending for the audience mode, a stamp in the class Sound Passport, and the teacher's 'Kaçırılanlar' list (pairs the class split on, trap words) with play buttons.
catalog.playerSetup:
The whole class, split into 2-4 teams of 4-10; it works with 12-40 students.
- Listening phases (Ses Avcısı, Four Corners, rematch) are whole class, and everyone answers every item.
- In the maze, the active team huddles and the seat-number spinner picks its speaker. The speaker says the word first, then the whole class echoes it (choral).
- Oyun Parkı: cooperative. 2-4 team lanes help one shared Gogo across the river. The path length is a multiple of the number of teams, so every team gets the same number of steps.
- Arena and Stüdyo: 2-4 teams race from the corners (or terminal stations) to the centre along routes of equal length.
- Adults' optional 'Mesaj İletildi' round pairs a speaker team with a listener team.
- A frozen speaker may use 'Koro kurtarışı' once per round: the team says the word together, with no penalty.
catalog.contentShape:
(1) sound items (primary):
- kind 'minimal-pair': a, b, ipaA, ipaB, contrast ('/v/ – /w/'), sentenceA/sentenceB (B1+ carrier sentences), tipTr, tts: true.
- kind 'ed-ending': a (e.g. 'walked'), key '/t/'|'/d/'|'/ɪd/'. Plural and 3rd-person -s items reuse this shape with /s z ɪz/.
- kind 'silent-letter': key = letter index.
- kind 'stress': key = index of the stressed syllable. Noun/verb pairs use a and b, always in a carrier phrase.
- kind 'rhyme': fillers for twisters and Echo cells.

(2) vocab items as maze cells: term, ipa (from words.js field 'i', e.g. "three" → "/θriː/"; never from the LLM), media.emoji/img (required for A1 and A2 Genç), concrete. Code tags each word with soundTags {phonemes[] (longest-match tokenizer, so eɪ, aɪ and ɪə are not read as ɪ), initial, final, syll, stressIdx (from ˈ), edClass, sClass}.

(3) pair items with rel 'sound': the twins placed at Kulak Yolu junctions. Code checks that exactly one phoneme differs.

(4) odd items with kind 'sound': the 'Odd one out' items, heard in Ses Avcısı.

(5) speaking-prompt items with mode 'talk', target 'snd:v-w', secs 20: the tongue twisters. The prompt stays within the text cap, and code checks by IPA that it holds at least 3 target-sound words.

(6) optional mcq items (fmt 'meaning' with ctx): the B2 'stress changes meaning' round, with 4 paraphrases.

A static CONTRAST CATALOG is owned by code and never generated: {id 'v-w', target '/v/', contrast '/w/', kinds, position 'initial'|'any'|'final', spellingTransparent (true forces Kulak Yolu), gestureKey, mouthKey (SVG sprite), tipTr (e.g. /v/ 'Üst dişlerini alt dudağına koy, titreşsin'; /w/ 'Dudaklarını u gibi yuvarla, dişler dudağa değmesin'; final d 'Sondaki d'yi t yapma, önündeki sesliyi biraz uzat'), throatTest, levelMin, excludeSets (BATH and LOT words that change between UK and US, e.g. dance, can't, hot), blocklist}.

A curated, self-hosted minimal-pair bank (about 300 pairs, with IPA, emoji and optional pre-rendered clips) covers words that are missing from words.js (vest, vet and whale are not there).

Code generates per game (never the LLM): maze {seed, rows, cols, cells[{r, c, itemId, role 'path'|'trap'|'branch'|'key'|'echo'|'twin'|'start'|'goal'}], walls, starts[], goal}, plus the cue order for 'Öğretmen okur'.

Code checks feasibility before the start. For example, a 7×7 Arena board needs about 24 target words and 16 contrast words. If the pool is too small, the game offers a smaller maze or a labelled top-up from the same level.

The LLM (a free prompt through the Material Maker endpoint) only proposes topic words, carrier sentences and twisters. Code classifies every sound and applies the teenSafe filter, the text caps and the blocklist.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Mind the Gap' (a Sound Lab). The motto is 'clear, not native': the goal is being understood.

Look and sound
- An editorial quiz-night tube map on cream (or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme), system sans.
- No mascot and no voice lines. Woodblock and piano cues, with a soft two-note piano chime at each station.
- The maze is drawn as the metro: stations are words, and lines are the open passages. Fogged stations appear as 'next stops'.
- 2-4 teams with city names or puns ('The Silent Letters', 'Minimal Pairs') start at terminal stations and race to Central. Each team's route has the same number of stops: the generator rotates one route shape and fills it with different words.

Rules on screen (English): Choose a station with the target sound. Announce it. Chain up to 3.

A turn
- The rotating spokesperson (picked by the spinner, with pair consultation) announces the next station like a metro announcer: 'Next stop: Thursday.' At A1-A2 it is the word alone; at B1+ it goes inside a carrier sentence from the pack, e.g. 'Next stop: I walked to work.'
- Scoring:
  - right station: 100
  - clarity bonus: +50 for Net
  - tickets on branch stations: +150 each at the end
- Optional 'Express' wager: the team declares 3 stations before moving. If all are right, the turn doubles; a miss loses the wager. Negatives are off by default.
- Wrong station: the right answer plus a one-line reason in English ('bread = /e/; ea is often short'), with the Turkish tip in the teacher chrome. Minus points are optional.
- Hints cost 25 each: the IPA of the lit stations, then a context sentence, then the Turkish mouth tip. The Turkish tip can be switched off for immersion classes.

Content: life and work (travel, food, work, health, shopping, phone calls).
- Examples: 'Please take a seat / sit', 'full / fool', 'I'd like / I like', 'I walked / worked all day', 'The three thousand threads were thin'.
- B1-B2 add word-family stress (PHOtograph / phoTOgraphy / photoGRAphic), noun/verb stress (a REcord / to reCORD), weak forms ('I can swim' /kən/ vs 'I can't swim'), linking and meaning-changing sentence stress.

Extra round 'Mesaj İletildi' (Message Delivered, 3-4 min, printable cue cards)
- A speaker from one team secretly draws a card (A or B dot) and says that twin.
- The other team points, all together, to the word they heard.
- When the message gets through, BOTH teams score, so clear speaking and careful listening are rewarded together.
- When it fails, the teacher taps 'söyleyiş' or 'dinleme' to file it in Kaçırılanlar.

'Anlaşılırlık önceliği' preset (default on, based on the Lingua Franca Core idea)
- The judge listens for vowel length, final consonants, clusters and stress.
- /θ ð/ said as a clear dental t/d, or as f/v, counts as Anlaşılır.

Ending: full scores, the path chant, the class clarity meter (the Net share in the first half vs the second half, plus the Ses Avcısı rematch), and 'Kaçırılanlar' with play buttons. The list prints as a home sheet with IPA and Turkish tips.

Rounds of 8-12 min, 10-25 min in total.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two ages, two rule packs. Level and skin are independent: grade 6-8, or the 'çocuksu görseller' tick, switches a class to Arena.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç): 'Gogo's River'

Look and sound
- Cream background, a bright river and big round stepping stones with pictures, with mist over the far stones.
- The team animals (panda, fox, lion, frog) cheer on the bank, and the Sound Tree waits on the far side.
- Andika-type font. Marimba sounds, no buzzers.
- A1 Genç stones show pictures only; the word writes itself under a stone after the class says it. A2 Genç stones show a picture plus the word.
- Gogo the parrot is both host and hopper, and demos a 25-second practice crossing first (not scored).

Three rules on one pictogram card (the teacher reads the Turkish version): Listen. Point. Say it together!

Cooperative play
- One Gogo, and all teams help it cross.
- Each team makes one step per turn, and the path length is a multiple of the team count, so every team gets the same number of steps.
- Kulak Yolu only; Ses Yolu appears only at A2 Genç 'Zor'.

A turn
1. Gogo says the word slowly (0.8x, automatic).
2. On '3, 2, 1... Show me!' the WHOLE class shows the sound's gesture. This is the whole-class moment every turn.
3. The seat-number speaker touches the stone and says the word.
4. The class echoes it twice with the gesture while Gogo parrots it.
5. The team lane gets a star, plus a second star for a clear voice. Judging is generous.

Wrong stone
- A soft 'boing' and a little splash. Gogo shakes the water off, giggles and hops back.
- Second try, with free hints in order: the mouth card plus the gesture, then both words slowly side by side, then Gogo says only the first sound ('vvv...').
- Still wrong: Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, the team gets an effort star (it goes to the class album), and Gogo hops on anyway.
- Nobody gets stuck, nothing is taken away, and nobody is out.

Extras
- Echo stones: mouse voice, person voice, lion voice (robot voice in 'Sessiz sınıf').
- Golden-feather side stones: the class votes thumbs up or down on the detour, and a feather becomes an album sticker.
- A 'Gogo says' stirrer: gestures only, nobody sits down.
- A lip-reading settler.
- Once per game, Gogo gets it wrong on purpose ('I see a ship!' under the sheep) so the class can correct it.

Listening round 'Gogo's Ear Game': pictures only. It starts with 'Same or different?', and students answer by gesture, A/B cards or stand/sit.

Twister: 3-5 words with pictures ('A big bug in a bag', 'Three free trees', 'Sheep on a ship'), said together at turtle, rabbit and cheetah speed.

Ending: every team gets a title (Super Listeners, Clear Voices, Brave Speakers, Best Echo). Gogo stamps the class Sound Passport and gains a new feather colour. A jar of music notes shows the class meter.

Pacing: timer off, 15-20 min fixed (3 rounds of 3-5 min plus a stirrer and a settler).

Kids checklist: 3 rules; explainable in 20 s with pictograms; no elimination; no score below zero; a whole-class response every turn; a splash instead of a fall.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç, and for any Genç class at grade 6-8): 'Signal Run'

Look and sound
- Dark navy circuit board, neon in the team colours, condensed display font.
- No mascot, no pastels, no 'superstar'.
- In 10 s, each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.
- Teams are glowing signal pulses that start in the corners of a 7×7 board and race to the Core in the centre. Every team's route has the same shape, rotated and filled with different words, so the race is fair.
- Nodes light up as a pulse arrives. Synth blips.

Rule card in English, with a Turkish toggle:
1. Pick a node with the target sound.
2. Say it; the class echoes.
3. Chain up to 3; STATIC ends your run.

Scoring
- 100 per right node.
- +50 'Clean signal' for Net.
- Keys on side nodes, 150 each.
- Combo x1.5 at 3 right in a row and x2 at 5 (accuracy only), with a floor at zero.
- The first pulse into the Core earns +2 keys, and the match ends at the end of that cycle.
- Hints: slow replay (1 pt), 50:50 hides one trap (2 pts), IPA plus mouth animation (1 pt).

Wrong node
- A 0.4 s 'STATIC' glitch (a static stamp in reduced motion). The streak breaks, and the node stays marked.
- The next team may steal by naming the right node and saying it (+1 key). The first team loses nothing.
- Stealing from a team stays off unless the teacher opts in.

Listening round 'Frequency Check': students write the word they heard (sheep or ship) on mini-whiteboards, which also checks spelling. In a crowded room, Four Corners is answered with fingers. A1-A2 Arena classes keep pictures and auto-read.

Commentator strip, at most once per turn: 'CHAIN x3', 'CLEAN SIGNAL', 'CLUTCH!'.

Twister finale 'Beat Mode': the twister goes over a drum loop at 80, 100 and 120 bpm. Each clean attempt is worth the same, and the tempo is only a Bronze/Silver/Gold badge.

Ending: a podium plus stat awards (Longest chain, Cleanest signal, Sharpest ears, Comeback), and never a last place. The class meter is shown as an equalizer.

Content stays teenSafe and concrete (school, sport, games, animals, food, tech). 12-20 min.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1 (Genç: Oyun Parkı with pictures only; adults: word plus emoji)
- Contrasts: two-way only, word-initial position, with concrete picture words:
  - /v/-/w/: vet/wet
  - /θ/-/t/: three/tree, thin/tin
  - /θ/-/s/: mouth/mouse, think/sink
  - /iː/-/ɪ/: sheep/ship, bean/bin, heel/hill
  - /æ/-/ʌ/: cat/cut, cap/cup, bag/bug, hat/hut
- Kulak Yolu only. Ses Avcısı starts with 'Same or different?'.
- Maze 4×4 for kids and 5×5 for adults, path of 5-6, chain 1.
- Auto read-aloud at 0.8x for kids; adults hear the word in the carrier 'I say ___'.
- Twisters of 3-5 words.

A2
- New contrasts:
  - /ʊ/-/uː/: full/fool, pull/pool
  - /æ/-/e/: pan/pen, man/men, bad/bed
  - final voicing /d/-/t/ and /g/-/k/: bad/bat, bag/back, dog/dock (the vowel is longer before a voiced end)
  - /ŋ/-/n/: thing/thin, sing/sin (no added g)
  - -s endings /s z ɪz/: Four Corners with 3 corners
- Words can have the sound in any position.
- Ses Yolu unlocks for spelling-opaque sets (oo in book/food, ea in bread/bead).
- Maze 5×5, path of 6-8, chain 2 in Arena and Stüdyo. 'Odd one out' by ear.

B1
- New contrasts:
  - -ed endings /t d ɪd/: walked/played/wanted, with the throat test
  - silent letters: walk, knife, Wednesday, island, listen, climb, half, hour, write
  - stress in 2-3 syllable words: Four Corners Oo/oO/Ooo/oOo
  - /ð/-/d/ and /θ/-/ð/: they/day, then/den, thin/this
  - cluster epenthesis pairs: sport/support, blow/below, state/estate
  - minimal pairs inside sentences: 'Can I borrow your pen / pan?'
- Maze 6×6 to 7×7, path of 8-10, chain 3.
- Twin bridges are said in one sentence. The IPA is shown after the reveal.

B2
- New contrasts:
  - weak forms and can/can't in sentences
  - contractions by ear: I'd like / I like, we'll / we
  - noun/verb stress pairs: a REcord / to reCORD, PREsent / preSENT, INcrease / inCREASE (always in a carrier phrase)
  - stress shift in word families: PHOtograph / phoTOgraphy / photoGRAphic, ECOnomy / ecoNOmic
  - linking: turn it off
  - meaning-changing sentence stress: 'I didn't say she took it' with 4 paraphrases. The teacher or a student reads it, because TTS cannot stress a word on purpose.
- Maze 7×7, path of 10-12, and 2-3 contrasts mixed across rounds.
- B2 Genç gets richer words on concrete topics, never abstract debate or adult domains.

The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial inside a group
- Kolay: one contrast, word-initial only, slower audio, and the first hint shown automatically after 10 s.
- Zor: near-neighbour traps (an /iː/ path with both /ɪ/ and /eɪ/ traps), less fog, and no pictures on the cells at A2+.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the contrast list by one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 8-25. Quick: 8-10 (Ses Avcısı plus a short maze). Standard: 15. Full: 18-20 for kids (fixed), 12-20 for Arena, 10-25 for Stüdyo.
catalog.teacherControls:
Setup (Turkish chrome, saved to the class profile; it reuses the /sinif-oyunu team bar, seat spinner and class profile)
- Contrast picker: the catalog is grouped by level. The 'Türk öğrenciler için en sık 8' chips are v/w, θ/t, ð/d, iː/ɪ, æ/e, æ/ʌ, final d/t and -ed. Each contrast carries a TYMM unit tag, and up to 3 contrasts can be mixed, one per round.
- Content source: a built-in topic intersected with the contrast, or a free prompt in Turkish or English. The prompt goes through the Material Maker endpoint with its rate limit. The LLM only proposes words and sentences; code classifies the sounds.
- An 'Önizle' list where any word can be struck out, and a feasibility report.

Audio
- TTS UK or US with a voice picker, and pre-recorded clips when they exist.
- 'Öğretmen okur': a printable cue sheet with IPA and a Turkish tip for each cue. Alternatively, the teacher opens the 4-digit seed code on a phone, which shows the same cue order with no network.
- 'Öğrenci okur': the Mesaj İletildi cards.
- Speed 0.6 / 0.8 / 1.0, auto-read on or off, a sound check, and mute everything.

Structure
- Which phases run: Ses Avcısı, Labirent, Tekerleme, rematch.
- Co-op or race, and the path rule (Kulak Yolu or Ses Yolu).
- Maze size, fog on or off, chain length 1-3, special cells on or off.

Listening response mode: cards, gestures, sides of the room, stand/sit, fingers or whiteboards.

Judging
- Net / Anlaşılır / Bir daha.
- Strictness: 'Cömert' (default) or 'Standart', plus the 'Anlaşılırlık önceliği' preset.
- Undo the last move, skip an item, and 'Koro kurtarışı' on or off.

Standard dials: timer ('Süresiz' by default for kids, +10 s, T to pause), huddle length, hint costs, Turkish tips off, negatives, wager, steal opt-in, comeback, reduced motion, and 'Sessiz sınıf' (the Echo cell's lion voice becomes a robot voice, and Four Corners becomes pointing).

Keyboard: Space replay, S slow, 1/2/3 judge, arrows move, U undo, H hint, T pause, N next, M mute.

Printables
- A/B cards (colour plus shape)
- gesture and mouth cards
- corner posters (Oo/oO/Ooo/oOo, /t d ɪd/, /s z ɪz/)
- the teacher cue sheet
- the Mesaj İletildi cue deck
- the Sound Passport page
- the Kaçırılanlar home sheet

The class profile remembers the stamped sounds and suggests the next contrast.
catalog.delightDetails:
Mouths and bodies
- Mouth-shape cards and animations for about 14 phonemes (front view of the lips plus a side view). They become static in reduced motion. They show on every reveal and are the first hint.
- A gesture for each sound that doubles as the answer, so the class answers with their mouths: bite the lip for /v/, round lips for /w/, tongue tip for /θ/, smile for /iː/, jaw drop for /æ/, a short 'uh' for /ʌ/, and pinched fingers for short vowels vs hands stretching apart for long ones.
- The throat test, with a buzz-meter animation for voiced and voiceless sounds.
- At A1 Genç, the word writes itself under the picture stone after the class says it: sound first, spelling second.

Oyun Parkı
- Gogo the parrot parrots every right word in a higher 'parrot voice' (TTS pitch 1.4).
- Gogo hops, splashes, shakes the water off, sleeps on a stone on the pause screen, and gets a new feather colour for each passport stamp.
- Once per game Gogo 'mixes up' a word so the class can correct it.

Arena
- Pulses of neon light run along the circuit traces, and a wrong node gives a STATIC glitch.
- Keys jingle, and the strip shows 'CHAIN x3' and 'CLEAN SIGNAL'.
- The twister Beat Mode runs on a drum loop.

Stüdyo
- Tube-map stations and a two-note station chime.
- A ticket-punch click for tickets, and the speaker as a metro announcer ('Next stop: Thursday').
- A 'Mind the gap' caption at Central.

For everyone
- Echo cells with mouse, person and lion voices.
- Twin cells joined by a tiny bridge icon, so twins read as a pair.
- The fog lifts as the class says the word together.
- The path-chant finale.
- The Sound Passport, printable, with '/θ/ ustası' stamps in the teacher view and a θ plus tongue picture for kids.
- The class meter: a jar of notes for kids, an equalizer in Arena, two quiet bars in Stüdyo.
- A seed code that syncs the teacher's phone cue list with no network.
- Colour-blind-safe A/B cards that use colour and shape.
catalog.risks:
Audio
- Browser TTS may have no English voice on Pardus-based MEB smart boards, and speakers are often weak or unplugged.
- TTS also mangles isolated minimal pairs and homographs (live, read, record, close).
- Mitigations: pre-rendered clips for the curated core, carrier phrases for homographs and stress pairs, the setup sound check, and a mandatory 'Öğretmen okur' mode (cue sheet with IPA and tips so non-native teachers feel safe, or the phone view by seed code).

Spelling gives the answer away (v/w, θ/t)
- Kulak Yolu plus fog. This follows the G16 rule in the roadmap: without sound, no text may give the answer away.

Subjective judging
- Choice (automatic) and clarity (teacher) are scored separately, and clarity is only a bonus.
- 'Cömert' is the default, and the judge listens for intelligibility, not a native accent.

Shy or embarrassed students
- Choral first, speakers picked by seat number, and 'Koro kurtarışı' for a speaker who freezes.
- Nobody is named, and the meter is class-level only.

Rude twins
- beach, sheet, piece and six have rude twins, and classes will say the wrong one on purpose.
- A hard blocklist applies in every mode, including adults, and also scans LLM words and twisters.
- wine/vine is blocked for Genç groups.

Wrong IPA or accent variation
- IPA comes only from words.js or the curated bank, never from the LLM.
- A phoneme-level check confirms each pair differs by exactly one phoneme.
- BATH/LOT words that change between UK and US are excluded when they matter, and a homograph list is applied.

Noise and space
- Echo cells and Four Corners are loud in crowded rooms and disturb the class next door. Mitigations: 'Sessiz sınıf' and pointing instead of walking.

Feasibility
- A narrow topic plus a rare contrast may not fill a maze. The feasibility check offers a smaller maze or a labelled top-up.

Race fairness
- Rotated route shapes keep the routes equal, and each round ends at the end of a full cycle.

Deaf or hard-of-hearing students
- Mouth visuals and gestures carry the reveal, so it never depends on audio alone.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (G16 Ses ayrımı sınıflandırma: without sound, no text may give the answer away)
C:/lg/src/data/words.js (UK IPA in field 'i' with the stress mark, e.g. three /θriː/, west /west/; vest and vet are missing, hence a curated pair bank)
Jenkins, J. (2000) The Phonology of English as an International Language (Lingua Franca Core: intelligibility over native accent)
Baker, A. Ship or Sheep? (Cambridge) — the classic minimal-pair tradition

issues: Setup is too long for the moment a teacher walks into a room.
