The steps are: contrast picker, then topic or prompt, then audio source, then the Önizle list with strike-outs, then the feasibility report, then the sound check, then (for kids) a Gogo demo crossing, then a rule card per phase. Realistically that is 3-5 minutes, not 60 s. The worst case is a new teacher who opens Önizle and starts reviewing 30 words while 28 kids wait.

There are too many phases for 15 minutes. The sequence is Ses Avcısı (with 4 rotating item formats), stirrer, maze, settler, twister at 3 speeds plus team attempts, rematch, path chant, ending and passport. Each has its own rules and its own response mode, and every transition costs 30-60 s of re-explaining and settling. The kids' '3 rules' claim holds for the maze only; the session as a whole teaches about 8 rule sets plus one gesture per sound.

Teacher cognitive load per maze turn is high. The teacher runs the spinner, presses an arrow key or taps (while the speaker calls 'Go left!'), presses 1/2/3 to judge, sometimes hits 'Bir daha' and repeats, then presses N or next. The Ses Avcısı items add a 'Sınıf ne dedi?' tap each. That is 4-5 inputs per turn while standing at the board and managing 28 kids. Arena 7×7 routes plus chain-3 multiply the arrow presses.

A single speaker cannot really be judged in a noisy room of 28. Once the class echoes, the individual attempt is masked. In practice the teacher presses 'Net' by default, so the clarity bonus (+50 Arena and Stüdyo) turns into noise or favouritism, and adults may dispute it.

Idle teams in the maze. In the Arena and Stüdyo race, three of the four teams only echo while the active team huddles for 15-20 s. In Kulak Yolu the app says the path word aloud to everyone, so non-active teams blurt the answer, the huddle becomes pointless, and the noise rises. Only the kids' co-op version has the whole-class '3,2,1 Show me' gesture every turn.

Fog and the maze add navigation, not learning. Each step is a binary (Kulak) or 2-3-way (Ses Yolu) choice, so the grid geometry, walls, branches and arrow keys are overhead. In Ses Yolu under fog, weak teams are guessing at 33-50% chance, and a wrong pick ends the turn, so the maze becomes luck-heavy.

Fairness in the race: chaining up to 3, combo multipliers (x1.5 and x2) and steals (+1 key) all compound in favour of the strongest team. The 'first into Core, match ends that cycle' rule means a strong team with chains can finish while others are halfway. Equal route lengths don't equalise turns once chains exist. In Stüdyo the Express wager widens gaps further. There is no comeback mechanic.
One strong student dominates the huddle. The spinner picks who speaks, but in team talk the confident kid decides the cell and whispers the word, so the chosen speaker just repeats it.

Gestures and physical responses are hard in Turkish public classrooms. Tongue-out for /θ/ and lip-biting cause giggles with 10-12 year-olds. Sides of the room and stand/sit are impractical with fixed desks and 28-40 students. Echo cells with lion voices plus Four Corners are loud and bother the class next door. Rude-twin trolling will happen during the echo even with the blocklist, because students invent their own.

Audio dependence on MEB boards. Pardus boards often have no English TTS voice and weak or unplugged speakers, and the whole game hinges on hearing the difference. The fallback 'Öğretmen okur' puts the discrimination burden on a non-native teacher who may themselves merge /v/-/w/ or /iː/-/ɪ/, and phones are often restricted in class. If the teacher's model is unreliable, the listening game teaches the wrong contrast.

Printable dependence: A/B cards for 28 kids, corner posters, mini-whiteboards (Arena 'Frequency Check'; many state schools lack sets), passport pages and cue decks. Each session needs prep the teacher may not have time for, and there is no zero-print path stated as default.

Stopping at any moment is only partial. The round ends at a full cycle, which is good, but if the bell comes mid-maze, the twister, rematch, meter and passport (the payoff) are lost. There is no 'jump to close' shortcut described.

Seat-number spinner: Turkish classes use okul numarası and class lists, not seat numbers, and absent students break it. With 28 kids and about 12 maze turns, 16 kids never speak individually. That is acceptable, but the spinner needs absence handling and 'not twice until everyone' memory.

For adults (10 people, 2-4 teams of 2-5) the dynamic is better, but the maze and fog read as a kids' mechanic. Adults usually want more individual reps and feedback per minute than a turn-based race gives: each adult speaks individually perhaps 3-4 times in 20 minutes. Mesaj İletildi is the strongest adult part yet it is only 'optional'.

Build size is L, and the ambition is huge: 3 skins, about 14 mouth animations with side views, a 300-pair curated bank with clips, a phoneme tokenizer, a maze generator with a feasibility check, a seed-synced phone view, and about 8 printables. There is a risk that a half-finished version ships with rough audio, which is fatal for a pronunciation game.
fixes: Add one-tap presets on the setup screen: 'Hızlı başla' chips such as 'sheep/ship · 12 dk · Oyun Parkı' that skip Önizle and the feasibility report, using only the curated bank. Make Önizle and the free prompt collapsible 'advanced' options. Run the sound check automatically during the Gogo demo instead of as a separate step.

Cut the default session to 3 beats: Ses Avcısı (6 items), Path (maze), Twister plus a 1-screen close. Make the stirrer, settler, rematch, path chant, Four Corners and Odd one out opt-in extras. Show one rule card per phase only the first time a class plays; the class profile remembers it after that.

Replace free grid navigation with a stepping-stone path. At each step, show 2 (Kulak) or 3 (Ses) candidate cells as big tap targets, so no arrow keys are needed. Keep the tube-map or circuit look as decoration of a linear route with optional side-branch forks. The whole turn then takes one tap from the speaker or teacher plus one judge key.

Merge judging into a single optional key. The default is choice-only scoring, and clarity judging is off for the race (or only adds a class-level star). Where it is on, judge the speaker BEFORE the class echoes: the speaker says it, the teacher presses 1/2/3, then comes the echo. Remove the per-item 'Sınıf ne dedi?' tap or make it optional, and default the meter to rematch-only.

Give every team something to do every turn in Arena and Stüdyo. All teams secretly show A/B or the gesture on '3,2,1' before the active team's pick is revealed, and every team that matched earns a small key or point. That kills blurting and idle time. In Kulak Yolu, play the word only after the lock-in countdown, and let non-active teams score by showing, not by shouting.

Fairness: cap chaining at 2 by default and make chain-3 or Express opt-in for adults. Remove combo multipliers for Genç Arena, or cap them so no team gains more than one extra step per cycle. Add a catch-up rule: the trailing team gets a free 50:50 or a 'rüzgâr' free step. End on a fixed number of cycles rather than 'first into Core'. Show the Arena podium by stat awards only.

Anti-domination: the speaker must pick the cell before team talk, and the team talk only helps pronounce it. Alternatively, the spinner reveals the speaker only after the huddle ends. The spinner never repeats a student until the list has cycled and has an 'absent' toggle, and it uses okul no or a pasted class list.

Gesture set: replace tongue-out and lip-biting with hand signs for the whole-class response (e.g. a V hand for /v/ and a W made with three fingers for /w/, thumb between the teeth shown only by the mouth animation). Make 'Sessiz sınıf' the default for Genç classes of 25+ and for Four Corners. Drop sides of the room and stand/sit from the default response modes.

Audio: ship pre-rendered clips (UK and US) for the entire curated core so the game never needs browser TTS for Kulak Yolu, and block contrasts that have no clip. In 'Öğretmen okur' mode, show the teacher a mouth or tip card for each cue and warn when a contrast is known to be hard for Turkish speakers to produce. Offer a laptop-plus-Bluetooth-speaker hint in the sound check. The seed-code phone view is a nice extra, not the fallback.
Make zero-print the default: fingers (1/2) and hand gestures for all responses. Printables are optional enhancements, and whiteboards are replaced by 'write in your notebook, show on 3'.

Add an always-visible 'Bitir' button that ends the current cycle and jumps straight to a compressed close (twister once plus passport stamp plus Kaçırılanlar), so the payoff happens even with 2 minutes left.

Adults: make Mesaj İletildi a standard Stüdyo phase rather than an extra, and add a pair-drill interlude where everyone says the pair to a partner for 30 s. That raises individual reps from about 4 to 20+. Frame the maze as a light scoring layer on top.

Scope for build: the MVP is Ses Avcısı plus a linear stone path plus twister, in 2 skins (Oyun Parkı and Stüdyo, with Arena as a palette swap), the top-8 contrasts, about 120 curated pairs with clips, and static mouth cards. Four Corners, -ed and stress corners, B2 weak forms, 14-phoneme animations, the phone sync and the Sound Passport come in v2. Reuse the /sinif-oyunu team bar and spinner as stated.

issues: It fills a real gap: no other game in the suite teaches pronunciation or listening discrimination. The level progression is well thought out: initial-position pairs at A1, final voicing and -s at A2, -ed, silent letters and stress at B1, weak forms and contrastive stress at B2. The pedagogy (hear, then choose, then say) is sound. Most problems are about scope and feasibility, not about the idea.

The content swap is mostly nominal. The real content is the contrast from the catalog plus the curated bank. A built-in topic or a free LLM prompt only narrows the word list, and topic ∩ contrast ∩ level is often tiny (e.g. 'food' ∩ /θ/-/t/ at A1 gives almost nothing). The feasibility check will then fall back to the generic bank most of the time. The hard requirement 'the teacher types a prompt and the content changes' is only weakly met, and a teacher who types 'hayvanlar' may feel the prompt was ignored.

A1 Genç, pictures only: many classic twins are not picturable or are not vocabulary a 9-year-old knows. Examples: west, wet, tin, sink, heel, hill, hut, bin, fool, pool vs pull, sin, dock. The kids end up drilling sounds in unknown words, which gives little language learning and makes the pictures ambiguous (is it a 'bin' or a 'trash can'?). A usable picturable A1 kids set is probably only 15-25 pairs, which is not enough to fill mazes plus Ses Avcısı plus the rematch without repeats.

Kulak Yolu choices are binary, so a team picks right 50% of the time by pure guessing. With chaining up to 3 and scoring in Arena and Stüdyo, luck swamps skill. The score says little about discrimination.

In Kulak Yolu the speaker 'says the word' after the app has already said it and the team has picked it. That is imitation, not production, and clarity judging then mostly measures echo. In Ses Yolu the speaker produces first, but only A2+ gets it and kids rarely do.

Ses Yolu asks students to find a cell 'containing /ʊ/' from spelling and word knowledge. That is abstract, metalinguistic and text-heavy. It is fine for B1+ adults, but too abstract for A2 Genç 'Zor' and for 12-year-olds unless every cell has audio on tap.

Audio is a single point of failure. Browser TTS on Pardus smart boards often has no English voice, and TTS blurs isolated minimal pairs (ship/sheep, full/fool are notoriously weak). The 'Öğretmen okur' fallback is risky: many Turkish EFL teachers do not reliably produce /v/-/w/, /æ/-/e/ or final voicing themselves, so the listening test may become invalid without anyone noticing.

Teacher clarity judging does not scale. In a 30-40 student room with choral echo, one speaker's single word at the board is hard to hear, and judging Net/Anlaşılır per step for every team is tiring. For kids, a public per-team 'clear voice' star turns the teacher's ear into a visible ranking of individual children's accents.

Gestures as whole-class answers suit 9-11-year-olds but backfire at 12-14. 'Tongue tip out' for /θ/ and 'bite the lip' in front of peers produce giggles and refusal, and Arena makes gestures one option among equals. Some gestures are not gestures at all ('a short uh' for /ʌ/), and gestures are easy to copy from a neighbour after the 'Show me!' moment.

Too much for a teacher to learn: 4 phases, 4 item formats, a stirrer, a settler, 2 path rules, 4 special cells, a wager, a steal, Mesaj İletildi, Four Corners posters, a Sound Passport, a seed-code phone sync, 7 printables, 10 keyboard keys. The kids pack keeps 3 visible rules, but the teacher has to run far more than that. Setup takes well over 60 s in practice, and build size L understates it.

Some Stüdyo pieces feel babyish or awkward for adults: Echo cells with mouse and lion voices, the path chant, the choral 'show me' gestures. The metro-announcer frame for a sentence ('Next stop: I walked to work') sounds unnatural. Adults also cannot practise production for their own weaknesses, because everyone gets the same contrast.

Race fairness: rotated route shapes are equal, but each route gets different words, so difficulty differs (e.g. an /iː/ route with 'bean, heel' vs one with 'leave, feel'). Under fog, that is unfair in a way no one can see.
B2 contrastive sentence stress relies on a human reader and 4 paraphrases. That makes it a reading-comprehension MCQ, not a maze item, and it barely fits the maze metaphor.

Rude-twin risk is handled with a blocklist, but kids will still deliberately mispronounce harmless pairs into other rude words (e.g. /æ/-/ʌ/ and /ɪ/-/iː/ neighbours outside the listed ones). The blocklist has to be phoneme-neighbour-aware, not a word list.
fixes: Ship an MVP first: Ses Avcısı ('Which one?' and 'Same or different?'), Labirent with Kulak Yolu, and the tongue-twister finale, with the 8 top contrasts. Defer Mesaj İletildi, Four Corners, Sound Simon, the lip-reading settler, Echo voices, the wager, the steal, the seed-code phone sync and B2 contrastive stress to v2.

Make pre-rendered audio mandatory for the whole curated bank: neural TTS rendered once at build time, UK plus US, self-hosted, with a carrier version for each item. Use browser TTS only for LLM top-up words, and mark those items 'otomatik ses'. The sound check should test a real minimal pair, not one word.

Be honest in the prompt path. Label it 'Konu kelimeleri daraltır' and show 'Bu konuda 7 uygun kelime bulundu, 17 genel kelimeyle tamamlandı' before starting. Also let the prompt pick the twister theme and the carrier sentences, where the LLM actually adds variety.

Build a separate A1/A2 Genç kid pair bank, restricted to both twins being picturable and in a kids' known-vocabulary list (e.g. sheep/ship, cat/cut, cap/cup, bag/bug, three/tree, mouth/mouse, pen/pan, man/men, bad/bed, dog/duck-style near pairs). If a twin is not picturable, the pair is A2+ adults only. Allow repeats by design (a spiral), and say so.

Reduce guessing: at A2+, junctions offer 3 lit cells (target, twin, and a near-neighbour trap such as /eɪ/ for /iː/). Score only first attempts, and never let a chain continue after an unscored guess.

Make production real: in Kulak Yolu, have the speaker say the chosen word BEFORE the model audio plays (choose, say, then hear the model), so the model becomes feedback, not a prompt. Keep choral echo afterwards.

Make clarity judging class-level for kids: no per-team clear-voice star; Net fills the shared jar instead. In Arena and Stüdyo, make the +50 clarity bonus optional and off by default when there are more than 25 students. Offer 'Koro' clarity (the whole team says it) as the default speaker mode for large rooms.
Make gestures the default only in Oyun Parkı. In Arena, default to A/B cards or fingers, and drop the tongue-out and lip-bite gestures there. Replace the /ʌ/ 'uh' with a real hand sign.

In 'Öğretmen okur' mode, warn the teacher in the chrome: 'Bu modda dinleme testi sizin telaffuzunuza bağlı'. Show the mouth tip next to each cue, and recommend playing the clips from a phone with a Bluetooth speaker as the better fallback.
Give every team's route the same words in a different order, or balance route difficulty by phoneme class and word frequency, so the race is fair under fog.

Stüdyo: remove the animal Echo voices and the path chant, and keep the tube map. Use natural carriers ('Next stop: Thursday' for words; for sentences, 'Announce: I walked to work today'). Add a 'Kişisel hedef' option where each team picks its own contrast from the class's Kaçırılanlar list.
Replace the word blocklist with a phoneme-neighbour check. Reject any cell word whose one-phoneme vowel or consonant neighbour is on a rude list, in all modes.
Export sound items to the shared pack so Hangman, the tile board and Bingo can run a 'sound' round. The pronunciation content then pays off across the suite, not only in this one L-size game.

issues: It fills a real gap. No other candidate trains sound discrimination, and Turkish EFL classes badly need it (v/w, θ/t, iː/ɪ, final devoicing, -ed). It should not be merged into a quiz. As written, though, it is XL, not L: 3 skins x 4 phases, plus Four Corners, Mesaj İletildi, Sound Simon, lip-reading, Beat Mode, Sound Passport, phone seed sync, 7 printables, and about 28 mouth sprites (14 phonemes, front and side views). This is the most over-scoped candidate I have seen, and the delight list will eat the core.

Everything depends on audio, and the plan treats that as a mitigation instead of the foundation. Browser speechSynthesis on Pardus/Linux Chromium smart boards often lists zero voices. Where it works, it clips short isolated words and is unreliable on final d/t (bad/bat), on vowel length, and on anything that relies on stress. The pre-rendered clips are called 'optional'. In practice they are the product, and the design never budgets them: about 300 pairs means about 600 clips, plus -ed/-s/stress items and twisters.

The UK/US accent mismatch is unmanaged. Words.js IPA is Oxford (UK), but the plan offers a TTS voice picker with a US option. A US voice reads 'hot' or 'can't' against a UK IPA reveal, so the automatic 'CHOICE' judgement and the on-screen IPA contradict the audio.

The maze is mostly decoration. The race routes are 'the same shape rotated', and Kulak Yolu makes every junction a forced two-way listening choice, so the board is a linear track with fog on top. Once the path is fixed there are no real routing decisions, and walls, fog and chain rules add build cost but no gameplay. Kulak Yolu turns out to be a themed listening MCQ, which duplicates Ses Avcısı. Only Ses Yolu (find a lit cell that contains the sound) is a genuinely new mechanic.

The fog conflicts with Ses Yolu. If only the neighbouring cells are lit and legible, a spelling-opaque set (book/food, bread/bead) with 2-3 lit options often has zero or two valid target cells unless the generator guarantees exactly one. That rule is not specified, so without it the board can be unsolvable or trivial.

The LLM's role is marginal and often useless. A free-text topic intersected with a narrow contrast (for example 'restaurant' x /v/-/w/) rarely yields 24 target words that are also in words.js with IPA, so most free prompts will fall into 'labelled top-up' and the 'swappable content' promise will be hollow for this game. LLM-written twisters will usually fail the rule of at least 3 IPA-verified target words, or will contain words that are not in words.js and so cannot be classified.

Phone seed sync breaks with LLM content. A 4-digit seed can reproduce the cue order offline only if the phone already has the exact pack. For a generated pack, the phone needs a network fetch, or the whole pack has to be encoded into a QR.

The scoring units are inconsistent. Arena hints cost '1 pt / 2 pts' while nodes are worth 100, and Stüdyo hints cost 25. The Stüdyo 'Express' wager ('a miss loses the wager') conflicts with 'negatives off' unless a floor is defined.
The setup is too long for a 60 s promise: level, skin, contrast, topic, audio source, Önizle strike-outs, feasibility report and sound check. Teachers who have used Baamboozle expect one tap to play.

Several delight items rely on audio effects TTS cannot deliver reliably across engines: pitch 1.4 'parrot voice' (the pitch parameter is ignored by many voices), the mouse/lion voices on Echo cells, and slow 0.6x rate on Linux voices. On a weak projector speaker, the sheep/ship difference is also inaudible from the back row whatever the source.

The mouth animations are high-risk. Amateur lip and tongue side views look clinical or wrong, and a wrong articulation diagram does active harm. They need a careful illustrator pass or a simpler, well-known schematic style.

Kids speaking /θ/ and /ð/ at 9-11 in front of 30 peers is still exposing, even with seat-number picking. Using 'Net' vs 'Anlaşılır' on children invites teacher bias. The clarity star for kids should just be generous, not a two-level judgement.

The UI text cap on the rule strip plus IPA plus the mouth icon plus the Turkish tip all compete for the projector at the same time. At the 4x4 kids size with pictures, the cells will be crowded on 1024x768 smart boards.
fixes: Build and test the CORE first (about M-L): (1) Ses Avcısı with 'Same or different?' and 'Which one?', whole class, the 'Sınıf ne dedi?' button and adaptive re-ask. (2) A TRACK game (not a free maze) with Kulak Yolu and Ses Yolu cells, the teacher's Net/Anlaşılır/Bir daha buttons, and chain rules per skin. (3) A tongue-twister finale at 3 speeds. (4) A 'Kaçırılanlar' list with play buttons. Push to v2: Mesaj İletildi, lip-reading, Sound Simon (make it a one-screen cue card), Four Corners posters, Beat Mode drum loop, Passport, phone seed sync, and B2 sentence stress.

Make clips the primary audio source. Pre-render the curated bank once, offline, with one high-quality en-GB neural voice (plus an optional en-US set later). Store it as small Opus/MP3 files (about 6-10 KB each, roughly 5-8 MB in total), lazy-loaded per contrast from /public and cached by a service worker. Use TTS only as a fallback for words outside the bank, and show a visible 'Sentetik ses' badge when it is in use. Ship the top-8 contrasts (about 120 pairs) at launch.
Lock the accent to UK (matching the words.js IPA) in v1. If US is added later, it needs its own IPA column and clip set, and BATH/LOT/r-coloured words have to be excluded per accent, not globally.

Make the fixed route explicit and make the choices on it matter. Each step offers 2-3 fogged stones. Branches exist only for Key/feather detours: an optional extra spoken word for a bonus, never a shortcut. Drop walls entirely. The generator guarantees exactly one valid target among the lit cells at each step, and a unit-tested validator rejects any board that breaks this.

Keep Kulak Yolu for kids and for spelling-transparent contrasts, but give each junction a different micro-format (twin pick, odd-one-out stone, echo stone) so it does not play like Ses Avcısı on a grid. Make Ses Yolu the headline mode for A2+ adults and Arena.

Limit the LLM to one job with a hard validator: given a contrast and a topic, it proposes carrier sentences and twisters that use ONLY words from a supplied whitelist (the bank words that pass the contrast filter). Code then re-checks every token against words.js and the bank, counts the target phonemes by IPA, applies the blocklist, and rejects the output otherwise. The topic only reorders or filters the curated bank and never creates cells. In the UI, say plainly that pronunciation games use the curated bank and the topic narrows it.

Write the phoneme tokenizer against the real words.js IPA format, with unit tests for: diphthongs (eɪ aɪ ɔɪ əʊ aʊ ɪə eə ʊə), length marks, ˈ/ˌ stress, syllabic consonants, optional (r) and bracketed schwas, and affricates tʃ/dʒ. The minimal-pair check should run at build time over the curated bank, not only at runtime.
Seed sync: generate the cue sheet as a QR that encodes the cue order and words directly (it fits easily for 20-30 items), so a phone can show it offline for any pack. Drop the 4-digit seed.

Unify scoring: 100 per step and hints at -25 in every non-kids mode, a hard floor at 0, and the wager risks only the points gained that turn. For kids: a star per step plus an effort star, with no clarity grading, just 'Harika!' for any attempt.

Setup: one screen with a 'Hızlı başla' button that uses the class profile's next suggested contrast, plus a collapsible 'Ayarlar'. Run the sound check automatically on the first audio play, with a 'Duyulmadı → Öğretmen okur' toast.
Parrot and funny voices: use WebAudio playbackRate or a pitch shift on the pre-rendered clips instead of TTS pitch, so the effect works on every device.
Mouth visuals: commission or carefully draw about 10 static front-view lip cards in one flat style, with side views only for θ/ð, v/w and iː/ɪ. Morph between 2 keyframes; no free-form animation.

Projector layout: 16:9 with a letterbox. Cells at least 120 px at 1280x720, and IPA and tips shown only on reveal, not in the fog state. On a 4x4 board for kids, show only the stone picture and its number until reveal.
Share the team bar, seat spinner, class profile, audience skins and timer with /sinif-oyunu and the other games, so this game only adds the board, the sound engine and the content bank.

catalog.rankReason: Fills a real gap: pronunciation and sound discrimination for Turkish speakers (v/w, θ/t, iː/ɪ, final devoicing, -ed). It depends on pre-rendered neural audio for the curated bank, which the whole suite needs anyway. MVP: Ses Avcısı, a track game (not a free maze) and a tongue-twister finale, with one-tap quick-start presets. It is teacher-judged, with no speech recognition (KVKK).

catalog.name: Sınıf Birliği: Lav & Canavar (Whole-Class Co-op vs. the Game)
catalog.familiarAs: Gimkit 'The Floor Is Lava' / Classcraft Boss Battle / Blooket Monster Brawl: a cooperative Kahoot in which the whole class plays against the game
catalog.oneLiner: The whole class is one side against the game. Each correct answer builds the tower higher above rising lava or wears down a boss, and each miss brings the threat a notch closer. Crews, roles, three phases and a spoken final stand turn a review quiz into a co-op raid that finishes on time.
catalog.howItPlays:
ONE ENGINE, TWO SKINS. The game tracks two shared numbers.
- GOAL (Hedef): the boss's HP bar, or the distance to the rescue (helicopter, drone or balloon) at the top of the tower.
- SAFETY (Güvenlik): the class heart pool, or the visible gap in blocks between the lava and the top of the tower.
In the Lav skin the lava follows the tower up and always stays SAFETY notches below the top. Every build lifts both, and every miss visibly closes the gap. A correct answer turns into Power, which moves the GOAL. A wrong answer is a strike that costs 1 SAFETY unless someone blocks it. There is one class result and no crew leaderboard.

AUTO-SIZED GOAL. The lesson-fit timer turns minutes into planned items: (minutes minus ~3 min overhead) × 60 / cycle seconds. A cycle is 75 s in Oyun Parkı, 55 s in Arena and 65 s in Stüdyo. The goal is: planned items × expected accuracy × average Power × 0.9.
- Expected accuracy is 0.8 in Oyun Parkı (because kids get second tries) and 0.7 elsewhere.
- The 0.9 factor makes the goal fall a little early, leaving room for the spoken final phase.
- BALANCE ENGINE (Denge): after the first 5 items it quietly rescales the value of one Power unit to the real accuracy, by at most ±25% and never after Phase 1. This keeps every level equally winnable, and the fight ends on time.
- The teacher chrome shows 'Hedef ≈ 16 soru'.

SETUP (60-90 s)
1. Choose the content: a built-in topic or a free-text prompt. The group chip gives the summary line, e.g. 'B1 Genç · Arena · Nazik · 30 sn · 20 dk', with a Değiştir link.
2. Choose the skin (Lav or Canavar) and the scene for the audience.
3. Choose the difficulty: Kolay, Normal, Zor, Çok Zor or İmkânsız (Gimkit's five tiers; kids see only the first three, as 1-3 flame pictograms). The tiers set the starting SAFETY (Normal: 5 in Arena, 4 in Stüdyo, 5 cushions in Oyun Parkı), the goal multiplier (0.85 / 1 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3), and Echo on or off (off from Çok Zor).
4. Form 3-6 crews (table groups, default 4), each with its seat numbers 1-5.
   - Arena: a 10 s ownership moment to pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
   - Oyun Parkı: each crew taps an animal mascot.
   - Stüdyo: auto names from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns, which the teacher can edit.
5. ROLES (Arena and Stüdyo; off in Oyun Parkı). Each crew takes one role card:
   - STRIKER: ×2 Power, but its misses cost 2 SAFETY.
   - GUARDIAN: 2 Block tokens per phase instead of 1.
   - MEDIC: after a strike, may try a quick heal item for +1 SAFETY, once per phase.
   - TECH: once per phase, may reroll an item or add +10 s.
   With 3 crews the roles are Striker, Guardian and Medic. Duplicate roles are allowed, except Guardian.
6. Oyun Parkı only: Gogo runs a 25 s practice round that does not score.

TURN CYCLE (55-75 s)
a) SPOTLIGHT. The next crew lights up. A seat-number spinner picks the speaker and skips seats that have already answered until the whole crew has spoken; dots under the emblem track this, and no names are ever used. The picked student may pass once per round ('Pas').
b) ITEM. The question appears first, and the options follow after the audience delay (2, 2.5 or 3-4 s). Every item has a speaker button; A1/A2 Genç items are read aloud automatically at 0.8x.
c) TEAM TALK. A huddle of 10, 15 or 20 s, then 'Boards up!'. EVERY crew answers:
   - The spotlight seat answers aloud (or the teacher taps the option).
   - The other crews show mini-whiteboards (Arena, Stüdyo) or A-D cards and TPR (kids: stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C).
d) REVEAL, if correct. The Power die rolls, shown as pips: 1-2 gives 1 unit, 3-5 gives 2, and 6 gives 3 units plus a CRIT flash. Power is multiplied by the role and by the streak (Arena and Stüdyo: ×1.5 at 3 in a row, ×2 at 5). Blocks thunk onto the tower, or the HP bar drops with a lagging white chunk and the boss says a hurt line.
   ECHO: the teacher taps the chips of the other crews whose boards were right, for +1 unit each (max +3). 'Hepsi doğru' marks them all in one tap.
e) REVEAL, if wrong. The streak breaks.
   - BLOCK: any crew with a right board may spend a Block token (1 per crew per phase) to cancel the strike, shown as 'BLOCKED!' in that crew's colour. A miss becomes a rescue by classmates.
   - Otherwise the threat strikes: SAFETY −1 (−2 for a Striker crew), with a lava surge and camera shake, or a boss attack.
   - The screen says 'Brave try!' and shows the correct answer, plus a one-line why in Stüdyo.
   - A Medic crew may then try its heal item.
   - The missed item returns once, 3-5 items later, tagged 'Rematch' (a cracked block to fix, or a shield on the boss).
f) RALLY METER. It fills with every correct answer and never resets. Every 5 correct answers the class votes by show of hands within 5 s for one class choice:
   - Shield: blocks the next strike.
   - Double: the next correct answer counts ×2.
   - Hint token.
   - Big Build / Big Hit: +3 units.
   - Freeze: 20 s, only with Canlı Lav.
   - Brain break: a 45 s stirrer.
g) ULTIMATE. A streak of 5 unlocks it. The whole class chants the model sentence of the last item twice (shown on screen, with TTS once), and the teacher taps 'Loud & clear'. The hit is +6 units with a short cinematic.
h) EVENTS. About every 6 items a lava bubble pops or the boss has a mood swing, showing a chance-card task (spell it, act it, whisper it, say it backwards) for +2 units. Kids get a joke line.

PHASES. The goal is split into thirds. At each third there is an interlude: 3 s for adults and Arena; for kids, the between-round 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler. It changes the item type and brings a boss taunt, a new portrait damage state, or a new tower platform (plank, then ladder, then platform).
- Phase 1, RECOGNISE: MCQ, T/F, pairs, odd one out, picture and sound items.
- Phase 2, PRODUCE: gap fills, unjumble, short answers and error fixes. Some error sentences are spoken by the boss as taunts ('You has no chance!'), and fixing one lands the hit.
- Phase 3, SPEAK: describe, act, opinion and role-play cards. The teacher judges with Great (3 units), Good (2) or Try again (a second attempt). In the Lav skin, Phase 3 is the 'Radio call' to the rescue helicopter.

CANLI LAV (optional, Arena and Stüdyo only). The lava also creeps up one notch every 90/60/45/30/20 s, depending on the tier. It freezes automatically during speaking judgement, explanations and a T pause. It is off by default, because the game is turn-based so that teacher talk is never punished.

FINAL STAND. It starts in the last 3 minutes, or when the teacher presses 'Son hamle'. A drumroll plays, and every crew answers 3 final items on boards at the same time; each right board is a hit. When the next correct answer can win, there is a slow-motion 'FINAL HIT' banner.

LAST STAND (Arena and Stüdyo). A SAFETY of 0 does not end the game at once. The class gets one revive item on everyone's boards, and each right board restores 1 SAFETY (max 3). If no board is right, the ending plays.

ENDINGS
- Win: the rescue arrives, or the boss is defeated, followed by the hero shot.
- Loss, or time runs out: 'The boss escaped', and its remaining HP carries over with scars into the next lesson; or 'The tower is saved, the helicopter returns next lesson'.
- The local class profile remembers the best streak, win streaks ('3 lessons without falling in!') and boss scars.
- Nobody scores for speed.

ROLES IN CLASS. The teacher runs the clock, taps right/wrong and echo, judges speaking, and reads the rule card. Students huddle, raise boards, block, vote, chant and speak.
catalog.playerSetup:
The whole class is ONE side against the game, organised into 3-6 crews: table groups of 3-5, 4 crews by default.
- Crews only rotate the spotlight and hold roles and Block tokens. There is no crew score or ranking.
- In the spotlight crew, a seat-number spinner picks the speaker and covers every seat before it repeats one. Nobody is picked by name.
- It works with 10-40 students. With fewer than 10, use 2 crews, or treat each pair as a crew.
- Adults only, opt-in and off by default: 'Rakip Kuleler' (Rival Towers). Two halves each build a tower under the same lava, and the higher tower wins. It is never offered to Genç groups.
skills: collaboration and negotiation in English (huddles, blocks, class votes)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO. An editorial quiz-night look, on cream or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, with system sans, no mascot and no voice lines. The caption strip is neutral ('Phase 2 · Fix it').

LAV SKIN
- 'Deadline': the office floods with unread email. Each correct answer clears a task card and stacks a filing cabinet, and the rescue is the Friday 5 pm bell.
- 'Everest Before the Storm': the class climbs from camp to camp while storm clouds rise as the threat, and a helicopter waits at the summit.

CANAVAR SKIN (dry-humour bosses)
- 'The Deadline Beast', a clock-faced beast.
- 'The Inbox Kraken': its tentacles are 'Re: Re: Re:' threads, and its defeat line is 'Fine. Marked all as read.'
- 'The Jet-Lag Giant': it yawns instead of taking hits.
- 'The Exam Examiner', with a red pen, for YDS/IELTS classes.
Taunts are plain English within the level cap. Some of them carry the target error, which Phase 2 has the class fix. The portrait moves through 3 damage states, with critical-hit numbers and HP numbers shown.

ROLES, with dry names
- The Closer (Striker): ×2 Power, a miss costs 2.
- The Firewall (Guardian): 2 blocks per phase.
- Wellbeing Officer (Medic): a heal item once per phase.
- The Fixer (Tech): a reroll or +10 s once per phase.

HINTS AND WRONG ANSWERS
- The hint ladder is definition, then example, then Turkish gloss. Each hint costs 1 Power, but a correct answer is always worth at least 1. The TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
- A wrong answer shows the correct answer plus a one-line why (whyTr/whyEn).

WAGER (optional, before Phase 3). The class stakes 1-2 SAFETY for ×1.5 on the next 3 items.

PHASE 3 SPEAKING DUEL. The teacher voices the boss in a 45-60 s role-play:
- B1: 'Persuade the Jet-Lag Giant to let you sleep.'
- B2: 'Complain politely to the Kraken about 300 unread emails.'

DIALS
- The Harshness dial is greyed out: this is a co-op game, so there are no steal or damage cards.
- The Comeback dial becomes 'Second wind'. On Light, a correct answer at SAFETY 1 also restores 1. On Strong, it also gives a free hint.
- Sounds are woodblock and piano, with a 0.6 s chime; music is off by default.

ENDING. A modest finale card and a 'team photo' of the crew names in front of the beaten boss or at the summit. Full stats: accuracy by phase, best streak, blocks and heals. Then the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list with why lines, which can be sent in one tap to the next lesson's warm-up or to Material Maker.

It is ideal for tired evening classes that don't want competition, and for exam classes.
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11; the default for A1 and A2 Genç)
This is a stripped ruleset, not the adult game re-coloured.

THE 3 RULES, on a Turkish rule card with pictograms that can be explained in 20 s:
1. 'Cards up!' Everyone answers every turn, with A-D cards or TPR.
2. A right answer makes the tower grow, or the volcano gets sleepier.
3. When the star meter is full, it's time for the Class Chant!

SCENES. They are non-violent by construction: you calm, feed or help, and never hurt.
- Lav skin, 'Yer Lav! / The Floor Is Lava': the playground game kids already know, set in a cartoon living room with a sofa, cushions, stacked books and toy boxes. The 'lava' is a pretend red blanket with googly eyes that follow the spinner. It blows bubbles that pop into jokes ('Lava is hungry!', 'Lava wants pizza!'). The crew mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog and so on) hop up cushion towers, and Gogo's hot-air balloon is the rescue.
- Lav skin, 'Penguin Party': penguins build an igloo tower on a melting iceberg.
- Canavar skin, 'Grumpy Volcano': correct answers are lullaby notes. It yawns, the final round is a whisper round, and it falls asleep smiling and snoring.
- Canavar skin, 'Pizza Dragon': the class feeds it the right toppings. It burps a sticker and becomes a friend.
- Canavar skin, 'Sock Goblin': the class returns its stolen socks in matching pairs (pair items). At the end it gets its own socks and waves goodbye.

GOGO THE PARROT hosts. He runs the practice round, says the answer after a miss, leads hello and goodbye, and sleeps on the pause screen, where the lava and the volcano nap too.

WHAT IS LEFT OUT FOR KIDS: no roles, no numbers on the die (its pips show 1-3 cushions or notes), no hearts as lives, and no timer by default. The timer, when turned on, is a calm 40 s ring that never turns red, with a marimba chime at the end.

WRONG ANSWERS
- A soft 'boing', then a second try with a free hint: the picture, then the first letter, then listen again.
- If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer and the class repeats it twice. The crew earns an effort star for the class album.
- Only then does the threat puff up one notch. If the teacher taps 'Most of us!' because most of the cards were right, the class saves it automatically and there is no puff. On a correct turn, the same button adds +1.

WHEN THE THREAT REACHES THE TOP. 'Oops! Floor!' (Gogo throws a new cushion, and everyone giggles) or 'ATCHOO!' (the volcano sneezes glitter). Nothing is lost. The next item is a 'Together question' answered in chorus, then 3 cushions come back. Nothing ever goes down: the tower never shrinks, and stars only go up.

TIMING. A fixed 20 min: 3 rounds (the phases) of 4-5 min. Between rounds comes a 45 s stirrer ('Floor is lava! Feet up!', a TPR freeze game) or a 60 s settler (Gogo's whisper count).

ENDING
- 1-3 stars, always at least 1. Reaching the goal unlocks the friend ending.
- Every crew gets a title: Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers, Loudest Chanters or Clever Builders.
- The class album gets a sticker.
- Celebrations last at most 2 s, and team-colour-and-shape confetti comes only at the finale. The sounds are a marimba pack, with no buzzers.

ARENA (ages 12-14; the default for B1 and B2 Genç, and suggested for grades 6-8 even at A1)

LOOK. Dark navy with neon crew colours and a condensed display font. The game is framed as a 'Raid' or 'Challenge'. There is no talking mascot, no pastel and no 'superstar', and Genç text uses 'Canavar/Titan/Raid' rather than 'boss'.

OWNERSHIP. In 10 s, each crew picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.

SCENES
- Lav skin, 'Magma Shaft': crews bolt together a climbing rig in a glowing shaft, with a rescue drone at the top, a lava shader, and camera shake on surges.
- Canavar skin, 'Homework Hydra': each head is one grammar target in the pack. When the class beats a head's items, the head folds into a paper plane and flies off. There is no cutting.
- Canavar skin, 'Glitch Titan': a pixel robot whose code the class patches. Its ending reads 'SYSTEM REBOOTED: friendly mode'.

RULES
- Roles: Striker, Guardian, Medic, Tech.
- Streak: ×1.5 at 3 in a row, ×2 at 5, and the Ultimate chant at 5.
- Block tokens and Rally choices.
- Hints are first letter, 50:50 and a gapped example, each costing 1 Power (a correct answer is never worth less than 1).
- A 30 s ring in the crew colour.
- A commentator strip, at most once per turn: 'COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH BLOCK!', 'CRIT!'.
- Mild steals don't exist here because it is co-op; blocks are the heroic move instead.
- Last Stand revive. If it fails: 'The Hydra escaped: scars saved for the rematch'.

ENDING. A 'Raid report' hero shot with the emblems and mottos, plus crew awards: Longest streak, Clutch block, Top medic, Clean sheet. There is never a last place. Synth blips, with an optional quiet thinking loop.

ALL GENÇ CONTENT, including any LLM-written boss lines, passes the teenSafe filter.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1 (Genç: 0-4 words, and the picture carries the meaning; adults: 10 words or fewer)
- Phase 1: picture MCQ (2 options for A1 Genç, 3 for adults), T/F about a picture, emoji or Turkish pairs, and 'listen and point' sound items.
- Phase 2: tap-gap with a 2-3 option picture bank, and chunked unjumble of 3 tokens.
- Phase 3: 'Say it!', where the class names the picture and adds a frame ('It's a ___.', 'I like ___.'), plus act cards.
- Timer: off for kids, optional 30 s for adults.
- The strike comes only after the second try, and expected accuracy is 0.8.

A2 (8 / 15 words)
- Phase 1: MCQ with 3-4 options, gap MCQ (past simple, comparatives) and odd one out.
- Phase 2: unjumble of 4-6 tokens, gap with a bank, and short qa.
- Phase 3: describe with starters (taboo-card describe mode, 0-2 forbidden words) and 'Ask the dragon 2 questions'.
- 30-40 s per item.

B1 (14 / 25 words)
- Phase 1: meaning and collocation MCQ.
- Phase 2: typed or spoken short answers, word family ('decide → ___'), transformations with a base ('(go) Say it in the past'), and 'Fix it' error items voiced by the boss.
- Phase 3: 30-45 s speaking prompts (opinion, advice, hypothetical), judged Great / Good / Try again.
- Hints cost Power, and there is a 30 s timer.

B2 (20 / 40 words)
- Rapid synonyms and collocations at 15-20 s (Stüdyo), error correction with the error span lit up on reveal, 2-slot gaps and register shifts.
- Phase 3: a role-play duel of 45-60 s (complain politely, negotiate, persuade), with the optional Wager for adults.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics ('Describe your rescue plan', 'Convince the volcano to rest'), not abstract debate.

AT ALL LEVELS
- The goal comes from cycle time × expected accuracy, and the balance engine rescales it after 5 items, so every level feels equally winnable.
- The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial shifts the word-band mix and the hint availability.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the content one level without changing the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-25. Oyun Parkı is a fixed ~20 min: 3 rounds of 4-5 min with 45-60 s interludes. Arena runs 15-25 min and Stüdyo 15-30 min. 'Lav sprint' is an 8-10 min, 2-phase variant for a warm-up or an exit review.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Skin and scene. Difficulty tier: Kolay to İmkânsız, with only 3 tiers for kids.
- Minutes, which set the goal automatically (shown as 'Hedef ≈ N soru'), plus a manual goal override.
- Crews (3-6) and seats per crew.
- Roles on or off, with manual role assignment.
- Phases on or off, and the item types in each phase (e.g. Phase 3 off on a quiet test-prep day).
- Canlı Lav on or off, and its rise interval.
- Timer: off, 40, 30, 20 or 15 s, or Süresiz. Options delay.
- Hint-ladder steps, with the TR gloss on or off. Echo on or off.
- Comeback: Off / Light / Strong ('Second wind').
- Which Rally choices are offered.
- Die or 'Sabit güç' (every correct answer = 2 units).
- Practice round on or off.
- Persistent boss and tower (carry-over) on or off.
- Class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena'). Only '7-B' ever appears on the student screen.

LIVE, by keyboard and on-screen buttons
- Enter: reveal. 1-4: pick an option.
- D / Y: mark a spoken answer Doğru / Yanlış.
- 1 / 2 / 3: judge speaking as Great / Good / Try again.
- B: block, with a crew picker. H: hint.
- T: pause, which freezes the lava and timers; everything naps.
- +: add 10 s. S: skip the item (it goes quietly to the reinsert queue).
- U: undo the last decision ('Aslında doğruydu').
- L: 'Tehdit +1', a manual lava rise or boss wind-up for drama. The rule card tells teachers not to use it to punish noise.
- K: freeze the threat. F: 'Son hamle' / finish him.
- Echo chips, and 'Hepsi doğru' or 'Most of us!'.
- Re-spin the seat spinner, grant a pass, and adjust heal or damage (SAFETY and GOAL) from the teacher drawer.

AFTER THE GAME
- 'Kaçırılanlar' list with why lines.
- Reinsert missed items into the next lesson.
- Export to Material Maker.
- Download the class poster (emblems and mottos only).
- Reset the class record.
catalog.contentShape:
It reads a normal content pack; no bespoke content is required. Code fills each phase slot from the pack by item type and difficulty, running easy to hard inside a phase.

PHASE 1, 'Tanı' (recognise)
- mcq (fmt: picture, meaning, gap, collocation).
- tf (about: picture, meaning, sentence-correct).
- pair, shown as one 'a' with 3 'b' options. The Sock Goblin uses pairs natively.
- odd.
- sound: a minimal pair asking 'which one?'. It also powers the kids' 'listen again' hint.
- vocab, rendered as picture MCQ from media.emoji or img plus distractors[3].

PHASE 2, 'Üret' (produce)
- gap: needs a bank for Genç and A levels; uses base for transformations.
- order: chunked for teens.
- error: uses wrong, right and span. The boss voices the wrong sentence as a taunt, and the span lights up on reveal.
- qa: accept[] for typed or spoken answers; teacherJudge for open ones.
- vocab, rendered as a gap, or as defEasy → term.

PHASE 3, 'Konuş' (speak)
- speaking-prompt (describe, ask, opinion, hypothetical), using starters, useful and secs.
- taboo-card (describe, act or draw), with 0-5 forbidden words.
- roleplay (B2 duel): roleB is the boss or the radio operator, voiced by the teacher, and the checklist feeds the Great/Good judgement.
- vocab 'Say it' at A1: a picture, then the word plus a frame.

QUICK ITEMS. Heal, 'Together' and revive items are quick tf items, riddles (all 3 clues read), or Phase 1 mcq items.

EVENTS. Only chance-card kinds reward, task and bonus are used; penalty and swap are ignored. The amount is clamped to +1..+3 units.

REINSERTION. A missed item returns once, 3-5 items later.

FIELDS THE GAME USES. The level word caps; target and unit (the Hydra's heads, and grouping in the review list); whyTr, whyEn and whyOpt (Stüdyo's why line); media or imageKey (required for picture items in A1/A2 Genç; unpicturable items are dropped from picture phases); teenSafe.

MINIMUM PACK for 20 min: about 24 items. That is at least 8 in Phase 1, at least 8 in Phase 2, at least 4 speaking items, and 4 quick heal items. If the pack is short, the game warns and shrinks that phase.

SKIN FRAME: pack.frames.raid, with these fields:
- skin: 'lava' or 'boss'.
- scene key.
- name and nameTr.
- intro.
- taunts[3] and hurt[3].
- phaseLines[2].
- defeat.
- friendEnding? (Oyun Parkı).
- errorTauntIds[]: the error items the boss 'says'.
- heads[]? (Hydra: the list of targets).
- teenSafe.

Built-in scenes ship with lines written for each level. For a free-text prompt (e.g. 'geçmiş zaman, 6. sınıf'), the LLM may re-theme the name and lines, e.g. 'The Past Tense Troll'. The validator checks the word caps and teenSafe, and checks that every taunt with an error comes from a real error item; if a check fails, the built-in lines are used.

SOURCES OF CONTENT
- grammar_mcq_* banks, including whyOpt.
- words.js (term, definition, IPA, Turkish, example) for vocab, gap, qa and sound items.
- idioms.js at B2.
- The rate-limited Material Maker LLM endpoint for free-text prompts.
catalog.delightDetails:
THE TOWER AND THE LAVA
- Tower blocks stack with a satisfying thunk.
- The milestones are plank, then ladder, then platform. For kids they are cushion, then book pile, then sofa arm, then bunk bed.
- The lava visibly chases the tower up. It has a glowing shader in Arena, googly eyes in kids mode, and a flat ripple line in Stüdyo.
- A camera shake on a surge.

THE BOSS
- The HP bar has a lagging white chunk.
- The boss portrait moves through 3 damage states. For kids these go grumpy, then yawning, then sleepy.
- Combo flames on the streak counter.
- Crit numbers.
- A slow-motion 'FINAL HIT' with a drumroll when one answer can win.

THE BOSS'S VOICE
- Its taunts contain the target error for the class to fix ('You has no chance!').
- Its defeat lines speak correctly.

THE HYDRA. Each head is labelled with the grammar target it stands for, so the defeated heads double as a map of what the class has mastered.

KIDS' TOUCHES
- Lava bubbles pop into jokes.
- 'Oops! Floor!' cushions and the volcano's glitter 'ATCHOO!'.
- A whisper round while the volcano falls asleep, which doubles as a classroom-management gift.
- Pause makes everyone nap: Gogo, the lava and the volcano all show Zzz.
- Gogo parachutes in with the right answer.
- The Pizza Dragon burps a sticker.
- The Sock Goblin gets its own socks at the end.

'BLOCKED!' flashes in the saving crew's colour, so a miss turns into a rescue by classmates.

HERO SHOT. The crew emblems and mottos line up at the top of the tower or in front of the beaten boss.

AFTER A WIN. The cooled lava turns into obsidian, and the tower becomes a monument with a plaque, e.g. '7-B · 47 m'.

MEMORY ACROSS LESSONS
- Boss scars next lesson (a plaster on the Kraken, duct tape on the Titan).
- Win streaks across lessons ('3 lessons without falling in!').
- A best streak remembered for each class.
- An 'İmkânsız cleared' badge.

ACCESSIBILITY. Crews differ in shape as well as colour. Reduced motion swaps every effect for a static stamp. Every voice line has a caption.
catalog.risks:
1. WEAK STUDENTS FEEL EXPOSED. The name wheel from the lava idea is replaced by a seat-number spinner, so nobody is named. Students also get the huddle, one pass, free hints for kids, and blocks that let classmates save a miss.

2. BLAME FALLS ON THE CREW THAT MISSED. SAFETY is shared, and no crew miss stats are shown anywhere. Echo and blocks reward helping. A crew chooses the Striker's double cost for itself.

3. IT BECOMES 'JUST A QUIZ'. Phases, the spoken final, roles, Rally votes, events and the Ultimate chant prevent it.

4. IT IS TOO EASY OR TOO HARD. The balance engine adjusts after the first 5 items, and there are the difficulty tiers, manual heal/damage, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.

5. REAL-TIME LAVA PUNISHES TEACHER TALK. The game is turn-based by default. Canlı Lav is opt-in and auto-freezes during explanations and judging.

6. TOO MUCH FOR THE TEACHER TO TAP. There is a one-tap 'Hepsi doğru' / 'Most of us!', keyboard shortcuts, Echo can be switched off, and speaking is judged with only 3 buttons.

7. NOISE DURING CHANTS. The chant is a fixed 5 s window with a visible 'Shh' fade, and celebrations are capped. The 'Tehdit +1' button must not become a punishment for noise, and the rule card says so.

8. THE GAME RUNS LONG. The goal is sized automatically, and there is the Final Stand in the last 3 min and the 'Son hamle' button. Time-up endings are framed as a carry-over, not a failure.

9. A LOSS MID-LESSON KILLS THE MOOD. Arena and Stüdyo get the Last Stand revive. Kids cannot lose at all.

10. 12-14-YEAR-OLDS FEEL BABIED. Arena is suggested for grade 6 and up, with no mascot, and the group label is never shown.

11. VIOLENCE AND TEENSAFE. Kids calm, feed or help instead of hurting. The Hydra's heads fold into paper planes. LLM-written boss lines are validated, with the built-in lines as a fallback.

12. DICE FEEL UNFAIR TO ADULTS. The 'Sabit güç' option removes them.

13. SPEAKING JUDGEMENT IS SUBJECTIVE. Items carry a checklist and useful words, and 'Try again' gives a second attempt. The teacher's judgement is never presented as an automatic accuracy check.

14. THE SAME ITEM KEEPS COMING BACK. Each item is reinserted at most once.

15. NO ENGLISH TTS VOICE. The fallback is 'Öğretmen okur'.

16. TOO FEW PICTURABLE ITEMS FOR A1/A2 GENÇ. The generator fills the gap, or the game suggests a different phase mix.

17. IT OVERLAPS THE MULTI-LESSON RPG. This game is a single lesson; the persistent boss is only a light carry-over hook.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (shared accessibility goals: keyboard, colour-independent cues, timer off, teacher judgement is not an automatic accuracy claim)
C:/lg/src/lib/game-classroom.mjs and src/pages/sinif-oyunu.astro (existing one-screen team engine and grammar MCQ flow to reuse)

issues: The kids' timing does not add up. Oyun Parkı is a fixed 20 min with three 4-5 min rounds, 45-60 s interludes and a 75 s cycle. That leaves room for only about 10-12 items, yet the minimum pack is 24 items and the auto goal assumes (20-3)*60/75 ≈ 13 items. The practice round, second tries, the 'Together' question and the chants make it worse: Round 3 (speaking) gets squeezed or cut at the bell almost every time.

Arena and Stüdyo put too much on the teacher each turn. After one item the teacher may have to: tap or confirm the answer, reveal, tap echo chips per crew, open the block crew picker, ask whether the Medic wants a heal and then run its item, handle an event every ~6 items, count a Rally vote every 5, and run the Ultimate chant. Standing at a smart board, that is 4-8 decisions per 60 s cycle, and the game stalls while the teacher reads the screen.

The keyboard shortcuts (Enter, 1-4, D/Y, B, H, T, U, L, K, F) are no help on a Turkish public-school smart board, where the teacher stands at the board with no keyboard in reach. Every live control needs a large touch target in a fixed spot. The teacher drawer (re-spin, heal or damage, pass) is several taps deep.

Answers can leak between crews. The spotlight seat 'answers aloud' while the other crews show boards. Unless every board is locked BEFORE the spotlight speaks, the other crews just copy the answer and Echo turns into free points. Whoever holds the marker also decides what goes on each board.

Classroom materials may not exist. Many state-school classes have no mini-whiteboards, and A-D cards must be printed, cut and handed out: 6 crews × 4 cards takes 5+ minutes the first time. The TPR fallback (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C) has no D, is ambiguous with 28 kids half-standing, and lets children copy the fastest mover.

The TPR and chant moments make 10-12 year-olds noisy: stand and sit votes, the class chant, 'say it backwards' events, 'Floor is lava! Feet up!' stirrers, 'Oops! Floor!' giggles. Settling 28 kids after each one takes 30-60 s that the timing plan does not count. The 5 s 'Shh' fade is optimistic.

Seat numbers are fragile. With 28 students in 6 crews, some tables have 6-7 students, but seats run 1-5. Absent students break the spinner, and kids forget their numbers or swap seats. The spinner then lands on an empty chair and the teacher has to re-spin by hand.

Most students are only half-active during Phase 3. One student speaks for 30-60 s, and the teacher judges while voicing the boss in a role-play duel. The other 27 kids (or the other 9 adults) have no task. This is the longest dead time in the session.

One strong student can still dominate. During the huddle the strongest student in each crew gives the answer and the spotlight student repeats it, so the spotlight rotation guarantees speaking, not thinking. Blocks and Echo reward the crews that happen to have strong students.

Risk 2 (blame falls on the crew that missed) is contradicted by the Striker role. Its misses cost 2 SAFETY, which is the crew-level exposure the design says it avoids. In a teen class, 'the Strikers made us lose' will be said aloud.
The Rally vote by show of hands 'within 5 s' means the teacher counts hands across 6 options and taps. In practice the loudest kids pick. With adults it is awkward and slow.

Nothing is at stake in Oyun Parkı. 'Most of us!' saves the class automatically, reaching the top only brings back 3 cushions, and the class cannot lose. After two lessons 11-year-olds notice the lava is harmless, and the engagement that pulls the threat design along fades. The kids who most need a reason to focus also get no signal that their answer mattered.

The adult version is over-gamified for 10 tired evening learners. Roles, a die, streak multipliers, Block tokens, a Wager, Last Stand and Rally votes add up to a lot of rule talk for a 20 min review. The whole-group score also hides individual gaps. With 3 crews of 3, each adult is the spotlight speaker only about 2 times.

The Power maths is opaque: die × role × streak × Double × Echo, with the balance engine rescaling units behind the scenes. Nobody in the room can predict whether the next answer can win, so the 'FINAL HIT' drama feels arbitrary. The hidden rescaling also makes teacher overrides (manual goal, heal) hard to reason about.

The build scope is large for one mode. There are about 12 illustrated scenes, each with 3 damage states, a lava shader, a Hydra that folds its heads into paper planes, a parrot mascot, stickers, carry-over scars and poster export. That is a lot of art before the core loop has been proven in one real class.

Stopping early mostly works: T pauses, 'Son hamle' starts the finale, and time-up counts as a carry-over. But if the bell rings in the middle of Phase 2, the spoken final never happens, and the carry-over boss only matters if the teacher uses the same class profile on the same device next lesson. That fails when the classroom computer's local storage is wiped or the teacher moves rooms.
fixes: Size the pack from the time, not the reverse. Oyun Parkı: 3 rounds × 4 items with an 18-20 min budget, and each interlude counted as a fixed cost. When 60% of the time has gone, skip to the next phase automatically, so Phase 3 always happens. Make the minimum pack check per mode (Oyun Parkı about 14 items, Arena and Stüdyo about 20).

Add a 'Hafif kurallar' default for the first 3 sessions: no roles, no Medic, no Rally votes, no events, and 'Sabit güç' instead of the die. Unlock the extras from the class profile once the class knows the loop. Keep at most 2 teacher taps per normal turn: the verdict, and 'Hepsi doğru' or 'Most of us'.

Build a fixed touch bar about 80 px high along the bottom edge that a teacher standing at the board can reach: Doğru, Yanlış, Hepsi doğru, Pause, Undo, Son hamle. Everything else goes in one drawer. Optionally let the teacher's phone act as a remote clicker (QR code, still one-screen) for pacing from the back of the room.
Lock the answer order: huddle, then 'Boards up!' with every board frozen, THEN the spotlight speaks. Echo only counts boards raised on the lock beat, and the screen shows a 3-2-1 'Kilitle' countdown.

Ship a printable one-page A-D card sheet (colour and shape per letter, crew mascot on the back), plus a 'kalem-kâğıt' option where crews write the letter on paper. Drop TPR as the answer channel for A-D items. Keep it only for 2-option or T/F items (stand = True, sit = False) and for the stirrers.

Change the seat spinner to 'seats 1-N per crew' with N set per crew at setup (up to 7), and add a one-tap 'boş' that removes a seat for this lesson. Offer a 'marker rotates' rule: the spotlight seat also writes the crew's board, which spreads the thinking.

Give everyone a job in Phase 3. While one student speaks, the other crews hold up a 'heard it' card for each checklist word they catch, and that becomes the Echo. Or run Phase 3 as pair speaking: all pairs talk for 30 s at the same time, then one pair performs. Cap the boss duel at 45 s.
Remove the Striker's double miss cost, or make it a class-level 'Risk turu' that the class votes on. Keep every crew-level risk out of any Genç group.
Replace the Rally hand-count vote with a teacher pick, or a spin over the 3 options that are allowed. For kids, remove the choice and give one automatic reward (Shield).

Give Oyun Parkı a gentle but real stake: a 3-star result driven by how many cushions are left or how fast the volcano falls asleep, shown as stars (never a loss). A 'Most of us' save should only count when about 70% of cards are right, and a small per-turn 'kaç kart doğru' dot row lets kids see that their answer mattered.

For adults, offer 'Stüdyo lite': no die, no roles, streaks only, the Wager kept as the single spicy choice, and the Kaçırılanlar list with why lines as the main payoff. Put 'Rakip Kuleler' first in Stüdyo, since many adults prefer some competition.

Make the Power maths readable. Show '+2' in plain numbers per answer, and show the rescaled goal openly as 'Hedef: 18 blok'. Make balance changes visible to the teacher only, and trigger 'FINAL HIT' only when it is really true.

Cut the MVP to one engine, one Lav scene per mode (Yer Lav!, Magma Shaft, Deadline) and one Canavar per mode (Grumpy Volcano, Glitch Titan, Inbox Kraken). Leave out the Hydra, carry-over scars, poster export and stickers. Add more scenes after a real pilot.

Store the carry-over state in the teacher's account (Supabase class profile), not only in local storage, so it survives a room change. If the bell rings before Phase 3, give a one-tap 'Çıkış bileti': one speaking prompt for the whole class to answer in chorus.

issues: Too many mechanics for Arena and Stüdyo. The class has to learn roles (4), Block tokens, Echo, Medic heals, Tech rerolls, the Rally vote (6 options), Ultimate, events, streak multipliers, the die, Last Stand, Wager and Canlı Lav. An A1/A2 adult class cannot be told these rules in English, and a teacher cannot explain them in Turkish in the 60-90 s setup. Rule overhead crowds out language time, and the class ends up playing the meta-game instead of using English.

The teacher's tap load per turn is too high. For 3-6 crews they must scan every board for Echo, decide Blocks, trigger Medic, judge speaking and run the spinner, which is unrealistic at 40 students. The 55 s Arena cycle will overrun.

The Oyun Parkı TPR code (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C) maps letters to arbitrary actions. Pre-readers at A1 Genç answer the action code, not the language, and can't reliably tell A from B on an option they can't read. Letter-coded A-D cards also assume the children can read the options.

Phase 2 'produce' for A1 Genç is tap-gap and a 3-token unjumble with word tokens, which is reading-dependent. Non-readers can't do it. Who taps is unclear (the teacher by proxy), so nobody actually produces anything.

Most students only recognise. Outside the spotlight seat, A-D cards and TPR are recognition. Real production (writing on boards, speaking) comes only in Arena/Stüdyo Phase 2 and in Phase 3, which the auto-goal can cut short when the goal falls early. The 0.9 factor helps, but the Balance engine and the dice further weaken the link between language accuracy and visible progress.

The d6 Power die and streak multipliers mean the same correct answer is worth 1 to 9+ units. Progress feels driven by luck rather than learning; this is bad for adults, and for kids the pips hide it without fixing it.

Spotlight pressure in Arena and Stüdyo: one randomly picked student answers aloud with the whole class's SAFETY at stake, and a Striker crew's miss costs double. Weak or shy 12-14-year-olds and anxious A1 adults feel exposed despite 'Pas' and Blocks. Blocks also make visible who saved whom.

Error taunts ('You has no chance!') model the incorrect form out loud. That is fine at B1+, but for A1/A2, and for Genç especially, spoken wrong input can stick. The kids' ruleset doesn't say error items are excluded.

Content realism from the built-in banks: grammar_mcq_* is MCQ only, and words.js has no images, no error sentences, no order/tf/odd/sound/speaking items. Most Phase 2 and 3 types must be derived by code or generated. Picture items for A1/A2 Genç need media or imageKey, which neither bank provides, so the 'picturable' Phase 1 for pre-readers may be empty without an image or emoji library.

Content realism from a free-text LLM prompt: one call must return about 24 items across 8-12 types, balanced across 3 phases, plus 4 heal items, chance cards and pack.frames.raid with validated taunts that reference real error items, all within word caps and passing teenSafe. The rate-limited DeepSeek endpoint will often fail validation partway, and silently shrinking phases undermines the planned lesson.

Timing arithmetic for Oyun Parkı: (20 - 3) × 60 / 75 ≈ 13.6 items, yet it adds 3 interludes of 45-60 s, second tries, Gogo's repetition and chants. The realistic count is around 10-11 items. That means about 3-4 items per phase, which is thin for learning and makes the 24-item minimum pack mostly unused.

Arena at A1 (a 13-year-old A1 class) gets a condensed display font on dark navy, commentator strips ('CLUTCH BLOCK!'), role cards and 30 s rings. The text and UI load is higher than A1 readers can handle, even with the content set to A1.

B2 Stüdyo, as 'rapid synonyms and collocations at 15-20 s', drifts back into a quiz. The strongest B2 language (the role-play duel) is a single 45-60 s turn by one crew per phase, so most B2 learners speak very little.

This overlaps the planned RPG (boss, d6/d20, hearts, events) and the existing Baamboozle board in item handling. Keep the boss art and the item runner shared, or three games will duplicate one engine.
fixes: Tier the rules by level as well as by audience. At A1/A2 (any audience), ship only 'Core': shared tower/boss, everyone answers, Block (1 per crew) and the Ultimate chant. Roles, Medic, Tech, Wager, Rally votes and Canlı Lav unlock only at B1+ or by an explicit teacher toggle. Show a Turkish rule card with a maximum of 5 rules for adults.
Replace the Power die with fixed Power by default (correct = 2, Great speaking = 3). Make dice an opt-in 'Şans' toggle for adults only, so progress maps to language.

Oyun Parkı answer mode: replace A-D letters and the TPR code with picture/colour-shape cards (the options shown as a red circle, blue triangle and so on, each with a picture). Children hold up the colour or shape that matches the picture they choose. Limit it to 2-3 options, and read every option aloud by TTS as it appears.

For A1 Genç, Phase 2 becomes 'Say it with me': picture, then the class says the word or chunk in chorus, then the spotlight crew says it inside a frame ('It's a ___'). Drop tap-gap and unjumble for non-readers, or make unjumble picture-strip sequencing. Keep reading-based Phase 2 for A2 Genç and up.

Make production universal. In Arena and Stüdyo Phase 2, every crew writes a word or short answer on a board, and Echo counts only written answers. In Phase 3, run 'Pair talk 30 s then one crew reports' so everyone speaks, not just the spotlight seat. Guarantee Phase 3 at least 4 min by reserving time, not only through the 0.9 factor.

Reduce the teacher's taps. Echo becomes one 'X/Y crews right' stepper (or 'Hepsi / Çoğu / Az'). Blocks are auto-offered when Echo > 0 and confirmed with one key. Medic and Tech are merged into a single 'Crew power' card per phase.

Soften the spotlight in Arena and Stüdyo: the spotlight crew answers collectively after the huddle (any member speaks), with the seat spinner as an optional 'Hot seat' toggle. Remove the Striker's double loss at A1/A2 and in Genç groups.
Restrict error taunts to B1+. At A1/A2, the boss says the CORRECT sentence with a missing piece ('I ___ a cat. Help me!'), so the wrong form is never modelled out loud.

Ship curated built-in 'Raid packs' per level: 8-10 topics × 8 groups, with emoji or image keys for A1/A2 Genç, and error, order and speaking items hand-written or pre-generated offline and checked. Derive tf, odd and gap from words.js and grammar_mcq_* with code rules, and state which types each topic supports.

Split LLM generation into 2-3 calls: Phase 1 and 2 items, Phase 3 speaking items, then the raid frame. Each call is validated separately, with a per-type fallback to the built-in bank, and the teacher preview lists what was replaced. Size requests to the real planned-item count (about 12 for kids, about 18 for adults) plus 25% spare.

Recalculate cycle and timing honestly (kids around 90 s including second tries) and show 'Hedef ≈ N soru · 3 tur' against the real interludes. For kids, allow 25 min or a 2-round mode, so each phase gets at least 5 items.
Arena at A1/A2: use a larger, non-condensed body font for items, make commentator strips icon-only, and keep all item text within A1 caps. Only the chrome is 'Arena'.

B2: turn Phase 3 into a whole-class 'duel ladder': each crew prepares 20 s, then two crews speak 30 s each, rotating across phases, so every crew gets at least one extended turn. Add collocation production (typed on boards) to Phase 2 rather than rapid MCQ.

Share one boss/threat renderer and item runner with the RPG and the /sinif-oyunu engine. Position this game as the single-lesson co-op review, and cut the cross-lesson carry-over to a plaque and a boss scar only.

issues: It is really XL, not L. There are 14 named scenes (Deadline, Everest, Deadline Beast, Inbox Kraken, Jet-Lag Giant, Exam Examiner, Yer Lav, Penguin Party, Grumpy Volcano, Pizza Dragon, Sock Goblin, Magma Shaft, Homework Hydra, Glitch Titan). Each needs a background, a threat animation, 3 damage or mood states, a win ending and a loss ending, and lines written per level. Then come 3 sound packs, the Gogo mascot, the dice, the Ultimate cinematic, the hero shot and the obsidian monument. Art is the schedule risk. Code is not.

The rules are bloated. The mechanics pile up: roles (4, with tokens per phase), Block tokens, Echo, the Rally meter with 6 votes, the Ultimate chant, events every 6 items, the Medic heal items, Tech rerolls, the streak multipliers, the Power die, CRITs, Rematch reinsertion, 3 phases, the Final Stand, the Last Stand, the Wager, Canlı Lav, Second wind, the 5 tiers, the hidden balance engine, carry-over scars and Rival Towers. Nobody can hold this in their head on a projector. The adult and Arena rule cards break the spirit of the 20-second explanation rule, even though that rule is formally only for kids.

The teacher's tap load per turn is unrealistic in a 55-65 s cycle. On one turn the teacher has to: mark the spotlight answer, scan 3-5 boards, tap Echo chips, and choose a Block crew with the picker. On a miss they also run the Medic heal item. Every 5th turn adds the Rally vote and every 6th an event. The teacher becomes a game operator, not a teacher. Animations for the die, the thunk, the HP lag and the surge add 3-5 s on top.

Echo and Block both need the teacher to judge every crew's board, in real time and from across the room. On a smartboard with no keyboard, the crew picker is extra taps. In practice teachers will skip them, and the co-op 'rescue by classmates' will quietly disappear.

The lava-follows-tower model is visually confusing. If the lava stays SAFETY notches below the top, then a correct answer that lifts the tower also lifts the lava, and kids see the threat rise when they succeed. The game then has two gauges (GOAL distance and SAFETY gap) sharing one vertical axis.

The balance engine is calibrated on Phase 1, which is recognition and easy, and it locks after Phase 1. Accuracy then drops in Phase 2 (production) and Phase 3 (teacher-judged). So the goal is systematically too hard exactly where the game should climax. The Power die adds variance that the engine can't see.

Phase 3 (speaking) breaks the rule of a whole-class response every turn. Only the spotlight crew speaks, and the other crews have nothing on their boards. It is also the slowest phase, and it lands at the end, just when the lesson clock is tight.

The kids' ruleset is not really 3 rules. The second try, the hint ladder, 'Most of us!', effort stars, the Together question, cushion refills, stirrers and settlers all apply in practice. The rules are fine for kids because the teacher runs them, but the code paths are a separate ruleset, which roughly doubles the test surface.
TPR mapping (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C) is chaotic with 4 options, and hard to read in a 30-student room. For A1 Genç the 2-option picture MCQ only needs stand or sit.

Picture items for A1/A2 Genç depend on media.emoji or an imageKey. Emoji look different on Windows smartboards, older Android panels and Chrome OS. words.js has no images, and the LLM cannot supply pictures reliably. This is the real content bottleneck for the kids default.

The keyboard map is overloaded and depends on context: 1-4 pick options, 1/2/3 judge speaking, and D/Y, B, H, T, S, U, L, K, F and + all do something. Smartboards and touch projectors usually have no keyboard, so every action also needs a large on-screen control. That is a lot of chrome on a screen meant to show the game.

A lava shader, camera shake and a glowing shader in Arena are risky on low-end classroom PCs and smartboard browsers if done in WebGL. Motion sickness and reduced-motion handling are also needed on a large projected screen.

It overlaps with other candidates. The boss fight overlaps the RPG candidate's encounters, and the item loop is the same as a themed MCQ quiz or Millionaire. What sets it apart is only the shared co-op frame. That is real and valuable, but it has to be kept visible, not buried under a matching number of competitive-game mechanics.

The Canavar skin for Genç Arena (Hydra heads per grammar target) needs every pack to be grouped into 3-5 target clusters. LLM packs from a free-text prompt often have a single target, and then the Hydra has one head.

The carry-over scars and the per-class win streaks rely on a local class profile in localStorage. That is lost when the teacher switches PCs, which happens constantly in Turkish schools with shared smartboards. The promise of 'the boss comes back next lesson' will often break silently.

LLM validation is mostly fine, because the game reads normal pack items and the raid frame is small. Two parts are weak: the check that 'every taunt with an error comes from a real error item', and the teenSafe filter for boss lines. They need concrete string-match rules, not trust.
fixes: Cut v1 to a single threat model and 6 scenes, one per skin per audience: Oyun Parkı 'Yer Lav' living room plus Grumpy Volcano, Arena 'Magma Shaft' plus Glitch Titan, and Stüdyo 'Deadline' plus Inbox Kraken. Build them as layered parametric SVG, so one rig serves the damage states. Everything else is v2.

Replace the two-gauge lava with a fixed-height scene. The rescue sits at a fixed altitude, the tower grows toward it on correct answers, and the lava rises ONLY on misses from the floor. The meaning is then instantly readable: up is good, red rising is bad. The Canavar skin just maps the same two bars to HP and hearts.

Merge Echo and Block into one mechanic that takes one tap: 'Kaç grup doğru?' as a 0-N stepper, or 'Çoğumuz doğru' ('most of us were right'). On a correct turn, extra right crews add +1 each (cap +3). On a wrong turn, 'most boards right' auto-saves the strike (class save). There are no tokens, no crew picker and no bookkeeping, and it matches the kids' 'Most of us!' so there is one code path.

Move Roles, the Medic heal items, Tech rerolls, the Wager, Canlı Lav, Rival Towers, tiers 4-5, carry-over scars and the Hydra to v2. Keep in v1: the streak (one ×2 at 3 in a row), the Rally meter with 3 choices (Shield, Double, Big Hit), one event every 6 items, 3 phases, the Final Stand and the Last Stand.
Make Power deterministic by default: correct = 2 units, streak = ×2. Keep the die as an opt-in 'Zar' flavour. Then the goal is exact ('Hedef: 16 doğru'), which the teacher can trust.

Calibrate by phase. Use per-phase expected accuracy (for example Phase 1 0.85, Phase 2 0.65, Phase 3 0.8 because of the teacher's judgement and second tries), and allow a small ±10% rescale at each phase boundary. Alternatively, drop the hidden rescaling and let the Final Stand always close the gap: the last 3 simultaneous items carry enough units to win if at least half the boards are right.

Phase 3 needs whole-class speaking. Run 30 s of pair talk on the prompt, then the spinner picks one seat to perform, and the class chants back one model sentence. Limit Phase 3 to 2-3 items, and let the teacher switch it off.
For A1 Genç, use 2-option items with stand or sit, and at most 3 options with left arm, right arm or both arms. Never use 4-option TPR. A-D cards are the default for 4 options.

Ship a curated picture set of about 300 topic words for A1/A2 Genç (the classroom topics), drawn in one flat style as SVG sprites. Picture items may only draw from words that have an image, and the LLM may only pick from that list for picture phases. Emoji are a last fallback, and the page self-hosts one emoji font (e.g. a Twemoji SVG subset) so they render the same everywhere.

Have a presenter remote. A second tab or a phone on the same session (a QR code with a local BroadcastChannel, or a Supabase realtime channel) holds all the judge buttons, so the projected screen stays clean. On the main screen, keep one collapsible bottom tray with large touch targets: Doğru, Yanlış, Çoğumuz, İpucu, Duraklat, Geri al. The keyboard map becomes a bonus, and the teacher learns only Enter, D, Y, T, U.

Render with Canvas 2D or SVG only. Lava is an animated gradient path with sine ripples, capped at 30 fps, with the effects falling back automatically when frame time is over 20 ms. Respect prefers-reduced-motion, and add an in-game 'Sakin görüntü' toggle for projectors.

Sound: synthesize about 20 sfx with WebAudio (thunk, surge, chime, boing, drumroll, crit) and keep 3 timbre presets instead of 3 recorded packs. That keeps the bundle under about 150 KB of JS per game.

Validate the LLM raid frame with code. Every taunt line in errorTauntIds must exactly equal the 'wrong' field of an error item in the pack.
