Every other line must pass the level word cap, a teenSafe blocklist and a violence-verb blocklist for Genç (kill, blood, die, etc.). Any failure falls back to the scene's built-in lines. Items get the normal pack validator: an answer is in the options, the options are unique, and the gap has exactly one blank.
Persist the class profile and carry-over in Supabase under the teacher's account, with localStorage as the cache, so the boss really comes back next lesson on a different smartboard.

Keep the co-op frame in front: the title screen says 'Sınıf vs Oyun'. Position this game as THE non-competitive option in the suite, and reuse its raid engine as the RPG's boss encounters rather than building two.

Minimum feature set that already feels proper: 2 skins × 3 audiences; a tower or boss with 3 visual states; shared SAFETY; the class-save tap; 3 phases with interludes; the Rally meter; the Final Stand; a win or carry-over ending with a hero shot; the Kaçırılanlar list; a lesson-fit goal; and a presenter remote. Polish goes into the feel: the thunk, the HP lag chunk, the boss taunt that is the target error, and the slow-motion final hit. It does not go into more rules.

catalog.rankReason: Whole class vs the game: the co-op option the suite lacks (teen 7.3). v1 has one threat model and 6 scenes, with 'Hafif kurallar' as the default (no roles, fixed power instead of dice) and packs sized to the lesson time. The tower grows to a fixed-height rescue and the lava rises only on misses, so the scene reads instantly.

catalog.name: Sınıf Diyor ki (The Class Says)
catalog.familiarAs: Family Feud / Family Fortunes / Ailece Birlikte
catalog.oneLiner: Teams guess the top answers to 'Name something...' questions, and the answers come from a 3-minute anonymous survey of this class ('We asked 28 students...') or from a generated '100 people in Türkiye' board. Answers are spoken in sentence frames, slots flip with the count, and there are strikes, a steal and a finale. The show ends with an 'Our class in numbers' slide that students report on ('Most of us...').
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (teacher chrome, Turkish, about 1 min)
- The summary line reads, e.g., 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 dk · Canlı anket', with a 'Değiştir' link.
- The teacher picks a content source:
  (a) Canlı anket: a live phone survey of this class.
  (b) Hazır panolar: built-in boards by topic (Food, School, Weekend, Travel, Work, Holidays, Animals, Technology...).
  (c) Yaz, üretsin: a free-text prompt, Turkish allowed, e.g. 'teneffüs ve kantin', and the LLM builds 6 boards.
  (d) Karışık: live prompts with generated backup boards for any prompt that gets too few answers.
- The lesson-fit timer sets the number of rounds (see pacing).
- A second device is optional. The teacher's phone opens a 'Kumanda' page (6-letter code). It shows the hidden answers and the controls, so the projector never leaks the board. Without a phone, the teacher can print a one-page answer sheet or use extended-display mode.

STEP 0 · LIVE SURVEY (3-5 min; optional, recommended)
- Starting the survey:
  - The projector shows a QR code and a 4-letter room code.
  - Students open languago.site/anket with no login and no name. Only a random device token is kept, to stop double voting.
- The prompts:
  - Students answer 5-8 prompts, one per round plus 1-2 spares ('Name something you do before school', 'Name a reason to learn English').
  - Each student gives one answer per prompt. With fewer than 15 respondents, the teacher can allow two answers per prompt to fill the board.
  - Typing has autocomplete from the level's word band.
  - A1/A2 Genç get picture buttons instead: 8-12 icons from the prompt's pictureChoices, plus a 'Başka' field.
- While students answer, the projector shows a filling bar ('23/28 answered'), anonymous dots and a quiet thinking loop. It never shows names or live answers.
- No phones:
  - Printable half-sheet slips (6 prompts, tick boxes for A1 Genç).
  - Two volunteer 'data clerks' type the tallies on the teacher's device during a settler.
  - Or the survey runs as an exit poll at the end of the previous lesson.
- Otherwise the game uses built-in or generated boards ('We asked 100 people in Türkiye...').

STEP 1 · MERGE REVIEW (1-2 min, teacher only)
- The pipeline:
  1. It normalises case and punctuation.
  2. It lemmatises and handles plurals using words.js.
  3. It matches answers against the seed board's aliases for that prompt.
  4. It fuzzy-matches spelling (edit distance 1, or 2 for words of 7+ letters).
  5. An LLM pass groups synonyms (burger/hamburger, 'play games'/'play computer games') and flags Turkish entries ('kedi' → cat) for review.
- The teacher sees cluster cards and can drag to merge or split, rename the display text, or bin rude or off-topic answers. Binned answers are never shown.
- An answer needs at least 2 votes to reach the board, so no one's unique answer can identify them. Singletons go to a teacher-only 'Tek cevaplar' list.
- The top N answers become the board.
- When the teacher taps 'Onayla', raw responses are deleted and only the counts are kept. The boards are saved to the class profile ('7-B anketi · Ekim') for reuse.
- Meanwhile the class does 'Prediction slips': each team writes its guess for the #1 answer of each prompt. These feed the 'Mind Reader' award later.

A ROUND (Stüdyo classic; the Arena and Oyun Parkı differences are in their versions)
1. PROMPT
   - The prompt appears and is read aloud. The TTS or 'Öğretmen okur' fallback reads it, and the speaker button repeats it.
   - The header reads 'We asked 28 students...' (live) or 'We asked 100 people in Türkiye...' (generated).
   - The empty slots slide in after the options-delay dial (2 s adults, 2.5 s Arena, 3-4 s kids), so students process the question first.
   - The answer frame chip sits under the prompt ('People ___ before school.').
2. FACE-OFF
   - The seat-number spinner picks one player per team. Nobody is picked by name.
   - Buzzer mode: the two players stand at the desk and the first to slap the bell or press a key (Q / P on the laptop, or a phone buzzer) answers in the frame. Buzzing before the slots appear locks that player out for 1 s.
   - 'Boards up' mode: both players write on a mini-whiteboard for 10 s and reveal at the same time. This mode removes the speed advantage.
   - The higher-ranked answer wins. If neither answer is on the board, the next pair goes. The winning team chooses PLAY or PASS.
3. CONTROL
   - The team's members answer one at a time in seat rotation, so everyone speaks. The rotation is shown as numbered seats, never names.
   - Before each reveal, the class chants the reveal call ('Survey says!').
   - Correct: the slot flips with a ding and shows the answer, its points and '8 of us'. The points go into the round bank.
   - Wrong: a strike X. Wrong guesses are NOT written on the board, so students have to listen. Repeating an answer that already failed counts as a strike.
   - One-word answers at A2+ get 'Full sentence, please!' with no strike and one retry. A too-general answer ('food' for 'pizza') gets the teacher's 'Close! Be more specific' button, once per round.
4. STEAL
   - After 3 strikes the rival team huddles (20 s adults) and gives ONE answer.
   - If it is correct, they take the whole bank plus that slot. If not, the controlling team keeps the bank.
   - A team that clears the board skips the steal.
5. REVEAL THE REST
   - The unrevealed slots flip one by one. Before each flip the class chorally guesses; this is listening input, not scored.
6. REPORT
   - At B1+ a spokesperson from the round winner reads one reporting sentence from the board ('Most of us have breakfast before school, but only a few of us walk to school.').
   - At A levels the class echoes the top answer in the frame.
- Round multipliers: in Stüdyo, round 4 is x2 and round 5 is x3.

SCORING
- Points = the % of respondents who gave that answer, rounded.
  - Live boards show the count under the points ('8 of us').
  - Generated boards are 'out of 100' and sum to 100 or less. The rest is 'other answers'.
- 'Wrong' costs nothing at any level. The only swing is the steal.
- Comeback (Light):
  - The trailing team picks the next prompt from two face-down category cards.
  - Its first correct answer each round gets a Slipstream +5.

3-4 TEAMS
- Face-offs rotate (A-B, C-D, A-C...).
- The teams not in the face-off play a SHADOW BOARD: during the round they secretly write up to 3 guesses.
- After the reveal, each shadow guess that matches a slot the playing teams did NOT find scores that slot's points. Idle teams keep listening and predicting.

FINALE
- The mode sets the default (see the versions). The Stüdyo default is 'Hızlı Tur' (Fast Money):
  - Two players from the leading team, or one pair per team if time allows.
  - 5 prompts. Player 1 has 20 s. Player 2 has 25 s, wearing headphones or standing outside the door, and must not repeat player 1's answers.
  - Target: half of the two-player maximum, rounded to 5 and shown as a thermometer (usually 130-170).
  - Success gives a +50 bonus. The finale can't eliminate anyone.

END
- The 'Our class in numbers' slide is an infographic of the top answers per prompt, with frames ('Most of us ___ before school', 'Nobody ___').
- It is a 2-3 min speaking follow-up. Pairs make 3 true sentences about their class. It can be exported as a PNG for the class album or wall.

TEACHER ROLE
- The teacher is host and judge on the Kumanda or the keyboard: 1-8 reveals a slot, X strike, P play/pass, S steal, Space 'Survey says', C 'Close!', Z undo, T pause, +/- edits points.

STUDENTS
- Students fill in the survey, huddle, answer in frames, chant the reveals, write shadow and prediction guesses, and report.
catalog.playerSetup:
- Default: 2 teams of up to 15 students each on one projector.
- 3-4 teams: face-offs rotate and the other teams play shadow boards.
- Players:
  - The seat-number spinner picks one face-off player per team each round.
  - The control turn rotates through every member.
  - The steal and the huddles are whole-team.
  - In the Hızlı Tur, a pair from the leading team plays (or one pair per team in Arena's Lightning Boards).
- Oyun Parkı: 2-4 teams that take turns in a carousel (no buzzing), and every team shows a secret guess each turn.
- Phones: one per student, or one per pair, for the survey only. The game itself needs one screen, with the teacher's phone as an optional remote.
catalog.contentShape:
Main item: 'survey'. Base fields, plus:
- prompt: EN; starts with 'Name...' or 'Tell me...'; within the group's word cap.
- promptTr: teacher chrome only.
- frame: the answer frame, e.g. 'It's ___.', 'People ___ before school.', 'Most of us ___ because ___.'
- answers[4-8]: {text (up to 3 words; 1 word + picture at A1 Genç), pts, aliases[3-10] (plural/singular, UK/US, contractions, common learner misspellings, EN synonyms), imageKey (required for A1/A2 Genç), frameExample ('People brush their teeth.')}
- source: 'class' or 'generated'
- respondents: live boards only
- audienceLabel: '28 students', '100 people in Türkiye', '100 kids' or '100 teens'
- pictureChoices[8-12]: A1/A2 Genç survey buttons, drawn from vocab or category-list items with media
- teenSafe: bool
- impersonal: must be true

VALIDATOR
- pts go down from the top answer. The top answer is 20-50. A generated board sums to 70-100.
- No alias belongs to two answers.
- The prompt is within the word cap.
- Blocklist for personal areas: body, family income, religion, grades, appearance of classmates.
- The teenSafe filter applies to every Genç board.
- A1/A2 Genç boards drop any answer without an imageKey. If fewer than 4 answers remain, the whole board is dropped.

GENERATOR
- The LLM is told to imagine respondents in Türkiye, so the top 'hot drink' is tea (aliases 'Turkish tea', 'çay' flagged for review).
- Each board also gets a seed alias dictionary that the live-survey merge reuses.

SUPPORTING ITEMS
- 'speaking-prompt' (mode 'survey'): the live survey question list {prompt, starters[] = the frame, secs}.
- 'speaking-prompt' (mode 'opinion'): 'Defend it' at B2 and the class-in-numbers debrief frames.
- 'vocab' and 'category-list': seed the picture choices, the aliases and whole kids' boards (e.g. the category-list 'Pets' → the board 'Name a pet').

LIVE SESSION ENVELOPE
{code, prompts[], responses (purged after merge), clusters[{text, count, members[], binned}], approvedBoards[] (saved to the class profile)}
skills: survey and reporting language (Most of us / A few of us / Nobody)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO · 'SURVEY SAYS'
Look and sound
- Editorial quiz-night set (cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme) with a long board of numbered slots.
- The #1 slot has a thin gold edge. Flips are a crisp 3D card turn with a piano ding and the points rolling up in 0.6 s.
- A strike is a large red X with a low woodblock and piano cluster, under 1 s.
- There is no mascot. Captions are neutral ('Round 4 · Double points').
- Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').

Rules (the full classic)
- Buzzer face-off, then Play/Pass, then control in seat rotation.
- 3 strikes, then the steal takes the bank.
- Rounds 4 and 5 are x2 and x3. The finale is the Hızlı Tur (Fast Money).
- Optional short answer clock in control: 8 s, off by default. A timeout is a strike only if the teacher enables it.
- Optional 'Defend it' (B1+ opt-in, default at B2):
  - Once per round, a team whose answer is not on the board can speak a 20 s justification in English ('I'd say quite a few people skip breakfast because they commute early').
  - If the teacher accepts it, there is no strike and the team gets half the lowest slot's points. The slot stays hidden.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default, which here only means steal-the-bank. There are no luck tiles, and the multipliers do the job wagers would do.

Example prompts
- 'Name a reason people are late for work.'
- 'Name something you shouldn't say at a job interview.'
- 'Name a typical Turkish breakfast food in English.'
- 'Name something people complain about in hotels.'
- 'Name a small-talk topic with a new colleague.'
- 'Name something you'd change about your city.'
- Live-survey favourites: 'Name a reason you're learning English.', 'Name an app you open first in the morning.'

Endings
- Full scores and a modest finale.
- The 'Kaçırılanlar' list: every unrevealed answer with its frame sentence, for a 2-minute drill.
- The 'Our class in numbers' slide with a reporting task: pairs write 3 sentences using 'the majority of', 'just under a third', 'hardly anyone'.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two different rule variants, not one skin swap. The group label is never shown to students.

OYUN PARKI (9-11) · 'GOGO'S POLL PARTY'
Look and sound
- A bright cream game-show set with a curtain and bulb lights.
- The slots are big picture cards: the flip shows the picture, the word and 1-3 stars.
- Gogo the parrot hosts:
  - He demos a 30 s practice round that doesn't score ('Name a colour').
  - He repeats every revealed answer, and the class echoes it chorally ('Pizza! Eight of us like pizza!').
  - He sleeps on the pause screen.
- A miss is a soft grey 'oops cloud' puffing above the board, with a marimba 'boing' and Gogo shrugging. Never a red X.
- Teams are animal mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog...).

The 3 rules (Turkish rule card plus pictograms: speech bubble → flipping card → three clouds)
1. Teams take turns. Talk for 10 s, then say 'I think... a cat!'
2. If it's on the board, the card flips and your team gets its stars (the top answer is 3 stars, the middle ones 2, the rest 1). If not, an oops cloud. Nobody loses stars.
3. After three oops clouds, Gogo shows the rest, and everyone says each answer together.

Every turn
- Whole-class moment: while the active team huddles, every team holds up a mini-whiteboard with its secret guess ('Boards up!'). Any board matching a flipped card earns a 'Me too!' sticker for the class album, not the score.
- Live survey only: after each flip Gogo asks 'Wave if you said it too!'. Waving is voluntary, and the prompts are harmless preferences.
- Timers are off by default. When on, a calm 40 s ring that never turns red.
- Hint ladder, all free: the picture silhouette of a hidden card, then its first letter, then Gogo reads the question again.
- Wrong twice: Gogo says one hidden answer and the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star (album).

Pacing and endings
- 3 rounds of about 4 min, with a 45 s stirrer between them.
- The finale is the 'Class Thermometer': a cooperative round of 5 quick prompts. All teams write, and every matching answer adds its points to one class thermometer. Reaching 100 unlocks the class sticker.
- Every team gets a title (Mind Readers, Best Listeners, Bravest Guessers), and the 'Our class in numbers' page goes into the class album as a sticker page.

Survey and prompts
- The survey uses picture buttons.
- Prompts: 'Name a pet.', 'Name something in your school bag.', 'Name a food you don't like.', 'Name a summer activity.', 'Name an animal at the zoo.', 'Name a sport.'
- Header: 'We asked 100 kids...'.

ARENA (12-14) · 'POLL CLASH'
Look and sound
- A dark navy set with neon slot edges in the team colours, a condensed display font and geometric emblems.
- In 10 s, teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
- A strike is a white 'SIGNAL LOST' glitch X with a synth blip.
- A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!', 'CLEAN SHEET').
- Header: 'We asked 100 teens...' or the class count.

Rules
- Face-off is 'Boards up' by default, simultaneous and 10 s. The buzzer is opt-in.
- Then Play/Pass. Control rotates via seat numbers, with an 8 s shot clock in the team colour.
- 3 strikes gives a 'Clutch': the rival huddles 15 s and gives one answer. If correct, it earns that slot plus 5, and the first team loses nothing.
- 'Steal the bank' is opt-in (mild steal, Yellow).
- Combo is accuracy-only: 3 correct in a row inside control is x1.5, and 5 is x2. Scores never go below 0.
- Hints cost 1-2 points from the bank, never below 0: first letter, then 'category of the #1 answer', then a gapped example.
- 4 rounds; the last is 'DOUBLE'.
- The finale is 'Lightning Boards': all teams at once, 5 prompts, 15 s each. Each team writes one answer per prompt and scores that slot's points. Nobody sits out.

Endings
- A podium plus stat awards (Mind Reader for the most #1 answers, Clutch, Clean Sheet, Longest Streak, Comeback). Never a 'last place'.
- The class-in-numbers slide is styled as a stats dashboard.

Prompts
- 'Name an app teens use every day.', 'Name something that makes a good friend.', 'Name a reason to be late for school.', 'Name a skill you want to learn.', 'Name something you'd take to a school camp.'

Both modes
- The teenSafe filter always applies. No dating, money, appearance, family or grades prompts, and nothing about brands (answers are generic: 'a video app', not a brand name).
catalog.levelTuning:
GENERAL RULE: level (A1-B2) and audience skin are independent. The level sets the prompt cap, the answer frame, the board size, the word band of answers and the reporting task.

A1
- Adults: prompts of 10 words or fewer ('Name a drink.', 'Name something in a kitchen.'). Single-noun answers with 'It's ___.' / 'I think it's ___.' Board of 5. The typed survey autocompletes from the A1 band. The report is choral ('Tea! 12 of us like tea.').
- A1 Genç: prompts of 0-4 words, with the picture carrying the meaning ('Name a pet 🐾'). Picture-button survey. Board of 4 picture cards. Everything is read aloud at 0.8x. The frame is 'I think... a cat!'.

A2
- Routines, likes and simple past. 'Name something you do on Sunday.', 'Name something people buy at a market.'
- Frame: 'People ___ on Sunday.' / 'We ___.' Board of 5-6.
- Genç: prompts of 8 words or fewer, pictures still on every card ('Name something you eat for breakfast').
- Adults (15 words or fewer): shopping, holidays, home.
- Report: 'X of us + verb'.

B1
- Reasons, habits, experiences. 'Name a reason people are late for work/school.', 'Name something you'd pack for a weekend trip.'
- Frame: '... because ___.' Board of 6. The steal must be a full sentence.
- Reporting language unlocks after each round: 'Most of us / Many of us / A few of us / Nobody...'.
- 'Defend it' is opt-in.
- Genç: prompts of 14 words or fewer, on concrete school, trip and hobby topics.

B2
- Opinions and hypotheticals. 'Name something you'd change about your city.', 'Name a skill schools should teach.', 'Name a habit that's hard to break.'
- Hedged guessing frames: 'I'd guess quite a few people said...'. Board of 6-8. 'Defend it' is on.
- The debrief is a mini-report with percentages and fractions ('just over a third', 'the vast majority').
- B2 Genç: prompts of 20 words or fewer. Richer language on concrete topics ('Name an invention that changed how teens live'), not abstract debate.

MIXED ABILITY
- Kolay: after strike 2, the first letters of the hidden slots appear and word-band answers are accepted generously. It shifts the mix one band down (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 answers).
- Zor: the answer only counts in a grammatically correct frame; otherwise the teacher taps 'Close!'.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the prompt bank one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 15-25; Arena 20-30; Stüdyo 25-40. Add 3-5 min for a live survey, or run it as an exit poll the lesson before.
catalog.teacherControls:
- CONTENT
  - Source: live survey, built-in boards, LLM prompt or mixed.
  - Prompt editor: reorder, swap, edit text and frame.
  - Survey options: answers per student (1 or 2), picture buttons on/off, survey length (5-8 prompts), exit-poll mode.
  - Merge-review screen: merge, split, rename, bin; the 2-vote threshold can be lowered only for classes under 12, with a warning.
  - Saved class boards.
- BOARD: answers shown (3-8); points vs '8 of us' counts vs both; header label.
- RULES
  - Face-off mode: buzzer, boards up, or the spinner picks one team to start.
  - Strikes: 2-4, default 3.
  - Steal: off / slot-only 'Clutch' / take the bank.
  - Round multipliers.
  - 'Defend it' on/off.
  - Frame strictness: off / A2+ / Zor.
  - 'Close!' limit per round.
  - Shadow boards on/off with 3-4 teams.
  - Finale type: Hızlı Tur / Lightning Boards / Class Thermometer / none. The finale target can be edited.
- TIMERS: shot clock on/off (8 s), huddle length, +10 s, T to pause, 'Süresiz'; the lesson-fit timer sets the number of rounds.
- HOSTING
  - Kumanda phone remote with hidden answers, or a printable answer sheet.
  - Keyboard: 1-8 reveal, X strike, P play/pass, S steal, C Close!, Space 'Survey says', Z undo, +/- points.
  - Manual reveal of any slot, 'reveal all', skip board, swap to a spare prompt.
- LANGUAGE: TR gloss of the prompt in teacher chrome (switch off for immersion classes), 'Öğretmen okur' fallback, read-aloud speed.
- OVERRIDES: skin, rule pack and single dials, all saved to the class profile.
catalog.delightDetails:
- THE FLIP: slots turn like real card boards.
  - The ding plus the points rolling up.
  - Live boards add '8 of us said this!' underneath.
  - The #1 slot gets a gold edge and a tiny trumpet (Stüdyo), a Gogo dance of 2 s or less (Oyun Parkı), or a neon crown (Arena).
- THE REVEAL CHANT: before every reveal the class calls out the mode's line. Stüdyo 'Survey says!', Oyun Parkı 'Show me!', Arena 'Drop it!'. The teacher can hold Space for suspense, and a sub-1 s drumroll plays on release.
- WRONG GUESSES VANISH: they are never written on the board, so everyone has to listen, and a repeated wrong guess is a strike.
- 'We asked 28 students...': the header uses the real class count, and the survey waiting screen fills with anonymous dots and a quiet loop.
- LOCAL FLAVOUR: generated boards imagine '100 people in Türkiye', so 'Name a hot drink' puts tea on top and 'Name a breakfast food' finds cheese, olives and eggs. Students recognise their world in English.
- PREDICTION SLIPS: made during the merge, they pay off at the end with the 'Mind Reader' award.
- SHADOW BOARDS: they let idle teams snipe the leftover answers.
- HEADPHONES GAG: in the Hızlı Tur, player 2 wears the teacher's headphones with music on, or waits in the corridor, and the class stays theatrically silent.
- GOGO:
  - Parrots every answer so the class repeats it; he is choral drill in disguise.
  - Shrugs at oops clouds.
  - Sleeps on the pause screen.
- ARENA: the 'SIGNAL LOST' glitch X, combo meter, team motto on the podium.
- 'OUR CLASS IN NUMBERS': the finale infographic.
  - Pictogram bars of each prompt's top answers, with reporting frames.
  - Exportable as a PNG for the class wall or album.
  - Kids get it as a sticker page.
  - It turns the game into a genuine speaking and writing follow-up.
- ANNOUNCEMENTS: each round's category is announced on a sliding card, and the trailing team picks it from two face-down cards.
- REDUCED MOTION: every flip and effect becomes a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- SURVEY MERGE ERRORS: a wrongly split synonym or an unmerged misspelling feels unfair. Mitigation: seed aliases, fuzzy and LLM grouping, and mandatory teacher review before the board is used, plus the 'Close!' button and point edits in play.
- ANONYMITY AND EXPOSURE: a unique answer or a personal prompt can out a student. Mitigation: only impersonal or harmless-preference prompts (validator blocklist), the 2-vote threshold, no names or logins, raw answers purged after merge, the 'wave if you said it' step voluntary and kids-only, and rude answers binned unseen.
- PHONES OFTEN BANNED OR RESTRICTED in Turkish schools, and Wi-Fi is weak. Mitigation: paper slips with data clerks, exit-poll mode, and generated boards as a first-class path, not a fallback.
- SMALL CLASSES give thin data. Mitigation: 2 answers per student, blending with the seed board, and spare prompts.
- FAST STUDENTS DOMINATE BUZZING. Mitigation: 'Boards up' face-off by default for Genç, spinner rotation and seat-rotation in control.
- THE TEACHER MUST SEE HIDDEN ANSWERS WITHOUT THE PROJECTOR LEAKING THEM. Mitigation: the Kumanda remote, a printable sheet, and extended-display mode. Mirroring is detected and warned about.
- IMPLAUSIBLE GENERATED BOARDS: Western-centric or illogical rankings. Mitigation: the Türkiye framing in the generator and the validator checks on descending points and sums.
- ANSWER DISPUTES AND NOISE during chants. Mitigation: the teacher is always the judge, undo, and a pause key. Chants are short.
- LOW-LEVEL LEARNERS MAY FREEZE when producing answers. Mitigation: picture buttons, frames on screen, free kids' hints, and Gogo modelling.
- BUILD: the live survey needs a realtime Supabase session with a TTL, and the merge UI is the costliest part. The board game alone is M, which is why the whole game is sized L.

issues: THE LIVE SURVEY FAILS IN THE CORE TARGET CLASSROOM. Most 10-12 year-olds in a Turkish public school have no phone in class, and school Wi-Fi is weak. The design's fallback, paper slips that two 'data clerks' type in during a settler, means about 28 x 6 = 168 entries. That is 10-15 minutes of work, not a settler, and it happens while 26 other children have nothing to do. In practice the live survey only works for adults or as homework or an exit poll.

MERGE REVIEW CREATES DEAD TIME AND LEAKS ANSWERS. The teacher has to drag cluster cards for 1-2 minutes, realistically 3-5, while 28 children are left with only 'prediction slips'. On a smart board the teacher's screen IS the class screen, so either the answers leak or the teacher does the review on a small phone. The LLM grouping pass adds latency and runs into the rate limit at the worst moment.

THE TEACHER CANNOT SEE THE HIDDEN ANSWERS ON A SMART BOARD. Extended-display mode rarely exists on an interactive board, which is a single display. A printed answer sheet is impossible for a board built from a survey five minutes earlier. That leaves the Kumanda, which needs the teacher's phone plus mobile data. If that path fails, the teacher is judging blind.

KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS ARE USELESS WHILE STANDING AT A SMART BOARD. Keys 1-8, X, P, S, C, Space, Z, T and +/- give 10 or more controls that assume a laptop. Any on-screen host buttons (for example 'reveal slot 3') would tell the class where the answer is.

JUDGING IS THE HEAVIEST LOAD ON THE TEACHER. They must match each spoken answer to its aliases in real time ('hamburger' = 'burger'?), remember every wrong guess because a repeated miss is a strike and wrong guesses are not displayed, enforce the frame ('Full sentence, please!'), rate 'Close!' answers, and run the timers, all at once. With 28 shouting children, remembering the wrong guesses alone will fail.

OYUN PARKI HAS A FIRST-MOVER ADVANTAGE. With a board of 4 cards and 2-4 teams in a carousel, the first teams take the obvious 3-star answers, and later teams face only the leftover 1-star cards or an empty board. Over 3 rounds of about 4 minutes, turn order decides the stars.

MINI-WHITEBOARDS ARE ASSUMED. 'Boards up' is the kids' face-off, the whole-class moment every turn, and the finale, but most Turkish public classrooms have no set of team whiteboards. Without them, the whole-class moment disappears.

'SEAT NUMBERS' DOES NOT MATCH TURKISH CLASSROOMS. Seats are shared double desks that move around. Students do have school numbers (okul numarası), but mapping those to teams takes setup time. The spinner and the seat rotation assume a roster that nobody has entered.

THE STÜDYO SCORE SWINGS TOO MUCH. Steal-the-bank combined with x2 and x3 in rounds 4-5 means rounds 1-3 hardly matter, and one lucky steal in round 5 decides the game. Also, with 2 teams, the team not in control is idle for the whole control phase, often 2-3 minutes, except for the steal huddle.

THE HIZLI TUR DOESN'T SCALE. Sending player 2 into the corridor is fine with 10 adults, but a child alone outside the door is a supervision problem in a public school. The shared headphones also need hygiene and hardware.

NOBODY GENUINELY OWNS THE 'STOP ANY MOMENT' CASE. The 'Our class in numbers' ending depends on survey data. If the bell rings mid-round, there is no defined 'end now' that awards the bank and jumps straight to the podium.

THE TEACHER HAS TOO MANY SETTINGS. There are 4 content sources, 3 face-off modes, 3 steal modes, strictness settings, shadow boards, 4 finales and more. A teacher on a 2-minute changeover between lessons won't touch them, so the defaults carry everything, and the 1-minute setup claim holds only for built-in boards.

IN OYUN PARKI, CHANTING PLUS WAVING PLUS 'ME TOO' STICKERS PLUS ECHOING EVERY ANSWER IS TOO MUCH. With 28 children, 4 call-and-response moments a turn becomes noise and makes the turns longer. 'Wave if you said it' also partly undoes the survey's anonymity.
fixes: For Genç groups, make GENERATED boards ('We asked 100 kids') the default, not the live survey. Offer the live survey as an 'Anket ödevi / exit poll' made one lesson earlier, and merge it at home before class. The in-class survey stays opt-in and is Stüdyo-first.

Replace data clerks with an 'El kaldır anketi' (hands-up poll) for Genç. The picture choices appear on the board, the class raises hands per option, and the teacher taps +/- counts, about 30 s per prompt. It needs no phones or merge, and it is fine for harmless preferences.

Move all merge review to the Kumanda, or run it before class. If it has to happen on the shared screen, show a 'Hazırlanıyor' cover with a 90-second warm-up game (a Gogo practice round) so there is no dead time. Skip the LLM grouping when picture buttons were used, because the counts are already exact.

Add a 'Yaz ve eşle' judging mode for the smart board: the teacher types or taps the spoken answer into a field and the engine matches it against the aliases, then flips the slot or adds a strike. The engine also keeps the list of wrong guesses on the teacher side and flags a repeat automatically. Then the teacher needs no hidden-answer view and has nothing to remember.

Design on-screen host controls that leak nothing: one large 'Doğru mu?' panel that opens only after an answer is entered, a strike button, and an overflow menu. Keep the keyboard shortcuts as extras for laptops.

Fix Oyun Parkı turn order. Rotate the starting team each round. Size the board to the teams (for example, one card per team plus 2). Or, in the kids' rule set, every team writes a secret guess each turn and every team whose guess matches earns the stars, so the active team only chooses which guess is flipped. That keeps it to 3 rules and removes the order effect.

Give a no-hardware fallback for 'Boards up': A4 sheets in plastic sleeves, or paper plus a marker, named in the Turkish setup card. Also offer 'hands-up choices', where the board shows 4 options for the class to vote on, when no boards exist.

Make the face-off pickers work without a roster. The default is 'Sıradaki oyuncu', where the team sends a different person each time and the screen shows a tally of turns per team. Offer an optional school-number range (for example 1-28) for the spinner.

For Stüdyo, change the default from steal-the-bank to Clutch (slot plus bonus) and cap the multipliers at x2 in the last round only. Keep the other team active during control: it writes shadow guesses (as in the 3-4-team rule) that score leftover slots.

Replace the corridor or headphones step in the Hızlı Tur with 'Arkanı dön ve yaz' (turn around and write): player 1 writes answers on paper, and player 2 faces away from the board while the teacher covers player 1's answers. Or make Lightning Boards the default finale for groups bigger than 12.

Add an always-visible 'Bitir' (finish) control that banks the current round, skips the finale and goes to the podium plus a short class-in-numbers page built from whatever boards were played. Show 'Kalan süre' (time remaining) in the teacher chrome, and suggest skipping a round when time runs short.
Hide the rule settings behind 3 presets per mode (Hızlı / Standart / Detaylı). Keep content and group selection on the first screen, so setup takes 30 s for built-in or generated boards.

Trim the Oyun Parkı rituals to one chorus per turn: Gogo repeats the answer and the class echoes it. Make 'Show me!' optional and drop 'Wave if you said it'. Add a visible noise-meter pause (Gogo sleeps) that the teacher can trigger.

issues: Level control works on the question side but not on the answer side. The prompt cap, the frame and the reporting task scale with level, yet the answers students must produce are whatever the crowd said most often, and those are almost always A1-A2 nouns (tea, phone, pizza, traffic). B1 and B2 players spend most of the game producing A1 words inside a frame. Only 'Defend it' and the debrief carry real B-level output.

Frames are easy to skip. In a buzzer face-off or under an 8 s shot clock, students blurt the noun, and a teacher running strikes, reveals and chants will not police 'People ___ before school' every time. The 'Full sentence, please!' rule at A2+ gives no strike and unlimited retries, so there is no incentive. Frame use will slide into single-word clicking.

The Oyun Parkı whole-class moment depends on writing: every team holds up a mini-whiteboard with its secret guess, and the kids' finale 'Class Thermometer' has all teams write. A1 Genç learners aged 9-10, who barely read or spell, cannot do this reliably. The step becomes the fastest writer copying a word, or Turkish words that cannot be matched. This contradicts the design's own picture-first A1 Genç path.

At A1/A2 Genç, the board is limited to answers that have an imageKey and the survey used 8-12 picture buttons. The guessable space is therefore the same small picture set, which the hint ladder's silhouette narrows further. Children who remember the survey screen can guess by elimination, so retrieval turns into recall of a menu. That is useful as picture-word recognition but weak as a 'Name something' retrieval task.

The LLM-generated 'We asked 100 people in Türkiye / 100 kids' header presents invented numbers as a real survey. Adults (especially B2 and teacher-trainee groups) will challenge rankings such as 'Why is olives #2?'. In the reporting phase, B1-B2 students would be building 'Most people...' sentences on fabricated data, which undercuts the reporting-language goal.

The live survey and merge cost 5-7 minutes of class time before anything scores (3-5 min survey plus 1-2 min teacher-only merge). The 'Prediction slips' filler covers adults, but young learners sit through a teacher-facing screen. A 9-11 class loses momentum, and for Oyun Parkı sessions of 15-25 min this is a quarter of the lesson.

Kids will type Turkish in the 'Başka' field and misspell heavily. The 2-vote threshold after fuzzy matching (edit distance 1-2) will drop many genuine child answers ('penguen', 'pengiun'), so kids' live boards will be thin or dominated by the picture buttons. The design does not route Turkish kid answers to an English learning moment.

Stüdyo rule load is high for A1 adults: Play/Pass, 3 strikes, steal-the-bank, x2/x3 multipliers, 'Close!', shadow boards and Hızlı Tur with headphones. The rules must be explained in Turkish, which is fine, but the setup does not scale rules by level, only by audience. A1 adult classes (often older, less gamer-literate learners) get the full classic.

B2 Genç is squeezed. Prompts are capped at 'concrete topics, not abstract debate', and the teenSafe blocklist removes money, appearance, family and brands. What remains ('Name a skill you want to learn') is B1 content with longer wording. B2 teens get no B2-specific task except the percentages debrief, and Arena does not enable 'Defend it' at B2 Genç.

In control, one student answers per turn and answers are not written, which gives good listening pressure. But with 15 per team and 4-6 answers per board, most students speak once per game at best. For low-level kids, the only guaranteed production is choral echo after Gogo. That is valid drilling, but it is repetition, not retrieval.

Built-in 'Hazır panolar' need hand-authored rankings with aliases, points and imageKeys for 8 topics × 4 levels × 3 audiences. Deriving them from category-list items (e.g. 'Pets' → 'Name a pet') gives an answer set but no plausible ranking, so built-in boards will have arbitrary point orders unless someone curates them.
fixes: Add a level-scaled answer layer. From B1 up, each slot has an 'upgrade' target from the words.js band (e.g. slot 'traffic' with the B1 upgrade 'traffic jam / rush hour'; at B2 'I'd guess quite a few said heavy traffic'). An answer that uses the band word or collocation earns +5 'Level up' points, or a star in Arena. At A2+, points are banked only when the answer comes in the frame, and a bare noun earns half points with no strike. The teacher's Kumanda shows the frame and upgrade next to each slot, so judging takes one tap: F = frame OK, U = upgrade.

Make frame use visible and cheap to judge: the frame chip lights up when the teacher presses F, and a 'Sentence streak' counter appears in Arena and Stüdyo. At Kolay the frame is accepted as said chorally by the team after the answer, which removes the burden from the individual speaker.

Replace writing in Oyun Parkı with picture holds: each team gets a printable A4 grid of the board's picture choices, or 3-4 picture fan cards (the PDF is generated with the board), and the team points to or holds up its guess. The Class Thermometer finale should use the same picture grids, or the teacher taps the team's pointed picture. Keep whiteboards as an option from A2 Genç up.

For A1/A2 Genç, set the survey picture set to 12 while the board shows only 4, and hide the list of choices during play (no menu screen). Put the silhouette hint last, after 'Gogo says the first sound', so retrieval comes before recognition. Add a spoken-label requirement: the team says the word and the frame; a pointed picture alone earns no star.

Relabel generated boards honestly: 'Tahmini pano' in teacher chrome, and on screen 'Our guess: 100 people in Türkiye' or 'Survey (imagined)'. Stüdyo B1+ adds a 20 s 'Do you agree?' debate hook, turning the implausible rankings into speaking material. Point the reporting task at live boards; for generated boards use 'The board says... but I think...' frames.

Split setup from class time. Make exit-poll mode (survey run at the end of the previous lesson or as homework) the recommended default, and let the merge happen outside class. When the survey runs live in Oyun Parkı, Gogo runs a 60 s 'Name a colour' practice round on the projector while the teacher merges, so kids are never idle.

Treat Turkish kid answers as content: the merge maps 'kedi' → cat and the flip shows 'kedi → cat!' with Gogo's echo. For Genç boards, lower the fuzzy threshold for known kid misspellings via the seed aliases. Allow the 2-vote threshold to count picture-button plus typed matches together.

Add a level-based rule preset under the audience skin: A1 and A2 Stüdyo default to 'Classic Lite' (no multipliers, no shadow boards, steal as slot-only Clutch, finale optional). B1-B2 get the full classic. Keep every rule as a dial.

Give B2 Genç (and B1 Genç as opt-in) Arena's own B-level task. Turn on a 'Defend it' variant called 'Make the case' (15 s, frame 'I'd say... because...'). Make the Arena stats dashboard debrief use fractions and hedges ('just under half of us'). Allow abstract-but-safe prompts such as 'Name a problem at our school' or 'Name something that makes a lesson boring'.

Raise speaking share: in control, the answering student's team echoes the accepted answer in the frame as a whole team. In Stüdyo, the round winner's report is done in pairs by every pair (30 s turn-and-tell) before the spokesperson speaks. Keep 'Kaçırılanlar' as a mandatory 2-min drill at A levels.

Author a small curated core instead of deriving rankings: about 12 boards per audience × A1-B2, with hand-checked Türkiye-plausible order and imageKeys for Genç. Use category-list items only for picture choices and aliases, and let the LLM supply the rest, validated with the existing descending-points and sum checks.

issues: SCOPE IS AN XL DISGUISED AS AN L. The spec bundles four products: (1) a Feud board engine, (2) an anonymous realtime survey app (/anket with QR, room codes, device tokens, TTL and purge), (3) an NLP merge pipeline (lemmatise, fuzzy match, LLM synonym clustering, drag-merge/split UI), and (4) a realtime phone remote (Kumanda). On top of that come 3 skins x 3 rule packs x 4 finales, shadow boards, prediction slips, Defend it, combo, Clutch, slipstream and hints. Only (1) is in the M range. The merge UI plus realtime alone is bigger than most other candidates in the suite.

Phone survey vs Turkish school reality. MEB restricts student phones, school Wi-Fi is weak, and anonymous open text from minors on a public endpoint is both a KVKK exposure and an abuse surface: slurs, a classmate's name typed as an answer, spam from outside the class via a leaked 4-letter code. A 4-letter code space is brute-forceable. The live survey is the headline feature, yet it will be the least-used path in state schools.

Merge review costs class time and teacher attention. Even at 1-2 minutes of drag-merging per prompt, 6 prompts on a smartboard with 28 kids waiting is a classroom-management hole. Drag-to-merge on a Windows smartboard (touch, often laggy IR panels) is fragile. 'Prediction slips' is filler that exists only to cover this dead time.

Generated boards are fiction presented as data. 'We asked 100 people in Türkiye' with LLM-invented percentages is misleading, and B2 debriefs that report 'just over a third' are reporting invented numbers. DeepSeek will produce plausible top answers, but the rankings, especially below #3, are noise. It will also drift Western, or into brand names, which the spec bans for teens.

LLM validity risks: alias collisions across answers ('chips' under both fries and crisps), aliases that are Turkish or mixed without a flag, answers above the level's word band, point sequences that are not strictly descending, ties, and totals over 100. The kids' rule needs an imageKey for every answer. The LLM will invent imageKeys that don't exist in the icon set, so most A1/A2 Genç generated boards will fall below 4 answers and be dropped.

Picture dependency for Oyun Parkı. imageKey is required on every card and pictureChoices needs 8-12 icons per prompt. That means an icon library of several hundred concrete nouns and activities ('brush teeth', 'walk to school') in one consistent style. No asset plan exists, and this is the real cost of the kids version.

Kids' version fit is weak. Guessing what OTHER people said is a second-order, theory-of-mind task. 9-10 year-olds at A1 mostly just name their own favourite, and with 4 picture cards and the silhouette hint the game collapses into 'guess which of 4 hidden pictures'. It passes the checklist (3 rules, no negatives), but the Feud core ('rank by popularity') is largely lost, and the carousel with a 10 s huddle is slow for 4 teams. 'Wave if you said it too' contradicts the anonymity promise, even as a voluntary step.

Rule sprawl hurts polish. Stüdyo has a buzzer face-off, Play/Pass, seat rotation, strikes, steal, x2/x3 rounds, slipstream, a comeback category pick, Close!, Defend it, the Full-sentence retry and the Fast Money finale. Arena adds combo, Clutch, hints that cost points, and the shot clock. The teacher must host all of it by keyboard. A real Feud feels good because it is simple and has one slick flip; this spec will ship with dozens of half-tested edge states. The undo (Z) across bank, steal and multipliers alone is non-trivial.

Fast Money is awkward in class. Sending player 2 into the corridor is a supervision and safety problem in Turkish schools, and shared headphones are unhygienic and fiddly. Scoring 10 answers in about 45 s also needs typed or teacher-entered matching against aliases, which is a separate UI.

Hidden-answer leakage. Without the Kumanda (realtime) the teacher must use a printout or extended display. The Window Management API for extended display is Chromium-only, and most classroom boards mirror. 'Mirroring is detected' is not reliably possible from the browser.

Duplication inside the suite. Lightning Boards and the Class Thermometer are the same 'everyone writes one answer per prompt' mechanic seen in category/STOP-type games. The survey data collection overlaps any 'poll/wheel/speaking-prompt' candidate. The core board (hidden ranked slots, teacher reveals) is distinct from MCQ quizzes and Jeopardy, so this is NOT a merge candidate on its core, but its finale variants should be cut.

Audio and TTS. The browser speechSynthesis quality on Windows classroom PCs is uneven and often lacks a good en-GB/US voice offline. Kids mode relies on read-aloud at 0.8x for every prompt and answer, so it will sound robotic or silent on some machines.
fixes: PHASE IT. v1 (M): built-in plus LLM-generated boards, keyboard/click hosting, printable answer sheet, and three skins with ONE shared core ruleset per mode. v1.5: 'Kağıt anket': paper slips plus a teacher-only tally screen, with no student devices and no realtime. v2: the phone survey and the Kumanda, behind a feature flag. Size v1 as M and label the full vision XL.

Core rules per mode, capped. Stüdyo: face-off, Play/Pass, 3 strikes, steal-the-bank, one x2 final round, and the finale. Arena: Boards-up face-off, 3 strikes, Clutch, and one combo only. Oyun Parkı: the 3 rules as written. Cut Slipstream, the comeback category pick, the shot clock, point-cost hints, Defend it (keep it as a later B2 toggle), prediction slips and shadow boards from v1.

One finale per mode. Stüdyo: a simplified Hızlı Tur with 5 prompts, both players answering aloud one after the other (player 2 turns their back to the screen; no corridor, no headphones) and the teacher tapping the matched slot or 'yok' on a pre-rendered 5x8 grid. Arena and Oyun Parkı: the Class Thermometer (cooperative). Drop Lightning Boards.

Honest framing for generated boards. The header says 'Tahmini pano' in teacher chrome, and 'Our guess: 100 people in Türkiye' / 'Guess the top answers!' on screen. Use a pts pattern (e.g. 35/25/15/10/8/7) snapped from the LLM's rank order instead of trusting its numbers. Reserve 'X of us' reporting slides and percentage debriefs for real class data (paper tally or live).

LLM contract and validator. Ask for strict JSON with RANK ORDER, not points, and assign points deterministically. Validate: 4-8 answers; each answer and alias lowercased and unique across the board (reject collisions or auto-drop the alias); every answer's headword found in words.js at or below the level band plus one (otherwise drop the answer, or regenerate if fewer than 4 remain); no digits or brands (a regex plus a small brand blocklist); Turkish-character detection flags aliases for review; prompt word count within the cap and starting with 'Name'. Generate 8 boards so that 6 survive; show the teacher a preview list with a 'yeniden üret' button per board.

imageKey from a closed vocabulary. Pass the LLM the exact list of available icon keys and let it choose only from it. The validator rejects unknown keys. Build kids' boards mainly from curated category-list/vocab packs ('Name a pet' → a pets category with icons), and use the LLM only for adult and Arena boards and for kids' ones that pass the icon check.

Icon budget. Use one consistent open-licence icon set (or a commissioned set of about 250 concrete nouns and routines), bundled as an SVG sprite and lazy-loaded per board. Limit kids' prompts to categories that have icons.

Rework Oyun Parkı around a concrete, first-order task. 'Guess what the class/kids picked' with a visible hint row of 8 picture choices (the 4 hidden ones plus 4 distractors). Teams pick and say the frame, the card flips if it's in the top 4, and the other teams show their pick on boards at the same moment. Drop 'Wave if you said it too'. Replace it with a choral echo, which stays anonymous.

If the live survey is built: use a 6-character code plus a QR with a signed session token, a TTL of 20 min, per-IP and per-token rate limits reusing the Material Maker limiter, the survey opened only while the teacher's screen is in the survey step, answers capped at 30 characters, and a profanity/name filter (a TR+EN list and a capitalised-word heuristic) before anything reaches even the teacher. Keep raw text server-side only until 'Onayla', then purge. Get a KVKK review and write a short notice on /anket.

Replace drag-merge with a one-tap review list. Auto-clusters are shown as rows ('pizza · 8 (pizzas, piza)') with 'Birleştir ↑', 'Ayır' and 'Çöp' buttons. Big touch targets, no dragging. The whole review is under 60 s for 6 prompts, with a 'hepsini onayla' default.

Presenter view without realtime for v1. A 'Gizli cevaplar' overlay toggled by holding a key or tapping a corner (for when the teacher turns the projector freeze on), plus a print sheet. Don't claim mirroring detection. Show a one-line tip: 'Projeksiyonu Genişlet moduna alın'.

Polish budget where it counts. One excellent flip (CSS 3D, 0.6 s, reduced-motion stamp), a rolling points counter, strike and ding sounds (under 20 KB each, 5-6 total per skin), the reveal-chant hold/release on Space, and the 'Our class in numbers' PNG export via canvas. These give most of the 'real game show' feel. Pre-record or bundle TTS audio for built-in kids' boards instead of relying on speechSynthesis.

Make the state machine explicit (round → faceoff → control → steal → reveal → report) as a pure reducer with a history stack. Undo then comes for free, and it can be unit-tested with fixtures of LLM boards before any skin work.

catalog.rankReason: Family Feud (adult 8), with answers in sentence frames and a good 'Our class in numbers' reporting ending. v1 uses built-in and LLM-generated boards ('We asked 100 kids') and a hands-up poll for Genç. The phone survey waits (MEB phone rules, KVKK, and moderation of open text from minors).

catalog.name: Dörtle! & XOX Arena (Four in a Row / Tic-Tac-Toe / Beehive)
catalog.familiarAs: Connect Four / Tic-Tac-Toe (XOX) / Blockbusters (Beehive, Hexalex)
catalog.oneLiner: One territory game with three boards. To claim a square (XOX), drop a disc (Dörtle!) or fill a hex (Kovan), a team must answer that cell's challenge. Choosing where to play (blocking, forking, going for the hard centre) matters as much as knowing the answer. Kids get a three-rule 3x3 sticker board, 12-14s a neon 'Match', and adults a 5x5 grid, a 7x6 Connect Four with sentence columns, or a Blockbusters beehive.
catalog.howItPlays:
ONE ENGINE, THREE BOARDS. Any content pack plays on three boards, and the teacher can switch boards between rounds ('Aynı içerik, üç tahta'):
- XOX: a square grid where a team claims any empty square.
- Dörtle!: Connect Four. A team picks a column and the disc falls to the lowest free slot.
- Kovan: Beehive / Blockbusters. A hex grid of letters where each team connects its own two sides.
Internally it is a single parametric board (rows, cols, win length, gravity on/off, square or hex topology), so every variant below is just a preset.

SETUP (about 60 s)
1. The teacher picks the content. Either choose a built-in category (a grammar_mcq unit, a words.js topic, idioms.js for B2) or type a prompt, e.g. '6. sınıf Unit 3 Yummy Breakfast, like/don't like'. The generator returns the items plus 5-7 short category labels.
2. The lesson-fit timer proposes a board, e.g. '15 dk -> XOX 3x3, 3 tahta'.
3. A profile line shows the settings, e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 15 dk', with a 'Değiştir' link.
4. Teams: the default is two halves of the class. With 3 teams the board switches to XOX 5x5 with 3 in a row. With 4 teams there are two parallel boards side by side (A v B and C v D), and turns alternate A, C, B, D.
5. Warm-up by mode:
   - Oyun Parkı: the parrot Gogo plays a 25 s practice round against the teacher on a mini board. It does not score.
   - Arena: a 10 s ownership ritual in which each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.

EVERY TURN (all boards)
1. SPEAKER. The seat-number spinner picks the active team's Speaker (kids and Arena). Adults use a rotating spokesperson. Nobody is ever picked by name. Each team also has a Captain who chooses the cell and changes every board, so the strategist and the answerer are different students.
2. PICK. The team names a cell and the teacher clicks it or presses a key: the numpad maps 7-8-9 / 4-5-6 / 1-2-3 onto the 3x3 grid, keys 1-7 pick a Dörtle! column, and arrows plus Enter work everywhere else. The cell zooms into a question card.
3. PROMPT. The item appears. A1/A2 Genç get a picture plus automatic read-aloud at 0.8x; everyone else gets a speaker button. Options appear after a delay: 3-4 s for kids, 2.5 s in Arena, 2 s for adults.
4. TEAM TALK. The huddle lasts 10 s for kids, 15 s in Arena and 20 s for adults. Then the screen shows 'Boards up!' and BOTH teams answer:
   - The active team answers for the claim.
   - The other team writes a 'shadow answer' on mini-whiteboards or holds up A-D cards.
   - Kids: every child also shows a card or does TPR (stand = A, sit = B, hands up = C).
5. ANSWER. The Speaker says the answer aloud.
   - MCQ, true/false and picture items: the teacher taps the option the Speaker named and the game judges it.
   - Open items: the teacher presses Reveal, the accepted answers appear, and the teacher taps a big tick or cross (keys Y/N).
   - B2 speaking cells: the buttons are Great / OK / Not yet.
6. RESOLVE. A correct answer claims the cell (a stamp, a disc drop or a honey fill) and shows a one-line model answer. A wrong answer follows the audience rule under WRONG ANSWERS.
7. CHECK. The game detects finished lines. It glows open threats, shows 'BLOCKED!' when a team plays into the other team's threat and 'FORK!' when a team makes two threats at once, then passes the turn.

XOX
- Sizes: 3x3 (3 in a row), 4x4 (3 in a row, Arena), 5x5 (4 in a row for adults; 3 in a row with 3 teams).
- Difficulty: the centre square is a 3-star question, so the strongest square costs the hardest question. On 5x5 the four inner diagonal squares are 2-star.
- Square faces show one of three things: a category icon plus label (the default), the difficulty stars, or nothing ('Gizemli kareler').
- Full board with no line: the team with the most squares wins. If that is level, adults and Arena play a one-question tiebreaker (a number answer; the closest team wins). Kids get 'Friends board!' and both teams take stars.

DÖRTLE!
- Sizes: Klasik 7 columns x 6 rows (4 in a row), Kısa 6x5 (4 in a row) for short lessons, and Drop 3 at 5x4 (3 in a row) for kids.
- Each column has a header: an icon plus a 1-2 word label ('Past simple', 'Food', 'make/do', 'Opposites').
- Difficulty ladder: rows 1-2 ask 1-star items, rows 3-4 ask 2-star, rows 5-6 ask 3-star. The game gets harder as it gets tense, and a late block costs a hard question.
- A ghost disc shows the landing slot before the team commits.
- Question columns draw from an item pool.
- Sentence columns: the header is a word or chunk ('take up', 'get used to', 'make a decision'), and the team must say a correct sentence that uses it.
- Form columns: the team must say the past form or past participle (e.g. 'go -> went').
- A sentence header refreshes after 3 uses, so sentences are not recycled.
- A full column closes.

KOVAN (Beehive)
- Board: a 5x5 hex rhombus (4x4 for kids). Team 1 connects top to bottom and Team 2 connects left to right.
- Each hex shows a letter (initials at B2, e.g. 'BTB'), and the answer starts with it: 'Starts with M: we drink it and it comes from cows.'
- Sıralı (turn-based) is the default. The team in control picks a hex. If it misses, adults let the other team answer, and the hex goes to whoever is right.
- Buzz mode is opt-in for adults and Arena. Hands go up and the teacher taps the colour of the first team. As on the TV show, the team that wins a hex picks the next one.
- The first pick of a board may not be the centre hex.
- A hex board can never end in a draw.

WRONG ANSWERS
- Oyun Parkı:
  1. A soft 'boing', then a free hint (picture zoom, then the first letter, then listen again) and a second try.
  2. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer and the whole class repeats it twice.
  3. The team gets an effort star for the class album.
  4. The cell 'naps' under a sleepy cloud for one turn, then wakes up with a fresh question.
- Arena: the streak breaks and the tile 'cracks' for one turn (the same lock rule). If the teacher has opted into mild steals, the other team's shadow answer may claim it.
- Stüdyo: steal is on. The other team gets 10 s to answer (with a full sentence at B1+) and claims the cell if it is right. The first team loses nothing. The teacher can switch to the lock rule.
- Any cell whose answer has been shown gets a fresh item from the spares.

END OF A BOARD AND THE SERIES
- The winning line draws itself across the board.
- Adults and Arena play best of 3. Kids play all 3 boards within a fixed time, even if one team has already won two.
- The team that lost the last board goes first on the next one and picks its categories from a fan of 3 category cards (comeback).
- Between kids' boards Gogo hosts a 45 s stirrer or a 60 s settler.
- A Rematch button replays the same pack with fresh items.

SCORING
- Oyun Parkı:
  - Every claimed cell adds a sticker to the team's strip.
  - The board winner gets 3 stars and the other team gets 2.
  - Nothing ever goes down.
- Arena:
  - Points per correct answer: 100 for a 1-star item, 200 for 2-star, 300 for 3-star.
  - Combo multiplier: x1.5 at 3 correct in a row and x2 at 5, based on accuracy only.
  - Hints cost 50-100 points, and the score never drops below 0.
  - Lines decide boards; points decide stat awards and tiebreaks.
- Stüdyo:
  - The score is boards won.
  - Optional extras: points, costed hints (definition, then example, then TR gloss), negative marking, and wagers on 3-star cells.
- Block bonus (Comeback Light): a correct answer that blocks an open threat earns a sticker, +100, or a 'Block' stat.

WHO DOES WHAT
- The teacher runs the keyboard: enters the cell the Captain names, judges, gives hints, handles timers and undoes mistakes.
- Students huddle, argue strategy in English (frames on screen at B1+: 'We should block them.', 'Let's take the centre.', 'If we go here, they will...'), write answers on their boards, and the Speaker says the answer aloud.
catalog.playerSetup:
The default on every board is the whole class in 2 teams (half v half).
- 3 teams: XOX 5x5 with 3 in a row, using three colours and three shapes.
- 4 teams (large public-school classes of 30-36): two parallel boards side by side on one projector. Turns alternate A, C, B, D.
Roles inside each team:
- The Captain chooses the cell and rotates each board.
- The Speaker is chosen by the seat-number spinner each turn (kids and Arena) or is a rotating spokesperson (adults).
- Everyone else writes a shadow answer on mini-whiteboards or holds up A-D cards, so the waiting team is never idle.
Adults also consult in pairs during Team talk. It works from 6 students (3 v 3) up to 36.
skills: strategy and team talk (suggesting and agreeing in English)
catalog.contentShape:
ENVELOPE. pack.frames.grid = {board ('xox'|'dortle'|'kovan'), rows, cols, win, gravity, topology ('square'|'hex'), cells[] | columns[] | hexes[], spares[], tiebreak[]}. The LLM writes only the items and the category labels. Code builds the board, assigns difficulty tiers and hex letters, and validates.

XOX CELL. {cat, catIcon (SVG or emoji key), face ('picture'|'label'|'stars'|'mystery'), diff (1-3; the centre is 3), itemId, spareIds[1-2]}.
- Items can be any answerable type: mcq, gap, qa, tf, odd, error, order, riddle and sound, plus speaking-prompt at B1+.
- A board needs 9, 16 or 25 items, plus 1 spare per cell.

DÖRTLE! COLUMN. {label (English, 2 words or fewer), labelTr, icon, mode ('question'|'sentence'|'form')}, plus ONE of:
- tiers {1: itemIds[], 2: itemIds[], 3: itemIds[]}: 2 rows per tier plus 1-2 spares. About 7 x 8 = 56 items.
- prompts[]: vocab or speaking-prompt references (term, frames, a model example for the teacher), refreshed every 3 uses. About 7 x 3 = 21 prompts.

KOVAN HEX. {letter (initials for B2 idioms and phrasal verbs), itemId (a qa item with letter set), spareIds[] (same letter)}.
- 25 hexes (16 for kids) plus about 10 spares.
- A1 Genç uses mcq with fmt 'picture' instead ('Which one starts with B?' with 3 pictures).

TIEBREAK. 1-2 qa items with answerKind 'number' and a tolerance.

VALIDATORS
- Every accept[] entry starts with the hex letter or matches the initials.
- The letter pool is built from the pack (minPerLetter). X, Q and Z are avoided below B2, and letters may repeat.
- No answer is used twice on one board.
- A clue never contains its answer or a member of its word family.
- A cell face or column label never gives away its answer.
- Word caps and the teenSafe filter apply per group.
- Gap distractors must be wrong in the gap.
- Each Dörtle! column has enough items in every tier.
- Sentence-mode prompts must be collocations, phrasal verbs or verbs, with a model example.
- Picture-dependent kids' cells need an imageKey; cells without one are dropped.

BUILT-IN SOURCES
- grammar_mcq units become columns or squares, keeping the curated whyOpt.
- words.js topics and definitions feed the clues (defEasy, with Oxford definitions of 18 words or fewer at B).
- idioms.js feeds the B2 initials hives.
- YLE/MEB topic packs with SVG pictures cover kids.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO (A1-B2 adults)

SKINS
- Classic XOX: cream paper tabletop; marks are drawn in fountain-pen strokes. The dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme is optional.
- Dörtle!: a walnut board with ceramic discs and a woodblock clack.
- The Hive: a quiz-night honeycomb in two team colours, with gold for the final path.
- No mascot. Captions are neutral ('Board 2 · Travel'). Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs' v 'Present Perfectionists').

BOARDS
- XOX 3x3 speed warmer (5 min).
- XOX 5x5 with 4 in a row and a 3-star centre.
- Dörtle! Klasik 7x6 or Kısa 6x5, with the difficulty ladder.
- Kovan 5x5.

CELL TASKS go well beyond MCQ:
- 'Fix it' (error)
- 'Make a question' (order or qa)
- 'Say it politely' (speaking-prompt, fn:request)
- 'Past participle?' (form column)
- collocation gaps
- life-and-work sentence columns ('make a decision', 'get on with', 'be in charge of'): 'Say a sentence about your job.' The teacher judges with tick or cross, and the model example shows afterwards.
Categories follow adult domains: travel, work, complaints, small talk, job interviews.

RULES
- Steal is on by default. The other team gets 10 s, and at B1+ the steal answer must be a full sentence.
- Overwrite is on at B2 and opt-in at B1. (It was called 'Devil' in the raw idea; it is renamed because some Turkish classes find that word off-putting.) Once per board per team, a team can answer a 3-star question to replace one opponent mark that is not part of a finished line.
- Optional wager on 3-star cells: if the answer is right, the team claims the cell plus one adjacent empty cell; if it is wrong, the other team claims the cell.
- Optional negative marking and costed hints: definition, then example, then Turkish gloss. The TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
- The 30 s timer is optional.

SERIES
- Best of 3. The loser of each board picks the next board's categories and goes first.
- A rematch is offered only after the series ends.
- Optional finale 'Altın Koşu' (Gold Run): all teams together have 90 s to connect a 4x4 board of initials.

ENDING
- Board-by-board scores.
- Stats: accuracy per category, blocks, forks, steals.
- 'Kaçırılanlar': every missed item with its answer and whyTr/whyEn, exportable as homework.
- Student screen in English, teacher chrome in Turkish.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two different games, not one game re-coloured.

OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1 and A2 Genç)

BOARDS
- 'Sticker Tac Toe': a 3x3 cork board. Claimed squares get the team's animal sticker with a stamp-and-wiggle. Panda v fox is the default.
- 'Drop 3': 5 columns x 4 rows, 3 in a row. Discs are the team mascots' faces and bounce twice with a marimba note.
- 'Bee Garden': a 4x4 hex of flowers. A right answer fills the flower with honey in the team colour, and a bee flies along the finished path.
Square faces are always pictures from the self-hosted SVG set, never text only (a cat square asks 'What's this?' or 'Say 2 things!').

RULES. Three rules on a pictogram card, explainable in 20 s. The card is in Turkish for the teacher; the student screen shows only tiny English ('Your turn!', 'Three in a line!').
1. Pick a square.
2. A right answer puts your sticker on it.
3. Three in a line earns a big star. (In Bee Garden: make a honey path across.)

KIDS CHECKLIST
- No elimination.
- Nothing ever drops below zero.
- No steals and no Overwrite.
- The timer is off by default (a calm 40 s ring if it is turned on, never red).
- A whole-class response every turn: A-D cards or TPR, then a choral echo ('Say it: banana!').

WRONG ANSWERS AND GOGO
- A wrong answer gets a free hint and a second try. If it is still wrong, Gogo the parrot says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star.
- The square then naps under a sleepy cloud for one turn. The failure imagery is never violent.
- Gogo demos the game on a mini board, sits on the board frame, and sleeps on the pause screen.
- When 'Gogo ipucu' is on, Gogo peeks at a square that would complete a line, for either team.
- One hidden 'golden egg' square per board: whichever team claims it, the whole class gets 2 album stickers (Green luck only).

PACING
- 3 boards of 4-5 minutes each, with a 45 s stirrer or a 60 s settler between them: 15-20 minutes in all.
- All 3 boards are always played.

ENDING
- Both teams get stars.
- Every team gets a title (Line Makers, Super Listeners, Best Helpers, Brave Guessers).
- Confetti in the team colours and shapes.
- A sticker goes into the class album.
- A draw becomes 'Friends board!' and both teams take 3 stars.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1 and B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç class at grade 6+)

FRAMING. Always a 'Match'. There are no animals, no talking mascot and no pastel colours, so a 13-year-old A1 class gets A1 content with Arena visuals.

BOARDS
- 'Grid Wars': 4x4, 3 in a row. Neon tiles; a shield flashes 'BLOCKED!'.
- 'Drop Zone': Kısa 6x5 Connect Four with plasma discs and a laser win line.
- 'Hex Clash': a 5x5 hex; energy flows along the path.

LOOK
- Dark navy with neon accents in the team colours.
- A condensed display font.
- Team emblems: bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond.
- A 10 s ownership ritual: emblem, colour, 3-word motto.
- A commentator strip shows at most one caption per turn ('COMBO x3', 'FORK!', 'CLUTCH BLOCK!').

RULES
- A 30 s timer ring in the team colour.
- A 15 s huddle.
- The seat spinner plus mini-whiteboards.
- Streak and combo points with a floor at zero.
- A wrong answer breaks the streak and cracks the tile for one turn.
- A mild steal through the other team's whiteboard happens only if the teacher opts in. Overwrite happens only if the teacher opts into Yellow.
- Two visible 'power nodes' per board. Claiming one gives a Retry token, and so does a 3-streak (Green luck).
- The rule card is in English, with a Turkish toggle.

PACING AND ENDING
- Best of 3, at 6-8 minutes per board.
- A podium with team stat awards: Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet, The Wall (most blocks), Fork Master.
- Never a last place, and no individual names.

CONTENT. The teenSafe filter applies to all Genç groups. Topics stay concrete: school, sport, games, food, animals, travel, nature. There is no dating, no brands and no adult domains (rent, salary, office, boss).
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Items: pictures and single words, 2-3 options, true/false about a picture.
- Kovan: a letter-sound hive for kids ('Which one starts with B?' with 3 pictures). Adults get the first letter plus a picture plus a clue of 10 words or fewer.
- Boards: XOX 3x3 for kids, 3x3 or 4x4 for adults; Drop 3 or Kısa Dörtle! in Question mode.
- Frames: 'It's a...', 'I can see a...', 'I like / I don't like...'.
- Word caps: A1 Genç 0-4 words, A1 10.

A2
- Items: 3-option gap MCQ; tap-bank gaps; odd one out; riddles read aloud ('It's yellow. Monkeys love it.' for B).
- Form columns ('Past simple: go -> ?').
- Kids' speaking cells: 'Say 2 things'.
- Boards: XOX 3x3 or 4x4; Dörtle! in Question or Form mode.
- Word caps: 8 (A2 Genç) and 15 (A2).

B1
- Items: short open answers; transformations; 'Make a question' (order); 'Fix it' (one error per sentence); target-tense sentences.
- Boards: XOX 5x5 with 4 in a row; Dörtle! Klasik with Sentence columns.
- Kovan clues are definitions from words.js ('Starts with R: to say no to an offer' for refuse).
- Adults: a steal answer must be a full sentence. Strategy frames appear on screen.
- Word caps: 14 (B1 Genç) and 25 (B1).

B2
- Items: open answers; collocation and phrasal-verb columns that need natural sentences about your own life; word families (decide / decision / decisive).
- Kovan: an idiom hive with initials ('BTB: to avoid the main point' for beat around the bush).
- Speaking cells judged Great / OK / Not yet ('Give advice using should', 'Speculate about this photo').
- Adults: Overwrite on; Buzz mode available.
- Word caps: 20 (B2 Genç) and 40 (B2). B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics, not abstract debate.

ACROSS ALL GROUPS
- The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial shifts the word-band mix behind the 1-star, 2-star and 3-star tiers.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one level without changing the skin.
- A long item is split into two cards rather than shrunk.
catalog.sessionMinutes:
5-25 in total; the lesson-fit timer picks the board size from the minutes left.
- Kids: 3 boards of 4-5 minutes plus stirrers, 15-20 minutes.
- Arena: best of 3 at 6-8 minutes per board, 20-25 minutes. A single board makes a 7-minute filler.
- Adults: XOX 3x3 warmer 5 minutes; XOX 5x5 or Kovan 10-15 minutes; Dörtle! Klasik 15-20 minutes (Kısa 10-12).
catalog.teacherControls:
BOARD
- Board type and size: XOX 3x3 / 4x4 / 5x5; Dörtle! 5x4 / 6x5 / 7x6; Kovan 4x4 / 5x5. Win length is adjustable.
- Switch board between rounds while keeping the same pack.
- Teams: 2, 3, or 4 (on parallel boards).
- Who starts: alternates by default, and the loser of the last board starts.
- Categories per square or column: automatic, or drag category cards onto cells.
- Face mode: label / stars / mystery.
- Centre difficulty and the Dörtle! difficulty ladder, each on/off.
- Column mode (Question / Sentence / Form) and 'refresh after N uses'.

RULES
- Wrong-answer rule: Nap/Lock, Pass, or Steal (with the full-sentence requirement for steals).
- Overwrite on/off, and how many uses.
- Wager cells on/off.
- Kovan: Sıralı or Buzz.
- Power nodes and the golden egg on/off.
- 'Gogo ipucu' and the threat glow on/off.

TIME AND HELP
- Timers: +10 s, T to pause, 'Süresiz'.
- Huddle length and options delay.
- Best-of-N and a time cap per board.
- Hint ladder (H) and the Turkish gloss on/off.

JUDGING AND FIXES
- Reveal (R), tick / cross (Y / N), Great / OK.
- Undo the last claim (U or Ctrl+Z, multi-step).
- Manual cell assign: right-click a cell and choose a team.
- 'Soruyu değiştir': swap a bad item for a spare without losing the turn.
- Clear a lock.
- Speaker spinner on/off.

OTHER
- The class profile line with its 'Değiştir' link.
- Keyboard map: numpad = the 3x3 cells, 1-7 = columns, arrows + Enter, F = fullscreen.
- Rematch with fresh items.
- Export 'Kaçırılanlar'.
catalog.delightDetails:
DÖRTLE!
- A ghost disc hovers over the chosen column and shows the landing slot.
- The disc falls on a gravity curve with a clunk and two small bounces.
- The ladder rungs (1, 2 and 3 stars) on the side light up as the column fills.

XOX
- Kids: stamp-and-wiggle stickers.
- Arena: neon tiles flip with a click.
- Adults: marks are drawn stroke by stroke in fountain pen.

KOVAN
- Hexes fill with honey from the bottom up in the team colour.
- A bee (kids) or a light pulse (adults and Arena) runs along the winning path.

ALL BOARDS
- Open threats glow softly: an open line of 3 in Dörtle!, 2 in a row on 3x3.
- A 'BLOCKED!' shield when a team plays into the other team's threat, and a 'FORK!' flash for a double threat.
- The winning line draws itself across the board: a rainbow for kids, a neon laser in Arena, an ink stroke for adults.
- Locked cells: a sleepy cloud (kids), cracked glass that reforms (Arena), pencil hatching (adults).
- Series tally marks under each team.
- At the end, a 5 s 'Maçın özeti' time-lapse replays the board filling up.
- The Arena teams' mottos show on the podium.

GOGO (kids)
- Sits on the board frame and peeks at a square.
- Dances for 2 s when a line is made.
- Parachutes the golden egg onto a square.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Team tokens differ by shape as well as colour (X/O, mascots, emblems), for colour-blind students.
- Reduced motion replaces drops and fills with a static stamp.

FINALE (optional, whole class)
- 'Altın Koşu / Honey Run': all teams together connect a 4x4 hive. It is timed at 90 s for adults and Arena and untimed for kids, and it earns a gold sticker for the class album.

SOUND
- Marimba for kids, synth blips for Arena, woodblock and piano for adults. Every effect lasts 1 s or less and is loudness-normalised.
catalog.risks:
- Only two teams really play. Mitigations: shadow answers on whiteboards, rotating Captain and Speaker roles, 3-team XOX, and 4-team parallel boards.
- Strategy can outweigh language, especially for 9-year-olds. Mitigations: kids stay on 3x3 or Drop 3; the ladder and the 3-star centre make key cells cost hard questions; mystery faces; 'Gogo ipucu' helps either team equally.
- Open answers need the teacher, since speech cannot be auto-graded. Mitigations: accepted answers show on Reveal, big tick and cross buttons, and a model example for every sentence column.
- Tic-tac-toe often ends in a draw. Mitigations: count squares and play a tiebreaker for older groups; 'Friends board' for kids. Kovan cannot draw.
- Dörtle! Klasik can run for 20 minutes. Mitigation: the lesson-fit timer proposes Kısa 6x5 or XOX instead.
- The first move is an advantage. Mitigations: alternate starts, the loser starts the next board, and in Kovan the first pick may not be the centre hex.
- Beehive letters are hard to fill at A1. Mitigations: the letter pool comes from the pack, letters may repeat, and A1 Genç uses the picture phonics mode. The letter is itself a hint, so a clue must not be guessable from the letter alone.
- The LLM may break the first-letter rule or put the answer inside its clue. Mitigation: the validator checks both and regenerates.
- Buzz mode favours fast students. Mitigation: turn-based play is the default.
- Steals can cause arguments. Mitigations: steals are off in Nazik modes, and any claim can be undone.
- Seven column labels are hard to read on a projector. Mitigation: labels of 2 words or fewer plus an icon, at a 5vh font floor.
- The raw idea's 'Devil' name may put off some classes. Mitigation: it is renamed Overwrite.
- 12-13-year-olds dislike childish visuals. Mitigation: Arena is suggested from grade 6.

issues: The time estimates are too optimistic. A kids' turn runs about 55-75 s: the Captain picks (with 14 kids shouting), the zoom, read-aloud at 0.8x, a 3-4 s delay before the options, a 10 s huddle, 'Boards up', the Speaker answering, the teacher's tap and the resolve animation. A wrong answer adds a hint, a second try, Gogo, a choral repeat twice and the nap. A 3x3 board that fills (or goes to a draw) takes 8-10 turns, which is 8-12 minutes, not 4-5. 'All 3 boards always played' plus stirrers comes to 30-40 minutes. An Arena 4x4 turn has a 30 s timer, a 15 s huddle and a delay, so a board is 12-15 minutes and best of 3 is 35-45 minutes, not 20-25. Dörtle! Klasik 7x6 takes 25-35 turns at 50-60 s each, which is about 25-30 minutes per board, so an adult best of 3 on Klasik cannot fit in any lesson.

Only 2 of 28 kids are really active per turn: the Speaker and the Captain. The shadow answer carries no stakes in Nazik mode (steals are off and nothing is scored), so after two turns the waiting team stops writing and starts chatting. The spec also assumes every child has a mini-whiteboard or A-D cards, and most Turkish public-school classes have neither.

A 10 s huddle with 14 children is fiction. In practice the loudest child shouts an answer and the Speaker repeats it, which is exactly the domination the Speaker spinner is meant to prevent. With 14 kids on a team, one Captain per board means only 3 children ever make a strategic choice in the whole session.

The 'seat-number spinner' has no real basis. Turkish classes have school numbers (okul no, e.g. 247, 1103), not seat numbers 1-14, and the desk layout changes. Without a roster step the teacher has to improvise a mapping, or the spinner lands on an absent student's number and dead time follows.

The keyboard-first controls (numpad, keys 1-7, Y/N, U, H, R, right-click to assign) do not work for a teacher standing at a smart board, who has only touch. Touch screens have no right-click, and the teacher cannot reach a laptop keyboard across the room. The control surface in teacherControls, about 35 options, is far too much to manage live.
