Four teams on two parallel boards on one projector halves the readability of an already dense grid. The A, C, B, D turn order means each team plays only every 4th turn, which is 3-4 minutes idle, and in a class of 36 that is where the chaos starts.

Strategy can override language. On 3x3 the first mover has a huge advantage and perfect play is a draw, so a team that answers more questions correctly can still lose to one clever Captain. That feels unfair to 10-year-olds, and 3 vs 2 stars does not soften it. Adults see through 3x3 at once: it is a draw machine unless the centre question is hard.

Kovan (hex connection) is abstract for 9-11 year-olds. 'Connect your two sides' on a hex rhombus takes more than 20 s to explain, and kids cannot see blocks or threats on hex adjacency. It fails the 'explainable in 20 s with pictograms' check in practice even though it has only 3 rules.

Kids' wrong-answer handling piles up dead time: the boing, hint 1, a retry, Gogo, a choral repeat twice, the effort star, and the nap cloud lasting a turn. In a weak A1 class, half the turns get this treatment and the energy drops.

Stopping at any moment is not supported. The kids' rule 'all 3 boards always played' and a series of 'best of 3' both assume the time exists. When the bell rings at board 2, move 5, there is no fair way to end.
Live LLM generation in class depends on school Wi-Fi and rate limits. A 56-item Dörtle! pack plus validation and regeneration can take 30-60 s or fail in front of 28 kids.

The adult sentence columns ('make a decision': say a sentence about your job) are good language work, but they put all the judging on the teacher, and 5 adults waiting 20 s while one pair thinks is fine only at B1+. The 10 s steal window with full-sentence judging creates arguments about what counts as correct, and the undo does not help with those.

The build is L and it multiplies: 3 boards x 3 audiences x 3 sizes, plus skins, sounds, Gogo, power nodes, the golden egg, overwrite, wagers, buzz, the finale and the time-lapse. Classroom value is concentrated in 2-3 presets, so most of that surface will go untested in real classes.
The game overlaps with the existing /sinif-oyunu (team tile board with MCQs). From the teacher's seat it looks like 'Baamboozle again with lines' unless the territory strategy stays clearly visible.
fixes: Base the lesson-fit timer on measured turn length, not a guess: about 60 s per turn for kids, 55 s for Arena and 45 s for adults. Show a realistic estimate ('~9 dk / tahta'). Default kids to 2 boards (3x3 or Drop 3), Arena to 1-2 boards on 4x4, and adults to XOX 5x5 or Kısa 6x5. Hide Dörtle! Klasik 7x6 unless 25+ minutes remain, and never offer best-of-3 on Klasik.

Add 'Bitir' (end now) as a first-class button. It resolves fairly: most cells, then most lines, then 'Friends board'. Kids always finish on a positive screen. Replace 'all 3 boards always played' with 'boards played until the time cap'.

Give the shadow answer stakes that the teacher never has to count. Before the reveal, one tap of 'Class echo' shows the answer to everyone: if most of the waiting team is right (the teacher eyeballs it and taps once), that team gets a small 'shadow sticker' or +50. For classes without whiteboards, the game provides a printable A-D card sheet and a no-equipment TPR mode (stand, sit, hands on head, point at window) as the default.

Replace the 14-person huddle with pair talk: 'Tell your partner' for 10 s, then the spinner picks the Speaker. Rotate the Captain every 3 turns, not every board, so 8-10 children get to choose a cell in a session.

Replace the seat spinner with a 10-second roster step: the teacher enters the class size, the game splits 1..N into two teams (printable desk number tags), and absent numbers can be struck with one tap. The roster is saved in the class profile. Add a 're-spin' button with no penalty.

Make it touch-first for the smart board: every action is a big on-screen button in a bottom teacher dock (Doğru / Yanlış / Göster / İpucu / Geri al / Duraklat). Long-press replaces right-click. The keyboard stays as a projector-plus-laptop bonus. Keep an 'Advanced' drawer for the 30 dials, and show at most 5 during play. Optionally let the Captain walk up and tap the cell, with a ghost-then-confirm step to avoid stray touches.
Drop the 4-team parallel boards. With 3-4 teams, use one XOX 5x5 (3 in a row) with 3-4 shapes, or 2 teams split into sub-squads that alternate Speakers. Cap each team's wait at 2 turns.

Weight language over strategy for kids: on 3x3 every correct answer also earns a sticker toward the team strip, and the board result is lines plus stickers, so a team that answers well is never shut out. Make centre-first illegal on 3x3 (it cannot be picked on turn 1), mirroring the Kovan rule. For adults, never default to 3x3 except as a 5-minute warmer.

Remove Kovan from Oyun Parkı by default: the kids' boards are Sticker Tac Toe and Drop 3 only, and Bee Garden is opt-in with an animated demo. Keep Kovan for Arena and adults, where Blockbusters is a strong format.

Trim the kids' wrong-answer chain to 2 steps: one hint and retry, then Gogo says the answer with one choral repeat. The cell stays open with a fresh question (no nap, and the effort star is optional) to cut dead time.

Pre-generate packs outside class: 'Hazırla ve kaydet' before the lesson, with an offline cache in IndexedDB. Built-in packs always work offline. Show generation progress and fall back to a built-in pack on failure.

For adult sentence judging, show on Reveal a 2-point checklist (uses the chunk correctly / correct tense) plus the model sentence, and make the steal window visible. Allow 'Kısmen' (partial) as 'no claim, no steal' to defuse arguments.

Scope the MVP: one parametric engine, but ship first XOX (3x3/4x4/5x5) and Drop 3 / Kısa 6x5 with the three skins. Kovan, Overwrite, wagers, buzz, power nodes, the golden egg, Altın Koşu and the time-lapse come in phase 2, after two real classroom trials.

Make it clearly distinct from /sinif-oyunu by putting line-making and blocking up front (threat glow and 'BLOCKED!' always on), and share the question-card component and item pipeline with sinif-oyunu rather than duplicating them.

issues: Low production per turn, especially at A1/A2. Most cells are MCQ, true/false or picture items: one Speaker names an option, and shadow answers are A-D cards. In a 30-child class that means about 10 s of language use per child per board. The choral echo only happens after a failure in Oyun Parkı, so there is none on a correct turn. At A1-A2 Genç the game risks turning into tic-tac-toe with recognition questions.

Strategy can outweigh language for 9-11s. The Captain role and the choice of where to play are carried out in Turkish; the strategy frames appear only at B1+. The game's real decisions ('block them!') happen in L1, and the language task is just a gate. The ladder and the 3-star centre only apply on some boards: 3x3 has only one 3-star cell, so any non-centre square is the same cost.

Bee Garden (a 4x4 hex board with a connect-your-sides win) is too abstract for 9-10-year-olds. Hex adjacency and 'a path from top to bottom' are hard to see on a projector from the back row, and it is the only kids' board where a child cannot tell at a glance who is winning. It also breaks the 'explainable in 20 s' check in practice.

Kovan letter phonics for A1 Genç clashes with Turkish L1. English letter names differ from Turkish ones (be/bee, ce/see, je/jay; C, J and G map to different sounds; I/İ). 'Which one starts with B?' is fine, but letters with a Turkish/English sound mismatch (C, J, G, Y, W) will mislead. A Turkish free-text prompt can also make the LLM produce Turkish-initial answers or Turkish characters (Ş, Ç, Ğ, Ö, Ü, İ).

The B2 idiom initials hive ('BTB') is listed with no audience split. Idioms are abstract, often culturally opaque, and fail teenSafe or concrete-topic rules for B2 Genç. Initials puzzles are also a word-game skill more than a language skill.

The Dörtle! 3-tier difficulty ladder assumes the LLM, or code, can rank difficulty reliably. For words.js items the CEFR band gives a tier. For grammar_mcq units (about 22 items each, all one level) and teacher-prompt packs, star tiers will be noisy, so a 'hard' late block may be trivial and vice versa. Klasik 7x6 also needs about 56 items, and one MEB unit prompt ('Yummy Breakfast, like/don't like') cannot yield 56 distinct items without heavy repetition.

Sentence and Form columns are misaligned with the young-learner curriculum. Past forms ('go -> went') appear under A2 generally, but MEB grades 5-6 (typical A2 Genç) do not yet cover past simple. Sentence columns at B1 Genç 'about your own life' need frames, or they stall at 12-13.

Adults at A1: picture-plus-clue Kovan and picture XOX faces risk feeling babyish, depending on the image set. Kids' SVG clipart must not leak into Stüdyo, and nothing states a separate adult picture style (photo or line icon).
The number tiebreak (closest numeric answer) tests trivia or estimation, not language, and needs level control (numbers above 100 at A1?).

The design exposes too many options (3 boards x 3 audiences x sizes x rule toggles) for a Build L. The level-fit risk is that the teacher-facing presets are wrong for a group while the teacher never sees it. Example: a 3-team XOX 5x5 with 3 in a row for a Genç group whose sizes are only 3x3 or 4x4.

Overlap: Kovan duplicates any separate Beehive or Kelime Oyunu candidate (the qa type description already names Beehive and Kelime Oyunu). The team tile board overlaps with the existing /sinif-oyunu Baamboozle board.
fixes: Add a choral or whole-class production step to EVERY correct resolve in Oyun Parkı and Arena, not just to failures. After a claim, the class says the model answer once ('Say it: I like bananas!'), and at A2+ the model is a full frame sentence, not a single word. Make 'Say 2 things' / 'Say it in a sentence' cells at least 1 in 3 at A2 Genç and above.

Show strategy frames at every level, with pictograms and read-aloud for kids: A1 Genç gets 'Here!' / 'Block!' / 'Centre!'; A2 gets 'Let's go here.'; B1+ keeps the full frames. The Captain must say the cell in English ('B2!' / 'Column 4!' / 'The panda square!') before the teacher clicks.
For Oyun Parkı replace Bee Garden with a linear 'Honey Path' (a 3-lane race of about 6 flowers, or a 3x4 square path), or drop hexes for kids altogether. Keep hex Kovan for Arena and Stüdyo only.

Kovan letter pool: English A-Z only (strip Turkish characters in the validator and reject answers containing them). For A1-A2 Genç, restrict letters to those whose English sound matches the Turkish letter (B, D, F, K, L, M, N, P, R, S, T) and always play the English letter name plus a sample sound as audio.

Split the B2 Kovan: idiom initials for adults only. B2 Genç uses word-family or phrasal-verb first letters on concrete topics ('Starts with G: to stop doing something' for give up) and passes teenSafe.

Derive difficulty tiers from measurable signals, not LLM labels: the CEFR band of the answer from words.js, the item type (recognition 1 star, gap 2 stars, production 3 stars) and the whyOpt error type. For grammar_mcq packs, assign tiers by task type (MCQ, then gap, then Fix-it or Make-a-sentence built from the same item) rather than inventing difficulty. The lesson-fit timer caps Dörtle! Klasik at packs with 56 or more unique items, and falls back to Kısa 6x5 or XOX when a teacher prompt yields fewer.

Gate Form and Sentence columns by a grammar whitelist per group and MEB grade (no past forms before the grammar profile allows them). Sentence columns at B1 Genç always show a sentence starter plus a model example on Reveal.

Adult A1 visuals: use a separate adult icon or photo set and plain-label faces; never mascot-style SVG in Stüdyo. The A1 adult Kovan clue stays at 10 words or fewer with picture support, but in a neutral style.
Make the tiebreak linguistic: a 'fastest correct sentence' or a 'spell it' letter round at the current level instead of a numeric estimate.

Ship in phases: v1 is XOX (all audiences) plus Dörtle! Kısa/Drop 3. Kovan comes later, or merges into a dedicated Beehive/Kelime Oyunu game if one exists. Lock size presets per audience (Oyun Parkı: 3x3 and Drop 3 only; 3 teams only for Arena and Stüdyo).

Give every kids' cell an imageKey plus audio (already required) AND make the A-D response cards picture-based, so an A1 child who cannot read the options can still respond; the option delay alone does not help non-readers.

issues: This is not just an MCQ quiz with a skin. Choosing where to play (blocking, forking, the gravity in Connect Four, connecting in the hive) is a real game layer. But the XOX board is structurally the existing /sinif-oyunu Baamboozle tile board plus a line-win check. Built as a separate codebase it duplicates the tile grid, question card, team bar, judging and undo in game-classroom.mjs.

The size is marked L but the spec is XL. It has 3 topologies x 3 audience skins = 9 visual boards. On top of that come 4-team parallel boards, Buzz mode, Overwrite, wagers, power nodes, a golden egg, Altın Koşu, a time-lapse replay, sentence-column refresh, a lesson-fit timer, an ownership ritual, Gogo's animations (sit, peek, dance, sleep, parachute) and about 40 teacher settings. Shipping all of it in v1 is the main risk to polish: everything would come out 70% finished.

Kovan (Beehive) is a separate game in all but name. It needs a hex renderer, hex hit-testing, BFS connection, letter-pool generation, a first-letter and initials validator and a separate picture-phonics mode, and its content is not shared with XOX or Dörtle! (the items must match a letter). The qa type list already names Beehive and Kelime Oyunu, so another candidate probably covers it. 'Same content, three boards' is not actually true for Kovan.

The wrong-answer rules are not defined for a gravity board. Locking or napping a Dörtle! cell blocks the whole column. A steal in Connect Four puts the stealing team's disc in a slot it did not choose, and that can hurt the stealer. 'A fresh item from spares' for a slot that the ladder places in a given tier needs a spare in that same tier.

Difficulty tiers (1-3 stars, the centre cell, the row ladder) cannot come from the LLM's own difficulty labels, because they are unreliable. Without a deterministic signal the 3-star centre is just flavour.

Load on the LLM: Dörtle! Klasik needs about 56 tiered items plus 7 labels, and XOX 5x5 needs 50. DeepSeek JSON at that size will often come back truncated or with duplicates, and some rules cannot be validated automatically: 'a clue is not guessable from its letter alone', 'the face does not give away the answer', 'the gap distractor is really wrong'.

Input: the numpad is missing on most school laptops and on smartboard PCs (the MEB etkileşimli tahta has no keyboard in use). Right-click to assign a cell manually does not exist on touch. Two side-by-side 7x6 boards with 4 teams cannot be read on a projector at a 5vh label floor.

Arena runs two scoring systems at once: lines win the board while points, combo and hint costs run in parallel. 12-14s will argue about which one counts. Stüdyo adds negative marking, wagers and Overwrite on top, which is too much rule text for a 10-minute filler.

Classic 3x3 tic-tac-toe is solved, and competent 12+ players will draw almost every time unless wrong answers break the pattern. Kids' boards rely on 'Friends board', which is fine, but Arena 3x3 or 4x4 with 3 in a row has a known first-move advantage.
Kids' Kovan: Hex-style connection is hard for 9-year-olds to read, and first-move advantage in Hex is severe. Banning the centre only partly helps.

Asset dependency: picture faces on every kids' square and the A1 Genç picture-phonics hive need a large self-hosted SVG picture set (300+ concrete nouns with imageKeys) that does not exist yet. This is a cross-suite blocker, not a cost of this game alone. Gogo needs a set of animated poses.

The shadow answer and the whole-class TPR are not captured by the software. They only work if the teacher enforces them, so the 'whole-class response every turn' checklist item is a promise the UI makes but cannot check.
fixes: Build it as a new board mode on the existing /sinif-oyunu engine: one parametric board module (rows, cols, win, gravity, topology) that reuses the question card, the judging (tick/cross, Reveal), undo and the team bar from game-classroom.mjs. Do not fork a second tile-quiz codebase.

Phase the build. v1: XOX (3x3, 4x4, 5x5) and Dörtle! (Drop 3 5x4, Kısa 6x5, Klasik 7x6), 2 teams, 3 skins, lock/steal/pass, undo, threat glow, BLOCKED!/FORK!, a self-drawing win line, best of 3, and a 'Kaçırılanlar' export. v1.1: 3-team XOX and Kovan. Cut or defer 4-team parallel boards, Buzz, wagers, power nodes, the golden egg, Altın Koşu, the time-lapse and the ownership ritual.

Move Kovan to the Beehive / Kelime Oyunu candidate, or build it as a separate preset with its own content pipeline (a letter-constrained qa generator). Change the claim 'same content, three boards' to 'same content, two boards (XOX and Dörtle!)'.

Specify the Dörtle! wrong-answer rule: no disc and the turn passes, and the column never locks. The steal is optional: the other team may decline or place its disc in that slot. Spares are keyed by tier, and a refill takes a spare from the landing slot's tier.

Set difficulty tiers deterministically: the curated grammar_mcq bank order or tags, the words.js CEFR band (e.g. A1 word = 1 star, A2 = 2, B1 = 3 at A2 level), and for LLM packs the word-band of the answer checked against words.js. Ask the LLM for a flat item pool only. Code places the items into cells, columns and tiers.

For LLM generation: request 1.3x the needed items in chunked calls of 20 or fewer. Validate with deterministic checks: schema, answer not in clue (with stem/lemma matching against words.js families), no duplicate answers, word caps, label of 2 words or fewer, and exactly one option equal to the key. Do a cheap second LLM pass only for 'is this distractor also correct?'. Drop failing items and top up from built-in banks rather than regenerating the whole pack.

Make touch the primary input: big tap targets, a long-press menu in place of right-click, and on-screen column arrows for Dörtle!. Keep the numpad and keys as extras, and add a digit-row fallback (1-9 for 3x3). Allow 4 teams only on XOX 3x3 or Drop 3 (two small boards), or use 4 teams on one 5x5 board with 3 in a row.

Give Arena one visible score that decides the winner: lines win the board, and points appear only in end-of-series stat awards. Hide combo maths behind the commentator strip. Put the Stüdyo options (Overwrite, wager, negative marking) behind an 'İleri kurallar' drawer and leave them off by default.
Offer three presets (Hızlı 5 dk / Standart / Turnuva) on the setup screen, with advanced dials collapsed. The class profile carries the rest.

Make the art and sound cheap and polished: draw discs, stamps, neon tiles and ink strokes procedurally in SVG or canvas; synthesise marimba, synth blips and woodblock in WebAudio (no audio files); use Gogo as 3-4 static SVG poses with CSS transforms. Share one reduced-motion path.
For kids' faces, gate picture mode on imageKey coverage and fall back to big icon plus word cards when the picture set is missing, so the game does not block on the shared SVG library.

Show a big 'Herkes göstersin!' (A/B/C/D cards / TPR pictogram) beat with a 3 s countdown before the Speaker answers, and optionally a tally button for how many hands were right. The whole-class moment is then part of the UI flow and not only a rule on paper.

At Arena and above, avoid the draw-prone 3x3 with 3 in a row: default to 4x4 with 3 in a row plus a blocked-corners rule, or 5x5 with 4 in a row, and keep 3x3 only for kids and the adult 5-minute warmer.

catalog.rankReason: XOX / Connect Four / Blockbusters: a strategy layer on top of the questions, and cheap as a board mode on c01's shell. Every claim needs a production step, and English strategy frames are shown at every level ('Here!', 'Block!'). v1: XOX and Dörtle! only, 2 teams, and a fair 'Bitir' button.

catalog.name: Takım Sırası (Sort & Order Relay)
catalog.familiarAs: Wordwall Group Sort / Rank Order / Unjumble, played as a team relay to the board
catalog.oneLiner: Teams send one runner at a time to the board. Each runner makes a single move: drop a card into the right group, couple a word into the sentence, or slot an item into a ranked line. The heat ends when the puzzle is solved, and only accuracy scores, never speed.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (about 1 min, teacher). Pick the group chip and a topic (built-in, a grammar unit or a free prompt). Build a match of up to 3 LEGS, each in one mode:
- SORT: cards go into 2-4 bins.
- BUILD: unjumble a sentence, a dialogue or (at B2) a paragraph.
- RANK: put events or process steps in sequence, or order a scale such as never to always.
- OPEN RANK (B1 and up): a reasoned ranking with no answer key.
Then choose the format:
- 'Sıralı Bayrak' (Turn Relay, the default): 2-6 teams share one board.
- 'Kulvar Yarışı' (Lane Race): 2 teams side by side. It needs a touch board such as a FATİH interactive board, or a second operator.
- 'Seslen' (Caller mode): for rooms with no touch board.
The lesson-fit timer sizes the heats. Put a tape line on the floor about 1.5 m from the board. Team members count off seat numbers 1-8, and each team gets a physical baton (a board marker, a soft toy, or the printable paper Gogo baton).

EACH HEAT
1. REVEAL. The bins or slots appear first with their labels (options delay: kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s). Then the numbered cards drop into the pool. Every move can be called out by voice, because:
   - every card has a number badge;
   - every bin has a letter plus a colour plus a shape (A red circle, B blue square, C yellow triangle, D green star), matching the printed A-D cards;
   - every sentence slot has a number.
2. TEAM TALK (kids 10 s, Arena 15 s, adults 20 s), then 'Boards up!'. Optional DESK DRAFT: each team pre-solves with printed strips of the same cards, or writes an order such as '3-1-4-2' on a mini-whiteboard. This way the whole team works, not only the runner.
3. RELAY MOVE. The screen shows 'Runner #3' in the active team's colour. The seat rotation starts from the spinner, and no names are ever shown. The runner takes the baton, walks up and makes ONE move:
   - The default is tap-tap (tap the card, then tap where it goes), because drags misfire on classroom boards. Dragging also works.
   - In Caller mode the runner stands at the line and calls the move ('Seven to B!', 'Word four goes first!'). The teacher types '7B' or '4-1', or taps.
   - In Stüdyo a runner may make one move OR one fix (moving a card that is already placed).
   The runner then hands the baton to the next seat number.
4. WHOLE-CLASS MOMENT, before the move locks:
   - Kids: everyone points to the bin, or holds up the matching colour card (TPR: left arm for A, right arm for B) on Gogo's 'Three, two, one, point!'.
   - Arena: the waiting teams flash their prediction on mini-whiteboards ('Scout' +1 when right, at most 3 per heat).
   - Stüdyo: each waiting team may call 'Objection!' once per heat.
5. CHECK.
   - INSTANT CHECK (default for kids and Arena). A right move snaps into place with a sound, earns points, and the card gets a corner in the team's colour. A wrong card tries the bin and rolls gently back to the pool with a soft 'boing'.
     - Kids: the same runner tries again with a hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo places the card and says it, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star.
     - Arena: the streak breaks and the card becomes a REBOUND. The next team's runner may place it for 1 point. The first team loses nothing.
   - CHECK AT THE END (default for Stüdyo). There is no feedback per move. When every card is placed, the team presses 'Kontrol'. The board shows only how many are correct ('9/12'), Mastermind-style, not which ones. Each runner then gets one fix, and the reveal marks every wrong card with its one-line why (whyTr or hintTr).
6. COMPLETION.
   - A finished sentence is read aloud by TTS with a word-by-word highlight, and the class echoes it (kids say it twice).
   - A finished sort reads out the bin contents.
   - A finished rank lights up its scale bar.
7. The heat ends when every card is placed or the heat cap runs out. A different team opens the next heat. The trailing team picks the next topic (Comeback: Light).

HOW THE FORMATS SHARE THE SCREEN
- TURN RELAY: SORT and RANK use one shared pool, and teams take turns placing one card each. BUILD gives each team its own track with a parallel sentence of the same pattern from the same unit. The active team's track grows large ('spotlight'), and the other tracks shrink to progress rows (at most 4 full tracks are visible).
- LANE RACE: both lanes hold the same content, shuffled differently, and both runners move at the same time. A shared 'baton beat' paces the swaps (Arena 10 s, adults 15 s, a calm 20 s chime for kids), so pace is never rewarded. The heat ends when both lanes are done. A lane that finishes early does an unscored 'Encore': it reads its sentences aloud.

SCORING (accuracy only; no speed points in any mode)
- Arena: 2 points for a first-try card, 1 for a rebound, +3 for completing the heat, +2 for a clean heat. Combo x1.5 after 3 clean moves in a row and x2 after 5. Hints cost 1-2 points, and the score never drops below 0.
- Stüdyo: 2 points for a first-try card, 1 after a fix. Optional -1 for a card still wrong at Kontrol. Optional 'Clean call' wager before a heat: +5 or -3.
- Kids: every correct card loads a crate or couples a carriage. Each heat earns 1-3 stars (3 stars = no help needed). The score never goes down.

GOLD CARD. One card per heat may be gold. Placing it correctly triggers a power at the class's harshness level:
- Green (kids): Gift 5, Everyone +2, Double, Shield, Brain break.
- Yellow (Arena, opt-in): Steal 5, capped at the other team's score.
- Red (adults, opt-in).

OPEN RANK (B1 and up)
1. Each student ranks the items alone on paper for 30 s.
2. The team agrees on one order during Team talk.
3. The spokesperson calls it out and the teacher enters it.
4. The board reveals every team's line, plus a class consensus calculated with a Borda count.
5. Each team gives one 'because' sentence using the starters.
6. The teacher awards 0-3 reason points from a checklist: a reason is given, a comparative or superlative is used, a useful phrase is used. The team furthest from the consensus gets a 'Maverick' mention.

ALTERNATIVE ORDERS
- Any order listed in alt[][] is accepted automatically. Identical tokens (for example two 'the') are interchangeable.
- 'Kabul' (key A) accepts an unlisted grammatical order for full points and saves it to the class pack.
- 'Tartış' freezes the game and shows both orders side by side for a 30 s class discussion.

TIEBREAK. Adults and Arena use one 'Intruder' card (an odd item), answered on whiteboards by all teams at once. Kids never tiebreak; the tied teams share the win.

ENDING. Titles and stickers for kids, a podium with stat awards for Arena, and full scores plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' review for adults. A rotation tracker makes sure every seat number runs before anyone runs twice.
catalog.playerSetup:
2-6 teams of 3-8 students (a class of 36 plays as 6 teams of 6). Pairs can act as teams in small classes (10 or fewer).
- Turn Relay: 2-6 teams on one shared board.
- Lane Race: exactly 2 teams. A class of 4 teams plays two back-to-back 2-team races, or switches to Turn Relay.
Each team gets a baton and seat numbers 1-8. The relay order follows the seat numbers, and the spinner picks the starting seat. Nobody is ever picked by name. Members who are not running have a job every turn: desk-drafting, predicting (Scout), judging (Objection), or joining the whole-class point or TPR.
Caller mode suits a classroom with a projector but no touch board, large classes (35+), or adults who prefer not to walk: the runner calls the move from the line or from their seat, and the teacher or a student 'operator' taps it in.
catalog.contentShape:
Code assembles HEATS from pack items. The LLM never picks the answer key.

SORT heat: {bins[2-4], cards[6-16], goldCard?, stowaway? (B2 only)}.
Bins come from one of two sources:
- (a) 2-4 category-list items. label, labelTr and media.emoji make the bin; the members become cards. Each bin gets at least 2 cards, and the bins are balanced.
- (b) A 'sorter' over other item types:
  - vocab: pos n/v/adj; form word/phrasal/idiom; syll 1/2/3; concrete vs abstract; family suffix -tion/-ment/-ness at B levels.
  - sound: ed-ending key /t/ /d/ /ɪd/; stress Oo/oO/ooO; rhyme; silent letter.
  - error: each item puts EITHER its wrong OR its right sentence into a Right/Wrong bin, never both in the same heat.
Validator:
- Every card fits exactly one bin. The LLM cross-checks this by asking 'which of these bins can X go in?', and cards that fit more than one bin are dropped (e.g. tomato fruit/veg, fish animal/food). The exception is the B2 Venn 'Both' bin.
- No card text gives away its bin.
- Every card stays within the group's word cap.
- In A1/A2 Genç every card needs media.img or media.emoji; unpicturable cards are dropped.

BUILD heat: an order item with kind 'sentence', 'dialogue' or 'events' (for the B2 paragraph build, the tokens are whole sentences with reference cues, as in G20).
- Fields: tokens[] in the correct order; alt[][] with every other valid order; chunked (teens get chunks such as 'every day' or 'a red ball'); hintTr; unit (e.g. a2-09).
- Code adds heuristic alternative candidates (a fronted time or place adverbial with a comma, 'also'/'too' positions, frequency adverb positions), and a second LLM pass verifies them by listing every grammatical order. Items with more than 4 valid orders are re-chunked or dropped.
- The engine normalises tokens so they give nothing away:
  - tokens are stored in lower case except 'I' and proper nouns;
  - whichever token lands first is capitalised automatically;
  - end punctuation is a fixed tile;
  - commas become tokens only from B1;
  - contractions stay one token;
  - the check compares strings, not token ids, so duplicate words are interchangeable;
  - the tokens must re-join into exactly the model sentence.

RANK heat: an order item. Sequences use kind 'events' or 'process' (daily routine, recipe, life story, a process). Scales are stored as kind 'process' with pack.frames.relay.scale {low, high, lowTr, highTr}, e.g. never to always, least to most polite. Ties are expressed through alt[][]. Text items give 'evidence chronology' (roadmap G10): the events come from a reading via textRef, and the reveal shows the evidence sentence.

OPEN RANK:
- a category-list with open:true (label = the criterion, e.g. 'Most useful on a desert island'; 5-6 members), plus
- a speaking-prompt in mode 'opinion' (starters, useful) for the 'because' sentence.
There is no key.

STIRRERS AND TIEBREAKS: odd items (items[4], odd, reasonTr, reasonEn at B levels).

ENVELOPE (computed by code): pack.frames.relay = {legs[{mode, heatIds[]}], scales{}, goldCardIds[]}.

BUILT-IN SOURCES:
- category-lists from YLE and MEB topics;
- BUILD sentences taken from the correct sentence of each grammar_mcq_a1..b2 item and tokenised, keeping the unit tag;
- vocab sorters from words.js (pos, IPA, syllables);
- idioms.js for B2 sorts by meaning;
- readings_*.js for event order.

PROMPT MODE: the teacher's Turkish prompt (e.g. '7. sınıf biyografi, geçmiş zaman') makes the LLM return order and category-list items with levels, and the same validators run on them.
catalog.teenVersion:
One content schema with two skins. The kids ruleset is stripped down, not the adult ruleset recoloured.

OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11, default for A1/A2 Genç): 'GOGO EXPRESS'

THEME. A train journey across a map. Gogo the parrot wears a conductor's cap and rides on the engine, and each heat is a station named after its topic ('Animal Station').
- SORT: load cargo into the right wagons (Farm wagon / Wild wagon). Crates plop in with a tiny bounce.
- BUILD: word carriages couple with a 'clack'. A finished sentence gets a short choo-choo, and the train puffs off to the next station.
- RANK: line up passengers on the platform (small to big, morning to night), with Gogo hopping up a ladder.

RULE CARD (read in 20 s in Turkish by the teacher, with pictograms):
1. Walk up with the baton and move ONE card.
2. Everyone points first!
3. Oops? Try again, and Gogo helps.

PLAY
- Check is instant, and tapping a card makes it speak at 0.8x.
- Timers are off by default. An optional 40 s calm ring never turns red, and a marimba chime sounds at 0.
- After 20 s a gentle 'move-along' glow shows the right bin. There is no penalty for it.
- A wrong card gets a soft boing, then a second try with a free hint (the bin wiggles, the first carriage locks, or the sentence is heard again). If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album.
- Scores are crates plus 1-3 stars per heat, and they never go down.
- Only Green powers exist: the Gold crate gives Everyone +2, Gift 5, Shield or Brain break.
- Lane Race becomes two trains on parallel tracks that pull into the station together.
- Nothing is ever eliminated, and there are no minus points and no losing imagery.

CONTENT. YLE and MEB topics: farm and wild animals, food, summer and winter clothes, toys, classroom objects, daily routine, can/can't, There is / There are.
- 2 bins (3 at A2) and 6-10 picture cards.
- Sentences of 3-5 words in 3-4 chunked carriages, with no commas.
- 3-4 picture items to rank.
- No Open Rank. Instead, an unscored 'Class Top 3' vote works as a settler.

PACING. 3 stations of 4-5 min each. Between them comes a 45 s stirrer or a 60 s settler:
- 'Human Sentence': 5 students hold printed A4 word cards at the front, and the class orders them.
- 'Four Corners Sort': everyone takes a card and walks to the bin corner.
- The settler: Gogo reads a sentence and the class draws it.
Total: 15-20 min.

ENDING. Every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Neat Sorters, Train Builders), and a station postcard sticker goes into the class album. Confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale.

ARENA (ages 12-14, default for B1/B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç class in grade 6+): 'CIRCUIT RELAY'

THEME. Dark navy with neon accents in the team colours, a condensed display font, and emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond). There are no animals and no mascot. In 10 s each team picks its emblem, colour and a 3-word motto.
- SORT: route data packets into ports.
- BUILD: 'compile' a code line. Tokens snap into a circuit that lights up end to end when the order is correct.
- RANK: a power bar for scales and a TIER LIST (S/A/B/C) for Open Rank.

PLAY
- A 10 s ring per move in the team colour.
- Streaks and combo (x1.5 after 3 in a row, x2 after 5; accuracy only).
- Scout predictions on mini-whiteboards, and rebound steals (the first team loses nothing).
- Hints: Anchor locks the first token (1 point). Split removes one wrong bin, or shows which half of the sentence a token belongs to (1 point). Ghost flashes the gapped sentence (2 points). The score never drops below 0.
- A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('CLEAN ROUTE', 'COMBO x3').
- The English rule card has a Turkish toggle.

CONTENT. Concrete, not abstract:
- MEB grade 7-8 style units: life events in the past simple for a biography, recipe steps for 'In the Kitchen', and sorting chores by 'I love / I don't mind / I hate'.
- Tier-list Open Ranks: best superpower, most useful invention, a survival kit for a space station.
- Everything passes the teenSafe filter.

NAZIK PROTECTIONS UNDERNEATH. No public last place, no names, a floor at zero, and Steal 5 only if the teacher opts in.

ENDING. A podium plus stat awards (Longest streak, Best scouts, Clean sheet, Comeback). 15-25 min.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1. Words per card: Genç 0-4, with a picture on every card; adults 10 or fewer.
- SORT: 2 concrete bins with 6-8 cards (animals, food; for adults: food / drink, a / an).
- BUILD: 3-5 tokens using SVO with be / have got / can. Kids get 3-4 chunked carriages, and each sentence has only one valid order.
- RANK: 3-4 items (size, times of day, routine).
- Hints are generous, and Kolay can pre-lock the first token.

A2. Words per card: Genç 8 or fewer, adults 15 or fewer.
- SORT: 3 bins with 9-12 cards (countable / uncountable, regular / irregular past, clothes by season, plural -s as /s/ /z/ /ɪz/).
- BUILD: 5-8 tokens, including do/does/did questions and a time phrase that can move to the front (listed in alt[][]), plus frequency adverbs.
- RANK: 4-5 items (never to always; story events with first / then / after that), plus 4-line dialogue order.

B1. Words per card: Genç 14 or fewer, adults 25 or fewer.
- SORT: 4 bins with abstract labels (linker function, make/do/take/have, -ed endings, formal vs informal, Right/Wrong sentences from error items).
- BUILD: 7-12 tokens covering present perfect, passive, relative clauses and adverb placement. Comma tokens appear, and several alternative orders are allowed.
- RANK: 5-6 items (certainty, politeness), plus event order from a reading with evidence.
- OPEN RANK starts here, with sentence starters.

B2. Words per card: Genç 20 or fewer, on concrete topics; adults 40 or fewer.
- SORT: 4 bins plus a Venn 'Both' bin and a stowaway card that fits no bin (gerund / infinitive with a change of meaning, idioms by meaning, fine register differences, word families).
- BUILD: 9-15 tokens with several clauses, inversion ('Not only did she...'), mixed conditionals and clefts, plus a paragraph build from 4-6 sentence tokens held together by reference words.
- RANK: fine-grained hedging scales and a reasoned ranking with a rubric.
- Adults default to Check at the end.

MIXED ABILITY. The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial changes, without changing the skin:
- the number of bins (-1 / 0 / +1);
- the number of tokens and how they are chunked;
- whether an anchor token is pre-locked;
- which hint rungs are available.
'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole pack by one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 5-30 (a single leg takes 5-8 min; a full match takes 15-20 min for kids, 15-25 min for Arena and 20-30 min for adults)
catalog.teacherControls:
The teacher chrome is in Turkish. Every dial is saved in the class profile.

BEFORE PLAY
- MATCH BUILDER: legs (Sort / Build / Rank / Open Rank / Karışık), heats per leg, a topic per leg (built-in, grammar unit or prompt), and the lesson-fit timer.
- FORMAT: Sıralı Bayrak, Kulvar Yarışı, or Seslen (Caller) mode.
- CHECK: Anında (instant) or Sonda Kontrol (check at the end). Moves per runner: 1, or 1 plus a fix.
- PACK PREVIEW: every heat with its key, with ambiguous or multi-bin items flagged, and one click to drop or regenerate an item.
- PRINT: Desk Draft strips for each team, A-D colour-and-shape cards, seat-number cards, and A4 word cards for 'Human Sentence'.

RULES AND DIALS
- TIMERS: a cap per move (off / 10 / 15 / 20 s), a heat cap, +10 s, T to pause, and 'Süresiz'.
- BOUNCE RULE: the same runner retries, the next runner takes it, or it rebounds to the next team.
- HINTS: each rung on or off, and a TR gloss toggle.
- EXTRAS: Gold cards on or off, the harshness level, the comeback dial, wagers and negative points.
- AUDIO: TTS speed with an 'Öğretmen okur' fallback, Gogo's voice on or off, sound and music volumes, and reduced motion.

LIVE CONTROLS
- ALTERNATIVE ORDERS: Kabul (key A) accepts an unlisted order and saves it to the class pack. Tartış freezes the game for a side-by-side comparison. The alt list can be edited in the preview.
- IN PLAY: undo (Z), skip a card, show the solution (S), reshuffle, move a card to the correct bin by hand, manual score adjustments, next runner, freeze.
- KEYBOARD CALLER: '7B Enter' sends card 7 to bin B, and '4-1' puts token 4 in slot 1. Arrow keys and Space (check) also work.
catalog.delightDetails:
KIDS (Gogo Express)
- Train carriages couple with a puff of steam.
- Crates plop in with a tiny squash-and-stretch.
- Gogo rides the engine roof in a conductor's cap and sleeps in the cab on the pause screen.
- Each station sign carries the topic.
- A ticket-punch sound closes each heat.
- Every station adds a postcard to the class album.

WHEN A SENTENCE IS COMPLETE (all skins)
- The words light up one by one in time with the TTS, like karaoke, and the class echoes the line.

ON THE BOARD (all skins)
- Every placed card keeps a small corner in its team's colour, so the recap credits who placed what.
- A 'ghost' outline shows where a tapped card will land.
- A wrong card rolls back gently instead of flashing red.
- The first word is capitalised automatically, so there is no giveaway.

ARENA (Circuit Relay)
- A correct code line 'compiles' with a glitch sweep of green light.
- The Open Rank tier list reveals every team's tiers side by side, followed by the class consensus.
- The runner's seat number appears on a jersey badge in the team emblem.

STÜDYO (Sort Desk)
- Type-block 'clack' sounds as tiles slide into the composing stick, and a letterpress 'print' marks a finished sentence.
- Folder tabs flip as cards are filed.
- The certainty scale is drawn as a thermometer gradient.

PERFECT HEAT
- Kids and Arena get a 'Perfect sort!' burst.
- Adults get a modest chime while the score rolls up.

ACROSS THE MATCH
- The end screen shows 'Everyone ran!' once each team's rotation is complete.
- The 'Human Sentence' and 'Four Corners Sort' stirrers reuse the printed cards, so the game spills off the screen and into the room.
catalog.risks:
- ONLY ONE STUDENT MOVES AT A TIME. Mitigations: Desk Draft strips, a whole-class point or TPR, Scout whiteboards and Objection, one move per runner, a 10 s cap in Arena, at most 6-8 per team, a rotation tracker so everyone runs, and physical stirrers.
- MORE THAN ONE ORDER IS VALID IN UNJUMBLES. Arguments are avoided by: alt[][] from heuristics plus an LLM verification pass; dropping or re-chunking items with more than 4 valid orders; interchangeable duplicate tokens; neutralising the capital-letter and full-stop giveaways; and the Kabul and Tartış buttons.
- SORT CARDS THAT FIT TWO BINS (tomato, fish). The single-bin validator catches them, and the teacher can fix one live. Overlap is allowed only in the B2 Venn bin.
- UNRELIABLE TOUCH BOARDS (FATİH calibration drift, dropped drags). Tap-tap is the default, hit areas are big, lanes are separate touch zones, and Caller mode is the fallback.
- CLASSROOM SAFETY AND NOISE. A tape line, a walking-only rule, a baton handoff at the line, and Caller-from-seat for classes of 35+.
- LANE RACE LEAVES OTHER TEAMS IDLE. It is limited to 2 teams; larger classes use Turn Relay.
- A PULL TOWARDS SPEED. There are no speed points by design, and the baton beat paces both lanes.
- LONG B2 SENTENCES ON A PROJECTOR. Font floors, a spotlight track, at most 4 visible tracks, and splitting items that are too long.
- SUBJECTIVE OPEN RANK SCORES. A rubric checklist capped at 3 points, so it rarely decides the match.
- LLM TOKENISATION ERRORS. The validator checks that the tokens re-join into the model sentence and stay within the word caps.

reviewVerdicts: feasibility: keep-with-changes -> Any separate Wordwall-style 'Group Sort', 'Unjumble' or 'Rank Order' candidate, and the 'Human Sentence' / 'Four Corners' stirrers. This game should be the suite's one sort-and-order engine. Open Rank should move to a speaking or opinion game (e.g. a WYR or tier-list candidate).

issues: SETUP IS NOT 1 MINUTE. Setup covers counting off seat numbers 1-8, forming 4-6 teams, handing out batons, taping a floor line, and handing out printed Desk Draft strips and A-D cards, which need a printer the day before (scarce in Turkish public schools). The first session realistically costs 6-10 minutes before the first heat. Every later session costs 3-4 minutes unless the class profile remembers the teams.

THE MOVE CYCLE IS SLOW. The spec is unclear whether Team talk happens once per heat or before every move. If it is per move, each kids' move takes about 45-60 s: 10 s talk, 3-2-1 point, walk, tap-tap, check, retry with hint, Gogo repeat, baton handoff. An 8-card sort is then 6-8 minutes, not the stated 4-5 minutes per station. The 15-20 minute kids' match would overrun to roughly 30 minutes.

THE RUNNER BLOCKS THE SCREEN. On a FATİH board, the student at the board stands in front of the pool and bins. Twenty-seven classmates cannot see what they are meant to point at or predict, which breaks the whole-class moment and Scout.

SHORT CHILDREN CANNOT REACH THE TOP OF THE BOARD. A 9-year-old cannot reach the upper third of a wall-mounted board. Bins or slots at the top are untappable. The teacher ends up lifting children or tapping for them, which kills the relay.

THE RUNNER IS ONLY A COURIER. Team talk and desk drafts happen before the move, so the strongest student decides and the runner carries the answer. Teammates also shout the answer across the room. The noise spikes every turn, and a weak runner learns nothing. The rotation guarantees equal walking, not equal thinking.

POINTING GIVES THE ANSWER AWAY. If the class points before the move locks, the runner (and in Arena, the rebound team) can copy the majority. If the runner moves first, the point comes after the answer is visible and means nothing. The order of steps 3-4 is ambiguous.

THE SHARED SORT POOL IS UNFAIR. Late placements are easier by elimination, and the last card is forced. With 6 teams each team places only 1-2 cards per heat, so the card a team happens to draw decides the heat. Fixed team order by heat also rotates who gets the forced card, so luck dominates.

BUILD IN TURN RELAY IS UNFAIR AND CONFUSING. Each team gets its own parallel sentence, and sentences of the same pattern still differ in difficulty. With 6 teams only 4 tracks are visible, so two teams cannot see their own progress. Children also lose the thread of their sentence while 5 other teams take turns between their moves.

CHECK AT THE END DOES NOT WORK ON A SHARED BOARD. A team presses 'Kontrol', but the pool is shared across teams. It is unclear whose '9/12' this is, and each runner fixing one card in turn stretches the heat. For 10 adults on a projector, walking to the board for one card each feels juvenile. Most adult classes will want Desk Relay (Caller mode), so the walking relay is wasted design for them.

THE TEACHER HAS TOO MUCH TO TRACK. In one Arena turn the teacher has to: watch the runner, check 5 whiteboards for Scout (+1, capped at 3), track combo, handle a rebound, a Gold card power, Objection, and Kabul or Tartış, all while typing '7B' in Caller mode. Standing at a board with 28 kids, the teacher will stop using Scout within five minutes, and its points become arbitrary.

LANE RACE IS FRAGILE. Two children tap one board at once. FATİH multitouch zones often misfire, and the two runners jostle each other. Everyone else is idle. It is exactly the chaos-prone mode, and it adds build size for a niche case.

STOPPING MID-HEAT IS UNDEFINED. When the bell rings mid-heat, the spec says nothing about partial credit or about crediting teams that have not had their turn. Kids at a tie share the win, but a mid-heat stop can leave one team a turn short.

THERE ARE TOO MANY OPTIONS. The build combines 4 leg modes, 3 formats, 3 skins, 2 check modes, 3 bounce rules, gold harshness, wagers, negative points, Scout, Objection and Open Rank. The match builder will overwhelm a teacher the first time, and a size-L build risks shipping everything half-polished.

OPEN RANK IS SLOW. It takes 30 s of solo ranking, then team talk, then each team calling its order out while the teacher enters 5-6 teams' orders, then 'because' sentences and rubric scoring. That is about 6-8 minutes of mostly teacher typing, and the scores are subjective.

PHYSICAL SAFETY AND NOISE. Batons get thrown, runners sprint despite 'no speed points' because kids race anyway, and the tape line gets ignored. Six teams cheering create noise the other classes will hear, and a Turkish public-school teacher will get complaints.
fixes: Pin down the turn cycle. Team talk happens ONCE per heat, where the team plans the whole heat with the desk strip. Each move is then capped at about 20 s with no per-move talk. The order is: whole-class point (all non-active teams) → runner taps → reveal. The active team's runner cannot see the point because the point happens with eyes on the teacher, or skip the point for the active team.

Lay the board out for classroom reach and sightlines. Every touch target (pool and bins or slots) sits in the bottom 55% of the screen, reachable by a 130 cm child. Labels and the enlarged 'current move' mirror sit at the top so the class can see over the runner. Add a 'runner stands to the side' tap strip at the board edge.

Make Caller-from-seat the default everywhere except small kids' classes. Walking becomes an optional 'Bayrak' flavour. Adults default to Desk Relay with the teacher or a student operator. This removes the safety issue, the occlusion and the reach problem.

Rebalance the shared sort. Each team gets its own dealt hand of cards of equal count and similar difficulty, shown in its colour, instead of one open pool. The last forced card auto-places unscored. Alternatively, run SORT as 'every team answers on whiteboards, one runner places', so all teams score every card.

For BUILD with more than 3 teams, use ONE shared sentence per heat. The teams take turns adding tokens, and every placement is visible. Otherwise cap Turn Relay BUILD at 4 teams, so no track is ever hidden.

In Stüdyo, drop per-team Kontrol on a shared pool. Either each team has its own board (sequential heats, one team per heat, all teams on the same content with reshuffled order), or Kontrol is class-wide, with points credited per corner colour.

Cut the teacher's live load. Scout, Objection, wagers, combo and Gold are OFF by default, and a 'Basit' preset is the default: instant check, one bounce rule, stars or points only. The side mechanics become 'Ekstra' toggles. Scout gets a single tap per team ('Tahmin doğru: A C D') instead of per-whiteboard judgment.
Drop Lane Race from v1, or restrict it to 'second operator present'. It adds chaos and idle time for little gain.

Add 'Şimdi bitir' (end now). It finishes the current round so every team has had an equal number of moves, auto-completes the remaining cards as a class read-aloud, and shows final standings. Pair it with a lesson-end timer warning at T-3 min that stops new heats from starting.

Add a realistic setup path. Offer a 'no print' mode (on-screen only, whiteboards optional) and an auto team maker from class size that is saved in the class profile. The teams, seat numbers and batons from last lesson are remembered, so the second session starts in under 1 minute.
Size heats against real timing. Kids: 6 cards per sort, 3-4 carriages. Heat estimate = cards × 30 s, shown in the builder, which warns when the match exceeds the lesson-fit time.
Simplify Open Rank. The teacher enters only the top 1 and bottom 1 per team (2 taps), not full orders. The consensus is shown from that, and reason points become a single +1 'good because' button.

Make the noise rule concrete. Add a 'quiet signal' key (a bell sound plus a freeze screen). The team that stays quiet during another team's turn earns a crate or star in the kids' skin. This rewards non-active behaviour.

issues: Sort, unjumble and rank are mostly RECOGNITION tasks. Caller mode makes the spoken output worse: 'Seven to B!' and '4-1' are codes, not English. Across a 20-minute match the only real production is the echo after TTS and one 'because' sentence in Open Rank (B1 and up). A1-A2 adults and most kids produce almost no English of their own.

Turn Relay SORT uses a shared pool the runner picks from freely. Early runners take the easy cards, and the last 1-2 cards in each bin can be solved by elimination. With 6 teams on 12 cards that is 2 moves per team, so the heat measures card luck, not language. Accuracy-only scoring does not fix this.

Turn Relay BUILD gives one token per runner per visit, and each team has its own sentence. A 7-token B1 sentence with 6 teams takes about 42 walks. With 20 s of team talk per turn, one heat becomes 10+ minutes, so the pacing numbers (15-25 min for 3 legs) do not hold at B1/B2 or with 5-6 teams. Moving one token also breaks the sentence into meaningless pieces for learners, because nobody holds the whole utterance.

A1 Genç learners who barely read: SORT with pictures works. BUILD does not, even as 3-4 chunked carriages, because 'a red ball' / 'I have got' cannot be pictured, and tap-to-hear on the board helps only the runner, not the team at their desks. RANK of 'morning to night' pictures is fine. BUILD should not be a default leg for A1 Genç.

The kids rule card claims 3 rules, but the real procedure has baton, seat numbers, spinner start, tape line, a whole-class point, the TPR arm mapping, desk drafts, effort stars, gold crates, a 20 s glow, a second try, repeat twice, and stirrers. It fails the spirit of the 20-second checklist for the TEACHER, who has to run all of it. The TPR arm mapping (left = A, right = B) also breaks at A2, where there are 3 bins.

Sound sorting (/t/ /d/ /ɪd/, stress Oo/oO) is listed as a vocab sorter without an age gate. For 9-11-year-olds and A1-A2 adults, IPA-labelled bins are abstract. Kids need clap-syllable or rhyme bins with audio on every card, not IPA symbols.

In Stüdyo, 'Check at the end' is unclear in Turn Relay, where several teams share one SORT pool: whose 9/12 is shown by Kontrol, and who gets the fix? Mastermind feedback only makes sense per team board (Lane Race or per-team tracks).

Adult fit: walking a baton to the board is the babyish-for-adults risk (some Turkish adult classes and corporate groups will refuse). Desk Relay exists, but it is described as an alternative, not the Stüdyo default.

Built-in BUILD sentences taken from grammar_mcq correct answers are often context-dependent (dialogue fragments, 'Yes, I do.') or depend on the stem. Many are short answers or contain the gapped structure only once, so a large share won't make good unjumbles. The claim that these sources are enough is unverified.

Scale RANK (politeness, certainty, adjective strength) is partly subjective even at B2: is 'great' weaker than 'amazing' for everyone? Ties via alt[][] help, but LLM-generated scales will often include contested middle items.

Prompt mode for A1/A2 Genç requires media.img or media.emoji on every card. Emoji cover concrete nouns only. A Turkish prompt like '5. sınıf daily routine / can-can't' will produce many cards that cannot be pictured and get dropped, so packs come out too thin. Nothing tells the teacher this before generation.

Level-dial coverage is otherwise good (word caps, token counts, bin counts, comma tokens only from B1, B2 Venn and stowaway), but the B2 paragraph build with sentence tokens puts a heavy reading load on a projector for B2 Genç (13-year-olds). It should stay adult-only or be optional for teens.
fixes: Replace code calls with a language call. In Caller mode and at every placement, the runner must say the content: 'Tiger goes in Wild', 'Cheese is uncountable', or read the built chunk aloud. The number+letter code stays only as the teacher's input shortcut. Add a 'say it to place it' toggle, ON by default for A2 and up, and ask for a because clause at B1 and up ('..., because it shows contrast').

In Turn Relay SORT, DEAL cards instead of letting runners pick. The spinner or the engine assigns a card per runner, balanced by difficulty, and the last card in any bin is never dealt as a forced move (keep a stowaway or a distractor in the pool at A2 and up). This removes elimination solving and card luck.

Change BUILD in Turn Relay to one visit = one whole chunk sequence, or the complete sentence prepared at the desk (the runner brings the desk-draft order and places it all, then reads it aloud). Keep token-by-token only for Lane Race with 2 teams. Recalculate the heat time with an explicit formula and cap it (for example, BUILD heats at most 4 teams in Turn Relay).

For A1 Genç, drop BUILD from the default legs (SORT + RANK only). Allow BUILD from A2 Genç, with audio for the whole sentence played to the class first ('listen, then build'), so it is a listening-to-order task rather than reading.

Collapse the kids procedure into a teacher-facing 'Kolay kurulum' preset: no seat-number cards, baton optional, no desk draft, TPR pointing to coloured shapes on the board instead of arm mapping (works for 2-4 bins). Keep effort stars and hide gold crates by default. Test it with a 1-page Turkish teacher cheat-sheet.

Age-gate sound sorters: kids only get syllable-clap (1/2/3 claps) and rhyme bins with audio on every card, and bins labelled with example words and icons, not IPA. /t/ /d/ /ɪd/ and stress patterns only from A2 adults and B1 Genç, and always with audio.

In Stüdyo, restrict 'Check at the end' to formats where each team owns a board (per-team BUILD tracks, Lane Race). For a shared SORT pool, use a delayed per-card reveal at the end of each round instead.
Make 'Desk Relay' (Caller from seats, rotating spokesperson) the Stüdyo DEFAULT. Keep walking relay opt-in for adults.

Filter the grammar_mcq BUILD source with code: keep only full declarative or question sentences of at least N tokens with no dialogue dependency, and tag the rest as unusable. Report the actual yield per unit in the pack preview, and top up with LLM items when the yield is low.

For scale RANK items, require an LLM plus heuristic 'contested pair' check. Any adjacent pair the second pass cannot order confidently becomes a tie in alt[][] or is dropped. Show teachers a 'tartışmalı' flag in the preview.

Before generation for A1/A2 Genç, steer the prompt to picturable content ('Bu seviyede yalnızca resmedilebilir kelimeler kullanılır') and ask the LLM to return an emoji or icon key per card. If fewer than the minimum cards survive, auto-switch the leg to RANK or suggest a built-in YLE category.
Keep the B2 paragraph build for adults (Stüdyo). For B2 Genç use a 3-4 sentence mini-story at most 12 words per sentence, with reference words highlighted.

reviews.mergeWith: Any separate Wordwall-style 'Group Sort', 'Unjumble' or 'Rank Order' candidate, and the 'Human Sentence' / 'Four Corners' stirrers. This game should be the suite's one sort-and-order engine. Open Rank should move to a speaking or opinion game (e.g. a WYR or tier-list candidate).
issues: Scope is XL, not L. It has 4 leg modes (Sort, Build, Rank, Open Rank), 3 formats (Turn Relay, Lane Race, Caller), 2 check modes, 3 skins, each with its own metaphor for every mode (train/wagons/platform, packets/compiler/power bar, folders/composing stick/thermometer), plus Gold cards, Scout, Objection, wagers, Kabul/Tartış and a rotation tracker. That makes about 9 bespoke scene treatments and a very large state machine. Expect the result to be half-polished in every mode instead of fully polished in any.

BUILD and RANK are the same engine (tokens into numbered slots), and SORT is a second engine (cards into bins). The design treats them as three games with three art metaphors per skin, which multiplies art and QA for no gameplay gain.

Check at the end on a shared Turn Relay pool is undefined. When several teams have each placed cards in one pool, which team presses Kontrol, who gets the fix moves, and how is a '9/12' count scored across teams? Mastermind-style feedback only works on a board one team owns.

BUILD in Turn Relay gives each team a 'parallel sentence of the same pattern'. With 6 teams that means 6 sentences of equal difficulty per heat. Neither the LLM nor the MCQ banks give reliably equal difficulty or length, so fairness complaints will follow. It also means up to 6 tracks competing for projector space.

Using the grammar_mcq banks as BUILD sources is weaker than it looks. MCQ correct sentences are often short gap frames, some carry context such as dialogue cues or names, and many have several valid orders (adverbials, time phrases). Automatic tokenising plus the alternative-order heuristics will produce a noticeable rate of disputable items.

Asking the LLM to 'list every grammatical order' is unreliable, because models both over-generate and under-generate permutations. With comma tokens from B1 and 9-15 tokens at B2, the valid-order space grows fast. Kabul/Tartış rescue the moment, but they cost class time and trust.

The single-bin validator for sorts ('which bins can X go in?') is also LLM-judged, so it inherits the same errors. Abstract B1 bins (linker function, register) are exactly where the model is overconfident. For example, 'however' vs 'although' both land in contrast, and 'Can you...?' can be neutral or informal.

The kids mode leans heavily on TTS (cards speak at 0.8x, karaoke read-aloud, Gogo lines). FATİH boards run Pardus/Linux Chromium, which often has NO Web Speech voices, and Windows boards vary. Without pre-rendered audio, the core Oyun Parkı loop breaks silently.

Lane Race needs two simultaneous tap-tap selections on one screen. That requires per-pointerId selection state and reliable multi-touch, and older FATİH IR frames often report one touch or ghost touches. The fallback, a second operator, sidelines the teacher.

Pacing is slow. Each move costs team talk (10-20 s), a walk (about 10 s), the whole-class point (5 s), the check or retry, and the handoff, so roughly 35-50 s per card. A 10-card kids station therefore takes 6-8 min, not 4-5, and a 12-card adult heat with 6 teams is about 8-10 min. The stated session times are optimistic. It is also unclear whether team talk happens once per move or once per heat.

There are too many side-rules for one screen and one teacher: Scout +1 capped at 3, Objection once per heat, rebound, combo x1.5/x2, hint costs, Gold powers, and wagers. The teacher must adjudicate whiteboard predictions live, and the UI has to show all of it without clutter.

Open Rank (Borda consensus, 0-3 rubric points awarded by the teacher, a Maverick mention) is a different game, a speaking and justification activity, bolted onto a relay engine. It doubles the UI states and the scoring paths.

Adults walking to the board in relay is a weaker fit. Most adult groups will choose Caller or Desk Relay, which turns the game into 'team calls a move, teacher types it'. That is a solid but ordinary format, so adultFit hinges on the Stüdyo look and the check-at-end deduction.

Asset load: a parrot mascot with states (riding, hopping, sleeping, pointing), train, wagons, crates, 8 animal team mascots, 6 Arena emblems, a self-hosted Andika-type font, a condensed display font, and about 15 SFX (clack, boing, choo-choo, ticket punch, marimba, woodblock, letterpress, glitch). All of it has to be made or licensed and kept small for an SSR page.
fixes: Build two engines only. (1) BINS: cards into 2-4 bins, plus an optional Both bin. (2) SLOTS: tokens into numbered slots, used by both BUILD and RANK, with an optional scale bar. Skin each engine once per audience with CSS variables and swappable SVG sprites (one train-wagon set, one neon set, one folder set). Do not draw bespoke art per mode.

MVP for v1: Turn Relay plus Caller (Seslen is just the keyboard input '7B' / '4-1' on the same board), Instant check for all skins, SORT plus BUILD plus RANK, Gold card with Green powers only, and the rotation tracker. Defer Lane Race, Objection, wagers, Scout scoring and Open Rank to v2. Move Open Rank to a separate opinion or tier-list game.

Make Check at the end available only where one team owns the board: Stüdyo BUILD tracks, or a 'Team Heat' variant where each heat belongs to a single team and the others Scout. In shared-pool sorts, always use instant check with per-card credit (the corner in the team colour already supports this).

Replace 'parallel sentence per team' with ONE shared sentence per heat that teams build token by token in relay (a runner adds or moves one token, and the team with the last correct placement gets the completion bonus). Or rotate heats so each team gets its own heat in turn. This removes the difficulty-parity problem and the track clutter.

Constrain generation instead of verifying after the fact. Prompt the LLM for sentences with ONE natural order (no fronted adverbials, no frequency adverbs at A1-A2 unless the unit targets them), and chunk movable adverbials into a single fixed tile. Then run deterministic checks: tokens re-join to the model, word caps, a CEFR band lookup against words.js, and no leaked capitals or punctuation. Use the LLM order pass only as a flagger that sends items to the Pack Preview for teacher approval, and cap B1 at 9 tokens and B2 at 12.

For sorts, prefer deterministic sorters wherever possible: pos, syllables and IPA from words.js, the -ed ending computed from the final phoneme, and regular/irregular from a verb list. Keep LLM category-lists for concrete YLE/MEB topics, and have Pack Preview visibly flag every LLM-judged abstract bin (register, linker function). Ship curated built-in banks for linkers, make/do/take/have and register rather than generating them.

Audio: pre-render TTS for built-in kids content at build time (small mp3/opus clips, or lazy-loaded per pack). For LLM packs, probe speechSynthesis.getVoices() on load and switch automatically to 'Öğretmen okur' with a big on-screen prompt when no English voice exists. Never make a core loop step depend on audio.

If Lane Race ships, lock each lane to its own screen half with independent pointer handlers keyed by pointerId, and let a physical keyboard or a second phone act as lane 2's input. Test on an IR-frame FATİH board before promising it.

Fix pacing. Hold team talk ONCE per heat (with desk-draft strips), then run the relay moves with a 10-15 s move cap. Size heats from the lesson-fit timer using a measured cost of about 30 s per move, and show 'kalan kart' so teachers can see the heat will end. Default kids stations to 6 cards.

Collapse the side-rules into one visible 'Bekleyen takımlar' job per skin: kids point, Arena Scout (the teacher taps who was right, auto-capped), adults Objection. Show exactly one of these at a time in the UI.

Add a real game layer so it isn't just 'Wordwall on a projector': a visible match track (the train map, the circuit board, the ledger) that advances per heat, the gold card, the per-team corner colours in the recap, and the 'Kaçırılanlar' export to the Material Maker. These are cheap and make it feel like a proper game.

Keep the Pack Preview and a single print sheet (desk strips plus A-D colour/shape cards plus seat numbers) in v1. They are cheap, they make the game classroom-proof, and the teacher who 'loves details' will value them most.

Budget assets explicitly: 1 mascot with 4 poses (SVG), 1 kit per skin of about 6 SVG pieces, 12 SFX (under 150 KB total, from a CC0 set), and 2 self-hosted fonts (subset Latin plus Turkish). Load skin assets lazily so the island stays under about 250 KB of JS/CSS before audio.

catalog.rankReason: Wordwall Group Sort / Unjumble / Rank Order as a relay, and the suite's one sort-and-order engine (BINS and SLOTS). Cards are dealt, not picked. Runners say the content ('Tiger goes in Wild'), not codes. Team talk happens once per heat, and touch targets sit in the bottom 55% of the board. Open Rank moves to c11.

catalog.name: Okuma Dedektifleri (Running Dictation Reading Relay)
catalog.familiarAs: Running dictation / reading race. It plays as a "case file" reading relay, with a no-print Flash mode and a dictogloss-style Radio mode.
catalog.oneLiner: A short levelled text is cut into 4-7 labelled "evidence cards" that are taped around the room or flashed on the projector. Teams relay the cards back from memory, then rebuild and order the text. Finally they answer the case questions from their own notes only, and they must prove each answer by naming the card and sentence it came from.
catalog.howItPlays:
0) SETUP (teacher, about 2 min before class). The setup screen shows one summary line, for example "B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · Duvar · 25 dk" or "A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Flaş · 20 dk", with a Değiştir link. The teacher picks a case in one of three ways: from the bank by level and topic, by typing a free prompt (Turkish is fine), or with "Kendi metnim" (paste any text; the app cuts it and drafts questions). The teacher then picks a mode:
- DUVAR (print): stations on the walls.
- FLAŞ (no print): the cards flash on the projector.
- RADYO: text-to-speech or "Öğretmen okur" reads each card, dictogloss-style.
If class size is over 32, or the teacher ticks "Sınıf dar / sıralar sabit", the app suggests Flaş. In Duvar mode the teacher prints:
- one A4 landscape station card per evidence card, with 2 copies of each above 30 students;
- one "Dava Defteri" rebuild sheet per team;
- double-sided answer cards (A-D on the front; the station symbols plus a "?" No-evidence card on the back);
- role badges and a rule poster.
Station cards go up far from the team tables, spread into corners so runners do not crowd, text facing the room. Each team gets a different START station so that traffic spreads.

1) BRIEFING (60-90 s). The rules appear with pictograms. The seat-number spinner picks each team's first Runner; the Writer and Checker(s) follow seat order, and nobody is ever picked by name. Optionally the teacher pre-teaches the glossary: up to 5 level+1 words, each with a picture and a speaker button. In Oyun Parkı, Gogo runs a 20-30 s practice round that does not score: a one-card mini case ("The cat is under the bed.") in which a cartoon runner reads, walks back and says it.

2) COLLECT / TOPLA (4-8 min, sized by the lesson-fit timer).
- DUVAR: the Runner walks to a station, reads the card (as often as they like), walks back and dictates it. The Writer writes it in the box on the Dava Defteri that carries that station's symbol. The Checker ticks the station on the tracker, checks spelling ("How do you spell 'caught'?") and says which card is still missing. After EVERY card the roles rotate (Runner to Writer, Writer to Checker, Checker to Runner), so everyone reads, speaks and writes. House rules: no pens or phones at the wall; speak only at your own table; one Runner out per team at a time; walk, don't run. The projector shows a calm timer, the station symbols and a rules strip.
- FLAŞ: before each card there is a 3-2-1 "Eyes!" countdown. The card shows for 4 s + 0.6 s per word (x1.5 for Genç, and the teacher can scale it from 0.75x to 1.5x). Only each team's "Eye" watches; Writers sit with their backs to the screen. Then comes a blank 20-30 s "Tell your team" window. The Eye rotates every card. Pass 2 re-shows all cards in a new order, and an optional pass 3 is a "Last look" at half the time.
- RADYO: each card is read twice at a slow pace (0.8x for kids). Teams note key words, then rebuild the text together.
When a team finishes, the teacher taps its badge ("bitti"). The first finisher does NOT get speed points. Instead it gets an early-finisher task: kids "Help Gogo: underline 3 clue words"; adults "Predict two questions the case will ask". The teacher's "Son 1 dakika" button starts a soft chime for everyone else.

3) ORDER / SIRALA (1-2 min). Card symbols are assigned in random order, so the reading order is a real task. Teams agree the order and write the code (for example C-A-E-B-D, or star-circle-heart-square for kids) on a mini-whiteboard. On "Boards up!" everyone reveals at once, and the projector slides the cards into the right order one by one.

4) PROOFREAD / KONTROL (2-3 min, optional). Teams pass their Dava Defteri to the next team along a swap chain the app shows. The projector reveals the original text card by card, with trap words underlined (silent letters, -ed, -s, doubled consonants, articles). Checkers circle the differences, and each team shows a hand band: 1 finger for 0-2 mistakes, 2 for 3-5, 3 for 6 or more. The teacher taps the bands. In digital mode (a team laptop or tablet with a join code, typed by the Writer only) a word-level diff replaces this step: capitals are ignored at A levels and UK/US spellings and contractions are accepted.

5) CASE QUESTIONS / DAVA SORULARI (5-8 min, 3-8 questions). THE TWIST: the original text is now hidden, so teams answer from their OWN notes, and accurate dictation pays off. Each question appears in text order by default, or as a grid of folder tabs from which the trailing team picks next (Comeback Light). The options appear after the options delay. After the huddle comes "Boards up!", and every team shows its A-D card at the same moment. At A levels, true/false questions use TPR (stand = True, sit = False). Open qa answers go on whiteboards and the teacher judges them against accept[]. The teacher taps each team's answer on a quick grid ("Hepsi aynı" then unmark exceptions) and reveals: correct = 2.
Then "Show the evidence!" Teams flip their answer card to the station symbol of the card that proves it (card-level evidence), or to "?" for a Not given item. At B1+ the rotating spokesperson also reads out the exact proof sentence. The teacher clicks that sentence in the full-text panel (magnifier cursor), and it lights up and is pinned to the question on the evidence board; +1 for every team that named it. If a team used the "Which card?" hint on that question, it cannot also take the evidence point.

6) FINAL TASK (2-3 min). A1-A2: pick the best title from 3 (one right, one too narrow, one wrong); kids pick "Which picture tells the case?". B1: write a headline of 6 words or fewer. B2: write a summary of 25 words or fewer. The teacher awards +1 to every valid entry and +2 to the best one; optionally the class votes, and a team cannot vote for itself. Adults can add a 30 s "Retell the case" by a spokesperson who must use 3 key words shown on screen, and an optional wager on the last question.

7) CASE CLOSED (1-2 min). The full text appears with every proof sentence highlighted and tied to its question with red string (the evidence board). A Turkish "why" appears for every item that half or more of the teams missed. A WANTED poster shows the most-misspelt word, with IPA and a speaker button, and the class spells it aloud together. The case-closed stamp plays, then the mode-specific ending (titles, podium or full scores), and the case is filed in the class album.

SCORING
- Stüdyo: answer 2, evidence +1, order 3, accuracy 3/2/1/0, headline 0-2, and optional negatives and wagers.
- Arena: the same base points plus a combo, with a floor at zero.
- Oyun Parkı: stamps and stars only, and a score never goes down.
There are no speed points in any mode.

HINT LADDER (reuses the station symbols)
- Kids (free): picture, then "Look at the star card!", then Gogo reads the proof sentence aloud.
- Arena (1 point each, floor 0): which card, then 50:50, then the first 3 words of the proof sentence.
- Stüdyo (1 point each): which exhibit, then a paraphrase clue, then the Turkish gloss of the key word. The Turkish gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.

TEACHER HOTKEYS: Space = next, T = pause, +10 s, Süresiz, E = evidence mode, R = re-flash a card.
catalog.playerSetup:
3-6 teams of 3-5 players (4 teams by default). The app suggests the team count from class size: 16-24 students gives 4 teams, 25-32 gives 5, and 33-40 gives 6, with 2 copies of every station card above 30 students.

Roles inside each team:
- Runner (Koşucu; called the "Eye" in Flash mode)
- Writer (Yazıcı)
- Checker(s) (Kontrolcü): tracks which cards are done, checks spelling and keeps the trip ticks.
Roles rotate after EVERY card, not every case, so no strong student dominates. In a 5-person team, two Runners alternate. The first Runner comes from the seat-number spinner, never by name. A student who cannot move keeps the Writer/Checker role, or the class plays Flash mode.

During the questions, the whole class responds at the same moment with printed A-D/symbol cards, TPR (A levels) or mini-whiteboards. At B1+ a rotating spokesperson reads the proof sentence and does the retell. Adults consult in pairs inside the team during the huddle.
catalog.contentShape:
One case is one "text" item plus 3-8 answerable items that point to it via textRef.

TEXT {id, type:'text', level, audience ('all'|'teen'|'adult'), teenSafe, topic, title, body, words (computed), sentences[] (computed; the splitter respects Mr./Dr./a.m./numbers/quotes), cards[] (computed by the cutter: {id, symbol, sentenceIdx[], words, imageKey (required at A1/A2 Genç), keyword (the gap word for the kids' gapped notebook, taken from words.js at or below the level)}), questionIds[], evidence {questionId: sentenceIndex | sentenceIndex[] | null (null = Not given)}, glossary[≤5] {en, tr, imageKey?}, twin? (B2 "Two witnesses": the id of the second text)}.

ORDER item: kind 'events'; tokens = the card ids in the correct order; alt[][] = other valid orders.

QUESTIONS
- mcq, fmt 'reading': textRef, options[3|4], answer, whyTr (90 chars or fewer), whyOpt[] (from the bank's per-option 'why'), whyEn (B groups), target ('detail'|'sequence'|'reference'|'inference'|'attitude'|'main-idea'|'vocab-in-context'|'tfng'). At B1+, True/False/Not given is an mcq with three fixed options; its evidence is null when the answer is Not given.
- tf, about 'text': used at A levels (TPR stand/sit).
- qa with textRef: short open answers, accept[1-6], teacherJudge for why-questions and summaries.
- speaking-prompt, mode 'story': the 30 s retell; starters ("The case is about...", "First...", "In the end..."); useful[] = 3-5 key words from the text.
Every question also stores paraphrase (bool). At B1+ it must paraphrase rather than copy the sentence (content-word overlap with the proof sentence at most 60%). Headline options are an mcq with target 'main-idea'.

CUTTER RULES
- The card word cap equals the group's text-load cap: A1 Genç 6, A2 Genç 10, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40.
- A sentence is split only if it is over the cap; then it is split at a comma or conjunction into two cards, never shrunk.
- Every card must hold the evidence for at least one question, and no card may hold more than two, so no card can be skipped.
- Symbols are assigned in random order, so symbol order is never reading order.
- The "Kısalt" step trims a bank text for kids: it keeps the first sentence plus the evidence sentences, up to the word target.

SOURCES
readings_a1..b2.js holds 37/37/37/30 texts in the shape {id, topic, title, text, questions[{q, options, a, why[]?}]}. A build script converts them: text becomes body, the questions become mcq items, and why becomes whyOpt. The evidence index is auto-guessed from the word overlap between (question + correct option) and each sentence, then confirmed once by the LLM. Low-confidence guesses are flagged for the teacher's "Kanıt düzenle" editor. B1/B2 Genç texts and the short A1/A2 Genç case files come from a curated teenSafe set plus the generator.

GENERATOR (free prompt)
Returns: title; a body within ±10% of the word target; questions with evidence sentence indices; glossary; 3 headline options; imageKeys for kids.

VALIDATOR
- Checks word and sentence caps.
- At least 90% of non-proper-noun tokens must be at or below the level band in words.js. Level+1 words go into the glossary, 5 at most.
