- Every evidence sentence must share a content word or a paraphrase with the answer.
- BLIND TEST: the LLM answers each question WITHOUT the text. Any question it gets right with high confidence is rewritten or dropped.
- Applies the teenSafe filter for Genç groups and enforces the per-card evidence rule.
One generation per case, cached in the class profile's "Dava arşivi", so the materials endpoint's rate limit holds.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: "CASE FILE" (an alternative skin is "NEWSROOM": teams are news desks, cards are wire reports, and the final task is the front-page headline).

LOOK AND SOUND. Editorial cream (or the dark "Karartılmış sınıf" theme). Manila folders; a typewriter face for headings only and system sans for all readable text. Stations are "EXHIBIT A-F". Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ("The Past Perfects", "Flat White"). No mascot and no voice lines, just a caption ("Case 2 · Technology"). The sound set is woodblock and piano, 1 s at most, and music is off.

CONTENT. Topics from the bank:
- A1 (~50 words): daily life, city, food, family.
- A2 (~90 words): travel, shopping, weekends, hobbies.
- B1 (~130 words): work, technology, health, education, environment, sport.
- B2 (~150-180 words): society, psychology, media, business, technology.
Adult life and work prompts work well ("a complaint email to a hotel", "a job-interview story").

MOVEMENT. Adults enjoy running dictation as a walk-and-talk energiser. Duvar is the default for up to 24 learners, and Flaş for crowded rooms. Radyo (dictogloss) is offered by default at B2.

EXTRA ADULT RULES
- "Sınırlı ziyaret" (Zor): each exhibit may be visited at most twice, a real memory challenge.
- Target-grammar diagnostic: in the proofread, the teacher's target (past perfect, passive, articles) is highlighted separately, so dictation errors become grammar data.
- True/False/Not given, reference ("What does 'they' refer to?"), inference ("What does the writer probably think about X?"), attitude and purpose questions.
- B2 "Two witnesses": two ~80-word accounts of one event. Questions ask which source says what, and the evidence must name the source and the sentence.
- Final: a headline of 6 words or fewer (B1) or a summary of 25 words or fewer (B2), teacher-judged (+1 for a valid entry, +2 for the best). Then the 30 s "Retell the case" by the spokesperson, using the 3 key words on screen.
- Optional "Final deduction" wager of up to 5 points on the last question.

SCORING. Answer 2; evidence +1 (optional -1 for a wrong evidence claim when negatives are on); order 3; dictation accuracy 3/2/1/0; headline 0-2. There are no speed points. Early finishers write two predicted questions and get +1 if either one is actually asked.

HINTS. Which exhibit, then a paraphrase clue, then the Turkish gloss; each costs 1 point, and the Turkish gloss can be switched off.

WRONG ANSWERS. The correct answer plus a one-line "why" (Turkish in the teacher chrome, English whyEn at B).

TIMERS AND PACING. An optional 30 s question timer and a 20 s huddle. Rounds of 8-12 min; 20-40 min in total.

ENDING. Full scores, a modest finale, and the "Kaçırılanlar" list: each missed question with its proof sentence and whyTr, plus the 5 most frequent dictation errors grouped by type (missing -s, articles, -ed, spelling). The list exports as a one-click printable homework sheet (the text + the questions + the evidence task).
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (9-11, default for A1 and A2 Genç): "LITTLE DETECTIVES / DEDEKTİF AJANSI"

THEME. Gogo the parrot is the Chief Detective, in a tiny deerstalker hat. Teams are animal agencies (Panda Agency, Fox Agency, Lion Agency, Frog Agency) with fingerprint-shaped badges. The text is a gentle "case file": "Where is Max the cat?", "The missing birthday cake", "Who ate the carrots?" (a rabbit did). Nothing scary, and the failure image is a sleepy magnifying glass with "Case still open!".

VISUALS. Warm, bright colours on cream; rounded shapes; an Andika-type font; prompt text at least 6vh. Station cards carry a big coloured SHAPE (red heart, blue star, green circle, yellow square, purple triangle), so they are colour-blind safe, plus a big picture of the sentence.

CONTENT
- A1 Genç: 25-35 words, 4 cards, one sentence per card, 6 words or fewer.
- A2 Genç: 50-60 words, 5 cards of 10 words or fewer.

RULES (3, on a pictogram card the teacher reads in Turkish, under 20 s)
1) Walk, don't run.
2) Read it, walk back, say it (no pencils at the wall).
3) Take turns: pass the badge after every card.

SCAFFOLDED DAVA DEFTERİ
- A1 Genç: each card's sentence frame is printed with ONE keyword missing, plus a picture box. The Runner brings back only that word and spells it with English letter names; the Checker ticks the matching picture.
- A2 Genç: the first two words of each sentence are printed.

FLASH. At least 15 s per card with the picture. The optional "Dinle desteği" reads the card once at 0.8x after the flash.

QUESTIONS. 3-4 per case, 4 words or fewer at A1 Genç and 8 or fewer at A2 Genç, with picture options A-C and automatic read-aloud at 0.8x. Every child answers every question (A-C cards; stand up = True, sit down = False). The seat spinner picks one child in the active team to point to the proof card's shape.

WRONG ANSWERS. A soft "boing", a hint ("Look at the star card!") and a second try. If it is still wrong, Gogo reads the proof sentence, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album.

SCORING. It never goes down. A stamp on the case file for every delivered card; 1 star per right answer; a magnifier sticker for the right evidence; 1 star for the right order. The first team to finish gets a helper job instead of points.

TIMERS. Off by default; when on, 40 s with a calm ring and a marimba chime. Huddle 10 s.

PACING (15-25 min)
- Round 1: Collect, 4-5 min.
- 60 s settler: "Detective freeze" (statues, then 3 slow breaths "through the magnifier").
- Round 2: Order + Check, 3 min.
- Round 3: Questions, 5 min.
- Finale (1 min): "Which picture tells the case?"

ENDING. Every agency gets a title (Sharp Eyes, Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Neat Writers, Brave Guessers) and a sticker for the class album. Confetti in team colours and shapes appears only at the finale, and celebrations last 2 s at most.

SOUND. Marimba, no buzzers, and an optional quiet thinking loop.

KIDS CHECKLIST: 3 rules; explainable in 20 s with pictograms; no elimination; never below zero; a whole-class response every question; non-violent failure imagery. All six pass.

ARENA (12-14, default for B1 and B2 Genç, and for any Genç class in grade 6-8): "INTEL RUN · CHALLENGE"

VISUALS. A dark navy/charcoal "mission map" with neon team colours and a condensed display font. Stations are "intel drops" marked with geometric glyphs. Team emblems: bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond. In 10 s, teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto ("Fast. Quiet. Correct."). There is no mascot and nothing cute. A commentator strip shows at most one line per turn ("EVIDENCE LOCKED", "CLEAN SHEET", "COMBO x3").

CONTENT
- A1/A2 Genç in Arena: the short picture-supported case files, with full audio.
- B1 Genç: 90-110 words, 6 cards of 14 words or fewer.
- B2 Genç: 120-140 words, cards of 20 words or fewer.
Topics are concrete and teenSafe: divers find a shipwreck; a 13-year-old inventor; a dog walks 100 km home; the museum mystery; a record climb; food in space. B2 Genç means richer language, not abstract debate: "How does Ela feel at the end?", not "Discuss remote work".

RULES
1) Walk.
2) No pens or phones at the drop.
3) Rotate every card.
The optional "Limited visits" rule (2 visits per drop) turns the round into a memory challenge. Flash lasts 12 s by default.

SCORING. Answer 2, evidence +1, order 3, accuracy 1-3. A combo of x1.5 at 3 clean questions in a row and x2 at 5 (a right answer with the right evidence counts as clean; accuracy only, never speed). The floor is zero, and hints cost 1 point. Timers are 30 s with the ring in the team colour; the huddle is 15 s.

OPT-IN (Yellow) "Challenge the evidence": a team may dispute another team's proof claim. If the challenger is right it gains +1, and the challenged team loses nothing.

ENDING. A podium plus stat awards: Longest streak; Clean sheet (zero dictation errors); Evidence master; Memory ace (fewest trips, from the Checker's ticks); Comeback. There is never a last place. Rounds last 5-7 min, 20-30 min in total.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Adults: ~50 words, 4 cards of 10 words or fewer (1-2 short sentences), present simple and there is/are.
- Questions: 3-4 literal questions (who/what/where/what time), 3-option MCQ or True/False, answerable by near-verbatim matching.
- Evidence is card-level; ordering 4 cards; final task = pick the title from 3.
- A1 Genç: 25-35 words, 4 one-sentence cards of 6 words or fewer with pictures; one-keyword gapped notebook; picture options; TPR True/False; questions of 4 words or fewer, read aloud.

A2
- Adults: ~80-100 words, 5 cards of 15 words or fewer; past simple, going to, comparatives, because/so.
- Questions: 4-5, including one sequencing question and one "why ... ? because ..." question.
- Evidence is card-level; final task = pick the title from 3.
- A2 Genç: 50-60 words, 5 cards of 10 words or fewer; notebook with printed sentence starters; questions of 8 words or fewer with picture options.

B1
- Adults: ~130 words, 6 cards of 25 words or fewer (Flash or Duvar).
- Questions: 5-6, including a reference question ("What does 'it' refer to?"), True/False/Not given, one inference question and one vocabulary-in-context question.
- Paraphrase is required, so pure word-matching no longer works. Evidence is SENTENCE-level, read aloud by the spokesperson.
- Final task: write a headline of 6 words or fewer.
- B1 Genç: 90-110 words, 6 cards of 14 words or fewer, teen-safe mysteries, inventions and animal records; one inference question; headline picked or written.

B2
- Adults: ~150-180 words, 6-7 cards of 40 words or fewer, or "Two witnesses" (2 x ~80 words). Radyo/dictogloss is offered.
- Questions: 6-8, covering attitude/purpose, inference, Not given and vocabulary in context. Some answers are open (teacher-judged: "explain in your own words").
- Evidence is sentence-level, plus the source in Two witnesses.
- Final: a written summary of 25 words or fewer and the 30 s retell; target-grammar diagnostic in the proofread.
- B2 Genç: 120-140 words, cards of 20 words or fewer, concrete narrative topics, feelings rather than opinions, a headline plus an optional retell.

KOLAY / ORTA / ZOR (inside any group). Kolay: cards 30% shorter, a 60% lower-band word mix, starters on the notebook and more flash passes. Zor: limited visits, one flash pass, sentence-level evidence one level early, and no Turkish gloss. "Bir seviye kolaylaştır" drops the text and question set one level while keeping the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-25 (Oyun Parkı), 20-30 (Arena), 20-40 (Stüdyo). One case takes about 18 min at A1 and about 30 min at B2; the lesson-fit timer trims questions, the proofread or the final task to fit.
catalog.teacherControls:
SUMMARY LINE AND SOURCE. The summary line comes with a Değiştir link; the result is saved in the local class profile. The case source is one of three:
- the bank, by level and topic;
- a free prompt with a word target;
- "Kendi metnim": paste a text; the app cuts it and drafts questions, which the teacher edits.

MODE AND ROOM
- Mode: Duvar, Flaş or Radyo (text-to-speech or "Öğretmen okur").
- Class size, plus the "Sınıf dar / sıralar sabit" tick (suggests Flaş).
- Number of cards (4-7) and card size via Kolay/Orta/Zor.
- "Sınırlı ziyaret" (limited visits).
- Flash time multiplier (0.75x-1.5x) and passes (1-3).

QUESTIONS AND TASKS
- Number and types of questions: literal, sequence, reference, inference, True/False/Not given, attitude.
- Evidence bonus on/off, and precision (card or sentence).
- "Açık kitap" toggle: shows the text after the first answer round, for weak classes.
- Proofread mode: peer check, teacher quick bands, digital typing, or off.
- Final task: pick, write or summary; retell on/off; wager on/off.
- Glossary pre-teach on/off; Turkish explanations and the Turkish gloss hint on/off.

PRINT PACK
- Station cards: A4 landscape, one per page, 2 copies above 30 students.
- A Dava Defteri per team (gapped for A1/A2 Genç).
- Double-sided answer/symbol cards, role badges and the rule poster.

DURING PLAY
- Space = next, T = pause, +10 s, Süresiz.
- "Son 1 dakika" chime, and tap a team badge to mark it finished.
- Quick answer grid, E = evidence mode (magnifier click), R = re-flash a card, skip a question.
- "Kanıt düzenle": fix a wrong evidence index live; the fix is saved to the pack.
catalog.delightDetails:
OPENING. The case opens as a manila folder stamped "CASE #A2-07", with a sticker-art polaroid of the setting and a row of face-down evidence cards.

PRINTED CARDS. They look like real evidence: a torn edge, a paper-clip graphic and a faint fingerprint watermark. The label is "EXHIBIT C" in Stüdyo, "INTEL" plus a glyph in Arena, or a big shape plus a picture for kids.

FLASH MODE. A slide-projector "clack" and a 3-2-1 "Eyes!" countdown; each card slides in like a photo under a desk lamp.

THE EVIDENCE BOARD. At the reveal, each question becomes a sticky note on a corkboard, and red string pins it to its proof sentence. Teams that found the evidence add their badge pin, so by the end the text is a detective's web. The magnifying-glass cursor makes the proof sentence glow as if under a UV torch.

CASE-CLOSED STAMP
- Kids: "Case solved!", with Gogo tipping his deerstalker, 2 s.
- Arena: a "FILE DECRYPTED" glitch, 1.2 s.
- Stüdyo: a red rubber-stamp thunk, "CASE CLOSED", 0.6 s.
Reduced motion swaps each one for a static stamp.

THE WANTED POSTER. The word most teams misspelt gets a "WANTED" poster with IPA, a speaker button and "Reward: 1 star", and the whole class spells it aloud together.

DICTATION DIFF. The rebuilt text sits next to the original, with differences shown as ink smudges. Target-grammar slips get their own colour ("the case of the missing -ed").

TEAM PROGRESS. Kids' case files collect a stamp for every card delivered, along a paw-print trail. Gogo repeats every proof sentence, and the class echoes it ("Gogo repeats!").

EARLY FINISHERS always get a job, so nobody sits idle.

CLASS ALBUM. Every solved case is filed in the "Dava arşivi" with the date and each team's title.

ARENA AWARDS. The Checker's trip ticks feed the "Memory ace" award.

STÜDYO. The Kaçırılanlar list becomes a one-click printable homework sheet.
catalog.risks:
MOVEMENT AND SAFETY. Crowded Turkish public classrooms with fixed desks and bags on the floor. Mitigations: the walk-don't-run rule card, spread stations and staggered start stations, one Runner out per team, and Flaş suggested above 32 students or when the room is ticked as tight.

NOISE AND CHEATING
- Runners may shout across the room: "speak only at your table".
- Runners may write on their hands or photograph cards with phones: the "no pens or phones at the wall" rule.
- In Flaş, Writers may peek: backs to the screen, with the Eye rotating.

PRINTING. Offer Flaş and Radyo; the whole print pack fits on 8-10 A4 pages.

QUESTIONS WITHOUT THE TEXT. Some questions can be answered from general knowledge. Mitigations: the blind-test validator, and the evidence requirement.

WRONG EVIDENCE INDICES. Auto-guessed indices for the bank can be wrong: LLM confirmation, low-confidence flags and the live "Kanıt düzenle" editor.

SENTENCE SPLITTING on abbreviations and numbers: splitter rules, plus a preview before printing.

CONTENT FOR CHILDREN. The B1/B2 bank texts (work, business, psychology, remote work) are unsuitable for them. Genç groups use only curated or generated teenSafe texts, and A1/A2 bank texts are trimmed with "Kısalt".

WEAK WRITERS. A1 Genç learners (grade 3-4) can barely write English sentences: hence the one-keyword gapped notebook and starters.

TEACHER LOAD. Reading 6 teams' boards takes time: default to 4 teams, the "Hepsi aynı" grid and double-sided answer cards.

TIME OVERRUN. The Collect phase can run over: the lesson-fit timer, the "Son 1 dakika" chime and a skippable proofread.

ACCESSIBILITY. A student who cannot move keeps a seated role; shapes plus colours make the cards colour-blind safe; the Radyo mode suits low-vision students.

COST. LLM cost and rate limits: one generation per case, cached in the Dava arşivi.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (G04 Dikteyle yeniden kurma, G11 Kanıt dedektifi)

issues: SETUP IS NOT 2 MINUTES IN A TURKISH PUBLIC SCHOOL. The teacher usually arrives from another class during a 10-minute break. Printing 5-7 A4 station cards (10-14 above 30 students), a Dava Defteri per team, 12-card answer decks per team, badges and a poster, then taping them in the corners, takes 5-8 minutes. Many teachers also pay for their own printing. Duvar mode will rarely be the real default for the kids' audience. Flaş is the true default there, yet it is specified as the secondary mode.

WALL CARDS CAN BE READ FROM THE DESKS. A4 landscape text that is big enough for 10-year-olds to read is also readable from nearby seats. Nearby teams then skip the running, and the far teams feel cheated. This is the most common running-dictation failure, and the design does not address it.

FLAŞ 'ONLY THE EYE WATCHES, WRITERS SIT WITH THEIR BACKS TO THE SCREEN' CANNOT BE ENFORCED with 28 children in fixed rows. Everyone faces the smart board, turning round in fixed desks is physically awkward, and the teacher cannot police 23 non-Eyes. In practice everyone watches, so the role structure collapses and strong students who remember fast dominate.

ACTIVE-STUDENT COUNT IN COLLECT: 5 teams of 5-6 give 5 Runners, 5 Writers and 5 Checkers. That leaves 10-13 children with no job at any moment, and in Flaş only 5 Eyes do anything during the flash. Idle 10-12 year-olds in a crowded room generate the noise that the 'speak only at your table' rule is meant to prevent.

CASCADING FAILURE (FAIRNESS). The twist, answering only from your own notes, means one weak or slow Collect round ruins the Order, Proofread, Questions and Evidence rounds for that team. A team that reached only 3 of 5 cards is hopelessly behind for the remaining ~15 minutes, and nothing mid-game rescues it except the 'Açık kitap' toggle, which is a global setting.

TEACHER CLICK LOAD PER QUESTION IS TOO HIGH to manage standing at the board. Each question takes about 7-8 teacher actions: next, reveal options, huddle, 'Boards up', tap the grid for 4-5 teams (plus exceptions), reveal, E for evidence mode, read the symbol cards of 4-5 teams, tap the evidence grid, click the proof sentence, then pin it. With 5-8 questions that is roughly 50 inputs, while the teacher also manages behaviour.

THE EVIDENCE ANSWER HARDWARE IS FIDDLY. 'Double-sided answer cards' actually means a per-team deck of A-D plus 4-7 station symbols plus '?', about 12 small cards. Teams will fumble, drop and lose cards, and the teacher cannot read small symbols from the front across 5 teams.

THE HINT LADDER CONFLICTS WITH SIMULTANEOUS ANSWERING. When every team huddles and reveals at once, it is unclear when and how one team asks for 'Which card?' without the other teams seeing it, and who taps it. As specified, it is unusable in the simultaneous flow.

PROOFREAD SWAP WITH KIDS CAUSES CHAOS. Passing notebooks along a swap chain across fixed rows, counting another team's mistakes and showing finger bands produces disputes ('that's not a mistake!'). The teacher also has to read 5 finger bands and tap them. This adds 3+ minutes of the noisiest kind of activity for little learning at A1/A2 Genç.

SCORING HAS TOO MANY INPUTS: answer 2, evidence +1, order 3, accuracy 3/2/1/0, headline 0-2, wager, combo, early-finisher +1, and the hint costs. Most of these need a manual teacher tap per team, and adults will lose the thread of why they are winning.

YOU CANNOT STOP AT ANY MOMENT. The phases are strictly sequential. If the bell rings during Collect or before the questions, nothing has been scored and the notes are lost. 40-minute lessons with a late start make this common. A realistic kids run is briefing 2 + practice 1 + Collect 6 + settler 1 + Order/Check 4 + Questions 8 (second tries, class echoes) + finale 2 = about 25-30 minutes, not 15-25.

LOW TEACHER VALUE-ADD DURING THE CORE PHASE. During Collect, the heart of the game, the app shows only a timer. Teachers already run paper running dictation for free, so the app has to earn its setup cost in the other phases, and those are the heaviest ones.

A1 GENÇ COLLAPSES INTO A WORD FETCH. Grade 3-4 Turkish children do not reliably know English letter names, and the notebook already prints everything except one keyword. The 'answer from your own notes' twist therefore becomes trivial, while the logistics cost (printing, movement) stays the same.

THE SCOPE IS TOO LARGE FOR V1 (L). The spec includes Two witnesses, the Newsroom skin, digital typing with a word diff, Challenge the evidence, wagers, Radyo text-to-speech, Kısalt, a blind-test validator and the Arena stat awards. The risk is that it ships late or buggy, in classrooms where nothing may fail.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES that will confuse the build: the flash time formula (4 s + 0.6 s/word x1.5 gives about 11 s for a 6-word kids card) against 'at least 15 s per card', and 'no card may hold evidence for more than two questions' against 3-4 questions spread over 4 cards.
fixes: Make Flaş (or a new 'Herkes izler' variant) the default for Oyun Parkı and Arena, and Duvar the default only for Stüdyo with 24 learners or fewer. In the Genç Flaş variant, the WHOLE class watches, pens down, and the team then rebuilds together (dictogloss-lite). This drops the unenforceable Eye/back-to-screen rule. Keep the Eye as the only person allowed to 'Re-flash' (R) once per team.

Duvar anti-peek: print cards as a fold-over flap ('KALDIR / LIFT') with the text on the inside, or use a small-font text body (14-16 pt) under a big symbol and picture that are readable from afar. Add the 'Kartları kapağıyla yapıştır' instruction to the print preview.

Cut the print pack to at most 1 page per team plus the station cards. Replace the 12-card answer deck with ONE A4 'answer mat' per team: A-D on one side, the station symbols in a big grid on the other, and a pencil or clothes-peg pointer. Alternatively, use a mini-whiteboard with the letter + symbol written together, e.g. 'B ★'.

Fold evidence into the answer reveal: teams show the answer AND the evidence symbol in one 'Boards up'. The teacher taps one grid row per team with two toggles (answer correct?, evidence correct?), with 'Hepsi aynı' prefilled from the majority. The app auto-highlights the stored proof sentence, so there is no magnifier click. Keep the magnifier click only as an override ('Kanıt düzenle'). Target at most 3 teacher inputs per question.

Add a 'Kurtarma flaşı' (rescue flash) at the end of Collect: any card a team missed is flashed once on the projector for everyone for 8 s. The team can therefore still play the questions, and its accuracy score reflects the loss instead of a zero on the remaining phases. Also let the app suggest 'Açık kitap' automatically for any single question that at most one team answers correctly.

Give every team member a job during Collect in 5-6 person teams: add a 'Resim avcısı / Picture matcher' who ticks the matching picture, and a 'Harf kontrol' who spells trap words back. Or run TWO runners per team in parallel to different stations (A-level only, 4 cards), halving Collect time and doubling the number of active students.

Hints in simultaneous mode must be CLASS-WIDE and free, with the teacher pressing 'İpucu' when half or more of the teams look stuck, or be removed entirely. Per-team paid hints only in Stüdyo, requested verbally BEFORE 'Boards up', with the teacher tapping that team's badge.

Kids' proofread: remove the peer swap. The projector reveals the original card by card and each team self-checks its OWN notebook, circling the words and counting stamps, not penalties. Make Proofread default OFF in Oyun Parkı and ON in Stüdyo, where peer checking of dictation errors is genuinely valuable.

Simplify scoring to 3 visible sources in Genç (answer, evidence, order) and 4 in Stüdyo (+ accuracy). Accuracy 3/2/1/0 should be auto-derived from the self-check count rather than teacher-judged. Headline votes, wagers and combos go behind 'Gelişmiş'.

Build 'Dur ve kaydet' (T held for 2 s): it saves the phase, scores and team notes state in the Dava arşivi and opens a 1-minute 'Mini kapanış' (show the text, 1 whole-class question, stamps). 'Devam et' resumes next lesson from the Order phase, with a 60 s recap flash of all cards. Have the lesson-fit timer plan for 40-minute lessons minus 5 minutes of start-up.

Add a live 'Collect board' so the app earns its place during Collect: the Checker comes to the smart board, or the teacher taps, to mark each card delivered per team. The projector shows each team's paw-print trail and prompts 'Fox Agency: kalp kartı eksik!' when there is a gap. This also feeds the Memory ace award without paper tick sheets.

A1 Genç: replace letter-name spelling with 'bring the word, point to the picture'. Offer the Radyo or Flaş variant as the default so that no printing is needed for a one-word fetch. Scope Duvar for kids to A2 Genç and above.

V1 scope: Flaş + Duvar, bank texts plus a free prompt, MCQ/TF with card-level evidence, Order, and the evidence board ending. Defer Two witnesses, Newsroom, the digital diff, Challenge the evidence, wagers, Arena stat awards and Radyo text-to-speech to v2.

Fix the spec inconsistencies: set the kids' flash time to max(15 s, formula), and let the cutter allow a 'bridge' card with no question at A1 (4 cards, 3 questions) while still requiring every card to be needed for Order.

issues: The B2 memory load is unrealistic. Running dictation of a 40-word card, or a 7-card, 150-180-word text, overloads working memory. Collect alone would run 12-15 min with 5 teams, and the game turns into a memory contest rather than a language task. In Flaş, a 40-word card shows for about 28 s to one Eye and cannot be relayed.

A1 Genç (grade 3-4) breaks the core loop. With the one-keyword gapped notebook, the rest of the text is already printed, so 'answer from your own notes' is no twist at all: kids answer from the printed frames. The game becomes a word fetch. That is fine for learning, but the evidence and ordering layers add rules the kids cannot use.

Spelling aloud 'with English letter names' is a known weak spot for Turkish children, who use Turkish letter names (e, i, a, y/j and g confusions). Without support, the Checker/Writer exchange stalls or slips into Turkish.

The kids' ruleset is not really stripped. The poster shows 3 rules, but in practice children still run roles (Runner, Writer, Checker) that rotate every card, symbol codes, a proofread swap chain, finger bands, evidence flips and TPR. The 20 s explanation claim passes on paper but not in the classroom.
The peer proofread with 1/2/3 finger bands is unreliable at A1-A2 and for any Genç group. Children cannot count their own dictation errors, and the step adds noise and time without learning.

Seven phases per case is too long for a 40-min lesson with a real warm-up. The A1 total of about 18 min is optimistic once printing, taping, role badges and the seat spinner are counted; the Genç timelines skip transition time.
Flaş assumes Writers sit with their backs to the screen. Turkish classrooms have fixed rows facing the board, so this is physically impossible for most teams, and peeking is unavoidable.

The content supply for kids is thin. readings_a1..b2 are adult texts, and no teenSafe kids' case bank exists; 'Kısalt' trims of adult texts produce stilted texts. For LLM-generated cases, 'imageKey required at A1/A2 Genç' has no image source defined: the LLM cannot draw, and a free-prompt topic like 'a dragon at the market' will not map to a fixed icon set.

The B1+ paraphrase rule (content-word overlap of 60% or less) plus sentence-level evidence clashes with 'answer from your own notes'. Teams whose dictation dropped the paraphrased word fail through a dictation miss, not a reading miss, so scores mix up spelling, memory and comprehension.
Arena 'Memory ace (fewest trips)' and Stüdyo 'Sınırlı ziyaret' reward cramming long chunks, which pushes weaker students out of the Runner role even though roles rotate.
The blind-test validator doubles LLM calls per case, and the evidence auto-guess plus LLM confirmation adds a third call. That puts pressure on the rate limit when a teacher regenerates.
The adult extras (wager, negatives, challenge, Two witnesses, grammar diagnostic, retell, summary) are each fine, but together they make the Stüdyo setup heavy. The summary line hides too many dials.
fixes: Cap card length by memory, not by the text-load cap. Relay chunk at most 8 words (A1/A1G at most 6), at most 12 at B1 and at most 15 at B2. Longer sentences split into 2 cards. Cap cards at 6 and texts at about 90 words (B1) and about 120 (B2) in Duvar/Flaş. Longer B2 texts go to Radyo/dictogloss only. Flaş time = 5 s + 0.8 s per word, with a hard max chunk of 15 words.

Oyun Parkı: replace the full loop with 'Picture Hunt'. Each station has a picture plus a 4-6-word sentence. The Runner brings back the keyword, and the team sticks the matching picture sticker or draws it. Then 3 picture-option questions. Drop proofread, symbol-code ordering and the evidence flip (ordering becomes 'put the pictures in order' on the projector together).
Add an English alphabet strip (letter names with Turkish-sound hints, e.g. E = /iː/, I = /aɪ/, J = /dʒeɪ/, G = /dʒiː/) to every Dava Defteri and the projector. Allow 'point to the letter' at A1 Genç.
Oyun Parkı uses 2 roles only (Runner, Writer) with a badge pass. The Checker job moves to the projector tracker.

Default the proofread to OFF for all Genç groups and A1-A2 adults. Replace it with a projector 'spot 3 differences' on one team's notebook shown by document camera or phone photo, or just the WANTED word.

Split scoring into 3 visible strands (Dictation, Order, Reading) with small caps on each, so a dictation failure does not zero comprehension. At B1+ let questions show the paraphrase anchor word in the glossary. Make the 'Açık kitap' second pass the default at A2 and B1 Genç.

Make Flaş the default in Turkish rooms, with 'Writers put their heads down / pens only' instead of backs to the screen. Show one card at a time to all Eyes simultaneously, then run a covered-screen tell window.

Before launch, ship a curated kids' bank: at least 25 cases each for A1G/A2G (with icons from a fixed Languago icon set) and 20 each for B1G/B2G. For LLM kids' prompts, constrain the generator to choose imageKeys from the enumerated icon list and reject cases where any card has no icon.
Run the blind test only on MCQ/T-F items, merge it with the evidence confirmation in one LLM call, and cache per case.
Offer a 'Hızlı dava' preset (Collect, Order, 4 questions, Case closed; about 15 min) as the default. The proofread, final task, retell and wager are opt-in extras, not default steps.
Replace 'Memory ace (fewest trips)' with 'Clean relay' (all cards delivered with at most 1 error). Keep Sınırlı ziyaret for B2 Stüdyo only.

issues: Scope is well beyond L. The spec has 3 modes (Duvar/Flaş/Radyo), 7 phases, a print pack, a digital join-code typing mode with word diff, Two witnesses, wagers, Challenge the evidence, Kısalt, a Kanıt düzenle editor, a lesson-fit timer, a class album and 3 skins with separate scoring. Built as written, it would be the largest game in the suite, and the least-used features would add the most risk (digital diff needs device join and realtime, which the site does not have for this).

In Duvar mode, the most-played mode for adults, the software does very little during the longest phase (Collect, 4-8 min): a timer and station symbols. The game feel comes from paper and movement. That is fine pedagogically, but the 'proper polished game' feel rests on the reveal phases (order slide-in, evidence board, case-closed). Those must be excellent or the game reads as 'a timer plus a quiz'.

The question phase is a generic projected MCQ/TF round with team boards. Without the evidence mechanic it duplicates any quiz/Reading Detective candidate. The evidence step (name the card symbol) is the only thing that makes it distinct, so it cannot be optional in the MVP.

Compounding failure: teams answer from their own notes, so a weak dictation leads to wrong answers, which leads to lost evidence points. The same weakness is punished 2-3 times. Weak classes will feel the game is unfair. 'Açık kitap' exists, but it is off by default and only opens after the first answer round.

Teacher load per question is high. The teacher reads 4-6 physical boards, taps each on a grid, runs an evidence round, clicks a sentence and taps proofread bands. With 6 questions that is about 12 input rounds from the teacher's laptop while standing at the board. Smartboard use with a finger (the magnifier cursor, clicking a sentence in dense text) is fiddly.

Oyun Parkı A1 Genç (ages 8-10) is overloaded despite 'passing' the checklist. The 3 rules hide rotating roles, spelling with English letter names, a gapped notebook, ordering with shapes, a TPR stand/sit round, a pointing round and a practice round. The phase count, not the rule count, is the real text and procedure load. Grade 3-4 learners spelling 'caught' by letter names is unrealistic, and teachers will likely run it teacher-led.

Flaş mode relies on Writers sitting with their backs to the screen. In fixed Turkish desk rows this means students twisting round in their seats, and peeking is trivially easy. Eye rotation every card in a 5-6 card case with 2-3 passes is a lot of reseating choreography.

Kids cards need 'a big picture of the sentence' (imageKey required at A1/A2 Genç). An LLM can't produce images, and a keyword-to-icon library cannot depict 'The cat is under the bed' as a scene. Without a curated scene-art set this requirement fails for generated content.

The cutter constraint (every card holds the evidence for 1-2 questions, cards 4-7, questions 3-8, word caps, and sentences never shrunk) is often unsatisfiable for generated or pasted texts ('Kendi metnim'). There is no defined fallback: merge cards, add questions, or allow an 'orphan' card.

LLM validation is expensive and fragile. Generation + evidence confirmation + a blind test of every question is 2-3 calls per case, against a rate-limited DeepSeek endpoint. The blind test is itself noisy: DeepSeek will 'guess' many A1 literal questions correctly from world knowledge (e.g. 'Where is the cat?' with the option 'under the bed'), so it would reject valid A1 items. The 60% paraphrase-overlap rule conflicts with the need for B1 reference and vocab-in-context questions to quote the text.

Sentence-level evidence depends on a robust splitter and on stable indices. Any teacher edit to the text (Kısalt, Kendi metnim edits) invalidates the evidence indices and the card cuts unless they are recomputed and re-confirmed.

Radyo mode depends on Web Speech API English voices. Many Turkish classroom smartboards (Android-based, VESTEL/Arçelik-type panels) and school PCs have no good en-GB/en-US voice, or none at all. Radyo is also a different activity (dictogloss) with its own UI, which is scope creep.

Asset list is heavy: Gogo in several poses (reads, walks, tips hat, sleeps), the corkboard, red string, sticky notes, manila folder, stamps for 3 skins, printed card templates with torn edge/fingerprint, 5 shapes plus 6 glyphs, 3 fonts (Andika, a typewriter face, a condensed display face, all self-hosted) and 3 sound sets.

The session length (18-30 min for one case, plus 2 min of printing and taping, plus peeling cards off the walls) consumes most of a 40-min Turkish lesson, so it will be used occasionally, not weekly. That is acceptable, but it argues for a cheaper build.
fixes: Cut the MVP to: Duvar + Flaş only; source = bank or free prompt; 4-6 cards; Collect → Order → Questions with card-level evidence → Evidence board → Case closed. Defer Radyo, digital diff, Two witnesses, wager, Challenge the evidence, Kısalt, proofread bands, retell and the class album to v2. Estimated build: M+ instead of L+.

Make the evidence board the hero and build it first. Use SVG: a corkboard with the text as paper strips per card, a sticky note per question, and an animated red string (stroke-dashoffset) to the proof card. Pins in team colours for teams that got it. Evidence stays card-level at all levels in the MVP (click a card, not a sentence), which also fixes the smartboard click-precision problem. Add sentence-level highlighting inside the card as a teacher-only option.

Replace the per-team answer grid with one 'which teams were right?' row of big team toggles, with 'Hepsi doğru' / 'Hepsi yanlış' shortcuts, and let evidence be marked with the same toggle row. Target: at most 2 taps per question per phase. Add a phone presenter view (a QR code to the same session, read-only plus buttons) so the teacher can score while walking.

Break the compounding penalty. Set 'Açık kitap' ON by default in Oyun Parkı and for A1-A2, as a 'Look again' lifeline (one per team) that re-flashes the proof card. Weight accuracy points so a team with a weak notebook can still win on evidence.

Redefine Oyun Parkı as teacher-led Flaş by default (no walking, no Writers turned round). The whole class watches the card and the class 'Eyes' team calls the keyword; ordering is by dragging the shape tiles on the smartboard; questions use TPR and A-C cards. Drop letter-name spelling to optional. Keep Duvar for Arena and Stüdyo.

Replace 'a picture of the sentence' with a composable scene: a small curated sticker set (about 60 nouns, 20 places, prepositions shown as positions) that the LLM picks from via a constrained imageKey enum. Validate the keys against the enum and fall back to a single noun icon. Bank A1/A2 Genç cases get hand-picked scenes.

Make the cutter constraint soft: allow at most one 'context' card with no question (marked visually), and if more cards lack a question, auto-merge adjacent cards or ask the LLM for one extra question targeting that card. Always show a card preview with question-to-card links before printing, and lock the indices once the teacher confirms.

Simplify validation to deterministic checks plus one LLM call. The generator must return an explicit {questionId: cardId, quote} for each question, and code verifies that the quote substring exists in that card. Drop the blind test for A levels; at B levels run it only in a batch prebuild for the bank, not live. Relax the paraphrase rule to 'the correct option is not a verbatim substring' for detail items only.
For 'Kendi metnim', recompute the cuts and require the teacher to confirm the evidence in the editor before play. Store an immutable snapshot (text hash + cards + evidence) in the Dava arşivi.

Detect English TTS voices at setup. If none exist, hide Radyo and 'Dinle desteği' and show 'Öğretmen okur' prompts instead. Optionally pre-render bank audio at build time for A1/A2 Genç cases only (small MP3s), never for generated content.

Share assets with the suite: the shape/glyph set, team emblems, mascot and stamp animation from a common kit; one self-hosted Andika plus the system stack. Use CSS/SVG for the typewriter-style headings (letter-spacing on a mono stack) rather than adding a third font. Keep all sounds under 1 s and share them across games.

Print pack: generate it with print CSS from the same card data (A4 landscape, symbol huge in the corner, text at 28-36pt, a fingerprint watermark as an SVG background), including a one-page 'teacher sheet' with a station map and the answer key. Test the output in Chrome/Edge print preview at 100%.
Add 'Hızlı dava' (12-15 min): 4 cards, Flaş, 3 questions, no proofread. This makes the game usable weekly within a 40-min lesson, alongside the full version.

catalog.rankReason: Running dictation with a case-file frame (adult 8): reading, movement and evidence. Flaş/'Herkes izler' is the default for kids and Arena; Duvar is only for Stüdyo with 24 learners or fewer. Wall cards are fold-over flaps, chunk length is capped by memory, and the red-string evidence board is the centrepiece. It later takes x03's dictogloss as its Radyo mode.

catalog.name: Issız Ada (Survival Council)
catalog.familiarAs: Lost at Sea ranking + The Oregon Trail + Blooket Crazy Kingdom (a survival-council decision game)
catalog.oneLiner: The class must survive a few days on an island, on a broken space station or in a city without power. Each day an event card forces a council decision. Teams pitch and vote in persuasive English, four shared meters rise and fall, and language challenges gather the supplies and the rescue signal that decide how the story ends.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (teacher, about 1 min). There are two content slots:
- 'Senaryo': a built-in scenario for the audience, or a Turkish prompt that the LLM turns into a survival envelope (e.g. 'Kapadokya'da balonla mahsur kaldık').
- 'Soru paketi': the challenge content. It can be a built-in category or grammar unit, the scenario's own word pack (the default), or an LLM prompt.
The lesson-fit timer sets the number of days. The setup screen shows one summary line, e.g. 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 sn · 40 dk · Desert Island · 6 gün', with a 'Değiştir' link. The print pack holds A/B/C vote cards, the salvage sheet, role cards with the phrase strip and the diary template.

CREWS. There are 4-6 teams, and each is a specialist crew that feeds one track:
- Cook: Food
- Scout: Water
- Doctor: Health
- Engineer: Signal (the rescue track)
- Captain (5+ teams): Morale
- Explorer (6 teams): map pieces toward the secret 'funny' ending
The shared meters are Food, Water, Health and Morale, each 0-100 and starting at 50. Signal runs 0-100 and starts at 0. The survival outcome is co-operative: one set of meters and one ending for the whole class. On top of that, teams compete lightly through Contribution points and Influence tokens.

DAY 0, SALVAGE (Lost at Sea; 5-8 min for adults, 3 min for kids).
1. Twelve picture items come from the wreck: rope, mirror, water bottle, torch, chocolate, map, pocket tool, blanket, whistle, plastic sheet, radio, first-aid kit.
2. In 2 min, each team ranks its top 5 on the salvage sheet, using the frame 'The ___ is more useful than the ___ because...'.
3. In 3 min the class reaches a consensus: teams nominate items and the teacher drags them into a consensus top 5 on screen.
4. The expert ranking is revealed, with a one-line 'why' for each item ('A mirror can signal a plane from very far away').
5. Each team's Survival Score is its distance from the expert ranking, shown as a bar rather than a harsh number. The closest team gets +2 Influence. The quality of the consensus sets the starting meters (45-60).
6. The 5 salvaged items join the camp inventory and unlock event options later. For example, 'Use the rope' appears only if the rope was saved, and a salvaged item makes the matching supply worth +6 instead of +4.

EACH DAY (4-6 min).
1. DAWN (10 s): a day card appears, the sky lightens, last night's drain animates and the weather is set.
2. EVENT (45 s): the event card flips and is read aloud (TTS, or 'Öğretmen okur') over a picture. After the options delay, 2-3 options appear. Each shows its visible cost icons. At B1+, hidden costs show as '?', and risky options show an odds pie.
3. TEAM TALK: a huddle of the dial's length, with the council phrase strip on screen.
4. PITCHES (1.5-2 min): the crews whose specialism the event touches pitch first, 20 s each. The seat-number spinner picks the speaker; nobody is picked by name. Any other crew may play one 'Objection!' by spending 1 Influence, which gives it 15 s. When a speaker uses a phrase from the strip, the teacher taps 'Frame used'. The team gets +1 Influence and the phrase ticks on the strip.
5. VOTE (30 s): on 3-2-1, every team raises its A/B/C card at once, and the teacher taps the counts. Each team has 1 vote and may add up to 2 Influence tokens, which are spent. The trailing team breaks ties (Comeback dial). The teacher can override any vote.
6. CONSEQUENCE (15 s): the meters wobble and then move, and hidden effects are revealed. One past-simple line is added to the Survival Diary ('On Day 3 we built a raft.'). The camp scene grows: shelter, raft, water collector.
7. GATHERING (2-3 min): 2-3 challenges from the Soru paketi. On 'Boards up!', every team answers at the same time on mini-whiteboards or A-D cards. Each correct team sends supplies to its specialist meter and earns Contribution. Then one harder EXPEDITION card, tied to the event word, goes to the team that lost the vote, or else to the trailing team. If it is missed, the mode's steal or retry rule applies.
   - Hint ladder: kids get picture, first letter, listen again, all free. Arena gets first letter, 50:50, gapped example, each costing 1-2 Contribution and never going below 0. Adults get definition, example, TR gloss, each costing Influence.
8. NIGHT (20-60 s): the night drain applies (Food -10 and Water -10 at Orta). An optional night card may follow (a dream, a strange noise, a visitor with a trade). At B1+ there is a 15-s RATIONS vote in the Oregon Trail style: Full, Half or Tiny, trading Food against Health and Morale.

CRISIS. When a meter hits 0, a crisis card deals a forced choice with a price: spend Influence, lose Signal, or make another meter pay. By default the game never ends early; each crisis only delays the rescue (Signal -15). In Hardcore (a Stüdyo opt-in), a second 0 ends the game with the early-evacuation ending.

FINAL DAY: 'Ship on the horizon' (or 'The radio works!'). Each crew gets one location clue, and its spokesperson describes it to the teacher, who plays the coast guard. Every clear description adds Signal. Then the rescue animation plays.

END. The class earns stars:
- 1 star: rescued.
- 2 stars: Signal at least 60 and no meter at 0 on the last day.
- 3 stars: Signal full and every meter at least 30.
Each mode then shows its own team ending, and the Survival Diary is exported.
catalog.playerSetup:
The whole class plays in 4-6 teams of 3-6 students, 12-36 students in all. Each team is a specialist crew that feeds one shared track. With fewer than 8 students, play 2 crews, each holding two specialisms.
- Oyun Parkı: 4 animal crews (panda, fox, lion, frog).
- Arena: 4-6 crews. In 10 s each picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
- Stüdyo: 4-6 crews of 2-5 with a rotating spokesperson. Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').
Mixed motive: survival is fully co-operative (one set of meters, one ending), and teams compete lightly for Contribution points and Influence. Nobody is ever eliminated. Speakers are chosen by the seat-number spinner, never by name.
skills: speaking: suggesting, agreeing, disagreeing, justifying, negotiating, conceding
modals (can/should/could/had better) and conditionals (first, second, third, mixed at B2)
reading short event texts, costs and odds
listening: read-aloud events and the radio-call finale
vocabulary: survival, nature, food, tools, the body, feelings
catalog.adultVersion:
'Survival Council' in the Stüdyo skin (editorial quiz-night look, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme; no mascot).

Five built-in scenarios:
- Desert Island: a holiday plane comes down in a storm.
- Mountain Crash: a winter cabin, no gore.
- 'Blackout: 48 Hours': a city without power, played as 8 six-hour blocks instead of days. Meters: Food, Phone battery, Warmth, Neighbours' trust.
- 'Mars Base' (B2): hidden consequences and interacting events.
- 'Startup Survival: 6 Months to Launch', a business reskin played in months. Meters: Cash, Team energy, Investor trust, Product. Salvage means choosing 5 of 12 resources, such as a senior developer, a big office or an influencer deal. Events include an investor call, a key employee quitting and a competitor launching.

The full ruleset:
- Influence economy. Teams earn Influence from correct answers, 'Frame used' taps and the English-only button. They spend it on extra votes (at most 2 per vote), Objections, hints and wagers.
- Wager rounds: a team bets 0-3 Influence on its Expedition card.
- Hidden effects and odds pies on risky options.
- The Oregon Trail rations vote at night, and crisis cards.
- Consensus mode (B2): the council has 60 s to agree unanimously, or the default 'wait and see' option happens.
- Optional Secret agendas (B2): each crew gets a printed hidden goal, e.g. 'Your crew wants to explore the cave', and earns bonus Contribution if it happens. This is real negotiation practice.
- Visitors with trade offers, in the style of Crazy Kingdom's throne-room guests.
- Harshness: Green plus Yellow by default. Red is opt-in: Mutiny (swap two crews' Influence), Storm (reset one crew's Influence), Virus (a Health drain that spreads unless the Doctor crew answers). Hardcore is also opt-in: a second 0 ends the game early.
- Wrong answers show the correct answer plus a one-line 'why', with optional minus Contribution.

Language targets: should/could/had better, first and second conditionals, concession ('Even though..., ...', 'I take your point, but...'), and hedging.

Ending: full Contribution scores; the 'Council Minutes' (every decision with its vote split); the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list; and a homework 'Report to the Coast Guard' with an auto-built third-conditional reflection from the class's real choices ('If we had kept the rope, we could have crossed the river.').
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (ages 9-11; default for A1 and A2 Genç)
'Kamp Adası / Treasure Island Camp' (also 'Dinosaur Valley' and 'Jungle Friends'). The host is Gogo the parrot, perched on the signal pole. This is a stripped ruleset, not a re-coloured adult game. The teacher explains it in 20 s from a Turkish rule card with pictograms:
1. CHOOSE: stand up for picture A, sit down for picture B. The whole class votes every day; the majority wins and the teacher breaks ties.
2. FIND: answer on your A-D card to bring fruit, water, hearts or smiles to camp.
3. FILL THE JARS before the boat comes.

Removed for kids: Influence, pitches, hidden effects, odds, risky options, rations, crises and steals.

How it works:
- The meters are four picture jars (apple basket, water bottle, heart, smiley sun), each with 5 notches and starting at 3. A jar never drops below 1 notch. A low jar gets a sleepy face, and a helper animal arrives: 'Monkey has bananas! Say: Thank you, monkey!' The whole-class chant refills one notch.
- Each event offers two pictures with a caption of 0-4 words ('Fish or coconuts?'). Both options are good; they just fill different jars.
- Day 0 is 'Pack your backpack': the class picks 3 of 8 picture items. No pick is wrong, because every item gets used later ('A rope! Great!').
- Gathering has 2 picture challenges per day, and every team answers on A-D cards, so the whole class responds. The seat spinner picks the reader. On a wrong answer there is a soft 'boing', a hint and a second try. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team's effort star goes to the class album. Each correct answer sends the team's animal to carry the item to the jar, and the team gets a sticker.
- Night is a 60-s settler: the lights dim, stars appear, the class counts them in English and whispers 'Good night, Gogo'. The only drain is 'The animals ate one apple' (Food -1 notch).
- The game runs 3 days (15-25 min), with a 45-s 'Island Moves' TPR stirrer between days: swim, climb, dig, jump.
- Finale: the boat always comes. The stars show how full the jars are and whether the treasure chest opened (map pieces come from correct answers). Every team gets a title: Best Fruit Finders, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers, Water Heroes.
- Failure images are harmless: rain soaks a hat, a crab steals a sock.
- Frames: 'I want the ___.', 'Let's ___!', 'Yes, please! / No, thank you.'
- Kids checklist: 3 rules, pictograms, no elimination, nothing below zero, a whole-class vote every turn, gentle failure.

ARENA (ages 12-14; default for B1 and B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç group at grade 6+)
'Stranded: Station Kommo-1' (a broken space station), or 'Volcano Island Expedition'.
- Look: dark navy HUD with neon team colours, emblems and a 10-s motto, framed as 'Survival Challenge · Mission Day 3'.
- Space meters: Oxygen, Power, Food, Crew Spirit, on the same engine.
- Council vote with Influence (at most 2 per vote) and rotating spokespeople chosen by the seat spinner. The 30-s timer is on.
- Gathering combo on Contribution: x1.5 at 3 correct in a row, x2 at 5.
- A missed Expedition card can be stolen by one other team, and the first team loses nothing. A mild 'Raid' (take up to 5 Contribution, capped at the target's score) is available only if the teacher opts in to Yellow.
- Hidden effects and odds from B1. Crisis cards cost Signal and never end the game.
- A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('CLUTCH SAVE', 'COMBO x3').
- Podium on Contribution, with stat awards: Longest streak, Best pitch, Diplomat, Clutch save, Comeback. There is never a last place and never a name on screen.
- teenSafe everywhere: no weapons, injuries, hunting or romance. A 'sick friend' becomes 'Leo has a stomachache'.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- 3-4 days. Two options, each with a picture.
- Meters show as icons only, with no numbers. No hidden effects or odds.
- Event text stays within the caps: A1 10 words; A1 Genç 0-4 words, with the picture carrying the meaning.
- Frames: 'I want ___ / Let's ___ / Yes! / No!'.
- Salvage: pick or rank 3 of 8.
- Challenges: picture-word vocab, pairs, riddles with 3 clues, true/false about pictures. Answers go on A-D cards.

A2
- 4-5 days, 2-3 options.
- Grammar: can/can't, should, going to, and comparatives in salvage ('The torch is more useful than the mirror because...').
- Frames: 'We should ___ because ___', 'I agree. / I don't agree.'
- Challenges: gaps with a tap bank, MCQs, unjumble (chunked for teens), odd one out.
- Diary lines are in past simple with one gap.

B1
- 5-6 days. Three options, one with a hidden effect revealed after the vote. Odds pies on risky options, and the rations vote at night.
- Grammar: first conditional plus giving reasons ('If we go to the cave, we'll find water, but...', 'I see your point, but...').
- Challenges: typed or spoken clue-and-answer, error sentences, gaps without a bank, a 'message in a bottle' text with 2-3 questions, taboo-card 'Explorer reports'.
- The Scout crew has a once-per-game Peek power: it sees one hidden cost before the vote.

B2
- 6-7 days. Events interact: a choice on day 2 sets a flag that changes day 5. Options carry several hidden costs, and visitors offer trades. Consensus mode and Secret agendas are available (adults).
- Grammar: second, third and mixed conditionals, concession and negotiation ('Even though..., provided that..., we'd be better off...').
- Challenges: error sentences, clue-and-answer items the teacher judges, debate or hypothetical speaking prompts, and a radio-call finale role-play with an information gap.
- The diary becomes a report with an 'If we had..., we would have...' reflection.

Across levels: the Kolay/Orta/Zor dial changes the night drain (5/10/15), event costs, the word-band mix and hint prices, but not the skin. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the pack one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 15-25 (3-min backpack + 3 days + finale). Arena 25-40 (4-5 days). Stüdyo 30-45 (5-7 days). Short game: 20 min (3 days, quick salvage).
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Scenario (built-in or a prompt) and challenge pack.
- Days, or lesson-fit minutes.
- Difficulty (night drain and costs).
- On/off toggles: hidden effects, odds, rations, Consensus mode, Secret agendas, Hardcore.
- Harshness level.
- Skin and rule-pack overrides, saved to the class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').

LIVE
- Override the vote.
- 'Sürpriz olay': deal one of 6 teacher cards (storm, visitor, lost pet, a bottle on the beach, a birthday on the island, a broken tool).
- 'İngilizce konuştunuz!': Morale +3 and +1 Influence for that team.
- A 'Frame used' tap for each team.
- Manual meter nudge (long-press; logged in the Council Minutes).
- +10 s, T to pause, 'Süresiz'.
- Skip gathering.
- 'Kurtarmaya geç': compress the remaining days into the finale.
- 'Öğretmen okur'.
- TR gloss on/off.
- Seat-number spinner.

PRINT
- A/B/C vote cards (with pictograms for kids).
- Salvage ranking sheet.
- Role cards with the phrase strip.
- Secret agenda cards.
- Survival Diary template for each level.
- Council Minutes and Kaçırılanlar sheet.
catalog.delightDetails:
- A day/night cycle over the scene: a sunrise gradient; stars and crickets at night; on the station, the Earth rising in the window.
- Weather that matches the event: rain streaks, wind in the palms, a solar-flare shimmer.
- Meters wobble for 400 ms before they move, and a 'ghost bar' previews the visible costs while the teacher hovers over an option.
- The camp grows with each decision (a shelter, a raft, a water collector, the salvaged rope hanging on a palm), so the scene becomes a record of the class's choices.
- The signal fire's smoke column rises with Signal. On the last day the rescue ship's silhouette appears on the horizon and grows as the finale plays.
- Each mode has its own vote sound: a woodblock gavel for adults, a synth blip in Arena, and a marimba 'glug' as a jar fills for kids.
- Phrases on the strip tick as they get used ('We used 7 of 9 council phrases').
- Gogo naps with 'zzz' on the pause screen and wears a tiny captain's hat on the final day.
- The kids' animal mascots carry supplies to the jars.
- Crisis cards tilt and shake gently, never with red flashing.
- The diary page fills with handwritten-style past-simple lines after each consequence.
- A final postcard reads 'Rescued on Day 7 · 7-B' over the class's finished camp.
- Crazy Kingdom-style visitors bring requests: a trader canoe, a lost robot, a friendly goat.
catalog.risks:
- Loud students dominate. Mitigations: the seat-number spinner, a 20-s pitch timer, specialist crews pitching first, Objections that cost Influence, and simultaneous card reveals for votes.
- Heated debate slides into Turkish. Turkish is allowed in the huddle at A levels, but pitches are in English with the phrase strip on screen, and the English-only Morale button rewards it.
- Randomness feels unfair. Kids get no risky options. From B1 the odds are shown. Code clamps and balances every effect, so no option is best on every meter.
- Influence snowballs. At most 2 tokens can be spent per vote, and the trailing team breaks ties and gets the Slipstream bonus on Expedition cards.
- The game runs long. Lesson-fit sets the number of days, 'Kurtarmaya geç' jumps to the finale, and gathering is simultaneous rather than team by team.
- Vote counting gets chaotic. Printed cards, a 3-2-1 reveal and teacher-tapped totals keep it quick.
- Scenarios can be sensitive. There are no earthquake, flood, war or refugees-at-sea scenarios. The LLM filter flags 'deprem', 'sel' and 'göçmen' and offers a gentler setting, and the Lost at Sea idea is framed as a holiday plane or sailing trip.
- The expert ranking is debatable. The 'why' is always shown, and the teacher can award Influence for a good counter-argument.
- LLM events can be unbalanced or unsafe. Effects are written as tokens and clamped, the teenSafe filter applies, and the game falls back to built-in events.
- Children worry about empty jars. A jar never drops below 1 notch, a helper animal refills it, and the rescue boat always comes.

issues: The teacher has too much to do while standing at the board. In one Stüdyo or Arena day the teacher taps 'Frame used' per team, tracks Objections and Influence spending for 4-6 teams, taps vote counts plus up to 2 Influence per team, judges pitches, judges the answers of 4-6 teams on 2-3 challenges, runs the Expedition, steals and hints, then the rations vote. That is roughly 25-40 taps a day while also managing behaviour. In a real class the teacher will stop tapping 'Frame used' by day 2, and the Influence economy will quietly collapse.

The ghost-bar hover, long-press meter nudge and 'T to pause' assume a mouse and keyboard. On a Turkish interactive smart board (touch-only, often with laggy long-press recognition) hover never happens, and long-press often fires a right-click or selection.

Language density is low for the time spent. A day is 4-6 minutes but holds only 2-3 challenges and 1 Expedition, so a 40-minute Arena game gives about 12-15 answer moments. Pitches are 20 s by 3-4 speakers, so in a class of 28 each student speaks English for perhaps 20 s in total. Most of the minutes go to reading events, animations, the dawn and night, and meter moves.

The two-minute team huddle with 28 lively 11-year-olds in 6 teams becomes loud Turkish chat. At A levels Turkish is explicitly allowed, and the only counter-weight is a Morale button the teacher has no bandwidth to press.

Salvage consensus does not scale. With 28 students, 'teams nominate items and the teacher drags them into a consensus top 5' in 3 minutes means six groups shouting at once. With 10 adults it works but takes nearer 8-10 minutes than 5, because adults love to argue the ranking. After that the expert-ranking reveal invites 'but a mirror is useless at night' debates that eat more time.

Timing does not fit the lesson. A Turkish public-school lesson is 40 minutes, and roll call plus settling eats about 5. Arena runs 25-40 minutes, and rules plus crew emblem and motto setup add 3-5, so it will not finish in one lesson. There is no save-and-resume across lessons, and 'Kurtarmaya geç' is the only bail-out.

Explaining the Stüdyo ruleset takes too long. Influence, Objections, wagers, hidden effects, odds pies, rations, crises, Secret agendas and harshness levels mean 5+ minutes of rules before any English is produced. Adults will be confused about Influence until about day 3.

Crew sizes for small classes are undefined. Ten adults in 4 crews means pairs of 2-3, which is fine, but the role-to-meter mapping needs 4 crews. The 'fewer than 8 students means 2 crews' rule leaves a gap at 8-11, and 5-6 crews of 2 make the pitching parade repetitive.

The seat-number spinner needs every student to have a known seat number. In a Turkish public school, where desks and pairs shift, the teacher must assign numbers in advance. The design never mentions this as setup.

The printing load is heavy: A/B/C cards per team, salvage sheets, role cards, diary templates and agenda cards. Public-school teachers often have no printer access that day. Mini-whiteboards are not standard in Turkish state classrooms, and without cards the simultaneous 'Boards up!' falls back to shouting.

Dominance persists inside teams. The spinner picks the pitcher, but the strongest student in each team still decides the vote card and writes the whiteboard answer. The kids' stand/sit vote is truly whole-class. The team A-D answer is not individual, so weak students can hide.

Kids version, Oyun Parkı: standing and sitting to vote with 28 children works, but 'every team answers, a wrong answer gets a hint and a second try' means the teacher checks 4 cards, re-hints 1-2 teams and waits. Slow teams create dead time for the others. At 3 days with 2 challenges each, children get only about 6 content items in 20 minutes, which is thin for a vocabulary lesson.

The kids' 60-second night settler plus the 45-second TPR stirrer between days is good pacing. However, counting stars and whispering 'Good night' with 28 ten-year-olds on a smart board can turn into giggling that takes 2 minutes to calm. 11-12 year-olds in Oyun Parkı may find it babyish, yet A1/A2 Genç defaults to it unless the teacher picks grade 6+.

The co-operative meters have no outcome stakes. The boat always comes and the game never ends early, so after day 2 the students see that decisions barely matter. Engagement drops unless Contribution competition carries it, and Contribution is exactly the bookkeeping the teacher skips.

The feature surface is XL. The game has 5 adult, 4 Arena and 4 kids scenarios with 14-18 events each, plus the LLM envelope, validator, print pack and three rulesets. The risk of shipping late or buggy is high compared with its classroom payoff. Much of the adult ruleset, such as Secret agendas, Mutiny and Virus, will be used rarely.
fixes: Add a 'Tek dokunuş' (one-tap) teacher mode as the default. The vote screen shows a big A, B and C button per team as one 4-6 × 3 grid, with no separate count or Influence taps. Influence is spent by the team telling the teacher, entered as '+' chips on the same grid. Contribution is awarded automatically only from challenge-grid taps. 'Frame used' becomes one global button that credits whichever team the spinner last picked.

Make the controls work on touch. Replace hover with tap-to-preview: the first tap on an option shows the ghost bar and the second tap selects. Replace long-press with a visible '±' drawer, and add an on-screen pause button in a fixed corner. Test at 1920×1080 on a smart board with 60 px minimum touch targets.

Raise language density. Make gathering a fast 60-90 s burst of 4-6 items answered simultaneously on cards, with one tap per team per item on a grid. Cut dawn, consequence and night animations to 5 s by default ('Hızlı sahne' on). Aim for at least 20 answer moments in 40 minutes.

Give the huddle a structure. Show a 'Say it in English' starter on screen and require one written line per team (e.g. 'We choose B because...') on the whiteboard or the back of the vote card, then reveal it with the vote. That turns Turkish chat into a short English output that must be produced.

Replace the salvage consensus with a per-team pick. Each team secretly picks its top 3 on the sheet, and the game shows a tally of the most-picked items as the class inventory, with no drag-and-drop negotiation. Then reveal the expert 'why'. Keep full consensus ranking as a Stüdyo opt-in with a hard 6-minute timer.

Add auto-save and a 'Sonraki derste devam' option so the game resumes on the same day with the meters, camp and diary intact. Default Arena to 3 days in a 40-minute slot, and show a lesson-fit warning when the estimate exceeds 'available minutes minus 8'.

Unlock rules in stages. Days 1-2 play with a vote and challenges only, Influence appears on day 2, and Objections and odds appear on day 3. Each unlock gets a 10-s card. Put rations, wagers, agendas and Red harshness behind a single 'Gelişmiş kurallar' toggle that is OFF by default.

Define crew counts by class size: 8-11 students make 3 crews, where one holds two specialisms (e.g. Doctor plus Captain); 12-20 make 4 crews; 21 or more make 5-6. For 10 adults suggest 3 crews of 3-4, so every adult pitches at least twice.
Let the spinner work without printed seat numbers. It can spin team plus 'person 1-6', with students numbering off inside their team at setup. Show a 5-s 'Numaralanın' step on the setup screen.

Make the game work with no printing. Offer an on-screen option where teams show A/B/C with fingers (1, 2 or 3 fingers) and answer A-D with 'four corners' or fingers. The print pack becomes optional, with a 1-page low-ink version.

Hold individuals accountable inside teams. Add an 'Rastgele üye' rule on Expedition cards: the spinner picks the member who must answer, and teammates may only help with the first letter. For kids, add a 'whole class says it' echo after every item so each child produces the word.

Kids: skip the second try when 3 of 4 teams are already correct, where Gogo reveals the answer and the class echoes it together, to cut waiting. Raise to 3-4 picture items per day. Let 11-12 year-olds default to Arena-lite, with Arena visuals and Oyun Parkı rules, when the teacher picks grade 5-6.

Give decisions visible stakes without harshness. The ending and camp postcard should differ clearly by stars, and each choice should permanently change the camp scene or unlock a named ending ('Treehouse ending', 'Raft ending'), so students care about the vote even though the boat always comes.

Scope the build down to M/L for v1. Ship 2 scenarios per audience with 12 events each and the core loop (salvage-lite, vote, gathering, night drain, finale). Defer Secret agendas, the harshness levels, the Blackout and Startup reskins, and LLM-generated full envelopes. Allow LLM generation of the challenge pack only until the envelope validator is proven.

issues: The mechanics grow with the SKIN, but the language demand should grow with the LEVEL. An A1 Genç class in Arena (suggested at grade 6+) or an A1/A2 adult class in Stüdyo gets Influence, 20-s persuasive pitches and Objections. A1-A2 learners cannot produce a 20-s justified pitch, so the council phase turns into Turkish talk or silence, and the most loaded part of the game produces the least English.

At A1/A2 the council is mostly a non-verbal vote: stand or sit, or raise an A/B/C card. For Oyun Parkı the only language in the decision phase is a 0-4-word caption and 'I want the ___'. Nearly all the learning sits in the Gathering quiz. That leaves a thin language yield for 15-25 minutes of narrative wrapper, compared with a plain Baamboozle round.

Gathering challenges from a generic Soru paketi (a grammar unit or category) are cut off from the story. A 'present perfect' MCQ that buys 'water' is just a quiz with a meter skin. Language is only tied to the scenario when the scenario's own word pack is used.

A1 kids who barely read: A-D answer cards assume they can read the four options. Riddles with 3 clues, true/false about pictures and gap tap banks all need reading. The design gives no picture-option answer format and no TTS for options.

The kids' ruleset removes nearly all tension: jars never drop below 1, both options are good, and the boat always comes. That is fine for 9-10-year-olds. But 11-13-year-olds in Oyun Parkı (A1/A2 Genç without the grade 6+ switch) will find it babyish, and the vote carries no consequence, so there is nothing to argue about even in L1.

Adult Stüdyo carries too many economies at once (Influence, Contribution, meters, Signal, hidden costs, odds, rations, crises, wagers, agendas, visitors). Most of the load is on L1 game-state reasoning rather than English, especially for A1/A2 adults, who also get a 30-45-min slot.

The expert ranking in Lost-at-Sea salvage is arguable, and 'distance from expert' scoring punishes good English arguments that reach a different order. At A-level adults, the 'The ___ is more useful than the ___ because...' frame is the only real production in an 8-min phase.

LLM realism is weak. One Turkish prompt has to yield a whole envelope that passes validation: 14-18 balanced events with effect tokens, a valid expertRank permutation, level-capped 'why' lines, picturable salvage and diary lines. Failure is likely, and the fallback to built-in events silently throws away the teacher's prompt ('Kapadokya balonu' turns into Desert Island).

Kids need a picture for every event and option. Built-in content alone is 13 scenarios × 14-18 events × 2-3 options, about 400-700 illustrations. LLM scenarios have no image source, so for A1/A2 Genç most generated events would be dropped under the 'unpicturable' rule, and the prompt path hardly works for the youngest groups.

Teacher load is high in class: tapping vote counts per team, 'Frame used' per team, 'English-only' taps, the spinner, overrides and reading events. The quality of production feedback depends on one adult tracking 4-6 teams in real time.
B2 teens are handled by Arena, but Consensus mode and Secret agendas, the best B2 negotiation practice, are adult-only. B2 Genç then gets less production than B2 adults, with no age reason for it.

The past-simple Survival Diary is automatic: the game writes 'We built a raft.', so students read it rather than write it. The writing skill is claimed but not actually practised unless the diary template is filled in by students.
fixes: Tie the council's language demand to LEVEL, not skin. A1: no pitches, just a picture vote plus a chorus of the chosen frame ('Let's fish!'). A2: 'sentence builder' pitches where the spokesperson reads a tap-assembled frame ('We should ___ because ___' with a picture bank), 10 s. B1+: free 20-s pitches and Objections. Arena at A1/A2 keeps the neon HUD but uses the A-level council.

Make the vote itself produce language at every level. Before the card goes up, each team must chorus its choice in the level frame ('We choose B because we need water'). The teacher's 'Frame used' tap becomes a whole-team chorus check, so the whole class speaks every turn.

Default the Soru paketi to the scenario's own vocab pack and make EXPEDITION cards always scenario-bound (the event word in a gap, a riddle or a taboo card). When a generic grammar pack is chosen, have the LLM or a template wrap the items in scenario sentences ('Complete the radio message: We ___ (be) here since Monday').

For A1 Genç, add picture-option answers (A-D cards show pictures, the options are read by TTS) and TTS on every caption, event and hint. Ban text-only item types (error, order with long chunks, text) in A1 Genç gathering.

Give Oyun Parkı a light but real stake: options differ visibly in which jar fills, and a 'jar goal' per day ('Today we need water!') makes the choice meaningful and lets kids say 'Water! We need water!'. Offer a 'Macera' variant for 11-13 A-level classes: Arena visuals with Oyun Parkı rules plus the A-level sentence-builder council.
Ship Stüdyo A1/A2 as 'Council Lite': no hidden costs, odds, rations, wagers or agendas; Influence only for frames used; 4 days. Unlock the full economy at B1 and the interacting events at B2.

Score salvage by argument as well as by distance. Teams whose justification the teacher accepts get +1 Influence, and the expert ranking is shown as 'one expert view'. At B1+ add a 60-s 'defend your #1' round so the phase produces more than one frame.

Split LLM generation into small, validated steps (scenario plus meters, then salvage, then events in batches), with retries per event. Keep the teacher's valid events and fill the gaps from the closest built-in scenario while keeping their setting name. Tell the teacher in Turkish what was replaced.

Solve the picture problem: for LLM scenarios, build events from a fixed icon and scene library (the LLM picks from enumerated scene and icon ids) instead of free-form pictures. Cut the built-in kids' scenarios to 2 at launch.

Cut the teacher's tapping. Votes can be one tap per option with a hand-count keypad; 'Frame used' becomes a single 'strip phrase heard' tap that awards the speaking team. Offer a 'Kolay yönetim' preset that turns off Objections, wagers and rations.
Give B2 Genç (Arena) Secret agendas and Consensus mode as opt-ins, with teen-safe agendas ('Your crew wants to build a treehouse').

Make the diary production real. At A2+ the game shows the diary line with a gap or as a picture prompt, and a team writes or says it before it appears. At B2 students write the 'If we had..., we would have...' reflection and the auto-built version is shown after them as a model.
Consider building this on the same story-node engine as the RPG/Crossroads candidate (a shared meters and fork engine), to reduce the XL cost while keeping it a separate game in the menu.

issues: Not a duplicate. The shared meters, council vote and salvage ranking make it the only candidate built around persuasive speaking, and Lost at Sea is a proven ESL activity that adults and 12-14s respond to. It does share its engine with the RPG and Crossroads candidates (story-node, choices, flags, diary). If the three are built separately, the fork/effects/flags runtime and the LLM validator get built three times.

The scope is an XL game with at least 15 subsystems: salvage ranking, 4 meters plus Signal, per-team Contribution and Influence, Objections, wagers, odds pies, hidden effects, rations, crisis cards, Hardcore, Consensus mode, Secret agendas, visitors, the Explorer map, Scout Peek, Red harshness (Mutiny/Storm/Virus), the radio finale and a third-conditional report. Shipped all at once it becomes a rules spreadsheet, not a polished game. Most of these features will be tested in class by nobody.

Teacher input overload on one smartboard. In a single day the teacher taps vote counts per option, Influence spent per team, 'Frame used' per team, English-only, a correct answer per team for 2-3 challenges plus the Expedition card, and runs the seat spinner, TTS and timers. With 6 teams that is roughly 30-40 taps per day while also moderating a debate. In practice the Influence economy will be ignored or tracked wrongly, and the game falls apart quietly.

The timing doesn't fit Turkish 40-min lessons. Stüdyo 5-7 days × 4-6 min, plus 5-8 min of salvage, setup and the finale, comes to 45-55 min. Arena at 4-5 days is also tight. There is no save/resume across lessons.

Signal is the co-op win track, but only the Engineer crew feeds it. The class's ending then depends on one team's quiz accuracy, and a weak team in that seat ruins the ending for everyone. Morale is fed only when there are 5+ teams, so with 4 teams it has no crew.

The HUD holds too many numbers: 4 meters, Signal, per-team Contribution, per-team Influence, the phrase strip, a timer and an odds pie. From the back row of a projected classroom this becomes unreadable clutter.

The gathering phase is a plain simultaneous quiz, the same core as sinif-oyunu and every quiz candidate. On its own it adds nothing new. The fiction only pays off if answers visibly move the camp and the meters.

LLM content risks. (a) expertRank is presented as 'expert', but an LLM invents it, and its salvage rankings for novel settings (Kapadokya balloon) are arbitrary, which undermines the scored reveal. (b) 'No event depends on an unpicturable item' can't be validated, because words.js has no images and there is no icon library to check refs against. (c) The whole-envelope output (meters, roles, 8-12 salvage items, 14-18 fork nodes with effects, flags, diary lines, endings) is long, and DeepSeek will often break JSON shape, invent flags that are never set, or exceed word caps. Falling back to built-in events silently discards the teacher's prompt.

Flags that interact across days (B2) and 'requires {item}' options can leave an event with only one valid option, or none, if the class didn't salvage the item. Nothing guarantees at least 2 available options.

The authoring load is large: 13 built-in scenarios × 14-18 events ≈ 200 events. Each needs a picture, effects, a diary line, TR glosses and level-capped text, plus per-skin scene art with camp growth layers (shelter/raft/collector per skin), weather layers, animated Gogo states and animal carriers.

Kids ruleset. 'Both options are good' plus a jar floor of 1 plus 'the boat always comes' leaves the vote without stakes. 9-11s will notice after day 1. Stand/sit voting for A vs B works, but the Oyun Parkı variant is really a picture-vocab quiz with a jar animation. It passes the checklist but feels thin for the effort.
