Browser TTS quality on Windows/Android smartboards (MEB Pardus boards) varies and may lack an English voice. Event read-aloud and 'letters read aloud' can't rely on it.
The Arena Raid and Red harshness (Mutiny/Storm) contradict the co-op frame and add more code paths for little teaching value.
fixes: Build a shared 'Hikâye Motoru' module (story-node runtime: fork/choice/effects tokens → clamp, flags/requires with a guaranteed ≥2 available options, diary lines, endings, validator). Share it with the RPG and Crossroads candidates, and reuse sinif-oyunu's question and hint engine for gathering. Keep Issız Ada as its own game on top of it.

Launch as an MVP (L, not XL): Day 0 salvage; a 4-meter + Signal day loop (dawn → event → huddle → pitches with the seat spinner → 3-2-1 card vote with count taps → consequence → 2 simultaneous challenges + 1 Expedition → night drain); crisis = Signal -15; stars; diary export. Defer Objections, wagers, rations, Consensus, Secret agendas, visitors, the Explorer map, Peek, Red harshness, Hardcore and Raid to v2, behind toggles, once real class feedback shows they're wanted.

Simplify Influence: one team-level counter, spent only on +1 vote (max 2) and pitch-first priority, and earned only from correct Expedition answers and 'Frame used'. Put 'Frame used' on large per-team buttons along the bottom edge. Cap teacher input per day with a single 'Consequence' confirm screen where the team's result is pre-filled.

Enter vote counts in one tap per option using a +/- stepper, or have teams hold up cards while the teacher just taps the winning option. In Oyun Parkı, drop counting entirely (stand/sit, the teacher taps the winner).

Let every correct answer choose its meter. A team taps an icon for which jar or meter gets the supply, with its specialism doubling the gain. Signal rises from the class total each day plus the finale radio call, so no single team gates the ending. With 4 teams, fold Morale into the Captain role, held by whichever team wins the vote.
Make lesson-fit the default: 4 days for 40 min (Stüdyo), 3-4 for Arena, 3 for kids. Add autosave to localStorage with 'Devam et' (resume next lesson), so 7-day B2 campaigns span two lessons.

HUD: the scene takes 70% of the screen. Meters are 4 large icon bars top-left and a smoke column for Signal. Team Influence and Contribution appear only in a collapsible bottom strip and during the vote. Show numbers on meters only at B1+ Stüdyo.

LLM pipeline: generate in two calls (1: meters, roles, salvage with why; 2: events in batches of 6). Use strict JSON schema prompts and a zod-style validator that repairs rather than rejects: re-clamp effects, drop orphan flags, strip 'requires' when the item is missing, truncate to word caps, and re-ask for only the failed nodes (max 1 retry). Show the teacher a preview list with a per-event 'Değiştir' before play, and label the salvage key 'Önerilen sıralama' rather than 'expert'. When falling back, say so in Turkish.

Build a curated icon library (~150 flat SVGs: survival items, foods, tools, weather, animals) with an id list. The LLM must pick salvage and option pictures only from that list, which makes 'picturable' checkable. Events in kids mode must use listed icons or they are dropped.

Reduce launch content to Desert Island (all modes), Stranded Kommo-1 (Arena), Blackout 48h and Startup Survival (Stüdyo), 12 events each, with per-skin art as layered SVG (background + 6 camp growth parts + weather canvas particles). Pre-generate event drafts offline with the LLM, then hand-curate them.

Give kids votes some stakes without harshness: the option chosen decides which scene part appears and which helper animal visits, and a 'surprise' reveal after the vote (a hidden treasure behind one picture) makes the choice feel real. Keep 3 rules. Add a picture-only printable A/B card.

Audio: ship pre-recorded or pre-generated MP3s for built-in event lines and kid prompts; TTS is used only for LLM content, with 'Öğretmen okur' as the automatic fallback when no en-* voice exists. Sound set (~15 SFX): gavel, synth blip, marimba glug, rain, crickets, wind, ship horn, jar fill, boing, sticker pop.

Smartboard input: all targets at least 64px, no hover-dependent features (the ghost-bar preview must also trigger on tap-and-hold), and a keyboard map for the presenter (1-3 votes, space next, T pause). An optional presenter view on a second window shows the hidden effects and the answer key.
Drop Raid, Mutiny and Storm entirely. They conflict with the co-operative core and the teenSafe or Nazik mode spirit, and they add test surface.

catalog.rankReason: The only persuasive-speaking council game (adult 8; Lost at Sea is proven in ESL). It is XL, so it comes later as an MVP on a 'Hikâye Motoru' shared with c04. It needs a one-tap teacher vote grid, a language demand tied to level rather than skin, and every vote chorused in a frame.

catalog.name: Sorgu Odası (Alibi & Two Truths and a Lie)
catalog.familiarAs: The Alibi game / Two Truths and a Lie / Would I Lie to You?
catalog.oneLiner: Real people take the hot seat. In one mode, teams spend a few questions to catch the lie among a generated character's three statements. In the other, two alibi partners are questioned separately while the screen lines up their answers on a timeline and flashes every contradiction.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (1 min). The setup line reads, for example, 'B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 30 sn · 40 dk' with a 'Değiştir' link. The teacher picks content (a built-in category, or a free-text prompt such as 'Kapadokya gezisi, present perfect') and a MODE:
(1) YALANCIYI BUL: 10-20 min, 4-6 characters.
(2) ALİBİ: 25-40 min, 3-4 suspect rounds.
(3) TAM DOSYA: 40-45 min. A teacher-played character comes first as a 5-min warm-up that models the question forms, then Alibi, then the review.
(4) ÖĞRETMENİN SIRRI: a 5-min filler. The teacher tells two truths and a lie about themselves. Sentence frames show on screen; nothing is typed or stored.
Teams: 2-5 (Alibi: 3-4). An optional print pack holds the secret character cards ('Gizli Dosya'), Alibi Sheets, Detective Notebooks (columns Q | A | B) and 1-2-3 vote cards.

MODE 1 · YALANCIYI BUL (about 3-4 min per character)
1) CARD. The character appears under a spotlight with an avatar, a name and a one-line intro. The 3 numbered statements then drop in one by one, following the options delay (kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s). Each statement has a speaker button.
2) HOT SEAT. The teacher sits in the hot seat (always at A1/A2 Genç), or a B1+ volunteer does. They hold the secret profile on the phone remote (via QR), in a presenter window, or on the printed Gizli Dosya card. The profile shows which statement is the lie, the truth behind it, a cover story with one planted slip, and a ready answer for every question chip.
3) QUESTIONS. Teams take turns spending question tokens (default 3 each), and the trailing team starts. Each turn has a huddle (10/15/20 s). Then the spokesperson asks one follow-up in English ('When did you climb it?'). The seat spinner picks the spokesperson for kids and Arena; adults rotate. Question chips scaffold the form (Where / When / Who / How long / Why / Have you ever...?).
- The teacher taps G for a clean question, which earns a grammar badge.
- The teacher taps R for a recast: the correct form shows for 3 s and the team asks again. The first recast costs no token.
The hot seat answers, and the tapped chip writes the question and answer into the interview log in the team colour.
4) VOTE. The lie-detector needle wobbles. On 'Show!', every team raises its 1/2/3 card at the same moment (kids: the whole class shows fingers). The teacher keys the votes in, hidden.
5) REVEAL. The lie flips red with a stamp and the truths turn green. The profile slides in with the truth and the planted slip highlighted, plus the log line where a team asked about it.
6) BEST QUESTION. The teacher may tap one question as 'Best question' for the Hall of Questions.
Code balances the lie position across characters, so 'it's always number 3' never works.

MODE 2 · ALİBİ (3-4 rounds, 7-9 min each)
1) CASE. A case file opens: 'Case 07: The office party cake vanished between 7 and 9 p.m. yesterday.' A 7:00-9:00 timeline bar fills the bottom of the screen.
2) PREP (adults 8-10 min, Arena 6, kids 5). EVERY team builds one shared alibi on its Alibi Sheet, using the prep cards on screen: where you were, when you left, who else was there, what you wore and ate, the weather, what was on TV, how you got home. The two suspects are picked AFTER prep, by the seat spinner (in Nazik mode: volunteers, plus a 'pass to a friend' joker). So everyone on the team has to learn the story.
3) SPLIT. Suspect B waits in the doorway, or wears headphones playing the waiting-room loop from the teacher's phone. Suspect A sits in the spotlight inside an ID frame with the team name.
4) QUESTION A (3 min, up to 8 questions). The other teams take turns asking, using the chips, and each question is pinned to a time slot. The scribe logs 1-3-word answers in column A. The scribe is the teacher, a student at the keyboard, or someone tapping picture chips. The suspect team stays silent; if it signals, the detectives get a free mismatch.
5) QUESTION B. B returns and column A is covered with 'CLASSIFIED' tape. The screen replays the same questions in the same order. At B1+, each detective team may add one new follow-up.
6) COMPARE. The tape tears away and A and B sit side by side on the timeline. For each row, the whole class shows thumbs up (same) or thumbs down (different) together. Then the teacher taps M (match), X (mismatch) or ~ ('close enough', which counts as a match). Mismatches flash red with a stamp and a clack, and the counter ticks up.
7) VERDICT. If mismatches reach the threshold (default 3), the stamp reads ALIBI BROKEN; otherwise ALIBI HOLDS. An optional forfeit card follows. At B2, one detective team presents the case in reported speech.
8) NEXT ROUND. The next team's suspects take the seat. At the end, the 'real culprit' is revealed as a joke (the office cat, the cleaning robot), so no student is ever truly guilty.

SCORING (Stüdyo values; Arena multiplies by its combo; Oyun Parkı uses stars, see the teen version)
- Yalancıyı Bul: a correct verdict scores 20, each unused token +5, and the best question +5. A student in the hot seat earns their team +10 for each team fooled; that team does not vote on its own character.
- Alibi: detectives score +10 for each mismatch their question exposed and +5 per grammar badge. The suspects' team scores +5 per matched row, plus 20 if the alibi holds.
- Comeback (Light): the last team gets a +5 Slipstream bonus when it scores, and it chooses the next character or case.
- Adult-only extras: an optional -5 for a wrong verdict, and a final wager character (bet up to half your points).
- No score ever goes below 0.

END. The Hall of Questions shows the best question from each round, followed by the awards. Adults also get the 'Kaçırılanlar' list: every recast question with its correct form, plus the full log, which can be exported as a 'police report' writing task.
catalog.playerSetup: The whole class plays in 2-5 teams of 3-8. In Alibi, 3-4 teams: each team supplies one suspect pair in its own round and is a detective team in every other round, so nobody is idle. There is one hot seat per character: the teacher, or a B1+ student volunteer. Roles: a spokesperson picked by the seat-number spinner (adults rotate; nobody is ever named); a scribe (the teacher, or a student at the keyboard or tapping picture chips); an optional timekeeper. It works with 12-36 students. With more than 32, keep 4 teams and cap Alibi at 3 rounds.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Sorgu Odası: Would I Lie to You? edition'.

LOOK. An editorial case-file look. On cream, a manila folder with a paper clip, labels in a typewriter accent (body text stays system sans) and a desk-lamp cone of light on the suspect's nameplate. The dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme is an interrogation room with venetian-blind shadows. There is no mascot. Neutral captions read 'Suspect B · Q5/8' and 'Case 03 · Travel'.

SOUND. Woodblock clacks for mismatches, a piano chord for reveals and a soft typewriter tick when the scribe logs (each 1 s or less). Music is off.

CHARACTERS. A travel blogger, a retired pilot, a chef, a startup founder, a wedding photographer, a night-shift nurse, an ex-circus juggler. Example (B1, present perfect vs past simple): 'I have climbed a volcano.' / 'I have met a famous chef.' / 'I have never flown in a plane.' The cover story leaks 'I flew back from Iceland the next day' when a team asks 'How did you get home?'.

CASES. Who took the office party cake? The leaked email. The dented company car. Who ate the last baklava in the staff kitchen? The broken coffee machine. The hotel key card that opened the wrong room.

GRAMMAR BY LEVEL. B1: present perfect vs past simple, 'used to', past continuous alibis. B2: past perfect, conditionals, indirect questions, and reported speech in the verdict ('He said he had been at the gym, but she told us they had taken a taxi at 7:30').

EXTRAS
- 'Would I Lie to You?' panel: two B1+ students each draw a character card, get 30 s with the secret profile, and defend their statements side by side.
- Wager round: the final character is a wager round.
- Harshness: Green and Yellow by default; Red is optional and off.
- Hints: a hint ladder on the chips (the wh-word, then the frame, then the full model question). Each rung costs 2 points, never below 0. The Turkish gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.

ENDING. Full scores, the Hall of Questions and 'Kaçırılanlar'. The exported Q&A log becomes a 'witness statement' homework task.

Teachers of corporate classes can keep to generated characters only, so colleagues never lie about their real lives.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two stripped rulesets, not re-coloured adult ones. The group label is never shown to students.

OYUN PARKI (9-11, Nazik ON): 'Gogo Dedektif'

LOOK AND SOUND. Warm cream, rounded cards, big pictures and an Andika-type font. Team mascots are animals (panda, fox, lion, frog...). Gogo the parrot wears a detective cap and holds a torch; the torch beam is the spotlight. Sounds come from a marimba pack, with no buzzers. The timer is off (40 s calm ring if switched on). Huddles last 10 s.

(a) TRUE OR SILLY? (Two Truths)
- Characters: a robot from the future, a talking cat, a young astronaut, a wizard apprentice, a dragon who loves ice cream.
- The teacher is always in the hot seat. A printable character headband adds to the fun.
- Rules (3, with pictograms): 1) Listen: 3 sentences. 2) Ask with a picture chip. 3) Show 1, 2 or 3 fingers for the silly one!
- Statements carry pictures. At A1 the silly lie can be seen in the avatar ('I have got 12 legs' next to a 4-legged cat).
- Each team has 2 chip questions. The teacher reads the answer from the phone.
- Reveal: the silly sentence pops like a balloon with a 'Silly!' sticker and Gogo laughs. The class repeats both true sentences twice.
- Practice round: Gogo's demo, which does not score: 'I can fly. I can swim. I can talk!' (Parrots talk!)

(b) TWIN STORIES (Alibi)
- Mysteries: 'Hammy the hamster is out!', 'The cookie jar is empty!', 'Where is the class football?'
- Photo Alibi: each team circles 1 picture per row on the printed sheet (place, food, friend, activity, T-shirt colour).
- Two volunteers become the 'twins'; the 'pass to a friend' joker is always available. Twin B waits by the door with headphones.
- Rules (3): 1) Two friends make one story. 2) We ask each friend the same 4 questions. 3) Everyone shows thumbs: same or different?
- The scribe taps picture chips, so the comparison is automatic and there is no typing.
- Match: the puzzle pieces click and the twins' team gets a star.
- Different: 'Oops! Mixed-up story!' The pieces wobble, Gogo scratches his head, and the WHOLE class does the silly action together ('Walk like a penguin!'). Nobody is punished alone.
- There is no 'guilty', 'police' or 'prison'. At the end Gogo reveals the real culprit: the class cat, with cookie crumbs on its whiskers.

KIDS CHECKLIST. The kids variant passes all six checks: 3 rules, a 20-s pictogram explanation, no elimination, scores never go down, a whole-class response every turn (fingers or thumbs), and non-violent failure imagery (balloons, puzzle pieces).

SCORING AND PACING. Stars: a right finger vote earns 2, each chip question 1, each twin match 1. A miss becomes an effort star in the class album. There are 3 rounds of 4-5 min with a 45 s 'Freeze like a statue' stirrer, 15-25 min in total. Every team gets a title (Best Twins, Super Askers, Sharp Eyes) and a 'Junior Detectives' sticker. The Turkish rule card and pictograms are for the teacher; students see tiny English ('Your turn!', 'Same?', 'Show me!').

ARENA (12-14; also for Genç groups in grade 6+ or when 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor' is ticked): 'LIAR LIAR' and 'BREAK THE ALIBI'

LOOK AND SOUND. Dark navy with neon team colours and a condensed display font. The spotlight is a scanner beam, the lie detector is a neon waveform, and 'ALIBI CRACKED' appears as glitch text. Sounds are synth blips. There is no mascot and no pastels. A commentator strip shows at most once per turn ('CLEAN QUESTION', 'CONTRADICTION!', 'LIE HUNTER').

OWNERSHIP. In 10 s, each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.

CONTENT
- Characters: a time traveller from 2080, a deep-sea explorer, a young inventor, a museum night guard, a drone racer, a mountain-rescue volunteer.
- Cases: 'Who changed the class Wi-Fi password?', 'The missing trophy before the final', 'Who hacked the quiz leaderboard?', 'The drone in the principal's garden'.
- The hot seat is the teacher at A1/A2 Genç. At B1/B2 Genç it can be a volunteer with the printed profile, whose team wins a 'Poker Face' bonus if at most 1 team finds the lie.

RULES
- 3 tokens per team and a 30 s timer ring in the team colour.
- Verdicts go on mini-whiteboards.
- Streak and combo: x1.5 at 3 and x2 at 5, counting clean questions and correct verdicts (accuracy only, never speed).
- A malformed question can be stolen by one other team that rephrases it correctly; the first team loses nothing.
- Suspects are picked by the spinner, with a pass joker.
- Forfeits are optional: the pair picks 1 of 3 or skips.

NAZIK UNDERNEATH. Scores never drop below 0, nobody is named and there is no public last place.

PACING AND ENDINGS. Rounds of 5-7 min. The finale is a podium plus stat awards: Iron Alibi, Lie Hunter, Sharpest Question, Clean Sheet, Comeback. There is an English rule card with a Turkish toggle.

CONTENT FILTER (both modes). All Genç content passes teenSafe: fictional characters and places only, nothing about real people, no dating, violence, brands, money or office domains. 'Crimes' are mysteries without victims.
catalog.levelTuning:
Statements and prompts respect the word caps: A1 Genç 0-4, A2 Genç 8, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40. A long intro is split into two cards.

A1
- Two Truths: can / have got / like / there is, with yes/no chips ('Can you...?', 'Have you got...?', 'Do you like...?'). Answers are 'Yes, I can.' plus one detail. The lie is obvious, from the picture or common sense. 2 tokens per team.
- Alibi for A1 Genç: 'Photo Alibi' in the present continuous ('It's a photo. Where are you? What are you eating?'). 4 fixed picture questions, picture-chip answers, auto-compare, threshold 2 of 4.
- Alibi for A1 adults: 5 fixed was/were questions ('Where were you? Who was with you? What was on TV? What was the weather like?'). Answers are nouns tapped from a word bank.

A2
- Two Truths: past simple and was/were; wh-questions with chips ('Where did you...?', 'When did you...?', 'Who did you go with?'). One planted slip exposes the lie. 3 tokens.
- Alibi: past simple ('Where were you at 8?', 'What did you eat?', 'How did you get home?'). 6 questions, chips on, 1-3-word typed or tapped answers, threshold 3 of 6.

B1
- Two Truths: present perfect vs past simple ('Have you ever...?' leading into 'When did you...?'), and 'used to'. The lie is subtle: its slip only comes out under a follow-up. A student hot seat is the default for adults.
- Alibi: past continuous with an interrupting past simple, anchored to timeline slots ('What were you doing at 7:30?', 'What were you doing when the fire alarm went off?'). 8 questions, plus 1 free follow-up per team for B. Mid-round the teacher may drop an evidence card ('A witness saw a red umbrella at 8:15'). Chips are optional; threshold 3.

B2
- Two Truths: past perfect, conditionals, mixed time, and hedged answers ('As far as I remember...'). The lie can only be inferred by combining 2 profile details; neither detail proves it alone. Fewer, sharper tokens (2). 'Would I Lie to You?' panel and a final wager.
- Alibi: open follow-ups with chips off (hint ladder instead) and indirect questions ('Could you tell us what time you left?'). Each team gets one Bluff card: a detective falsely quotes suspect A to trap B, using reported speech ('Your partner told us you had taken a taxi'). 10 questions, threshold 3-4. The verdict is presented in reported speech from a frame.
- B2 Genç: richer language on concrete topics (inventions, expeditions, school events), never abstract debate.

ACROSS LEVELS
- A1/A2 Genç: every statement, chip and alibi option needs an imageKey, and items that cannot be pictured are dropped. Read-aloud runs automatically at 0.8x; other groups get a speaker button on every item.
- The Kolay/Orta/Zor dial shifts the chip level, adds or removes a token, changes how obvious the lie is, and moves the threshold by 1, without changing the skin. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole profile one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Yalancıyı Bul 10-20 (4-6 characters) · Alibi 25-40 (3-4 rounds) · Tam Dosya 40-45 · Oyun Parkı 15-25 · Öğretmenin Sırrı filler 5
catalog.contentShape:
pack.frames.sorgu = { characters[], alibi, ownStory[] }. Question templates are code-owned. The LLM never invents template ids; it only fills answers keyed by them. The library is shared with c26 'Kim Yaptı?'. Each template has an id (e.g. 'past-where', 'pastcont-at-time', 'pp-ever', 'pp-when-followup', 'b2-indirect-when'), level, chip text EN, icon/imageKey, tense tag and slot type.

1) characters[] (4-8 'character' items). Fields: name (fictional, from the name pool), avatar (sticker key), intro (one line), statements[3], lieIndex, profile[6-10], answers {'<statementIdx>:<templateId>': text}, plus two extensions: tells[] (profile facts that expose the lie, stored as string references to the lie's key noun or number) and reveal (a one-line truth, e.g. 'Truth: I have never left Turkey. My passport is empty.').
How it is generated: the LLM returns 3 CLAIMS. Each claim has text, trueFacts[], truthAnswers {tplId: text} and a coverStory {answers {tplId: text}, slip: the one answer that leaks the truth}. CODE then picks lieIndex (balanced across the pack) and compiles the item: profile = the facts supporting the truths + at least 2 exposing facts for the lie; answers = truth answers for the truths + cover answers for the lie.
Validator:
- every statement is within the word cap and uses the target grammar (light regex/POS check, e.g. have + past participle);
- every truth is supported by at least 1 profile fact;
- the lie has at least 2 tells (at B2, only their combination proves the lie);
- at least 6 chip answers exist per claim;
- no real people; Genç groups get fictional places only, and adults get no checkable facts about real places;
- teenSafe applies to Genç groups.

2) alibi = { cases: 'roleplay' items (3-6), prepCards: 'speaking-prompt' items (mode 'ask'), forfeits: 'chance-card' items (kind 'task', task 'act'|'sing'|'speak'|'spell', a short text in English and textTr for kids; a whole-class version for Oyun Parkı), evidenceDrops: 'chance-card' items (kind 'bonus', one-line witness facts for B1+) }.
Each case roleplay item maps: scenario = the case headline, setting = place + time window {from, to} for the timeline, roleA = Suspects {info: prep categories, goals: 'agree on every detail', useful: answer frames}, roleB = Detectives {goals: 'find 3 differences', useful: question frames}, twist = the evidence drop, checklist = teacher criteria (e.g. 'used past continuous with at + time'), secs = prep time, plus jokeCulprit (the cat or robot revealed at the end).
Each prepCard carries prompt ('What did you eat?'), starters (answer frames), useful[≤5] and, for A1/A2 Genç, media.emoji or imageKey options (4-6 pictures per row for the Photo Alibi sheet).
Kids' cases must avoid the words steal, police, prison, guilty and crime.

3) ownStory[]: 'speaking-prompt' items (mode 'talk') with starters such as 'I have been to...', 'I can...', 'I have never...', for Öğretmenin Sırrı and the opt-in student version. Topics are limited to hobbies, abilities and places; nothing personal is typed or stored.

Runtime state (not content): log rows {questionTplId, filledText, team, slot, ansA, ansB, mark 'M'|'X'|'~', badge}, votes, tokens, streak.

A free-text Turkish prompt maps to a category plus a grammar target. 'Bu karakteri yenile' and 'Bu vakayı yenile' regenerate a single item.
catalog.teacherControls: Mode (Yalancıyı Bul / Alibi / Tam Dosya / Öğretmenin Sırrı). Tokens per team (1-5). Questions per suspect (4-12). Verdict threshold (2-5, or a share of the questions). Prep timer and per-suspect timer, with +10 s, T to pause and 'Süresiz'. Chips on/off and chip level (one level lower for mixed classes). Hint ladder and the Turkish gloss on/off. Scribe mode: teacher types, student scribe, picture chips, or paper-only (a Detective Notebook in which the teacher just taps M/X). Hot seat: teacher or student, with the student option unlockable at any level. Secret profile shown on the phone remote (QR), in a presenter window on an extended display, or on a printed card. Lie-position balancing on/off. Reveal, next character and 'regenerate this one'. Evidence drop button (B1+). Bluff cards on/off (B2). Forfeits: off, whole-class, or pair picks 1 of 3. Steal on malformed questions (Arena default; optional for adults). Optional negatives and wager (adults). Comeback dial. Harshness level within what the mode allows. Suspect picking: spinner, volunteers, or spinner plus pass joker. Keyboard: Space next, R reveal, G grammar badge, E recast, M/X/~ mark rows, B best question, 1-5 select team, P show/hide the log. Print pack: Gizli Dosya cards, Alibi Sheets (picture version for A1/A2 Genç), Detective Notebooks, 1-2-3 vote cards, character headbands. Export the Kaçırılanlar list and the Q&A log as a PDF homework sheet. The class profile ('7-B · A2 Genç · Arena') remembers every setting.
catalog.delightDetails: A police-lamp spotlight on the suspect's nameplate: a desk lamp in Stüdyo, a scanner beam in Arena, Gogo's torch circle in Oyun Parkı. An ID frame with the team name and a height chart behind it (a playful 'photo booth' frame for kids, never a mugshot). 'CLASSIFIED' tape over column A that tears away for the comparison. A two-track timeline where A's and B's answers sit in time slots and the contradictions glow red on the exact minute, marked with a ✗ shape too, so the red is colour-blind safe. A mismatch counter that ticks up with a clack (a marimba 'boing' for kids). A stamp for ALIBI HOLDS / ALIBI BROKEN (Twin stories! / Oops! Mixed-up story! for kids). A lie-detector needle, or a neon waveform in Arena, that wobbles as the hidden votes come in and swings to the lie on reveal. A dramatic card flip: the lie turns red, the truths green, and the planted slip in the log is highlighted with 'This gave it away'. Code balances the lie position, so a team that always guesses 3 gets caught out. Every question a team asks sits in the log in its team colour, so teams can see their own contribution. The Hall of Questions at the end, with the best question of each round framed like an award. The joke culprit reveal, so nobody leaves 'guilty' (the office cat with frosting on its paw, the cleaning robot, the class cat with cookie crumbs). Evidence-drop cards that land on the desk with a paper-slap sound. A 'Case closed' folder that slides into a filing cabinet between rounds. A coffee-ring stain on the adult case file. Printable character headbands for the teacher. Gogo's parrot demo ('I can talk!' is true). Arena stat awards: Iron Alibi, Lie Hunter, Sharpest Question, Clean Sheet, Comeback. Reduced motion swaps every animation for a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- Students slip into the past simple where the past continuous is the target. Chips and timeline slots are anchored to 'at + time' and 'when...', the teacher recasts with one key, and the Kaçırılanlar list reviews it.
- Alibi runs long with many teams. Cap it at 3-4 rounds, prep all teams at the same time, keep answers to 1-3 words, and let the lesson-fit timer cut the question count.
- Shy students. The team builds the alibi together, suspects are picked by spinner with a pass joker (volunteers in Nazik mode), and nobody is named. Oyun Parkı forfeits are done by the whole class.
- Suspect B overhears. Use the doorway or headphones; column A stays under the tape, and the suspect team must stay silent (a signal gives the detectives a free mismatch).
- Arguments over whether two answers match. The class votes first and the teacher's M/X/~ is final; '~ close enough' counts as a match.
- An inconsistent generated profile. Code picks the lie, the validator requires at least 1 support per truth and at least 2 tells for the lie, and the teacher can regenerate one character.
- Invented facts about real places. Genç groups use fictional settings only; adults get no checkable facts.
- A teacher who cannot improvise in the hot seat. Every chip has a pre-generated answer, plus neutral fallback lines ('I can't remember exactly').
- A student in the hot seat reveals the lie by accident. Give them 30 s to read and a 'poker face' tip. Student hot seats are off for Oyun Parkı.
- Kids and 'guilt'. No crime words, a joke culprit, and non-violent stamps.
- Privacy in the personal version. Only the teacher does it by default; students opt in with safe frames, and nothing is typed or stored.
- Corporate or adult classes where lying about real lives feels awkward. Use generated characters only.
- Scribe typing slows the game. Use picture chips, a student scribe or the paper-only mode.
reviewVerdicts: logistics: keep-with-changes -> c26 (Kim Yaptı?): share the question-template library, timeline, log and print engine, but keep this as a separate game on the menu
feasibility: keep-with-changes -> c26 (Kim Yaptı?) as a shared 'Dedektif' engine only: template library, case file UI, stamps, log and print pack. The two games stay separate modes.

reviews.mergeWith: c26 (Kim Yaptı?): share the question-template library, timeline, log and print engine, but keep this as a separate game on the menu
issues: WALKTHROUGH, 28 kids, Alibi / Twin Stories. Minutes 0-3: setup, plus handing out the printed Photo Alibi sheets (these must be printed the day before, and public-school printers are unreliable). Minutes 3-8: 4 teams of 7 each circle one picture per row. In practice 1-2 kids per team hold the pencil and 5 chat, so noise peaks here. Minutes 8-10: pick the twins, send B out. Minutes 10-14: ask A 4 questions, but only the twin and 1 spokesperson are active and about 25 kids wait. Minutes 14-17: B is questioned. Minutes 17-19: compare, the first real whole-class moment. With 3-4 rounds of 7-9 min plus 5-10 min of prep, Alibi does not fit a 40-min Turkish lesson that really lasts about 32-35 min once you take off roll call and settling. Tam Dosya at 40-45 min has no buffer at all.

Sending suspect/twin B 'into the doorway' is a supervision and liability problem in a Turkish public school: an unsupervised child in the corridor, the müdür yardımcısı walking past. The headphones option assumes the teacher has headphones and a spare phone. In practice B stands 2 m away and hears everything, which quietly breaks the core mechanic.

The teacher's cognitive load in Yalancıyı Bul is the biggest single risk. At A1/A2 Genç the teacher is at once the hot seat actor (reading answers from the phone), the host (tapping G/R/chips, managing the token turn order), the judge and the behaviour manager. That is two devices and four roles while standing at the board. The keyboard shortcuts (Space/R/G/E/M/X/~/B/P/1-5) don't help on a touch-only smart board, which usually has no keyboard attached.

The phone remote over a QR code assumes the phone and board share internet. Many MEB smart boards (Pardus/EBA) have filtered or no internet, phone use in class is sometimes discouraged, and LLM generation needs the network. There is no stated offline or pre-cached path.

Active students at once: in the question phases only 2-3 of 28 are active (hot seat or suspect, spokesperson, scribe). Whole-class moments (finger vote, thumbs) come only at the END of each cycle, not every 30-60 s. That fails the spirit of the kids checklist's 'whole-class response every turn', because one 'turn' is 3-4 min long.

Fairness across Alibi rounds. Later suspect teams have watched the earlier interrogations, so they know the question bank and can patch their stories. They also have more waiting time to rehearse. The round-1 suspects are at a structural disadvantage.

Fairness within a team. The whole team's Alibi fate rests on 2 randomly picked students in one round, and the spinner can land on the weakest pair. In Nazik mode volunteers are used instead, so the same confident students volunteer every time.

Scoring noise. Detectives get +10 for each mismatch 'their question exposed', but which team asks which slot depends on the turn order. A team can ask its best questions and still score 0 because its rows happened to match. That feels arbitrary to adults and to competitive 12-14s.

Match arbitration costs time. With typed 1-3-word answers, 'at home' vs 'in my house' vs 'my flat' triggers a debate on every row. Thumbs voting first, then the teacher's M/X/~, doubles the time per row. With 8 rows that is 3-4 min of comparing.
The '~ close enough counts as a match' option plus the teacher being final invites accusations of favouritism from 12-14s ('Hocam ama onlar da farklı dedi!').

Too many knobs. There are 4 modes, 3 skins, and about 25 teacher controls, 5 scoring systems (points, stars, combo, badges, Slipstream, wager, Poker Face) and forfeits. The claimed '1 min setup' is only true on the second use. The first-time teacher needs a 2-minute guided default.
A1 Genç Two Truths where the lie is visible in the picture ('12 legs') makes the question-token phase pointless: kids will shout the answer before any question is asked.

Stopping at any moment is not defined. If the bell rings in the middle of an Alibi round (rows compared only for A, or half-compared), there is no rule for scoring a partial round or for resuming next lesson.
Adults (10 students, 3 teams of 3-4) fit well. But with only 3 teams the suspect team is 1/3 of the class, and the 2 non-suspects on that team sit idle for 7-9 min because they 'must stay silent'.

Noise. Prep huddles with 4 teams of 7, thumbs, 'Walk like a penguin!' and marimba boings are fun, but there is no built-in quiet signal or noise-down routine for returning to a listening task, and this game is all careful listening.
The student scribe typing on a smart board keyboard is slow (on-screen keyboard, Turkish layout). The paper-only mode then loses the automatic timeline, which is the game's main visual payoff.
fixes: Add a lesson-fit planner. The teacher enters the real minutes (default 35 for public school) and the game auto-sizes the rounds. Kids' Alibi defaults to 2 rounds × 6 min after one shared 4-min prep. Tam Dosya is only offered at 45+ min. Show a live 'bitiş tahmini' clock.

Replace 'B waits in the doorway' with in-room separation. Twin B turns to face the back wall and the whole class does a 20-s 'noise curtain' chant or song while A is questioned. Or better, run A and B SIMULTANEOUSLY on paper: both suspects answer the same 4-6 on-screen questions secretly on slips or mini-whiteboards, then reveal. Detectives' live follow-ups stay for B1+ adults only. Keep the doorway only as an adult option.

Presenter/remote split. When the teacher is in the hot seat, ALL host controls move onto the phone remote: next, G, R, vote entry, reveal. The board shows only the student view. Provide a no-network fallback: a printed Gizli Dosya plus big on-screen touch buttons (min 64 px) for every shortcut, with no keyboard needed.
Offline pack. Generate and cache the pack before class (a 'Derse hazırla' button stores it locally). The game must run fully offline from cache, with QR/remote optional.

Add a whole-class micro-response inside every question turn, not just at the end. After each hot-seat answer, the whole class shows 'suspicious / believable' with thumbs or a 1-2-3 prediction. That is also a quick way to calm noise.

Fix the Alibi round-order advantage. Randomise the question subset per round from a larger code-owned pool, reveal only the prep CATEGORIES (not the questions), and scale the threshold by round, or give round-1 suspects a +5 'first up' bonus.

Make each team's suspect performance a pair-of-pairs: two pairs per team, questioned on 3 rows each. Two pairs spread the risk, and no single student 'loses it for the team'. In Nazik mode, use a volunteer rotation list that blocks repeat volunteers until everyone has had a turn.
Replace per-question mismatch credit with shared detective credit. All detective teams earn +5 per mismatch found in the round, plus the per-team grammar badges. That removes the turn-order luck.

Answer matching. For A1-B1 use closed answer sets: tap a picture or a word from a 4-6 option list per row, so matching is automatic and there are no arguments. Keep free typing plus M/X/~ only for B2 adults. Show a 'rule of thumb' line: same meaning = match.

Ship a 'Hızlı başla' default per group (one tap: 3 characters, teacher hot seat, tokens 2, no scribe) and hide the advanced dials behind 'Gelişmiş'. Merge the scoring into one system per skin: stars for Oyun Parkı, points plus combo for Arena, points for Stüdyo. Drop Slipstream plus Poker Face plus wager from the defaults.
For the A1 Genç 'visible lie', use it only for the non-scoring Gogo demo. Scored characters hide the picture of the lie statement until the reveal, so the questions still matter.
Define 'Dersi bitir' at any moment: score only the compared rows, show the partial podium, and save the state to the class profile with 'Kaldığı yerden devam' for next lesson.
Give the suspect team a job while it waits (adults): the silent teammates predict which rows will mismatch on a slip, scored +3 each if correct. This keeps them engaged without letting them signal.
Build in a noise routine: a clap-back or 'Freeze!' card the teacher can trigger with one tap before every listening phase, with the visual timer going quiet until the room is quiet.
Default the scribe to picture/word-bank chips at every level below B2, and put the student scribe on the phone remote rather than the smart-board keyboard.
Share the engine with c26 (templates, timeline, log, print pack) to cut build size from L toward M, and list Öğretmenin Sırrı as a filler on the homepage in its own right.

issues: Oyun Parkı 'True or Silly' at A1 makes the lie visible in the avatar ('12 legs' next to a 4-legged cat). Kids can vote correctly without asking or understanding a single question, so the chip-question step is decoration, not learning.

A1/A2 Genç question production is mostly one spokesperson reading a chip aloud, and the teacher then reads a pre-written answer from the phone. The rest of the class only listens and raises fingers. The language demand is receptive plus choral repetition, with close to zero real question formation for about 80% of the kids.

The Oyun Parkı pacing doesn't add up. 'Twin Stories' needs 5 min of prep, a split, two question passes and a comparison, which can't fit the stated '3 rounds of 4-5 min' or the 15-25 min total. Realistically it's one Alibi round per lesson, or the prep has to shrink to about 2 min.

The A1 Genç 'Photo Alibi' uses the present continuous ('It's a photo. Where are you?'). It breaks the alibi logic, since alibis are about the past, and it's a strange frame to model. It's really a picture-memory game, which is fine, but it should be labelled and designed as one.

The Alibi prep load for 9-10-year-olds assumes every team member memorises a shared story because the suspects are picked after prep. In Nazik mode the suspects are volunteers anyway, so that rationale falls away and the rest of the team idles during prep.

Kids' 'Mixed-up story' incentives: suspects score for matches, and nothing stops weak readers from answering at random. Thumbs up/down is the only whole-class moment, and it judges sameness of pictures, not language.

Student hot seats at B1 Genç and above (and adults) read 6-10 profile facts plus answers from a phone. That's a reading-aloud task under pressure, not spontaneous speaking, and at the B1 Genç 14-word cap the profile text is heavy for a 12-year-old.

The B2 'lie inferred only from combining 2 profile details' is invisible to the detectives unless the hot seat happens to voice both. That's too abstract for B2 Genç and frustrating even for adults without a hint mechanic.

The LLM content burden is high. Each character needs 3 claims x 6 or more template answers plus cover stories and a planted slip, and it has to stay within word caps and the grammar target. At A1 (a 4-word cap) a coherent cover story with a slip is close to impossible. 'tells[] as string references' is a fragile consistency check.

The free-text example 'Kapadokya gezisi, present perfect' conflicts with the rules 'Genç: fictional places only' and 'adults: no checkable facts about real places'. Teacher prompts will often name real places and people, and the spec doesn't say what happens then (silent fictionalisation vs refusal).
Built-in categories need a large curated bank: characters x levels x 3 audiences, each with full answer grids. 'Pick a built-in topic' won't be realistic at launch unless it is narrowed.
The keyboard map contradicts itself. The flow says R = recast, but controls list R = reveal and E = recast. A teacher mis-key reveals the lie mid-game.

Scope creep: 4 modes, about 25 dials, a phone remote, a presenter window, print packs and PDF export, plus a template library shared with c26 'Kim Yaptı?'. The teacher-facing setup is too dense for a quick in-class start, especially at the Oyun Parkı level.

A2 typed 1-3-word scribe answers and the B1 open follow-ups slow the Alibi down. With 4 teams, detectives ask about 2 questions each per suspect, so individual speaking time per student is tiny in a 36-student class.
Adult corporate classes: 'office cake / leaked email / dented company car' is fine, but A1 adults answering with noun taps can feel like a kids' worksheet.
fixes: Oyun Parkı Two Truths: make the lie hidden in the picture and revealed only by a chip answer. For example, the avatar shows a normal cat, and 'Can you swim?' gets the answer 'Yes! I swim every day' with a splash picture. Voting then depends on listening to the answers.

Add a whole-class choral step to every kids' turn. The class repeats the chosen chip question with the spokesperson before the teacher answers, and picture-only answers are shown AFTER the class guesses what the answer will be. That turns the turn into listening practice, not just finger-raising.

Make the kids' Alibi 'Twin Stories' a single-round mode (2-min picture prep, 4 questions, auto-compare, about 8 min) and fill the rest of the lesson with True or Silly. Fix the stated durations: 'Oyun Parkı 15-25 min = 3 True-or-Silly characters + 1 Twin Stories'.
Rename the A1 Genç Alibi to 'Photo Twins' (describe a picture from memory: 'I'm eating pizza') and keep the past-tense alibi for A2 and up. Don't claim alibi grammar at A1 Genç.
In Nazik mode, pick the twins BEFORE prep, and give the other team members prep jobs: one picks the picture per row, and one practises the questions the detectives will ask. That way nobody idles.

Give the kids' twins a small bonus only when they SAY the answer sentence (e.g. 'I was in the park' or 'I'm eating pizza'), not just when they point to a picture. That makes production the scoring currency.

For student hot seats, show at most 4 profile lines plus the chip answers, and use a 'say it your way' badge for paraphrasing instead of reading. At B1 Genç, default to the teacher hot seat unless the teacher turns the student option on.

B2 combined tells: add a 'Detective note' hint card that a team can buy with one token, which reveals one related profile fact. Drop the combined-tells requirement for B2 Genç and keep a single planted slip.

Split generation: at A1/A2 the LLM fills slot values into code-owned sentence templates (noun, place, number), not free sentences. Validate the tells by structured keys (e.g. fact.key = 'transport', value = 'plane'), not string matching.

When a free-text prompt names a real place or person, auto-fictionalise it with a visible notice (e.g. 'Kapadokya' becomes a fictional 'Peri Vadisi' for Genç groups), or keep the real place for adults but restrict statements to personal experiences with no checkable facts. Show the teacher the substitution.

Launch with a narrow built-in bank: 6 characters per level band (A1-A2, B1-B2) x 2 audiences (kids and teen/adult skins, sharing content where teenSafe) and 4 cases per audience. Use the LLM for the rest.
Resolve the key map: R = reveal (with a confirm or hold-to-reveal), E = recast, G = grammar badge. Put the map on a teacher cheat-sheet overlay.

Ship v1 with 2 modes: Yalancıyı Bul and Alibi. Make Öğretmenin Sırrı a free static filler card and Tam Dosya a preset. Hide the advanced dials behind 'Gelişmiş'. Consider merging the Alibi mode's case engine with c26 so the shared template library isn't built twice.
For large classes, have every detective team write its predicted suspect answer on a mini-whiteboard before B answers. That gives everyone a production moment and adds a 'Mind reader' point.
A1 adults: use sentence-completion taps ('I was at ___ with ___') that build a full spoken sentence, and give them the adult case-file skin, so it never looks like a picture worksheet.

reviews.mergeWith: c26 (Kim Yaptı?) as a shared 'Dedektif' engine only: template library, case file UI, stamps, log and print pack. The two games stay separate modes.
issues: Scope is far beyond an L. As written it is 4 modes x 3 skins x 2 sub-games (Two Truths and Alibi). On top of that come a phone remote over QR, a presenter window, a print pack (5 document types plus headbands), PDF export, a hint ladder, Bluff cards, evidence drops, a wager, the Would I Lie panel, streak combos, steals and stat awards. Realistically that is XL, and it carries the highest risk of never feeling finished.

The real game happens in the room, out loud. On screen it risks being a glorified logging form. The polish depends on how fast the teacher can input things, not on the art. Every question needs a chip tap, a time-slot pin, answer A typed or tapped, answer B typed or tapped, an M/X/~ mark, and optional G, R and B taps. At 8 questions x 2 suspects, that is 40+ inputs per round from a teacher who is also moderating the room.

Free English follow-ups won't match the chips. 'Replay the same questions to B' works only if each question was captured as a chip or as typed text. When a spokesperson asks something off-chip, the log is empty or the teacher has to type it live.

The Kaçırılanlar list and the 3-second recast assume the system knows the correct form. It only knows the chip's model question. An off-chip question has no correct form stored unless the teacher types one.

Key conflict: the rules text uses R for recast, but the keyboard map gives R to reveal and E to recast. The grammar badge G and the best question B are also context-dependent. Smartboard users have no keyboard at all, so every action needs a large on-screen button.

LLM generation is the weakest link in Two Truths. Each claim needs trueFacts, truthAnswers for at least 6 templates, a coverStory with a single 'slip' answer, and tells stored as string references. Code can check the schema, word caps and template ids. It cannot check semantic consistency: whether the slip really leaks the truth, whether the truths are really supported, or the B2 rule that only the combination of two tells proves the lie. A 'have + past participle' regex is also crude, and irregular participles and negatives break it.

Cover-story answers that contradict each other, or a truth answer that accidentally contradicts the profile, will ruin a reveal in front of a class. Nothing in the validator catches cross-answer contradictions.

The phone remote over QR needs a realtime channel (Supabase realtime or polling), pairing, reconnection and school Wi-Fi reliability. That is a big risk for a feature whose job, showing the secret profile, a printed card or a second window does just as well.

The Alibi logistics are heavy for young learners. Twin B waits in the doorway with headphones playing a loop from the teacher's phone, two volunteers take the pair roles, and the Photo Alibi sheet has to be printed. The A1 Genç Alibi is really a picture-matching memory game, which is fine, but 9-year-olds have to sit through prep, questioning A, questioning B and a comparison. The whole-class response comes only at the compare step, so the checklist item 'every turn' is borderline during the questioning phases.

Kids' Two Truths at A1 ('I have got 12 legs' next to the avatar) is trivially obvious. It works as a listening warm-up, but it has almost no deduction. Kids will love it for about 2 characters and then get bored.

The picture requirement for A1/A2 Genç means every statement, chip and alibi option needs an imageKey. That is a large illustration or emoji-mapping library, and LLM-generated items will often have no picturable key and get dropped, which leaves thin packs.

The asset list is long: the Gogo parrot and poses, character avatars (about 20 per skin), ID frames, a height chart, a lie-detector needle, a waveform, stamps, CLASSIFIED tape, a filing cabinet, a coffee-ring stain, and 3 sound packs of about 12 SFX each. Without a shared kit it will look inconsistent.
Tam Dosya is not a mode. It is a playlist of existing modes, and the 5-minute teacher warm-up duplicates Öğretmenin Sırrı.

Two Truths overlaps with a plain Hot Seat or Taboo candidate, since both are about spoken questioning of a person in the seat. Alibi overlaps with c26 Kim Yaptı (case file, suspects, joke culprit, shared template library). Building both separately doubles the UI.
The Arena steal on malformed questions and the adult -5 and wager add rule surface that the teacher must adjudicate live. That is a risk of disputes, and the benefit is small.
fixes: Split the build into phases. MVP (M size): Mode 1 Yalancıyı Bul plus Öğretmenin Sırrı, one skin kit per audience driven by CSS tokens, teacher hot seat, a presenter view in a second window via window.open plus BroadcastChannel, and printable Gizli Dosya cards. Phase 2: Alibi with picture or tap scribing. Phase 3: extras (Bluff cards, evidence drops, wager, Would I Lie panel, stat awards). Drop the QR phone remote from v1, and drop Tam Dosya as a mode; make it a 'lesson plan' preset.

Make Alibi input one-tap. Each case ships with a FIXED question list (6-10 template chips) that is pinned to time slots in advance. Answers are tapped from 4-6 generated options per question, plus an 'other' free-text field. The comparison then happens automatically (same option = match), and the teacher only overrides with ~. Free follow-ups at B1+ are logged as a single 'extra' row that the teacher marks X/M, with no text captured.
Record recasts only against chip questions: the model form comes from the template. The Kaçırılanlar list shows 'Target form' per template used, not a transcription of what the student said.

Resolve the key map. Suggested: Space next, V reveal, G badge, R recast, M/X/C mark (C for close), B best, 1-5 teams, L log. Mirror every key with a large on-screen button bar that can be docked left or right for smartboards, and make the hidden vote a row of per-team 1/2/3 buttons in the presenter view.

Make generation safer. The LLM returns only claims and answers keyed by enumerated template ids (JSON schema with enum). Code compiles the lie position and the profile. Then run a second, cheap LLM 'consistency judge' pass that answers yes/no per check (slip leaks the truth, no answer contradicts a truth, tells present). On failure, auto-regenerate that claim once, then flag it for the teacher. Always show the teacher a preview of the secret profile before play, and ship a curated built-in bank of about 12 characters and 6 cases per level x audience so the game never depends on the LLM.

Replace the regex grammar check with a small tense-tag table: each template id declares its tense, and the LLM's answer is checked against a closed list of auxiliaries and irregular participles taken from words.js. Treat a failure as a warning, not a rejection.

Kids (Oyun Parkı): make Two Truths the main kids mode and Twin Stories optional. Keep the whole class active during questioning: after each answer, the class echoes the question chorally. Twin B can simply face the wall while the class whispers, which drops the headphone requirement. Raise the kids' deduction slightly after the first round, with the lie picturable but not visible in the avatar.

Picture support: use one self-hosted SVG emoji set (OpenMoji or Twemoji subset, ~400 icons) as the imageKey vocabulary. The LLM must choose imageKeys from that closed list, and code rejects any key outside it. That makes A1/A2 Genç content reliably picturable.

Assets: a single illustrator-style kit per skin of about 25 pieces (the Gogo set of 4 poses, 12 avatar stickers, stamp, tape, needle, frame). Synthesise every SFX with WebAudio (clack, marimba, synth blip, typewriter tick) so there are no audio files and no licensing issues. Honour prefers-reduced-motion.

Share one 'Dedektif' engine with c26 Kim Yaptı: the case file component, timeline, stamps, template library, log and print pack. Keep the game identities separate: Sorgu Odası is speaking and questioning, Kim Yaptı is deduction and reading.
Cut the Arena steal and the adult negatives and wager from v1. Keep the combo on accuracy only. Fewer adjudication moments means fewer disputes and a faster pace.

Minimum feature set that makes it feel like a proper game: spotlight reveal of the statements with TTS, token pips per team, a presenter view with the profile and ready answers, simultaneous hidden vote plus an animated needle swing, a card-flip reveal with the slip highlighted in the log, lie-position balancing, and the Hall of Questions. For Alibi add the CLASSIFIED tape tear, the two-track timeline with red ✗ contradictions and the verdict stamp. Nothing else is required to ship.

catalog.rankReason: Two Truths and a Lie / Alibi with real people in the hot seat: strong question formation for adults (8). It shares the Dedektif engine with c26 (question templates, timeline, print pack) but stays its own game. MVP: Mode 1 plus 'Öğretmenin Sırrı'. Separation happens inside the room (no child sent to the corridor), and Alibi input is one tap on fixed question chips.

catalog.name: Sahtekar Kim? (Social Deduction)
catalog.familiarAs: Spyfall / The Chameleon / Mafia-Werewolf (Vampir Köylü) / Among Us / Gimkit Trust No One
catalog.oneLiner: Everyone knows the secret word except the impostor. Each player gives one English clue, the group argues with a 'because' and everyone points on 3. The same game scales up to a narrated, non-violent Town Mystery or a phone-based Crew mission, where review questions earn the evidence.
catalog.howItPlays:
ONE GAME, THREE MODES. The lesson-fit timer suggests a mode. All three share the same frames panel, the 'Point on 3!' vote and the reveal.
A) KELIME SAHTEKARI (quick): 8-20 min, for every group, including A1 and kids. This is the core mode.
B) KASABADA GIZEM (Town Mystery): 25-40 min, for Stüdyo and Arena at A2 and up. Kids play the whole-class case 'Kurabiyeleri Kim Aldı?' instead.
C) GEMI GÖREVI (Impostor Crew): 25-40 min on student phones, for Arena and Stüdyo at A2 and up.

A) KELIME SAHTEKARI. A round takes about 3 min.
FORMATS
- STAGE (default): each team sends one delegate, chosen by the seat spinner, so 4-7 players sit facing the class wearing big letter signs A-G. The rest of the class forms Jury teams that never see the secret.
- PARALLEL: every table of 4-7 plays at once, and the projector paces all the tables.
STEPS
1. Topic Grid (10 s): a 4x4 grid (3x3 at A1 or on Kolay) of one category flips in. Each cell has a word and a picture, with coordinates A-D and 1-4. Pictures are mandatory for A1 and A2 Genç. In the first round, every grid word is read aloud and the class echoes it.
2. Secret deal (15-20 s). The teacher picks one of four routes:
   (i) LAMINATED CODE CARDS (print once, reuse with any topic). The app rolls a colour-and-shape die and a number die and names the lookup table ('Table III · Blue star · 4'). The crew look up the cell ('C2'). The impostor's card has the same back and layout but shows the skin's impostor icon. Each card carries 4 tables, so memorising an earlier round never helps. Kids' cards use colour only, with a starred mini-grid for each colour and a Sun side and a Moon side.
   (ii) PHONES: players join with a QR room code (no accounts). The card is hold-to-peek and auto-hides. Crew and impostor screens have an identical layout, colour and vibration.
   (iii) PASS THE TABLET: tap to see, tap to hide, then a blank 'Pass to seat D' screen.
   (iv) HEADS DOWN (no print, no phones). Everyone puts their head down and the teacher taps one stage shoulder. The narrator says 'Stage players, except the impostor, look!' and the secret cell glows for 5 s. Then 'Heads down... heads up!' The Jury keeps their heads down throughout.
3. Who starts: a spinning arrow picks a seat letter, and a strip shows the clockwise order. In phone mode the impostor is never first.
4. Clue round: each player gives ONE clue using the level frame on screen. Each player gets a 10-15 s ring; kids are untimed. Players may not say the word, use Turkish or point at the grid.
   - The teacher can drop each clue into the clue strip ('C: cold') so the discussion can quote it.
   - A player who freezes taps 'Clue helper'. It shows generic pictogram frames for the category (colour, size, place, sound, action) and never reveals the word.
   - At B1 and up there is an optional second clue round, or 'Soru turu': each player asks the next one a question ('Would I need a passport for it?').
5. Discussion with the frames panel: kids 20 s of point-and-say, Arena 45 s, Stüdyo 60-90 s.
   - B1 and up: 'Justify to vote'. Before the vote, someone must give a 'because' sentence about a clue.
   - The most-suspected player gets 10-20 s to defend ('I said cold because...').
6. Vote: 'Point on 3!' with a 3-2-1 drumroll. The stage players point at the same moment, and each Jury team holds up a letter card or a mini-whiteboard. The teacher taps the most-pointed letter.
   - Tie: each tied player gives one more clue, then the stage votes again once. If it is still tied, the impostor escapes. For kids, the Jury breaks the tie.
7. Reveal: the accused shows the card or taps the phone, and the card flips. If the impostor is caught, they get a LAST CHANCE to name the secret word from the grid. Kids may point first and then say it with Gogo; Arena has a 5-s clutch timer. A right guess steals the round.
8. Word moment: the secret cell glows and is read aloud, and kids repeat it twice as a class. The teacher can star the sharpest clue, which goes into the Clue Gallery. The teacher view shows a model clue at the group's level.
9. Rotate: roll again or re-deal. A grid stays for up to 3 rounds, then a new grid comes in. Card mode shows 'Shuffle the cards!'. The spinner picks the new delegates, never a name.
SCORING
- Stage mode:
  - Impostor not caught: the impostor's team gets +3.
  - Caught, but guesses the word: the impostor's team gets +2 and the crew teams +1.
  - Caught and misses the word: the crew teams get +2.
  - Jury teams: +1 for the right letter, and +1 more for also naming the word (they never saw it).
  - Teacher-tap bonuses: Sharp clue +1, target structure used correctly +1 (B1/B2), Best bluff +1.
- Parallel mode: each table keeps a printed score strip. The projector keeps a class meta-score from a hands-up count ('Impostors caught: 4 of 5').
VARIANTS
- GIZLI AJAN (B1/B2; phones or printed slips only): the odd player gets a near-neighbour word (tea instead of coffee) and does not know it, so nobody knows who the impostor is.
- ZOR (phones only): the crew's card also lists 2 forbidden words.
- NEREDE? (B1 and up): the category is places, and each crew member also gets a role at that place and answers in character.

B) KASABADA GIZEM (Town Mystery): a non-violent Mafia or Werewolf for a circle of 8-14.
1. Setup: roles come on phones or on printed cards with identical backs.
   - The app suggests the role counts: 8 players = 2 thieves, 1 detective, 1 guard and 4 townspeople; 12 players = 3/1/1/7. At B2 there is also a Journalist, who once per game publishes one true headline.
   - Every player gets a persona name tent ('Baker Rosa'). Accusations name the persona, never the classmate.
2. NIGHT (about 60 s). The screen dims, crickets play and the moon rises.
   - A narrator voice, or the teacher reading the printed script, says: 'Everyone, close your eyes... Thieves, open your eyes and point...'
   - The teacher taps the targets on the teacher remote (a phone joined with the teacher QR) or notes them on the printed night sheet, never on the projector.
   - The Detective points at one player and gets a silent thumbs up or down. The Guard protects one player, and never the same one twice in a row.
3. MORNING (rooster, sunrise): 'The thieves locked Baker Rosa in the bakery!' That player becomes a Ghost. If the Guard picked the right player: 'The Guard was there!'
4. TOWN TASK (60-90 s): one review item on screen, with options after the audience delay, answered on mini-whiteboards or phones.
   - A correct majority unlocks an EVIDENCE card. The code builds it from the real role map ('One thief is sitting on the window side'), and it is pinned to a cork board with red string.
   - A wrong answer only means there is no clue.
5. DAY (A2 2 min, B1 3 min, B2 5 min): discussion with the level panel.
   - An accusation needs a reason sentence plus a seconder who gives a DIFFERENT reason.
   - The accused then gets a 30-s defence. At B2 the class also asks two 'Where were you when...?' questions, checked against the persona's timeline card, which has a gap the thieves must lie around.
   - There are at most 2 trials a day.
6. VOTE: thumbs on 3, or on phones. The majority sends the accused to the Town Hall, where they become a Ghost, and the role card flips.
7. GHOSTS are never idle:
   - They answer Town Task items, and their answers count double toward the Evidence meter.
   - Each Ghost may ask one yes/no question a day.
   - They keep the Village Diary, one sentence per day.
8. WIN: the town wins when every thief is in the Town Hall, and the thieves win when they equal the town. The lesson timer can call a Final Vote instead.
   - Finale: a printable newspaper front page with a generated headline that uses persona names, and the Diary sentences as the article.
   - Big classes: the rest of the class forms the Newsroom (they write the Diary and cast one 'public poll' vote), then the groups swap. Alternatively, run twin villages with a student narrator reading the printed script.

C) GEMI GÖREVI (Impostor Crew): 12-35 players on phones.
1. Join: players scan a QR room code and get a codename with an emblem ('Comet-7'). There are no free-text names.
2. Roles: each player is secretly Crew or Impostor, about 1 impostor per 6 players and never more than 4.
3. TASK PHASE (4-6 min): everyone answers review items.
   - A correct answer gives +1 energy and fills a zone bar on the projected ship (Engine, Oxygen, Navigation, Shields). A wrong answer gives 0 (Stüdyo can switch on -1, with a floor at 0).
   - Impostors answer too, so they still practise and have to keep their accuracy believable.
4. SPENDING ENERGY
   - Crew can SCAN a codename for 3 energy. The result is 'clear' or 'inconclusive': impostors always come back inconclusive, crew half the time.
   - Impostors buy SABOTAGE: Blackout (the bars are hidden for 20 s), Fake Trail (a false clue is posted) or Jam (one scan is blocked for 30 s).
   - Impostors can NEVER change anyone's answers, energy or bars.
5. EMERGENCY MEETING: it starts automatically every 5 min, or when a player uses their one button press per game.
   - Phones lock, and the projector shows the evidence board.
   - There are 60-120 s of discussion. An accusation must use a frame and a reason, and the accused must reply with a defence frame.
   - Players vote on their phones, and Skip is allowed. The majority ejects a player: 'Comet-7 was not the impostor.' A tie or a Skip means nobody leaves.
6. GHOSTS keep answering, and their correct answers still repair the ship. They have a stamp-only ghost channel ('Watch Zone B!').
7. WIN: the crew wins by ejecting every impostor or by filling all the bars. The impostors win by equalling the crew or by running out the clock.
PROJECTOR-ONLY FALLBACK: Crew runs on the Town engine with the ship skin, printed roles and mini-whiteboard repair items.
catalog.playerSetup:
QUICK MODE
- Stage + Jury (default): 4-7 delegates, one from each team of 3-8, sit on stage. Everyone else plays as a Jury team, so a class of 16-36 plays at once.
- Parallel: tables of 4-7 play at the same time (5 tables in a class of 30).
- One impostor per group. Two only with 8+ players at B1/B2.
- Kids: the teams are animal-mascot teams. 'Kedi ikilisi' lets two shy children share the Cat card.

TOWN MYSTERY
- One circle of 8-14 players.
- The rest of the class is the Newsroom (Diary writers plus one poll vote) and swaps in for the next game. Alternatively, run twin villages.

CREW
- 12-35 individuals on phones.
- Above about 20, run two ships on a split projector, each discussing in its own half of the room.

KIDS' CASE ('Kurabiyeleri Kim Aldı?')
- The whole class plays in 4-6 teams, with no individual roles.

EVERY MODE
- The seat spinner and the teams pick who plays, never a student's name.
- On screen, players appear only as letters, personas or codenames.
skills: speaking: describing and defining with one precise clue
vocabulary (topic sets, near-synonyms in Gizli Ajan)
listening (the Jury deduces the word from clues; narrator scripts)
question formation (Soru turu, ghost questions, B2 interrogation)
speculation modals and hedging (B2: must/might/can't have)
quick-fire grammar and vocabulary review (Town tasks, Crew repairs, the kids' case)
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO
- Look and sound: the editorial quiz-night look (cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme). No mascot and no voice lines, just neutral captions ('Round 2 · Travel'). Woodblock and piano sounds.
- Language: English on the student screen and Turkish in the teacher chrome.
- Team names come from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').

QUICK MODE: 'The Mole'
- The impostor card is a manila folder stamped MOLE. At the reveal the folder slides out with a CONFIRMED or CLEARED stamp.
- Topics: jobs, travel places, kitchen, apps and tech, hobbies, film genres, workplace objects, emotions, health, and abstract nouns at B2 (freedom, deadline, privacy).
- At B1/B2, clues must use the round's target structure (relative clauses, 'You'd probably use it if...', passive, second conditional). The teacher taps +1 when it is used correctly.
- Soru turu question rounds.
- Gizli Ajan is the default from B1. Near-neighbour pairs make it hilarious: tea/coffee, flat/house, colleague/friend.
- Nerede? location variant: crew also hold a role at the place (airport: pilot, passenger, security officer) and answer in character.
- Scoring: points, optional minus points, and a WAGER. Before the reveal, the suspected player may bet up to 3 points that the table picked wrong.

FULL MODE: 'Maple Town Thieves' or 'The Office Leak' (who is leaking the merger?)
- All roles, including the Journalist.
- Days last 5 minutes at B2.
- Persona timeline cards give the alibis. The language targets are speculation modals (must have, might have, can't have), hedging ('I'm not 100% sure, but...') and rebuttal ('That doesn't add up, because...').
- Event cards use the Green and Yellow Harshness levels ('Swap turn order', 'Rumour: defend your last clue'). Red is off.
- An optional first-language tax, off by default: a player who argues in Turkish loses their vote that day.

CREW MODE: 'Freighter Kestrel-9'
- The optional -1 for a wrong answer, with a floor at 0.

ENDINGS
- Full scores.
- The 'Kaçırılanlar' list: grid words used wrongly and missed task items.
- The Clue Gallery: the teacher-starred clues, kept as model sentences.
- Optional homework: a 100-120-word police report written from the game log.
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (9-11; default for A1/A2 Genç): 'Sinsi Kedi / Sneaky Cat'

SKIN AND HOST
- A cream-and-bright spaceship crewed by astronaut animals. The team mascots are panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger and rabbit.
- The impostor is a Sneaky Cat hiding in a cardboard box. The alternative skin is Bakery Town.
- Gogo the parrot hosts:
  - He runs a 20-30-s unscored demo with three cartoon friends, and the class spots the cat.
  - He reads the grid words aloud at 0.8x, and the class echoes them.
  - He says the word after a miss.
  - He sleeps on the pause screen.

THREE RULES (a Turkish rule card with 3 pictograms, explained in 20 s)
1) Everyone sees the secret picture, except the Cat.
2) Say ONE clue, not the word.
3) Point at the Cat on 3. A caught Cat can still guess the picture.

KIDS CHECKLIST: PASSED
- No elimination: everyone plays every round.
- Stars only, and nothing is ever lost.
- A whole-class moment every round: Jury teams hold up letter cards A-F, and afterwards the whole class says the secret word twice with Gogo.
- Non-violent failure: a caught Cat says 'Miyav! Kedi yakalandı!' and pops out of the box. An escaped Cat flies off on a paper plane with a fish.

HOW IT PLAYS FOR KIDS
- The grid is 3x3 with big pictures, and on-screen text stays within 4 words.
- A clue is one word, a colour or a size, or a gesture plus one word for actable items.
- Discussion is 20 s of point-and-say ('I think it's B!' 'Yes!' 'No!' 'Me too!').

KINDNESS DIALS
- 'Gönüllü kedi': the teacher picks the Cat from volunteers during heads-down.
- 'Kedi ikilisi': two children share the Cat card.
- A 'Game reasons only' card.

STARS
- Cat caught: 1 star to each crew team.
- Cat escapes or guesses the picture: 2 stars ('Sneaky Star') to the Cat's team.
- Jury team names the right letter: 1 star.
- Sounds are marimba, with no buzzers, and each sticker burst lasts at most 2 s.

PACING
- 3 rounds of 3-4 min. Between rounds comes a 45-s stirrer, 'Impostor in the line-up' (odd one out: 4 pictures, and the class points at the one that doesn't belong).
- About 12-15 min in total.

THE LONG KIDS MODE IS NEVER HIDDEN-ROLE ELIMINATION. It is 'Kurabiyeleri Kim Aldı?':
- Six cartoon animal suspects are in the bakery, and no classmate is ever a suspect.
- The class answers picture items with A-D cards or TPR (stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C).
- Each correct answer earns a clue from Gogo. On screen it shows a picture plus 'red hat'. Aloud he says 'The thief has got a red hat.' At A2: 'The thief was in the park at five.'
- Wrong answer: a soft 'boing' and a second try with a hint. After a second miss, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the clue is still given, along with an effort star.
- Teams flip down suspects, then accuse: 'I think it's Fox because he has got a red hat!'
- The culprit confesses ('I was hungry! Let's share!') and the cookies are shared.
- 8-10 min per case, replayed 2-3 times.
- Ending: every team gets a title (Super Detectives, Sneakiest Cats, Best Clue Givers, Great Listeners), and the class album gets a 'Cat Catchers' sticker with the day's words.

ARENA (12-14; default for B1/B2 Genç, and suggested for any Genç group at grade 6+): 'Glitch Hunt'

LOOK AND FEEL
- Dark navy with neon team colours and a condensed display font.
- In 10 s, each team picks an emblem (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond), a colour and a 3-word motto.
- The impostor is 'the Glitch', revealed with a 'SIGNAL LOST' glitch effect.
- A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('CLEAN READ', 'CLUTCH GUESS', 'BEST BLUFF'), and sounds are synth blips.
- The rule card is in English, with a Turkish toggle.

QUICK MODE
- The same rules as Stüdyo, with a 45-s discussion and a 30-s clue ring in the team colour.
- Jury teams answer on mini-whiteboards.
- Combo on jury reads: x1.5 after 3 right, x2 after 5. It counts accuracy only, and the floor is zero.
- Gizli Ajan is available at B1/B2.

FULL MODES
- 'Night Shift' town mystery: opt-in at B1/B2 Genç, with a fixed-frame version for A2 Genç.
  - The thieves are Glitches who 'freeze' a player.
  - A frozen player becomes an Offline Helper who holds up phrase cards and powers the Evidence meter.
- 'Station Breach': crew mode on phones.

CONTENT AND PROTECTIONS
- Content passes the teenSafe filter, and topics follow MEB grade 6-8 units (Occupations, Downtown, Public Buildings, In the Kitchen, The Internet, Tourism).
- Players appear only as codenames and personas.
- There is no public last place, a 'Game reasons only' card, and the 'Sessiz sıfırla' reset.

ENDING
- A podium plus stat awards (Sharpest Clue, Best Bluff, Cold Reader, Comeback), and never a 'last place'.
catalog.levelTuning:
TWO AXES: the level sets the language, and the audience sets the skin and the rules.

A1 and A1 Genç
- Grid: 3x3 (Kolay) or 4x4 of concrete A1-band words with pictures, every word read aloud.
- Clue: one word, or 'It's + colour/size/adjective'. Genç may add a gesture.
- One clue round.
- Discussion: 'I think it's B!' / 'Yes!' / 'No!' / 'Me too!'. No justification is required; adults are encouraged to add 'because + one word'.
- Town Mystery only as the listening version: the teacher or Gogo narrates, and the class votes by pointing with 4 fixed phrases.
- No Crew mode.
- Prompts: at most 4 words for Genç, 10 for adults.

A2
- Grid: 4x4.
- Clue: a phrase ('in the kitchen', 'for cold days'), or 'It's got...', 'You can... it', 'You find it in the...'.
- The accuser must give a 'because'. Frames: 'I agree' / 'I don't think so'.
- Town: the fixed-frame version, with 2-minute days and yes/no ghost questions.
- Crew: fixed frames and yes/no scan checks. Tasks are A2 grammar MCQs (past simple, comparatives).
- The kids' case clues use past simple and clock times.

B1
- Clue: a full sentence ('It's something (that) you...', 'It's a kind of...').
- Two clue rounds, or Soru turu.
- An accusation needs a seconder with a different reason, plus a 10-20-s defence.
- Frames: 'I suspect... because...', 'That doesn't make sense because...', 'Your clue was too general.'
- Gizli Ajan and Nerede? are unlocked.
- Town: all roles and 3-minute days. A bonus for a correct relative clause.

B2
- Clues must use the round's target structure ('You'd probably use it if...', passive, second conditional), +1 when correct.
- Interrogation: 'Where were you when...?', checked against the persona timeline.
- Speculation modals (must/might/can't have), hedging and rebuttal.
- Gizli Ajan is the default.
- Topics: abstract nouns for adults; rich concrete topics for B2 Genç, never abstract debate.
- 5-minute days.
- Optional police report or Village Diary writing.

MIXED ABILITY AND TEXT CAPS
- Kolay: 3x3 grid, more frames, an easier word mix (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words).
- Zor: phones show 2 forbidden words per secret, and fewer frames.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the frames panel and the word band by one level.
- Text caps follow the dial table: A1 Genç 0-4, A2 Genç 8, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Quick mode: 8-20 min, about 3 min per round; kids 12-15 min including the demo and the stirrer. Town Mystery or Crew: 25-40 min, plus a 2-min animated tutorial the first time. Kids' 'Kurabiyeleri Kim Aldı?': 8-10 min per case, played 2-3 times.
catalog.contentShape:
QUICK MODE
- One category-list: label (4 words or fewer, EN), labelTr, media.emoji, and 12-24 members. The code picks 9 or 16 per grid and rotates them.
- The members resolve to vocab items with:
  - term and alt[]
  - media.img or media.emoji (an imageKey is required for A1/A2 Genç, and unpicturable members are dropped)
  - defEasy and defTr (teacher view only)
  - distractors[3] (the first same-field distractor is the Gizli Ajan decoy)
  - actable (allows gesture clues)
  - the CEFR band from words.js
- Optional extras:
  - one taboo-card per member (forbidden[2]) for Zor
  - roleplay items for Nerede? (setting = the place; roleA and roleB titles plus extra role titles)
  - speaking-prompt items (mode 'ask') as Soru turu starters
  - odd items for the 'Impostor in the line-up' stirrer
- STATIC, never from the LLM: the frame panels for clue, accuse, second, defend, agree and disagree at each level; the rule cards; the narrator scripts; the skins.

TOWN MYSTERY
- A story skin: title, titleTr, setting, role names, narrator lines per phase within the level's word cap, and headline templates.
- 8-16 character personas: name from the name pool, avatar, intro, and a profile with a 4-slot timeline for B2 alibis.
- 10-20 task items (mcq, gap, tf, qa).
- 6-10 chance-card events (Green or Yellow only).
- EVIDENCE cards are computed by code from the true role map and the persona attributes, never by the LLM, so they are always true.

KIDS' CASE
- One case frame: theme, caseIntro, 6 suspects with attrs (look, item, place, time, activity), culpritId, 4-5 clues by round, confession, mature=false.
- 6-10 picture items to earn the clues: mcq 'picture', tf 'picture', pair 'emoji'.

CREW
- 30-60 task items (mcq, gap, tf, pair, qa), served per student with missed items coming back.
- A ship skin: zones and sabotage names.

GENERATION AND VALIDATION
- A Turkish or English prompt ('mutfak eşyaları, 6. sınıf') returns the category-list, or a story skin for 'uzay istasyonu'.
- Validators check:
  - category coherence: every member is in the category; no synonyms or near-duplicates in one grid (cup/mug); no member that stands out trivially
  - the level band via words.js
  - teenSafe for Genç
  - picture keys
  - word caps
- The teacher previews the grid and can swap or lock any cell.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- One summary line with a 'Değiştir' link ('B1 · Stüdyo · Standart · 20 dk · The Mole').
- Mode: Quick, Town or Crew.
- Format: Stage + Jury, or Parallel tables.
- Secret-deal route: code cards, phones, pass-the-tablet or heads-down.
- Topic: built-in YLE, MEB grade 5-8 and adult life/work categories, or a free-text prompt with a grid preview where cells can be swapped or locked.

QUICK-MODE DIALS
