MIXED ABILITY: Kolay / Orta / Zor shifts the suspect count (-1 / 0 / +1), the word-band mix, whether the question builder is available and how many hints there are, without changing the skin. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the level profile but keeps the skin and the case.
catalog.sessionMinutes: Oyun Parkı 20-25 · Arena 30-40 · Stüdyo 30-45 · Kısa sürüm 20 (2 rounds, 4 suspects, no twist)
catalog.teacherControls:
CASE: built-in library or a free prompt; 'Aynı dava, yeni suçlu' re-roll; preview with the solver proof ('each round leaves 6→4→2→1').
SIZE: suspects 3-6, places 3-6, methods 0-5, WHEN on/off, rounds 2-5, liars 0-2, red herring on/off, twist on/off and which round, extra tokens 0-5; the lesson-fit timer suggests all of these.
QUESTIONS: the question builder on/off (default on at A, off at B); ✓/✗ for free questions with template buttons and a token refund; a 'No comment' button.
VOICE: TTS voice presets per suspect (pitch and rate only, never accents) or 'Öğretmen okur'; show/hide answer text (listening mode); replay.
PRIVATE CLUES: envelopes, 'Heads down!' or QR phones.
PACE: mode timers, +10 s, T to pause, 'Süresiz'.
HELP: reveal a public clue early; privately eliminate a suspect for a struggling team ('bir şüpheliyi ele'; free for kids, costs points otherwise); sharpen a blurry clue for free.
SCORING: negatives, wager, Early call and Arena Intercept (each opt-in); Sharpest Question pick; Comeback Off/Light/Strong.
SAFETY: mature theme (adult B only, off by default); teenSafe is forced for Genç.
VIEWS: a GM panel with the fact cheat sheet, who is lying and the solution, shown in a second window, on the teacher's phone or on the printed sheet. On the main screen the solution appears only on a 2-s hold of S plus confirmation, never on a single keypress.
PRINT: picture grids for kids and Cluedo grids for adults, suspect cards, numbered envelopes, accusation slips with frames, live-mode role cards, badges and Agent ID cards, the teacher cheat sheet.
PROFILE: skin, Nazik rules, Kolay/Orta/Zor, 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' and the TR gloss toggle, all saved in the local class profile.
catalog.delightDetails:
- The case opens as a manila TOP SECRET folder with a paper clip and a 'CASE #' stamp. Kids get a sticker-covered notebook with Gogo in a deerstalker; Arena gets a holographic 'CASE #047' boot-up.
- A magnifying-glass cursor really enlarges the text under it, so it doubles as a legibility tool.
- Avatars are built from attribute layers, so the red cap really shows. The clue icon, the avatar layer and the printed grid all use the same art.
- The cork board shows Polaroid-style documents with pushpins in team colours and red string between related clues: neon laser lines in Arena, wool yarn for kids.
- Clue reveals make a typewriter clack for adults, a marimba 'pling' for kids and a synth blip in Arena, each 1 s or shorter.
- Tells: at B1+ the liar's portrait sweats or glances away, but only when someone asks about the fact they lied about. At B2 the innocent liar sweats too, as a red herring. In Arena a lie-detector needle wobbles.
- Blurry clues are really smudged, and sharpening one animates like a lens focusing.
- Arena's lab test has a UV lamp that makes the fingerprint glow.
- 'Heads down!' has a closed-eye icon and a soft 5-s tick.
- The CASE CLOSED stamp lands with a thunk and an ink splat.
- The timeline replay moves tiny figures across the map, with the culprit's path dotted red and 'LIE' flashing beside the document that exposed it.
- Kids get a kind ending: the culprit says sorry and shares, Gogo parrots the key sentence, and the badge is printed with the class name and date.
- Arena gets Agent ID cards with the unit's emblem and motto.
- Adults get a newspaper front page quoting the winning accusation.
- A case drawer in the class profile files each solved case with its stamp.
- Reduced motion swaps every effect for a static stamp. Team colours always come with shapes.
catalog.risks:
- Unsolvable or contradictory case: code owns the facts, the solver proves the case unique, the validator matches exact strings, and failures fall back to code-template text. The twist is pre-planned in the logic, never improvised.
- LLM text leaks another suspect's facts: the validator forbids other suspects' attribute strings, and the templates are strict.
- Private information on one screen: printed envelopes, 'Heads down!' or QR phones. Kids have no private clues at all.
- Too much reading at A1: pictures, TTS at 0.8x, word caps, split cards.
- Violence or crime for kids: incident whitelist and teenSafe lexicon ('took' or 'hid'). Adult murder only behind the mature toggle.
- Early guessing: the Stüdyo Early call has a real cost. Kids decide only at the final point.
- Weak readers left out: rotating roles, and the Reader reads aloud.
- Teacher overload: the app answers, B-level questions map to template buttons, and a cheat sheet is always at hand.
- Stereotyping a 'criminal look': the culprit is random, attributes are neutral clothes and objects, names are gender-balanced from the pool, and TTS never uses accents.
- A real student's name typed into the prompt: names come only from the pool.
- Lies confusing lower levels: no liars below B1 by default.
- Running over time: lesson-fit sizing, the 2-round short version and a 'Son ipucu şimdi' button.
- One student dominating: the seat spinner and rotating roles.
- LLM cost and rate limits: one cached generation per case, re-rolls with no LLM call, and built-in cases that work offline.
- Live-mode improvising breaks the logic: 'Not on your card → I don't remember.'

issues: The time budget does not fit a real 40-minute public-school lesson. Arena with 6 units × 3 rounds needs 18 turns. A real turn takes 75-100 s: seat spinner, 15-s huddle, 'Boards up', the question, a teacher ✓/✗, the TTS answer at 0.8x and often a lab item. That is 23-30 min for the investigation alone. Add 2 min briefing, 6-10 min accusation (6 speakers reading 2 reasons each, plus teacher validation), 3 min reveal, and 3-5 min handing out grids and envelopes after the bell. The total is about 45-50 min, against a stated 30-40 and about 34 usable minutes.

Oyun Parkı's pacing contradicts itself. It promises '3 rounds of 3-4 turns (about 70 s each)', but play is 4-6 teams each taking one turn per round. With 6 mascot teams, some teams only get 2 turns, or rounds run 7+ min. The spec never says which.

The kids' deduction is trivial and gets shouted out. Everything is public and 'public clues alone leave exactly 1'. By round 2, the fastest two or three kids in a class of 28 will call out 'It's Zip!', and the case is over for everyone else. The team competition then shrinks to A-D card stars, which don't depend on the mystery at all.

Active-student ratio: in Arena and Stüdyo only the spinner-chosen speaker of the active team produces language on each turn. With 6 units that is 1 of 28 students. Everyone else takes notes at best, and 12-year-olds whose unit isn't up will chat. The lab test is private to one unit, so 5 units sit idle during it.

'Heads down!' fails with 12-year-olds. Someone always peeks, the 5-s flash causes arguments ('they looked!'), and it makes 5 units sit idle with nothing to do. Envelopes are better, but the teacher has to walk envelope #4 to a unit mid-turn, which leaves the board. Other units also see which envelope number was handed over and can infer things from that.

Print logistics break the promised flexibility. Numbered envelopes, grids, suspect cards and slips have to be printed for each case. A same-day LLM case, or 'Aynı dava, yeni suçlu', makes last week's printed envelopes wrong. Turkish public schools often have limited printer access. Without print the game loses its private channel and the kids' cross-out grid. Setup is realistically 15-20 min of prep (cutting and stuffing envelopes), not about 1 min.

Teacher cognitive load at the board is very high in Arena and Stüdyo. At once the teacher runs the spinner, the huddle timer, ✓/✗ on free questions plus choosing the matching template button live, token accounting, envelope distribution, Intercept adjudication, and the cheat sheet on a second device. At the end they must validate up to 12 reasons against the cheat sheet in real time. Mapping a free B-level question to a template button under pressure is error-prone. A wrong mapping gives a true answer to the wrong question, and the logic breaks.

Fairness and runaway leader: at B levels public clues leave 2 suspects, so private lab clues decide the case. The strongest unit wins more lab tests, so it gets more clear clues and then the WHO 30 points. Blurry clues and Comeback Light (pick first) do not offset this. In Stüdyo, a correct Early call in round 2 means that team has solved it and is disengaged for the remaining rounds.

No meaningful stop at any moment. Deduction only pays off at the reveal, so a lesson cut short by a bell or an announcement is unsatisfying. 'Son ipucu şimdi' exists, but there is no single 'wrap up in 5 min' path that jumps straight to the accusation and reveal and keeps the scoring fair.
Replayability with the same class is weak. Once the class knows the case, the only replay is a re-rolled culprit, which invalidates the prints. Kids' cases are few and would be burnt in one term.

Legibility on a smart board: documents such as the CCTV log, receipts and the cork board with Polaroids and red strings are dense. From the back row of a 28-student room they are unreadable. The magnifier cursor only helps where the teacher points.

Live mode with 12-14-year-olds: volunteers improvise, giggle or give the game away, and one confident student in the suspect role takes over the lesson. The rule 'Not on your card → I don't remember' will not hold without active policing.

Noise: the rules for kids include a choral question repetition, a choral answer, a TPR stirrer and '3-2-1 point'. Good for engagement, but with 28 children and 6 teams earning stars from A-D cards, the teacher has to scan 6 raised cards every turn to award stars. Stars for 'each team showing the right card' means counting cards across the room each turn.

Build size is XL, with three rule packs, a solver, a validator, a print pack, TTS voices, live mode, QR phones and envelopes. There is a high risk the kids' mode ships as the least-tested path, even though it is the biggest classroom use.
fixes: Make the time budget turn-based, not round-based. The lesson-fit timer should compute turns = teams × rounds × 85 s and refuse settings over the limit. Default to 3-4 teams in a 40-minute lesson, and give a 28-student class 4 units of 7 with sub-roles, not 6 units. Make 'Kısa sürüm' (2 rounds) the default for public-school Genç classes.

Oyun Parkı: drop per-team turns. Run it as ONE whole-class agency with 6-8 'clue moments' in total, where the teacher or Gogo picks the action. Every moment is a whole-class A-D or TPR item, and stars go to all teams with the right card. Add a big 'Gizli tut!' rule and a 'secret guess' card: each team silently marks a suspect number on its card after each clue. The winner is revealed only at '3-2-1 point', which stops shouting from spoiling it.

Give idle units a simultaneous task every turn. While one unit interviews, the others fill a 'witness notes' gap on their slip, or answer the same lab item on mini-whiteboards for a smaller reward (a Parallel Lab). Nobody should sit through a turn with nothing to do.

Drop 'Heads down!' for Genç groups. The private channels become envelopes, or a digital-free option: the clue is shown as a 4-digit code on screen, and only the winning unit holds the printed decoder key, so no walking and no peeking. The envelope number should not be visible on screen, e.g. hand over a 'sealed' card from a shuffled stack.

Make print re-roll-proof. Print generic envelopes numbered 1-12 with a QR/short code or a blank line, and let the screen say which to open. Or print 'clue cards' on demand as a single A4 page per team that is cut once. Add a 'Baskısız mod' that works fully on one screen (all clues public, units compete on lab accuracy and accusation reasons), and make it the default for public schools.

Reduce teacher load. Offer only template-chip questions for B1 Genç as the default (free questions for adults only). Add a single 'Öğretmen kokpiti' view on the teacher's phone that shows the next action as one big button. Auto-track tokens, stars and envelopes. At the accusation, pre-tick reasons the app can match (the slip picks from a fact list plus a sentence frame), so the teacher only judges the grammar.

Add a catch-up mechanic that works on deduction, not just points. A unit that is 2+ clues behind gets its blurry clue auto-sharpened at round end, or the 'bir şüpheliyi ele' help for free. Early call: if a team is right, it becomes 'consultant' and scores for asking a Sharpest Question for others, so it stays engaged.

Add a big 'Bitir: 5 dk' button. It jumps straight to a compressed accusation (WHO plus 1 reason, chorus or boards) and a 60-s reveal, and scores only what has been earned. Also add 'Kaydet ve devam et' to continue the case next lesson from the case drawer.

Legibility: for the smart board, show documents one at a time as full-screen cards with a minimum 36 px body text. The cork board is a summary view only. Add a 'Sınıf büyüklüğü: kalabalık' dial that raises the font size and hides decorative strings.

Live mode for Arena: teacher opt-in only. Cards have a 'script' with 5 fixed answers, and there is a 'Kart dışı → Bilmiyorum' buzzer sound the teacher can hit. Keep app-voiced suspects as the default for 12-14.

Replayability: ship at least 8 built-in cases per audience, not 5. Add a 'Vaka motoru' that re-skins the same logic grid with a new theme vocabulary (pack swap), so the same class gets a new case without a new LLM call. Track 'played by this class' in the class profile.

Scope the build: ship the MVP as Stüdyo plus Arena with public clues plus lab points and a print-free default, and Oyun Parkı as the whole-class variant. Defer QR phones, Intercept, wagers, live mode and the timeline replay to v2.

issues: B1 gives away the culprit. At B1 there is exactly one liar and it is always the culprit, so the first document that exposes a lie solves the case. That breaks the solver's own rule that 'no single clue solves the case'. The sweat and glance-away tell is worse: at B1 it fires only on the culprit, so a team can solve the case by watching the portrait and use no English at all.

Most of the deduction happens in Turkish. The real thinking (crossing off, cross-checking the CCTV log against the receipt) happens during the huddle, and nothing asks for English there. English production comes down to one Questioner's sentence per turn plus 1-2 accusation reasons. With 5 teams, 3 rounds and one action per turn, a single student speaks roughly once per lesson. Listening and reading load is high, but spoken output is low.

The lab tests are disconnected from the case. When the lab pack is 'any grammar unit or vocab category', fixing a Present Perfect error sentence to 'unlock a fingerprint' is just a coat of paint. The language doesn't feed the deduction, and at B levels the lab becomes a quiz nested inside a mystery.

Free teacher prompts can't cover every grammar point. The case generator only validates past simple, past continuous, modals of deduction and reported speech (regex). A teacher who types 'present perfect' or 'comparatives' or 'future plans' into the case prompt gets either a quiet fallback to template past-tense text or a mismatch. The design never says which grammar a case can carry.

A1 Genç learners who barely read are only partly served. The core loop still depends on a printed picture grid, attribute icons and chip templates like 'Has he got a 🧢?'. That works as Guess Who. But Search 'documents' and 'public clue cards' at 0-4 words still assume decoding, and A-D answer cards for every clue need printing plus logistics. Without the print pack, A1 kids have nothing to cross out.

A2 Genç (9-11) gets past simple wh- questions, clock times and documents of 8 words or fewer. For Turkish state-school 9-11-year-olds, past simple with times is usually grade 7 content. Where/when/who-with past questions from chips are a stretch, and the attribute load (4-5 suspects × 4 places) is heavy for this age.

B2 Genç: modals of deduction in the past (must have / can't have + past participle) as a REQUIRED accusation component is steep for 12-13-year-olds even at a nominal B2. Reported speech with past perfect in witness lines adds to that load. There is a risk of the teacher rejecting valid reasons and demotivating the class.

A1 adults: 'Who Ate the Manager's Birthday Cake?' with has got / is wearing picture chips will feel like Guess Who for kids unless the documents and humour carry it. The A1 adult experience depends heavily on tone, and 'there was / was in as a chunk' is the only adult-grade grammar.

At B levels the teacher is overloaded and questions become inauthentic. Every free question must be judged ✓/✗ AND mapped live to a template button, or the answer is 'I don't remember.' Real, interesting questions (Why…? Did you like the manager?) hit a wall, which teaches students to ask only template-shaped questions. That undermines the 'free questions' promise.

Printed envelopes conflict with the re-roll. 'Aynı dava, yeni suçlu' re-seeds the culprit and the clue plan, so any pre-printed numbered envelopes and cheat sheets go stale. At A2 Genç and above the private-clue channel relies on printing, and teachers will reuse old prints by mistake.

Downtime. Only one team acts per turn, and in Arena and Stüdyo a turn can run 60-90 s (huddle, question, listen, notes). The other teams' job is to listen to public answers, but without a structured whole-class response (unlike Oyun Parkı) the 12-14 group will drift.

Build size is XL, with three full rule packs, a solver, an LLM pipeline, live mode, a print pack, TTS voices and the Intercept, Wager and Early call options. For level fit this means some levels will ship half-tested. B2 needs six attribute dimensions with WHEN, two liars, a red herring and contradictory witnesses. That is hard to generate reliably and hard for a class to track on one projector.
fixes: Split the liar from the culprit at B1: the liar is the culprit only about 50% of the time, and otherwise an innocent with a harmless secret. Hold back the lie-exposing document until the last round, and add a solver rule that exposing a lie removes at most one other candidate. Drop the sweat tell at B1, or trigger it on at least one innocent every case, and never let it fire only on the culprit.

Make the huddle produce English. Each team's Note-taker fills a 'Case notes' frame on the grid in English ('X was in the ___ at ___ → NOT X'). The Speaker must say one elimination sentence aloud each round ('It wasn't Mimi because she was in the garden'), and the teacher ticks it for points. At A levels, give the chip frames 'It isn't ___. He hasn't got a ___.'

Default the lab pack to CASE-LINKED items generated from the fact table: gap-fill the suspect's alibi, fix the error in a witness line, unjumble the receipt line. Show a small 'Konu dışı laboratuvar' warning when the teacher picks an unrelated grammar unit.

Publish a grammar-compatibility list in setup. The case can carry have got, can, there is/are, is wearing, past simple, was/were, past continuous, modals of deduction and reported speech. For other targets (present perfect, comparatives, future), route the grammar to the lab pack only and tell the teacher in Turkish that the case stays in the past tense.

Add a no-print path for A1 Genç. Keep an on-screen shared picture grid that the class crosses out together by pointing and choral 'NO!', and handle every clue moment through TPR (stand up if it's yes) instead of A-D cards. Make every clue picture-only at A1 Genç, with TTS reading the 0-4 words twice.

Lower A2 Genç to WHO plus a 3-location WHERE and 4 suspects. Offer 'past simple' as opt-in and default instead to present-tense 'Where is ___ now?' / 'Is she in the kitchen?'. Turn clock times on only when the MEB grade is 7 or higher.

At B2 Genç, make modals of deduction optional-with-bonus: a plain 'because' reason is valid, and a modal reason scores +5 extra. Use one liar, not two, and contradicting witnesses as an option only. Keep reported speech to 'said (that)' in the simple past, with no past perfect required.

For A1 adults, default to the documents-and-humour case with adult suspects (the office, the flatmates) and WHO + WHERE using 'there was / was in', and never use cartoon avatars. Also add a 'Yetişkin A1' preview check so the teacher sees the tone before class.

Add a 'Diğer soru' button for off-template free questions. The teacher gives a canned in-character deflection or a quick typed/spoken answer marked as non-evidence, and the question still earns the ✓ point. Show the template list to B-level teams as 'Kanıt soruları' so they learn which questions pay off.

Print a case seed code and a date on every envelope and cheat sheet. A re-roll shows 'Yeni zarflar yazdır' and blocks the envelope channel (switching to 'Heads down!' or QR) until a reprint matches the seed.

For Arena and Stüdyo, add a whole-class 'Everyone decides' moment every turn: after each public answer, every team shows YES or NO for 'Does this rule out X?' on mini-whiteboards for 1 point. This cuts downtime and turns listening into accountable comprehension.

Phase the build. The MVP is the Guess-Who core (WHO + WHERE, public clues, chips, picture grid, the solver) for all 8 groups, plus the 3 skins. Add liars, witnesses, WHEN, live mode, Intercept and Wager in v2, after class testing shows the B-level cases stay trackable on one projector.

issues: SCOPE: This is more than XL. It combines a constraint solver, a clue scheduler, a two-pass LLM pipeline with a validator, 3 skins, 3 rule packs, 4 level profiles, layered avatars, floor-plan maps, a timeline replay, TTS voice presets, 3 private channels (envelopes, Heads down, QR phones), live-mode role cards, 6+ printables, a GM second window and a case drawer. It is the riskiest candidate in the suite. As specified it would cost as much to build as 3-4 of the other games together.

The solver is the EASY part: even at B2 there are only about 1,000 (who, where, how, when) tuples, so brute force is trivial. The HARD part is meeting all the clue-plan constraints at once: a second route for every elimination at B levels, a candidate count that drops every round, no single clue that solves the case, public clues leaving at most 2 suspects, each lie exposed by exactly one document, and a red herring that eliminates nothing. On small fact tables no valid plan may exist for a given seed, and the design gives no fallback for that.

LLM validation is weaker than it looks. Exact-string checks catch leaked attribute strings, but not semantic leaks or contradictions. For example, 'she left before the party started' implies a time, 'the garden was locked' eliminates a place, and 'he hates sweets' implies a motive. Any flavour tail, document or witness line can quietly add a fact that eliminates an option the solver never saw. The case then becomes unsolvable or trivially solvable, and nothing detects it.

Kids design flaw: at A1 the attributes are visual (colour, clothes, body features) and they are drawn on the portraits. Asking a suspect about a red cap is pointless when the whole class can see the cap. At A1 the deduction is really 'clue card + look at the pictures', which is Guess Who. The interview phase adds nothing unless it asks about hidden facts (what's in the bag, where were you, can you ...).

Grammar inconsistency in the kids chips: the class asks the suspect directly, so the question should be 'Have you got a cap?' to fit the reply 'Yes, I have!'. The design writes 'Has he got a cap?', which is a question about the suspect to a third person. The chip templates teach a mismatched pair.

The Oyun Parkı version has no competitive deduction. Everything is public, nobody lies, public clues alone solve the case, and everyone points at the end, so every team reaches the same answer. The stars come only from whole-class A-D items. That makes it a guided picture story plus a quiz. It can still be charming, but the 'detective' mechanic is thin and could feel like a quiz with a skin.

The lab tests are generic quiz items dressed as forensics (fingerprint = fix the error, and so on). With lab content from any unit, this mode duplicates the MCQ, gap and error mechanics of every other game in the suite. The mystery layer only earns its place through the interview, document and deduction loop.

Private clues on one screen are fragile. 'Heads down' for 5 s with 4-6 teams means 4-6 heads-down cycles per round, which is slow and invites peeking. The printed envelopes must be regenerated whenever the case changes, and 'Aynı dava, yeni suçlu' silently makes an already printed pack wrong. A blurry clue needs a second printed version of every envelope. QR phones add a real-time backend (Supabase realtime or polling) with sync and auth risk.

Teacher load at B levels: for every free question the teacher has to judge the grammar, pick one of about 12 template buttons in real time, handle the token refund and log the correction, all while projecting. That is a lot of interface for a live classroom and will slow each turn to 90 s or more.

TTS risk: Web Speech voices differ a lot between smartboard PCs, many Turkish Windows installs have only one English voice or none, and a pitch/rate preset on one voice does not sound like different characters. Voice identity for suspects will be inconsistent.

Art is the biggest asset cost. The design needs layered avatars in 3 art styles (cartoon animals and robots, illustrated teens and androids, adult editorial), attribute layers for every look and item, location imageKeys for many themes, top-down floor plans per case, method icons, props for the document types (receipt, ticket, CCTV), plus kids' picture scenes. LLM-generated themes ('robot dog on a space station') will often ask for places and objects that have no art, so kids' packs lose most of their content or fall back to generic images.

There are too many scoring variants: combo, wager, early call, intercept, negatives, token bank, Sharpest Question and Comeback in 3 modes. Each one multiplies the QA work and the explanation load, and the deduction itself is the fun.

The timing adds up to too much: 6 teams × 3 rounds × (15-s huddle + action + judging), plus the public clue, twist, accusation reading and reveal, is 40+ minutes before any extras. The 20-25 min kids target with 4-6 teams only fits if the turns are whole-class rather than per team.
Overlap: 'Kim Yaptı?', Alibi and the Guess Who kids play are already implied by the case/character types in the catalog. If those exist as separate candidates, they duplicate this one.
fixes: Ship in 3 phases. V1: 6-8 HAND-AUTHORED built-in cases (2 per audience, spread over the levels) as JSON checked by the same solver at build time, with no LLM and no QR phones. V2: a template-only generator ('Aynı dava, yeni suçlu' and code-generated cases from a theme vocab list). V3: LLM flavour text. This keeps the first release M-L instead of XL.

LLM text: the facts are only ever rendered by code sentence templates. The LLM may write only (a) intro, confession and bios from a fixed slot schema, and (b) flavour tails of at most 8 words from a closed list of emotions and mood words, never nouns, times or places. Add a second validator pass that tags every noun, time and place in the LLM text and rejects any that are not in the fact table for that item. Documents are template-built; the LLM only varies their layout words.

Solver: generate the fact table and the clue plan together in a seeded retry loop (for example up to 200 seeds, well under 50 ms). If no plan satisfies every constraint, relax them in a fixed order (red herring, then the second route, then monotonic drop) and show the relaxed rule in 'Önizle'. Unit-test this with 10,000 random seeds per level in CI.

Kids: split the attributes into VISIBLE ones (on the portrait, used in public clue cards) and HIDDEN ones (asked in the interview: 'Were you in the kitchen?', 'Have you got cake in your bag?', 'Can you jump high?'). Make the chips second person ('Have you got...?' / 'Yes, I have!'). Have one hidden fact per round decide the last elimination, so the questions matter.

Kids: turn the per-team turns into class turns. Teams take turns CHOOSING the action (who to ask, where to look), but the whole class answers every item. That keeps the 20-25 min target and the 'whole-class moment every turn' checklist item.

Tie the lab content to the case by default and make that the only option in V1. Lab items must use the case vocabulary and the target grammar (for example, unjumble a suspect's alibi sentence, gap-fill the receipt). An unrelated grammar unit can come in a later version. This keeps the game from being a generic quiz with a noir skin.

Private clues: in V1 only printed envelopes and 'Heads down', and Heads down only for 2-3 teams. Print the pack with a case+seed code on every page, and show a red warning 'Basılı paket geçersiz' if the teacher re-rolls after printing. Put the blurry and clear versions on the same envelope card as two fold-halves (the fold opens only after the second lab test), so there is no second print run.

Teacher panel for B levels: put a phone or second-window 'suspect answer grid' (rows = template questions, columns = suspects) in the GM view. The teacher taps the cell and ✓ in one gesture, and the correction log is optional (a long-press). Aim for under 3 s of teacher interaction per question.

Voices: the default is 'Öğretmen okur' with the answer text on screen. TTS is an opt-in with an on-setup voice test button. For built-in cases, consider pre-rendered short MP3s (about 30-60 KB each) of the suspect answers so identity is consistent.

Art budget: one shared layered avatar system (base + hat + glasses + scarf + bag + colour) drawn in ONE flat vector style and re-themed by palette and outline weight per skin, rather than 3 art styles. Use about 12 generic locations (kitchen, garden, classroom, lab, library, gym, office, hotel lobby, ferry deck, museum hall, corridor, storeroom) as reusable SVG floor-plan tiles. Map the LLM's theme places onto these slots rather than inventing new art.
Collapse scoring to one table per mode with at most 4 opt-ins. Cut the confidence wager OR Early call (keep Early call), and cut the combo in Stüdyo. Keep Intercept out until V2.

Cut or defer: QR phone channel, live-mode printables for B1 (keep them for B2 only in V1), the minute-by-minute timeline walk animation (replace it with a static path drawn on the map plus 'LIE' flags), the magnifier cursor (use a zoom button instead), and the case drawer (V2).

Polish that is worth building in V1: the manila folder intro, the CASE CLOSED stamp with a thunk, the cork board with pins and string, the blurry-to-sharp lens animation, and a big-target deduction grid that works on a touch smartboard (min 64 px cells, tap to cycle ?/✗/✓).
Merge: if 'Kim Yaptı?', Alibi or a Guess Who kids game exist as separate candidates, fold them in here as this game's A1 kids and B1-B2 live-mode presets instead of building separate games.

catalog.rankReason: The detective case (adult 8, teen 5.7) has the biggest scope in the suite: a solver, a clue scheduler and an LLM pipeline. If built, v1 is 6-8 hand-authored cases checked by the solver, with no LLM, no phones, and whole-class agency for kids. It takes c04's case frame and c10's case modes.

catalog.name: Kaçış Odası (Escape Room + Tıkla-Keşfet command mode)
catalog.familiarAs: Breakout EDU / Genially escape room / point-and-click 'escape the room'
catalog.oneLiner: A locked room on the projector with 3-7 locks and a countdown. Teams solve language puzzles from jigsaw evidence packs, and the engine turns their correct answers into the lock codes (the LLM never makes a code). In Komut Modu the same room becomes a point-and-click game: the class tells an on-screen hand what to do in English ('Look under the bed', 'Use the key on the box') until the last lock opens.
catalog.howItPlays:
ONE ROOM, THREE WAYS TO PLAY. The teacher picks one at setup. All three share the same sticker scene, story wrapper and code engine.
A) KİLİT MODU (Breakout, the default): teams solve evidence packs to open locks.
B) KOMUT MODU (Tıkla-Keşfet): the whole class commands an on-screen hand through a chain of object puzzles. One screen, no packs.
C) TAM MACERA: a 3-5 minute Komut opening in which the class commands the hand to find each team's lock envelope ('Look under the bed' reveals Lock 2's card), followed by Kilit Modu.

KİLİT MODU, STEP BY STEP
0) Setup (1 min). Pick the group chip plus a built-in category, or type a prompt (Turkish is fine). The engine builds the room, the locks, the codes, the printable packs and the teacher answer sheet. The optional ÖNİZLEME mode auto-plays the room at 10x speed so the teacher can check it before class.
1) Practice lock (20-30 s, unscored). This is a 2-wheel colour lock. In Oyun Parkı Gogo demos it; Arena gets a tutorial lock with the SYSTEM caption; Stüdyo gets an optional 'Kilit 0'. The whole class sees how an answer becomes a wheel.
2) Briefing (60 s or less). The intro is read by TTS and kept within the group's text cap. A long intro becomes 2-3 caption cards, and kids get picture panels. The stakes are framed per skin: 'The museum closes in 25 minutes' for adults, 'Open the toy box before the party!' for kids.
3) Roles (10-15 s). The seat-number spinner hands out jigsaw cards A-D and the Runner. Kids' roles are pictograms: Eyes (look and read), Ears (Gogo's audio), Pencil (writes the code), Feet (runner). Nobody is ever picked by name.
4) Solve. Each lock's information is split by the engine across 4 cards, so no single card can solve it. Example for a word lock: card A has gap sentences 1-2, card B has sentences 3-4, card C has the word bank, and card D has the wheel key (which item feeds which wheel). The rule 'Keep your card - say it!' means cards are read aloud, never passed around, which forces spoken English inside the team. A pack can be a PDF with cut lines, 4 tabs on a team device (QR, no login), or zoomable cards on the projector in screen-only mode. On devices, MCQ stems appear first and the options follow after 3-4 s (kids), 2.5 s (Arena) or 2 s (adults).
5) Lock kinds. The engine builds 3-7 per room from pack items and computes every code itself:
- WORD: 3-5 gap, vocab or qa answers whose first letters spell a code word. The engine picks a real level word first, then chooses items that fit it.
- NUMBER: MCQs whose displayed option order is fixed by the engine so that the correct option numbers read the code; or count something in a text, read a time off a timetable, a date or an ordinal.
- SORT: sort 8 words into 2 boxes; the count in box A is a digit.
- ORDER: unjumble a sentence; the tiles carry small numbers that read the code only in the correct order.
- FUSE BOX: tf statements set switches (true = up, false = down); this is a direction lock.
- MAP: follow directions on a 5x5 sticker grid to get an arrow sequence. The sentences come from engine templates.
- COLOUR: read descriptions and set the colour dial. Every colour also has a shape and a label, so colour-blind students can play.
- PICTURE: listen to TTS and tap 3-4 pictures in order.
- ODD ONE OUT: in each set, the position of the odd item is one digit.
- READING NOTE: an email, poster, diary or timetable of 40-120 words with one question and a single number or word answer. A verifier blind-solves it.
- ERROR (B1+): the number of the line with no mistake is the digit.
- SOUND (B1+): -ed endings or minimal pairs by TTS (/t/ = 1, /d/ = 2, /ɪd/ = 3).
- RIDDLE (B2 and Arena): 'What am I?' with 3 clues; the answer is the password.
- CIPHER (Arena): a simple symbol or shift cipher on a pack word.
6) Entering a code. In device mode the team types it and the wheels spin into place. In paper mode the Runner uses the CODE KIOSK at the board (masked entry on the touch screen or on the teacher's phone remote), or shows the code on a mini-whiteboard to the teacher only.
- Correct: the lock animates open and gives a master-door fragment (a letter plus a sticker) and one story line.
- Wrong: that lock only gets a cooldown for that team, rising 10 s, 20 s, then 30 s. Kids get an 8 s 'sleepy lock' instead of an alarm. A wrong code gives no partial feedback, which stops brute-force guessing; hints give the feedback instead.
7) Hints. Each team gets 3 tokens per room, with the cost set by audience. The ladder per lock is: NUDGE (the method: 'Look at the first letters!'), then CHECK (the engine names the wrong item; in paper mode the team reads its answers to the teacher's remote checklist), then REVEAL one item.
8) Flow. Locks run in a line or in 2 parallel branches (the default at B1+ and in Arena), so one hard lock never stalls a team. The master door needs every fragment.
9) Early finishers. They open the Bonus Vault (Stüdyo), the Golden Lock (Arena) or the Sticker Chest (Oyun Parkı), which hold harder items or one riddle. In co-op they may also use 'Gift a hint' to send a free hint to any team.
10) Master door. The fragments spell the final word, a pack term the engine chose. The class reads it aloud together and says what it means, and the door creaks open for the finale.
11) Time up.
- Oyun Parkı never loses: 'Gogo gives you 3 more minutes!' once, then Süresiz.
- Arena gets a 2-minute Overtime; an 'Overtime escape' still counts and earns a badge.
- Stüdyo ends with the locks opened so far; the remaining answers go to the debrief, and the teacher may extend the time.
12) Debrief (3-5 min):
- each lock's answers with whyTr (whyEn at B levels);
- an automatic 'most-missed items' list built from logged entries;
- a hands-up vote for the hardest clue;
- the red herring revealed;
- the words met, which can be saved as a Languago word list.

KOMUT MODU (TIKLA-KEŞFET), TURN BY TURN
1) The projector shows an illustrated room built from the sticker library, with hidden hotspots, an inventory bar and a hand cursor.
2) Each turn starts with a huddle (10 s kids, 15 s Arena, 20 s adults). The spinner then picks the team's Voice, who says ONE command: VERB + OBJECT (+ PREPOSITION + OBJECT).
3) How commands get in:
- A1-A2: a VERB BAR with pictures (LOOK AT, TAKE, OPEN, USE...ON, PUSH, READ, PUT...IN/ON/UNDER, GIVE...TO, TALK TO) and an object picker; the teacher clicks what was said.
- B1: the teacher or a student scribe types the command into a small parser.
- B2: a free parser accepts complex commands ('Put the painting back where it was').
4) ACCURACY GATE (A2+, can be switched off). A command counts only if it was said with the article and the right preposition. Otherwise the hand shrugs, the screen shows a recast ('Look UNDER the bed?') and the team tries once more.
5) The hand acts: it opens the drawer or lifts the rug. The response line is read by TTS, and the inventory updates. A silly but valid command gets a funny refusal ('You can't eat the lamp.').
6) Kids only: before the hand moves, the whole class echoes the command with a TPR gesture ('Open the box!' with opening hands). This gives the whole-class response every turn.
7) The chain has 4-10 steps, for example: find the torch, look under the bed, find the note, read the note, open the safe with the code in it. The last step is always a lock from the same lock engine.
8) Scoring. A useful command (it moves the chain on or finds an inventory item) earns 1 star (Oyun Parkı) or 100 points (Arena, Stüdyo). The secret bonus object earns 1 sticker or 50 points. A correct but useless command costs nothing, and the turn passes.
9) BLIND GUIDE (B1+). Only one team sees the scene, on its device or a printed still, and describes it ('There's a lamp on the desk, next to the window'). Another team gives the commands. The roles swap every step.
10) The teacher's remote shows the hidden walkthrough, with the next useful command in grey. As a hint, the teacher can pulse a glow on a hotspot.
catalog.playerSetup:
- KİLİT MODU CO-OP (the default in Oyun Parkı): 3-6 teams of 3-5. Each team owns one lock and its pack, and the master door needs every team's fragment, so the class escapes together.
- KİLİT MODU RACE (the default in Arena, optional in Stüdyo): 3-6 teams of 3-5. Each team has the whole room, on a device (QR, no login) or a printed packet. Each team gets a reshuffled variant with the same items but different wheel orders and codes, so a code shouted across the room is useless. The projector shows only the progress doors.
- KOMUT MODU: 3-5 teams take turns through a rotating Voice picked by the seat spinner, and the whole class may suggest. One screen.
- TAM MACERA: a whole-class Komut opening, then co-op or race.
- Team size: in teams of 3, the engine merges jigsaw cards C and D. Teams of 5-6 add Runner and Recorder role cards.
- Devices: zero devices is fine (printed packs or zoomable cards on screen), and one device per team is optional. The teacher runs the game from the laptop plus an optional phone remote (QR), so the GM panel and the codes never appear on the projector.
catalog.contentShape:
ENVELOPE: pack.frames.escape
- title, titleTr, skin, intro, outro. Skins: 'toyroom' | 'zoo' | 'wizard' | 'space' | 'pirates' | 'robot' | 'arcade' | 'temple' | 'lab' | 'hotel' | 'airport' | 'office' | 'attic' | 'detective'.
- timerMin (computed by the lesson-fit timer); mode: 'coop' | 'race' | 'command' | 'full'.
- locks[]: lock items {id, kind, title, itemIds[], derive, flavour, hints[3]}. The code is computed.
- branches?: [[lockIds], [lockIds]].
- finalVault {fragmentWord, fragmentOrder}: both computed. fragmentWord is a pack vocab term whose length equals the number of locks.
- bonusVault {itemIds[]}.
- redHerring? (a decoy card; B2 or the Zor setting only).
- room:
  - sceneKey: a background from the sticker library.
  - objects[]: each {id, sticker (library key), names[] (accepted nouns such as 'the red box'), pos, states[], relations (in/on/under/behind), actions {look, take, open, read, push, use:{with, result}, put:{prep, target}, give:{to, result}, talkTo}, responses (within the group's text cap), funnyRefusal}.
  - chain[]: each {step, canonical command, accepts[] (verb+object patterns), reveals (an object, lock or itemId), hintTr}.
  - bonusObject; verbs[] (the level whitelist).

ANSWERABLE ITEMS: at least 12 at A1, about 30 at B2.
- mcq: number locks; whyOpt is reused in the debrief.
- gap / vocab / qa: word locks. The first letter must be the same for every accepted form (answers, alt[], alsoOk[]), or the item is rejected for firstLetters locks.
- order: order lock; the engine prints the code numbers on the tokens.
- category-list: sort lock (2 lists).
- tf: fuse box, and picture true/false for kids.
- odd: odd-one-out lock.
- text, plus its mcq/qa/tf items with textRef: the reading lock (blind-solved).
- error: error lock, B1+.
- pair: picture or definition matching; the matched numbers read the code.
- sound: sound lock, B1+, with tts.
- riddle: riddle lock and the B2 bonus.

MADE BY THE ENGINE, NEVER THE LLM:
- all codes and wheel counts;
- the fixed option order of MCQs inside number locks;
- the map-lock grids and direction sentences (templates within the level's grammar whitelist);
- colour-lock descriptions and cipher texts;
- the 4-card jigsaw split for every lock;
- the per-team race variants;
- the PDF packs and the teacher answer sheet.

BUILT-IN CONTENT:
- a category gives words.js terms with emoji or imageKey for word and picture locks;
- a grammar_mcq_* unit feeds number locks, and the teacher can set a grammar target per lock;
- readings_* feed reading and count locks;
- idioms.js feeds a B2 idiom lock.

PROMPT MODE:
- Call 1 returns the escape envelope plus items in the item-type schemas, with no codes.
- Call 2 blind-solves the reading note and every lock's items.
- If a lock's answer does not match, or its derivation is ambiguous, the engine swaps in a bank lock of the same kind and flags it 'yedek' in the preview.

VALIDATOR:
- the group's text caps;
- teenSafe for every Genç group;
- every sticker key exists;
- the command chain is solvable by a state-graph search from the start state;
- the bonus object is reachable;
- no code word is on the offensive-word blocklist, no code is trivial (1111, 1234), and no code equals a visible answer.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO: 'Escape Room Night'.

LOOK AND FEEL
- An editorial noir look, in cream or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme.
- Props look real but carry no brands: boarding passes with the team name printed as the passenger, emails, receipts, sticky notes, timetables, hotel notices, lab labels.
- No mascot and no voice lines. A neutral caption only ('Lock 3 of 5 · Passive').
- English on the student screen, Turkish in the teacher controls.

ROOMS
- 'Checkout in 10 Minutes' (A1-A2 hotel room: imperatives and prepositions). The ideal Komut Modu room: find the passport, the charger and the ring.
- 'The Recipe Vault' (A2: food, quantities, countable and uncountable).
- 'Airport Lounge Lockdown' (A2 travel: gates, times, announcements; a map lock through the terminal).
- 'The Locked Office: find the password before the investor arrives' (B1: emails, schedules, polite requests).
- 'The Time Capsule' (B1 past tenses).
- 'Grandma's Attic' (B1 Komut Modu: found objects tell a family story in past tenses).
- 'Room 404' (B2 hotel mystery: passive voice, deduction with must have / can't have).
- 'The Detective's Office' (B2 riddles, conditional hints).
- 'Transit Zone' (B2: notices, word formation).
The teacher can set a language focus per lock ('Lock 2: present perfect'), taken from the grammar units.

RULES AND SCORING
- Co-op or race, chosen by the teacher.
- Points: 100 per lock, +50 for a clean unlock (right on the first try), -50 per hint (optional negatives), +150 for the Bonus Vault.
- Finish time is only the tiebreaker, unless the teacher turns on 'Klasik yarış', which ranks by finish time plus 1 minute per hint.
- Optional wager at the final vault: bet up to 200 points on opening it at the first try.
- Wrong code: an 'ACCESS DENIED' flash and a 10/20/30 s cooldown.
- Hints: 3 tokens (nudge, then check, then reveal), each adding 1 minute. A Turkish-gloss nudge can be switched off for immersion classes.
- Roles: the spokesperson and Runner rotate every lock. Pairs confer inside the team, and jigsaw cards are read aloud.
- The timer is strict by default. A heartbeat and speeding music in the last minute are opt-in.

KOMUT MODU FOR ADULTS
Typed parser from B1, Blind Guide, a 'Funniest command' award, and dry object lines ('The plant doesn't want to talk. It's had a long day.').

ENDING
- A full score table with escape times.
- The 'Kaçırılanlar' review list (item, correct answer, whyTr/whyEn).
- The hardest-clue vote.
- An optional certificate: 'Escaped with 04:12 left'.
catalog.teenVersion:
OYUN PARKI (9-11, the default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç): 'Help Gogo!'
This is a stripped ruleset, not the adult one re-coloured.

FRAMING
Never 'trapped' and never danger:
- 'Open the toy box before the party!'
- 'Help the zoo animals find their breakfast'
- 'Fix Gogo's spaceship'
- 'The Wizard's Kitchen: make the potion'
- 'Pirate Island treasure' (no weapons)
- 'Robot Factory'
- 'Chocolate Factory' (no brands)

LOOK AND MODE
- A warm cream palette, chunky rounded locks with big picture wheels, and animal team mascots (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin, bear).
- Co-op is the default: each team owns one lock and the class escapes together.
- A1 Genç rooms have 3 locks. If there are more teams, the extra teams get copies of a lock or the Sticker Chest.

THE 3 RULES (a pictogram card, explainable in 20 s)
1) Keep your card - say it!
2) Find the code - give it to Gogo.
3) Stuck? Ask Gogo (free).

KIDS CHECKLIST
- No elimination. The clock never ends the game: at 0 a marimba chime plays and 'Gogo gives you 3 more minutes!', then Süresiz.
- No score below zero: stars and stickers only.
- A whole-class moment every turn. Whenever any lock opens, the class echoes its answers and the code word twice with Gogo; in Komut Modu everyone repeats the command with a gesture.
- Non-violent failure: a wrong code makes the lock sleepy for 8 s (snowflakes, a yawn). No alarm and no red.
- The clock is a calm ring that is never red, and there is never a heartbeat.

GOGO THE PARROT
- Demos the unscored practice lock.
- Reads every clue aloud at 0.8x ('Öğretmen okur' if there is no English voice).
- Gives hints in a speech bubble: picture, then first letter, then listen again.
- After a team's 2nd wrong code on a lock, points at the card that feeds the wrong wheel.
- After the 3rd, says that answer; the class repeats it twice and the team earns an effort star for the class album.

LOCKS FOR KIDS
- PICTURE: listen, then tap pictures in order.
- COLOUR: colour plus shape plus label.
- NUMBER: count the apples.
- FUSE BOX: picture true/false.
- WORD: picture wheels at A1, letter wheels from A2.
Codes are 3 characters. The 'Adım adım' device option lights one wheel per correct item. Paper packs are picture cards with 0-4 English words each.

PACING AND ENDING
- Each lock is one round of about 4-5 minutes. After lock 2 comes a 45 s 'Gogo stretch' (TPR: Stand up! Open the door! Turn the key!) with the clock paused.
- Every team gets a title: Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Sharp Eyes, Bravest Guessers.
- A room sticker goes into the class album, confetti falls in team colours and shapes, and there are printable certificates.
- Kids' Komut Modu room: 'Gogo's Messy Bedroom' (in/on/under, toys, colours, 4 steps with verb pictures).

ARENA (12-14): 'Breakout Protocol'
The default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç. It is also suggested for grade 6+ or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor'.

LOOK
- Dark navy with neon team colours, a condensed display font and geometric emblems.
- No cartoon animals and no talking mascot. A SYSTEM caption strip ('ACCESS GRANTED', 'CLEAN UNLOCK x3', 'CLUTCH!') appears at most once per lock.
- Ownership in 10 s: each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto, which are painted on its door.

ROOMS
'Arcade Glitch' (stuck inside a retro game level), 'Signal Lost' (spaceship reboot), 'Temple of Echoes', 'Deep Sea Station', 'Cyber Lab Lockdown', 'Robot Factory: Override'.

RULES
- Race is the default; co-op is available.
- Points come from accuracy only. The combo counts clean unlocks, or item accuracy in device mode: x1.5 at 3 in a row, x2 at 5. The score has a floor at zero.
- Wrong code: ACCESS DENIED and a 15 s cooldown. The streak breaks, and nothing is lost.
- Hints: first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example. Each costs 1 point or 30 s and never takes a score below 0.
- Extra challenge: a cipher lock, a riddle, and one red herring from B1 Genç (it can be switched off).
- Time up: a 2-minute Overtime, and an 'Overtime escape' still counts.

ENDING
A podium for the top 3 plus stat awards (Clean sheet, Longest streak, Comeback, Codebreaker, No-hint run). Never a last place and never an individual's name.

ACROSS BOTH AUDIENCES
- A 13-year-old A1 class gets the Arena visuals with A1 content and full picture and audio support. A 9-year-old B1 class keeps Oyun Parkı.
- Every Genç room passes the teenSafe filter (no brands, dating, horror or violence; a 'heist' becomes 'recover the lost crown') and uses YLE-style and MEB-unit concrete topics.
- B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics, not abstract debate.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1 (Genç and adults)
- Locks: 3 (Genç) or 4 (adults), with 3-4 items each: picture, colour, number, fuse-box and simple word locks.
- Codes: one-step derivations and 3-character codes (picture wheels for A1 Genç).
- Text: prompts of 4 words or fewer (Genç) or 10 or fewer (adults). No reading note for Genç; a 25-40 word sign or poster for adults.
- Komut: LOOK/TAKE/OPEN/USE/READ with pictures; in/on/under; a 4-step chain.
- Time: 15-20 min.

A2
- Locks: 4-5. Gap-fill word locks with a tap bank, a map lock (turn left, go straight, next to, opposite, between), 40-60 word notes, a sort lock.
- Codes: 4 characters.
- Text caps: 8 words (Genç), 15 (adults).
- Komut: commands must include the article; adds next to, behind, in front of and between; a 6-step chain.
- Time: 20-25 min.

B1
- Locks: 5-6 in 2 parallel branches. An 80-120 word note (email, diary, timetable), an order lock, an error lock, a sound lock (-ed endings), odd-one-out by grammar, and a cipher in Arena.
- Codes: two-step derivations (answer, then letter, then reorder by the numbers on the cards).
- Komut: notes to read, an 8-step chain with multi-step logic, the typed parser, and Blind Guide unlocked.
- Hints: 3.
- Time: 25-35 min.

B2
- Locks: 6-7 in 2 branches. An inference riddle, a word-formation lock (family[]), an idiom lock, distractors that look close, and one red-herring card.
- Codes: 5 characters.
- Hints: 2 by default.
- Komut: the free parser accepts complex commands and relative clauses ('Put the painting back where it was', 'Use the key that was in the vase'); 8-10 steps.
- Time: 30-45 min.
- Caps: 20 words (Genç), 40 (adults).

INSIDE A GROUP
- The Kolay/Orta/Zor dial: Kolay pre-sets the first wheel and adds a word bank to every word lock. Zor adds the red herring and one extra lock.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' swaps in the lower level's lock types and word bands without changing the skin.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-45 plus a 3-5 min debrief: Oyun Parkı 15-25 (3 locks), Arena 20-35, Stüdyo 25-45 (5-7 locks); Komut Modu alone 10-30. The lesson-fit timer sizes the room from the minutes available: about 4 minutes per A1 lock up to about 7 per B2 lock, plus a 2-minute buffer.
catalog.teacherControls:
SETUP
- Mode (co-op / race / Komut / Tam Macera).
- Number of locks; linear or 2-branch order; a grammar target per lock.
- Paper, device or screen-only mode.
- Red herring on/off, the Kolay/Orta/Zor dial, and 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'.
- ÖNİZLEME: an auto play-through before class.

PRINTING
- Team packs as a PDF: one page per team, cut lines, jigsaw cards A-D, a QR on each card.
- The teacher answer sheet with every code and walkthrough.

DURING PLAY (from the laptop or the phone remote via QR)
- Timer: +1/-1 min, pause all (T), Süresiz, heartbeat and music on/off.
- Hints: hints per team (0-3 or free), hint cost, and 'give a hint to team X'.
- Locks: alarm and cooldown length on/off; 'unlock for team' force-open; restart one lock with reshuffled items; end early with the summary.
- Projector view: 'Oda' (the room) or 'İlerleme' (progress only, never answers). The GM panel blurs itself if it is dragged onto the projector.

KOMUT MODU
- The walkthrough panel with the next useful command.
- Pulse a hotspot glow as a hint.
- Accept or reject a command; accuracy gate on/off.
- Verb bar on/off; clicking or typing mode.
- Reset the room.

ALWAYS
- Reduced motion.
- A Turkish rule card to read aloud (Oyun Parkı), or an English rule card with a Turkish toggle (Arena).
- Autosave with 'Devam et' to resume in the next lesson from the same locks and clock.
- The class profile is saved locally (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena').
catalog.delightDetails:
LOCKS AND THE ROOM
- Lock wheels spin into place with one click per wheel and a solid thunk when the code is right.
- The room starts dim (for kids, grey like a colouring-book page) and lights up or fills with colour bit by bit as the locks open.
- The finale plays a creaking door with light spilling in.
- The final word is a pack word, and the class says it together.

OYUN PARKI
- Gogo repeats the code word like a parrot ('Cat! Cat!').
- He sleeps and snores softly on the pause screen, and waves hello and goodbye.
- A wrong code gives a sleepy lock with snowflakes and a yawn.
- Stickers stamp onto the team banner when a lock opens.
- Gogo's lost feather is the bonus object in every kids' room.

ARENA
- A 1.2 s glitch flash for ACCESS DENIED.
- The team's emblem glows on the progress strip when it opens a lock.
- 'CLUTCH!' when a lock opens in the last 60 seconds.
- A podium with stat awards.

STÜDYO
- Props that look real, with the team's name printed on the boarding pass.
- An ink stamp when a lock opens.
- A rubber duck hidden in the hotel bath.
- A printable certificate: 'Escaped with 04:12 left'.

KOMUT MODU
- A hand cursor that really acts: it lifts the rug and rattles a locked drawer.
- A running inventory bar.
- Objects with personalities in their refusals.
- A secret bonus object in every room.

EVERYWHERE
- Printed packs carry a 'GİZLİ / TOP SECRET' stamp, the team emblem and scissor icons on the cut lines.
- Countdown music speeds up in the last minute (Arena and Stüdyo, mutable), with an opt-in heartbeat.
- Sound packs: marimba for kids, synth blips for Arena, woodblock and piano for adults. Every effect is 1 s or shorter and loudness-normalised.
- Reduced motion swaps every effect for a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
- Brute-forcing codes. Mitigation: escalating per-lock cooldowns, no partial feedback, codes of 3-5 characters, and trivial codes (1111, 1234) blocked.
- Copying across teams in race mode. Mitigation: each team gets a reshuffled variant with different codes, plus a masked code kiosk.
- One student doing everything. Mitigation: jigsaw cards, the 'Keep your card - say it!' rule, and roles from the spinner.
- A bottleneck at one lock. Mitigation: parallel branches and the hint ladder.
- Early finishers. Mitigation: the Bonus Vault, Golden Lock or Sticker Chest, and 'Gift a hint'.
- Puzzles that are too hard or ambiguous. Mitigation: the ÖNİZLEME play-through, the blind-solve verifier, rejection of items whose accepted forms derive different code characters, and automatic 'yedek' swaps.
- LLM mistakes with codes. Mitigation: the LLM never makes a code.
- Heavy preparation. Mitigation: one click makes the room, the packs and the answer sheet.
- No printer. Mitigation: screen-only zoomable cards.
- Parser frustration. Mitigation: the verb bar, teacher-mediated input, and recasts.
- Only the Voice speaks. Mitigation: the huddle, rotation, and the kids' whole-class echo.
- Losing progress. Mitigation: autosave, unlike Genially.
- Kids upset when time runs out. Mitigation: Gogo's 3 extra minutes, then Süresiz.
- 12-13-year-olds finding it babyish. Mitigation: the Arena skin.
- Anxious groups. Mitigation: the heartbeat is off by default and never plays in Oyun Parkı.
- Colour-blind students. Mitigation: colours always come with a shape and a label.
- Noise during race mode. Mitigation: the Runner whispers or shows a mini-whiteboard.
- An offensive code word. Mitigation: a blocklist.
- No English TTS voice. Mitigation: 'Öğretmen okur'.
- Sticker-library art cost. Mitigation: keep it bounded at about 12 room backgrounds and about 150 objects.

issues: Real classroom hardware breaks the 'GM panel never on the projector' rule. In most Turkish state schools the smart board (EBA/Vestel panel) IS the computer. There is no separate teacher laptop, school Wi-Fi is often filtered or off-limits to phones, and student phones are restricted. So the phone remote, device mode and QR packs may all be unavailable, and the answer panel ends up on the only screen, which the whole class can see.

Device mode is effectively unavailable for the kids' class, so paper or screen-only become the real defaults. Screen-only zoomable cards destroy the jigsaw: when 6-7 teams read all the cards off one board, nobody holds private information, and the one student nearest the board dominates.

Paper setup is not 1 minute. Take 7 teams x 3 locks x 4 jigsaw cards plus envelopes and a teacher sheet. That means printing (often one shared school printer with toner limits), cutting about 80 cards and stuffing envelopes, which is 15-25 minutes of prep per room. Worse, when the next class asks to play again, the cards come back crumpled or missing.

The numbers don't fit 28 kids. The design says 3-6 teams of 3-5, but 28 kids need 6-7 teams of 4-5, while A1 Genç co-op has only 3 locks. 'Extra teams get copies of a lock or the Sticker Chest' leaves half the class on duplicate work or side content, and the master door then does not really depend on them.

The pacing text contradicts itself for kids. Co-op says each team owns one lock and works in parallel, while pacing says 'each lock is one round of about 4-5 minutes' with a stretch after lock 2, which is sequential. A teacher cannot tell from the rules whether the class works simultaneously or in turns.

Audio locks collide with parallel play. PICTURE locks, SOUND locks and Gogo reading every clue at 0.8x all need the single room speaker. With 6 teams working at once, only one team can hear its audio at a time, and the others either wait or talk over it.

The code kiosk becomes a bottleneck and a crowd. Six or seven kid Runners converge on one touch board. Queueing, jostling and teams watching each other's masked entries turn a Turkish classroom of 28 into chaos, and each entry also needs a team-select tap so that per-team cooldowns work.

The CHECK hint in paper mode, where a team reads its answers to the teacher's remote checklist, puts the teacher in a one-to-many service desk. With 6 teams asking within the same 2 minutes, the teacher is stuck at one table while others idle or get loud. Teacher cognitive load is far above what can be run while standing at the board: timer, hints per team, cooldowns, force-open, the Komut verb-bar clicks and accuracy-gate judgements.

In co-op the weakest team becomes the public bottleneck. The whole class waits at the master door for the one team that has not opened its lock, and 27 children know which team it is. 'Gift a hint' and force-open help, but the social pressure lands exactly on the students the design wants to protect.

Komut Modu has very low activity per student. It is one Voice per turn, a 4-10 step chain and 5 teams, so each team gets 1-2 turns in 10-15 minutes and each child speaks once at most. The kids' echo helps, but it is imitation, not production. Points also depend on luck: whichever team gets the turn when a useful command is available scores, and a team that says a correct but useless command gets nothing through no fault of its own.
Komut replayability is near zero. Once a class solves 'Gogo's Messy Bedroom', parallel classes in the same grade (6-A and 6-B share corridors and breaks) spoil it, and the room cannot be reused.

Race-mode fairness: in linear lock order a team that stalls on lock 1 is hopelessly behind for the rest of the session. The 2-branch order helps only from B1 up, and it is not the default for A1-A2 adults.

The kids' '3 rules' card hides a larger procedure. Seat-spinner roles, the Runner, the kiosk, cooldowns, 'keep your card' and the envelope order still add up to about 7 operational rules that the teacher must manage. Explaining it the first time takes 3-4 minutes, not 20 seconds.

Stopping at any moment is only half-solved. Autosave keeps the clock and the locks, but paper packs, half-written codes and roles walk out of the room at the bell. Next lesson's resume costs 5 minutes of redistribution, and absent students leave holes in the jigsaw.

Noise: 'Keep your card - say it!' across 7 teams, plus a speeding countdown and Runners at the board, creates a noise level that Turkish public-school teachers get told off for by neighbouring classes. There is no built-in noise brake.

Scope: three play modes, 14 lock kinds, a state-graph parser, blind guides, race variants, PDF jigsaw generation and a sticker library of about 150 objects make this XL+. The Komut parser alone is a second game, and the risk is that none of it reaches the polish the teacher expects.

Adult evening course (10 people): this mostly works. With 2-3 teams of 3-5, jigsaw talk is genuine and the masked kiosk is fine. But 25-45 minutes plus a debrief is most of a 90-minute evening, and adults who arrive late (common in evening courses) cannot join a jigsaw team mid-room.
fixes: Add a 'Tek ekran' hardware profile as a first-class mode. It is detected or chosen at setup: no phone remote and no student devices. A 'Öğretmen görünümü' key (hold, or a 2-finger tap in a corner) shows the answers for 3 seconds and then hides them. Codes are entered on a numeric pad whose keys shuffle, so onlookers cannot read them. Never assume a second screen.

Replace cut jigsaw cards with a no-cut 'Katlanır A4' pack: one A4 per team per lock, folded into 4 quadrants labelled A-D, and each seat reads only its own quadrant. Print once, reuse by laminating, and add a 'Sınıf seti' option that numbers the sheets so they can be collected and counted at the bell.

For kids, make co-op run in STATIONS rather than one-lock-per-team. Build 6-7 locks for 28 kids at A1 (short 2-item locks), or have teams rotate through 3 lock stations every 4 minutes on a board-driven signal. That way every team does real work that feeds the door, and the stated pacing contradiction disappears.

Schedule audio: audio locks become whole-class moments ('Gogo reads Lock 2 for EVERYONE now'), triggered by the teacher and played once for all teams. Never run parallel per-team audio on one speaker. The printed card shows a speaker icon and the text for 'Öğretmen okur' as a fallback.

Kill the Runner crowd. Kids hold up a mini-whiteboard or an A4 code card, and the teacher walks to the team and types the code (one tap selects the team via its mascot button), or the board calls teams to the kiosk in order. Cap it at one Runner at the board at any time, with a visible 'Sıra: Tilki' queue.

Replace teacher-mediated CHECK with a self-check. Each lock sheet has a scratch-off or fold-under strip showing the first letter of each answer, or the kiosk accepts a per-item check ('Item 3 = ?' gives a tick or a cross) at the cost of a hint token. The teacher stays free to roam.

Protect the slowest team in co-op. When one team is last, auto-offer Gogo's help after X minutes, and have the finished teams become 'Helpers' who walk over and give ONE spoken clue in English (a scored 'Gift a clue', not a free answer). Never show a 'waiting for Team X' banner, only the door filling up.

Tighten the kids' first run. Use a 90-second pictogram onboarding with an unscored practice lock the whole class does together, drop per-team cooldowns in favour of a single shared 'sleepy' animation, and hide roles beyond Eyes/Ears/Pencil until the second session.

Rework Komut scoring to be class-wide in Oyun Parkı (no per-team points; the class earns the stars), and in Arena/Stüdyo award points for an accurate command even when it is not useful. Add 'everyone whispers a command to your partner' before the Voice speaks, so each turn involves every student.

Give Komut replayability: randomise hotspot contents and chain order per session from a room template (the key may be in the vase OR under the rug), with 2-3 seeded variants per room, so parallel classes cannot spoil each other.

Make 2-branch lock order the default for race mode at every level, and add a 'catch-up' rule: a team 2+ locks behind gets a free nudge automatically. Show progress as doors opening, not a ranked list, until the end.

Add a noise brake: a 'Sessiz kod' toggle where the board shows a volume meter via the mic (optional), or a teacher hotkey that freezes the clock with a 'Shh... the lock is sleeping' screen until the class is quiet.

Make 'Bell mode' robust: one click on 'Zil çaldı' saves the state, prints or shows a 'where we are' slide, and at resume re-issues roles by seat number so absent students' quadrants are reassigned automatically.

Adults: offer a 15-20 minute 'Espresso room' (3 locks) for 90-minute evening lessons, and a 'late arrival' role (the Checker, who verifies codes before submission) so latecomers join without breaking a jigsaw.

Cut scope for v1. Ship Kilit Modu co-op and race with about 6 lock kinds (word, number, sort, order, fuse box, reading note) plus the paper and single-screen profiles. Move Komut Modu to its own later game (or merge it into an RPG/point-and-click candidate if one exists) and add Tam Macera only after both work.

issues: Too much of the thinking is puzzle logic, not language. First-letter codes, wheel-key cards (card D says which item feeds which wheel), B1 'answer, then letter, then reorder by the card numbers', ciphers and counting the box-A total all use class time on meta-reasoning. A team can get every English item right and still be stuck on the derivation. This is worst for 9-10-year-olds, who struggle with abstract mapping even in their first language.

A1 Genç learners who barely read cannot do 'Keep your card - say it!' in Kilit Modu. Reading gap sentences aloud to teammates assumes decoding skill they do not have yet. Picture cards with 0-4 words fix the reading load, but then the jigsaw has nothing to say aloud except single nouns, so the promised spoken negotiation does not happen.

Team talk will be in Turkish at every level below B2. The rule only makes students read the card text in English. Negotiating, agreeing and turning answers into a code will all happen in Turkish, so for most of a 25-minute Kilit room the English is receptive (reading and listening).

Kilit Modu fails the kids checklist item 'a whole-class response moment every turn'. In co-op each team works in parallel for 4-5 minutes per lock, and the whole-class echo happens only when a lock opens. The class can go several minutes with no shared moment. Komut Modu passes this item; Kilit Modu does not.

The '3 rules' for kids are really more. Roles (Eyes, Ears, Pencil, Feet), the Runner, the code kiosk, the wheel key, the cooldown and the Sticker Chest are all procedure the children must learn. It cannot be explained in 20 seconds unless most of it is removed for Oyun Parkı.

In prompt mode, word locks cannot be built reliably. The engine picks a real code word, then looks for items whose first letters spell it. With a teacher prompt that yields 12-15 topic items, the letters often will not fit. The fallback is a 'yedek' bank lock that is off-topic, so a 'Çanakkale' or 'my town' prompt ends up with foreign content in half the locks.

An LLM-authored Komut room is unrealistic. Asking DeepSeek to write a consistent object and state graph with relations, actions, accepts[] patterns and sticker keys from a free prompt will often fail the solvability search, or pass it with dull or illogical chains. Built-in categories also do not map onto rooms: a 'jobs' or 'present perfect' category has no natural room.

The B2 free parser ('Put the painting back where it was', 'Use the key that was in the vase') is a research-grade NLU problem. In class it will misfire, and a teacher override on every turn kills the pacing. The B1 typed parser has the same problem in a milder form.

The accuracy gate (article plus preposition) is right for A2 adults, but harsh for A2 Genç in front of the whole class. It also judges speech that the teacher then enters on the team's behalf, so its accuracy depends on how honest the teacher is.

The ERROR and SOUND locks are listed as B1+, but Arena gives B1 Genç learners ciphers, riddles and red herrings. That is extra puzzle difficulty that does not scale the language. The B2 Genç idiom lock and word-formation lock on abstract items risk the 'too abstract' failure the design itself rules out.

Sound locks rely on browser TTS for -ed endings and minimal pairs. Quality varies, the 'Öğretmen okur' fallback depends on the teacher's accuracy, and the same fallback is used for Gogo's 0.8x reading of every clue. With no English voice, a kids' room loses most of its support.

Too much to build and too much to learn at setup. There are 14 lock kinds, 3 modes, 3 skins, race variants, PDF packs, a kiosk, a phone remote, a parser and a sticker library. The teacher faces a heavy setup screen, and level tuning across 14 kinds x 8 groups will not be tested in real classes.

Komut Modu is really a separate game: a whole-class, turn-based imperatives and prepositions game (TPR). It is the strongest language-learning piece here, but it sits behind Kilit Modu as a sub-mode and overlaps with the RPG, Treasure Map and Kim Yaptı? candidates.

Adults: the core fits well. One gap is that A1 adults get a 25-40 word sign but mostly picture, colour and number locks, which can feel childish unless the props stay realistic (receipts, timetables).
fixes: Make the code derivation language-light and uniform. Each correct item fills its own wheel directly (the 'Adım adım' style as the default), and wheels show pictures or words, not letters. Keep first-letter codes and reorder steps only for Stüdyo B1+ and optional 'Zor'. Cut ciphers entirely, or add them only as the Golden Lock bonus.

Oyun Parkı Kilit Modu: remove the jigsaw 'read aloud' requirement at A1. Use listen-and-point cards instead: Gogo reads (TTS), and the child holding the matching picture card holds it up and says the word. Remove the Runner, the kiosk and the wheel key. The team taps the answer on the projector or on one device.

Add a whole-class beat every 60-90 s in Oyun Parkı Kilit Modu, with the clock paused. Gogo reads one item from the next lock, and the whole class shows or says the answer. Alternatively, run A1-A2 Genç Kilit Modu as a whole-class lock sequence (one lock at a time, teams take turns) rather than parallel team work.

Add a printed or on-screen 'Team Talk' phrase strip per level ('I think it's...', 'Card B says...', 'Is it A or B?', 'Let's try...'). Give a +1 star or +50 'English only' bonus that the teacher awards, so the negotiation moves into English.

Prompt mode: restrict LLM-built locks to kinds that do not depend on letters: number (MCQ order), sort, fuse box, order, reading note and odd one out. Use word locks only from built-in banks, or when the generated pack is big enough. Ask the LLM for 2x the needed gap/vocab items so the engine has letters to choose from.

Komut Modu: never let the LLM author the room graph. Ship 8-12 hand-authored room templates with a fixed state graph, and let content swap only through slots (the note text, the code, object labels, the reading item). Map built-in categories to recommended rooms, e.g. food to the Recipe Vault.

Drop the B2 free parser. At B1-B2 use the verb bar plus typed arguments with fuzzy matching, and make the teacher's accept/reject the source of truth. To add B2 challenge, require complex commands only as spoken bonus ('say it with a relative clause'), judged by the teacher.
Make the accuracy gate off by default for Genç. In Oyun Parkı replace it with a whole-class recast echo that never blocks the turn.
Split Komut Modu out as its own suite game (e.g. 'Tıkla-Keşfet: Say it, Hand!'), keeping the shared room and lock engine. Keep Kilit Modu as the escape room. 'Tam Macera' stays as a combined option.
Cut v1 scope to about 6 lock kinds: picture, number (MCQ), fuse box (tf), sort, order and reading note, plus word from banks. Add sound, error, riddle, map and colour later, after classroom testing.

For B1-B2 Genç, raise difficulty through language (longer notes, error locks, inference questions on concrete MEB topics), not through ciphers and red herrings. Replace the B2 Genç idiom lock with concrete phrasal verbs.
Detect whether an English TTS voice exists at setup. If there is none, warn the teacher and turn off sound locks and Gogo's reading for kids' rooms, or offer pre-generated audio for bank items.
A1 adults: keep realistic props (a hotel receipt, a boarding pass, a timetable) even for number and colour locks, and never use picture wheels in Stüdyo.
Add a 'language minutes' check to ÖNİZLEME. It reports the share of steps that need an English answer against steps that are pure derivation, and warns when derivation dominates.

issues: Scope is really two or three games. Kilit Modu is a Breakout EDU engine. Komut Modu is a point-and-click adventure with a parser, a state graph, hotspots, an inventory and an animated hand. Tam Macera glues them together. Each could be its own XL build, and together they are the riskiest candidate in the suite. Komut Modu also overlaps the RPG, Crossroads and Treasure Map candidates, which share story nodes and command-driven exploration.

There are 14 lock kinds (word, number, sort, order, fuse, map, colour, picture, odd, reading, error, sound, riddle, cipher). Each one needs its own derivation code, projector UI, device UI, print layout, hint ladder and debrief view. That is about 14 x 5 surfaces. Polish will be spread thin, and a few will ship half-finished.

The word-lock derivation runs backwards for prompt mode. 'Pick a real level word first, then choose items that fit it' works with words.js. With LLM content, the engine cannot force the answers to start with the right letters, so prompt-mode word locks will often fall back to 'yedek' bank locks. That undercuts the promise that the teacher's own prompt drives the content.

LLM-generated Komut rooms are not realistic. Objects, relations, action maps, responses, a solvable chain and sticker keys that must all exist in a bounded library make up a deeply nested schema. DeepSeek will often produce chains that are unsolvable or trivially short, or that use a sticker that doesn't exist. The state-graph validator will catch this, but the regenerate rate will be high, and a slow second LLM call costs money and hits the rate limit.

The art cost is understated. About 12 backgrounds and about 150 objects, in three audience skins (cream/rounded, neon/geometric, editorial noir), plus a hand cursor with open, lift and rattle animations, plus Gogo the mascot with demo, sleep, point and wave states. Room lighting that fills in bit by bit needs layered or greyscale versions of every scene. This is the biggest polish risk. Mismatched or clip-art stickers will make it feel like a generic Genially.

The live channels (device mode via QR with no login, the phone remote, race-mode progress doors) need real-time sync between devices, probably Supabase Realtime plus anonymous sessions. That brings in backend work, reconnect handling, and classroom wifi and school firewalls. Autosave with 'Devam et' across lessons across devices adds more state-sync risk.

Print packs need a PDF with cut lines, QR codes, 4-card jigsaw splits, per-team race variants and a teacher answer sheet. Client-side PDF generation (jsPDF plus QR) with Turkish glyphs and emoji or pictures is fiddly. Emoji do not render reliably in PDFs.

The 'CHECK' hint in paper mode (a team reads its answers to the teacher's remote checklist) and the Runner, code kiosk and masked entry flow put a lot of load on the teacher during a noisy race. The teacher becomes the bottleneck the design tries to avoid.

Kids fit. Cutting and handling 4-card jigsaw paper packs with 9-year-olds costs 5+ minutes of logistics. In co-op, 'each team owns one lock' means a slow team holds up the class ending. 'No partial feedback' on wrong codes frustrates young learners until Gogo steps in on the 2nd try. A 20-second rule explanation hides a lot of process: roles, cards, the kiosk and the runner.

On smartboards and touch screens, spinning code wheels by dragging is unreliable. Wheels need big tap arrows. Masked kiosk entry on a shared touch board visible to the whole class is not really masked.
