Build the kids' picture options as parametric SVG, not art assets. Use about 25 simple objects (ball, cat, box, hat, apple...) x 8 colours x size x 5 prepositions (on/under/in/next to/behind), plus 1-2 characters. The engine composes the target and three one-attribute distractors, so any 'a big red ball'-type seed renders automatically. Restrict A1T seeds to this grammar (det + adj + noun [+ prep + noun]) so content always renders.

Validate all generated content deterministically. Count words to the level cap. Check every token against the words.js band for the level. Check the target structure with a regex or lemma (a past form, 3rd person -s, a number). Planted traps must come from a curated list of minimal pairs, numbers and names in the sound bank, not from the LLM. Balance rows by length (±1 word) and by trap count. Turn Turkish free-text prompts into a topic, then generate seeds from the bank or the LLM.
Drop the microphone noise meter. Replace it with a teacher-tapped 'Sessizlik bonusu' (quiet bonus) star per row, or a purely decorative animated 'whisper level' mascot with no mic.

Add whole-class moments every round, not just at the end. Before the reveal, the class votes on 'Which row kept it best?' with a show of hands. During the reveal, the class guesses the lost word before it drops back in. Then the class does a choral repeat of the original, with TTS at slow and then normal speed. Rotate row order each round so a different student is last and a different one starts.

For adults, rename and reframe it as a 'Dikkat: Tuzak!' (Watch out: trap!) listening warmer. Default to 'fold and pass' written relay or a cupped-hand whisper. Put the teaching value in the reveal: each drift links to its sound item (thirteen/thirty stress, minimal pair) with TTS contrast and a mouth tip, and misses feed Kaçırılanlar. Keep dictogloss as the substantial adult mode and score it by idea units with a teacher tap per unit (got/partly/missed), not auto-grading.

Polish the reveal as the showpiece. Word chips flow along a drawn 'row path' with a sound per hop. Lost words fall and fade, replacements slide in with a wobble, and at the end the original and the drifted version play back to back (TTS). Offer a skin per audience: balloons and Gogo (Oyun Parkı), a signal waveform with glitch letters (Arena), and a calm typographic diff (Stüdyo).

Keep the kids ruleset to the 3 pictogram rules. No scores in Oyun Parkı, only stickers (one for trying, one for a match). Use a 'Say again' token as a visible, usable object per row. Add a 'relay card' fallback (write and fold) for students who don't want whispering, and for hearing-impaired students.

Put the build estimate at M only for Mode A plus C. The core pieces are an LCS word aligner with normalisation (contractions, digit and number words, case, punctuation), the seed generator and validator, the parametric picture composer, the reveal animation, a printable PDF, the Kumanda seed view and TTS playback. Assets: about 25 SVG objects, one mascot, and 6-8 SFX (whoosh, pop, chime, drop, parachute, fanfare). No external engines.

catalog.rankReason: Whisper chain: fun, but each student gets little language, it is three games in one, and the screen matters only at the reveal (6.0). Keep Fısıltı Zinciri as a small later stirrer with a tap-to-toggle reveal. Its dictogloss mode moves to c32.

catalog.name: Hazine Yolu (Race Board: Ask-Tell Ladders & Treasure Map)
catalog.familiarAs: Snakes and Ladders (Yılan Merdiven) / pirate treasure-hunt board / Mario Party
catalog.oneLiner: Teams race along a ladder board or a treasure map where every square is a Quiz, Ask or Tell task. Correct answers climb ladders, charm snakes and pay for risky shortcuts. Children get Gogo's jungle ladders with stars; 12-14s and adults get a real route map with forks, events, gold and a final wager.
catalog.howItPlays:
SETUP (60-90 s)
1. The teacher picks the group chip, a topic (built-in category or a free-text prompt, Turkish is fine, for the LLM) and the lesson length. The lesson-fit timer sizes the board from that. The setup screen shows one summary line, e.g. 'A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk · 30 kare', with a 'Değiştir' link.
2. Teams: 2-6, with 4 recommended. Teams set themselves up by skin. Oyun Parkı: each team taps an animal token. Arena: in 10 s each team picks an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto. Stüdyo: teams get city, coffee or grammar-pun names.
3. Optional BUILD YOUR BOARD (2 min, ring timer; on by default for kids). Each team places one ladder and one snake by saying it in English: 'From seven to eighteen!' The class repeats the numbers and the piece snaps in with a click. The engine enforces the limits: a ladder is at most 10 squares, a snake at most 5 (Nazik) or 8, no snake head in the first 3 or last 2 squares, no overlaps, and no snake head on a ladder base. The team's emblem appears on the ladder it built. In Arena this becomes 'Rig the map': one zip-line and one quicksand, placed on marked slots only.
4. Oyun Parkı only: Gogo the parrot plays a 25 s practice turn that does not score. He rolls, hops, gets one question wrong (boing), tries again, and charms a snake.

ONE ENGINE, TWO BOARD SHAPES (both built by code from pack items; the LLM never draws the board)
- LADDER BOARD (default for Oyun Parkı, optional for the others): a serpentine 20 (4x5), 30 (5x6) or 50 squares. Every square has a colour AND a pictogram: QUIZ blue ❓, ASK orange 💬, TELL green 🗣, EVENT purple ⭐, or plain. A 30-square board has 4 ladders and 4 snakes.
- MAP BOARD (default for Arena and Stüdyo): a route graph of 30-45 squares in 3-4 regions. Each region is one category (a topic or a grammar target), and the trailing team picks the next region's category. At a FORK the team chooses the safe road (longer, mixed squares) or the shortcut (about 40% shorter, but every square is a difficulty-3 item). Ladders become zip-lines or express trains; snakes become quicksand or missed connections. A CHECKPOINT flag stands at each region start, and nothing ever sends a team behind its last checkpoint. Fog of war clears as teams explore.

A TURN (about 45-75 s)
1. MOVE. There are three modes and the teacher can switch at any time.
   - ZAR (die). The default in Oyun Parkı. A student taps the big die, or the teacher presses Space. Kids use a 1-2-3 die (faces 1,1,2,2,3,3) so the board lasts longer and more squares get played. The token hops one square at a time while Gogo and the whole class count aloud in English.
   - HAMLE (stake). The default in Arena and Stüdyo. In a huddle (10/15/20 s) the team calls Step 1, 2 or 3, which means an easy, medium or hard question. Correct moves that many squares; wrong means the team stays. Agency beats luck.
   - KARMA. Roll the die to move, then call a stake for gold (easy 2 / medium 4 / hard 6).
2. TASK. In Zar mode the landing square sets the task; in Hamle mode the stake question is the task and the landing square adds its effect.
   - QUIZ: an mcq, gap, tf, odd, riddle, order, sound or vocab item. The question appears first and the options follow after the options delay; then the huddle; the seat-number spinner picks the speaker. Kids: the whole class shows A-D cards or does TPR, and the active team's card counts. Arena: mini-whiteboards.
   - ASK: the active team's speaker asks another team a question built from the card. At A1 the card shows '🍕 you / like?' and the speaker says 'Do you like pizza?'. The target team is tapped; teams already asked this round are greyed out, so every team gets asked. The other team's speaker answers in a full sentence. The teacher judges with quick chips: Question form ✓, Full answer ✓, Follow-up ✓ (B1+). Both teams can score: the asker earns 1 for a correct question, the answerer 1 for a full answer. Whole-class moment: kids raise hands for 'Me too!' and the class counts them aloud ('Twelve!'); Arena students show thumbs up or down.
   - TELL: the speaker talks for the level's time about the card, which shows a picture, up to 3 starters and up to 5 useful words, while the calm ring timer runs. The class listens for a target word or structure and taps the desk or stands when they hear it. The teacher judges with chips: Kept going ✓, Used the target ✓.
   - EVENT: a chance card from the allowed harshness pool, or a map event (see below).
3. LADDER BASE (vine / zip-line / express train). The team gets one ladder question at difficulty +1. Correct climbs, with rising notes. Wrong stays put; nobody ever falls from a ladder.
4. SNAKE HEAD (friendly snake / quicksand / missed connection). 'Snake charmer' rule: one correct answer puts the snake to sleep (Zzz) and the team stays. A wrong answer slides the team down. Under Nazik a slide is at most 5 squares and never passes a checkpoint. Stars, gold and miles are never lost to a slide.
5. SCORE. Kids earn stars (1-3 per task). Arena earns gold: the item value times the combo (x1.5 at 3 correct in a row, x2 at 5, based on accuracy only), with a floor at 0. Stüdyo earns miles.
6. WRONG ANSWER, by audience.
   - Kids: a soft boing and a second try with a free hint. If it is still wrong, Gogo says the answer, the class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star for the class album.
   - Arena: the streak breaks, and one other team may steal by being first with its whiteboard up. The stealer gets the gold and the first team loses nothing.
   - Stüdyo: the correct answer and a one-line 'why' (from whyTr/whyEn), with optional minus miles.

MAP EVENTS (Arena and Stüdyo; event density Low, Medium or High)
- Treasure chest: pick 1 of 3 closed chests. There is always a reward: gold or an item.
- Mystery chest: for Genç groups it is never empty (1-8 gold plus a funny find, e.g. 'a sock'). For adults it can be empty ('Just a rubber duck.').
- Storm: answer a bonus question to sail through with +2. Otherwise the team is 'anchored' and its next move is at most 1 square. Nobody ever misses a turn.
- Kraken surge (Arena) / Rush hour (Stüdyo): ALL teams answer on mini-whiteboards, and every correct crew rides the wave 1 square forward. 'Wrong crews go back 2' exists only as a Yellow or Red opt-in.
- Golden hour: the next correct answer is doubled.
- Shop (Supply drop in Arena, Duty free in Stüdyo). Teams spend gold: Radar 3 (reveal the next 3 squares and the next category), Scanner 4 (one 50:50), Rope 5 (ride the next zip-line without a question), Shield 6 (ignore the next quicksand).
- Dig site: a 5x5 grid (A-E, 1-5) opens over the island. The speaker calls a coordinate in English ('C four!'), then spells a word or answers a vocab item. Correct means dig: 3-10 gold, a Golden Key (skip one snake), or 'Just sand!' with a waving crab. Genç groups always get at least 1 gold.
- Fork call: at a fork the team announces its route with a frame ('We'll take the shortcut because...') and earns +1 for a complete sentence.

ENDGAME
- Oyun Parkı: no exact roll is needed; overshooting lands on the chest. The first team to arrive opens the treasure chest (sticker burst). Then comes GOGO'S RESCUE ROPE: every other team answers one whole-class question and gets pulled into the chest, one team at a time. Every team receives a title, and the class album gets a sticker.
- Arena and Stüdyo: the final square needs a GATE or CUSTOMS question at difficulty 3 of the group's level. The first arrival earns +10 and triggers LAST CALL: every other team gets one more turn, and any team that arrives during it earns +5. Stüdyo then plays the Duty-free wager: each team bets up to half its miles on one final question. The highest gold or miles total wins. Ties go to most tasks correct, then to the team closest to the X.
- Lesson-fit safety: when 4 minutes remain, 'Final stretch' starts automatically (Rescue Rope for kids, Last Call for the others), so the game always ends before the bell.

TEACHER DURING PLAY
- A floating 'Hata not' button (key E) logs errors heard during Ask and Tell. The teacher types a note or taps a chip such as 'did + V2' or 'missing -s'. At the end, a 'Let's fix these' slide shows the errors anonymously.
- Keys: Space roll, 1-4 answer, Y/N judge, U undo, T pause, +/- 10 s.
- The teacher can drag tokens, set the die, give stars or gold, and skip an item.
catalog.playerSetup: 2-6 teams on one shared screen, 4 recommended; kids max 4 unless 'Everybody' squares are set to High. Teams have 3-6 students, so it fits classes of 12-36. Inside a team, the seat-number spinner picks a new speaker for every task, and nobody is ever picked by name. Ask squares pair the active team with a second team, so two teams speak every turn. The whole class responds every turn: A-D cards, TPR, survey hands, counting the hops, or listening for the Tell target. Stüdyo adds pair consultation before the rotating spokesperson answers.
catalog.contentShape:
One pack serves every square. Every item carries base fields plus diff 1/2/3, topic and a teenSafe flag.
- quiz: mcq, gap, tf, odd, riddle, order, sound and vocab items. Built-in quiz content comes from the grammar_mcq_* banks (including whyOpt) and from words.js (defEasy, emoji, IPA and TR gloss). A ladder or snake question is a quiz item at diff+1.
- ask: speaking-prompt items with mode 'ask'. Fields: prompt (the question cue, e.g. 'where / go / last weekend?'), starters[] (answer frames), followUps[] (B1+), useful[] and target, e.g. 'fn:past-questions'.
- tell: speaking-prompt items with mode talk, describe, story or opinion. Fields: secs set from the level, media.emoji (required for A1/A2 Genç), up to 3 starters, up to 5 useful words, and target. Taboo-card items with mode 'describe' can also be used as Tell cards.
- Border control squares (Stüdyo B1-B2): roleplay cards.
- Kraken or 'Everybody' squares: category-list items, e.g. 'Name 3 fruits', or easy mcq.
- dig: vocab items with the hangman field true (spellable).
- boss/gate: qa items at diff 3 (teacherJudge allowed at B2) or error items.
- events: chance-card items. Code builds them from templates tagged Green, Yellow or Red, and clamps every amount. The LLM only writes flavour lines (with textTr for A1 Genç), capped by the level's text limit.
Counts for a typical 25-minute, 4-team game: about 40 quiz items (roughly 40% diff 1, 35% diff 2, 25% diff 3), 12 ask cards, 12 tell cards, 10 ladder/snake items, 3 boss items, 6 dig words, 8 Everybody items and 16 events. No item repeats within a game, and unused items feed a reroll and the review list.
Board frame (pack.frames.board, computed by code): template ('ladder20'|'ladder30'|'ladder50'|'map-S'|'map-M'|'map-L'); squares[{id, kind ('start'|'quiz'|'ask'|'tell'|'event'|'ladder'|'snake'|'fork'|'shortcut'|'checkpoint'|'chest'|'mystery'|'storm'|'kraken'|'shop'|'dig'|'finish'), next[], to?, region?, x, y}]; regions[{name, categoryId}]; skin.
The LLM path: the teacher's prompt, plus the merged AudienceProfile (text caps, word bands, grammar whitelist, teenSafe), goes to the generator. The validator drops items over the word cap. For A1/A2 Genç it also drops items without an imageKey from picture squares. Ask and Tell cards for Genç groups must avoid adult domains.
catalog.adultVersion:
STÜDYO 'Grand Tour' (Dünya Turu), for adults A1-B2.
- Look and sound: an editorial vintage travel-poster map on cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme, in a system sans. No mascot and no voice lines. A neutral caption reads 'Leg 2 · Istanbul · Food & restaurants'. Woodblock and piano sounds; music is off.
- Regions: 3-4 city regions, each one category, e.g. London · Small talk, Istanbul · Food, New York · Work, Tokyo · Past simple. Built-in adult categories cover life and work tasks: travel, hotels, restaurants, job interviews, complaints, small talk, health, shopping and renting a flat.
- Board pieces: ladders are Express trains or Direct flights. Snakes are Missed connections, Strikes or Lost luggage. At a snake the charmer becomes 'Talk your way out': a 30 s line to the gate agent (a speaking prompt), or a quiz item if the teacher prefers.
- Rules: movement is Hamle (stake), so skill drives the race. Ask cards cover life, work and opinions, and from B1 the asker must add one follow-up. Tell lasts 40-60 s. Border control squares (B1-B2) are a 60 s information-gap role-play between two teams: one team is the officer, the other the traveller, and the teacher judges from a checklist.
- Events, shop and harshness: Duty free is the shop. Rush hour is the everybody event. Mystery chests can be empty. Yellow events are on by default (Steal 5 miles from a team you tap, capped at that team's score; Swap turn order). Red is opt-in: Swap scores, Reset, and 'Jet lag', which doubles the cost of the next wrong answer.
- Scoring: miles with optional negatives, set by the teacher. Hints cost miles: definition, then example, then Turkish gloss, and the gloss can be switched off for immersion classes. Comeback is Light: the last team gets +1 Slipstream on each correct answer and picks the next city's category.
- Endgame: the Customs question guards the finish, followed by Last Call and the Duty-free wager.
- End screen: the full scoreboard with each team's PASSPORT, stamped with every city it visited. 'Kaçırılanlar' appears as postcards home (each missed item with the right answer and why). Then the 'Let's fix these' slide of logged errors.
- Pacing and extras: rounds (legs) of 8-12 min, 20-40 min in total. Build-your-board is off to save time. An alternative adult-only board, 'Career Ladder' (promotions as ladders, 'Monday morning' and 'missed deadline' as snakes), is never offered to Genç groups.
catalog.teenVersion:
Two stripped rule packs, not one re-coloured.

(A) OYUN PARKI 9-11: 'Gogo's Jungle Ladders' (Orman Merdiveni)
- Look and host: cream background with warm jungle colours, rounded shapes and an Andika-type font. The board is a 20-square (A1) or 30-square serpentine. Ladders are vines. Snakes are friendly, smiling slides in sunglasses: a team slides down with a 'wheee!' and lands on a soft leaf. Tokens are animals with English names (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin, bear). Gogo the parrot hosts. He repeats the correct answer (a parrot, so it models choral repetition), counts the hops, and sleeps on the pause screen.
- THREE RULES, on a Turkish rule card with pictograms that can be read in 20 s:
  1. 🎲 Tap the die and hop.
  2. ❓💬🗣 Do the square's job together to earn a star ⭐.
  3. 🌿 Answer to climb the vine. 🐍 Answer to make the snake sleep, or slide, wheee!
- Every turn has a whole-class moment:
  - Hops: everyone counts aloud.
  - Quiz: A-D cards or TPR (stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C).
  - Ask: 'Me too!' hands, counted aloud.
  - Tell: stand up when you hear the target word.
  - Events: the whole class does the Brain break, e.g. 'Jump like a frog!'.
- Pictures and pace: every item has a picture and automatic read-aloud at 0.8x. The timer is off by default; when on, it runs 40 s with a calm ring that never turns red and a marimba chime. Hints are free: picture, then first letter, then listen again.
- Safety rules:
  - Stars never go down, and a slide never costs stars.
  - Snakes are at most 5 squares long.
  - Events are Green only: Gift a star to a team you tap, Everyone hops 1, Double stars, Shield ('the snake is asleep'), Brain break.
  - Nobody misses a turn.
  - No exact roll is needed at the finish.
- Build-your-board is on, and teams practise numbers while placing their pieces.
- Ending: the first team opens the treasure chest, then Gogo's Rescue Rope pulls every other team in. Every team gets a title (Fastest Explorers, Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Climbers, Star Collectors), and the class album gets a sticker. Confetti in team colours AND shapes plays only at the finale.
- Timing: fixed at 20 min, in rounds of 3-5 min with a 45 s stirrer ('Gogo says: touch something green!') or a 60 s settler (trace the word in the air).
- Kids checklist: at most 3 rules ✓; explainable in 20 s with pictograms ✓; no elimination ✓; no score below zero ✓; a whole-class response every turn ✓; non-violent failure imagery (a playground slide, a sleeping snake) ✓.

(B) ARENA 12-14: 'Treasure Map Challenge' (Harita Yarışı)
- Look: a dark navy night-expedition map with neon route lines in team colours, a condensed display font and geometric emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond). Each crew leaves a glowing trail showing the route it took. No cartoon animals, no talking mascot, no pastel colours.
- Rules: Hamle stake movement (the die can be switched on). Forks with red-dashed shortcuts, zip-lines, quicksand, fog of war, Kraken surge, Supply drop and the Dig site. Gold scoring with a combo meter on the team flag, floored at 0. Wrong answers can be stolen, and the answering team loses nothing. A commentator strip appears at most once per turn ('SHORTCUT TAKEN', 'COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!'). Yellow events (steal gold capped at the target's score; swap turn order) run only if the teacher opts in.
- Nazik underneath: checkpoints, no push-back by default, no individual naming.
- Ending: a Gate question at the finish, then Last Call. The finale shows a podium for the top 3 plus a stat award for every other crew (Longest streak, Boldest route, Map explorer, Comeback, Clean sheet). There is never a 'last place'.
- Suggested automatically for grade 6+: a 13-year-old A1 class gets A1 content with full pictures and audio on the dark map.

Content for both: the teenSafe filter applies. Pirates carry no rum, weapons or skull flags. Chests are 'finds', never gambling, and the mystery chest is never empty. No adult domains. Topics follow YLE and MEB units (animals, food, school, my day, clothes, sports, weather, holidays, places in town), each with pictures.
catalog.levelTuning:
A1
- Board: 20 squares for kids, map-S for others. Die: 1-2-3.
- Quiz: picture MCQ from vocab with emoji, picture true/false, picture odd-one-out, and a sound item (hear and choose).
- Ask: fixed frames from a picture cue ('Do you like...?', 'Have you got...?', 'Can you...?'); answers like 'Yes, I do. / No, I can't.' plus one word.
- Tell: 'Say 3 things' with starters (It's..., I like..., I have...). Genç 20 s, adults 30 s; adult cards are functional, e.g. 'Check in at the hotel'.
- Hamle tiers: 1 = choose the picture, 2 = spell with letter tiles, 3 = hear and choose without the picture. At A1, hard is still a picture or audio item.
- Prompt caps: A1 Genç 0-4 words (the picture carries the meaning), A1 adults 10.

A2
- Board: 30 squares for kids, map-M for others.
- Quiz: gap with a tap bank (past simple irregulars, comparatives, 'going to'), order (chunked unjumble) and riddles with 3 clues.
- Ask: Wh- questions in the past, built from cues ('Where / go / last weekend?'); the answer must be a full sentence.
- Tell: sequencing starters (First..., Then..., After that...). Genç 25 s, adults 40 s.
- Snake charmer: tap or type.
- Prompt caps: 8 words (Genç) / 15 (adults).

B1
- Board: map-M with 2 forks. Shortcut squares are open qa items.
- Quiz: context MCQ (messages, posters), error items (tap the error, then choose the fix) and typed gaps with alsoOk.
- Ask: must include one follow-up question (+1).
- Tell: a structure target (used to, present perfect, first conditional) that the class listens for. Genç 30 s, adults 50 s.
- Prompt caps: 14 words (Genç) / 25 (adults).

B2
- Board: map-L with 3 forks.
- Quiz: open qa that the teacher judges, word-family transforms, error items with whyEn, and idioms with their literal Turkish meaning.
- Ask: opinion prompts; the answer must justify a view and concede a point ('I see your point, but...').
- Tell: adults 60 s opinion or a JAM-style talk where other teams may challenge hesitation. Genç 40 s, with richer language on concrete topics ('the best school trip ever'), not abstract debate.
- Boss: a diff-3 open answer. Stüdyo adds the Border control role-play.
- Prompt caps: 20 words (Genç) / 40 (adults).

Across all levels
- Difficulty tiers are relative to the level: at A1 a hard item is still a picture item, and at B2 an easy item is already an open answer.
- The Kolay / Orta / Zor dial shifts the word-band mix (A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words) and hint availability without changing the skin.
- 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops the whole pack one level.
catalog.sessionMinutes: 15-40 (Oyun Parkı fixed 15-25; Arena 20-30; Stüdyo 20-40; the lesson-fit timer sizes the board and forces the Final stretch 4 minutes before the end)
catalog.teacherControls:
- Board: template (ladder 20/30/50, map S/M/L), movement mode (Zar / Hamle / Karma), die (1-3 or 1-6).
- Task mix % (Quiz / Ask / Tell / Event sliders) and speaking times per level.
- Snake charmer rule on/off, maximum slide length, and checkpoints on/off.
- Build-your-board on/off with its time limit.
- Finish rule: overshoot OK / exact roll / Gate question.
- Event density (Low/Medium/High), Harshness (Green/Yellow/Red, clamped by audience), Comeback (Off/Light/Strong: Tailwind +1/+2 and the trailing team picks the category), and shop on/off with prices.
- Timer (Süresiz / 30 / 40 s, +10 s, T pause), huddle length, options delay, hint ladder, TR gloss on/off, and minus points on/off (Stüdyo only).
- 'Everybody' square frequency, and Ask target fairness (every team gets asked once per round).
- 'Hata not' error notepad (key E) and the 'Let's fix these' slide.
- Teacher judging with ✓/✗ and rubric chips on open answers; skip or replace an item.
- Pacing: drag a token manually, set the die for pacing, give stars, gold or miles (taking never goes below 0), and multi-step Undo (U).
- 'Öğretmen okur' when no English voice is available.
- Region categories: pick them or let the trailing team pick.
- Class profile saved locally, e.g. '6-B · A1 Genç · Arena'.
- Printouts: board or map poster, A-D answer cards, and team tokens for a paper fallback.
catalog.delightDetails:
- Moving: the token hops square by square with rising xylophone notes (kids) or soft blips while the whole class counts aloud, and Gogo counts along. A ladder climb plays a rising scale, and vine leaves rustle in the kids' skin.
- Snakes: a slide plays a 'wheee!' down a playground-style snake for kids and a soft trombone 'wah-wah' (under 1 s) for adults. A charmed snake yawns, puts on its sunglasses and falls asleep with a floating Zzz, and the token walks over it.
- Build-your-board: pieces snap in with a satisfying click, and the building team's emblem is carved into its own ladder.
- Stars and gold: stars pop out of a finished task and fly to the team token. On the map, a gold counter on the team flag rolls up and coins rain briefly into the crew's chest.
- Map events: fog of war peels away like old paper as crews explore. The Kraken surge shows a neon tentacle silhouette and a wave that lifts the right crews forward. At the Dig site sand sprays out; a miss shows a crab waving a tiny 'Just sand!' sign, and a find shows a shaking chest that bursts open.
- Arena: each crew leaves a neon trail showing its route (the finale replays every crew's route), and the finish is a slow-motion 'photo finish'.
- Stüdyo: categories appear on a Solari departure-board flip, and cards look like boarding passes. Each team's passport fills with city stamps, and 'Kaçırılanlar' arrive as postcards.
- Gogo: he sleeps on the pause screen, flaps to the answer after a miss, and waves every team goodbye at the chest.
- Accessibility: every square type and team uses colour AND shape, and reduced motion swaps every effect for a static stamp.
catalog.risks:
1. Luck can frustrate. Hamle stake movement, stars or tasks as the tiebreak, the Tailwind, checkpoints and 5-square Nazik slides limit it, and the finale always carries a 'Most stars' or 'Clean sheet' title.
2. Ask and Tell cannot be auto-checked. The teacher judges with ✓ and one-tap rubric chips, and the Ask card's model answer is shown only on the teacher's side.
3. Turns get long with 5-6 teams. The recommended maximum is 4. Everybody or Kraken squares and the whole-class moment keep the other teams busy, and the lesson-fit timer forces the Final stretch.
4. Overlap with c02 (the Monopoly-style property board). Keep this game a race or adventure with no property economy, but share the board engine (tokens, dice, events, Undo) to cut build cost.
5. The speaking prompt banks for kids and teens have to be curated by age and topic. Otherwise LLM Ask and Tell cards drift into abstract or adult domains; the validator applies teenSafe and the text caps.
6. A 50-square board or a large map is hard to read on a projector. The camera follows the active token and zooms, and pictograms stay at least 6vh.
7. Pirate themes carry alcohol, weapon and gambling baggage. teenSafe art rules forbid them, and mystery chests are never empty for Genç groups.
8. Build-your-board can eat time. It is limited to 2 minutes, with preset positions as a fallback.
9. The Dig site and the shop add complexity. They are off in Oyun Parkı and adjustable through event density.
reviewVerdicts: logistics: keep-with-changes -> c02 (shared board engine); consider moving the map/expedition mode into the RPG candidate
feasibility: keep-with-changes -> c02 (share the board engine only: tokens, die, events, Undo, camera, teacher dock). Move the Dig site to any Battleship/grid candidate.

reviews.mergeWith: c02 (shared board engine); consider moving the map/expedition mode into the RPG candidate
issues: The board-size maths does not work. Four teams with 45-75 s turns give 3-5 min per round, so in 20 min each team gets about 4-6 turns. The 1-2-3 die averages 2, and ladder, snake and charmer questions add time on top. A 20-square board then needs 7-9 turns to finish, and a 30-square board for A2 kids needs 10 or more. In practice no team reaches the chest before the Final stretch starts, and the 'race' becomes a Rescue Rope ceremony every time. The lesson-fit timer 'sizes the board', but the spec never shows the turns-per-team calculation.

Turns are really 90-150 s, not 45-75 s, with 28 kids. A child walks to the board and taps the die, the class counts the hops, the landing task runs with its huddle and spinner, then a ladder or snake square adds a second question. On a wrong answer the kids variant adds a second try with a hint, then Gogo gives the answer, then the class repeats it twice. One unlucky turn can therefore hold three questions plus choral repetition, while three teams (about 21 children) mostly watch.

The 'whole-class moment' on quiz squares is hollow: only the active team's A-D card counts. Ten-year-olds quickly learn that raising a card on other turns earns nothing, and they stop doing it. That is the biggest source of dead time and noise.

TPR answers (stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C) and 'stand up when you hear the target word' in a crowded Turkish classroom lead to copying, chair noise and a 60-90 s settle-down each time. The teacher also cannot read 28 bodies accurately to decide whether the active team was right.

The hotkeys (Space, 1-4, Y/N, U, E, T) assume a laptop within reach. A teacher standing at a smart board has no keyboard, and many Turkish classrooms have the PC at the side desk. Every judge, undo or error note becomes a walk or a hunt for small UI.

Build-your-board with 4 kid teams, spoken numbers and board limits (no snake head in the first 3 squares, no overlaps, no head on a ladder base) will lead to rejected placements, arguments and some deliberately 'evil' snake spots. Realistically it takes 4-5 min, 20-25% of a fixed 20-min game, before a single content item is played.

Teacher cognitive load is too high in Arena and Stüdyo. There are 2 board shapes, 3 movement modes (Karma is confusing), forks, fog, regions chosen by the trailing team, shop prices, dig site, storms, Kraken, golden hour, steals, combo, checkpoints, the Hata not log and rubric chips. While standing at the board the teacher runs rules, not language. The Teacher controls list has more than 25 dials.

Hamle stake movement lets strong teams always call Step 3 and weak teams play safe with 1. That creates a runaway leader in a race structure, and the Light Tailwind (+1) cannot counter a team that moves 3 squares per turn. The stakes also depend on diff 1/2/3 tags, and LLM-generated difficulty tags are unreliable.

Kids fairness contradiction: the first team to the chest 'wins' by dice luck, yet stars are the effort currency. Children will protest 'we had more stars!' and the spec never states which one decides. Meanwhile the Rescue Rope makes arrival meaningless, so the win condition is muddy for 10-year-olds.

Arena steals depend on who is 'first with its whiteboard up' among 3 teams. The teacher cannot adjudicate that fairly, and it causes disputes. Many public schools also have no class set of mini-whiteboards and markers.

The seat-number spinner inside teams of 7 needs seat numbers assigned and remembered, which is extra setup. Nothing supports shy children who are picked for a 20-40 s solo Tell in front of 28 peers, so expect freezes and dead air.
Ask squares need target selection, two speakers, and three judging chips, and 'Me too!' hands are counted aloud. Counting 12-20 hands takes 20 s and becomes a shouting contest.

No instant stop: the design handles a timed end (Final stretch at 4 min), but not the bell coming early, a principal walking in or a fight breaking out. There is no one-tap 'Bitir now' that jumps straight to a fair ceremony, and no save-and-resume for continuing next lesson.

The adult version is thin on value per minute. Mystery chests, dig site, shop and wager are fluff for 10 adults who came for speaking practice. With 2-3 teams, the Ask fairness and Kraken systems add little, and some adults read Snakes and Ladders as childish even under the Grand Tour skin.

A 30-45 node map graph with fog, forks, regions and neon trails on a washed-out classroom projector is hard to read from the back row. The camera zoom then hides the other teams' positions, which kids constantly ask about ('where are we?').

Scope overlaps heavily with c02 (the Monopoly-style board: dice, events, shop, currency) and with the RPG (map events, story forks). As specced this is really two games, a kids ladder race and a teen/adult expedition map, in one Large build.
fixes: Compute the board from real turn counts: squares = expected turns per team × average advance × 0.8, assuming 100 s turns for kids and 75 s for adults. Show this as 'Bu ayarla her takım ~6 tur oynar' on setup. For a fixed 20-min kids game, default to a 20-square board with the 1-6 die on the ladder variant, or cap the board at 15 squares for the 1-2-3 die.

One question per turn, hard cap. If a team lands on a ladder or snake square, that square's question replaces the landing task; it never adds a second one. The kids wrong-answer flow becomes: a hint and a second try; if that is still wrong, Gogo says the answer once and the class echoes it once.

Make every quiz square an 'all teams answer' moment. Every team answers on its own team card (one A-D card set per team, held up by the rotating card-holder), and every correct team earns 1 star, but only the active team moves. This removes dead time and keeps 28 kids engaged without solo pressure.

Drop TPR and 'stand up' as answer modes for classes over 20; use desk taps, hand signals or team cards instead. Keep TPR only for Brain-break events that the teacher triggers deliberately, capped at 30 s with a visible settle countdown (5-4-3-2-1 quiet hands).

Build a big on-screen teacher rail for smart boards: large ✓ / ✗ / Undo / Pause / Skip buttons pinned to one edge, reachable at child height, plus a phone-remote option (QR code). Treat the hotkeys as a bonus for laptop users, not the primary control.
Make Build-your-board an opt-in pre-lesson activity or a 60 s 'pick one of 3 preset layouts' vote. Snakes are placed by the engine only, never by teams, which removes spite placement.

Split the design. v1 is ONE ladder board engine used by all three audiences with reskins (vines / zip-lines / express trains), Zar or Hamle only, 4 event types, no shop, dig site, fog or Karma. The map, forks, shop and dig site move to the RPG or share c02's economy engine in v2.

Hamle fairness: limit Step 3 to at most 2 uses per team per round, or give trailing teams +1 square on any correct answer. Give the last team a free 'double die' once per game. Pre-tag difficulty for built-in banks, and let the validator re-rank LLM items by word band and length rather than trusting the LLM's diff tags.

Kids win condition: make it cooperative. The CLASS races Gogo's boat to the island, all team stars add to a class total that decides the finale, and team titles are given for behaviour and categories. Otherwise say explicitly that stars decide the winner and arrival only unlocks the chest. Never use both.

Replace 'first whiteboard up' steals with a sealed simultaneous reveal ('3-2-1 göster'), where every correct team gets half the value. Provide a printable A-D card and team-card fallback for schools without mini-whiteboards.
Speaker support: let the picked child choose 'solo' or 'with a buddy' (two voices, full stars). Kids Tell becomes 'say 2 things' in 15 s, with a team chorus fallback after 5 s of silence.
Ask squares: replace hand counting with a quick 'Me too' tap on the teacher rail with a rough count (few / half / most), or skip the count at over 20 students.
Add a one-tap 'Şimdi bitir' button. It ends in under 20 s with titles from the current state and saves the game so it can resume next lesson (localStorage class profile).

Adults: default to 2-3 teams, a 40/40/20 Ask/Tell/Quiz mix and border-control role-play from A2 up. Cut mystery chests, dig site and shop from the Stüdyo defaults, and let the error log and 'Kaçırılanlar' postcards carry the value.
Readability: keep a permanent mini-map strip of all team positions at the top even while zoomed, set a minimum square size for 30 squares at 1080p, and use a high-contrast projector theme by default.

Share the token, die, event, undo and ceremony engine with c02. Consider merging the teen/adult map expedition into the RPG candidate, so this game stays the simple, fast race for kids and a low-prep speaking race for adults.

issues: Speaking is the strongest feature, and also the part least likely to exist at launch. None of the built-in banks has speaking prompts with the needed fields: no ask or tell items with starters, useful words and targets, no emoji or imageKey, no teenSafe flag, and no diff tag. words.js has no pictures and grammar_mcq_* has no difficulty tiers. The built-in path for Ask and Tell (about 24 cards a game) has to be authored from nothing, and without it the game falls back to a Baamboozle-style quiz on a board.

The pacing numbers don't add up for kids. A 1-2-3 die averages 2 squares a turn, so 20 squares take about 8-10 turns per team (ladders help, snakes cost). With 4 teams that is 30-40 turns at 45-75 s each, or 25-50 minutes, against a fixed 20 minutes. At A2 Genç with 30 squares it is worse. Most classes will never reach the chest by play and will always finish through the forced Final stretch and Rescue Rope, so the race feels fake.

A1 Genç children who barely read can't do Ask or Tell unaided. The card '🍕 you / like?' expects a 9-year-old to build question inversion from a text cue, and 'Say 3 things' for 20 s alone in front of the class is too much for many A1 Turkish 3rd-4th graders. The design gives no audio model of the target question and no choral or pair fallback. The likely result is silence, or the teacher saying it in Turkish.

Arena at A1 or A2 (a 13-year-old beginner class) gets the full adult-grade rule load: forks, shortcuts at difficulty 3, fog, Kraken, Supply drop, Dig site, combos, steals and gold. Only the kids pack is held to the 3-rule checklist. The rules are read in Turkish, but every rule turn still asks for English strategy talk ('We'll take the shortcut because...') that is far above A1. The game gets heavy on rules while the English stays thin.

The difficulty tiers are unreliable on both content paths. The LLM labels diff 1/2/3 inconsistently, and the curated MCQ banks have no difficulty labels at all. Hamle (staked movement) depends on 'Step 3 = hard' actually being harder. If it isn't, teams always stake 3 and the strategy disappears (adults at B2 will notice within two turns).

Adults: the Snakes and Ladders core, even reskinned as Grand Tour, is still a luck-and-position race. At B2 the language happens on Ask, Tell and Border control squares, while half the turns are quiz items that other games in the suite already cover. Adults at B1 and B2 may see the board as a wrapper around the talk. The value comes from the speaking squares, and the Task mix sliders could let a teacher drop them.

The picture requirement starves the LLM path. The validator drops A1/A2 Genç items without an imageKey from picture squares, but emoji can't show abstract verbs, feelings, time or grammar targets (for example 'going to' or comparatives). With a free-text prompt such as 'geçmiş zaman düzensiz fiiller', most items get dropped, and the pack can't supply around 40 quiz items plus 24 speaking cards.

It asks for a lot of content: about 110 items per game (40 quiz, 12 ask, 12 tell, 10 ladder/snake, 3 boss, 6 dig, 8 Everybody, 16 events), each tagged by type, difficulty, target and teenSafe. The LLM would generate this every time a teacher types a prompt, which means waiting time, rate-limit pressure and more chances for invalid items.

Judging puts a heavy load on the teacher: every Ask turn needs 2-3 rubric chips for two teams, every Tell needs chips, and the error notepad runs alongside. With 30 students at A1 kids this slows every turn. 'Follow-up ✓' at B1 and 'concede a point' at B2 can't be told apart at projector speed.
Arena's 'first whiteboard up steals' can't be judged fairly in a real classroom, and 12-14s will argue about who was first. It adds conflict, which goes against the Nazik rule pack.
Dig site ('C four!') and Build your board ('From seven to eighteen!') practise numbers, which fits A1 but is filler at B1-B2 and takes 2+ minutes of board time away from the language target.
Scope is L, and the game overlaps c02 (the property board) and the tile quiz. Nine event and shop subsystems on top of the ladder board risk shipping late, with the speaking layer thin.
fixes: Write a curated speaking bank before building the board: about 40 Ask and 40 Tell cards for each audience (Genç: YLE/MEB units; adult: life and work) and each level A1-B2. Each card carries emoji or imageKey, starters, useful words, target and teenSafe. Add diff tags to grammar_mcq_* offline, with a script that uses option-distractor heuristics plus one LLM pass followed by human spot-checks. Launch only once the built-in path covers Ask and Tell for all 8 groups.

Size the board from the lesson length instead of a fixed template: squares ≈ (minutes × 60 / turn secs / teams) × average move. For kids at 20 minutes with 4 teams that gives 12-15 squares, or use a 1-2 die with 16 squares. Show a live progress check, and if a team falls far behind, add ladders on the fly (Gogo drops a vine) so that it really arrives by play before the Final stretch.

Make A1 Genç speaking easier: (1) Gogo plays the model question and answer aloud before the student speaks ('Listen: Do you like pizza?'). (2) The whole class says it first in chorus, then the chosen speaker repeats it. (3) Tell becomes 'Point and say' (3 labelled pictures, one word each) rather than 20 s of free talk. (4) Give a 'Pair talk' option where the whole team says it together, not one child alone.

Add 'Arena Lite' as the automatic default for Arena at A1-A2: the Arena look with the kids ruleset, meaning no shop, no dig, no Kraken, no forks and at most 4 rule lines. Show the fork-call frames as tap-to-read sentence strips ('We take the... because it is short/safe') so it stays within A1-A2.

Put the Task mix floor inside the engine: at least 35% Ask and Tell squares in every template, and Stüdyo B1-B2 defaults to 50% speaking. Label the Quiz-only mode as 'hızlı tekrar', not the default, so the game stays a speaking game.

For Hamle, draw tier 3 at pack-build time from the next CEFR band or item type (A2: typed gap or no-picture audio; B2: open qa judged by the teacher), not from diff labels. This keeps 'hard' reliably harder, and the engine can show the success rate per tier after the game.

When the LLM path can't find pictures, fall back without dropping items: an abstract item moves to a non-picture square type (listen and choose with TTS, or a picture of a scene). If the pack is still short, top it up from the built-in category closest to the prompt, and tell the teacher in one Turkish line.

Cut the LLM request down: generate only the Ask and Tell cards and the quiz items (about 60); build events, dig words and Everybody items from templates and words.js. Cache each generated pack in the class profile so it can be replayed.

Cut judging to one tap: a green 'Tamam' by default, with a long press for rubric chips. Show the Ask model answer on the teacher's side only. At B1-B2 show the follow-up or concede frame on the student card, so judging becomes 'did they use the frame?'.

Replace 'first whiteboard up' with a fair steal: every team holds up its whiteboard on the count of 3, and every correct team gets half the gold. That keeps everyone answering at once and avoids arguments.

Turn Build your board and Dig site on by level: Build your board by default for A1-A2 only, Dig site for A1-A2 and as a spelling item for B1+. At B1-B2 use that time for Border control or for challenges on Tell talks.

Build a smaller v1: one engine shared with c02, the ladder board plus map-S/M, Zar and Hamle movement, Quiz/Ask/Tell/Event squares, and Green/Yellow events only. Add shop, dig, Kraken, fog and passports in v2 once the speaking layer has been tested in class.

reviews.mergeWith: c02 (share the board engine only: tokens, die, events, Undo, camera, teacher dock). Move the Dig site to any Battleship/grid candidate.
issues: Scope is really two or three games under one name: a serpentine ladder board, a procedural route graph with forks, fog of war and regions, plus a shop, a Dig site (a Battleship clone), build-your-board, a Kraken event, passports and a wager. As specified it is XL, not L. It is the riskiest candidate for shipping late or half-polished.

Procedural map-graph layout (30-45 nodes, 3-4 regions, forks, shortcuts about 40% shorter, readable at projector distance with pictograms of at least 6vh) is the single hardest engineering piece. Auto-layout of branching paths tends to look like a generic node graph, not a treasure map. The polish promise ('a real route map') depends on it.

The pacing maths does not close. A turn is 45-75 s, so 4 teams take about 4-5 min per round, and a 20-min game gives each team about 4-5 turns. At an average of 2 squares per turn (1-2-3 die or Hamle), plus a few ladders, a 30-square kids board and a 30-45-square map will rarely finish naturally. The forced Final stretch or Rescue Rope becomes the normal ending, and the race feels unfinished.

Arena and Stüdyo have two competing win conditions: first to the X (+10) versus the highest gold/miles. If gold decides, the race and the forks matter little; if position decides, gold is noise. Students (and the teacher) will be confused about what they are optimising.

Too many movement modes (Zar / Hamle / Karma) and dials (task-mix sliders, harshness, comeback, event density, shop prices, finish rule, die type, slide length). Each mode multiplies the QA matrix across 3 audiences x 4 levels x 2 board shapes.

'Model answer shown only on the teacher's side' assumes a presenter view. On one projected screen or a smartboard there is no private side, so it needs a hold-to-peek or a second-window design. The keyboard shortcuts (Space, E, U, Y/N) are useless when the teacher stands at a smartboard.
Arena steal ('first team with its whiteboard up') is a human-judged race, which is contentious with 12-14s. The software cannot adjudicate it.

LLM load is heavy: about 100+ items across 8+ item types per game (40 quiz, 12 ask, 12 tell, 10 ladder, 3 boss, 6 dig, 8 everybody, flavour lines). One DeepSeek call will not reliably return valid JSON of that size within rate limits, and latency at setup will be 30-90 s. Tell/Ask cards for Genç need emoji/imageKey, and emoji-as-picture for abstract cues ('where / go / last weekend?') is weak.

The kids 3-rule card hides extra rules (ladder question at diff+1, snake-charmer second chance, free hint ladder, Rescue Rope, build-your-board constraints). It is honest to the letter of the checklist, but the teacher still has to run them.

Build-your-board for 9-11s (each team says 'From seven to eighteen!', constraint checking, snap) is charming, but with 4 teams it easily takes 3-4 min of a 20-min lesson and yields invalid placements that need explaining.
Adults: Snakes and Ladders reads as childish. 'Grand Tour' only escapes that if the map is truly high-quality; the Career Ladder alternative is gimmicky. Adult fit hinges on art quality.

Overlap: the map/forks overlap an RPG/Crossroads/Treasure Map story-node candidate, the Dig site duplicates a Battleship candidate, and the shop/gold economy drifts toward c02. The quiz squares alone are 'MCQ quiz with a board'. What makes it distinct is Ask/Tell speaking plus movement, and that should be the identity.

Assets needed are substantial: Gogo the parrot (at least 6 states: idle, count, boing, fly-to-answer, sleep, wave), 8 animal tokens, a friendly snake (slide, yawn, sunglasses, sleep), vines, a chest, 6 geometric emblems, neon trail rendering, a vintage poster map, a Solari flip, boarding-pass cards, passport stamps, a crab, a Kraken silhouette, and about 20 SFX across 3 sound sets. That is feasible as SVG, but it is the bulk of the polish budget.

The TTS 'read-aloud at 0.8x' depends on an English speechSynthesis voice. Many Turkish school PCs and smartboards lack one or have a poor one, so kids' sound items and picture-audio 'hard' tiers break silently.
fixes: Ship an MVP of ONE engine with ONE path model: a hand-authored set of 6 board templates (ladder20, ladder30, a 24-square jungle path, a 28-square night map with 1 fork, a 28-square Grand Tour with 1 fork, and a 36-square version with 2 forks), stored as JSON with SVG backgrounds drawn once per skin. No procedural graph layout. Regions are colour bands on a fixed path.

Cut from v1: the Dig site (hand it to the Battleship candidate), the shop/items, fog of war, Kraken, Karma mode, the Duty-free wager, Border control and Career Ladder. Keep checkpoints, forks (max 2), ladders/snakes, Ask/Tell/Quiz/Event squares and Last Call. Add the rest behind 'Gelişmiş' in v2.

Make position the only win condition for every audience: the first team to the finish wins, then Last Call places the rest. Use stars/gold only as a tiebreak and for stat awards. Alternatively, always rank by squares advanced. Remove '+10 gold vs total gold' ambiguity.

Size boards from real turn maths: squares ≈ expected turns per team x 2.2 average move x 0.9. For 20 min with 4 teams that gives about 20 squares, not 30. Show the teacher 'Tahmini bitiş: 18 dk' on setup and let the lesson-fit timer adjust the die (1-3 to 1-6) mid-game if the race lags.
Two movement modes only: Zar (default for Oyun Parkı) and Hamle (default for Arena and Stüdyo). Karma is dropped.

Add an on-screen teacher dock (a collapsible bottom-right bar with Roll, ✓, ✗, Undo, Pause, Hata not, Peek) sized for smartboard fingers. Keys remain as accelerators. Model answers go behind a press-and-hold 'Peek' or an optional presenter window using BroadcastChannel.

Replace the whiteboard-race steal with a deterministic one: the steal goes to the next team in turn order (a 'Rebound'), or the teacher taps which team answered first, shown as tap-to-claim buttons per team colour.

Generate content in staged small calls with a strict schema per item type (quiz batch, ask/tell batch, flavour lines) and validate with zod-like checks: word caps per level, CEFR band lookup against words.js, the teenSafe blocklist, required emoji/imageKey for Genç, answer-in-options for MCQs, unique distractors, and dedupe. Top up any shortfall from the built-in banks (grammar_mcq_*, words.js) so the game can always start within 10 s and fill in LLM items as they arrive. Chance cards stay code templates, with the LLM producing flavour text only.
Curate built-in Ask/Tell card banks for the YLE/MEB topics (about 30 cards per topic per level band) before relying on the LLM. Speaking cards are this game's USP and must be good offline.
Kids build-your-board: default to 'Hızlı yerleştir'. The engine proposes 2 ladder/snake positions and each team just says the numbers aloud to confirm (30 s total). Full placement becomes an opt-in.

Keep the kids rule card truthful. The ladder question and snake charmer become the same visible rule ('Answer to climb or to wake up the snake... it sleeps!'), with a picture, and hints are automatic, not a rule.
Detect English voices at setup. If none, default to 'Öğretmen okur' and hide audio-only hard tiers, so a hard tier is never unplayable.

Asset plan: one SVG sprite sheet per skin (Gogo with 6 poses using CSS/transform animation, not frame-by-frame), 8 animal tokens reused from a shared mascot set across all kids games, and about 18 short SFX. Budget the polish time for the token hop and camera follow, the ladder climb, the snake slide and the finale. Those four moments are what make it feel like a real game.

Share the board engine with c02 explicitly (path model, token movement tween, die, event deck, Undo stack, camera zoom), but keep this game economy-free. Its identity is 'the speaking race': the Ask and Tell squares, with a whole-class moment on every turn.

catalog.rankReason: merged into c02. One board engine (tokens, die, events, undo, camera, teacher dock). Its ladder race with Ask/Tell squares becomes c02's Oyun Parkı ruleset 'Hazine Yolu', and the Ask/Tell square types join every ruleset. The Dig site goes to c20, and the route/expedition map idea goes to c04.

content.summary: One content model, lg.pack/1, serves built-in categories, AI packs, teacher packs, imports and remixes. A pack is an envelope (group, topic, origin, review, version) around a FLAT list of typed items. There are 19 answerable or card item types: vocab, mcq, gap, qa, tf, error, pair, order, category-list, odd, riddle, taboo-card, speaking-prompt, roleplay, survey, text, sound, character and chance-card. Three frame types hold scenario games: story-node, case and lock. Games declare what they need and read packs through adapters. Pure-code derivations (vocab to mcq, qa, pair, taboo-card or order; error to tf; category-list to odd or sort) let one 40-word vocab pack play in about 15 games, like Wordwall's switch template. Levels are controlled in code, not by prompting. Eight group profiles (A1, A2, B1, B2 adult; A1T, A2T, B1T, B2T for ages 7-14) set weighted cumulative word pools, grammar whitelists built from the real unit ids, word and character caps, option counts, taboo counts, speaking time and Turkish support. A lexical profiler checks every item. The LLM never sets ids, level, difficulty, kidSafe or codes. Generation fits Vercel Hobby's 60 s limit because the browser orchestrates several short serverless calls: input guard and cache, then a 3-5 s planner that shows an 'Anladığım şu' card, then grounding in words.js/YLE/banks, then 3-6 parallel JSON chunks (thinking off, each call 40 s or less), then schema and deterministic validators, then a blind-solve verifier running in parallel, then one repair pass, then teacher review, then save and cache. Target: a full pack in about 45 s, with a fallback to the nearest built-in pack. Child safety has five layers, and teen packs play only after the teacher approves them. Prompt injection is contained: the teacher text is data only, and the group, level, counts and game come from the UI. The built-in catalogue has 110 categories (vocabulary, grammar, speaking/functional, pronunciation, MEB grade packs with the 2026-27 split between the 2018 program and TYMM, LGS, YDS/YÖKDİL, Cambridge YLE/KET/PET). Checked in C:/lg: grammar unit ids and titles are a1-01..a1-21, a2-01..a2-20, b1-01..b1-22 and b2-01..b2-22 (for example a1-01 To Be, a2-09 irregular past, b1-12 PP just/already/yet, b2-04 mixed conditionals). grammar_mcq_a1 has 462 items. cefr_grammar_syllabus.json tags every module for primary, middle and adult with priority and complexity. buildCuratedClassTopics() in src/lib/game-classroom.mjs can be reused as the grammar-pack builder. New data files proposed: src/data/game-groups.js, src/data/game-lexicon.js, src/data/game-categories.js, src/data/yle.js and scripts/build-packs.mjs.

itemTypes.name: Kelime kartı / Word card (words, chunks, phrasal verbs, idioms, collocations)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + term (English, 1-4 words, ASCII a-z plus space, hyphen, apostrophe), form ('word'|'chunk'|'phrasal'|'idiom'|'colloc'), alt[] (accepted variants: UK/US spelling, plural, contraction), pos ('n'|'v'|'adj'|'adv'|'prep'|'phr'|'num'), media.emoji or media.img (required for teen groups when concrete), defEasy (10 words or fewer, only words at or below the group level), def (fuller English definition, B groups; Oxford text allowed if it is 18 words or fewer), defTr (1-3 Turkish glosses), example (contains term, within the group sentence cap, no 'something', slashes or fragments), gap {text with exactly one ___, answer, alsoOk[]}, distractors[3] (same pos and semantic field, WRONG in the gap), taboo[0-5]?, ipa? (from words.js), syll? (syllable count), family[]? (decide/decision/decisive, B groups), lit? (literal Turkish for idioms, from idioms.js), drawable (bool), actable (bool), concrete (bool), hangman (computed: letters only, 3-12 long, or a phrase at B)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i001","type":"vocab","aud":"all","diff":1,"level":"A1","skill":"vocab","tags":["toys","yle-starters"],"src":"bank:lex#kite","term":"kite","form":"word","alt":[],"pos":"n","media":{"emoji":"🪁"},"defEasy":"A toy. It flies in the wind.","def":"a light toy that flies in the wind on a long string","defTr":"uçurtma","example":"My kite is red and yellow.","gap":{"text":"It's windy! Let's fly my ___.","answer":"kite","alsoOk":[]},"distractors":["doll","bike","ball"],"taboo":["fly","wind"],"drawable":true,"actable":true,"concrete":true,"hangman":true}
itemTypes.levelControl: The term must be in the group pool at or below the group level. Up to 10% of items (A groups) or 20% (B groups) may be level+1, flagged 'stretch-word'; teacher word lists override this. Clue shown per group: A1T/A2T use emoji or picture plus defTr; A1/A2 use defEasy; B1/B2/B2T use def (defEasy as a fallback); B1T uses defEasy. Phrasal, idiom and colloc forms only from B1/B1T (A2T gets only get up, put on, take off, turn on/off). Hangman length: 3-8 letters A1T, 3-10 A2T, 3-12 others, multi-word phrases from B1. Taboo count per group comes from the group profile. Distractors must share pos and topic and must not appear in the key's synonym list.

itemTypes.name: Çoktan seçmeli / Multiple choice
itemTypes.fields: base fields + fmt ('gap'|'meaning'|'picture'|'collocation'|'dialogue'|'context'|'reading'), stem (exactly one ___ when fmt='gap'), ctx? (short message, poster, chat or dialogue for LGS/KET-style context items), options[3|4] (key stored at any index; the game shuffles at presentation), answer (index), whyTr (90 chars or fewer, names the rule), whyOpt[]? (per-option Turkish reason, from the curated banks), whyEn? (B groups), target (e.g. 'past simple irregular'), unit? ('a2-09'), textRef? (text item id)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i014","type":"mcq","aud":"all","diff":2,"skill":"grammar","tags":["zoo-trip","unit:a2-09"],"src":"ai","fmt":"gap","stem":"Yesterday we ___ to the zoo.","options":["go","went","goes"],"answer":1,"whyTr":"'Yesterday' geçmişi anlatır: go → went.","whyOpt":["Geniş zaman; 'yesterday' ile kullanılmaz.","","He/she/it için geniş zaman."],"target":"past simple irregular","unit":"a2-09"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Options: 3 for A1T/A2T, 4 for the others. Stem char caps: A1T 45, A2T 60, A1 60, A2 80, B1T 90, B1 110, B2T 110, B2 120. Option caps: A1T 12, A2T 15, A1 25, A2 30, B1T 25, B1 40, B2T 35, B2 60 chars. The target unit must be in the group grammar whitelist. No NOT stems for teens; at most 10% for adults. 'All/none of the above' is banned. Options must be homogeneous. Distractors come preferably from the Turkish L1 error catalogue. The blind-solve verifier must pick the key with no alternative answer.

itemTypes.name: Boşluk doldurma / Gap sentence (tap or type)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + text (1 slot; 2 slots only at B2), answers[slot][] (every accepted form, including contractions and UK/US spellings), bank[]? (tap options; required for teens and A groups on the board), base? (word to transform, e.g. '(go)'), hintTr?, target, unit?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i020","type":"gap","diff":2,"skill":"grammar","tags":["unit:b1-01"],"src":"ai","text":"I have lived in this city ___ 2019.","answers":[["since"]],"bank":["for","since","ago","from"],"hintTr":"Başlangıç anı (2019) → since; süre (5 yıl) → for.","target":"for / since","unit":"b1-01"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Typed answers only for B groups or device mode (ETAP boards pop up the on-screen keyboard, and typed cloze is the hardest format for recall). Everyone else gets bank tiles: 3 options A1T/A2T, 4 others. Transformation with base from A2/A2T. Sentence word caps from the group profile. The verifier's alsoAcceptable answers are merged into answers[].

itemTypes.name: İpucu-cevap / Clue and answer (Jeopardy, Grand Race, Beehive, Kelime Oyunu, Hot Potato)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + clue, accept[1-6] (all valid answers), answerKind ('word'|'phrase'|'number'|'sentence'), letter? (Beehive: the answer starts with it), len? (computed), tolerance? (number answers, estimation tiebreakers), hintTr?, value? (Jeopardy tier, computed from diff), teacherJudge (bool: open answers the teacher accepts; accept[] is the model answer)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i031","type":"qa","diff":1,"skill":"vocab","tags":["shopping"],"src":"ai","clue":"The opposite of 'expensive'.","accept":["cheap","inexpensive"],"answerKind":"word","hintTr":"ucuz","teacherJudge":false}
itemTypes.levelControl: Clue within the group sentence cap. A1T/A2T clues are an emoji or picture, or 7 words or fewer. answerKind 'sentence' only for B groups, always teacherJudge. accept[] must cover the obvious synonyms (verifier). The Beehive letter is checked by code.

itemTypes.name: Doğru / Yanlış
itemTypes.fields: base fields + about ('picture'|'meaning'|'sentence-correct'|'text'|'pack-fact'), statement, isTrue, fix? (the corrected statement when false), whyTr, textRef? (for 'text')
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i040","type":"tf","diff":1,"skill":"vocab","tags":["animals"],"src":"derived:i002","about":"picture","statement":"This is a giraffe.","media":{"emoji":"🐘"},"isTrue":false,"fix":"This is an elephant.","whyTr":"Resimdeki hayvan fil: elephant."}
itemTypes.levelControl: Language accuracy or pack-grounded facts only, never open world trivia. 'pack-fact' must quote a text item or the curated fact table. Teens: picture/meaning/text statements of 7-10 words. 'sentence-correct' from A2. About 50% false. The fix is required when false.

itemTypes.name: Hatalı cümle / Error sentence (Sentence Auction, Fix it)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + wrong, right, span [start,end) character offsets of the error in wrong, errorType ('article'|'3rd-s'|'be+verb'|'aux-question'|'tense'|'for-since'|'preposition'|'plural'|'uncountable'|'comparative'|'word-choice'|'word-order'|'capital'|'spelling'), whyTr, unit?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i052","type":"error","diff":1,"skill":"grammar","tags":["unit:a1-05","l1-trap"],"src":"derived:bank:mcq:a1-05#7","wrong":"She go to school by bus.","right":"She goes to school by bus.","span":[4,6],"errorType":"3rd-s","whyTr":"He/she/it ile fiile -s gelir: goes.","unit":"a1-05"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Exactly one error, with a span of 3 words or fewer. The errorType must target a structure in the group grammar whitelist. Teens: visible form errors only (no register or collocation subtleties). B2 may use aspect, collocation and preposition subtleties. Auto-derived from curated MCQ distractors (the distractor put into the stem) and re-verified.

itemTypes.name: Eşleştirme / Pair (Memory, Match, Bingo, Spot the Match)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + a, b, rel ('tr'|'emoji'|'def'|'syn'|'ant'|'colloc'|'qa'|'half'|'past'|'idiom-meaning'|'sound'), aMedia?, bMedia?, set? (pairs are unique only within their set)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i060","type":"pair","diff":2,"skill":"vocab","tags":["collocations"],"src":"ai","set":"s1","a":"make","b":"a mistake","rel":"colloc"}
itemTypes.levelControl: rel by group: emoji/tr for A1T/A2T; tr/def/ant for A1/A2; syn/colloc/half/past/idiom-meaning from B1/B1T. The validator requires 1-to-1 matching inside a set, so no b may fit two a's (checked with the synonym map and the verifier). Both sides must pass the lexical profiler.

itemTypes.name: Sıralama / Unjumble and sequence
itemTypes.fields: base fields + kind ('sentence'|'events'|'dialogue'|'process'), tokens[] (in correct order), alt[][] (other valid orders), chunked (bool: tokens are chunks such as 'every day' for teens), hintTr?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i071","type":"order","diff":2,"skill":"grammar","tags":["unit:a1-06"],"src":"derived:i005","kind":"sentence","tokens":["Where","does","your","cousin","live","?"],"alt":[],"chunked":false,"hintTr":"Soru: Where + does + özne + fiil"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Token caps: A1T 5 (chunked), A2T 7, A1 8, A2 10, B1T 12, B1 14, B2T 14, B2 16. Events/process: 4 steps for teens, 6 for adults. The verifier lists other grammatical orders (adverb positions) and they go into alt[].

itemTypes.name: Kategori listesi (İsim-Şehir STOP, Group Sort, Codenames clusters, Hot Potato, Impostor)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + label (EN, 4 words or fewer), labelTr, media.emoji?, open (bool: any valid answer counts and the teacher judges; members are examples), members[{text, alt[]?, level (computed), tr?}] (8-40), byLetter (computed index for STOP), minPerLetter (feasibility threshold for the letter pool), multiWord (bool)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i080","type":"category-list","diff":1,"skill":"vocab","tags":["home","kitchen"],"src":"ai","label":"Things in the kitchen","labelTr":"Mutfaktaki eşyalar","media":{"emoji":"🍳"},"open":false,"members":[{"text":"fridge"},{"text":"cooker","alt":["stove"]},{"text":"cup"},{"text":"plate"},{"text":"fork"},{"text":"spoon"},{"text":"kettle"},{"text":"sink"}],"minPerLetter":0,"multiWord":false}
itemTypes.levelControl: Members come from the group pool. A1T gets 8-12 concrete, emoji-able members. Abstract or open labels ('A reason to be late', 'Something you can make', 'A phrasal verb with up') only for B adults. STOP letters are drawn only where byLetter meets minPerLetter at that level.

itemTypes.name: Farklı olanı bul / Odd one out
itemTypes.fields: base fields + kind ('meaning'|'grammar'|'sound'|'spelling'), items[4], odd (index), reasonEn? (B groups), reasonTr
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i090","type":"odd","diff":1,"skill":"vocab","tags":["food"],"src":"derived:category-list","kind":"meaning","items":["banana","carrot","apple","grape"],"odd":1,"reasonTr":"Havuç bir sebze; diğerleri meyve."}
itemTypes.levelControl: Teens: meaning only, with concrete categories. Sound and grammar kinds from A2/B1 (e.g. -ed /ɪd/ vs /t/). The verifier must find exactly one defensible odd item; any alsoAcceptable answer blocks the item.

itemTypes.name: Bil bakalım / 'What am I?' riddle
itemTypes.fields: base fields + answer, accept[]?, frame ('What am I?'|'Who am I?'|'Where am I?'), clues[3] (hard to easy), media.emoji?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i100","type":"riddle","diff":2,"skill":"vocab","tags":["animals"],"src":"ai","frame":"What am I?","answer":"penguin","clues":["I live in a very cold place.","I can swim, but I can't fly.","I am a black and white bird."],"media":{"emoji":"🐧"}}
itemTypes.levelControl: Each clue within the group sentence cap. A1T uses have got / can / is only. The verifier must guess the answer from clue 3 alone, and clue 1 alone must not give it away. People riddles: fictional or job-based only, never real people.

itemTypes.name: Söyleme! kartı / Taboo, Hot Seat, Draw or Act card
itemTypes.fields: base fields + target, ref? (vocab item id), forbidden[0-5], frames[] (sentence starters), mode ('describe'|'draw'|'act'|'any'), catHint? (category shown to the guessing team), defTr (teacher check only), media.emoji?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i110","type":"taboo-card","diff":2,"skill":"vocab","tags":["travel"],"src":"derived:i044","target":"passport","forbidden":["travel","country","airport","document"],"frames":["You need it when...","It's a kind of..."],"mode":"describe","catHint":"Travel","defTr":"pasaport"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Forbidden count: A1T 0 (picture plus frames, draw or act), A2T 2, A1 2, A2 3, B1T 3, B1 4, B2T 4, B2 5. The Turkish translation is always forbidden by rule. The validator rejects forbidden words that equal the target or share its stem or word family. The verifier must describe the target in 15 words or fewer at the group level without forbidden words, otherwise the card is dropped. Frames are required for A levels and teens. A1T mode is draw/act only for concrete, drawable or actable terms.

itemTypes.name: Konuşma kartı / Speaking prompt (wheel, Just a Minute, WYR, chance tiles)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + mode ('talk'|'describe'|'wyr'|'opinion'|'debate'|'story'|'hypothetical'|'survey'|'find-someone'|'jam'|'ask'), prompt, optA?/optB? (wyr), side? ('for'|'against', debate), starters[≤3] (sentence frames), followUps[≤3], useful[≤5] (words or phrases), secs, target? (grammar/function, e.g. 'fn:advice' or 'unit:a2-16'), media.emoji?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i120","type":"speaking-prompt","diff":1,"skill":"speaking","tags":["animals","wyr"],"src":"ai","mode":"wyr","prompt":"Would you rather be a fish or a bird?","optA":"a fish 🐟","optB":"a bird 🐦","starters":["I'd rather be a ... because I can ..."],"followUps":["Where would you live?"],"useful":["swim","fly","sea","sky"],"secs":30}
itemTypes.levelControl: Expected output and time: A1T 1 framed sentence, 15-20 s, picture. A2T 2 sentences, 30 s. B1T 30-45 s with 'because'. B2T 45-60 s, simple pros and cons. A1 1-2 sentences, 20 s. A2 2-3 sentences, 30 s. B1 45-60 s plus 'why'. B2 60-90 s plus a counter-argument. Modes allowed: debate only for B2/B2T (light). Hypothetical from B1 (A2T only with frames). Starters are required for A levels and all teen groups. Teen and all-audience prompts never ask for personal data (address, weight, family income) and use family-neutral wording.

itemTypes.name: Canlandırma kartları / Role-play with information gap
itemTypes.fields: base fields + scenario, setting, roleA {title, info[], goals[≤3], useful[]}, roleB {title, info[], goals[≤3], useful[]}, twist?, checklist[] (teacher success criteria), secs
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i130","type":"roleplay","diff":2,"skill":"function","tags":["hotel","fn:complaint"],"src":"ai","scenario":"A problem at the hotel","setting":"hotel reception","roleA":{"title":"Guest","info":["You are in Room 214.","The shower is cold."],"goals":["Explain the problem","Ask for a new room","Ask about breakfast time"],"useful":["I'm afraid...","Could I...?"]},"roleB":{"title":"Receptionist","info":["Room 305 is free.","Breakfast is from 7 to 10."],"goals":["Say sorry","Offer a solution","Ask for the room number"],"useful":["I'm sorry about that.","Would you like...?"]},"twist":"Room 305 is next to the lift. It's noisy.","checklist":["polite request with could","explains the problem clearly"],"secs":120}
itemTypes.levelControl: A1T: no free role-play (use order kind 'dialogue', 2-4 lines). A2T: scripted cards with frames. B1T and above: information gap. Adults A1: 3-4 exchange frames. B2: negotiation with conflicting goals. The validator checks that each of A's goals can be answered from B's info (shared fact strings) and vice versa, and that at least one goal needs negotiation from B1 up. Teen settings: school, shop, museum, canteen, club; no workplace money or dating.

itemTypes.name: Sınıf Diyor ki / Survey board (Family Feud)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + prompt, answers[5-8] {text, pts, aliases[]}, source ('class'|'generated')
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i140","type":"survey","diff":1,"skill":"vocab","tags":["holidays"],"src":"ai","prompt":"Name something you take to the beach.","answers":[{"text":"towel","pts":30,"aliases":["beach towel"]},{"text":"sunscreen","pts":25,"aliases":["sun cream","suncream"]},{"text":"hat","pts":15,"aliases":["cap","sun hat"]},{"text":"sunglasses","pts":12,"aliases":["glasses"]},{"text":"ball","pts":10,"aliases":["beach ball"]},{"text":"water","pts":8,"aliases":["a bottle of water"]}],"source":"generated"}
itemTypes.levelControl: A groups and teens: single-word answers from the pool. B groups: phrase answers. pts must total 90-110. Aliases are required for plural and UK/US forms. Teen prompts avoid personal and family details. A live class survey replaces generated points when the teacher runs one.

itemTypes.name: Okuma metni / Reading text (Reading Detective, escape-room note, LGS context)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + title, body, words (computed), sentences[] (computed split), questionIds[] (mcq/tf/qa items with textRef), evidence {questionId: sentenceIndex}, glossary[≤5] {en, tr} (level+1 words only)
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i150","type":"text","diff":1,"skill":"reading","tags":["pets"],"src":"ai","title":"Max the Dog","body":"This is Max. He is my dog. He is brown and white. He has got big ears. Max can run fast, but he can't climb trees. He likes bones and balls.","words":31,"questionIds":["i151","i152"],"evidence":{"i151":3,"i152":4},"glossary":[]}
itemTypes.levelControl: Word counts: A1T 30-50 (25 words or fewer per screen, following MEB grades 5-6), A2T 60-90, B1T 90-130, B2T 120-170, A1 40-60, A2 80-110, B1 120-160, B2 150-220. At least 95% of tokens must be in the pool (names excepted). The verifier blind-solves every question from the text, and each question needs its own evidence sentence.

itemTypes.name: Telaffuz / Sound item (minimal pairs, -ed, silent letters, stress, rhyme)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + kind ('minimal-pair'|'ed-ending'|'silent-letter'|'stress'|'rhyme'), a, b?, ipaA, ipaB?, contrast (e.g. '/ɪ/ – /iː/'), key? ('/t/'|'/d/'|'/ɪd/', stressed syllable index, or silent letter index), sentenceA?/sentenceB? (context sentences), tipTr (mouth tip), tts: true
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i160","type":"sound","diff":1,"skill":"pron","tags":["l1-trap"],"src":"bank:words#sheep","kind":"minimal-pair","a":"ship","b":"sheep","ipaA":"/ʃɪp/","ipaB":"/ʃiːp/","contrast":"/ɪ/ – /iː/","sentenceA":"Look at that big ship!","sentenceB":"Look at that big sheep!","tipTr":"sheep'teki /iː/ uzun ve gülümser gibi söylenir.","tts":true}
itemTypes.levelControl: A1T/A2T: picture-able minimal pairs and rhymes only. -ed endings from A2/A2T. Silent letters from A2. Word stress from B1/B1T. Weak forms and schwa at B2. IPA comes from words.js and is never written by the LLM. Contrasts come from the Turkish-speaker list (/w/-/v/, /θ ð/-/t d/, vowel length, /æ/-/e/, final devoicing, s-cluster epenthesis).

itemTypes.name: Karakter kartı / Character (Two Truths and a Lie, Guess Who, Hot Seat, Alibi)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + name (fictional, from the name pool), avatar (sticker key), intro, statements[3], lieIndex (chosen by code), profile[6-10] (facts), answers {questionTemplateId: text}
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i170","type":"character","diff":2,"skill":"speaking","tags":["pirates","unit:a2-03"],"src":"ai","name":"Captain Mira","avatar":"pirate-2","intro":"I am a pirate. I live on a big ship.","statements":["I have got a green parrot.","I was born on a ship.","I can't swim."],"lieIndex":2,"profile":["has got a green parrot called Pip","was born on a ship","swims with dolphins every morning","loves maps","is afraid of spiders","has got a red boat"],"answers":{"q-hobby":"I love reading old maps.","q-morning":"I swim with dolphins every morning."}}
itemTypes.levelControl: Always fictional; no real people for any group. The profile must support the true statements and contain at least 2 facts that expose the lie (checked by string references). Statement length follows the group caps. The grammar target (e.g. past simple, have got, present perfect experiences) must be in the whitelist.

itemTypes.name: Şans kartı / Chance or event card (Monopoly, Snakes & Ladders, RPG events, Stranded)
itemTypes.fields: base fields + kind ('reward'|'penalty'|'task'|'swap'|'bonus'), task? ('speak'|'act'|'spell'|'draw'|'sing'|'answer'), text, textTr? (rules help for A1T), amount (coins or steps; clamped by the game engine), secs?
itemTypes.example: {"id":"i180","type":"chance-card","diff":1,"skill":"speaking","tags":["daily-routine"],"src":"ai","kind":"task","task":"act","text":"Act out your morning routine. Your team guesses 3 verbs.","textTr":"Sabah rutinini canlandır. Takımın 3 fiil tahmin etsin.","amount":100,"secs":45}
itemTypes.levelControl: Text within the group sentence cap. Teen penalties are gentle and never eliminate a team (the YLE 'shields, not fail' model). No gambling words ('bet', 'casino') anywhere; teens get stars or coins. The engine clamps effects, so an LLM value can never unbalance a game.

itemTypes.name: Hikâye düğümü / Story node (RPG, Crossroads, Treasure Map) — lives in pack.frames.story
itemTypes.fields: id, act (1|2|3), kind ('intro'|'gate'|'npc'|'riddle'|'trap'|'chest'|'fork'|'shop'|'camp'|'boss'|'ending'), narration, npcName?, npcLine?, choices[{label, to, effects?:{hp, gold, item}}], slot? {types[] (answerable item types), skill, count, diff} (code fills it with pack items), outcomes? {success, fail}, scene (background or sticker key); story envelope: {title, titleTr, skin ('fantasy'|'space'|'jungle'|'pirates'|'city'|'office'|'travel'|'mystery'), nodes[], endings {win, lose, funny?}}
itemTypes.example: {"id":"n3","act":1,"kind":"gate","narration":"A big stone door. A small dragon sits in front of it.","npcName":"Pip","npcLine":"Answer my questions and I open the door!","slot":{"types":["mcq","qa","riddle"],"skill":"vocab","count":3,"diff":1},"choices":[{"label":"Go in","to":"n4"}],"scene":"castle-door"}
itemTypes.levelControl: Code generates the topology (ids, edges, kinds, difficulty per path), and the LLM writes only narration, NPC lines and choice labels, with the whole outline in context. Narration caps: A1T 2 sentences of 7 words or fewer, A2T 25 words, B1T 40, B2T 60, A1 25, A2 40, B1 60, B2 90. The validator checks that every node is reachable, no link dangles, at least one win ending exists, and the lexical level holds. Teen skins are never scary or violent: the boss is 'defeated' by answers and ends up friendly.

itemTypes.name: Gizem dosyası / Mystery case (Kim Yaptı?, Alibi) — lives in pack.frames.case
itemTypes.fields: theme, caseIntro, suspects[4-6] {id, name, avatar, attrs {look, item, place, time, activity}}, culpritId, clues[{id, attrRef, round, text}], answers {suspectId: {questionTemplateId: text}}, confession, mature (bool)
itemTypes.example: {"theme":"The missing birthday cake","caseIntro":"The cake was on the kitchen table at 3 o'clock.
