platform.ageAdaptation:
TWO AXES, NOT ONE. The group chip sets two independent things. (1) The LEVEL profile (A1-B2): word caps, CEFR word bands from words.js, grammar whitelist and hint types. (2) The AUDIENCE mode: skin plus rule pack. There are three audience modes:
- 'Oyun Parkı' (children, 9-11): default for A1 Genç and A2 Genç.
- 'Arena' (12-14): default for B1 Genç and B2 Genç. It is also suggested for any Genç group when the teacher picks MEB grade 6-8, so a 13-year-old A1 class gets Arena visuals with A1 content and full picture and audio support.
- 'Stüdyo' (adults): default for A1-B2.
On top of these sits the rule pack 'Nazik mod'. It is ON in Oyun Parkı. In Arena it is ON, except that mild steals are allowed if the teacher opts in. It is OFF in Stüdyo. The teacher can override the skin, the rule pack or any single dial, and the result is saved in a local class profile (e.g. '7-B · A2 Genç · Arena'). The group label never appears on the student-facing screen, so 13-year-olds are never shown 'A1 Kids'.

GAMES ADAPT THEIR RULES, NOT JUST THEIR SKIN. Each game ships three rule variants plus art, and the kids variant is a stripped ruleset, not the adult one re-coloured. Before the kids variant ships, it must pass a checklist: at most 3 rules; explainable in 20 s with pictograms; no elimination; no score below zero; a whole-class response moment every turn; non-violent failure imagery. Examples:
- Hangman: Oyun Parkı 'Balloon Rescue' (8 misses; balloons pop and the mascot parachutes down safely; picture hint; letters read aloud). Arena 'Code Breaker' (6 misses; a vault with laser locks; streak bonus). Stüdyo 'Word Vault' (6 misses; category plus definition clue; optional wager).
- Board game: Oyun Parkı 'Town Tour' (stamps instead of money, no bankruptcy, fixed 20 min). Stüdyo 'Property' (rent paid in sentences, trading, a rent cap as runaway brake).
- RPG: kids get 'correct = guaranteed success, the die only sizes the reward' on a d6 with hearts, and heroes 'fall asleep' instead of dying. Adults get a d20 with Great/Good/Weak targets.

DIAL TABLE (Oyun Parkı / Arena / Stüdyo). The numbers are design defaults to test in class, not research values.
1 VISUALS. Oyun Parkı: warm bright palette on cream, rounded shapes, big pictures, a self-hosted font with a single-storey a (Andika-type), and animal team mascots named with English A1 words (panda, fox, lion, frog, tiger, rabbit, penguin, bear). Arena: dark navy/charcoal with neon accents in the team colours, a condensed display font, geometric team emblems (bolt, flame, wave, comet, crown, diamond) and 'Challenge'/'Match' wording. Stüdyo: editorial quiz-night look (cream, or the dark 'Karartılmış sınıf' theme), system sans, no mascots, and team names from cities, coffee drinks or grammar puns ('The Irregular Verbs').
2 MASCOT. Oyun Parkı has one recurring host. Proposal: a parrot, working name 'Gogo' (from Languago). A parrot repeats words, which models choral repetition, and it is deliberately not an owl. It demos every game in a 20-30 s practice round that does not score, says the correct answer after a miss, hosts the hello and goodbye rituals, and sleeps on the pause screen. Arena has no talking mascot, only a 'commentator' caption strip ('COMBO x3', 'CLUTCH!') at most once per turn. Stüdyo has no mascot and no voice lines, just a neutral caption ('Round 2 · Travel').
3 TEXT LOAD. Maximum words in a student-facing prompt: A1 Genç 0-4 (the picture carries the meaning), A2 Genç 8, B1 Genç 14, B2 Genç 20; A1 10, A2 15, B1 25, B2 40. The generator and validator enforce these caps. A long item is split into two cards rather than shrunk. Prompt font floor: 6vh for kids, 5vh for Arena, 4.5vh for adults.
4 PICTURES AND AUDIO. In A1/A2 Genç every item needs an imageKey from the self-hosted SVG set; unpicturable items are dropped from picture-dependent games. These groups get automatic read-aloud at 0.8x. Everyone else gets a speaker button on every item. If there is no English voice, the fallback is 'Öğretmen okur' (the teacher reads).
5 OPTIONS DELAY (question first, options later): kids 3-4 s, Arena 2.5 s, adults 2 s.
6 TIMERS. Oyun Parkı: off by default; when on, 40 s, a calm ring that is never red, and a marimba chime at 0. Arena: 30 s, on, with the ring in the team colour. Stüdyo: optional 30 s. Always available: +10 s, T to pause, and 'Süresiz'. There are no speed points in any mode.
7 HUDDLE ('Team talk'): kids 10 s, Arena 15 s, adults 20 s, then 'Boards up!'.
8 WHO ANSWERS. Kids: a whole-class response every turn (printed A-D cards, or TPR: stand for A, sit for B, hands up for C) plus the seat-number spinner for the active team. Arena: the spinner plus mini-whiteboards. Adults: a rotating spokesperson and pair consultation. Nobody is ever picked by name.
9 HINT LADDER. Kids: picture, then first letter, then listen again, all free. Arena: first letter, then 50:50, then a gapped example; each costs 1-2 points but never takes a score below 0. Adults: definition, then example, then Turkish gloss, each costing points; the TR gloss can be switched off for immersion classes.
10 WRONG ANSWERS. Kids: a soft 'boing' and a second try with a hint. If it is still wrong, the mascot says the answer and the whole class repeats it twice, and the team gets an effort star (it goes to the class album, not the win count). Arena: the streak breaks, and one other team may steal by answering; the first team loses nothing. Adults: the correct answer plus a one-line 'why', with optional minus points.
11 SCORING. Kids: stars (1-3) and stickers, and a score never goes down. Arena: points plus a combo (x1.5 at 3 correct in a row, x2 at 5; based on accuracy only), with a floor at zero. Adults: points, optional negatives, and wager rounds.
12 LUCK AND HARSHNESS. The Harshness dial has three levels.
- Green (the only level for kids): Gift 5 to a team you tap, Everyone +2, Double, Shield, Brain break.
- Yellow (opt-in for Arena): Steal 5 from a team you tap (capped at that team's score), Swap turn order.
- Red (opt-in for adults): Reset, Swap scores, Virus.
Adults get Green plus Yellow by default. The Comeback dial (Off / Light / Strong) is Light everywhere: the last team gets a Slipstream bonus when it answers correctly, and the trailing team picks the next category.
13 CELEBRATION. Kids: at most 2 s per event (sticker burst, mascot dance), with confetti in team colours AND shapes only at the finale. Arena: at most 1.2 s of combo text plus a synth sting, and a podium at the finale. Adults: a 0.6 s chime plus the score rolling up, and a modest finale. Reduced motion replaces every effect with a static stamp.
14 SOUND. Kids: a marimba/xylophone pack, no buzzers. Arena: short synth blips. Adults: woodblock and piano. Every effect is at most 1 s and loudness-normalised. Music is off by default for adults; kids and Arena have an optional quiet 'thinking' loop.
15 PACING. Oyun Parkı: rounds of 3-5 min, 3 rounds, with a 45 s stirrer or 60 s settler between rounds (15-25 min in total). Arena: rounds of 5-7 min, interludes optional. Stüdyo: rounds of 8-12 min, 20-40 min in total. The lesson-fit timer sizes the board from these numbers.
16 ENDINGS. Kids: every team gets a title (Best Helpers, Super Listeners, Bravest Guessers), and the class album gets a sticker. Arena: a podium plus team stat awards (Longest streak, Comeback, Clean sheet), and never a 'last place'. Adults: full scores plus the 'Kaçırılanlar' review list.
17 CONTENT. Every Genç group runs through the teenSafe filter: no alcohol, dating, violence, gambling, horror, politics or brands, and no adult domains (rent, salary, office, boss). B2 Genç means richer language on concrete topics, not abstract debate. Kids' categories follow YLE-style topics and MEB units, with pictures. Adults get life and work task categories (travel, job interviews, complaints, small talk).
18 RULES LANGUAGE. Kids: a Turkish rule card for the teacher to read, plus pictograms; student-facing strings are tiny English ('Your turn!'). Arena: an English rule card with a Turkish toggle. Adults: English on the student screen, Turkish in the teacher chrome.

12-13-YEAR-OLDS. Arena exists for them:
- Never show them cartoon animals, a talking mascot, 'Good job, superstar!' or pastel colours.
- Frame it as a 'Challenge' or 'Match'.
- Ownership: in 10 s, teams pick an emblem, a colour and a 3-word motto.
- Streaks, combo meters, stats and a dark theme are the defaults.
- The Nazik protections stay underneath: no public last place, no individual naming, and a floor at zero.
Arena is auto-suggested when the grade is 6+ or when the teacher ticks 'Bu sınıf çocuksu görsellerden hoşlanmıyor'. The reverse also works: a 9-year-old B1 class (private school) keeps Oyun Parkı, because level and skin are independent.

MIXED ABILITY. A 'Kolay / Orta / Zor' dial inside each group shifts the word-band mix (e.g. A2-Kolay = 60% A1 words) and hint availability without changing the skin. 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır' drops one level, because MEB's nominal levels often overstate public-school classes.

IMPLEMENTATION. AudienceProfile = merge(levelProfile[A1..B2], audienceMode[park|arena|studio], rulePack[nazik|standart], classOverrides). Every game and the LLM generator read the same merged object. The setup screen shows it as one summary line ('A2 Genç · Oyun Parkı · Nazik · Süresiz · 20 dk') with a 'Değiştir' link.

platformFeatures.feature: Sınıf Kabuğu: shared shell and game plugin contract
platformFeatures.detail: One module that every game plugs into. A game supplies only: id, Turkish name, content needs (item types and minimum counts), three rule variants (park/arena/studio), a pure reducer reduce(state, action) and a board renderer. The shell supplies everything else: setup, teams, scores, judging, timer, sound, keys, freeze, pause, save/resume, presenter sync, end screen and print. State = seed + content pack + settings + an append-only action log. Undo, autosave, resume, presenter mirroring and replay all come from that one log. Build order: shell, content schema and validator, one game ported (the existing /sinif-oyunu, fixing its Esc, undo, targeting and casing bugs), then the other games.

platformFeatures.feature: Hızlı Başlat: one-screen setup in under 60 s (under 10 s on repeat)
platformFeatures.detail: Flow: game card, then a sheet with four rows of big chips: Sınıf profili/Grup (8 groups) → Konu → Takımlar (2-8, default 4) → Süre (10/20/30/40, plus Kurs 60/90), then a big 'Başlat'. 'Geçen dersteki gibi başla' pre-fills the last group, pack, team names and length for that class profile. Everything else sits folded under 'Gelişmiş'. The 'Başlat' click also enters fullscreen, takes the wake lock and unlocks audio (all three need a user gesture).

platformFeatures.feature: Universal content pack schema and 'Başka oyunda oyna'
platformFeatures.detail: One item schema with these fields: type (word/mcq/tf/sentence/pair/category/taboo/prompt/survey), term/prompt, answer, alternatives[], distractors[], hint ladder, whyTr, exampleEn, ipa, tr, imageKey, level, topic, teenSafe, notPicturable, teacherNote. Each game declares its needs (e.g. Codenames-type 25 words, board game 36+). A pack page shows 'Bu paketle oynanabilir' badges and greys out games it can't feed, with a 'Eksikleri tamamla' button (fields derived from words.js first, the LLM second). After any game: 'Aynı paketle başka oyun' and 'Yeni sorularla rövanş'.

Tabs: Hazır kategoriler (icon grid filtered by group), MEB ünitesi (grade → theme → sub-theme, with grade mapped to group automatically), Languago bankası (grammar_mcq units, idioms, readings), Kendi listen (paste words or a Quizlet/Wordwall TSV; auto-filled with TR, IPA, example and level from words.js) and Yapay zekâ ile (free prompt in Turkish or English). Kütüphanem (saved packs) is pinned first once it has items.

platformFeatures.feature: AI generation with 'Anladığım şu' confirmation, validators and preview/edit
platformFeatures.detail: The prompt goes to a game-specific endpoint (not the Material Maker prompt, which forces academic contexts from B1 up and has no age flag). Group, level and counts come only from UI allowlists; the teacher's text is treated as data. A fast planner call returns editable chips (topic, focus, grammar target, group) before full generation. Settings: thinking off, strict JSON, one retry. Code-side validators check: exactly one correct MCQ key; the answer is present in the options; no key cue (longest option, a/an agreement); taboo lists don't contain or make the target impossible; no Turkish letters in Hangman answers; word caps; CEFR level check against words.js (off-level words underlined with a level badge); dedupe; teenSafe. The preview table shows per-item ✎ / ✕ / ↻ Benzeri / Daha kolay / Daha zor, and an 'AI' badge. Approval is required before children see the pack. Output is rendered only with textContent.

platformFeatures.feature: Derse hazırlan: pre-generate, cache, export, offline
platformFeatures.detail: Packs are saved to IndexedDB and optionally to the teacher account. They export and import as .languago.json (USB stick) and share as a short code. The library shows 'Çevrimdışı hazır ✓'. If AI fails in class, it offers the closest built-in pack. Needed because the limiter is 5 generations per 10 min per IP, a whole school shares one IP, and generation can take 20-180 s.

words.js has no topic tags. Add a reviewed topic index (YLE-style 20 topics, A2 Key/B1 Preliminary topic headings, MEB units), noun-sense entries for homographs (chair, arm, face...), about 450 missing children's words, simple definitions (10 words or fewer, using only A1-A2 words) and an imageKey into one self-hosted, licence-checked SVG icon set. Native emoji render differently per OS on projectors.

platformFeatures.feature: Audience profile engine (level × mode × rule pack)
platformFeatures.detail: Merges the level profile, the Oyun Parkı/Arena/Stüdyo mode, the Nazik/Standart rules and class overrides into one object that all games and the generator read. The setup screen shows a one-line summary with 'Değiştir'. The group label never appears on the student screen. Full dial table in ageAdaptation.

2-8 teams. Each team = an Okabe-Ito colour + a shape (circle, triangle, square, star, hexagon, diamond, heart, cross) + mascot/emblem + name, always shown together on the score chips, turn band, claimed tiles, tokens and timer ring. The yellow team uses dark ink and an outline. A per-skin name generator gives one-tap names: kids get alliterative English adjective-animal pairs, Arena gets emblem names, adults get cities/coffee drinks/grammar puns. Free typing is allowed. Brand orange and teal stay out of the play area so the team colours own the screen. Names render inside lang='en' with locale-independent uppercase (no 'QUİZ KİDS').

platformFeatures.feature: Score tray with undo/redo and history
platformFeatures.detail: Always visible. Tapping a team opens +1/+5/+10/-1/-5/-10, 'Tam değer gir' and rename. Every change goes to a history list ('Mavi +10 · Soru 7') with Ctrl+Z/Backspace undo and redo. An undo animates the points flying back, so the class sees the correction. In Nazik mode scores are floored at 0. H hides scores until the end.

Big buttons with icon + word + key: ✓ Doğru (C), ½ Kısmen (half points, e.g. 'say it as a full sentence'), ✗ Yanlış (W), ⤼ Geç (0, never Esc). In 'Herkes cevaplar' mode it is a multi-select of correct teams, then Enter. 'Cevabı kabul et' accepts an unlisted answer and adds it to that pack's alternatives. Red/green is never used alone.

İpucu 1 → İpucu 2 → Cevap (R) → 'Neden?' (Turkish one-line rule) → optional 'Bonus: make a sentence'. Each hint step shows its point cost before it is pressed. The reveal card shows the word, IPA (stress marked), TR and a speaker button.

A ring in the active team's colour. T pauses, +10 s button, 'Süresiz' option, options delay, huddle timer. At 0 a soft chime plays (never an alarm). Quiet ticking in the last 5 s is optional. Clicking the ring edits the time live. No speed points anywhere.

NEXT: Space/Enter/PageDown/→. BACK: PageUp/←. 1-8: award to team n (Shift+n subtracts). 0: nobody. Ctrl+Z/Backspace: undo. '.' or B: freeze/blackout. F: fullscreen. M: sound cycle. T: timer. R: reveal. H: hint. ?: help overlay (printable). Esc is never bound to a game action because it exits fullscreen. Letter shortcuts are off in letter-input games (Hangman), which use an on-screen A-Z pad instead.

The whole turn becomes a linear sequence driven by ◀ ▶ only: question → think → reveal → 'who scored?' (NEXT cycles teams, '.' toggles) → next turn. The teacher can walk the room with only a clicker in hand.

During play, preventDefault on F5, Ctrl+R and Shift+F5, with a toast: 'Sayfa yenilenmedi, oyun kayıtlı (çıkmak için Menü)'. A beforeunload confirm while a game runs. A 'Tam ekrana dön' pill appears bottom-right when fullscreen is lost.

The action log is saved to localStorage after every action; a tiny 'Kaydedildi ✓' tick fades each time. On load: 'Kaldığın yerden devam et? 7-B · 14/24 karo · Mavi 60, Turuncu 45 · 12 dk önce' with a board thumbnail, [Devam] [Yeni oyun]. Named slots: 'Sonraki derse kaydet'. The save exports as a file as a backup, since school machines may wipe localStorage.

platformFeatures.feature: Fullscreen, wake lock and audio unlock
platformFeatures.detail: All three happen inside the Başlat click. The wake lock is re-requested on visibilitychange and shown as a small 'Ekran açık kalacak' sun icon. HTTPS-only APIs fall back silently.

On '.', B or S: a soft chime and a full-screen card with three variants: 'Hands on head ✋', a silent 5-4-3-2-1 dot countdown, or pure black. The timer is paused and the board hidden; any key resumes. Clicks don't leak through, so the teacher can annotate over it with Pardus Kalem.

Shows no answers. Contains: Devam, Kurallar, Ayarlar (dials live-editable), Takımlar (rename, move a player, add a team mid-game), Kaydet ve çık, Oyunu bitir (goes to the end screen, never just closes). Kids skin: the mascot sleeps. Arena: 'PAUSED'. Adults: a calm clock.

M cycles Tümü → Sadece efektler → Sessiz, remembered per device. Per-skin packs, each effect at most 1 s and loudness-normalised, music off by default for adults. 'Sessiz sınıf' preset (visual only). Every audio cue has a visual equivalent.

Sized in vh/vmin: question 6-8vh, options ≥4.5vh, smallest student label ≥2.5vh (the 8H floor, about 30 px at 1080p). Auto-fit shrinks only down to the floor, then splits the item. A−/A+ persists per class. An 'Arka sıra testi' screen. Two contrast modes, 'Aydınlık sınıf' (dark on cream) and 'Karartılmış sınıf' (light on navy). No thin fonts, no text on photos without a solid plate. Tested at 1280x720, 1080p and 4K@200%.

Student-tappable targets in the lower two-thirds, at least 64 px (80 px on ETAP) with 12 px gaps. Tap-select then tap-place instead of drag. No hover-only states. A 400 ms tap debounce with a visible ripple. No focused text inputs during play, so the ETAP keyboard never pops up. An optional 'Çocuk yüksekliği' layout lowers the grid and keypad further. No WebGL requirement; works on Chromium 117-class browsers.

Assumes a mirrored or single-screen board. Answers render only after R. 'Cevap anahtarını yazdır' prints a one-page key (number, answer, alternatives, teacher notes). A private word for describe/draw games uses a cover-screen flow ('Herkes gözlerini kapatsın' 3-2-1, word shows for 3 s, auto-hides), or a paper deck.

Turn flow: think ring, then 'Boards up!' / 'Show!' chime. Teams raise printed A-D cards or mini-whiteboards, or use TPR answering in kids mode. The teacher multi-selects the correct teams: the active team scores and other correct teams get small shadow points (or class-power points). A class-level '5/6 takım bildi' tally appears.

platformFeatures.feature: Kim cevaplıyor? seat-number spinner and captain badge
platformFeatures.detail: Students number off 1-6 inside each team (Numbered Heads Together). The spinner (at most 1.2 s) picks a number for the active team or all teams, avoids the same number twice in a row, and shows dots for numbers already used. A rotating captain badge (a crown for kids, an armband in Arena, 'Spokesperson' for adults). No names needed.

'Kaç dakikan var?' sizes the grid, question count and rounds from the audience pacing. A 'Son 5 dakika' banner turns the next round into the final round. The game always ends on the end screen before the bell. If the time runs out mid-round: 'Sonraki derse kaydet' or 'Şimdi bitir'.

Comeback (Kapalı/Hafif/Güçlü) and Harshness (Yeşil/Sarı/Kırmızı) dials sit on the setup screen with plain Turkish descriptions. Power cards are tick-able one by one. Cards that target a team make the acting team choose the target by tapping it (with confirmation), never auto-next. Power tiles look identical until opened. Seeded placement.

Podium or titles (depending on the audience). 'Words we met' with TTS, IPA and TR. A 'Kaçırılanlar' list (items answered wrong or skipped, with answer and 'Neden?') plus buttons: 'Yanlışları tekrar oyna' (a 2-minute mini-round), 'Yazdır' (worksheet and exit ticket) and 'Sonraki derse ısınma olarak kaydet'. Always ends with a 1-minute production prompt ('Use 3 of today's words in a sentence'). Class-level only; no per-student data.

All buttons, settings and rule cards are in Turkish; every learning item sits inside lang='en' elements for correct casing, hyphenation and TTS voice. toLocaleUpperCase('en') everywhere. Typed answers are normalised (ı→i, İ→I, UK/US spellings, contractions). The rule card has an 'English version' toggle.

Reduced motion (automatic from prefers-reduced-motion, plus a manual toggle) replaces flips and confetti with fades and stamps. 'Rahat okuma' (1.5 line spacing, cream background, fewer words per card, not a dyslexia font). Colour is never the only signal (shape + icon + word). Visible focus. Every action is keyboard-operable. aria-live announces score changes and turn changes.

Rosters and names stay only in this browser, or the class uses seat numbers only. Team names and rosters are never sent to the LLM or the server, and never put in URLs or share codes. A warning under the prompt box: 'Öğrenci adı veya kişisel bilgi yazmayın'. No voice recording. The noise meter (if used) processes audio locally.

Add to the sw.js precache (versioned): the game hub, shell and game bundles, sound packs, self-hosted fonts, the SVG icon set and the built-in banks. Single-domain assets with no third-party CDN at game time (school filters). A status pill: 'Çevrimdışı hazır' or 'İnternet yok, yerel içerikle devam', with no blocking modal. A help page 'Okul ağında açılmıyorsa' with a printable request for the school's BT sorumlusu.

platformFeatures.feature: Content safety layer for built-in banks
platformFeatures.detail: A teenSafe flag and blocklist over words.js, grammar_mcq and idioms (beer, wine, gun, drug, boyfriend, prison... plus adult contexts like boss or office). Unreviewed validator-warned items stay out of Genç packs. Kid-unsafe idioms ('kill two birds...') are flagged. Optional LLM rewrite of an adult context into a school or home one.

platformFeatures.feature: Rules card, demo round and game-language slide
platformFeatures.detail: Every game opens with a 20-second rules card (pictograms + 3 lines) and an optional practice turn that does not score (the mascot hosts it in kids mode). A 'Game language' slide lists level-scaled sentence frames ('Is there an E?', 'I think it's... because...') that stay on a bottom strip during play.

Every game shows 'Tahta kodu: MANGO-42'. The code is built from easy English nouns with no Turkish-only letters, so reading it aloud is micro-practice. Entering the code recreates the same board, order and power-tile placement for a parallel class. Replaces Math.random in the current page with the existing seeded builder.

Print CSS / the existing PDF route, black-and-white friendly (shapes + patterns, not just colour). A-D answer cards (big letter + shape + pattern, seat number on the back) and the answer key are must-level. Also: team name tents, a paper scoresheet, flashcards, taboo and bingo decks with IDs, board sheets (A3), certificates and a 4-per-page exit ticket. A 'Projeksiyon yok' mode makes the app a teacher-only control panel.

'Projeksiyon penceresini aç' opens an audience window linked by BroadcastChannel (offline, no server). The laptop shows the answer, 'Neden?', teacher notes, the next item and all controls. If screen.isExtended is false, a one-line guide: 'Windows: Win+P → Genişlet'. In Chromium, 'Projeksiyona yerleştir' uses the Window Management API. The audience window receives only redacted public state.

platformFeatures.feature: Interludes: stirrers, settlers and brain breaks
platformFeatures.detail: Offered between rounds, or on the 'Çok gürültülü' / 'Çok uykulu' buttons. A 45 s stirrer (TPR actions from the pack's verbs, 'Simon says' with no elimination) or a 60 s settler (a silent picture puzzle, whisper round, or categorising). 'Çok gürültülü' also lowers the volume. Default on for Oyun Parkı, offered in Arena, off for Stüdyo.

'7-B · A2 Genç · Arena' stores: skin and dials, team name set, roster (numbers or local names), last packs played ('Bu paketi 2 kez oynadınız'), the missed-items queue and the class album (stickers, defeated bosses, countries visited). No cross-lesson individual leaderboard; any progress view is class-level.

Paste a roster (kept locally) or use numbers. A name wheel with 'seçileni çıkar'. 'Rastgele dengeli takımlar' deals round-robin, 'Sıra sıra' makes teams by desk rows. Students can be moved between teams mid-game without changing scores. The result is projectable or printable.

speechSynthesis with an en-GB/en-US voice picker, speed 0.8/1.0, and a slower 0.6 on long-press. Automatic for A1/A2 Genç, a speaker button elsewhere. Hidden if no English voice exists, with 'Öğretmen okur' mode as fallback. Tested in Chrome and Edge on Windows.
Missed items return later in the same game, and in kids mode as 'rescue' items that are worth a little more. In the RPG they become 'lost words' to rescue for HP.

During speaking games the teacher taps N to jot an overheard error (typed on the laptop, or chosen from a list of common Turkish-L1 errors). At the end an anonymous 'Let's fix these' slide appears, with no names.
Visible only in the presenter view and on the printed key: a common Turkish-speaker error for the item, a follow-up speaking question and a CEFR tag.

platformFeatures.feature: MEB curriculum mapping and plan note
platformFeatures.detail: Grade → group auto-map (2-4 A1 Genç, 5-6 A1/A2 Genç, 7-8 A2 Genç) with 'Bir seviye kolaylaştır'. The curriculum version is stored per grade and school year, because of the transition between the old units and TYMM (verify against current textbooks). 'Plan notu' exports a Turkish paragraph (tema, hedef yapılar, etkinlik, süre, değerler) for the günlük plan.
Kolay / Orta / Zor shifts the word-band mix, timer length and hint availability without changing the skin or level.

One tap on 'Bu soruyu gizle' removes a bad item for the rest of the game and from this teacher's future packs. Accepted overrides are remembered per pack. Items missed by more than 80% of teams, or overridden twice, are flagged for review.

'Sınıf Oyunları' cards with generic Turkish names (no trademarked names or art). Each card shows chips ('~15 dk · 2-8 takım · A1-B2 · Genç ✓'), a 3-second looping preview (static when reduced motion is on) and 'Bu paketle oynanabilir' when a pack is selected.
A 20-second tour points at Başlat, puan, geri al, dondur and bitir, plus a printable A5 'Kısayol kartı' with a drawing of a clicker showing which button does what.

A durable per-teacher quota stored in Supabase, because the in-memory limiter resets per serverless instance. Shows 'Bu ay 18/150 AI paketi'. Before generating, it suggests existing packs ('Benzer hazır paket var').
Chain 2-3 games on one pack in stir/settle order (e.g. warmer → main game → cooler) with a total-time estimate that fits 40 minutes.

Pair with a 4-digit code or QR (Supabase Realtime). Gives next/judge/score/undo/freeze and a SECRET screen (answers, charades words). Off by default, and never required: MEB rules discourage phones in class.

platformFeatures.feature: Optional QR join (adults and private courses only)
platformFeatures.detail: QR plus a 6-digit code, no logins, names picked from a generated list. Devices show the question and options. Late join on. The server never sends the key before reveal. Hidden for Genç groups.
Kids mode, off by default. A loudness bar from the laptop mic during huddles; teams earn a 'Quiet bonus' star for staying under the line. Processed locally, nothing recorded.
Teams write 2 items on paper. The teacher types them into a quick form with an AI 'fix grammar' button, and the class plays its own deck.
Kahoot-style spreadsheet import. Library tabs Benim / Okulum / Herkese açık, with only teacher-approved packs public, a report button and 'Kopyala ve düzenle'.
For the RPG and long board games. The class keeps XP, items and the boss's remaining HP, and resumes with a 'Previously on...' recap card.

classroomPrinciples: One screen, no student logins. Every game is fully playable from the teacher's laptop and projector. Paper, a second window, phones and QR are optional add-ons, never requirements (MEB bans student phones in state schools).
The teacher is host and judge. Judging is one tap, correcting is one tap (undo), and the teacher can override any rule, score or item mid-game.
Everyone answers, one team scores. Every turn includes a whole-class response moment so 25 students are never just waiting.
Accuracy over speed. No speed points anywhere; timers are visual, pausable, extendable and switchable off.
Nobody is ever out. 'Out' becomes helper, ghost, asleep or a lost heart, and the student keeps practising.
Kind by default, harsh only by choice. Luck and power cards are behind visible dials; kids get only positive effects, and a team-targeting card always lets the players pick the target.
Teams are ranked, individuals never. Students are called by seat number, not name; scores live inside one game; any long-term progress is class-level and cooperative.
Built for the back row. The 8H text floor, high contrast, no information carried by colour alone, and readable on a washed-out projector.
Learn the controls once. Same shell, same keys, same judge bar and same freeze button in every game, so the rules explanation is only about the new mechanic.
Adapt the rules, not just the skin. Kids' variants are stripped rulesets with pictures and audio; 12-14s get the Arena look, not cartoons; adults get strategy and relevance.
Content first, games second. One validated pack plays in any game; AI content is previewed and approved before children see it.
Prepare at home, play in class. Nothing in a lesson waits on the network or the LLM; everything works offline after the first load.
Short rounds, a fixed ending and a rhythm of stirring and settling. The game always reaches its end screen before the bell.
Every game is a lesson. The reveal teaches (why, pronunciation, TR), and the end screen turns misses into the next warmer or a worksheet.
Privacy by design. No student data leaves the browser, and nothing personal is asked of students.
Turkish for the teacher, English for the learning, marked with the correct lang attribute.
pitfallsToAvoid: Binding game actions to Esc. It exits fullscreen; the current /sinif-oyunu skips a turn on Esc.
Losing a game to F5 or Ctrl+R from a clicker or a crash. Intercept, autosave every action, offer resume.
Leaking answers on a mirrored projector or a single-screen ETAP board. Presenter view must be optional, never assumed.
Power cards that auto-target 'the next team' (current code) or reset a child's score to zero. The acting team chooses the target; kids get green cards only.
No undo or score editor. One misclick or a dispute then becomes permanent.
Projector text sized for laptops (17 px options). Anything below about 4.5vh fails the back row.
Colour-only team identity or red/green-only right/wrong. About 8% of boys can't tell them apart, and projectors wash colours out.
lang='tr' plus CSS uppercase turning English i into İ (QUİZ, WİN). This is critical in Hangman and in team names.
Speed points, buzzers and 'first to shout' rules. The same 2-3 fast students dominate and noise escalates.
Turn-only games where one team works and the rest idle.
Elimination of students or teams, in any game.
Babyish visuals, talking mascots or 'Good job, superstar!' for 12-14s and adults. The group label (A1 Genç) must never appear on the student screen.
Over-celebration: long confetti and loud sounds on every answer raise noise and tire the class. Keep the big effects for the finale.
Live AI generation in class. The limiter is 5 per 10 min per IP, a school shares one IP, and generation can take 30 s or more. Pre-generate and cache.

Trusting LLM output without validation: two correct options, wrong keys, off-level words, taboo lists that forbid the answer, adult topics in kids' packs. Also rendering its output with innerHTML (XSS once packs are shared).
Reusing the Material Maker prompt, which forces academic contexts from B1 up and has no age flag.
Assuming words.js can drive categories as-is. It has no topics or images, often keeps the rare verb sense (chair, arm), and has adult words in the A1-A2 lists.
Drag-and-drop, hover states and targets near the top of a high-mounted board. Small hands can't reach or drag.
Focused text inputs during play on ETAP boards, which pop up the on-screen keyboard over the game.
Third-party CDNs, fonts or analytics at game time. School filters block them and connections drop.
Storing or sending student names (to the server, the LLM, URLs or share codes). A KVKK problem.
Persistent individual leaderboards or badges across lessons (Hanus & Fox: motivation and exam scores fell).
Games with no fixed end that overrun the bell, and long board games with no 'save for next lesson'.
Loud or looping sound by default in thin-walled schools. Mute must be one key.
Trademarked names or art (Monopoly, Jeopardy!, Millionaire, Taboo, Baamboozle, Among Us). Use generic Turkish names.
Reading-heavy screens for A1 Genç, whose MEB English is listening- and speaking-first. Pictures and audio must carry the meaning.
Relying on TTS alone. Voices vary by OS, and board speakers are weak or off; always keep 'Öğretmen okur' and visual equivalents.
Settings overload at setup. More than 4 decisions before Başlat and teachers abandon the tool; everything else goes behind 'Gelişmiş' with good defaults.
Brand orange in the play area clashing with the orange team. Keep chrome neutral during play.
detailIdeas: The active team's colour tints a thin frame around the whole screen, with its shape as a faint watermark in the corner, so the back row always knows whose turn it is without reading.
Points fly as a '+10' chip from the tile to the team's score, which rolls up like an odometer. On undo the chip visibly flies back, so the class sees the correction happen.
Board codes are easy English nouns plus a number ('MANGO-42', never Turkish-only letters), so reading the code to a colleague is itself a bit of English.
Kids' team names are alliterative English pairs (Brave Bears, Clever Cats, Happy Hippos). Tapping the name shows the Turkish ('Cesur Ayılar'), a tiny vocab lesson at setup.
Confetti at the finale falls in each team's colour AND shape (triangles for the triangle team). Reduced motion replaces it with a big static shape stamp.
The timer ring fades from team colour to neutral grey, never to red, and ends with a two-note marimba chime instead of a buzzer.
Every hint button shows its cost as a small badge ('−2') before it is pressed, so there are no surprise deductions.
Tapping any English word on a reveal card speaks it at 0.8x; a long press says it slowly at 0.6x, with the stressed syllable highlighted in the IPA.
When the teacher accepts an unlisted answer, a toast says 'Bu cevap pakete eklendi', and next time it is accepted automatically.
The NHT spinner shows a row of small seat dots under each team, filling in as each number answers, so everyone sees the turns are fair.
A captain badge rotates each round: a crown in Oyun Parkı, an armband in Arena, 'Spokesperson' text for adults.
In Oyun Parkı the mascot sleeps with a 'Zzz' on the pause screen and yawns awake when the game resumes. Arena pauses with a subtle scanline 'PAUSED', adults with a calm analogue clock.
The freeze screen ends with a 1-second 'Thank you!' before the board returns, modelling the classroom language.
When a team hasn't scored for three turns and comeback is on, a small wind icon appears by its chip ('Slipstream'), so the catch-up help is visible and not a hidden rig.
Ties: kids share the win with a 'Dream Team' title; adults and Arena get an automatic estimation tie-breaker ('How many items in this pack start with S?'), closest wins.
The end screen never says 'kaybeden'. Titles are computed from real stats: longest streak, fewest hints used, biggest comeback, most rescued words.
A cooperative 'Class Power' bar fills with every correct answer from any team. At the top it unlocks a whole-class dance break or bonus sticker, a shared goal above the team race.
Kids' class album: each finished game adds one sticker (a defeated monster, a visited town, a filled balloon) to the class's collection page, belonging to the class, not to any student.
On 23 Nisan the Oyun Parkı skin adds balloons and bunting. On 24 Kasım the end screen says 'Happy Teachers' Day!' to the teacher. It can be switched off in settings.
Gentle seasonal touches in the Oyun Parkı background (falling leaves in November, snow in January, spring flowers in April), synced to the real date, off with reduced motion.
The resume card shows a mini thumbnail of the board, the scores and '12 dk önce', so the teacher knows instantly it's the right class's game.
'Previously on...': resuming a saved long game in the next lesson opens with a 3-line recap and the scores, read aloud in kids mode.
The 'Arka sıra testi' screen is an eye-chart of English sentences; the teacher asks the back row 'Can you read line 3?', so even the calibration is English practice.
Printed A-D cards carry the letter, the on-screen shape and a B/W pattern (stripes, dots), plus the seat number on the back, so one card set serves both voting and the spinner.
Fold-able team name tents printed with the team emblem and shape stand on the desk groups, matching the on-screen chips.
The exit ticket prints 4 per A4 page with the 3 most-missed items, saving paper in schools with strict print quotas.
A tiny 'Kaydedildi ✓' tick fades after each action, and a small sun icon means the screen won't sleep. Quiet reassurance, never a modal.
Every tap on the smartboard shows a soft ripple, so children see it registered and don't bang the board twice (the 400 ms debounce catches the rest).
The keyboard help overlay ('?') draws a clicker and shows which button does what, and prints as an A5 card to keep by the laptop.
Game cards on the hub show honest chips ('~15 dk · 2-8 takım · A1-B2 · Genç ✓') and a 3-second silent preview loop.
The 'Herkes cevaplar' reveal plays a card-flip sound, and the class-level tally ('5/6 takım bildi') gives the teacher an instant check of understanding with no names.
A long press on Undo opens a timeline of the last 10 actions to jump back to any point after a dispute.
Each team gets one 'İtiraz' (challenge) card per game. Using it opens a teacher decision screen with the key and accepted answers side by side, which defuses arguments.
The 'Çok gürültülü' button drops the volume and offers a 60-second silent settler; 'Çok uykulu' offers a 45-second TPR stirrer built from the pack's own verbs.
A sentence-frame strip at the bottom of speaking turns ('I think it's ___ because ___.') changes with the level and fades away after 3 successful uses, as the scaffold becomes unnecessary.
A kids' wrong answer turns into a choral moment: the mascot says the word, a 'Say it with me!' bubble appears twice with a bouncing dot over each syllable.
Setup remembers the last 3 packs per class and warns gently ('7-B bu paketi geçen hafta oynadı, yeni sorularla mı?').
When fullscreen is lost, a small 'Tam ekrana dön' pill appears at the bottom right, never covering the board.
The first run greets the teacher once ('Hello, teacher!') in kids mode, then never again unless reset: welcoming, not nagging.
Team chips show a small '1 2 3 4 5 6' seat row in the team colour during 'Kim cevaplıyor?', so the chosen number lights up right where the team looks.

clusters.name: Kutu Avı 2.0 (Tile Board)
clusters.familiarAs: Baamboozle Classic / Classic Jr (rebuild of the existing /sinif-oyunu)
clusters.rationale: All three are the same hidden-tile team board: teams open numbered or picture tiles that hold a question or a power card. The best parts of each go in. From 0: a 'luck dial' for how chaotic power cards get. From 45: an animal-picture tile skin for kids and a wager-and-steal quiz night for adults. From 75: everyone answers at once, a random team member is picked to speak, and the teacher judges with one key. This is the reference game for the shared classroom shell. Teacher-requested.

clusters.name: Kelime Şehri / Hazine Adası (Monopoly-style Board)
clusters.familiarAs: Monopoly / Emlak Ticaret
clusters.rationale: One property-economy board. Teams roll, answer the square's question to buy a district, pay rent or answer to cut it, and answer harder items to build houses. Türkiye Turu (68) and City Tour (46, 80) are skins of the same engine, not separate games. Age adaptation: adults get a city tour with real-life tasks, trading and negotiation at B1+. Kids get Treasure Island, collecting treasures with no rent and no bankruptcy. Save-and-continue-next-lesson, real-dice input and a timed ending (80) fit how a real class runs. Teacher-requested.

clusters.name: Kelime Kurtar (Hangman without gallows + Çarkıfelek mode)
clusters.familiarAs: Hangman / Adam Asmaca, Wheel of Fortune (Çarkıfelek)
clusters.rationale: The same hidden-word, guess-a-letter mechanic. Wheel of Fortune (65) is already the adult mode in 18 and 47: spin, call consonants, buy vowels, solve a chunk or idiom, then USE it in a sentence. Clue ladders with paid steps (56, 77) use the fields words.js already has: emoji or Turkish, then the definition, then a gapped example, then IPA and audio. A big on-screen keyboard helps. Kids save a mascot's balloons, so there is no gallows. Teacher-requested.

clusters.name: Büyük Macera (Class Quest RPG)
clusters.familiarAs: Classroom RPG / D&D-lite / Classcraft / choose-your-own-adventure
clusters.rationale: The whole class is one party on a branching story map. Guild or hero teams have one special ability each. Every node is a scene written at the class's CEFR level plus a language challenge, the class votes at crossroads, and a co-op boss ends the run. Crossroads (39) is this game's story-and-vote layer, so it becomes a short 10-15 minute 'story-only' mode with multiple endings, not a separate game. For kids: 'befriend' creatures and no losing to classmates. For adults: persuasion and request encounters. Teacher-requested.

clusters.name: Milyoner Merdiveni (Millionaire Ladder)
clusters.familiarAs: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire / Kim Milyoner Olmak İster
clusters.rationale: A 10-15 step difficulty ladder with safe steps and three lifelines. The good ideas combine well: a relay order so each student takes one step (20), 'shadow play' so every other team answers on ABCD cards and nobody sits idle (50), and 'Sınıfa sor' using printed cards instead of phones (79). Kids get a shorter ladder with picture questions. B1+ gets 'why' justifications for lifeline choices.

clusters.name: Kategori Kapışması (Category Board)
clusters.familiarAs: Jeopardy / Factile
clusters.rationale: A category-by-value board with Daily Doubles and a wagered Final round. It is distinct from the tile board because categories and values are visible, so choosing strategically is the game. It combines buzz-in with an 'every team answers on whiteboards' mode that stops buzzer dominance (19, 76), and gives each team one challenge card. It adds question formation and short written answers.

clusters.name: Büyük Yarış (Everyone-Answers Race, with a League mode)
clusters.familiarAs: Blooket Racing / Kahoot team mode / board race / Süper Lig standings
clusters.rationale: Every team answers every question at the same moment on ABCD cards or mini-whiteboards, and correct teams move forward, so nobody waits. The weakest team gets a catch-up boost. Sınav Ligi (64) keeps the same simultaneous-answer core with a football skin and exam-style LGS/YDS items: an optional 'LGS rule', and a standings table that carries over from lesson to lesson. That makes it a mode, not a separate game. Kids get car or animal racers; adults get a league table.

clusters.name: Sınıf Birliği: Lav & Canavar (Whole-Class Co-op vs. the Game)
clusters.familiarAs: Gimkit The Floor Is Lava / Classcraft Boss Battle / Blooket Monster Brawl
clusters.rationale: The whole class plays against the game, not against each other. Correct answers build the tower above the rising lava (6) or damage a boss (37), and wrong answers let the threat advance. The lava and the boss are skins of one mechanic. It works as a single-lesson co-op review with roles, phases and a spoken final phase. That makes it distinct from the multi-lesson RPG, and it suits mixed-ability or anxious classes.

clusters.name: Anlat-Çiz-Canlandır (Taboo / Hot Seat / Pictionary / Charades)
clusters.familiarAs: Tabu, Hot Seat / Backs to the Board, Heads Up, Sessiz Sinema, Pictionary, Activity
clusters.rationale: One core: one player guesses a secret word while the team gets it across. Several raw ideas already combine describe, draw and act (49, 67, 73), so Draw or Act (22) is a spinner mode, not a separate game. The literal-idiom Pictionary (61) becomes an idiom deck: the screen shows the funny literal Turkish from the 'lit' field in idioms.js. Forbidden words are auto-proposed from words.js and scale from mime plus 3 words (A1 teen) to 5 forbidden words (B2) (57). A Turkish-slip penalty key (67), the secret card on a phone (21), a pausable 60-second timer and whole-class reverse charades mean no child performs alone.

clusters.name: Sahtekar Kim? (Social Deduction)
clusters.familiarAs: Spyfall / The Chameleon / Mafia-Werewolf (Vampir Köylü) / Among Us / Gimkit Trust No One
clusters.rationale: Hidden roles, discussion and a justified vote. The quick mode is Word Chameleon (7): everyone but the impostor knows the word, each gives one clue, then the group votes. The full mode is Town Mystery or Impostor Crew (29, 44): phones deal secret roles, a narrator voice guides the night, repair tasks are review questions, and nobody can vote without justifying it in English. It is a non-violent 'thief' theme for kids. It targets opinion, agreeing and disagreeing, and speculation modals.

clusters.name: Konuşma Çarkı (Speaking Wheel, Story Dice & Just a Minute)
clusters.familiarAs: Wordwall Random Wheel / Open the Box / Baamboozle Story Dice / BBC Just a Minute / Would You Rather
clusters.rationale: A speaking-first prompt engine: spin for a speaker and a topic, then talk. 10 already lists Just a Minute, so the fluency challenge with fair hesitation, repetition and off-topic challenges (28) is its competitive mode. Story Dice and Chain Story give co-operative storytelling in the target grammar. The warmers pack (34: Would You Rather, Chain Story) supplies the calm 3-10 minute starters and settlers. Its Bingo and Fact-or-Fib parts are covered by c16 and c27. Kids get picture dice and sentence frames; adults get 60-second opinion topics.

clusters.name: Hafıza Kartları (Memory Match)
clusters.familiarAs: Memory / Pairs / Concentration (Wordwall Matching Pairs, Baamboozle+ Memory)
clusters.rationale: Turn-based flipping of two cards to find a pair: word and picture, word and definition, EN and TR, verb forms, or collocation halves. Using the pair in a sentence earns a bonus. It is a calm, memory-driven dynamic unlike any quiz. Kids get picture-picture and picture-word pairs; adults get collocations and irregular verbs.

clusters.name: Dörtle! & XOX Arena (Four in a Row / Tic-Tac-Toe / Beehive)
clusters.familiarAs: Connect Four / Tic-Tac-Toe (XOX) / Blockbusters
clusters.rationale: A territory game: to claim a column, square or hex a team must answer that cell's challenge, and blocking and forking make strategy matter as much as knowledge. The three ideas are the same game on different grids. Kids get a 3x3 grid; adults get a 5x5 grid or the beehive, with sentence-production cells at B1+.

clusters.name: Hız Avı (Swat & Spot Speed Race)
clusters.familiarAs: Slap the Board / Whack-a-Mole / Balloon Pop / Dobble (Spot It!)
clusters.rationale: Both are speed-recognition races on the projector. One student per team races to touch or name the right item: floating fish, balloons or moles when a clue is read or played (13), or the one item shared by two Dobble cards (33). These are two modes of one fast, physical, listening-and-recognition game. Kids get pictures; adults get definitions and audio clues.

clusters.name: Şifre Kır (Class Codebreaker Wordle)
clusters.familiarAs: Wordle / Flippity WordMaster
clusters.rationale: Deduction from letter feedback: teams guess whole words and read green and yellow tiles. This is a different core from Hangman's letter-guessing and Kelime Oyunu's definition-to-word, and it is calm, reasoning-heavy spelling practice. Kids get 4-letter topic words and a picture clue after 4 tries; adults get 5-6 letters.

clusters.name: Kelime Tombala (Listening Bingo)
clusters.familiarAs: Bingo / Turkish Tombala ('Çinko!')
clusters.rationale: Everyone plays at once on unique printed or phone cards while the screen calls clues: audio, picture, definition, gapped sentence or synonym, by level. 'Çinko' and 'Tombala' are verified instantly by the card's ID. It is the calm 'settler' for big or noisy classes, and a key listening game.

clusters.name: Takım Sırası (Sort & Order Relay)
clusters.familiarAs: Wordwall Group Sort / Rank Order / Unjumble, as a team relay
clusters.rationale: A physical relay: one member per team steps up for each move to sort items into groups, unjumble a sentence or rank items. It is the only game focused on syntax and word order, with a movement-based team dynamic.

clusters.name: Gizli Ajan Kelimeler (Codenames)
clusters.familiarAs: Codenames
clusters.rationale: Spymasters see a secret key on a phone and give one-word clues so their team can find its agents on a 5x5 word or picture grid while avoiding the trap. Nothing else trains lexical networks and team negotiation this way. Kids use the picture version.

clusters.name: İsim-Şehir STOP! (Category Rush)
clusters.familiarAs: İsim-Şehir-Hayvan / Scattergories / Stop the Bus
clusters.rationale: The same game in all three ideas, and every Turkish student already knows it. A letter is spun, teams write one word per level-appropriate category, and any team can shout STOP. Unique answers score double, and answers are checked live against words.js (level badge, Turkish meaning, spelling hint). It is one of the few writing and spelling-production games.

clusters.name: Amiral Battı: Grammar Fleet (Battleship)
clusters.familiarAs: Amiral Battı / Battleship
clusters.rationale: Rows and columns are word sets, so to fire a shot a team must SAY the correct sentence or question built from the coordinate. It is controlled spoken-accuracy practice (question forms, short answers) inside a strategy game. Kids get simple 'Is it a...?' grids.

clusters.name: Sınıf Diyor ki (Family Feud / Class Survey)
clusters.familiarAs: Family Feud / Family Fortunes / Ailece Birlikte
clusters.rationale: Teams guess the top answers to 'Name something...', using data from a live 3-minute phone survey of this class or a generated '100 people' set. Face-offs, three strikes and steals follow. It is a distinct speaking-and-listening show format with survey and reporting language at B1+ ('Most of us...').

clusters.name: Cümle Mezadı (Grammar Auction)
clusters.familiarAs: Grammar Auction (Languago roadmap G06)
clusters.rationale: Teams bid a budget on sentences they believe are correct, then win money back by correcting the wrong ones they bought. The sentences are built automatically from the grammar MCQ banks: the key gives the correct version and the distractors give learner errors. It is the error-correction game. Kids get coins and picture sentences with an A1-A2 grammar focus.

clusters.name: Hazine Yolu (Race Board: Ask-Tell Ladders & Treasure Map)
clusters.familiarAs: Snakes and Ladders (Yılan Merdiven) / pirate treasure-hunt board / Mario Party
clusters.rationale: A race-to-the-finish board, as opposed to c02's property economy. Teams move and trigger Ask, Tell or Quiz squares. A correct answer climbs a ladder or charms a snake away, and on the map variant teams choose risky shortcuts or safe paths and hit event squares. Snakes and Ladders is the kids' skin; the treasure map or trek is the older one.

clusters.name: Tik Tak Bomba (Hot Potato Word Chain)
clusters.familiarAs: Pass the Bomb / Hot Potato (Sıcak Patates)
clusters.rationale: A whole-class spoken warmer: a category or letter chunk appears, a hidden timer ticks, and each student says one valid word and passes the object. Whoever holds it at the bang takes a penalty card, and nobody is eliminated. It has a unique physical, rapid-retrieval dynamic for any age.

clusters.name: Kaçış Odası (Escape Room + Tıkla-Keşfet command mode)
clusters.familiarAs: Breakout EDU / Genially escape room / point-and-click 'escape the room'
clusters.rationale: The class escapes a locked room before the countdown by solving language puzzles for the lock codes. The engine computes the codes from correct answers, never the LLM (71). The point-and-click room (42) is the same escape goal played by spoken commands ('Look under the bed', 'Use the key on the box'), so it becomes a command-driven mode for imperatives and prepositions. Kids get a toy room; adults get a lab or hotel.

clusters.name: Dedektif Dosyası (Detective Mystery)
clusters.familiarAs: Cluedo / murder-mystery party / Guess Who?
clusters.rationale: Teams interview on-screen suspects, search locations, 'lab-test' clues with language challenges and cross off who, where and how on a deduction grid, then must justify the accusation. Code guarantees exactly one suspect fits; the LLM only writes the case in the target grammar. Kids get a 'missing cake' case; adults get past-tense and deduction-modal cases.

clusters.name: Sorgu Odası (Alibi & Two Truths and a Lie)
clusters.familiarAs: The Alibi game / Two Truths and a Lie / Would I Lie to You?
clusters.rationale: Real people in the hot seat are questioned to catch a lie. This differs from c26, where the suspects are generated and on screen. Pairs invent an alibi and are questioned separately while the screen tracks answers side by side and flashes contradictions (43). Alternatively, the teacher or a volunteer plays a generated character with three statements, and teams spend limited questions to find the lie (74). It targets question formation and past continuous.

clusters.name: Issız Ada (Survival Council)
clusters.familiarAs: Lost at Sea ranking / The Oregon Trail / Blooket Crazy Kingdom
clusters.rationale: Seven days on an island or a broken space station. Each day brings an event, teams argue for decisions, shared meters rise and fall, and challenges earn supplies. It is the main discussion game for suggesting, agreeing, disagreeing and conditionals. Kids get a friendly island with picture choices.

clusters.name: Gizli Görev (Secret Mission Info-Gap Pairs)
clusters.familiarAs: Info-gap role-play cards / secret-mission speaking game
clusters.rationale: The only pair-work game. Partners hold secret role cards with hidden information and three goals each, must talk to complete them, adapt to a twist card midway, and tick off each other's goals. It focuses on functional language and runs quietly, with the whole class in pairs at once.

clusters.name: Kelime Oyunu: English Edition
clusters.familiarAs: Kelime Oyunu (tv2 word show)
clusters.rationale: A familiar Turkish TV format. A ladder of words runs from short to long, each with a definition clue, teams race one overall clock, and buying a letter lowers the word's value. The core is producing the word from its definition under time pressure, which differs from Hangman's letter-guessing and Wordle's feedback deduction.

clusters.name: Telaffuz Labirenti (Pronunciation Maze & Minimal Pairs)
clusters.familiarAs: Pronunciation maze / minimal pairs / four corners (TYMM curriculum games)
clusters.rationale: The dedicated pronunciation game. The class steers an avatar through a word maze by choosing and saying words with the target sound, aimed at contrasts Turkish speakers mix up (for example /v/-/w/, /æ/-/e/ and /θ/). 'Ses Avcısı' adds a minimal-pairs listening round.

clusters.name: Okuma Dedektifleri (Running Dictation Reading Relay)
clusters.familiarAs: Running dictation / reading race
clusters.rationale: Leveled texts (about 50 words at A1, about 150 at B2) are cut into evidence cards. Teams collect them by running to printed cards or watching timed flashes, write them down, answer questions and point to the proving sentence. It is the main reading, dictation and writing game, with a movement dynamic.

gaps.gap: No whole-class movement or physical-response game (Simon Says, Stand up if..., Four Corners, Opinion Line).
gaps.why: For 9-11-year-olds, TPR is the default warmer and brain break, and the rule table already assumes TPR ('stand for A, sit for B'). Right now it exists only as a response method, and no game is built around it. It is also the cheapest way to meet the 'whole-class response every turn' rule. See x01.

gaps.gap: No mingle game and almost no pair work that A1 Genç can do.
gaps.why: c29 is the only pair game, and its role cards are text-heavy, which breaks the 0-4 word cap for A1 Genç. Find Someone Who (roadmap G15) and the picture info-gap (G02, G14) were dropped from the clusters. Whole-class simultaneous speaking is the dynamic that raises talk time most in classes of 30-40. See x05 and x04 mode 3.

gaps.gap: Listening to connected speech is missing. Every listening moment is a single item (bingo calls, swat clues, minimal pairs).
gaps.why: No game has students hear a sentence or text and rebuild it (dictation, dictogloss, whisper chain). Roadmap G04 (Dikteyle yeniden kurma) was lost in the merge. Also missing is a 'Dinleme modu' that hides a text item and plays it aloud, so that c01, c05, c07 and c32 could run listening versions. See x03.

gaps.gap: No word-building game from a letter pool (Bir Kelime Bir İşlem's word round, Boggle, anagram, Scrabble-like).
gaps.why: Every Turkish student knows 'Bir Kelime' (8 letters plus a joker, longest word wins), and teachers already project home-made versions of it in school. It trains spelling and vocabulary retrieval in a way that Hangman, Wordle and Kelime Oyunu don't. See x02.

gaps.gap: Visual attention and memory games (What's Missing / Kim's game, Spot the Difference, picture dictation, eyewitness) are missing.
gaps.why: 'What's Missing' was part of raw idea 34, but the c11 merge only reassigned Bingo and Fact-or-Fib, so it silently disappeared. These are standard ESL projector games for kids, and they are the natural home for there is/are, prepositions and past continuous. See x04.

gaps.gap: Many roadmap mechanics were dropped without a decision: G03 jigsaw reading, G05 collocation domino, G09 map-directions info-gap, G17 stress changes meaning, G20 building a text from discourse chunks, G21 register transformation, G23 predict-and-update reading, G25 co-op logic puzzle, G26 word-family building, G28 repair duel, G30 4/3/2 retell.
gaps.why: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md lists 30 mechanics, and several have no cluster. The teacher will notice. Either map each one as a mode (G05 as a domino mode in c12, G23 and G03 in c32, G25 in c26 or c25, G09 in c29 or x04, G30 and G24 in c11, G26 in c22 or x02) or mark it as deliberately out of scope.

gaps.gap: Writing beyond single words is thin, and the 'use it in a sentence' bonuses have no content type.
gaps.why: Written production only appears in c19 (single words), c15 (spelling), c30 and c32 (copying). c03, c12, c20 and c30 all award 'use it in a sentence' points, but no item type holds the words to use, the target structure, model answers or a checklist, so the judge bar has nothing to show. Add a 'build' item {mustUse[], target, models[], checklist[]}.

gaps.gap: There is no honest feasibility check for 7-9-year-olds and pre-literate A1 Genç.
gaps.why: In MEB grades 2-3, English is mostly listening and speaking. c10, c15, c18 (word version), c19, c22, c26, c28, c29, c30 and c32 all depend on reading or writing. The requirement says every game works for young learners, so each cluster needs a declared no-reading variant (picture Codenames, oral STOP, pointing instead of writing) or a visible 'from age 10' tag in the hub.

gaps.gap: Most cluster rationales describe only kids and adults, not the Arena (12-14) variant.
gaps.why: Snakes and Ladders (c23), Treasure Island (c02), picture Memory (c12) and balloon Hangman all read as childish to 13-year-olds, and the design says Arena must never feel like kids' stuff. Each cluster needs an explicit Arena theme plus rule change (for example c02 'Theme-park tycoon' with no rent, c23 'Parkour run', c12 'Card Clash' with streaks) before build.

gaps.gap: High-school classes (15-18) and teen-safety outside 'Genç' are not covered.
gaps.why: teenSafe is tied to the Genç groups (7-14), but meb-9-11-tymm and the lise classes will select B1/B2 and get Stüdyo with adult topics (rent, salary, office) and Red harshness. words.js contains beer, wine, drunk, casino, gun and kill. Make content safety a third independent axis ('Okul güvenli'), on by default unless the teacher ticks 'Yetişkin kursu'.

gaps.gap: Several mechanics depend on phones, but students can't use them.
gaps.why: MEB has banned phones in classrooms by circular since 2023-24, and KVKK makes collecting data from minors sensitive. The affected pieces are c09 (secret card on a phone), c10 (roles dealt to phones), c18 (spymaster key on a phone), c21 (3-minute phone survey) and c16 (phone cards). Every one needs a no-phone path: printed seeded key cards, a 'heads down, row starters look' peek screen, the teacher's Kumanda, or a hand-count survey.

gaps.gap: The games are not planned for real classroom hardware (FATİH smartboards running Pardus ETAP).
gaps.why: These are Linux boards, and ETAP 23 has known touch-calibration problems. They may have no colour-emoji font and no English Web Speech voice. media.emoji must therefore render from a self-hosted SVG set (Twemoji CC BY 4.0, OpenMoji CC BY-SA or Noto Apache-2.0), built-in banks need pre-rendered audio, and the hub should be tested on an ETAP board.

gaps.gap: The picture layer that A1/A2 Genç depend on doesn't exist yet.
gaps.why: words.js has no emoji or image fields at all. The design requires an imageKey on every A1/A2 Genç item, and more than 10 kids variants need pictures (c12, c13, c14, c16, c18, c23, x01, x04). A curated sticker set of about 800-1,200 concepts, plus a concept-to-word mapping, is a prerequisite and should be scheduled first.

gaps.gap: The word bank is too thin to check open-answer games.
gaps.why: words.js has about 5,670 lemmas and no inflected forms (went, children and apples are missing). It has no countries, cities or first names (only months and days are capitalised). It holds only about 750 five-letter and about 680 four-letter lemmas across all levels. c19 needs countries and cities, c15 must validate guesses, and c24 and x02 accept any word, so they all need an inflection generator, an irregular-forms table, a proper-noun list (countries, capitals, Turkish cities, first names) and the accepted-answer memory.

gaps.gap: Copying Oxford definitions is a licensing risk.
gaps.why: The words.js metadata says the A1-C1 definitions are 'Oxford-derived', and the content model allows 'Oxford text if 18 words or fewer'. A length limit is not a licence, and languago.site is public. Rewrite defEasy/def (an LLM paraphrase plus review) or build on Wiktionary/WordNet text with attribution.

gaps.gap: Pronunciation content has no verified source for generated words, and speech checking for children needs a privacy decision.
gaps.why: An LLM's IPA is unreliable, so sound items for LLM topics need words.js IPA or CMUdict, and unverified items should be dropped. Browser speech recognition sends children's voices to a cloud service, which is a KVKK problem, so c31 should stay teacher-judged.

gaps.gap: The content model has structural holes for specific games.
gaps.why: There is no 'scene' frame (objects, positions, counts; needed by x04, prepositions and describing). There is no 'grid' frame for c20 Battleship (row set × column set → the correct sentence for each cell). c28 needs events and dilemmas with meter effects, but story-node effects only cover hp, gold and item. There is no 'dialogue' item with speaker turns (LGS dialogue completion, two TTS voices), no 'command' item for TPR, and no per-item pre-rendered 'audio' field for offline use.

gaps.gap: Not every game works with both content doors (built-in topic and LLM prompt).
gaps.why: STOP needs categories that cut across topics, Battleship needs a grid, Wordle needs words of a fixed length, Codenames needs 25 words that can be clued, Kelime Oyunu needs lengths 4-10, and most vocabulary games get worse with a grammar topic. The picker needs a game × pack feasibility check with a named fallback ('Bu paketten yalnızca 4 Wordle kelimesi çıkıyor: komşu kategoriden tamamla / şu oyunu öner').

gaps.gap: There is no non-competitive default for adults who dislike competition.
gaps.why: Only c04, c08, c28 and c29 are co-operative. Add a third rule pack, 'İşbirliği', where the class chases one shared target ('the class needs 25 stars') instead of team scores, available in every scored game. Stüdyo setup could ask 'Rekabet sever mi?'.

gaps.gap: Large classes get too little talking time.
gaps.why: With one screen and four teams of ten, each student speaks for seconds per lesson. A 'Masa modu' (parallel desk play) fixes this: printable boards and cards for c02, c12, c13, c23 and x05, played in groups of four while the screen runs the shared dice, timer, card reveal and answer key.

gaps.gap: No flashcard pre-teach step, and no retrieval across lessons.
gaps.why: Teachers present and drill words before a game (slow reveal, flash, whisper-shout choral repetition). Gogo's demo round teaches the rules, not the words. Smart repetition only works inside one session. Add an 'Önce öğret' flashcard step for every pack, a 'Geçen dersten' door that builds a warmer from last lesson's Kaçırılanlar, and an exit-ticket plenary.

gaps.gap: Some categories are missing.
gaps.why: Missing are numbers, dates, prices and spelling as a listening category for all ages (thirteen/thirty, and the English letter names A/E/I, which Turkish speakers confuse); calendar packs for 23 Nisan, 29 Ekim, 24 Kasım, the Bayrams and Yılbaşı; brand-free gaming and esports words for Arena; YKS-YDT (the 12th-grade exam, which private-course teachers need); and classroom survival language for A1 adults.

gaps.gap: The hub has no activity metadata for choosing a game.
gaps.why: The teacher picks by situation: energy (calm or lively), noise, movement, prep (printing?), minutes, skill and minimum age. Without these tags the 'Game hub' can't answer 'Bugün ne oynasam?' or build a ready 'Nöbetçi ders' (zero-prep substitute lesson) playlist.

newCandidates.name: Gogo Diyor ki! / Ayağa Kalk (Simon Says, Stand Up If, Four Corners, Opinion Line)
newCandidates.familiarAs: Simon Says, 'Stand up if...', Four Corners, Opinion Line / human spectrum (TPR games)
newCandidates.oneLiner: The whole class answers with their bodies (stand, sit, point, mime, move to a corner or along a line) while the screen calls commands, statements or questions, and a trap phrase keeps everyone listening.
newCandidates.howItPlays: The teacher picks 1-3 round types, 2-4 minutes each. (1) COMMANDS: TTS (or the teacher, in 'Öğretmen okur' mode) gives a command from the pack ('Touch your nose', 'Walk like a penguin', 'Show me something blue'). The action picture appears 1.5 s after the audio, so listening comes first. Students obey only when the command starts with the trap phrase. Traps start at 1 in 5 and rise to 1 in 3. (2) STAND UP IF / TRUE-FALSE: a tf item or a survey line. Stand = true (or 'I have'), sit = false, hands on head = not sure. At the reveal, the class repeats the correct sentence twice. (3) FOUR WALLS: an mcq whose options map to the four walls (or 1-4 fingers when the room is tight). Pairs consult for 10-20 s, then everyone points or moves. (4) OPINION LINE (B groups): the window side is 'strongly agree' and the door side 'strongly disagree'. The seat spinner picks 2-3 students to justify, using the starters on screen. Then 'Changed your mind? Move!'. The class plays against the game, not against each other. The teacher taps a 3-level estimate (1 Everyone / 2 Most / 3 Some), which fills a class meter. Nobody is ever out. The last round is always a calming 'sit down if...' sequence that ends with everyone seated.
newCandidates.playerSetup: Whole class at once (up to 40). Optionally, desk rows act as teams with row captains. A seated-only filter suits fixed desks.
skills: grammar (imperatives, can, present perfect 'have you ever', conditionals)
newCandidates.adultVersion: Stüdyo 'Stand Up If / Opinion Line', with no Simon Says trap. 'Stand up if you have ever...' (present perfect) is followed by a spinner-picked 'When was that?' (past simple). This builds a class-report moment ('About half of us have...') that can feed c21. Four Walls reviews mcq items after a 20 s pair consultation. The Opinion Line runs debate prompts with useful language on screen ('I see your point, but...'). There are no scores by default. The seated business-class variant uses fingers or colour cards. The editorial look has no mascot.
newCandidates.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Gogo Says!' has three rules, all shown as pictograms: (1) Listen for 'Gogo says'. (2) No 'Gogo says'? Freeze! (3) Everybody plays. Students caught by a trap strike a funny freeze pose (statue, robot, tree) for 3 s and stay in, so there is no elimination. Gogo sometimes gets a trap wrong himself ('Oops!'). Command sets follow the units: body parts, actions, animals ('Hop like a frog'), colours, classroom objects, feelings. Audio plays at 0.8x, stars go into the class jar, and a score never goes down. ARENA 'Captain's Orders / Reflex Sync' has no parrot and uses a neon COMMAND strip. Gaps shrink to 2 s. Commands have several steps ('Clap twice, then touch your left shoulder') and include left/right, memory commands ('Do the last two again'), and a 'Squad Sync %' per row. The combo builds on 'Everyone' ratings. 'Stand up if...' uses safe, cool prompts (can do a handstand, has been to Kapadokya). It is framed as a reflex challenge, not a kids' game.
newCandidates.levelTuning: A1 / A1T: one-verb commands with body parts, colours and numbers; picture support; 'Stand up if you have a cat'. A2 / A2T: two-step commands with and/then, prepositions ('Put your pen on your book'), adverbs (slowly, quietly), 'Stand up if you can...' and 'if you like...'. B1 / B1T: conditional commands ('If you're wearing black, touch your head'), present perfect surveys, sequence commands, Four Walls with context mcqs. B2 / B2T: relative clauses and double conditions, an opinion line with justification and concession, and a persuasion round ('Convince two people to move'). Screen text follows the word caps; commands are mostly audio.
newCandidates.sessionMinutes: 3-10 as a warmer, brain break or settler; 15 as a full set
newCandidates.contentShape: A new 'command' item: {text, verb, bodyPart?, picture, seatedOk (bool), movement ('none'|'hands'|'stand'|'walk'), trapAllowed}. It is generated from vocab items with actable=true plus command frames. tf items with about='picture'|'sentence-correct'. survey / speaking-prompt with mode 'survey' or 'opinion' for 'Stand up if' and the opinion line. mcq for Four Walls. A curated safe-topic list decides which 'Stand up if' prompts are allowed.
newCandidates.delightDetails: Listening comes first: the picture follows the audio. The teacher panel has a 'mirror' hint because left and right flip when the teacher faces the class. A 'Sleepy Gogo' settler slows and softens the commands until heads are on arms. Every card carries a seated-safe icon. At the end, a class map of the adult survey results turns into review sentences in Kaçırılanlar. The trap phrase can be personalised ('Captain says', 'Teacher says').
newCandidates.teacherControls: Trap rate, speed, seated-only and hands-only filters, round-type toggles, the 3-level class estimate keys, repeat audio, Öğretmen okur, safe-prompt list editing, row-teams toggle.
newCandidates.risks: Noise and crowding in classes of 35-40: seated-only is the default for public schools. 'Stand up if' can expose personal facts: only curated safe topics are allowed (never family, religion, money, health or body), and teenSafe applies. Judging a whole class is fuzzy, so the game uses estimates and never scores individuals. 13-year-olds may find Simon Says childish, which the Arena reframing addresses. Students with limited mobility get a hands-only equivalent for every command.
sources: C:/lg/docs/classroom-games-roadmap.md (the TPR response mode is only assumed, not built)

newCandidates.name: Harf Havuzu (Bir Kelime-style Letters, Boggle Grid & Anagram)
newCandidates.familiarAs: Bir Kelime Bir İşlem (word round), Countdown letters, Boggle, anagram / Scrabble-like word building
newCandidates.oneLiner: Letter tiles are drawn, and teams race to build the longest or the most real English words. Each word is checked instantly against the word bank; kids unscramble a picture word from big tiles instead.
newCandidates.howItPlays: MODE 1 'Bir Kelime' (default for adults): (1) A captain calls 'vowel' or 'consonant' eight times; the engine guarantees at least 3 vowels. The tiles flip, and the 9th tile is a joker '?'. The pool is always seeded from one pack word, so a topic word is always hidden in it. (2) Teams think for 30 s (45 s in Nazik) to a soft ticking loop. (3) 'Boards up': every team shows its longest word on a mini-whiteboard. (4) The teacher types two letters and taps each team's word from autocomplete. The engine checks that the letters are available and that the word is real (lemmas plus generated inflections), then shows its level badge and Turkish meaning. Scoring uses the TV table: 3→3, 4→4, 5→5, 6→7, 7→9, 8→11, 9→15. On equal length, the word without the joker wins, as on the show. (5) Reveal: 'Did you see this?' shows the hidden topic word and the longest word possible at the group's level. A team earns +2 for using its word in a sentence (teacher judge). MODE 2 'Kelime Avı' (Boggle): a 4x4 grid, seeded so it holds at least N topic words; teams list words for 2 minutes; a word no other team found scores double, as in İsim-Şehir. MODE 3 'Karışık Harfler' (anagram / conundrum): a scrambled pack word with a clue ladder (picture, then defEasy, then Turkish). Everyone answers on boards.
newCandidates.playerSetup: 2-6 teams of 3-6, one mini-whiteboard per team. Kids play whole class. Pairs can play a quiet mode.
newCandidates.adultVersion: Stüdyo quiz-night letter tiles (a generic look that does not copy the TRT show). The TV scoring table and joker apply, with 30 s per round. B1-B2 get a 'Word family' bonus: say another form of your word (decide → decision). The final round is a 9-letter conundrum of a topic word; hands-up buzzing, one attempt per team. Kaçırılanlar lists the best words the class missed, with their meanings. No wagering.
newCandidates.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Gogo's Letter Soup' has three rules: look at the picture, say the letters, build the word. A big picture (a cat) sits beside large lowercase tiles (Andika-type font, single-storey a). The whole class spells aloud together while the active team's seat-picked student taps the tiles in order on the board. Every tile sounds out its phonics sound and its letter name. Then comes 'How many words can we make from ELEPHANT?': a whole-class brainstorm where every valid word adds a sticker to the class jar. There is no longest-word race, no losing, and every turn has a response from the whole class. ARENA 'Word Forge' has dark tiles that glow in the team colour, a 30 s forge per round and a streak for a valid word every round. A 'Legendary word' (7+ letters) gets a 1.2 s sting. The Boggle mode becomes 'Grid Raid' (90 s, unique words double). Team stats at the end: Longest word, Most words.
newCandidates.levelTuning: Anagrams for kids: A1T 3-4 letters, A2T 4-6, B1T 5-7, B2T 6-8, always with a picture. Letter pools for adults: A1 has 7 letters and 3 vowels, words of 3+ letters, and a picture or TR clue for the seeded word. A2 has 8 letters and bonus stars for A1-A2 band words. B1 has 9 letters plus a joker, 45→30 s and the word-family bonus. B2 has 9 letters plus a joker, 30 s, a bonus for C1+ words, and a 'use it with a collocation' sentence. Any real word counts at every level; the level only changes the bonuses.
newCandidates.sessionMinutes: 5-15 (one round takes about 90 s; 6-8 rounds make a 12-minute block)
newCandidates.contentShape: The pool frame is computed by code, never by the LLM: {letters[8], joker, seedWord (a pack vocab term), solutions[] (computed), bestAtLevel[] (computed)}. Validation uses words.js lemmas plus an inflection generator and an irregular-forms table, plus the pack terms. Proper nouns are off. An offensive and teen-unsafe blocklist applies to both solutions and displayed words. Anagram mode uses vocab.term, media, defEasy and defTr. Both content doors work, because the LLM or the built-in topic only supplies the topic words.
newCandidates.delightDetails: Each tile flips with a marimba note pitched by its position. The letter bag follows English letter frequency. The captain's vowel/consonant call gives the team ownership. Input is normalised for the Turkish keyboard (ı→i, İ→I) so a typed answer isn't rejected. Near-miss spellings ('recieve') trigger a spelling tip and go into the Hata defteri. The 'Did you see this?' reveal is the moment that teaches.
newCandidates.teacherControls: Vowel/consonant balance, timer, joker on/off, minimum word length, dictionary strictness (lemmas only or with inflections), an 'accept anyway' key that saves to accepted-answer memory, topic seeding on/off, bonus-level band, and the mode selector.
newCandidates.risks: Dictionary coverage: words.js has no inflected forms, so the inflection table and 'accept anyway' are required. Random letters can form rude words, so the blocklist filters solutions and displays. Typing on a smartboard is slow, so the teacher uses two letters plus autocomplete. Weak teams only find 3-letter words, so Nazik mode counts all valid words together as a class total. Do not use the TV show's name or logo as the title: use 'Harf Havuzu' and describe it as 'Bir Kelime tarzı'.
