newCandidates.name: Kulaktan Kulağa (Whisper Chain, Paper Telephone & Dictogloss)
newCandidates.familiarAs: Kulaktan kulağa / Chinese whispers / Telephone, Gartic Phone-style paper chain (write-draw-write), Dictogloss
newCandidates.oneLiner: A sentence travels down each desk row by whisper, or by write-draw-write on folded paper, and the screen shows word by word how much of it survived; a dictogloss mode rebuilds a short text heard twice.
newCandidates.howItPlays: MODE A 'Fısıltı Zinciri' (rows are teams): (1) Seeding happens with no phones. Either the screen shows 'Row starters look now; everyone else heads down' for 5 s (answer-leak guard), or the teacher hands out printed, numbered, folded seed slips, or the seed appears on the teacher's Kumanda. Each row gets a different sentence of equal length and target. (2) Each student whispers once down the row. A row may spend one 'Say again' token. (3) The last student writes the sentence on a mini-whiteboard; A1T students point to one of four pictures on screen instead. (4) Reveal: the teacher taps the arrived words from chips. The engine aligns them with the original and colours words kept, changed or lost. Points go to kept content words, plus a bonus if the target structure survived (third-person -s, a past form). A 'Plot twist of the day' prize celebrates the funniest drift. (5) The class says the original sentence together. MODE B 'Kâğıt Telefon' (age 12 and up, adults): printable strips. Student 1 writes a sentence from a prompt in the target grammar and folds it. Student 2 draws it and folds so only the drawing shows. Student 3 describes the drawing in writing, and so on. The screen runs 45-60 s step timers and calls 'Pass!'. At the reveal, rows read their chains aloud, the class votes for the most surprising chain, and the teacher ticks target use. MODE C 'Yeniden Kur' (dictogloss, B groups): TTS or the teacher reads a 40-140 word text twice. Students jot key words, then teams rebuild the text in 6 minutes. The reveal highlights the idea units (from the text's sentences[] and content words) and the target structures each team got.
newCandidates.playerSetup: Mode A: desk rows as teams (4-8 rows of 4-6), which fits fixed-desk classrooms. Mode B: groups of 4-6. Mode C: groups of 3-4. All teams play at the same time.
newCandidates.adultVersion: Stüdyo uses the whisper chain as a 5-minute warmer built on drift traps: numbers (thirteen/thirty, fifteen/fifty), names, and minimal-pair words. The reveal links each drift to a sound item and its mouth tip. Dictogloss is the main adult mode, with news-style anecdotes at level; its reveal feeds missed structures into Kaçırılanlar. Paper Telephone with neutral prompts works as an icebreaker for new courses. There are no penalties, and the game is calm and quiet by design.
newCandidates.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Gogo's Secret' has three rules, all shown as pictograms: whisper once, pass it on, the last friend points to the picture. Seeds are 2-4 word picture phrases ('a big red ball'). The last student chooses among four pictures that differ in one detail (red/blue, on/under), so nobody writes. Every row gets a sticker for trying and an extra one for a match. Gogo says the original, and the whole class repeats it twice: a whole-class moment, no elimination, no scores below zero. ARENA 'Signal Relay': squads 'transmit a code' of 6-12 words with a built-in twist (a number, a name, a past form), and the reveal shows 'Signal integrity %'. The 'Draw & Guess Chain' is the highlight for this age, because the Gartic-style format is familiar to them. Stats: Most words saved, Best glow-up.
newCandidates.levelTuning: A1T: 2-4 word picture phrases, answered by pointing. A2T: 5-8 words, answered by writing with a word bank. B1T: 8-12 words with one target structure, written. B2T: 12-16 words with two clauses, plus Paper Telephone. A1 adults: 5-7 words carrying numbers, times and names (practical listening). A2: 8-10 words. B1: 12-15 words, dictogloss of about 60 words. B2: dictogloss of 100-140 words with 3 target structures and idea-unit scoring.
newCandidates.contentShape: Seed sentences come from vocab.example, gap text with the answer filled in, or order tokens joined, and are balanced per row by length, word level and target. Kids' final choices use 4 picture options that differ in one attribute (an mcq with fmt 'picture'). Dictogloss uses a text item (sentences[] and words computed) plus target tags. Printable seed slips and fold strips are generated per row.
newCandidates.delightDetails: The reveal animates lost words dropping out and replacements sliding in. Drift traps (numbers, names) are planted on purpose and explained afterwards. A 'Say again' token per row adds strategy. The noise meter shows 'whisper level', so this is a game that rewards quiet. At the end, TTS plays the original and the drifted version back to back. The printables carry row numbers and fold lines.
newCandidates.teacherControls: Seed delivery (screen peek, printed slips or Kumanda), sentence length and target, number of repeats, final answer mode (point, write or say), dictogloss speed and number of readings, TTS or Öğretmen okur, a key to accept a variant.
newCandidates.risks: Whispering into ears can feel uncomfortable or unhygienic, so allow a hand-cupped whisper or a written pass. Some students distort the sentence on purpose; scoring by kept words rewards accuracy. The seed can leak when projected, so use printables or the peek screen. Dictogloss is too heavy below B1T. Students with hearing impairments should use the paper modes.

newCandidates.name: Tanık! (What's Missing, Eyewitness & Spot the Difference on code-built scenes)
newCandidates.familiarAs: Kim's Game / What's missing?, Spot the Difference (Farkı bul), Listen and Draw (picture dictation), eyewitness memory quiz
newCandidates.oneLiner: A scene built by code from the pack's picturable items flashes on screen. Teams recall and describe it, name what vanished or moved, or find the differences between paired A/B sheets, and every answer is checkable because the engine knows where each object is.
newCandidates.howItPlays: The engine composes a scene: a background (room, kitchen, park, classroom, street, beach, café, airport gate) plus 6-16 stickers taken from the pack, each with a colour, a count and a position relative to landmarks (on, under, next to, between, behind). Questions and answers are computed from this, so nothing is hallucinated. MODE 1 'What's missing?': 6-12 labelled items are shown and read aloud for 20-30 s. The screen goes dark ('Close your eyes!'). One or two items disappear; at higher levels items move, change colour or change count. Every team answers on boards ('The umbrella is missing', or at B 'The cat was under the table; now it's on the chair'). MODE 2 'Eyewitness': a busy scene shows for 20-40 s, then hides. 5-8 computed questions follow: tf 'There were three cups on the table', mcq 'What colour was the man's bag?', qa 'How many birds were there?', and at B1 'What was the woman doing?'. Everyone answers each one, then the scene returns with the relevant object highlighted. MODE 3 'Farkı Bul' (pairs): printed A/B sheets of one scene with 5-7 computed differences. Partners cover their sheets and find the differences only by talking ('In my picture there are two apples.' 'In mine there are three!'). The screen shows a timer, language frames and the circled reveal. A 'Resim Dikte' variant has TTS or the teacher describe the scene while students draw; the reveal comes with a self-check list ('Is there a cat under the table?').
newCandidates.playerSetup: Modes 1-2: the whole class in 2-6 teams, all answering. Mode 3: the whole class in pairs at the same time.
skills: grammar (there is/are, prepositions, past simple/continuous, quantifiers, deduction modals)
newCandidates.adultVersion: Stüdyo 'Eyewitness' uses scenes adults recognise (hotel lobby, café, airport gate, shop with prices and signs) in a flat editorial illustration style with a muted palette. A1-A2 do Spot the Difference with prices, times and signs. B1 works on past continuous witness statements. B2 uses deduction modals ('He must have been waiting for someone') and writes a three-sentence 'witness report' that is compared with the scene. The game is co-operative or scored, as the teacher chooses.
newCandidates.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Gogo's Room / What's missing?' has three rules: look, close your eyes, say what's missing. It shows 6-8 big stickers, with labels read aloud at 0.8x. The whole class points or calls out, then Gogo reveals the item hidden behind his wing ('Gogo took it!'), and everyone repeats 'The ball is missing!' twice. Stars are never lost. Spot the Difference in pairs has 3-5 differences, supported by an 'In my picture...' pictogram frame. ARENA 'Recon' is a dark HUD with a 'scan' sweep across the scene for 20 s. Questions come as 'intel checks', perfect recall builds a streak, and a 'Moved or missing?' hard mode is available. The end award is 'Sharpest eyes'.
newCandidates.levelTuning: A1T: 6 items, 1 missing, nouns, colours and numbers. A2T: 8-10 items, there is/are, prepositions, 2 changes. B1T: 12 items, past simple and continuous questions, changes of position and colour. B2T: 14-16 items, comparative and relative-clause questions ('the girl who was holding...'). A1: shop or café scene with prices and there is/are. A2: 'Was there...?' in past simple. B1: past continuous witness reports. B2: deduction modals, a written report, and 7 subtle differences (a few vs a lot of).
newCandidates.sessionMinutes: 5-10 (What's Missing warmer); 10-20 (Eyewitness or Spot the Difference)
newCandidates.contentShape: A new computed 'scene' frame: {bg, objects[{imageKey, vocabId, colour, count, anchor, relation}], variants{A,B,diffs[]}, questions[] (computed tf/mcq/qa)}. It draws on vocab items with media.img and concrete=true. Placement rules keep scenes sensible (cups on tables, birds in trees). A grammar-only pack falls back to a generic scene, with the grammar carried by the question templates.
newCandidates.delightDetails: A soft 'camera flash' opens each look. The reveal zooms onto the answer. A/B sheets print with a fold line and big A and B labels so partners can't peek. The self-check list for picture dictation is generated automatically. A 'class memory record' carries over between lessons. A colour question is never the only cue, for colour-blind students.
newCandidates.teacherControls: Look time, number of objects, number and type of changes (missing, moved, colour, count), question templates, background, print A/B sheets, re-show key, colour-question toggle, a 2 s 'peek' hint in Nazik mode.
newCandidates.risks: The whole game depends on a large, consistent sticker set (words.js has no image fields), and scene quality makes or breaks it. Abstract topics can't be pictured, so the game falls back to generic scenes. Memory games can frustrate weaker learners, which the peek hint and team answers soften. Public schools may not be able to print, so Mode 3 can also run half-screen on the projector with one partner facing away.

newCandidates.name: Sınıfı Dolaş (Find Someone Who, Find Your Partner & Card Swap)
newCandidates.familiarAs: Find Someone Who / human bingo, mingle 'find your partner' cards, Go Fish-style 'Do you have...?' card swap
newCandidates.oneLiner: Every student holds a printed card and asks classmates questions in English to find the person who matches, fill a grid, or complete a set; the screen runs the timer, the question frames, pair checks and the debrief.
newCandidates.howItPlays: MODE 1 'Eşini Bul' (mingle match): the engine prints exactly as many card halves as there are students (odd numbers get a teacher card). Halves are pair items: picture/word, word/definition, question/answer, sentence halves, present/past, idiom/meaning. The one rule is never to show your card: ask and answer instead ('Have you got something you wear on your head?'). Matched pairs stand together. The teacher types the two tiny card codes, the screen confirms, and each pair reads out its match. The pairs then become the teams for the next game (team-maker hook). MODE 2 'Kimde Var?' (Find someone who): a printable grid (3x3 for kids, 4x4 for adults) of 'Find someone who can swim / has been to Ankara'. Genç groups use fictional role cards by default for privacy. A student needs a follow-up answer before writing a name. A line counts as 'Bingo!'. In the debrief the teacher taps hand counts per square, which gives a class chart and report sentences ('Twelve of us can swim') and can feed c21. MODE 3 'Takas' (seated, groups of 4): collect sets of four (for example 4 animals from one habitat) by asking 'Do you have a...?'. It is calm and works at fixed desks.
newCandidates.playerSetup: Whole class at once (up to 40). 'Row mingle' means asking only your row and the row behind, for fixed desks. Mode 3 runs in groups of 4.
newCandidates.adultVersion: Stüdyo 'Networking Mixer' is the first-day icebreaker for a course. Students get fictional business profiles (character items: 'Find the person who works in İzmir and needs a supplier'), or real but safe 'Find someone who has ever...' prompts. A follow-up question is required before a name counts. B2 adds a needs/haves negotiation mingle: each person trades to fulfil a need. There are no scores, so it suits adults who dislike competition. The debrief asks 'What surprised you?'.
newCandidates.teenVersion: OYUN PARKI 'Find Your Friend!' has three rules: ask, answer, find your friend. A1T uses identical picture pairs ('Have you got a panda?' 'Yes, I have! / No, I haven't.'), and Gogo models the frame on screen. In the seated option, cards pass along the rows. Everyone ends up with a friend, nobody is left out, and there are no scores. ARENA 'Duo Hunt / Squad Draft' shows a timer and a counter of duos found. The Find Someone Who prompts suit this age (has a game high score, can do a handstand, has been to Kapadokya). The resulting duos become the squads for the next Challenge, which gives the students ownership.
newCandidates.levelTuning: A1T: identical picture pairs, 'Have you got...?'. A2T: picture/word, 'Do you like...?' and 'Can you...?'. B1T: sentence halves, question/answer, 'Have you ever...?'. B2T: word/definition, idiom/meaning, a follow-up question required. A1: personal information on fictional ID cards ('How do you spell it?'). A2: routines and last weekend (fictional). B1: present perfect experiences, collocation halves. B2: needs/haves negotiation and paraphrasing definitions without reading them aloud.
newCandidates.contentShape: Pair items (with the set field for uniqueness) are cut into card halves carrying a hidden 2-character check code. speaking-prompt or survey items with mode 'find-someone' fill the grid, each with followUps[]. character items supply fictional profiles. category-list sets of 4 supply the swap mode. A class-size input drives exact card counts.
newCandidates.delightDetails: The pair-check codes let the teacher verify a match in 2 s without reading every card. A teacher card covers odd class sizes. The screen keeps the question frame and a 'Say it again, please' repair chip visible. The hand-count debrief turns into a live bar chart and ready-made report sentences. Pairs roll straight into the next game in the lesson playlist.
newCandidates.teacherControls: Class size, mingle radius (free, row or table), timer, card type, fictional or real prompts, print, check-pair key, debrief counts, whether a follow-up is required.
newCandidates.risks: Movement in crowded rooms: seated and row-mingle options exist. Noise: the noise meter helps, and the mingle is short. Privacy in 'Find someone who': fictional cards are the default for Genç, and sensitive topics are never used. Social exclusion: random cards decide partners, students never choose. It depends on printing; the fallback is a numbered on-screen list students copy from ('You are number 7: write this word').

otherFixes: c24 'Tik Tak Bomba': bomb imagery breaks the 'non-violent failure imagery' rule for kids and is a sensitive image in Turkish schools. Title it 'Sıcak Patates' everywhere, with a popcorn or jack-in-the-box pop for Oyun Parkı. The 'penalty card' becomes a silly bonus task for kids.

c20 Battleship and c14 swat/whack-a-mole: give Oyun Parkı non-violent skins ('Treasure Divers: find the hidden pets'; pop bubbles or balloons instead of swatting flies or hitting moles). Keep 'fire' and 'sunk' for Stüdyo only.

c10 and c27: social deduction and 'catch the liar' single out one classmate, which conflicts with 'nobody picked by name'. In Oyun Parkı the impostor is Gogo or a whole team, and nobody votes on an individual child. In Arena, votes target the role card or seat code, never a name. Full Town Mystery should be adults and Arena opt-in only.

Wager mechanics (c05 risk, c06 Daily Double and Final, c22 bidding, c01 luck dial): teenSafe bans gambling, so for Genç groups frame them as 'confidence tokens' that can't be lost below zero, with no money wording.
c09 'Turkish slip' penalty: for Oyun Parkı make it a non-punitive 'Gogo squawks: In English, please!' followed by a re-say. Only Stüdyo deducts points.

c21: replace the 'live 3-minute phone survey' for all school groups with a hand-count survey the teacher taps in (MEB bans phones in classrooms). The '100 people' generated set must be labelled as invented.
c18 Codenames and c09 secret cards: add printable seeded key cards (the board seed prints a matching key) and a 'heads down' peek screen, so spymasters and describers never need a phone.
c16 Tombala: printed cards only for Genç groups (no phone cards). Never attach prizes, because tombala has gambling associations at New Year.

c15 Wordle and c30 Kelime Oyunu: add a per-pack feasibility check (words.js has only about 750 five-letter and about 680 four-letter lemmas at all levels combined). Top up from neighbouring categories and say so, and validate guesses against lemmas plus inflections.

c19 STOP: add a proper-noun list (countries, capitals, Turkish cities, first names), because words.js has none. Allow multi-word answers at B, and give Genç groups picture categories (oral STOP for A1T).
c31: judge pronunciation by the teacher only. No cloud speech recognition for minors (KVKK). Take IPA only from words.js or CMUdict, never from the LLM.
c32 running dictation: add a no-running version for fixed desks (timed flashes, or the evidence card passed along the row). Fold in roadmap G03 jigsaw reading and G23 predict-and-update as modes.

c12 Memory: add roadmap G05 collocation domino as a chain mode. c26 Detective: add G25 co-op logic grid as the Oyun Parkı variant. c29: add G09 map directions for A1-A2 and G28 repair cards. c11: add G30 4/3/2 retell.
c07 League: apply the 'LGS rule' (3 wrong cancel 1 correct) only to LGS items. YDS and YÖKDİL have no negative marking, so a YDS league must not use it.
c03 Hangman and every typed game: normalise the Turkish keyboard (ı→i, İ→I, ş/ğ never valid) before checking answers. Show English letter names on the on-screen keyboard for A/E/I confusion.

Trademarks: in the student-facing UI use generic titles (Property board, Category board, Word Vault) with no logos or trade dress of Monopoly, Jeopardy, Taboo, Codenames, Wordle, Millionaire, Family Feud, Gimkit or the TRT 'Bir Kelime Bir İşlem'. Names of the originals may appear only in teacher-facing 'familiar as' text.
Team identity: always pair team colour with a shape, emblem or letter (Stüdyo has no mascots, so give it monogram badges). Projectors wash out colour, and roughly 8% of boys are colour-blind.
Arena's default dark navy theme may look grey on low-lumen projectors in sunlit rooms. Ship a 'light Arena' (neon on light slate) and add a 2-second projector contrast check in setup.
Hub filters: tag every game with energy (sakin/hareketli), noise, movement, print needed, minutes, skills and minimum age, and offer a zero-prep 'Nöbetçi ders' playlist per group.

Add the proposed item types and frames to the universal pack schema before the games that need them: build (sentence production), command (TPR), scene (x04), grid (c20), dialogue (LGS and TTS), event/dilemma with meter effects (c28), and a per-item audio URL for offline listening.
